articles.title: Disney and Old Navy Team Up for New Haunted Halloween Line of Cozy Flannels, PJs and Totes
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Camila Quimper Plus Icon Camila Quimper View All July 30, 2026 4:36pm Courtesy of Old Navy If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. It may still be summer, but Disney’s Halloween merchandise lineup is getting a fall refresh. The company is teaming up with Old Navy for the Haunted Harvest collection , a new assortment of cozy apparel and accessories inspired by Disney ’s Halloween favorites. Disney x old navy Haunted Harvest Collection Like many of Disney’s seasonal merchandise drops, the latest collection brings its recognizable characters and storytelling into a new lineup of fan-focused products. The Old Navy collaboration features autumn-inspired designs for babies, toddlers, kids, adults and even pets, with styles made for pumpkin patch trips, Halloween celebrations and fall family photos. Related Stories Lifestyle Hulu Eliminated Its Free Trial -- Here's a Workaround Lifestyle Nordstrom Anniversary Sale's 24 Best Beauty Buys: Le Labo, La Mer and More Premium Picks The 40-piece assortment covers all the fall essentials, including cozy flannels, pajamas, hoodies, crewnecks, socks and accessories. Shoppers can expect warm autumn colors, heritage-inspired textures, spooky plaids and playful Disney graphics throughout the collection. Prices range from $7.99 to $54.99. Old Navy cardmembers can shop the collection early starting Thursday, July 30, while the full collection officially launches for everyone on Friday, July 31. The Old Navy partnership continues a strong year for Disney merchandise releases, following major franchise moments including the live-action remake of Moana and the release of Toy Story 5 (which brought along a nostalgia-fueled collab with Away luggage ). As Disney continues expanding its consumer products business, the company is finding new ways to bring its most recognizable IP to fans through seasonal collections, retail partnerships and merchandise inspired by its biggest stories. Exclusive Drop Old Navy x Disney Minnie Mouse Boxy Cropped T-Shirt $24.99 at Old nAVY A classic boxy white tee that goes with everything, now with a little Disney magic added in. Old Navy x Disney Mickey Mouse Flannel Shirt $49.99 at old navy No fall wardrobe is complete without a heritage flannel, and this one gets a Disney twist with Mickey pumpkin details throughout. Old Navy x Disney Mickey Mouse Mini Bucket Bag $29.99 at old navy A Halloween bucket in bag form, this double-lined style fits sweet treats or everyday essentials. Old Navy x Disney Mickey Mouse Cardigan $49.99 at old navy Available in a rich, brown and burgundy fair isle pattern. Old Navy x Disney Pajama Top $29.99 at old navy A cozy Halloween night pick, this ribbed pajama set features a cream colorway and playful chipmunk print. Old Navy x Disney Pajama Pants $36.99 at old navy Complete the look with matching pull-on pajama pants . Disney Mickey Mouse Crew Socks $8.99 at old navy Stock up on fall-ready basics with these Fair Isle crew socks , available in two classic prints for under $9. Old Navy x Disney Mickey Mouse Sherpa Slippers $26.99 at old navy Plush insoles, sherpa uppers and a spooky Mickey pumpkin print make these slippers a cozy pick. Old Navy x Disney Packable Tote Bag $9.99 at old navy A packable tote perfect for apple picking, candy runs and farmers market trips. Choose from a plaid or black Disney design. The 40-piece Old Navy and Disney Haunted Harvest collection officially launches Friday, July 31 at Old Navy , with early access on July 30 for cardholders . THR

articles.title: The Affordability Squeeze Has Come for Brandy Melville’s TikTok Star Staffer
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 30, 2026 6:35pm Brandy Melville store on July 7, 2024. Photo by Cristina Arias/Cover/Getty Images The creator economy met the affordability squeeze this week in New York when TikTok darling and Brandy Melville SoHo staffer Allegra Pinkowitz was unceremoniously fired from her position with the controversial fast-fashion retailer after nearly two and a half years. While one may not think the part-time retail gig of a high school junior is notable news, Pinkowitz is also an up-and-coming TikToker with a following of 162K-plus. Last year, she was the subject of a New York magazine article titled “The Most Popular Girl in SoHo is a Brandy Melville Employee,” about the flocks of girls who have been showing up to watch her fold clothes during weekend shifts or after school. Related Stories Lifestyle Disney and Old Navy Team Up for New Haunted Halloween Line of Cozy Flannels, PJs and Totes Music Boy George Drops Out of London 'Jesus Christ Superstar' Production After Stirring Controversy With AI-Generated Pro-Israel Song When Pinkowitz received the news from a male manager by phone on Thursday, she was on TikTok faster than you can say vibecession. After an announcement clip set to rapper ASN JAYBOOG’s “Stanley Earl,” she was back hours later to dish on how it all went down. “This was so unexpected. You guys don’t understand — I’ve been working there for almost two and a half years,” she explains in the clip as she applies makeup; she told her fans she was about to get in the shower when a text arrived. @allegrasgrwm my @Katie Fang moment #nyc ♬ original sound – allegra “It’s basically like, ‘Can you just give me a call whenever you have a minute?’ … He’s basically like, ‘We didn’t make as much money as we were hoping to this summer, so we’re laying off a bunch of people,'” she explained in a series of video cuts of her doing her beauty ritual. “It was just basically, ‘But I’ll hold on to your contact, and if anything comes up in the fall, maybe you can come back.’ This was extremely unexpected.” Pinkowitz, whose TikTok fame drew crowds of upward of 20 fans at a time to Brandy Melville’s flagship lower Broadway store, was told that her firing had nothing to do with her work ethic. She added that the layoff “stings more because I’ve always talked really positively about this brand online,” and reassured her followers that she wasn’t there to hate on the brand. “I’m so sad. I expected a little bit more loyalty, but now I’m in the market for a new job,” the teenager said, holding back tears at moments throughout the clip. A first firing is always tough, but for Brandy Melville’s fanbase, the job loss means a central figure of the SoHo scene is gone. Criticized after switching to a more California-centric style for its one-size-fits-all apparel (it’s a small) and for reportedly favoring conventionally attractive, mostly blonde staff, the Italy-founded and now U.S.-based brand known for bleached wood, muted tones and T-shirts reading “NANTUCKET” saw further backlash after an investigative Business Insider story was published and later adapted into a 2024 documentary for HBO Max, called Brandy Hellville & the Cult of Fast Fashion . The film, in which Pinkowitz appears, features staffers discussing the body dysmorphia they developed while working for Brandy Melville and trying to fit into its image and its small clothing — sizing that was eventually changed to a tone-deaf “one-size-fits-most.” Pinkowitz’s recounting of the call — in which the manager cited lagging sales as the reason for layoffs — is hard to square with the many accounts of a mobbed SoHo location with lines out the door. It’s difficult to imagine all those tweens stopping in to catch a glimpse of Pinkowitz without buying anything. In 2025, Brandy Melville’s annual sales reached $283 million, with steady 10 to 15 percent year-over-year growth. Retail analysts say the brand’s business model yields unusually high profit margins, thanks largely to its one-size-fits-most approach and its social-media-driven marketing strategy. THR

articles.title: ‘Pachinko’ Star Kim Minha to Host Busan Film Festival’s Opening Ceremony
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 30, 2026 9:34pm Kim Minha Myunggu Han/Getty Images for Apple TV+ Pachinko star Kim Minha will host the gala opening ceremony of this year’s Busan International Film Festival . Asia ‘s leading cinema event customarily features two Korean stars at its kick-off event, but organizers revealed Friday that Kim will hold down the duties solo when BIFF raises its curtain on Oct. 6. Busan launched its first-ever main competition section last year for its landmark 30th edition. This year’s event will continue to try to build momentum for the section, establishing the Busan Awards Grand Prize as Asia’s premier cinema honor. Related Stories Business Europe to Boycott World Cup in FIFA Protest Movies Andy Garcia's Starry L.A. Noir 'Diamond' Lands at Sony Pictures Classics Kim is best known worldwide as young Sunja in Pachinko , Apple TV’s sweeping adaptation of Min Jin Lee’s bestselling novel, in which she shared the saga’s central role across timelines with Oscar winner Youn Yuh-jung. The part, spanning the series’ two seasons in 2022 and 2024, turned the actress — who debuted in 2016 — into one of the most closely watched young talents in Korean film and television. She has stayed busy since, with credits including the Dinsney+ series Light Shop , TVING’s Way Back Love and Typhoon Family on Netflix, along with this year’s film Hana Korea . She won best actress in the international competition at the 2025 Seoul International Drama Awards and best new actress at the 2025 Blue Dragon Series Awards. In announcing the appointment, BIFF credited the “depth and emotional precision she brings to every role” and her growing stature as a star of Korea’s new generation. “Known for her poised yet spirited presence, she is expected to bring warmth and confidence to the opening ceremony and set the tone for this year’s festival,” organizers said in a statement. BIFF’s 31st edition runs Oct. 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and other venues across the South Korean port city. THR

articles.title: Sadie Sink’s Secret Role in ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Finally Revealed
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 30, 2026 10:00pm Sadie Sink and 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Kevin Winter/Getty Images; Everett Collection Logo text [This story contains spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day .] Sadie Sink ‘s top-secret-ish role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day has finally been revealed. The reason I say “ish” is because despite Marvel and Sink remaining tight-lipped, fan rumors have been swirling about her casting since even before the first trailer that dropped in March included a two-second clip of a mystery person in a green jacket. This led fans to speculate that Sink was playing powerful mutant Jean Grey, as the character is known to have fiery red hair (much like Sink) and wear the color green, at least in some of her classic comic book appearances. Related Stories Movies Spider-Man: The Last Blockbuster Franchise Hollywood Hasn't Screwed Up Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Aims to Make Box Office History as It Targets High-Flying Opening Now that the Tom Holland -led film has hit theaters, I’m happy to congratulate those behind the rumors for being correct. Throughout the Brand New Day press tour leading up to the film’s release on July 31, the Stranger Things actress seemingly dodged all questions surrounding any specifics of her role. Earlier this month, during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter , director Destin Daniel Cretton shared that all the secrecy with Sink’s character has to do with the moviegoing experience. “Keeping what Sadie’s doing under wraps, you’ll honestly understand when you see the movie. The movie is a better movie if you don’t know certain things,” he said. “I wish people didn’t know anything when they go in to watch this movie, but we’re not doing it for any other reason but to protect the experience of the fans. And whoever goes on opening weekend, you are going to have a much cooler experience if you go in not knowing certain things.” Brand New Day has Holland back in the Spidey suit, with Zendaya and Jacob Batalon also reprising their roles as MJ and Ned, respectively. The fourth installment, coming off the box office success of 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home , sees Peter Parker living entirely alone as Spider-Man in a world that doesn’t remember him. That’s until mounting pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him triggers a dangerous change, while a powerful new villain emerges. Last year, while chatting with THR , Sink admitted she was looking forward to when she could finally talk about her Spider-Man role, as “There’s so much I want to share.” “Spider-Man has always been my favorite,” she said at the time. “I love Spider-Man. I love Tom’s Spider-Man, especially. To be a fan of something and then join it is a familiar feeling for me, because I was a fan of Stranger Things before I joined the show, but I was super excited about what they had planned. I also worked with the director, Destin Daniel Cretton, in one of the first movies I ever did when I was 14, so it’s kind of a full-circle moment. I had an amazing time working on that film.” Spider-Man: Brand New Day is currently playing in theaters. THR

articles.title: The Hollywood Left and the Blacklist: A Chat With the Curator of Locarno’s Timely Retrospective for the Age of Trump & Co.
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 30, 2026 10:30pm 'A King in New York' Courtesy of Roy Export SAS The retrospective at this year’s Locarno Film Festival feels particularly timely, maybe even scarily so. Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist promises to put the spotlight on “one of the most turbulent and politically charged periods in the history of American cinema,” including the “Red Scare” and the infamous Hollywood blacklist of the McCarthy era. After all, during the period from 1947 to the early 1960s, Hollywood professionals suspected of communist ties faced a crackdown. The Swiss festival’s cinematic look back will provide “a complex portrait of an era in which creatives were confronted by unprecedented abuse of state and industry power and which they met, courageously, with fierce artistic resistance,” Locarno highlighted. Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist will “re-examine this repressive yet defiantly creative era, which mirrors the political attacks on free speech and artistic freedom seen again today.” Related Stories Movies 'Pachinko' Star Kim Minha to Host Busan Film Festival's Opening Ceremony Business Europe to Boycott World Cup in FIFA Protest Produced in partnership with the Cinémathèque Suisse and with the support of UCLA Film & Television Archive, the Locarno retrospective was once again curated by Ehsan Khoshbakht . He has compiled a program of more than 50 films – fiction, documentaries, and shorts – and newsreels featuring such directors, writers, and stars as John Garfield, Joseph Losey, Dalton Trumbo , Dorothy Parker, Richard Wright, and Charlie Chaplin . It will explore various works to shine a spotlight on a time of polarized politics, allegations of communist infiltration of Hollywood in the Cold War, and the Hollywood blacklist that upended careers and forced artists to adopt pseudonyms or go into exile overseas. Among the films featured in the retrospective are the likes of Lewis Milestone’s The North Star (1943), None But the Lonely Heart (1944), directed by Clifford Odets, Crossfire (1947) from director Edward Dmytryk, Bernard Vorhaus’ Amazing Mr X (1948), Abraham Polonsky’s Force of Evil (1948), The Sound of Fury (1950), directed by Cy Endfield, Fred Zinnemann’s High Noon (1952), Charlie Chaplin’s A King in New York (1957), Hollywood on Trial (1976) by David Helpern, Martin Ritt’s The Front (1976) with Woody Allen, and 1996’s Red Hollywood , directed by Thom Andersen and Noël Burch. The 79th Locarno Film Festival runs Aug. 5-15. ‘The Front’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Sony Pictures Khoshbakht talked to THR about Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist , why it is “the timeliest” retrospective he has ever worked on, Hollywood’s role today, and the role of Charlie Chaplin and other stars in the showcase. Have you been working on this retrospective for Locarno for a long time, and how easy was the decision that the time was ripe for it? I had this project lined up for the future because it needed some proper research, but all of a sudden, I thought it was for now, because it’s about what’s happening right now. Even some of the terminology from back then is back in use. For instance, if you see press releases from the White House, there are some headlines with phrases that come right out of the McCarthy playbook, which is quite astonishing. They mention “the radical Left” and “radical propaganda,” among other things. But what is so interesting is that now both Left and Right, and the Center, have appropriated the terminology of that era to their own advantage. For instance, there was this Wall Street Journal headline saying basically: “McCarthyism is back – this time it’s woke.” So you can define McCarthyism as well, either as woke or anti-woke is McCarthyism. It’s just this confusion about the meaning of words and phrases that, back in the day, at least had some clear meaning – most of it completely wrong, but they were used in a very specific way. Curating retrospectives takes a lot of work and research. Can you share some insight into how long you researched this topic and these films? I had seen almost all of the films, so I knew my films, and that’s the most important part. But this is one of those subjects that comes with hundreds of books, and new books are being published every year. So, you want to catch up with the literature. There is also some other really interesting stuff, such as the declassified FBI files. That makes it far more exciting to dive into this episode in the history of American cinema. ‘Force of Evil’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Paramount There are also the oral histories and books that the victims of the blacklist, especially The Hollywood Ten, wrote from the late ’70s onwards about their own experience. There are contradictions, there are paradoxes, I guess a bit of egocentrism, but when you put them together with the rest, it gives you a relatively accurate picture of how things unfolded from ’47 onwards. I love the title you guys picked for the retrospective, Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist . How long did you think about what to call this showcase? Many good titles have been used by writers of books. One of those titles I love very much is Tender Comrades [: A Backstory of the Hollywood Blacklist ]. I thought the title should make clear that this is about not one subject, but actually two subjects. One is red, and one is black. Red is a reference to the Hollywood Left, which was active before the blacklist was introduced in 1947, and then black is for the blacklist. This is a program that actually studies the journey of the Hollywood Left from the early ’40s until the late ’60s. When Locarno unveiled this latest retrospective, you said this is the most timely retrospective you have put together. This is your third one for the Locarno festival, but you have done so much other work. How is this one different? It is my most timely retrospective so far, and it is something very special. The fact that we are talking about this is also special, because, sadly, The Hollywood Reporter was one of the key players in the blacklist episode, playing the role of a cheerleader for the FBI and for the [House of Representatives’ investigative committee known as the] House Un-American Activities Committee. ‘Native Son’ film still, courtesy of Kino Lorber If you asked me, if you put a gun to my head, why the blacklist happened, and I had to give you only one reason, I would tell you that it happened because of the union wars, because writers were successful in establishing the Screen Writers Guild, which Hollywood disliked very much, and which The Hollywood Reporter disliked. They didn’t want the writers to be powerful. The Hollywood Reporter didn’t miss any chance to attack the writers who were involved in the foundation of the Screen Writers Guild to the extent that in its reviews, when listing the cast and crew, it refused to list the name of the writer of the film, if it was someone like Dalton Trumbo. Some of these writers were making big money for Hollywood, like Trumbo, for instance, who was very well paid, and Ring Lardner Jr. In an attack directed at Lester Cole, they even published a front-page editorial by the editor of The Hollywood Reporter . And in that editorial, they mentioned his Communist Party membership number, which was secret information that even Cole didn’t have, because you didn’t really need that number. But the FBI had some spies in the Communist Party, and they had stolen that information, and that information was used. But it was not just The Hollywood Reporter . You had Catholic groups and others also campaigning behind the scenes. You have mentioned Trumbo and others. Some of the other faces and names that audiences will come across in the retrospective include the likes of John Garfield, Dorothy Parker and Charlie Chaplin. Can you talk about some of the big names and what roles they played? We have three different groups. One group is non-Americans, such as [German playwright] Bertolt Brecht, who testified [before the House Un-American Activities Committee], and the day after, he left the country for good. Otherwise, it would have been the Hollywood Eleven instead of The Hollywood Ten. But they couldn’t do much with him anyway because Brecht was not American, so the best they could have done was to deport him. But he was clever and said to hell with you, I’m going to go back home. Ehsan Khoshbakht, courtesy of Margherita Caprilli Courtesy of Margherita Caprilli Chaplin falls into that same category, because Chaplin was also not an American citizen. He was a British citizen. But the case with Chaplin is so unbelievably complex. Chaplin, even before the Communist Party of America started to gain more membership, was the subject of FBI surveillance. There are extensive records of him, and we are going to publish some of them in the book. They followed every movement of this man, because they were so afraid of him, in a sense, because he was perhaps the most popular and the most recognizable human figure on Earth. And he was very progressive. America was neutral at the beginning of the war, and the America First groups wanted to stay out of the war, but Chaplin, being British, was actively campaigning for the war. And then when America entered the war, Chaplin was campaigning for the Soviet allies, because that’s what President Roosevelt asked people to do to promote goodwill, because the U.S. needed the Soviets, and without them, they wouldn’t be able to win this war. And he was, you know, logistically, technically, absolutely right. So, so you have this group of non-Americans, and Chaplin is the most extreme case. The obsession with Chaplin, the anti-Semitic stories being circulated by the Hearst Media and the FBI about this man. Everything about him is so complex. Then you have a second group, which includes not the standard Hollywood people, but people who are also affected. This is the first time I’m showcasing the work of these people, too, such as [poet and writer] Dorothy Parker. She is not exactly a Hollywood person, but a celebrity, a writer, someone who stepped into Hollywood occasionally, but her world was mostly outside. I also have Richard Wright, the great African-American writer, in the program, and even Artie Shaw, the great jazz musician and bandleader. These are people who were affected by the blacklist. Artie Shaw, for example, went into self-imposed exile in Spain. David Halpern’s ‘Hollywood on Trial,’ courtesy of Corinth Films Courtesy of Corinth Films Finally, the third group has the very famous Hollywood people who were affected, the Hollywood Ten and beyond. It is much more than the Hollywood Ten in this program, because I think some of the people who were not part of the Hollywood Ten were actually far more interesting than some of its members. Film programs in the past refused to show works of people who named names, meaning people who eventually lost their integrity and became collaborators. But this program features works of such people as well because they were also believers. I think every program so far, perhaps unwittingly, has celebrated the idea of political martyrdom. I don’t believe in that, and I’m just interested in the Left, whether they stayed believers until the end or they just couldn’t take it anymore. One good example is Ben Maddow, one of the finest writers in Hollywood. After a while, he just couldn’t accept the fact that all these greatest scripts that he was writing were appearing on screen with the name of someone else. So he named names. I noticed that your retrospective is mixing genres and types of media, including not just films, but also old newsreels… Yes, I am trying to paint a more diverse but also broader and more accurate picture of the left and the blacklist in Hollywood. That’s why I decided to include many things, thanks to the UCLA Film & Television Archive, which is a partner in this. They have the best collection of material you can get on this subject. They have recently scanned original newsreels by Hearst Media, which was, in terms of media support of the witch hunt, at the forefront. Hearst Media produced many anti-communist newsreels and very harshly worded ones, in particular about the Hollywood Ten. I’m showing six of them. It’s very interesting because today, the word terrorist is used for anyone who is ideologically disliked and commits acts of violence. It should be easier to be able to say this person is a terrorist, and that person is “just” a criminal. And the term terrorist was used against communists in the ’40s, as we see in the news reels. It’s very interesting how these phrases sort of get recycled, and anyone opposing something you see as a person who poses a threat to your ideology. The word “terrorist” has been a standard term in American politics during the Trump administration. ‘The Hollywood Blacklist: The Survivors Tell Their Stories,’ courtesy of Cloud Studio SAS Your retrospective also mixes fiction and documentary features. What docs can audiences expect? There are going to be world premieres of two new documentaries. One is a documentary, driven by Eddie Muller, the writer and film noir expert. It is about Abraham Polonsky, who wrote some of the greatest films for blacklisted artists, but directed only one film, Force of Evil , before he was blacklisted. He couldn’t make another film until 20 years later, when he made Tell Them Willie Boy Is Here with Robert Redford. Eddie Muller believes he’s the greatest American writer. So there is this new feature documentary about him that has many great people, including directors and other Hollywood figures, talking about him. This film is called Dangerous Citizen : The Life and Times of Abraham Polonsky . The title comes from one of the declassified FBI files that said he was a very dangerous citizen. There’s also another documentary based on footage shot by a student during a party in Los Angeles in the early ’80s, where all the surviving members of the blacklist got together. This French woman, Marie- Dominique Montel, shot this footage and didn’t do anything with it until now, which is quite exciting. She’s been turning it into a documentary in color. So it will show us unseen footage of many of those Hollywood 10 people who were still alive then. The title is La Liste Noire d’Hollywood: Par ceux qui l’ont vécue , [or in English:] The Hollywood Blacklist: The Survivors Tell Their Stories . You mentioned the political situation and division in the U.S. of our day. How much political consciousness and activism do you see in current Hollywood? I have not seen every single film coming out of Hollywood, but some of the major titles that I have seen, for instance, Paul Thomas Anderson ‘s One Battle After Another , are open about it. I think he actually likes to study the period of the blacklist, because the film shows one of the many reincarnations of that culture of radical politics morphing into disillusionment and, in this case, political violence. ‘Dangerous Citizen: The Life and Times of Abraham Polonsky’ film still, courtesy of Black Pool Productions The Hollywood Left never transformed into something violent. And this is, I think, one of the great advantages that that movement had. If you compare films like Force of Evil , in which everybody and everything is corrupt from bottom to top, you will say, “Oh, Hollywood is very lame these days,” because nobody dares to paint a picture as bleak as some of these artists painted, especially in film noir and in crime thrillers. I think no period in Hollywood was as politically involved, within the confines of mass entertainment, as the ’30s and ’40s. However, you have far more political films made in Hollywood in the ’60s and ’70s. But the difference is that in the ’30s and ’40s, they were in the very heart of Hollywood, big titles that were making a case for change. in the ’60s and ’70s, when the definition of art house cinema became more prominent, it became something more niche, something for a specific group. Have you come across any particularly over-the-top, maybe even funny anecdotes in your research? In the FBI reports, they were also studying John Huston’s film The Treasure of the Sierra Madre, for which Huston won the best adapted screenplay and director Oscars, and his father, Walter Houston, won the best supporting actor Oscar. The FBI report says there’s one scene in the film in which Walter Houston [explains the value of gold using Marxist economic theory from Karl Marx’s Das Kapital, without directly mentioning it]. And they said you have to be very aware of these subversive messages. Don’t forget that these filmmakers came out of the Great Depression and saw people in kilometer-long queues for food, a cup of coffee, or a piece of bread. They saw abject poverty, broken families, suicide, and massive joblessness. And they were responding to that. That socialist attitude was in direct response to the way the capitalist economy failed in America, as well as elsewhere, in the early ’30s. You had a sort of activism not only in Hollywood but everywhere in that period when people were directly engaged with politics, joining the picket lines. Robert Rossen, the winner of the best film Oscar in 1949 for All the King’s Men , was on the frontline of any picket line during the strikes of the early ’40s. ‘None But the Lonely Heart’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Warner Bros. Did Hollywood studios have actual concerns with the creatives on the blacklist? Studios didn’t really believe that these writers were a threat. They gave in only when there was a huge amount of pressure from the outside. Their desire is to continue with these people because they are bringing money into the business and writing great scripts, for example, Trumbo and Lester Cole are very successful. They need them. They want them. So when the blacklist comes into effect, everything goes sort of underground. They continue writing, but under assumed names, and they keep winning Oscars. Trumbo is a great example of that. He won the Oscar twice after he got blacklisted [, namely for 1953’s Roman Holiday , initially credited to a front, and 1956’s The Brave One , credited to a pseudonym, Robert Rich], and one of those films is one with plenty of political messages. Do you maybe have an example of a film in the retrospective from creatives who named names, as you mentioned earlier? The most notorious of them is the 1954 film On the Waterfront . Three of the major talents involved in the making of that film are people who named names. There is Elia Kazan, the director who became a collaborator. There is Budd Schulberg, the screenwriter, who was a collaborator. And there is Lee J. Cobb, one of the actors in the film. This is a key film that, like many, used McCarthyism as the background for exploring fear, paranoia, and segregation in American society. The most famous example is High Noon , which is also in the program. Is there anything else you’d like to mention or highlight? We have a Western written by a woman, Karen DeWolf, in the retrospective. The film is called Silver Lode , which is similar to High Noon . It’s about a man who is about to get married, and then he’s accused of something, and he has to clear his name. He’s alone, and the whole town turns against him. These have all been seen until now as allegories of McCarthyism. But one of the reasons I’m doing these programs is that there are all these ideas. Now watch a film and see whether you see it as an allegory of McCarthyism or something else. It could be something else. The positive thing about the retrospective is that you have the chance to test certain ideas, to examine them again and see how accurate they are. THR

articles.title: Sony Pictures Sees Revenue Drop 13 Percent In Latest Quarter; Big Gains In Music
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All July 30, 2026 10:34pm From left: Stella Fitzgerald, Nate Bargatze, Charlotte Tucker and Birdie Borria in 'The Breadwinner.' Frank Masi/Sony Pictures Sony Pictures Entertainment’s operating income for its fiscal first quarter (the three months ending June 30, 2026) was up 21 percent to $154 million from the comparable period a year before, with Q1 sales down 13 percent to $1.98 billion year-on-year. SPE comprises the motion pictures division, television productions and media networks. The motion pictures unit (which includes movie sales from theatrical, home entertainment and television/streaming) saw Q1 revenue fall 13 percent to $645 million from $742 million from a year ago, the drop attributable to lower revenues from theatrical in the period. SPE released only one theatrical movie in North America in the period, the Nate Bargatze comedy The Breadwinner . In the same period the year before SPE released four films — Until Dawn, 28 Years Later, Karate Kid: Legends and Materialists . Related Stories Movies The Hollywood Left and the Blacklist: A Chat With the Curator of Locarno's Timely Retrospective for the Age of Trump & Co. Movies 'Pachinko' Star Kim Minha to Host Busan Film Festival's Opening Ceremony SPE’s overall increase in profitability for the quarter is also partly down to the decreased marketing costs due to the reduced number of theatrical releases. The motion pictures unit’s next quarter should see a massive spike in revenue and profit with the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day on July 31 expected to open to record box office globally. SPE’s TV unit saw Q1 revenue reach $571 million, down 32 percent from $841 million in the same period a year earlier. The large drop in the TV unit’s revenue is down to the decreased delieveries of series in the period. SPE’s major streaming television productions from the period included the latest seasons of Amazon Prime Video’s The Boys , Starz’s Outlander and Apple TV’s For All Mankind and Star City. Broadcast staples Jeopardy! and Wheel of Fortune , and their various spinoffs, as well as ABC’s Shark Tank added to the TV unit’s revenues. Third quarter revenue from media networks (that includes TV channels and digital channels including the fast growing Crunchyroll anime streamer) was up 10 percent to $744 million from $674 million. The company revealed that it ended the period with 38 television channels and that Crunchyroll had over 21 million paid subscribers as of March 2026. Elsewhere, Sony’s music division saw Q1 revenue jump 22 percent (557.9 billion yen from 459 billion yen for the same period a year ago). The music division saw a boost from the renewed interest in Michael Jackson’s music, coinciding with the theatrical release of the Lionsgate biopic Michael . Both Jackson’s Thriller and Bad were among the best performing albums for Sony in the period. Sony’s best-selling music artists for Q1 2026 were Michael Jackson ( Thriller and Bad ), Ella Langley ( Dandelion and Still Hungover ), Bad Bunny ( DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS and Un Verano Sin Ti ), Raye ( THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE ), SZA ( SOS ) Luke Combs ( The Way I Am ) and Peso Pluma and Tito Double ( DINASTÍA ). First quarter revenue in the Game & Network Services unit (which includes PlayStation hardware and software sales and services income) was flat at 937.1 billion yen. PlayStation 5 hardware sales hit 1.6 million units in the period, down from the 2.5 million units shifted a year ago (down 36 percent). But looking ahead, Sony is in prime position to benefit from the likely hysteria around the release of Take-Two Interactive’s long-awaited video game Grand Theft Auto VI later this year. PlayStation Network monthly active users hit 125 million in Q1, up from 123 million MAUs from the same period the year before. Sony also revealed that cumulative sales of PlayStation 5 hardware had hit 93.7 million as of March 31, 2026. THR

articles.title: British YouTuber and Rapper Yung Filly Found Not Guilty of Raping Woman in Australia
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 31, 2026 12:11am Yung Filly performs at Parklife Festival in 2022. Photo by Shirlaine Forrest/WireImage British YouTube star and rapper Yung Filly has been found not guilty of rape in an Australian court. The verdict was reached by a Perth jury after an 11-day trial. The 30-year-old, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, was found not guilty on three counts of sexual penetration without consent, but he was found guilty on two counts of assault occasioning bodily harm. The jury could not come to a decision on three other counts of rape, according to the BBC . Barrientos will remain on bail until August, when the court will decide his sentencing date. Prosecutors will also decide on the next steps for the three hung jury verdicts, including whether to press ahead on the rape charges. Related Stories Business Europe to Boycott World Cup in FIFA Protest Movies Andy Garcia's Starry L.A. Noir 'Diamond' Lands at Sony Pictures Classics The internet personality and rapper had been accused of sexually assaulting a woman, then 20 years old, after performing at a Perth nightclub in 2024. He had pleaded not guilty to all six counts of sexual penetration without consent, three counts of assault occasioning bodily harm, and one count of strangulation. Barrientos told the court that he “fancied” the woman when they met at his concert. He was in the VIP area while she leaned over the barrier. “I recall putting my hand on her waist,” he told the court, adding that he had not put his hands down her pants or touched her breast. The “vibes were good” when they arrived at his hotel later in the evening, he added, explaining that his security guard took her phone away as a “standard practice” to protect their privacy. The woman claimed they had consensual sex before the encounter turned violent and she told him to stop. The West Australian reported that Barrientos allegedly bit her neck, cheek and breast, causing bruising and swelling. Barrientos is known for his work with the Beta Squad, a group of young YouTubers who make comedic videos. Individually, each of them has gained their own following. Barrientos has accrued over 1.7 million subscribers on the site and 2.4 million on Instagram. He has also presented multiple BBC Three programs. THR

articles.title: ITV Bullish in First Results Since Confirming Sky Deal, Orders Share Buyback of $135M
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 31, 2026 1:16am 'Love Island' U.K. Season 13. ITV2 ITV has reported revenue growth of 2 percent in the first half of the year and revealed a £100 million ($135m) sharehold buyback in what CEO Carolyn McCall has described as a show of “commitment to attractive shareholder returns” in the wake of Sky ‘s £1.6 billion ($2.13b) acquisition of the broadcaster’s network and streaming businesses. In the first results since the industry-rattling mega-deal was announced , ITV said the buyback and interim dividend of 1.7p totaling around £60 million ($80m) represents an “early return of part of the previously announced £950 million net cash return expected on completion of the sale.” McCall said on a call with reporters early Friday: “The announcement of the sale […] was a defining moment to ITV.” Related Stories News British YouTuber and Rapper Yung Filly Found Not Guilty of Raping Woman in Australia Business Sony Pictures Sees Revenue Drop 13 Percent In Latest Quarter; Big Gains In Music “And crucially,” she added, “it will also unlock the value of ITV Studios .” (The company’s production arm is not part of the deal, though the report shows Sky will commit to buying £2.1 billion in ITV Studios content between 2028 and 2032.) After news of the deal, the focus for ITV will likely be on its content and big-hitters at ITV Studios ( Love Island , Rivals at Disney+), making it a potential takeover target. McCall mentioned the Sky-ITV transaction is subject to regulatory approval, with the U.K.’s Competition and Markets Authority having launched its review. Given this is a media merger, ITV is expecting Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to issue a Public Interest Intervention notice “in due course,” but they still estimate the merger will complete around a year from now. They have not interacted with Nandy since announcing the deal, McCall also said. A combined Comcast -owned Sky and ITV would create a formidable British media group. Under the proposed structure, Sky would acquire ITV’s networks and streaming businesses (Media & Entertainment) — including the ITV channel portfolio and ITVX — while ITV Studios, the production outfit behind franchises such as Love Island , Britain’s Got Talent and Netflix hit Fool Me Once, is to be spun off as a standalone listed company, reconfirmed by McCall on Friday. The merged operation will sit alongside Comcast’s NBCUniversal assets, bringing together ITV’s mass-reach advertising business, public-service broadcasting obligations and sports rights with Sky’s subscription TV, streaming, broadband and mobile operations. Media & Entertainment (M&E) delivered a run-of-the-mill first-half performance, with total revenue up 2 percent. Total advertising revenue increased by 3 percent, with Q2 up 8 percent year-on-year. This was driven by the men’s World Cup, which attracted strong advertising and sponsorship demand from both U.K. and global brands across advertising categories, and “supercharged engagement on [streaming platform] ITVX,” according to the report, which delivered record H1 viewing, up 27 percent, with digital advertising revenue up 13 percent year-on-year. Notably, ITV Studios’ revenue in the U.K. was up 17 percent this half-year, but down in the U.S. by 17 percent and internationally by 24 percent, suggesting the company could be hitting a wall when it comes to that much-needed U.S. expansion. Looking ahead, the company has “good visibility” over the full-year outlook and revenue, margin and profit will be weighted to H2 and particularly Q4, when a “really strong delivery schedule” comes into play. This includes The Gentlemen , The Woods and SuburraMaxima for Netflix, Line of Duty season seven and Vigil season three for the BBC. THR

articles.title: HBO Max Picks Up ‘Friday the 13th’ Prequel Series ‘Crystal Lake’ Across Europe
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 31, 2026 1:39am Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees in 'Crystal Lake' Peacock Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired A24 ’s Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake for HBO Max across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, excluding the U.K. and Ireland. The series is set to debut on HBO Max across the region later this year. Peacock has Crystal Lake for the U.S. and will be premiering the show stateside in October. Peacock originally ordered the series back 2022, with Bryan Fuller initially attached as writer and showrunner. But creative differences led Fuller to leave the project in May 2024, saying that A24 “decided to go a different way with the material.” Related Stories Business ITV Bullish in First Results Since Confirming Sky Deal, Orders Share Buyback of $135M News British YouTuber and Rapper Yung Filly Found Not Guilty of Raping Woman in Australia Brad Caleb Kane (Max’s It: Welcome to Derry ) is now credited as creator, writer and showrunner on the series. Crystal Lake stars Emmy Award nominee Linda Cardellini ( Dead to Me , Mad Man ) as Pamela Voorhees, the mother of the notorious Friday the 13th killer Jason. The series picks up a year after Jason’s drowning death in the town lake. But the arrival of two strangers investigating her past sets off a series of events that prompts the residents of Crystal Lake to question who Pam Voorhees really is. William Catlett co-stars as local police chief Levon Brooks. Devin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins and Gwendolyn Sundstrom co-star. Callum Vinson plays a young Jason Voorhees. Kane is executive producing Crystal Lake together with A24 and an executive producing team that includes Marc Toberoff, Victor Miller, Robert M. Barsamian, Robert P. Barsamian, Stuart Manashil, Tyson Bidner, Michael Lennox and Roy Lee. THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’?
articles.full_text: Jul 30, 2026 8:00pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’? By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’? 8 hours ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: Sadie Sink Is [SPOILER]. How Her Role Sets Up Marvel’s Next Reboot 11 hours ago ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’s’ Breakout, Ryan Reynolds’ Jeanpool Stunt and More Comic-Con Highlights 3 days ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ,” now playing in theaters. Where in the world is Spider-Man going next? After saving New York City in “Brand New Day,” Tom Holland ‘s friendly neighborhood Spider-Man looks like he’s heading off-world once again. The post-credits scene in the latest Sony and Marvel movie revealed that the hero will return to the MCU and seems to be leaving Earth in his next appearance. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement First, like many fans have theorized for months, Sadie Sink is playing X-Men member Jean Grey in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” She’s the primary antagonist in the movie, though it’s later revealed that the Department of Damage Control kidnapped and killed her older sister Sara. Once he realizes the cause of Jean’s Damage Control crusade, Spider-Man convinces her to release the psychic bubble she creates that freezes nearly every New Yorker at the end of the movie. He also saves her from getting shot by Jon Bernthal’s Punisher and gets hit by the sniper rifle bullet himself. At the end of the movie, Spidey recuperates, and Jean heads out of town (and possibly to Xavier’s School for Gifted Youngsters upstate). Popular on Variety In the final moments of the movie, Holland’s Peter Parker runs into his former best friend Ned (Jacob Batalon) at a cafe. Due to Doctor Strange’s spell at the end of “No Way Home,” the world has forgotten who Peter is, so Ned only recognizes the stranger after he crashed his house party earlier in the movie. With nothing to lose, Peter reintroduces himself to Ned and they perform their secret handshake without missing a beat. All of a sudden, Ned seems to regain his memories of Peter just as the film ends. Does that mean Zendaya’s MJ could also remember Peter? Could true love’s kiss actually reawaken her love for him? Earlier in the movie, it’s also revealed that Ned has created a Spidey-tracking app that he uses to follow the hero’s location. During the post-credits scene, the app reappears as it attempts to pinpoint where the wall-crawler is. However, the Spidey Tracker starts to zoom out so far that it’s clear Spider-Man isn’t in New York City or even on Earth. The app locates the hero out in space, and then the movie announces that “Spider-Man will return” — but it’s unclear when or how. Currently, Holland isn’t on the call sheet for the sprawling cast of “ Avengers: Doomsday .” The team-up film brings together many of the A-listers on the Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men and Thunderbolts teams, but no Holland. However, that doesn’t count out a surprise appearance or cameo from the web-slinger, especially considering the entire MCU is coming together to battle Robert Downey Jr.’s evil mastermind Doctor Doom. If Holland doesn’t reappear in “Doomsday,” then the post-credits scene could point to a role in “Avengers: Secret Wars,” the follow-up scheduled for next year. If the movie follows the comic run of the same name, it could bring together every hero from across the MCU multiverse into one dimension called Battleworld. In the comics, Battleworld stitched together all the different worlds and plopped every hero and their variant into one new universe. If the MCU followed suit, that could be the reason the Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men are eventually able to share one universe. Could that also bring together past Spider-Man stars Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield, who crossed over into “No Way Home”? Fans will have to wait and see in “Secret Wars,” but that could be how Holland lands his next MCU appearance. LISTEN: Credit Risks: Top S&P Global Analyst Breaks Down the Paramount-Warner Bros. articles.title: Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21%
articles.full_text: Jul 30, 2026 8:58pm PT Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% Company raises guidance for FY 2026 operating income by 8%, citing higher expected profitability in PlayStation games segment By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% 7 hours ago Disney Expected to Sell 50% Stake in A+E to Hearst for More Than $1 Billion 13 hours ago Apple Sales Rise 16% to Record $109 Billion for June Quarter, Services Revenue Falls Short of Forecasts 14 hours ago See All Kristoffer Tripplaar/ Sipa USA Sony Pictures Entertainment posted a sales decline for the June 2026 quarter, offset by growth at Crunchyroll, while Sony’s music segment saw revenue increase 21%. The PlayStation games unit had flat sales for the period and a 37% increase in operating income driven by U.S. tariff refunds. Revenue for Sony Pictures for the quarter ended June 30 was $1.978 billion, down 13% year over, while operating income rose 21% to $156 million. The company said the sales decline was due to a decrease in series deliveries in television productions — revenue was down 32%, to $571 million. SPE also had lower revenue from theatrical releases: $30 million in the most recent quarter from its sole release in the period (TriStar’s comedy “The Breadwinner”) vs. $132 million from four releases in the year-earlier period. Total revenue in the Motion Pictures group was $645 million for the June quarter (-13%). Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement The higher revenue from anime streaming service Crunchyroll was mainly due to paid subscriber growth. As of the end of March, the service had more than 21 million paid subscribers, and Sony said it continued to gain subs in the June quarter. Popular on Variety Overall for the quarter, Sony’s Q1 of fiscal year 2026, the company posted revenue of 2.837 trillion yen ($17.8 billion), up 8%, and net income of 342.2 billion yen ($2.15 billion), up 32%. For full-year fiscal 2026, Sony upped its consolidated operating income forecast by 8%, to 1.72 trillion yen ($10.8 billion), citing ​an expected increase in profitability in the PlayStation business. A major gaming title release coming this November is Take-Two Interactive’s “Grand Theft Auto VI,” which should provide a lift to the PlayStation division. Sony raised guidance for FY26 total revenue by 2%, to 12.5 trillion yen ($78.5 billion) compared with 12.48 trillion yen in FY25. In the PlayStation division, sales for the June quarter were flat at 937.1 billion yen ($5.88 billion) and operating income rose 37%, to 202.0 billion yen ($1.27 billion), lifted by the impact of U.S. tariff refunds after the Supreme Court invalidated President Trump’s global tariffs in February 2026. Total PlayStation monthly active users reached 125 million accounts in June, up 2% year over year. Total playtime during the quarter decreased 4% from the year-prior period, but Sony said “user engagement continued to be solid” and noting a tough comparison with Q1 of FY25, which “benefited from season updates to major titles and new hit titles.” It sold 1.5 million PS5 units in the June quarter compared with 2.5 million in the year-earlier period. Sony’s music segment pulled in revenue of 562.0 billion yen ($3.53 billion), an increase of 21%. That was led by the impact of foreign exchange rates; higher revenue from live events and merchandising in recorded music; and a bump in streaming revenue. For the June quarter, streaming revenue growth rates on a U.S. dollar basis were up 10% year-on-year for recorded music and up 8% for music publishing. Operating income for the music segment rose 14% to 105.9 billion yen ($665 million). The average exchange rate used for Sony’s June quarter figures was 159.3 yen to $1 U.S. dollar. Regarding the recent Kumamoto earthquake, Sony said it has several semiconductor facilities located in Kumamoto prefecture and neighboring prefectures. “While all these facilities were affected by the earthquake, there were no major casualties,” the company said. Sony’s production sites in Nagasaki, Oita and Kagoshima had no significant damage to buildings or equipment and production has resumed. articles.title: Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Introduces an Angry and Angular Ari: Album Review
articles.full_text: Jul 30, 2026 9:15pm PT Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Introduces an Angry and Angular Ari: Album Review By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Influence Media Partners to Acquire Anthem Entertainment’s Publishing and Film & TV Assets in $600 Million Deal 14 hours ago Ryan Bingham Signs With WME (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago Grammy Chief ‘Saddened to Hear’ That BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Awards 1 day ago See All On the surface, Ariana Grande ’s “Petal” is a sister album to its predecessor, 2024’s “Eternal Sunshine” — it was made with the same two collaborators, Ilya Salmanzadeh and Max Martin, and it also was entirely written, performed and produced by the three of them. Usually, that formula means a chapter two: more of the same but different. Not this time. This sister is darker, moodier and a lot more blunt than “Sunshine,” and her emotions are more volatile, less heartbroken, and much less internalized. It’s a different Ariana, musically and especially lyrically. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement Grande braced her fans for a change in a widely circulated interview earlier this week. “I think [fans] will feel familiarity and comfort in it,” she said of the album. “Yet at the same time it’s very experimental and different for me, and also I wrote from a place that I don’t usually, which is unfiltered rage,” she laughed. “I usually am too shy to tap into that, and I think this time I didn’t filter as much as I usually do.” Popular on Variety “This is rage?,” some may think at first listen, because it’s still a pop album, even though it moves into weirder territory musically than she has in the past. And let’s be real: With her pretty, pristine soprano, it’s hard to imagine what an Angry Ari (“AngRI”?) would sound like. But lurking below the shiny surface of many of the songs are lyrics like: “Just know that I will find my way from you like flowers from a tomb”; “All of my favorite stories end in some kind of catastrophe”; “I’m not a victim, bitch, I’m practically drowning in my blessings”; “Good luck on your way to hell.” Likewise, the NSFW lyrics of her recent albums moves into a whole new realm: “Pussy so sweet a tear fell from his eye”; “This sex is bout to make a grown man cry”; “The grass is way greener since I been beneath ya”; and if those were too subtle, “No one fucks you like I do.” And for good measure, there’s a mission statement: “Keep my heels tall, my ego small, but I’m still Grande.” The heartbroken but resilient Grande from the last album is nowhere in sight — with one exception, these songs are about vengeance or sex, and about whom is bound to be the subject of endless online chatter. The album’s lead single, “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” is a solid introduction to the sound of the album’s more experimental tracks: It’s beautiful but odd, with a crinkling synthesizer hook over a spare beat, creating an haunting setting for her lush, multitracked vocals; her growth as a melodicist is on full display in the mellifluous, multisyllabic middle section. As she promised, there are familiar-sounding songs and moments (“Kiss Me,” “Freak”), but there’s also music that would be more expected from FKA Twigs or even the Weeknd — Ilya executive-produced the album with Grande (Martin contributes to just three songs), so his more-adventurous inclinations have come to the fore. “Like I Do,” probably the album’s darkest song musically, is based around the lovely eight-note wordless figure she sings at the beginning, but soon gives way to an ominous, hulking rhythm musical track; several songs are built around Ilya’s trademark malfunctioning-computer synth lines. The hard-hitting title track pairs a busy, complex melody with a thudding Portishead rhythm; it’s like two different songs playing in synch. But even relatively straightforward songs don’t sound like anything she’s done before. “Never Get Over Me” has an icy funk groove with a silky soulful vocal — and, far off in the distance, that psycho siren-like sound from “Kill Bill” (thematic link!) whenever Beatrix Kiddo is about to act out her unfiltered rage. “Bad Thing (Bunny Hop)” is a fast, new wave-esque track with a flash of “Blinding Lights”; “Big Feelings” has a sultriness that we have rarely heard from her in the past. The one exception is the closing track and prettiest song, the ballad “Nowhere, Nobody,” driven by a heavily echoed guitar and a percolating rhythm track, a showcase for Grande’s lush, layered vocals, which bring back the wistfulness of “Eternal Sunshine.” It, and the album, end on an English-teacher-enraging note by quite deliberately finishing with a preposition: “There’s nowhere else and there is nobody else/ that I’d rather be … with.” “Petal” is not an easy or obvious career move — it’s probably the biggest musical departure of her career, but it’s also her most musically and lyrically accomplished album. She continues to grow as a virtuoso singer and vocal arranger, soaring to the top of her range with ease, but also showing nuance in her emotion as well as the kind of innovation she showed on the elaborate singing-along-with-herself loops featured on the “Sunshine” tour. Eight albums into her discography, Ariana Grande continues to surprise. articles.title: ITV Sees ‘Solid’ Results in First Half of 2026, Reports $26 Million Loss Due to Fast Food Advertising Regulations
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 12:06am PT ITV Sees ‘Solid’ Results in First Half of 2026, Reports $26 Million Loss Due to Fast Food Advertising Regulations By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest ITV Sees ‘Solid’ Results in First Half of 2026, Reports $26 Million Loss Due to Fast Food Advertising Regulations 4 hours ago Jared Leto Documentary Director on Exposing Sexual Misconduct Allegations and the ‘Mystery’ of Why He Hasn’t Been Held Accountable 17 hours ago ‘The Master and Margarita’ Adaptation Gets Long-Awaited U.S. Theatrical Release After Legal Battle (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All ITV ITV has unveiled “solid” if underwhelming results for the first half of 2026, with a 2% uplift across its major profit centers. Total group revenue stayed steady at £1.9 billion ($2.5 billion). These are the first results published since it was revealed ITV are selling their media and entertainment arm to Comcast-owned Sky. Production outfit ITV Studios will be spun off as an independent listed company. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement ITV’s group adjusted EBITA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, and Amortization) also held steady at £145 million, marginally up (by 2%) from £142 million in 2025. Popular on Variety That figure is still a significant drop from the £212 million reported in the first six months of 2024. At the time, ITV put this down to the Euros soccer tournament delivering a massive boost, but it doesn’t appear the World Cup has had a similar impact. The disparity could be because of the variation in the England soccer team’s performance across the two tournaments: while they made it through to the finals of the Euros, sustaining and building interest throughout the tournament, the team were knocked out of the World Cup in the quarter finals, which led to a drop in viewing figures in the U.K. Still, ITV said its total advertising revenue grew by 8% year-on-year, which they put down to the World Cup, saying it had attracted “strong advertising and sponsorship demand.” The news at ITV Studios was less sunny, particularly given the company is set to be spun-off, making it an acquisition target. Total revenue again held steady with a 2% uplift but EBITA dropped by 9% to £97 million from last year’s £107 million (itself a 20% drop on the previous year). That’s despite a number of high-profile titles including “Love Island, “Rivals” for Disney+ and “The Gentlemen” for Netflix. ITV said the figure was due to the “phasing of deliveries,” a number of which were backloaded to the second half of the year. But the media conglomerate admitted that the first half of 2025 saw a number of “large deliveries to streaming platforms” – including “One Piece” and “The Better Sister” – which were “not repeated to the same scale” in the first half of 2026. One of ITV’s success stories is its streaming platform ITVX – believed to be the main driver of the Sky acquisition – which continued to deliver record viewing, growing by 27% in the first half the year. Advertising revenue also rose by 13% year-on-year although it took a £20 million ($26 million) hit from the introduction of the government’s regulations on junk food commercials, which were introduced in Oct. 2025. ITV said it is working “closely with advertisers to mitigate the impact.” ITV also warned that advertising is like to drop by 5% in the next quarter, “reflecting the current macroeconomic headwinds” meaning that by the nine-months mark results will be flat. “ITV delivered a solid H1 performance and we remain on track to deliver our full-year guidance, including good revenue growth in ITV Studios and strong, profitable digital revenue growth within Media & Entertainment,” said CEO Carolyn McCall in a statement. “Macro-economic headwinds remain, but we are focused on the performance of both businesses, with continued momentum, disciplined execution of our strategic priorities and a strong second half delivery schedule in ITV Studios.” Meanwhile shareholders were granted a windfall with McCall announcing an interim dividend of 1.7p as well as a £100 million share buyback. McCall also confirmed the regulatory process is underway on the Sky/ITV acquisition and the culture minister is expected to watch it closely. Seasoned publicity veteran Chris Duggan has been appointed to the newly-created role and will work across Element’s stable of producers to promote their projects and lead corporate communications, reporting directly to founders and co-CEOs Ed Guiney and Andrew Lowe. articles.title: Oscar-Qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival Expands to 10 Arenas, Adds AI and Dance Competitions (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 1:56am PT Oscar-Qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival Expands to 10 Arenas, Adds AI and Dance Competitions (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Oscar-Qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival Expands to 10 Arenas, Adds AI and Dance Competitions (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ Celebrates 10 Years as Longest-Running Two-Part Play in Modern West End History – Global Bulletin 23 hours ago ‘Ramayana’ Trailer: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash Face Off in First Part of Nitesh Tiwari’s Epic 1 day ago See All BISFF India’s Oscar-qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival (BISFF) has expanded its competition to 10 arenas of cinema for its 16th edition, adding new categories for AI-made films and screendance. BISFF received a record 3,340 submissions this year from more than 100 countries, according to organizers. Of those, 1,726 came from international entries, 756 from India, 306 from Karnataka, 284 in animation and 118 each in the queer, AI film and screendance categories. The festival expects more than 5,000 delegates and 1,000-plus filmmakers and artists. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement The new sections include AI (Machine Made Movies), open to films created entirely or partially using AI tools, and Dancing Lens, a competition for screendance works that treat choreography and cinematography as inseparable. Three sections – International, Indian and Animation – remain Oscar-qualifying. Popular on Variety Anand Varadaraj, founder and artistic director of BISFF, said: “Sixteen years ago, BISFF was a small room of filmmakers and curators who thought young talent deserved a real platform to show early work and get serious feedback. We started with 30 films. Now we get 3,000 plus, and alumni go on to win Oscars. That’s the power of taking short films seriously. This edition gathers everyone who knows that the most vital cinema today lives in under thirty minutes.” This year’s edition centers on the theme “ACT,” structured around three imperatives – Do, Perform and Behave. Every competition category this year features more than 30 titles from India and abroad – the largest lineup in the festival’s history, organizers said. Varadaraj said: “The quality of the films this year has been exceptional. As a curator, this has been the most demanding selection process I’ve experienced. We revisited the shortlist several times to ensure every film was evaluated fairly and that the final programme reflects the best work submitted. I hope audiences will enjoy discovering these films as much as we enjoyed bringing them together.” The international competition will bring some 28 films to India for the first time, with highlights including “La Ligne de Vie (The Lifeline)” (Hugo Becker, France), “Close Your Eyes Hind” (Amir Zaza, Netherlands), “I Gaze at the Sky” (Alexandra Strunin, Poland), “The Written Hour” (Coke Arijo, Spain) and “Round and Round” (Hayato Otogi, Japan). The section will be judged by Maike Hohne, an artistic director based in Hamburg, Germany; Indian filmmaker Umesh Vinayak Kulkarni; and international film critic Christopher Dalton. More than 20 of the selected Indian titles will premiere publicly at BISFF for the first time, with highlights including “Hudke Ki Pyaang Pyaang, Dhol Ki Ghamaika” (Arun N. Fulara), “Small Clouds” (Shubham Sumit), “Aasmani” (Sayani Gupta), “Bandini” (Deepti Chawla), “Mehta & Co.” (Rohit Sen) and “Shadows Of The Moonless Nights” (Mehar Malhotra), which was selected for La Cinef at Cannes earlier this year. The Indian jury includes Sridhar Rangayan, Sulakhyana Baruah and Devanshu Singh. The new AI Films Competition will showcase work exploring AI’s growing role in shaping how stories are conceived and made, raising questions around authorship and the future of filmmaking, organizers said. Beyond screenings, BISFF 2026 will host three industry pillars: the Discovery Film Market with Producer Bazaar, connecting more than 100 filmmakers with more than 50 buyers, distributors, broadcasters, OTT platforms and financiers; the Echoes Film School Conference, presented in partnership with RV University; and a series of panels, workshops and masterclasses. That slate has previously featured Shoojit Sircar, Sriram Raghavan, Naseeruddin Shah and Mahesh Narayanan. Industry conversations this year include sessions titled “New Pathways for Global Distribution” and “Vertical Cinema: The Next Screen?,” focused on emerging distribution models and mobile-first viewing habits. BISFF draws more than 5,000 delegates annually and generates more than 300,000 website hits per year, according to the festival. The festival runs Aug. 14-16, with an online component from August 6-16. The in-person festival will be held across venues including Suchitra Film Society, RV University, LitSchool, Knowledgium Academy, Bangalore International Centre, Indian Heritage Academy, Alliance Française and Goethe Institut – Max Muellar Bhavan. articles.title: World Cup Boycott Backed by All 55 UEFA Countries as Asian, North and Central American, Caribbean Members Oppose FIFA Stake Sale
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 2:10am PT World Cup Boycott Backed by All 55 UEFA Countries as Asian, North and Central American, Caribbean Members Oppose FIFA Stake Sale By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest World Cup Boycott Backed by All 55 UEFA Countries as Asian, North and Central American, Caribbean Members Oppose FIFA Stake Sale 2 hours ago ‘Balcanica,’ Starring Matilda De Angelis, Picked Up by M-Appeal Ahead of Venice World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Getty The Asian Football Confederation has joined the North, Central America and Caribbean football association and UEFA in opposition to FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s proposal to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors. On Thursday, all 55 UEFA member associations pledged to boycott FIFA soccer competitions if president Gianni Infantino’s proposal is approved. “The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world’s leading football nations,” the AFC said in a statement on Friday, according to BBC Sport . “Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.” Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement On Friday morning, Infantino’s senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro also resigned over the proposal, calling it “a bad deal for football.” Popular on Variety Both the AFC and Concacaf stopped short of a boycott but made clear their disapproval of Infantino’s plan. The UEFA decision to boycott came out of an emergency meeting Thursday, days after FIFA announced the plans Tuesday. The first test of the stance arrives in October, when the Women’s World Cup play-offs are scheduled. UEFA said a statement after the meeting: “UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.” The new company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, has been valued at about $20 billion. FIFA would seek to sell a roughly 20% stake in the entity. Among the potential investors is Thrive Eternal, led by Joshua Kushner, brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, according to the Financial Times. Among the opponents of the plan are the sport’s governing bodies in North America and Europe. Concacaf, which runs soccer in North America, Central America and the Caribbean, said it was “deeply concerned by the lack of due process” when the plan was conceived. The federation said it was disappointed that the plan has been revealed “before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.” UEFA, which runs the sport in Europe, said FIFA’s plan “crosses a line that [soccer’s] governing institutions should never cross.” It added, “The soul and governance of [soccer] are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of [soccer]. It is not FIFA’s to sell.” UEFA is fast-tracking efforts to hold an emergency meeting of its member associations this week, sources told ESPN, to discuss plans, including a potential World Cup boycott. The FIFA plan is subject to ratification by its 211 national member associations. Concacaf represents 41 members, while UEFA has 55. Under the plan, funds raised from the sale of a stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise would be used in part to increase annual payments to members from $2 million a year to $5 million. Each would also receive a one-off payment of $20 million. FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement, “Every FIFA member association should have an opportunity to seek a fair share of the available funding to shape its own future, deciding for itself rather than relying on others. This is about the democratization of [soccer] worldwide.” Among other opponents of the plan are U.K. prime minister Andy Burnham, who said, “The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Much of the opposition to FIFA’s plan is focusing on the role of Infantino, and his relationship with President Trump. Football Supporters Europe, which represents fans, said, “The World Cup is not for sale. Enough of this charade. [FIFA] member associations — and everyone who cares about the future of the game — must stand up to the man who wants to sell world [soccer].” UTA Partner Jeremy Barber on Joining UNICEF Board and Enlisting Hollywood to Tell Organization’s Stories: ‘I Believe We’re Here to Take Care of Each Other’ (EXCLUSIVE) Mel Robbins, Ludacris, Paris Hilton, Priyanka Chopra Jonas and More Than 70 Creators Set for UTA’s Cannes Lions Slate Ken Ziffren on the Fight for a New Spin on Fin-Syn, Six Decades of Hollywood Dealmaking and Awaiting a ‘Cacophony of Decisions’ in AI Cases ‘Strictly Business’ Cannes Lions Edition: Fox’s Rob Wade and Billy Parks Bet on Bringing Scale to the Business of Creators LISTEN: Mike Hopkins on Prime Video’s Evolution, the Bundling Boom, How MGM Changed Amazon, the Future of Bond and No Regrets on ‘Melania’ LISTEN: Jon Miller on Media Merger Mayhem: ‘Globalization Is Winning’ Loading comments...
