articles.title: ‘Los Vampires’ Review: Dueling Draculas Spar in an Alluring if Unevenly Executed Flashback to Early-Talkie Hollywood
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 2:25am PT ‘Los Vampires’ Review: Dueling Draculas Spar in an Alluring if Unevenly Executed Flashback to Early-Talkie Hollywood Writer-director Craig Mitchell’s conceit imagines sinister doings on the shared set of Universal’s famous 1931 “Dracula,” which was shot with both English and Spanish-language casts. By Dennis Harvey Plus Icon Dennis Harvey Film Critic Latest ‘Black Zombie’ Review: An Engaging Doc on How the Flesh-Eating Hordes of Screen Fame Obscured Painful Real-Life History 1 hour ago ‘Ferine’ Review: Motherhood Begets Beastliness in Andrea Corsini’s Upscale Horror 21 hours ago ‘Big Break’ Review: Comedy Quartet Meets Serial-Killer Peril in an Amusing, Tongue-in-Cheek Thriller 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Handshake Partners The talkies’ arrival was a major hardship in many respects for the movie industry, as theater owners had to install expensive new equipment, and studios could no longer easily export fresh product to lucrative foreign markets. One solution weighed to the latter dilemma was making alternative versions of features in different languages. Universal took that idea farther than most in late 1930 by shooting “Dracula” twice on the same sets, with entirely different casts and directors. One was, of course, the legendary Tod Browning film with Bela Lugosi. The other, directed by George Melford (who’d guided Rudolph Valentino in his most famous role as “The Sheik”), had Spanish emigre Carlos Villarias as the caped bloodsucker. It was forgotten for decades until a 1990s restoration and revival led some latter-day viewers to pronounce it the better of the two. Related Stories Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs That curious footnote to cinematic history has now inspired “ Los Vampires ,” the first directorial feature in decades from scenarist Craig Mitchell . Like the 2000 Willem Dafoe vehicle “Shadow of the Vampire,” this is a fiction spun from the reality of a fabled production shoot. Henry Ian Cusick and Thomas Kretschmann play fictionalized stand-ins for Villarias and Lugosi, as immigrant actors touchy about “sharing” a starring role that could be a huge break for both. Popular on Variety In the somewhat convoluted progress of Mitchell’s script, their ego war is eventually eclipsed by fears there’s a genuine murderer on the loose — perhaps even an actual vampire. Not always very precisely balanced between horror, homage and mystery, this intriguing if unevenly realized construct will nonetheless lure genre fans and nostalgists alike with its imagined back chapter of golden-age Hollywood. It starts with nervous Luis de Ossario (Cusik) arriving on the Universal soundstage, where he’s dismayed by a front-office representative’s command that he watch the dailies of English-language scenes shot during the day, then precisely mimic them in Spanish each night. Pride insists he ignore that directive — after all, he too has been a star, called the “Spanish Sheik” by fan mags. But it’s additionally irritating when he’s approached by Romanian thespian Kurt Orlov (Kretschmann), who’s essayed the Count to great success onstage, and likewise advised to imitate his every gesture and intonation. Refusing to do so, Luis stirs a rivalry and potentially endangers his own employment. Still, the dual production goes on as planned. Anxiety heightened by the exhausting nocturnal schedule, Ossario is further rattled by glimpsing sexually explicit footage presumably shot as blackmail fodder. It involves Vianca Sugura (Daniela Couso), the beauteous albeit wholly inexperienced young woman hired as ingenue. Other unsettling revelations include word that the actress originally hired for that part was killed — a fate that later befalls others, including convent-raised Vianca’s protectress Sister Aubrey (Carol Abney). There are additional, underdeveloped subplots. The intended enigmatic blurring between illusion, reality, the supernatural and sordid here too often just feels unfocused, with occasional detours into humor contributing to a wobbly tone. The best sequences seize upon the atmospheric potential of recreated studio-Gothic sets, though there’s surprisingly scant use of B&W film-within-the-film bits. Itself shot entirely on a soundstage, “Los Vampires” occasionally betrays budgetary limits in unconvincing period flavor, despite good work from production designer Ricardo Jattan and costumer Petra Larsen. The lead actors do well enough on this slippery slope. Cusick and Kretschmann offer complementary chords of variable petulance and insecurity, as newcomer Cuoso ably negotiates her character’s shifting ambiguities. The supporting cast turns are competent if sometimes broad. If Mitchell’s resolution to his script’s dangling questions feels somewhat rote, a graceful epilogue leaps several decades forward to end matters on an interesting, unexpected note. While the Lugosi “Dracula” was a huge hit, the Spanish version’s disappointing box office helped curtail future such endeavors in Hollywood, particularly since fast-evolving dubbing technology soon provided a cheaper alternative. Far from a mere copy of its English-language equivalent, however, Melford’s movie is considerably longer, with marked differences of dialogue, narrative sequence and costuming. Those who found Browning’s take too stagey have judged its doppelgänger more fluidly cinematic. Still, only one person became a celluloid legend from Universal’s gambit — and that person wasn’t Carlos Villarias, who outlived Lugosi by two decades yet never achieved anything like the same renown. ‘Los Vampires’ Review: Dueling Draculas Spar in an Alluring if Unevenly Executed Flashback to Early-Talkie Hollywood Reviewed online, July 23, 2026. In Fantasia Festival. Running time: 104 MIN. Production: A Handshake Partners presentation of a 24 Horses, Buddha-Cowboy production. (World sales: Handshake Partners, Los Angeles.) Producer: Ty Donaldson. Executive producers: Craig Mitchell, Scott Bridges, Paul Hazen. Crew: Director, screenplay: Craig Mitchell. Camera: Simon Coull. Editor: Evan Millard. Music: Josh Mancell. With: Henry Ian Cusick, Daniela Couso, Thomas Kretschmann, Oscar Nunez, Jefferson Mays, Carol Abney, Jorge Diaz, Jake Regal, Andrew Baldwin, Roman Phillips. (Spanish, English dialogue.) articles.title: ‘Black Zombie’ Review: An Engaging Doc on How the Flesh-Eating Hordes of Screen Fame Obscured Painful Real-Life History
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 2:42am PT ‘Black Zombie’ Review: An Engaging Doc on How the Flesh-Eating Hordes of Screen Fame Obscured Painful Real-Life History Maya Annik Bedward’s documentary looks at nearly a century of zombie cinema through the lens of cultural appropriation, as a gross distortion of the Haitian culture and beliefs that first inspired it. By Dennis Harvey Plus Icon Dennis Harvey Film Critic Latest ‘Black Zombie’ Review: An Engaging Doc on How the Flesh-Eating Hordes of Screen Fame Obscured Painful Real-Life History 2 hours ago ‘Ferine’ Review: Motherhood Begets Beastliness in Andrea Corsini’s Upscale Horror 21 hours ago ‘Big Break’ Review: Comedy Quartet Meets Serial-Killer Peril in an Amusing, Tongue-in-Cheek Thriller 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Kino Lorber In Hollywood’s original horror heyday of the 1930s and ’40s, it would have been hard to imagine another figure challenging the classic terror quartet of Dracula, Frankenstein monster, werewolf and mummy — let alone that the lowly zombie would ever become serious competition. Yet while those aforementioned creatures still get rehabilitated on a regular basis, they’re now greatly surpassed in popular visibility by a cannibal undead that didn’t even exist in the genre until more recent decades. Related Stories Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Maya Annik Bedward ’s Canadian documentary “ Black Zombie ” explores that surprise evolution. But hers isn’t a genre fan’s focus so much as a cultural anthropologist’s eye, honing in on how the screen zombie has exploited and distorted the Haitian religious beliefs that provided its initial inspiration. Kino Lorber is opening the Canadian documentary in the U.S. on Sept. 11th; Raven Banner will release it on home turf the same date. Popular on Variety Today zombie entertainment is so ubiquitous, it encompasses enormously expensive blockbusters (“World War Z”), big-screen franchises (like the “28 Days” films), an entire “Walking Dead” multimedia empire, comedies (“Shaun of the Dead” being the most famous) and myriad other expressions. Often involving animated corpses who are “fast-moving” — making their hunger for living flesh an even greater peril — these images break from the standard late-20th century convention of slow, shuffling if still bloodthirsty dullards, a template established by George A. Romero’s 1968 sleeper smash “Night of the Living Dead.” At neither speed, however, do they have much to do with the zombie’s prior, much-less-frequent pulp appearances. Those had roots in 1929’s bestselling “The Magic Island,” one of several questionable works of journalism by the writer, adventure and occult sensation-seeker William Seabrook. (His most credible tome was probably the subsequent “Asylum,” which detailed his institutional recovery from alcoholism.) He claimed to have seen laborers in the cane fields of Haiti who were seemingly in a trance, incapable of speaking. The notion of zombies went back to that Caribbean nation’s days as a European colony, when huge numbers of largely African slaves were brutally disciplined and frequently worked to death by a white-settler minority. It was rumored that some got drugged or otherwise rendered “soul lost,” so they would toil without rest or protest. Thus within Haitian culture, zombies were victims, robbed of independent will by cruel masters. Seabrook’s primary focus was on Vodou aka voodoo rituals, which had long constituted an underground religious practice amongst populations outwardly accepting of Catholicism. But his mention of “zondis,” the dead supposedly revived via magic for cane harvesting, ignited the popular imagination. It soon got fictionalized as the post-“Dracula” Bela Lugosi vehicle “White Zombie” (1932), then in other films, notably the Val Lewton-produced “I Walked With a Zombie” a decade later. Their suspense arose not from anything that happened to or at the hands of zombie-fied “natives,” but the terror that such hypnosis might be used on Caucasian protagonists — especially pretty young ingenues. Bedward elicits commentary from latter-day scholars, historians, and Vodou priests. They dissect how these representations reinforced superstitious racial stereotypes in a vintage “exotica” mode, one reprised at least as recently as Wes Craven’s 1988 “The Serpent and the Rainbow.” Those movies are seen as part of an ongoing disempowering of the Haitian peoples, who have been continually hobbled by occupiers, imposed foreign debts and political instability. The myth of witless, “savage” zombies only helped perpetuate the idea that Haitians cannot be trusted to control their own destiny. “Black Zombie” illustrates that point with an engaging mix of clips, interviews, old newsreel footage, brief animations and B&W staged sequences with Anderson Mojica as an 18th-century slave who’s first subsumed by, then overcomes his “zombie” state of passive toil. (It is suggested that depriving laborers of salt intake might have had such stupefying effects.) Horror fans may be disappointed that the later waves of zombie cinema get rather fleeting address here, though we do hear from legendary gore FX maestro Tom Savini and the late Romero’s “Night of the Living Dead” co-writer John Russo. (The latter says their ultra-low-budget breakout settled for its hungry-ghoul gist only because they couldn’t afford the trappings of a science-fiction tale.) The whole cannibalism conceit has scant connection to Vodou lore, so it’s of little relevance to the director’s main thesis here. However, some of her experts do opine that the manic, devouring hordes of modern depiction discreetly amplify new paranoias: not just the “fear of Blacks” implicit in earlier zombie thrillers, but wealthy nations’ current panic over “invading” Third World immigrants, climate-change refugees, and so forth. Now, zombies simply “represent otherness,” as one observer puts it. The authorities Bedward solicits intel from often speak reluctantly, having been burned before: They’re all too familiar with filmmakers feigning sincere interest, only to deliver yet another bloody screen cartoon of Haitian history and beliefs. While “Black Zombie” isn’t quite the genre “greatest hits” parade many viewers may be hoping for, it does provide a thought-provoking perspective — one that might add some depth to your next experience of undead cinema, however purely escapist. ‘Black Zombie’ Review: An Engaging Doc on How the Flesh-Eating Hordes of Screen Fame Obscured Painful Real-Life History Reviewed online, July 25, 2026. In Fantasia, SXSW, Hot Docs festivals. Running time: 93 MIN. Production: (Documentary — Canada) A Kino Lorber release (U.S.) of a Third Culture Media, Hungry Eyes Media presentation of a Documentary Channel Original production in association with Canada Media Fund, Telefilm Canada, Rogers Documentary Fund. Producers: Maya Annik Bedward, Kate MacCallum Fraser, Hannah Donegan. Executive producers: Jennifer Holness, Bedward, Fraser, Michael Paszt, Andrew Thomas Hunt, James Fler, Slash. Crew: Director, writer: Maya Annik Bedward. Camera: Duraid Munajim, Ricardo Diaz. Editors: Avril Jacobsen, Jay Cheel, Peter Denes, Lawrence Jackman. Music: David Arcus, Melissa Laveaux, Lister Haussman. With: Yves-Gregory Francois, Anderson Mojica, Erol Josue, Mambo Labelle Deese Botanica, Slash, Tom Savini, Tananarive Due, Zandashe Brown, Joe Ollmann, John Cussans, Kaiama L. Glover, Dominique Taffin, John Russo, Wade Davis. articles.title: Inside Netflix and Prime Video’s Fight to Reshape France’s Streaming Rules: ‘It’s an Unsustainable Equation’
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 4:31am PT Inside Netflix and Prime Video’s Fight to Reshape France’s Streaming Rules: ‘It’s an Unsustainable Equation’ By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest George and Amal Clooney Evacuate French Home as Wildfire Threatens Brignoles: ‘We Remain Fully Part of This Community’ and Will ‘Contribute to Its Rebuilding’ 22 hours ago Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50 2 days ago Canal+ Group’s Revenue Jumps 40% as MultiChoice Deal Boosts Earnings and Subscriptions 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Cédric Bertrand While Canal+ has just agreed to invest more than $1.1 billion in French and European films over the next five years, Amazon Prime Video and Netflix are fighting in court and behind closed doors to loosen France’s streaming regulations. Both services have launched separate legal challenges before France’s Conseil d’état, the country’s highest administrative court, while also negotiating with regulators and the film industry over the future of France’s investment and windowing rules. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement Since January 2022, subscription streaming services such as Netflix, Prime Video and Disney+ have been required to invest 20% of their annual French revenue in local film and television production under France’s implementation of the European Audiovisual Media Services Directive. Popular on Variety France’s film industry also negotiated separate agreements with individual streamers governing both their cinema investment commitments and their place in the country’s windowing system. Netflix’s agreement expired at the end of 2025 and has not been renewed. “For us, it’s an unsustainable equation: more obligations, a less favorable release window, and the latest Canal+ agreement locks in the current system,” a source close to Netflix said. Although its industry agreement has lapsed, Netflix’s investment obligations have not. The platform must still invest 20% of its French revenue in local production, while its release window has slipped from 15 months back to the default 17 months after negotiations over a new agreement stalled. Free-to-air broadcasters gain access to films just 22 months after their theatrical release, leaving Netflix only a five-month exclusivity period despite its growing financial commitments. That windowing rule explains why Netflix is skipping Cannes every year as the festival requires every film competing for a Palme d’Or to come out in French theaters. Having failed to secure a 12-month release window, Netflix is now shifting the fight. Rather than focusing primarily on earlier access to films, the company has begun publicly calling for a cap on mandatory investment obligations . Netflix now invests more than $287 million annually in French films, series and documentaries, including roughly $68 million in movies that are theatrically released, such as Gilles Lellouche’s Cannes-premiering romance “ Beating Hearts ” (pictured above). It’s also working with renowned French filmmakers on Netflix original movies, for instance Jacques Audiard’s next movie . The company argues that, unless the rules change, U.S. streaming services could account for nearly half of all financing for French production by 2030, according to estimates cited by Le Monde . Prime Video’s battle has centered on a different issue — how its investment obligations should be calculated. Unlike other streaming services, Prime Video is bundled with Amazon Prime, making it difficult to isolate the value of the video service from other benefits such as free delivery and music streaming. Its investment convention with France’s media regulator ARCOM expired only days ago and was just extended for another six months while negotiations continue. What’s currently being debated is a revised proposal that would give the streamer the option to invest $103 million annually across cinema and audiovisual production for a window greater than 12 months, or invest $126 million for a window at 12 months, according to a source close to the discussions. Prime Video ideally wants Disney’s nine-month slot. But ARCOM has denied it, saying that if Amazon wants Disney’s release window, it should make a comparable commitment to financing theatrical films. Disney, whose recent acquisitions include Ladj Ly’s anticipated period epic adventure film “Dumas: Black Devil,” currently directs 14% of its French revenue toward cinema investment, well above the regulatory minimum. If it fails to reach an agreement, Prime Video defaults to the same position as Netflix, with access to films 17 months after theatrical release while contributing only the regulatory minimum toward French production. Canal+‘s recently signed $1.1 billion agreement with France’s film industry has raised the stakes even further. In exchange for its investment commitment, the pay-TV giant keeps its privileged six-month release window — the earliest currently available in France. But the agreement is tied to the current balance of the country’s windowing system, meaning that any concession granted to Prime Video or Netflix would clash with Canal+. If another major streaming service such as Prime Video or Netflix were granted access to films within 12 months, Canal+’s agreement would automatically trigger a three-month renegotiation period with the film industry. Canal+ would then risk losing its six-month exclusivity and instead revert to a nine-month release window, according to a source involved in negotiations. Back in court, Netflix is challenging the latest version of France’s windowing system at the Conseil d’état, arguing that it creates an uneven playing field. While Disney+ secured a nine-month release window by committing a higher percentage of its French revenue to theatrical films, Netflix says it invests more in absolute value yet remains stuck at 17 months. Prime Video has joined Netflix in challenging the legal mechanism that extends France’s windowing rules to streaming platforms that did not sign the underlying industry agreement, arguing they should not be bound by terms they never accepted. Separately, Netflix has launched another legal challenge against recent amendments to France’s SMAD decree requiring streaming platforms to dedicate part of their audiovisual investment specifically to documentaries, animation and live performance. Netflix France’s VP of content Pauline Dauvin penned an open letter published in Le Monde, warning that these sub-quotas are turning cultural diversity into a “checklist,” hurting their editorial freedom and unfairly singling out streamers because comparable obligations do not apply to traditional broadcasters. No timetable has been set for either case, although decisions could come later this year or early next. The fight is also shifting to Brussels, where the European Commission is preparing to review the Audiovisual Media Services Directive, and Netflix is lobbying for clearer limits on how far member states can go in imposing investment obligations on platforms. During a recent visit to Brussels, Netflix’s co-CEO Ted Sarandos also urged EU policymakers not to overlook YouTube, which he described as a “straightforward direct competitor” to streamers and broadcaster which isn’t subject to comparable investment obligations. ‘Human Centipede’ Creator Reveals Last Movie ‘The End of Tom Six’; He Filmed for Six Years While Living in Isolation With Multiple Sclerosis (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board View All July 23, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes a detail about the premiere episode of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Each episode of The Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe tells a story of its four protagonists, Stuart ( Kevin Sussman ), Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ), traveling to another alternate reality as they try to fix the device built by Sheldon and Leonard and the multiverse Armageddon it created. Each episode’s opening credits also tell their own story via a series of fourth wall-busting amusing messages to the viewer embedded into the animated title sequence set to a differently arranged theme song by Danny Elfman. The series of notes are capped by a spoiler, which in the Episode 1 credits reads “Barry Dies.” Related Stories Casting 'The Earliest Show': Chris Pratt, Lamorne Morris & Sarah Silverman Among 14 Guest Stars News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators & Stars On Premiere's Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath Who is Barry? He turned out to be Denise’s boyfriend in post-apocalyptic Pasadena who dies pretty meaninglessly when he says “Follow me!” and charges first into the heavily guarded CalTech, leading Stuart and Bert, joined by Denise, in their mission to break in and take Sheldon and Leonard’s machine. While the title sequence spoiled one death, the series’ premiere featured a bigger, more shocking killing of an original Big Bang character, Raj (Kunal Nayyar), who had been imprisoned at CalTech by Barry Kripke (Bowie). You can read all about it here . Deadline asked Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators Chuck Lorre, Bill Prady and Zak Penn about the clever, custom title sequences. DEADLINE: Was this about one of you being really unhappy with the streaming culture of people skipping opening credits? LORRE : Me. PRADY : Chuck said people make these brilliant opening credit sequences that people watch one time. LORRE : And then you can click on the button that says ‘Skip Titles’, and I went, “Well, it’s a terrible waste of time and money and creativity. What if we made a title sequence that you could skip but you shouldn’t? And that would mean every title sequence have to be different and worth watching. And then we got a gift from the gods when Danny Elfman said yes, I’ll write a theme and produce a theme song, and he rearranged it and and remixed it and did variations on it throughout the 10 episodes as well, so the end result was a title sequence that hopefully is surprising and fun to watch. DEADLINE: And the spoiler part, where did it come from? Chuck, was it you again? Because some of them are really spoilers; ‘Barry Dies’ is a real spoiler. PENN : Yeah, that was I think something we all liked the idea of right off the bat is, why not? Who cares? We were like, let’s try it. Let’s just see what happens if we put a spoiler in the title, and we were just trying to keep ourselves entertained and do things that were different. PRADY : I mean, not much more than it made us laugh, the notion that, especially in the online television watching culture, there’s all of this stuff about spoilers, people hunting for spoilers, people trying to avoid spoilers. What if there’s a spoiler and it’s just sort of kind of meaningless? PENN : Also, I always felt like if we say “Spoiler: Gary Dies,” a lot of people are going to think, well, It’s not going to be that simple. So it would still be shocking when he actually does die. I’m counting on people being cynical about it. LORRE : I’m counting on people laughing. PRADY : The answer to a lot of questions is because it made us laugh, and we hope it makes other people laugh. DEADLINE: Some of the spoilers are really mild, but this one was like, first: who’s Gary?, and then it was that simple, he just died. PRADY : He died, didn’t he? And he really just died. PENN : Yeah, it’s just totally pointless. LORRE : “Follow me.” PRADY: “Follow me.” Oh. Musical Variations The Simpsons theme composer Elfman recalled “the crazy thing” that happened after he was asked to write main title music for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe and, as a Big Bang fan, agreed to do it. “I wrote it, Chuck loved it, and he said, ‘So here’s the thing. I need you to do 10 variations on it,'” Elfman said. “I thought about it for two seconds. No one’d ever asked me to do that before but I just said, ‘You got it.'” And he did it, drawing inspiration from the particular episode for its unique theme music. “It wasn’t even difficult,” he said. “Each episode, just mix it up and try things. It was really just fun.” Danny Elfman recalls how Chuck Lorre requested 10 different variations of the 'Stuart Fails to Save the Universe' theme: "No one's ever asked me to do that before" pic.twitter.com/MmlmZScV7o — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 22, 2026 Unveils First Results Since Sky Deal; Studios Biz Bullish Despite U.S. Declines Fremantle Hires ‘Narcos’ Exec As Global Scripted Chief Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309M Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation ‘You Are Here’ For BBC & Starz ‘This Is Birmingham’: TV Series Adaptation Of Surprise Prime Video UK Hit In Works View All January 26, 2026 4:00am Christian Vesper Fremantle Christian Vesper is exiting his role as Fremantle ‘s CEO of Global Drama and Film. The news brings to an end a ten-year run at the super-indie, during which time he executive-produced shows such as Picnic at Hanging Rock and films including Bugonia and Pillion . Vesper has joined Fremantle from AMC Networks in 2016, after a five-year period at the cable network. At Fremantle, he was a key player in the company’s switch from a largely unscripted producer to one also a player in scripted. During his tenure, Fremantle released 80 films and is on track to release its hundredth this year. Related Stories Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz Cancellations and Renewals 'American Idol' Renewed For Season 25 At ABC He was based in London and reported to Fremantle Group COO and CEO for Continental Europe Andrea Scrosati, who will lead the film and drama teams on an interim basis alongside the wider management teams at those units. Watch on Deadline “With Christian at the helm, we have established our drama and film business and delivered both consistent success and critical acclaim,” said Scrosati. “Our scripted portfolio is today a key component of our business and recognised across the industry. Christian is a creative at heart, and his vision has helped build the credibility of our drama and film slate. We appreciate that he now wishes to focus on new horizons, and we all wish him well in the future.” “After ten years with Fremantle, I have decided that the time is right to step down from my role as CEO Film and Drama,” added Vesper. “I would like to thank Jennifer Mullin and Andrea Scrosati for their incredible support, ambition and creative spirit, enabling us to build our film and drama capabilities. I am extremely proud of what we have achieved together, and the fact we will deliver our 100th film this year underlines the progress made.” Under Vesper’s leadership, Fremantle struck scripted partnerships with Emma Stone and Dave McCary’s Fruit Tree Productions; Kristen Stewart, Dylan Meyer and Maggie McLean’s Nevermind Pictures; Pablo and Juan de Dios Larraín’s Fabula; Rachel Weisz and Polly Stokes’ Astral Projection; Edward Berger’s Nine Hours; Johan Renck and Michael Parets’ Sinestra Films; Sarah Condon’s Fair Harbour; and Richard Yee and Krishnendu Majumdar’s Me+You Productions. Vesper was also exec producer on the Oscar-nominated Emma Stone and Jesse Plemons starrer Bugonia , Cannes prize winner Pillion , Daniel Craig pic Queer , Maria , Australian series Picnic at Hanging Rock and BBC/TVNZ miniseries The Luminaries . More recently, he worked to set up Fox’s Baywatch rival. Elsewhere, he worked with Angelina Jolie on Without Blood , Joe Wright on Sky Italia’s M. Son of the Century and Tom Alfredsson on Faithless . Prior to Fremantle, he had a 14-year spell at Sundance TV, the AMC Networks channel. There he worked on Rectify , The Honorable Woman , The Last Panthers , Top of the Lake and Deutschland 83 . He also had roles at HBO, iFilm, October Films and USA Films. With the two leads now cast, production on the feature film based on the first of Emily Henry’s adult romance novels that came out in 2020 will likely start production soon. Related Stories Books Which Emily Henry Books Are Becoming Movies? ‘Happy Place,’ ‘Book Lovers,’ Among Others Acquisitions Tango To Adapt Emily Henry’s Novel ‘Book Lovers’ Into Movie For everything we know about the Beach Read movie, read on: When will the Beach Read movie come out? 20th Century Studios will release the film theaters on May 7, 2027; it originally had been set for May 14. Is the Beach Read movie in production? Watch on Deadline Director Yulin Kuang posted on Instagram that production had wrapped July 30, 2026. Filming commenced June 8, as unveiled by Kuang, who posted a shot of Phoebe Dynevor and Patrick Schwarzenegger doing a camera test. Who will be in the Beach Read movie? Deadline broke the news of Kevin Bacon’s and Andie MacDowel’s casting in the film. We also first reported the casting of Kristin Davis and Tig Notaro . As Deadline exclusively reported, Bridgerton alum Phoebe Dynevor , who led the first season of the Shonda Rhimes and Netflix series based on Julia Quinn’s books, will star as January Andrews . Deadline also broke the news that Patrick Schwarzenegger , fresh off The White Lotus Season 3 and Love of Your Life with Margaret Qualley, will portray Augustus ‘Gus’ Everett . “‘Patrick is a slow burn,’ is what I wrote in my notes after meeting him for the first time. There was something about the way he talked about his feelings on love and romance that I couldn’t forget. But I was unconvinced we’d found our Gus, because I knew we had to be exhaustive in our efforts, given how important this character is to readers,” writer/director Yulin Kuang said on Instagram .

articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary?

Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board View All July 30, 2026 6:22pm Story Arc (L-R): Tommy Walker, Laurem Lapkus, Kevin Sussman in Episode 2 of 'Stuart Fails To Save the Uiverse' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 2 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Related Stories News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short After Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ) got separated from Stuart ( Kevin Sussman ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ) at the end of the first episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe as the guys were transported from the post-apocalyptic CalTech lab to an alternate universe, Stuart made it his mission to find Denise — or that alternate reality’s version of her. He tracked her down to find her “happily” married to Gary (Tommy Walker), the same guy who was Denise’s boyfriend in post-apocalyptic Pasadena in the premiere where he was senselessly killed by CalTech guards. Happily is in quotes because in that universe, society is ruled by an evil AI through a buzzer on everyone’s neck which sends electric shocks through their body if they express any negative emotion. “Denise, you and I are destined to be together, and I have come from a parallel universe to claim you,” Stuart said while sitting in Denise and Gary’s living room. Deadline asked Sussman about Stuart’s gutsy move. ”That’s interesting that you bring that up because that’s pretty un-Stuart like,” he said. “So I guess if there is some growth for Stuart, it’s that his love for her pushes him into a kind of assertiveness that he never would have had on the original show.” Lupkus spoke about Denise’s unhappy marriage, which had driven her to drinking, and Stuart’s arrival. “In that universe, we have buzzers on our necks that stop us from ever being rude or saying what like anything that’s not totally happy, so she’s conditioned at that point to just act like everything’s fine, and to have someone coming into her apartment saying like, you don’t have to live like this like, I’m gonna get you out of here, she can’t even react because she knows that she’ll just be writhing on the floor,” Lapkus said. “So I think, as we see later, she gets swept up in it with him, but then her real feelings for him start to return, and she can feel again.” Added Sussman, ” Yeah, and it actually is a good metaphor for anybody who’s ever felt stuck in a relationship.” What about Gary? Once again, he was left behind as by the end of the episode, Denise had joined Stuart, Bert and Kripke, and she and Stuart were seen holding hands while leaping into the next universe together. “I think Denise has some sort of love for Gary, even if he’s the wrong guy for her, because she’s excited to see him every time she sees him, and she’s back with him over and over again,” Lapkus said. “There are those people in your life where you’re like, you got to break up with that guy, but she kind of likes him for some weird reason, and then she cares for him, so when he’s killed over and over, that’s also pretty upsetting.” Added Sussman, “It’s bad enough when your loved one is murdered once.” Unveils First Results Since Sky Deal; Studios Biz Bullish Despite U.S. Declines Fremantle Hires ‘Narcos’ Exec As Global Scripted Chief Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309M Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple July 23, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal View All July 30, 2026 6:23pm Story Arc 'The Big Bang Theory', (L-R): Simon Helberg, Melissa Rauch, Mayim Bialik, Jim Parsons, Kunal Nayyar, Johnny Galecki, Kaley Cuoco, Kevin Sussman in "The Hesitation Ramification" Season 7 Michael Yarish/Courtesy Everett Collection SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 2 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Related Stories News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath As Stuart Fails To Save the Universe revealed in the Episode 2 opening credits spoiler (You can read all about the show’s unique, ever-changing main title sequence here ), “Zack is in this one.” Zack, a recurring character on The Big Bang Theory played by Brian Thomas Smith, was Penny’s ( Kaley Cuoco ) dim-witted but kind-hearted on- and off- boyfriend while she and Leonard (Johnny Galecki) were broken up. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from The Big Bang Theory creators Chuck Lorre & Bill Prady and Zak Penn , has established a pattern with the first two episodes, each featuring a surprise return of a Big Bang Theory original cast member. Following Kunal Nayyar’s appearance as Raj in Episode 1 where he is shockingly killed by Kripke (John Ross Bowie), Cuoco showed up in the second episode alongside Zack (Smith). In it, Penny is a leader of the resistance against an AI-imposed mind control in an alternate universe where everyone is forced to be perpetually nice and happy by shock-inducing buttons on their necks. Zack is her second in command. (L-R): Brian Posehn, Brian Thomas Smith, Kevin Sussman , Kaley Cuoco and John Ross Bowie in Episode 2 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ Multiverse and all, why did the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators opt to have Penny be with Zack as if her relationship with Leonard — one of the hallmarks of The Big Bang Theory from the pilot — never happened? “Because that’s what happened in that universe, we don’t know what Leonard is doing in that universe,” Prady said. “Every universe gives every character a completely different history. There’s no continuity because they lived a different life, they lived in a different world. That Penny lives in a world where an evil AI controls people through shock collars, and so she had a completely different experience.” Added Lorre, “There was no Cheesecake Factory in her life,” a reference to Penny’s place of work for most of Big Bang ‘s run. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe presents a very different version of Penny who is pretty ruthless, violently slapping Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Bert (Brian Posehn) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) to “deprogram” them and ordering them killed with no hesitation once she realizes that they don’t know how to defeat the AI overlord. The trio are ultimately saved by a drone attack launched by the AI, with Penny, Zack and the rest getting incapacitated while Stuart, Bert, Kripke, along with Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), use Leonard and Sheldon’s machine to transport themselves to another universe. With Raj teetering on the edge of madness in Season 1, are Big Bang OGs relishing going dark in the spinoff? “Beyond,” Prady said. Added Lorre, “Beyond. It was fun to do something different, that was part of the promise, come and play with us, and we’ll make sure that you’re playing a version of your character you never got to play before, an entirely different approach to the character, and that was fun for the actors.” Said Penn, “And everyone wants to play the bad guy, that’s always the most fun role.” Episode 2 also includes appearances from The Big Bang Theory ‘s Christine Baranski and Riki Lindhome. Baranski, who played Leonard’s mom Beverly on the mothership series, is the host of the 30-month re-education program Stuart, Bert are Kripke are forced to attend as a version of herself. (Interestingly, neither Stuart nor Bert or Kripke reacted to her uncanny resemblance to their friend’s mother.) ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ E2: Christine Baranski Lindhome, who did only three but memorable guest appearances on Big Bang as Ramona Nowitzkis, an obsessive CalTech graduate student, plays a version of the same character who is now a receptionist from hell at her alma mater. ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ E2: Riki Lindhome Unveils First Results Since Sky Deal; Studios Biz Bullish Despite U.S. Declines Fremantle Hires ‘Narcos’ Exec As Global Scripted Chief Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309M Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? The Golden Globe winner recently noted that the cast took a 25% pay cut in attempt to keep the CBS procedural going past its 14-season run, which lasted from 2010 to 2024, before it was succeeded by the Donnie Wahlberg-led spin-off Boston Blue . “ Blue Bloods was a labor of love… I think for everybody,” he said on the Where Everybody Knows Your Name podcast. “The real truth to that is in the last year of [ Blue Bloods ], at our last family dinner, everybody wanted to come back. We’d already taken a 25 percent cut in salary. We’d already done all sorts of things to keep the show going.” Related Stories News ‘Boston Blue’ Promo Reveals Season 2 Release Date News Donnie Wahlberg Offered CBS “50% Of My Paycheck” To Film ‘Boston Blue’ Entirely In Boston Selleck continued, “It was very frustrating because… out of the top 100 shows on broadcast television, Blue Bloods was number six in our fifteenth year. Nobody wanted to leave. Everybody was gonna stay on. That’s hard to get. It may be some kind of record to have the same cast intact for that length of time. Usually if it wasn’t a family, it would be different, but you know, you couldn’t very well replace Jamie [played by Will Estes] or Danny [Wahlberg] or anybody with another actor. Watch on Deadline Having previously starred in shows like Magnum, P.I. , Friends and Las Vegas , Selleck raved about his experience starring as patriarch, Commissioner Frank Reagan, on the Robin Green and Mitchell Burgess cop family drama. “Maybe people don’t realize, but a lot of shows become miserable to work on. You get a lot of egos and ‘I’m not coming out of my dressing room until he’s coming out’… and it’s miserable,” explained Selleck. “ Blue Bloods was never that.” Following Blue Bloods ‘ 2024 finale, Wahlberg reprised his role as Det. Danny Reagan in the spin-off Boston Blue , which premiered in October and has been renewed for Season 2 , returning Oct. 9. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Besting ‘No Way Home’s $50M U.S. Previews – Thursday PM Box Office
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Besting ‘No Way Home’s $50M U.S. Previews – Thursday PM Box Office ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309 Million Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record ‘The Odyssey’ Passes ‘Oppenheimer’s $330M U.S. Lifetime B.O. In 13 Days Before ‘Spider-Man’ Swings In – Box Office Update View All July 30, 2026 10:09pm Tom Holland as Spider-Man Sony Pictures EXCLUSIVE: When it comes to breaking box office records this weekend, look out, because Spider-Man: Brand New Day will do whatever a spider can, starting with tonight as the Sony /Marvel Studios co-production is outstripping the Thursday night previews of the 2021 previous chapter Spider-Man: No Way Home, which did $50M . All of this makes sense given the $80M advance ticket sales figure we heard about for the Tom Holland and Zendaya $225M net production. No Way Home (which had previews begin at 3PM on its first Thursday) posted the third best previews ever behind 2019’s Avengers: Endgame ‘s $60M (6PM start time) and 2015’s Star Wars: Force Awakens ‘ $57M Thursday night. Now with more than $50M , Brand New Day stands as the third best U.S./Canada previews ever for a theatrical release, the best previews ever for a Sony movie, and the best previews post Covid. The Destin Daniel Cretton directed Spider-Man sequel began showtimes at 12 noon today, and its preview cash will include Wednesday night’s Prime Video member screening. Some sources were hearing that Brand New Day ‘s preview money tonight was exceeding Avengers: Endgame . We’ll know by tom’w morning if it’s higher. Related Stories News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day's $309 Million Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record News Tom Holland Says There's "A Whole Plan" For Passing Spider-Man Baton To Another Actor: "I Have A Really Clear Vision" No Way Home ‘s previews of $50M only repped 41% of its $121.96M first Friday. That resulted in the second best opening ever at the domestic box office with $260.1M behind Avengers: Endgame ‘s all-time high of $357.1M. Force Awakens ‘ $57M previews accounted for 48% of its first Friday which was $119.1M. At one point in time Force Awakens 3-day start of $247.96 held the all-time opening record in North America, but it eventually fell to fourth. NRG had a low domestic opening estimate of $195M for Brand New Day, but exhibitors and other tracking services such as Greenlight Analytics believe it’s significantly higher from $260M to even maybe $300M. Watch on Deadline Some analysts begin to nerd out arguing that we need to take into account start time for the previews here on Brand New Day, and the time of year before making forecasts. Seriously, it doesn’t matter: this is a ton of money and the most we’ve seen in quite some time, putting away the previous post Covid preview record of $38.5M belonging to Deadpool & Wolverine two Julys ago. And the other amazing thing about this Spider-Man is that he’s raking in all this cash without the help of Imax screens (which we saw Barbie do three years ago as Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer claimed them). So far, Brand New Day has the best Rotten Tomatoes audience score out of the nine live-action Spider-Man movies with 98%. Critical score is strong at 90% certified fresh, which is just under the 93% of No Way Home. Tonight’s estimates are according to sources. articles.title: ITV Reveals Early Share Buyback Of $140M Before Sky Deal Completes As Broadcaster Unveils First Set Of Results Since Confirming The Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal ITV Studios Bosses Bullish Despite U.S. & International Declines As ‘Love Island’ & ‘The Gentlemen’ Maker Prepares To Go Independent ITV Reveals Early Share Buyback Of $140M Before Sky Deal Completes As Broadcaster Unveils First Set Of Results Since Confirming The Deal View All July 30, 2026 11:24pm 'Love Island's Maya Jama ITV2 ITV has a gift for shareholders this morning to the tune of £100M ($140M) as it releases its first financial results since the Sky deal was confirmed, which slightly improved on the prior year. The broadcaster is today revealing a £100M share buyback, which CEO Carolyn McCall described as an “early return of part of the previously announced £950 million net cash return expected on completion of the sale” of its network biz to Sky. The news will be welcome by shareholders who may have to wait patiently until at least mid-2027 to see larger returns on the £1.6B deal. The ITV share price has been a constant source of consternation for several years now and many had been pushing for a sale for a long time. McCall said the separate move to continue with an interim dividend of 1.7p totalling £60M “reflects our commitment to attractive shareholder returns.” Related Stories Executives All3Media International's Jonathan Hughes Exits For ITV Studios After Banijay Merger News ITV, Jeff Pope & Lauren Cowell Teaming On "Devastating" Drama About Social Media's Impact On Kids ITV said again today that it expects the Sky deal to complete midway through next year and it expects the Culture Secretary, Lisa Nandy, to issue a Public Intervention Notice to examine one of the biggest deals in the history of British broadcasting. That deal, which will see a crown jewel of British TV become part of the NBCUniversal entertainment empire, is still subject to this rigorous regulatory approval process, coming as Nandy says she is “minded to intervene” in the mega-bucks WarnerMount deal. Watch on Deadline Today’s results were the first to be published since ITV closed the deal to sell its network and streaming biz – called its Media & Entertainment (M&E) arm – to Sky, although its ITV Studios division will not be sold and is going independent. ITV’s half-year results for the first six months of 2026 were middling, with total revenue rising 2% to £1.9B, the same percentage figure as ITV Studios revenue, which moved to £912M, and M&E revenue, which increased to £975M. This disrupted the recent pattern of ITV Studios tending to grow by larger proportions than M&E. In fact, adjusted EBITDA in the M&E division rose an impressive 37% to 48M while ITV Studios’ EBITDA was down 9%, although the period did take in the soccer World Cup, a lucrative time for the ITV network. Ad revenue was up 26% and digital ad revenue shot up 31%, again probably down to the World Cup. ITV Studios will soon be unleashed onto the market at a time when rivals Banijay and All3Media have merged, creating a production super-giant. Banijay’s CEO earlier this week played down reports that Banijay is interested in swooping for ITV Studios. At the same time, Sky has commited to spend £2.1B on ITV Studios content between 2028 and 2032 and Sky-owned Great British Bake Off producer Love Productions will be sold to ITV Studios. Notably, ITV Studios’ revenue in the UK was up 17% during the period but down 17% in the U.S. and 24% internationally, again reflecting a reversal of previous fortunes. Inroads with the American streamers has been one of ITV Studios’ pillars of growth for several years. ITV Studios has “a really strong delivery schedule” for the second half of this year, it said, including Line of Duty Season 7 for the BBC and another series of The Gentlemen for Netflix. McCall said: “The recently announced sale of M&E to Sky represents a substantial milestone for ITV. This transaction will unlock significant value for shareholders, with a net cash return of around £950 million, excluding any contingent consideration, and continued ownership of an attractive, growing global content business in ITV Studios. Underpinned by its world class talent, global scale and unique IP library, ITV Studios is well positioned to deliver above-market profitable organic revenue growth at industry leading margins, strong cash generation, attractive returns to shareholders and an investment grade balance sheet.” Last year, ITV profits were slashed during the first six months of the year. Ulmer will help the company bridge the North American content industries with Southeast Asia’s production infrastructure. He will focus on bringing U.S. and international projects into Southeast Asia, leveraging Wave Films’ production infrastructure across the region to facilitate cross-border production. Headquartered in Singapore, Wave Films operates production and post-production capabilities across Malaysia, Philippines and Cambodia. The company is currently line producing Pierre Morel’s The Good Samaritan in Malaysia and has recently produced or line produced projects including Dark Red , filmed in India earlier this year; Chihiro Amano’s Magical Secret Tour , filmed last year in Singapore; Korean drama Kidnapping Day, and reality shows including Bachelorette and Asia Express . Add our cross-border production model, and the fact that we can park a project in the right country for the right tax break, locations or stage access, and you have a very compelling package for any North American producer looking east.” Ulmer said: “North American producers are leaving money on the table if they are not looking at Southeast Asia. The region has the crews, the stages, the locations, the expertise, and the incentives. What it needs is a single point of contact in Los Angeles who can guarantee delivery. articles.title: ITV Studios Bosses Bullish Despite U.S. & International Declines As ‘Love Island’ & ‘The Gentlemen’ Maker Prepares To Go Independent
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal ITV Studios Bosses Bullish Despite U.S. & International Declines As ‘Love Island’ & ‘The Gentlemen’ Maker Prepares To Go Independent ITV Reveals Early Share Buyback Of $140M Before Sky Deal Completes As Broadcaster Unveils First Set Of Results Since Confirming The Deal View All July 31, 2026 12:53am 'The Gentlemen': co-produced by ITV Studios-owned Moonage Pictures Netflix ITV Studios bosses are remaining bullish in the face of declining U.S. and international revenues as the Love Island maker prepares to be unleashed onto the market. Of concern for ITV Studios , this morning’s ITV half-year results showed a 17% revenue decline in the U.S. and a 24% slide internationally, reflecting a reversal of previous fortunes. On a results call with press, ITV Studios chief Julian Bellamy put this mainly down to a “softening of demand” in the free-to-air space and said it “underlines the broader importance” of the producer-distributor pushing further into making shows for streamers and developing its Zoo 55 digital arm. Related Stories News ITV Reveals Early Share Buyback Of $140M Before Sky Deal Completes As Broadcaster Unveils First Set Of Results Since Confirming The Deal Executives Ahead Of Comcast Split, NBCUniversal Appoints People Inc. Veteran Christopher Halpin As CFO “Let’s not forget, we’re on the up,” Bellamy said bullishly, as he pointed out that overall ITV Studios revenues grew 2% during the first six months of this year to £912M ($1.2B). “We feel confident about the progress we are making.” Watch on Deadline ITV CEO Carolyn McCall added: “We need to clarify that we don’t see a softening of the market, this was one small segment of the market.” ITV Studios has made growth with the American streamers a cornerstone of its strategy over the past few years and there will nevertheless be jitters about the decline in revenue across the pond. Helping allay those jitters are some big shows set to deliver during the latter half of 2026 including The Gentlemen Season 2 for Netflix and Apple TV’s Guilty Creatures, both made by ITV Studios indies. When the Sky -ITV deal completes around this time next year, ITV Studios will be unleashed onto the market and will become a publicly listed company. McCall backed ITV Studios today as having “terrific competitive advantages” with “extraordinary IP” and refused to budge on the question of whether ITV Studios will look for a buyer once it becomes independent. This came a few days after the CEO of Banijay downplayed the idea of the French behemoth swooping for ITV Studios now that it is merging with All3Media. “We’re confident about competing because we have scale,” said McCall of ITV Studios. “We are a globally scaled diversifed business and feel we don’t have any issue with our scale. And the other thing for our shareholders is that they are hugely supportive of having a listed pure play studios business. They support that strongly.” “A huge amount of speculation about virtually every company in America” McCall was quick to refuse comment on rumors further up the chain that ITV’s new owner Sky will itself be sold now that it has been divested by Comcast . “There is a huge amount of speculation about virtually every company in America so I can’t really comment,” she added. She once again backed Sky’s commitment to ITV News once the £1.6B deal completes. She noted that the pay-TV giant has made it “extremely clear” there will be “two distinct separate editorial voices for news” along with “opportunities to supercharge and promote” ITV’s regional news coverage on Sky. ITV delivered a set of solid if unspectacular results this morning, including strong profits for the soon-to-be-sold networks biz, mostly due to the World Cup. It also revealed an early share buyback of £100M for shareholders, which comes prior to the Sky-ITV deal completing. articles.title: Fremantle Hires Katie O’Connell Marsh As Global Scripted Chief
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation ‘You Are Here’ For BBC & Starz ‘This Is Birmingham’: TV Series Adaptation Of Surprise Prime Video UK Hit In Works View All July 31, 2026 3:00am Katie O'Connell Marsh Myung J. Chun/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Katie O’Connell Marsh has been named Fremantle ‘s next global scripted boss, Deadline can reveal. Baywatch and M. Son of the Century producer Fremantle has been seeking out a UK-based executive to effectively replace Christian Vesper , the CEO of Global Drama and Film who exited his post in January. Following an extensive hiring process that attracted top tier scripted candidates, former Gaumont International Television and Platform One chief O’Connell Marsh emerged as the front runner, according to several sources, and she has now officially landed the role. Related Stories Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz Cancellations and Renewals 'American Idol' Renewed For Season 25 At ABC Her official title of will be CEO, Fremantle Global Scripted Hub, a newly-created drama and film division. She will take up the role in August. Given she is currently U.S.-based, she will relocate to London. Watch on Deadline O’Connell Marsh will report to Andrea Scrosati, Fremantle’s Group COO and CEO Continental Europe, with a dotted line to Jens Richter, CEO Commercial and International, and will sit on the Global Leadership Team. Part of the move is creation of the Fremantle Global Scripted Hub, which will provide creative, commercial and strategic direction across Fremantle’s scripted labels. She will work closely with local teams, share best practice and build a connected global scripted business across drama and film. Additionally, O’Connell Marsh will oversee Fremantle’s annual scripted investment budget, recommending spend in projects and selected third-party opportunities. She will also work closely with Richter’s Commercial & International team on sales forecasts and commercial analysis to support investment decisions. O’Connell Marsh, a veteran scripted exec who has U.S. and international experience, has a reputation for backing premium, commercially-driven series such as Netflix crime drama Narcos and Apple TV’s Invasion . Her work as an exec producer on Narcos helped establish the notion that non-English language dramas were palatable to global streaming audiences. In 2010, she established Gaumont International Television, the U.S. arm of French studio Gaumont. There, she produced the likes of Netflix series Hemlock Grove , NBC’s Hannibal and animated streaming comedy F is for Family . O’Connell Marsh later had a short spell at DreamWorks Animation as Head of Global Live Action TV before establishing Platform One , which made Apple TV’s Invasion and Showtime’s Rust . She then became Vice Chair of Boat Rocker Studios after Canadian firm Boat Rocker bought Platform One. Most recently, she has been an exec producer for Apple and board member at EuropaCorp, while also advising Bain & Company. “We are delighted to welcome Katie to Fremantle as our new CEO of the Global Scripted Hub,” said Scrosati. “She is a highly accomplished, passionate and commercially astute executive with a deep understanding of global audiences and market trends. “She joins us at an incredibly exciting time as we continue to build on the strength of our diverse scripted slate, our award-winning creative labels, and the exceptional talent both on and off screen, that defines our scripted business. Her creative instincts, strategic vision and proven ability to attract and nurture world-class talent will be invaluable as we continue to grow our scripted business and further strengthen Fremantle’s position as a global leader in premium storytelling.” Her predecessor, Vesper, spent nearly a decade with Fremantle, striking a range of talent deals and developing shows from the upcoming Baywatch TV revival to more complex fare such as My Brilliant Friend , The New Pope and The Luminaries . He also led a push into feature film making and exec produced movies such as Pillion , Poor Things and Bugonia . Fremantle released 80 pics during his tenure. Vesper was also based in London and reported to Fremantle Group COO and CEO for Continental Europe Andrea Scrosati, who has since been leading the film and drama teams on an interim basis alongside the wider management teams at those units. “I am thrilled to be joining Fremantle at such an exciting time,” said O’Connell Marsh. “I have long admired the strength of its creative vision, its exceptional scripted labels and the critical acclaim achieved across its world-class slate. Fremantle has built a truly unique home for storytellers, combining creative excellence, outstanding talent and global ambition. “As the industry continues to evolve, the greatest opportunities will come from bringing together exceptional talent, international collaboration and a commercially driven approach. I am especially looking forward to working closely with Jennifer Mullin, Andrea Scrosati and the outstanding teams across the business to build on Fremantle’s success and help shape the next chapter of growth for its scripted business.” Strategic review Fremantle is best known for entertainment formats such as Got Talent , The X Factor and Pop Idol , but has expanded into scripted through the likes of Maxton Hall: The World Between Us , My Brilliant Friend , Sandokan: The Pirate Prince and Sullivan’s Crossing . Production companies within the group have been responsible for shows such as the Deutschland… franchise, Normal People and Shtisel , and films including Pillion , The Hand of God and Poor Things . In March, Fremantle’s parent company, RTL, revealed the results of a strategic review amid falling revenues, with cost saving plans announced at Fremantle and RTL Deutschland. Among the measures was a decision to stop fully financing films, but sources within Fremantle insist it remains a player in the movie space. With her TV background, it is not clear how extensively Marsh’s role will cover film. Fremantle is attempting to navigate and increasingly complex and competitive global market. Rivals Banijay Entertainment and RedBird IMI-owned All3Media completed their merger earlier this month, and now claim the combined entity is the largest independent production business ever created, while ITV Studios is set to become a solo player when its parent, ITV, is sold to Sky . Mediawan has bought the likes of The North Road Company and, along with Banijay, has been tipped to buy Lionsgate, while many expect ITV Studios to be a takeover or merger target, though its bosses have claimed it would not need a “transformational deal” that would combine its assets with another such as Fremantle. Well-placed sources in Europe have suggested that Bertelsmann-owned RTL look at how Fremantle operates once former Warner Bros. Discovery exec Clément Schwebig fully gets his feet under the table at RTL. Schwebig replaced the long-serving Thomas Rabe as RTL CEO in May , as Fremantle posted steady but unspectacular Q1 revenues of €372M ($423M). Rabe remains Chairman and CEO of Bertelsmann, but is set to exit at the end of the year. articles.title: Alan Cumming-Backed Block The Merger Submits Evidence To UK Culture Sec; Argues WarnerMount Will “Directly Impact UK Documentarians’ Ability To Tell Diverse Stories”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal ITV Studios Bosses Bullish Despite U.S. & International Declines As ‘Love Island’ & ‘The Gentlemen’ Maker Prepares To Go Independent ITV Reveals Early Share Buyback Of $140M Before Sky Deal Completes As Broadcaster Unveils First Set Of Results Since Confirming The Deal View All July 31, 2026 3:16am Alan Cumming speaks on stage during the BAFTA Film Awards Stuart Wilson/BAFTA/Getty for BAFTA The Alan Cumming -backed Block the Merger coalition has submitted evidence to the UK Culture Secretary over why the Paramount -Warner mega-merger should be blocked. Four of the groups that make up the coalition said they provided Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy with “market data and first-hand professional evidence as she determines whether to intervene.” UK parliament is now in recess for the summer and Nandy, who has already said she is “minded to intervene,” will not deliver her decision until September 1 at the earliest. Since the recess, the $110B merger has slammed the brakes in the U.S. after 12 States sued. Related Stories News Paramount Sacrificed Some Cinema History To Win Approval For Its Warner Deal, But Will It Be Enough To Safeguard Europe's Theatrical Business? Books 'The Final Girl Support Group' Heads To Paramount As Film Directed & Adapted By Christopher Landon; Aperture & Muschiettis' Double Dream Producing The Block the Merger organizations, which are the Archival Producers Alliance, the International Documentary Association, the UK’s Documentary Film Council and Democracy Defenders Fund, complained WarnerMount would become the third largest linear broadcaster in the UK before HBO Max’s “rapid growth” is even taken into account. Watch on Deadline They also put forward the argument that for the first time the CNN and CBS News archives, two of America’s most historically significant broadcast news archives, will be under a single owner, “directly impacting UK documentarians’ ability to tell diverse stories.” “As the coalition has made clear, this merger is not a done deal, and filmmakers, journalists, archive producers, unions, and consumer advocates on both sides of the Atlantic will keep working to make sure it never is,” the organizations said. The news comes two weeks after The Traitors host Cumming posted a vid backing Block the Merger in which he said WarnerMount would “all [be] answering to a giant conglomerate beholden to Donald Trump, autocrats and oligarchs.” A few days later he co-authored an op-ed with Benedict Cumberbatch describing the deal as a “calamity.” The UK opposition to the deal has been vehement as both American congloms have a far-reaching footprint, including linear network 5 (previously Channel 5) and numerous production outfits. The European Union gave the merger the greenlight last week.
