articles.title: ‘The Walking Dead’ Renewed By Netflix In 5-Year, $500M Co-Exclusive Deal With AMC Global Media
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade In Major NY Streaming Shift, DAZN Becoming Exclusive Home For YES And MSG Networks; Gotham Sports App To Sunset Crunchyroll And Starz Launch Bundle On Prime Video Ari Emanuel Backs Paramount-WBD Deal In WSJ Op-Ed, Blasts States’ Antitrust Lawsuit As “Trash” View All July 30, 2026 4:03am 'The Walking Dead' Josh Stringer/AMC Netflix has renewed The Walking Dead , paying $500 million to AMC Global Media for five years of rights to the original zombie franchise and all of its spinoffs. The deal is co-exclusive, enabling the series to also stream on AMC+ starting next year. The 371 episodes of the original series and its six spinoffs will stream on Netflix in the UK, Italy, Australia., New Zealand and other new territories along with the U.S., where it has been (on DVD and online) since 2011. The news broke Thursday morning ahead of AMC Global Media’s second-quarter earnings results. Related Stories News Everything We Know About 'Outer Banks' Season 5 So Far News Irish Comedian Joanne McNally Inks Netflix Deal For Debut Hour Special 'Pinotphile' Included in the deal are the original show plus Fear the Walking Dead , The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon , The Walking Dead: Dead City , The Walking Dead: The Ones Who Live , The Walking Dead: World Beyond and Tales of The Walking Dead . Watch on Deadline The original series premiered on Halloween in 2010, going to run for 11 seasons and provide a company-defining economic engine for AMC Global Media. Originally known as Rainbow Media when it was a division of Cablevision, AMC spun off and had its IPO just a few months before the premiere of The Walking Dead . For Netflix, the renewal comes amid heightened investor scrutiny of engagement on its service. Many of its original titles have seen ratings declines in their second seasons, leading to questions about its competitive position, though it remains a dominant force with industry-low churn and best-in-class technology. When it comes to bringing new relevance to library content, the “Netflix effect” remains a potent phenomenon, and The Walking Dead is a prime example. “Audiences have discovered and loved The Walking Dead on Netflix for nearly 15 years and the show continues to attract new fans,” said Lori Conkling, Vice President of Licensing at Netflix. “We’re excited to partner with AMC Global Media to continue to expand that access to more audiences around the world and bring the entirety of The Walking Dead Universe to Netflix.” “We are thrilled to expand our long-time partnership with Netflix around The Walking Dead,” said Kristin Dolan, CEO of AMC Global Media. “This deal creates a global destination for this universe – all shows, all episodes – making the franchise more accessible than ever to fans around the world. In addition, the co-exclusive agreement allows us to bring the original series to AMC+ for the first time early next year. Netflix has been an important partner in making The Walking Dead one of the most successful franchises in the history of entertainment. This agreement is a fantastic result for our companies, for the fans and for this timeless IP.” Meta Stock Tanks In Jittery Market On Massive AI Investment & Mixed Q2 ‘Chicago Fire’ Original Joe Miñoso Leaving In Season 15 Of NBC Drama Westwood Bruin Theater Eyes Fall Reopening As Exhibitor Takes Over Lease Denies Sexual Assault Allegations Made By Four Women In BBC Doc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Olivia Wilde Teases Next Directing Project ‘Naughty’: “Way Bigger Than Anything I’ve Ever Taken On”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 8:56pm Olivia Wilde attends the Los Angeles premiere of Magnolia Pictures' 'I Want Your Sex' at DGA Theater Complex on July 28. Kevin Winter/Getty Images It’s an Olivia Wilde summer, and the star is not slowing down anytime soon. In between stirring up awards buzz for her film The Invite and leading Gregg Araki’s new movie I Want Your Sex , Wilde is also gearing up for her next directing vehicle, Naughty . It was announced on Tuesday that Jennifer Aniston and Peter Dinklage would be starring in the holiday comedy, and that evening Wilde opened up about the project while on the red carpet for the Araki film. “I can’t believe it. This is a project we’ve been working on for years; it’s a passion project and I fought and fought and fought to get this made. I feel so grateful that we get to make it because it is a movie that aims to be in the spirit of Rob Reiner, a comedy that has a tremendous amount of heart at its core,” Wilde told The Hollywood Reporter . Related Stories Movies Jennifer Aniston, Peter Dinklage to Star in Olivia Wilde's Santa Movie 'Naughty,' Set for 2027 Release Movies Tom Holland Says He'll Play Spider-Man "For as Long as They'll Have Me" After 'Brand New Day': "If This Movie Does Good, I Guess We'll See!" She added that, like The Invite , it will juggle both the comedy and the tragedy, “but it’s also a much bigger endeavor and is something that is way bigger than anything I’ve ever taken on. I feel very honored in this day and age to be able to direct an original theatrical comedy for a studio at this level. Universal is putting a tremendous amount of trust in me and the ability to be able to direct Jen and Peter, among a host of other incredible actors who are hopefully coming on board; I just couldn’t be more excited.” Naughty is currently in pre-production, and follows Mallory (Aniston), who is embroiled in a custody battle with her ex. Her last hope is to track down Santa Claus (Dinklage) and get him to testify in the divorce hearing. It will be Wilde’s fourth film in the directing chair, following 2019’s Booksmart , 2022’s Don’t Worry Darling and this year’s The Invite , and is set for theatrical release on Nov. 5, 2027. THR

articles.title: Evan Rachel Wood Says She’s Not Returning for ‘Practical Magic 2’ Because It’s “Not Following the Book”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 9:07pm Evan Rachel Wood Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Evan Rachel Wood is sharing the reason she believes she wasn’t asked to return for the upcoming Practical Magic sequel. During a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight , the actress said it doesn’t seem like Practical Magic 2 will be following the book. The sequel was adapted from author Alice Hoffman’s The Book of Magic , which was the follow-up to her first novel Practical Magic . “I read the book and it seems like they’re not following the book,” Wood said. “I think in the book it would have made sense to bring me back; I think in the way they’re redoing it and approaching it, it didn’t make sense.” Related Stories Lifestyle Mena Suvari to Record Audiobook for New Novel From 'Practical Magic' Author Alice Hoffman (Exclusive) Movies Pam Abdy and Sandra Bullock Talk Paramount-Warners Deal and 'Practical Magic 2' The 1998 film followed two witch sisters (played by Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman), raised by their eccentric aunts, as they face a curse that threatens any man who falls in love with an Owens woman. Wood and Alexandra Artrip played the daughters of Bullock’s character, Sally Owens. Earlier this month, Wood took to Instagram to confirm for fans that she wouldn’t be reprising her role in the new film. “I am getting asked about this a lot, so l’ll just clear it up now; I was not asked to come back and be in the Practical Magic sequel,” she wrote at the time. “l offered my services, even if it was one scene or one line. I was told they are recasting. I am sorry to disappoint the fans. It was not in my control or my choice. I would have happily rejoined my sisters.” In the sequel, Joey King was recast to play Wood’s character, while Maisie Williams will be playing the younger sister of Artrip’s character from the first film. Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing will also be reprising their characters, Aunt Jet and Aunt Franny, respectively. Wood also told ET that she’s “sad” she doesn’t get to return because “we bonded with that cast so much as children, and so to miss out on the opportunity to look at that cast and look at that house as an adult and see the history in our eyes, it’s something that can’t be faked.” Practical Magic 2 hits theaters on Sept. 11. THR

articles.title: ‘The Rookie’ Star Eric Winter Reveals Cast Filmed Alternate Season 8 Ending in Case Show Was Canceled
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 9:53pm Eric Winter and Melissa O'Neil in 'The Rookie' season eight finale. Disney/Mike Taing Logo text Eric Winter, who plays Tim Bradford in ABC ‘s The Rookie , has revealed that the cast filmed an alternate ending to season eight in case the show was canceled. In the last episode’s final moments, which aired in May, Tim proposes to Lucy Chen (Melissa O’Neil) . However, the newly engaged couple are kidnapped minutes later. While chatting with People at Comic-Con 2026 over the weekend, Winter said, “We didn’t know when we wrapped last season if we would ever come back.” Related Stories TV 'Dancing With the Stars,' '911' and 'Scrubs' (but Not 'Celebrity Jeopardy!') Set Fall Debut Dates on ABC TV WNBA on Sling TV: Here's How to Watch the 2026 WNBA All-Star Game Live Online Due to the uncertainty about the show’s future at the time, he explained, “We even shot an alternate ending to the show” that “would’ve been different.” However, Winter didn’t offer any details about the alternate ending, as it would be a “spoiler.” ABC officially announced that The Rookie had been renewed for a ninth season in April. It didn’t come as a big surprise, as the police procedural is a high performer for ABC , ranking in the top 15 network entertainment series among adults 18-49. “Anytime we find out we have another season with this great group of people, it’s an exciting time,” Winter said of the renewal news. When chatting with The Hollywood Reporter ahead of season eight, O’Neil shared her reaction to the way fans ride or die over Tim and Lucy’s onscreen relationship, aka Chenford. “It’s one of those special things that I think you can write for it as much as you want, but unless all of the right elements and spices kind of come into play, it might not work. So I feel really grateful,” she said. “He’s a wonderful professional scene partner to have, and all of the material that we’ve been given is special. But we have a good friendship and a chemistry that I think parlays really well into the relationship, especially because we started off not only with a power dynamic, but there was a little bit of … we chirp each other.” The Rookie also stars Nathan Fillion, Alyssa Diaz, Richard T. Jones, Mekia Cox, Shawn Ashmore, Jenna Dewan and Lisseth Chavez. Season nine is expected to premiere in early 2027. THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to China’s Biggest Superhero Opening in Seven Years
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 28, 2026 10:53pm Tom Holland in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Sony Pictures Could it be that Hollywood’s superheroes have begun to rediscover their powers in China ? Perhaps not yet — but their friendly neighborhood standard-bearer certainly has. Spider-Man : Brand New Day opened across China on Wednesday at a pace the market has not seen for a U.S. comic-book movie in at least seven years, earning more than $16.5 million (RMB 112 million) by midday, with local ticketing giant Maoyan projecting a $37.4 million (RMB 254 million) first-day total. No other superhero title has come close to such heights since Spider-Man: Far From Home bowed to $36 million in 2019. Sitting in a distant second is Venom: The Last Dance with $9.4 million earned on its first day on Chinese screens in 2024. Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Review: Tom Holland Bares His Soul in a Superhero Installment That Balances Self-Reflection With Action TV 'Babylon Berlin' Sets Finale Date, Unveils Video Game, Documentary, Audio Spinoffs And Chinese box-office trackers foresee even bigger things for Tom Holland’s latest swing in the spider suit. Maoyan’s full-run forecast, published on the eve of release, pegs the film’s ultimate China total at a whopping $255 million (RMB 1.73 billion), with rival tracker Dengta going higher still at more than $265 million (RMB 1.8 billion). Such projections routinely get revised as a run matures — day-one forecasts especially — but a finish anywhere near that range would rank as Hollywood’s biggest China gross since Avengers: Endgame in 2019, surpassing even Avatar: The Way of Water ‘s $246 million. The Beijing industry has been buzzing all week about Brand New Day ‘s box-office potential. Presales finished at $18.6 million (RMB 126.2 million) — the best of any imported film of the past three summers. The film appears to be benefiting from some pent-up demand for Marvel’s most iconic character. Spider-Man: Far From Home , the last entry to play in Chinese theaters, opened to a strong $98 million over its debut weekend in 2019, finishing at $199 million. That title remains the last U.S. superhero film to clear $100 million in China. Huge sales were expected for its follow-up, the $1.92 billion-grossing Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021), but the film never opened in China after local regulators reportedly balked at the prominence of the Statue of Liberty in the movie’s climax, and Sony declined to cut around it. In the years since, U.S. superhero cinema has fallen out of favor in China even more dramatically than elsewhere. Marvel titles were blocked from the market by regulators from mid-2019 to early 2023, and earnings since the ban have been comparatively withering. Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ($87 million in 2023) and Venom: The Last Dance ($94 million in 2024) stand as the era’s biggest superhero totals, while nearly all other recent entries have limped to sums in the low teens. Chinese audiences, meanwhile, have transferred their enthusiasm to homegrown blockbusters. But Spider-Man has always stood apart, and Sony and Marvel courted the market accordingly. China was given the world’s earliest release date for Brand New Day — Wednesday’s bow comes two days ahead of North America’s — along with an exclusive Imax launch unavailable to fans in the U.S., where large-format screens remain occupied by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . Holland and Zendaya flew to China for last week’s local premiere in Shanghai, where Holland charmed local media with an account of Jackie Chan visiting the film’s London set (the Chinese action icon’s famed stunt team reportedly helped choreograph some of Brand New Day ‘s action sequences). Directed by Shang-Chi ‘s Destin Daniel Cretton, Brand New Day picks up four years after No Way Home , with a forgotten Peter Parker protecting New York alone — and the strain beginning to weigh on him. The film has earned strong reviews from critics , with its Rotten Tomatoes’ score currently hovering around 90 percent. Analysts are projecting a North America opening in the $180 million range for a global launch over $425 million. THR

articles.title: BTS Will Not Be Submitting to 2027 Grammy Awards
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 11:23pm Jung Kook, V, Jin, RM, Suga, Jimin and J-Hope of BTS accept the Artist of the Year award onstage at The 52nd American Music Awards held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on May 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Rich Polk/Dick Clark Productions/Getty Images Global powerhouse BTS has announced that they will not be submitting for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards. The seven-member K-pop group announced their decision in a coordinated Instagram story Wednesday local Korean time. “We have decided not to submit to the Grammys this year,” a translation of the message reads. “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the message continues. “Thank you to ARMY and everyone who is always with us.” Related Stories Music Hunting a Myth in the Wisconsin Woods Music Gabe Simon on Working With Noah Kahan to Craft 'The Great Divide' BTS’ decision comes just a little over a month after the introduction of a new category for the 2027 Grammy Awards, the Asian pop music performance category. The addition has received mixed reactions in K-pop spaces online, but BTS is the first artist to announce they’re going to sit out of the awards. The group members’ choice to specify both region and language is relevant, as the category specifics that the songs entered music include “meaningful use” of any Asian language. BTS, in the midst a banner comeback year, was an obvious frontrunner for the new category and have been nominated in other Grammy categories in years past. The Recording Academy’s description of the new award reads, “This category recognizes artistic excellence in Asian pop music performances originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop, with meaningful use of one or more Asian languages. Awards are presented to the performing artist(s).” All seven members returned to the trailblazing boy group and to group activties last year following their mandatory military enlistment in their home country of South Korea, working on their first new album in years. They released that album, Arirang , in March, which debuted No. 1 on the Billboard 200 while their lead single “Swim” landed at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The Recording Academy hasn’t issued a statement, though The Hollywood Reporter has reached out for comment. THR

articles.title: Banijay Entertainment First-Half Revenue Drops 2 Percent in First Post-All3Media Deal Update
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 28, 2026 11:43pm Harry Kane #9 of England competes for the ball against Brian Gutierrez #26 of Mexico during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 match between Mexico and England at Mexico City Stadium on July 05, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. Richard Pelham/Getty Images In its first financial update since the close of its mega-combination with All3Media ( The Traitors , Squid Game: The Challenge ), production giant Banijay Entertainment ( Peaky Blinders , Black Mirror , Big Brother , Survivor , MasterChef ) posted a first-half revenue decline of 2.2 percent to €1.37 billion ($1.56 billion) amid reduced production volume. The latest results do not yet include the performance of All3Media , whose financials will be part of the results from the second half of this year. Banijay Entertainment’s production revenue dropped 11.9 percent, with the company citing “anticipated phasing in production,” while distribution revenue rose 10.5 percent, “fueled in particular by a format sale in the first quarter.” The company didn’t disclose which format that was. It emphasized, though, that “content production and distribution revenue is expected to normalize by year-end.” Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swings to China's Biggest Superhero Opening in Seven Years TV 'Babylon Berlin' Sets Finale Date, Unveils Video Game, Documentary, Audio Spinoffs Banijay Entertainment is part of Banijay Group, which reports its results grouped together with the company’s live events business. The latter recorded a 49.8 percent revenue increase in the first half, driven by the Winter Olympics and the FIFA World Cup. “The FIFA World Cup generated unprecedented player acquisition and engagement, supported double-digit pro forma revenue growth and strengthened our ability to grow across all products,” the company said. “In Entertainment & Live, record live activity and continued momentum across our content portfolio in distribution partly offset the anticipated phasing of content production, demonstrating the strength and diversification of our business model.” François Riahi, CEO of Banijay Group, touted the latest results. “2026 is definitely a transformational year for Banijay Group,” he said, citing “the completion of the combination of Banijay Entertainment and All3Media,” along with other deals. They “grant the group more scale, more diversity in terms of geography, channels of distribution, and a better strategic positioning to achieve all its strategic goals, creating new opportunities for both growth and value creation.” And he noted: “In the second half, we will enhance the integration processes in our two business units and will start delivering synergies.” THR

articles.title: ‘As Light as Air’ Is a Hypnotic Experimental Doc About Collective Ecstasy in a City in Pakistan (Locarno Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 28, 2026 11:59pm 'As Light as Air' Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival As Light as Air is the title of Pakistani filmmaker Umair Bilal’s feature debut, which will world premiere on Aug. 11 in the Critics’ Weeks lineup of the 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland. But things are not only light but also hypnotic in the cinematic world that the experimental documentary invites people into. After all, it dives into spiritual life in Sehwan, Pakistan, a Sufi city “shaped by pilgrimage, folklore and collective ecstasy,” as the press notes highlight. Sufism is the major expression of mysticism in Islam. Related Stories Business FIFA Faces Revolt Over $20B World Cup Sell Off Plan Movies 'Bloody Tennis,' Tunisian Horror and a Surgeon With Kleptomania: Quirky Films at Locarno “Every day, pilgrims, wanderers, and seekers arrive in a Sufi town carrying grief, hope, and longing,” reads a synopsis on the festival’s website. “Drawn together by music and devotion, they surrender themselves to a shared state of trance.” Bilai also produced the film and handled cinematography together with Konstantin Stell. The editor is Siddhant Sarin, while Sui Sofie Heinz and YANT are responsible for the music. “My connection to the city of Sehwan is personal. My mother followed Sufism and took me to shrines when I was a child, so returning years later carried a distant sense of familiarity,” Bilai shares in a director’s statement. “I was drawn to such places, where people gather to experience states that feel transcendental. In a world that can feel increasingly suffocating, these spaces offer something close to sanctuary, a temporary release from the weight of everyday life.” When he first arrived to film, he approached Sehwan as “an observer, trying to understand the repetitive patterns and rituals that have been followed for centuries,” the filmmaker highlights. “But the space of spirituality felt beyond rationality. By spending long hours with the inhabitants of Sehwan, and allowing myself to move at the town’s own rhythm, I began to let go of that need to understand everything, and instead let myself feel the space. The more I surrendered, the more it revealed itself. Gradually, I became part of its rhythm.” THR can now reveal the trailer for the film. Watch it below to get a first sense of that meditative and trance-like quality of As Light as Air . THR

articles.title: Jared Leto Accused of Sexual Misconduct by Four Women in New BBC Doc
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman , Lily Ford July 29, 2026 1:45am Jared Leto photographed at the 'Tron: Ares' Berlin premiere in 2025. Courtesy of Getty Jared Leto faces new sexual misconduct accusations from multiple women, with some of the allegations occurring when the women were teenagers. On Wednesday, the BBC revealed that in total 10 women have come forward with allegations against the Oscar-winning actor and frontman of rock band Thirty Seconds to Mars as part of a new BBC documentary titled Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret. Four of the women have accused Leto of criminal sexual conduct, all occurring when they were teenagers, according to the BBC. The allegations against the 54-year-old stem from incidents between 2002 and 2016. Related Stories TV Bill Nighy, Gemma Arterton, Nell Tiger Free Set for PBS, BBC Adaptation of 'The Portrait of a Lady' General News Donald Trump Drops Part of His $10 Billion Defamation Lawsuit Against the BBC In the BBC report, one of the women claims she was sexually assaulted by Leto in a motel bathroom when she was 17. A second woman says Leto threatened her with sexual assault when she was 19, after being “unexpectedly” left alone with him in a hotel. The third woman reveals she had sex with Leto when she was 17 in California, in a state where she would have been underage and the act classified as statutory rape. This same woman also claims she had a conversation with the actor about her age and he “shrugged off” concerns about California’s age of consent. The fourth woman claims she groomed by Leto, saying he “abused his celebrity status by making repeated sexually explicit phone calls to her when she was 16.” She adds that on at least one occasion, Leto suggested they should have sex. This fourth woman also alleges that she was subsequently sent a non-disclosure agreement to prevent her from talking about her relationship with Leto, but that she refused to sign it. The BBC says it has seen the NDA. A fifth woman claims that when she was 14, Leto had made a lewd comment about her chest during an autograph-signing event and then instructed a security guard to take her backstage at a music festival. The woman claims her mother confronted Leto at the time, but the actor repeated the lewd comment. An additional four women claim they received calls from Leto when they were younger that were “strange and often very sexual.” The BBC says it has “corroborated” a number of the women’s accounts with friends and family who were told about the encounters with Leto at the time. In some cases, the British broadcaster states, reporters have also seen pictures and messages that support the claims. Two men who worked with Leto’s band told the documentary staff were “uncomfortable” about the way Leto would interact with teenage girls. They say he would sometimes invite them backstage to his dressing room or invite them to the house where he was recording. “I think everyone thought the age gap was way too big,” one of the men, unnamed in the BBC report, says. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to Jared Leto’s reps for comment on the investigation, but had yet to hear back when this story was published. Sexual misconduct allegations have long dogged the Dallas Buyers Club and Tron star. In June 2025 , Leto‘s reps denied that the actor engaged in sexual misconduct or inappropriate relationships with women after an Air Mail exposé. That investigative report contained interviews with nine women, the majority of whom are anonymous. They alleged that Leto behaved inappropriately with them, and some say they were underage at the time they came in contact with the actor. The Air Mail piece also published a viral Twitter post shared by actor Dylan Sprouse in 2018. It reads: “Yo Jared Leto, now that you’ve slid into the DMs of every female model aged 18-25, what would you say your success rate is?” Filmmaker and DC chief James Gunn replied: “He starts at 18 on the internet?” THR

articles.title: ‘Bloody Tennis,’ Tunisian Horror and a Surgeon With Kleptomania: Quirky Films at Locarno
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 29, 2026 2:00am 'Bloody Tennis' Courtesy of augenschein Filmproduktion The Locarno Film Festival , whose 79th edition takes place Aug. 5-15, always features world premieres from around the world by established and up-and-coming auteurs, new hidden gems and cinematic discoveries, along with highlights from the festival circuit. But audiences can also expect the unexpected. After all, Locarno also features quirky, edgy and offbeat movies just waiting to unspool. So, buckle up for a ride on the wilder and more unorthodox side of the cinematic spectrum as THR presents its look at some of the more unusual-sounding films at Locarno79. Related Stories TV 'Babylon Berlin' Sets Finale Date, Unveils Video Game, Documentary, Audio Spinoffs Movies New Mike Leigh, Pablo Larrain Films in San Sebastian Competition Wandering Trees ( Alberi erranti ) Director: Salvatore Section: International competition ‘Wandering Trees,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Once upon a time in Sardinia. Piero and his son Giuliano lived alone in a farmhouse filled with injured animals that they cared for. But the local notables wanted to drive them out because they lived like vagrants. One day, snow fell, and Piero disappeared, while the animals were killed. So, Giuliano had no choice but to search for his father. On his journey, he met Maddalena, and it was love at first sight. Giuliano’s dreamlike search across a wounded landscape explores the wonder and special experience of childhood, a time in life that provides a possibility of resistance against the violence of the adult world. The filmmaker puts it into magical images – and words. “To tell a love story, you mustn’t be afraid to open up emotionally,” says Mereu, who also wrote the script with Alberto Capitta, in a director’s note. “But to embark on a fairy tale, you need to risk something. When you accept its rules, you have to accept everything – even the unthinkable.” Objet A Director: Ann Oren Section: International competition ‘Object A’ Courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films Ready for a bold, playful and stylized excursion into fragile relationships between humans as well as humans and nature, intimacy, desire, identity – and kleptomania – that uses the body as the core of its cinematic language? Well, Objet A is ready to bend your mind and leave you unsettled! “Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons bound by love, control and irresistible fixations,” teases a synopsis. But there is more: “She is compelled to steal objects; he longs to become one. When an accident brings the enigmatic Gaia into their lives, unexpected desires begin to take shape, unsettling the careful balance that has long defined their relationship.” Berlin-based visual artist and filmmaker Ann Oren ( Piaffe ) returns to Locarno to serve up a film, which she wrote with Geoffroy Grison, that features cinematography by Juan Sarmiento G. ( The Voice of Hind Rajab , A Poet ) and editing by Hansjörg Weißbrich ( Rose , Late Shift ). It stars Aenne Schwarz ( All Is Well , Every You Every Me ) as Ingeborg, Louis Hofmann ( All the Light We Cannot See , The Forger , Dark ), and Simone Bucio ( Piaffe , The Ivy ) as Gaia. “I’m interested in human desire and how it connects us to other species,” Oren says in a director’s note. “The human body is the starting point for my cinematic language: the more control we have over it, the more we separate ourselves from the natural world.” Bloody Tennis Director: Nikias Chryssos Section: Out of competition ‘Bloody Tennis,’ courtesy of augenschein Filmproduktion The world of elite sports is taken to disturbing new heights full of brutality and painful ambition in the new film from Nikias Chryssos ( The Bunker , Rave On , A Pure Place ). “Sophie joins a prestigious tennis academy where the brutality of competitive sports is taken to its extreme, and only the hungriest survive,” warns a synopsis. Sandra Guldberg Kampp ( Assassin’s Creed , Electric Child ), Helena Zengel ( News of the World , The Legend of Ochi , System Crasher ) and others star in the movie, along with Elina Löwensohn ( Schindler’s List ), and Zlatko Burić ( Triangle of Sadness ), with an original score by Jim Williams ( Titane , Raw ). If that’s not enough for you yet, the press notes also promise, or should that be: threaten, “blood-sucking leeches, hard-hitting serves and delicious nightmares.” Game on! Bakma Abdelhamid Bouchnak Section: Out of competition ‘Bakma,’ courtesy of Chams Ghorab You have surely never seen Tunisia like this. And you likely haven’t seen a film from Tunisia like this before. What Bouchnak unleashes onto Locarno screens is an urban horror thriller, which he also wrote and edited, with cinematography by Chams Ghorab. Animalistic violence takes on a different meaning in this movie. Commissioner Ali and Khaled investigate the ritualistic murder of a young woman. So far, so horrible. But there is more, as a synopsis highlights: “Her limbs have been severed, her head is missing, and in its place, the killer has grotesquely sewn the head of a dog.” Locarno artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro, in unveiling this year’s festival lineup, highlighted said about Bakma : “It’s a film that, in a very specific way, addresses the political corruption in Tunis at the moment. It’s also a very bitter commentary on what’s left of the so-called Arab Spring that ignited the overthrow of some regimes – and, as you’ll remember, it originated in Tunis.” Tomorrow a Long Time Ago ( Morgen vor langer Zeit ) Director: Luise Donschen Section: Filmmakers of the Present Competition Not much dialogue is used, or needed, in the new film from Donschen ( Casanovagen ), which stars Gerti Drassl and Manuela Biedermann and others. After all, life and actions say more than words. Amid German reunification in 1990, the 50-year-old Patty first loses her job and then her friend Jelena. “In a small East German town, she collects discarded objects and meets the younger Franz,” teases a synopsis. “When her flat becomes so full of belongings that she can no longer enter it, she sets out into a colorful forest. A journey through landscapes and history begins, carrying away more than just her.” The movie has a personal dimension for the filmmaker who grew up in the GDR. “Inspired by my childhood experience of German reunification, the film captures the moment when the present splits into ‘before’ and ‘after’,” the moment when everything seems completely unseen and very familiar at the same time.” Donkey Princess ( Princesa Burro ) Directors: Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña Section: International competition ‘Donkey Princess’ Courtesy of Benjamin Echazarreta Once upon a time… wait a second, isn’t that how we started this journey into the mind- and genre-bending films at Locarno79!? But wait, this one is different, although love plays a key role again. Diana is the princess of an ancient kingdom. Her father, King Arthur, has forbidden love. So, when Diana falls in love with Lalo, the King banishes him. A synopsis teases where things go from here: “Using a magical bracelet, Diana travels to other worlds in search of her love. Discovering that her father manipulates her decisions, she must face her fears and change her destiny.” The travels of the protagonist allow the director duo to play with the look and feel of the places she visits. “Diana travels through parallel worlds where each universe transforms the film’s genre,” León and Cociña explain. “The film brings this constant mutation of realities into live action, where fantasy reshapes everything.” So, who’s ready for a cinematic trip!? THR

articles.title: FIFA Faces Revolt Over $20B World Cup Sell Off Plan
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 29, 2026 2:01am FIFA President Gianni Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump at the final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Alex Livesey - Danehouse/Getty Images World soccer governing body FIFA and its controversial CEO Gianni Infantino are under fire over plans to sell off a stake in FIFA’s commercial operations to private equity investors. The plan would see FIFA set up a new entity, called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), that would bundle all the money-making operations associated with the soccer World Cup — including broadcast rights, sponsorship, ticket sales and licensing fees — and sell a significant stake in the new operation to private investors. FIFA is valuing the new commercial venture at around $20 billion. Related Stories Movies 'As Light as Air' Is a Hypnotic Experimental Doc About Collective Ecstasy in a City in Pakistan (Locarno Trailer) Business Banijay Entertainment First-Half Revenue Drops 2 Percent in First Post-All3Media Deal Update After news of the plan broke on Tuesday, FIFA confirmed it is working with U.S. investment bank JP Morgan to set up the new entity. Thrive Capital, an investment company founded by Joshua Kushner, brother of Donald Trump ’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, is leading the search for investors. The backlash was immediate. European soccer governing body UEFA condemned the plan, saying the sport “isn’t FIFA’s to sell.” “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” UEFA said in a statement. “The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.” U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham joined the fray, taking to social media to post that “football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine. The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine. The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never… — Andy Burnham (@andyburnham) July 28, 2026 FIFA says the FFE could raise an additional $10 billion for its member organizations, the 211 national soccer leagues that make up the association. If members approve the plan, FIFA said it could more than double funding to its member associations from $8 million to $20 million a year, a huge sum for the majority of FIFA members. Infantino defended the plan as a way to spread the wealth generated by the World Cup globally. “This is about the democratization of football worldwide,” he said in a statement. Others see a money grab. FIFA and Infantino have been sharply criticized for the commercialization of the recent World Cup , held in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. FIFA expanded the event from 32 to 48 teams, greatly increasing the number of games, allowed a pricey resale market for tickets, and introduced controversial “hydration breaks” which stopped play and allowed for additional advertising during matches. The 2026 tournament was the most lucrative in history, with FIFA expected to announce revenues of more than $15 billion for the event. Given Joshua Kushner’s connection, via his brother, to President Trump, many also see a potential political conflict of interest. Infantino already has close ties to the U.S. President. After Trump complained about not winning the Nobel Peace Prize, Infantino invented the “FIFA Peace Prize” and then awarded it to POTUS in December. UEFA claims FIFA undermined the integrity of this year’s World Cup when it intervened to overturn a red card given to USA striker Falorin Balogun after Trump called and asked Infantino to do so. This week, Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, launched an investigation into Infantino and FIFA’s ties to Trump’s administration and businesses. THR

articles.title: Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds
articles.full_text: Jul 29, 2026 12:00am PT Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration 4 hours ago Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds 4 hours ago How Lan Hongchun’s Teochew Film ‘Dear You’ Turned a Forgotten Postal Tradition Into China’s Unlikely Hit: ‘Dialect Is Never Going to Be a Liability as Long as You Have Great Ideas’ 20 hours ago See All Getty Images The Indian Premier League cricket tournament’s business value has climbed to $20.6 billion, up 11.4% year over year, according to Houlihan Lokey’s 2026 IPL Valuation Study released Wednesday, as record-setting sales of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals reset franchise pricing across the league. The league’s stand-alone brand value rose 10.3% to $4.3 billion, marking a second consecutive year of double-digit growth for both metrics. The report placed the 2026 figures in historical context: the IPL’s business value stood at $15.4 billion in 2023, $16.4 billion in 2024 and $18.5 billion in 2025. On a per-match basis, Houlihan Lokey noted, only the NFL ranks ahead of the IPL globally. Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) The 2026 season’s defining commercial event was the sale of two franchises. Royal Challengers Bengaluru was acquired in March by a consortium including the Aditya Birla Group, the Times of India Group, David Blitzer’s Bolt Ventures and Blackstone’s BXPE for $1.78 billion, the most expensive single IPL franchise transaction on record. The deal, in an all-cash structure, came after seller United Spirits Limited had targeted $2 billion. Rajasthan Royals followed in May, sold to the Mittal family and Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla for $1.65 billion, after an initial agreement with a U.S.-based consortium led by Kal Somani collapsed during exclusivity. Together the two deals total $3.43 billion. Popular on Variety “The most telling development this year did not come from our models; it came from the market. Two franchises changed hands – Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) for $1.78 billion and Rajasthan Royals (RR) for $1.65 billion – and the buyers, from Blackstone and the Aditya Birla Group to ArcelorMittal, the Serum Institute, and the global sports investor David Blitzer, are precisely the caliber of capital we have long argued the league was built to attract,” said Harsh Talikoti, director in Houlihan Lokey’s financial and valuation advisory business. The report found viewership undergoing what it called a platform migration rather than a decline. Total reach across television and digital hit 1.06 billion screens, up 7% year over year, even as linear television ratings fell 18.8% and average per-match viewership on television dropped 26%. Total IPL 2026 revenue projections, including broadcasting rights, sponsorships and ticket sales, exceed $1.8 billion. At the franchise level, RCB topped both the brand value and business value rankings for the first time in league history, its brand worth rising 16% to $312 million on the strength of back-to-back IPL and Women’s Premier League titles. Mumbai Indians ranked second at $264 million despite a ninth-place finish, while Kolkata Knight Riders overtook Chennai Super Kings for the No. 3 brand spot at $245 million. Sunrisers Hyderabad and Rajasthan Royals rounded out the top six, both securing playoff berths, while Lucknow Super Giants finished last on both business and brand value at $122 million following Rishabh Pant’s decision to step down as captain. Satyan Gajwani, co-owner of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and chair of Times Internet, said the franchise’s fan engagement drove the acquisition decision. “RCB’s fanbase intensity and connection are unparalleled, which made this a special opportunity,” Gajwani said. Ness Wadia, co-owner of Punjab Kings and one of the league’s founding investors since 2008, said the IPL remains in its early stages of growth. “I still think the IPL is only getting started,” Wadia said. Beyond the headline transactions, the report examined what it described as the league’s structural appeal to private equity relative to other global sports properties. The BCCI places no cap on private equity ownership of an IPL franchise and imposes no minimum hold period, in contrast with the NFL’s 10% per-fund limit, the NBA’s 20% cap and the Bundesliga’s 50+1 rule limiting outside investors to a 49% economic interest. Each franchise also receives roughly $55 million annually from the BCCI’s centrally negotiated media pool before any team-level revenue is counted, a structure the report likened to a contracted annuity. Non-media revenue such as team sponsorships, gate receipts and international expansion is also growing quickly. Houlihan Lokey said non-media revenues have expanded at a 22% compound annual rate since the pandemic, with several IPL owners acquiring stakes in England’s The Hundred, including Reliance Industries’ purchase of a stake in Oval Invincibles and Sun Group’s acquisition of Northern Superchargers. Houlihan Lokey projected the league’s 2028-32 media rights cycle, currently valued at $6.2 billion, could grow by 80% to 100%, citing an uninterrupted 18% compound annual growth rate in rights value since 2008 and expanding international viewership. That estimate cuts against a separate forecast from Media Partners Asia, which projected in a March report that the 2028–32 cycle would instead hold flat at approximately $5.4 billion, with per-match value declining 13%, from $13.2 million to $11.5 million, as the league’s expanded 94-match format dilutes individual game value. MPA attributed the flattening to the JioStar merger of Viacom18 and Disney Star, which it said removed the competitive tension between bidders that drove the 2022 auction’s near-threefold increase, and warned that rights holders in the current cycle face cumulative losses of $1.8–2 billion. ‘Viva Carmen’ Review: The Visuals Do the Singing in a Ravishing Animated Riff on Bizet’s Opera Asghar Farhadi’s Cannes Film ‘Parallel Tales’ Sells Across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Canada Through Charades (EXCLUSIVE) Cannes Breakout Comedy ‘Jim Queen’ Closes Key Deals Ahead of Annecy Screening (EXCLUSIVE) France’s National Film Board to Reduce Funding for Productions That Fail Gender Equality Targets ‘Lucy Lost’ Review: A Winsome Family Animation With Welcome Narrative Complexity Netflix Calls for Cap on French Content Investment Rules, Warning Current System Is ‘Unsustainable’ Loading comments... articles.title: BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration
articles.full_text: Jul 29, 2026 12:03am PT BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘The King’s Warden’ Leads Korea to Best First Half Box Office Since Pandemic 15 minutes ago BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration 4 hours ago Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds 4 hours ago See All Getty Images BTS will not submit its music for consideration at the 69th Grammy Awards , scheduled for Feb. 7, 2027, the group announced on Wednesday. All seven members – RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jungkook – posted the same statement on their individual instagram accounts. “We have decided not to submit for Grammy consideration this year. We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language. We thank Army and everyone who has always stood by us.” Related Stories Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) Former ‘This Morning’ Host Holly Willoughby Heads to YouTube for New Lifestyle Series The announcement lands just over a month after the Recording Academy unveiled a new Best Asian Pop Music Performance category. “This category recognizes artistic excellence in Asian pop music performances originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop, with meaningful use of one or more Asian languages. Awards are presented to the performing artist(s),” the Academy’s description of the category reads. Popular on Variety Variety has reached out to the Recording Academy for comment. BTS has been nominated for Grammys before, including in the Best Pop Duo/Group Performance and Best Music Video categories, but has never won. All seven members have been voting members of the Recording Academy since 2019. Expectations for a first BTS win had been running high heading into next year’s ceremony. The group released its fifth studio album, “ Arirang ,” in March following the completion of the members’ mandatory military service, and the record topped Billboard’s main singles and albums charts, generating significant global response. BTS is currently on “World Tour Arirang,” having just closed out the run’s European dates in Paris. The group followed that with an appearance at the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final Halftime Show on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, performing their 2020 single “Dynamite” during an eleven-minute set shared with Madonna, Shakira and Justin Bieber. No World Cup final had ever staged a halftime show before this one, in the tournament’s 96 years of existence. BTS took the field in custom red outfits designed for the tour, each bearing a member’s name alongside the number seven. The group picks the tour back up on the U.S. side starting Aug. 1, back at the same New Jersey stadium. Goodbye, Stars Hollow. Davies Shows (EXCLUSIVE) 6 days ago See All Variety via Getty Images Jared Leto has been accused of criminal sexual conduct by four women, who claim the offenses occurred when they were teenagers. In a new BBC documentary “Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret” — airing Wednesday — a total of 10 women come forward with allegations against the actor and musician, nine of whom the BBC says are sharing their stories for the first time. One of the women accuses the Oscar winner of assaulting her in a motel bathroom when she was 17. Another claims Leto threatened her with sexual assault when she was 19. A third in the doc describes how she allegedly had sex with Leto in California when she was 17, under the age of consent, which therefore would be classified as statutory rape. She claims the actor “shrugged off” a conversation about the age of consent being 18 in the state. Popular on Variety In the doc, the BBC says that it has seen an NDA that the fourth woman was asked to sign to stop her from discussing her relationship with Leto. She refused to sign the NDA. Four other women accuse Leto of making “strange and often very sexual” phone calls to them when they were younger. All the women that feature in “Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret” claim the interactions occurred between 2002 and 2016, when the actor, now 54, was in his 30s and 40s. DJ Allie Teilz publicly accused Leto of sexual misconduct, alleging he assaulted and traumatized her when she was 17 years old. It prompted others to come forward with similar claims. articles.title: Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50
articles.full_text: Jul 29, 2026 2:52am PT Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50 By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50 1 hour ago Canal+ Group’s Revenue Jumps 40% as MultiChoice Deal Boosts Earnings and Subscriptions 20 hours ago Canal+ Seals Landmark Pact to Invest Nearly $1.1 Billion in French and European Films 2 days ago See All Getty Images Kavinsky , the French electro music producer and DJ whose hypnotic anthem “Nightcall” became a cult classic after opening Nicolas Winding Refn’s 2011 film “ Drive ,” died on Tuesday. He was 50. The artist was found dead at his Paris home on Tuesday evening. Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of his death, though no foul play has been reported. French media said the musician had complained of headaches in the days leading up to his death, according to Reuters . Related Stories YouTube Ad Sales Keep Growing at Healthy Clip, Rising 13% to $11 Billion in Q2 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) While Kavinsky had long been a respected figure on France’s electronic music scene, “Nightcall” transformed him into an international cult favorite. Produced with Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo of Daft Punk and featuring vocals from Lovefoxxx of Brazilian band CSS, the song helped define the film’s aesthetic and became one of the signature electronic tracks of the 2010s. Popular on Variety Kavinsky most recently performed the song alongside Phoenix and Angèle at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games closing ceremony, which was broadcast globally, introducing it to new audiences over a decade after “Drive’s” release. Born Vincent Belorgey in Seine-Saint-Denis in 1975, he came to music relatively late after first working as an actor and appearing in films by longtime friend Quentin Dupieux. Inspired by 1980s action movies, arcade games and sports cars, he developed the fictional persona of Kavinsky, a mysterious, undead driver said to have returned from a fatal Ferrari crash to make electronic music. He emerged in the mid-2000s through the influential French label Record Makers, releasing the EPs “Teddy Boy,” “1986” and “Nightcall” before touring alongside artists including Daft Punk and Justice. His debut album “OutRun,” released in 2013, expanded on the retro-futuristic sound that would become synonymous with the growing synthwave movement. After a long hiatus, he returned with a second album, “Reborn,” in 2022. Although he never achieved the mainstream commercial profile of fellow French electro artists such as Daft Punk or Justice, Kavinsky had a large influence on a generation of producers drawn to nostalgic, cinematic electro music, and helped popularize the synthwave genre well beyond France. articles.title: ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia
articles.full_text: Jul 29, 2026 3:39am PT ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor headline a generic but watchable Prime Video release made slightly more interesting by toxic friendship dynamics among the human bait. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia 35 minutes ago ‘Pinocchio: Unstrung’ Review: Killer Puppetry Is the Best Thing About This Killer Puppet Slasher 3 days ago ‘Bad Counselors’ Review: A Stealthily Christian Comedy Makes Believers of Two Rowdy Frat Bros 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Prime Video “Under Paris,” “Deep Water,” “Thrash,” “Chum” — the shark movies come so thick and fast these days, there’s scarcely any time between them to deem it safe to go back in the water. That said, if this recent run of films is to be believed, regular old beaches are fine these days. Seems the toothy predators are increasingly seeking less obvious locations to graze on wet human flesh: a mid-Pacific plane-crash site, the City of Lights, and now, in “The Devil’s Mouth,” a dark, dank, tight-squeeze cave in idyllic coastal Thailand. This claustrophobic danger zone brings a smidge of novelty to director Jeff Wadlow ‘s aquatic thriller, but the formula is otherwise familiar: five hot young things on vacation, one bull shark very much in business mode, and a pecking order that most viewers can guess five minutes in. Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) It’s odd that the shark movie has lately joined the romantic comedy in the ranks of genres most favored for straight-to-streaming fodder, since its pleasures, from “Jaws” onwards, have traditionally been communal, cinematic ones: From the safety of your sofa, a great white jump scare just doesn’t land in quite the same way. A Prime Video release, “The Devil’s Mouth” sometimes feels ill-suited to the small screen, given the frequently squint-inducing murkiness of its setting; on the other hand, the very lax progression of Aja Gabel and Myung Joh Wesner’s Black List-featured script feels tailored to the requirements of second-screen viewing, with character tensions brewing slowly and repetitively between sporadic feeding frenzies. Popular on Variety If the dialogue and characterization never rise above the pedestrian, however, those tensions do at least bring some malicious rooting interest to the essential survival drama — with a strain of toxic friction evident from the get-go between nice-girl protagonist Sarah ( Kathryn Newton ) and her narcissistic BFF Max ( Lana Condor ), a self-declared “CEO of fun,” on their luxury post-graduation vacation. Both stars are better than their thin roles require them to be, with Condor clearly enjoying an opportunity to spike her wholesome “To All the Boys” star persona a bit; perhaps her young fans will resist how blatantly the film’s sympathies are stacked in Sarah’s favor. Or perhaps not: Sarah has a pretty rough time of it from the start. The unpaired fifth wheel on what is otherwise a lovey-dovey couples’ trip — with Max and mutual college friend Adrienne (Tommi Rose) accompanied by their respective, equally bland boyfriends James (Nico Hiraga) and Greg (Gavin Casalegno) — Sarah is quite literally an afterthought when, at the end of a day’s yacht hire in a picturesque cove, the other four set sail while she’s still in the water, leaving her at the mercy of a smack of jellyfish. Cue an initial sea-creature attack less bloody than those to come, but perhaps the film’s most eerily and alarmingly constructed setpiece. A cursory apology from Max (“I’m trying to be accountable here,” she says, unconvincingly) doesn’t quite smooth the waters between the two by the time of the group’s next adventure: a remote coastal cave-swimming expedition led by local guide Wat (“The White Lotus” star Tayme Thapthimthong). A cautionary-tale tone soon sets in as the entitled Americans, led by Max, repeatedly overrule Wat’s native expertise. (The safer cave route he recommends is marked on the map in green; the one they choose is marked in red. How many more flags do you need?) You can hardly blame him for leaving them to their fate when, several caves in, ravaged remains float to the surface, followed in short order by the dreaded fin slicing through the water. How did the beast find its way into these cramped quarters? “I don’t think this is something we need to figure out right now,” says one of the guys, and fair enough, even if that rather lets the screenwriters off the hook. A more immediate priority is navigating a route out of this cave network, with the shark, given limited room to roam, tailing them at every turn. Needless to say, not everyone’s going to make it out alive. The panic-inducing narrowness of the potential escape routes make a change from the genre’s usual spatial dynamics, with Wadlow — recycling some of the atmospherics from his 2020 “Fantasy Island” film, minus the fantasy — and DP James Kniest exploiting those most effectively in a couple of extended, suitably suffocating underwater setpieces. It’s the shark’s appearances, surprisingly, that lack bite. Denied a point of view or much in the way of a closeup, the CG killer never feels a particularly distinctive or palpable presence, while its lunges take on a fairly predictable pattern. The gore, meanwhile, is unexpectedly discreet, which is a strange place for the film to exercise subtlety: A washed-up sea turtle with a cartoon-style bite taken out of it is the most visceral sight here, and the most saddening. The human bait, on the other hand? Have your fill, buddy. ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia Reviewed online, July 28, 2026. Running time: 104 MIN. Production: A Prime Video release of an Amazon MGM Studios presentation in association with Lionsgate of a Thunder Road Films production. Producers: Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, Jeff Wadlow. Executive producers: Carsten H.W. Lorenz, Will Flynn, Sam Greenberg. Crew: Director: Jeff Wadlow. Screenplay: Aja Gabel, Myung Joh Wesner. Camera: James Kniest. Editor: Sean Albertson. Music: Bear McCreary. With: Kathryn Newton, Lana Condor, Gavin Casalegno, Nico Hiraga, Tommi Rose, Tayme Thapthimthong. Goodbye, Stars Hollow. articles.title: ‘The King’s Warden’ Leads Korea to Best First Half Box Office Since Pandemic
articles.full_text: Jul 29, 2026 3:57am PT ‘The King’s Warden’ Leads Korea to Best First Half Box Office Since Pandemic By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration 4 hours ago Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds 4 hours ago How Lan Hongchun’s Teochew Film ‘Dear You’ Turned a Forgotten Postal Tradition Into China’s Unlikely Hit: ‘Dialect Is Never Going to Be a Liability as Long as You Have Great Ideas’ 20 hours ago See All BA Entertainment Local films drove Korean box office recovery in the first half of 2026, with total industry revenue reaching KRW579 billion ($399.1 million) on 57.05 million admissions, up 41.9% and 34.2% year-on-year, respectively, according to figures released by the Korean Film Council (KOFIC). Local titles accounted for the bulk of that growth. Korean-film revenue totaled KRW370.2 billion ($255.2 million) from 37.37 million admissions, an increase of 81.7% and 74.9% year-on-year. It is the strongest first-half showing for local cinema since the pandemic, with revenue now equivalent to 94.2% of the pre-pandemic first-half average calculated across 2017 to 2019. Related Stories Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) Content Creators vs. Emmys: Dropout Shut Out Again, 'Subway Takes' Lands First Nomination International films generated KRW208.8 billion ($143.9 million) in revenue from 19.68 million admissions in the same period. Admissions dropped 6.9% year-on-year, but revenue still rose 2.3%, a gain the council attributed to heavy premium-format ticket sales for titles including “ Project Hail Mary ” and “ Avatar: Fire and Ash .” Premium-format screenings made up 30.2% of total revenue for “Project Hail Mary” and 49.9% for “Avatar: Fire and Ash.” Popular on Variety “The King’s Warden” led all releases for the half, pulling in KRW163.1 billion ($112.4 million) from 16.91 million admissions to become the highest-grossing Korean film ever released. “ Colony ” ranked second with KRW60.5 billion ($41.7 million) from 5.74 million admissions, while “Salmokji: Whispering Water” placed third on KRW33.3 billion ($23 million) from 3.24 million admissions, giving Korean titles a clean sweep of the top three releases. KOFIC noted that strong results this half came not only from period dramas and action blockbusters but also from mid- and small-budget romance and horror titles, pointing to a wider range of genres and scales among successful local releases. Premium-format screenings continued their growth streak, generating KRW45.7 billion ($31.5 million) in revenue for the first half, up 56.3% year-on-year and accounting for 7.9% of total revenue. The council said the trend has climbed steadily since the pandemic as theaters lean on premium formats to differentiate their offerings. The average ticket price for the first half rose KRW551 (¢38) year-on-year to KRW10,150 ($7), reflecting both that shift toward premium formats and higher ticket prices more generally. Showbox Corp. led the distributor rankings, capturing a 48.6% revenue share worth KRW281.4 billion ($194 million) after distributing four releases – “The King’s Warden,” “Colony,” “Salmokji: Whispering Water” and “Once We Were Us” – that all performed well. The Walt Disney Company Korea placed second, taking a 13.8% share worth KRW43.1 billion ($29.7 million) across nine titles that included “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” “Toy Story 5” and “The Devil Wears Prada.” In the independent and arthouse segment, “Backrooms” led the category, taking in KRW12.4 billion ($8.5 million) from 1.16 million admissions. “Ran 12.3” placed second, with “My Name” rounding out the top three. articles.title: Banijay Entertainment H1 Revenues Dip Slightly In First Earnings Update Since All3Media Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm Banijay Entertainment H1 Revenues Dip Slightly In First Earnings Update Since All3Media Deal ‘Blast’ & ‘Idhayam Murali’ Actress Preity Mukhundhan Lands IMDb Breakout Star Award View All July 28, 2026 11:19pm 'MasterChef' and 'The Traitors' now part of the same group at Banijay Entertainment Fox/BBC Banijay Entertainment’s first financials since its merger with All3Media showed half-year revenues down slightly at €1.37 billion ($1.56 billion), as production volume fell. Sales at the independent European production giant were down 2.2% on the same six months in 2025, which reflected “anticipated phasing in production and distribution.” The numbers do not include All3, whose financials will be included in quarterly reports from Q3. Banijay’s production revenue fell 11.9%, while distribution was up 10.5% “fuelled in particular by a format sale in the first quarter.” Banijay is anticipating numbers to tick up in the second half of the year, with Q4 earmarked for significant activity. Related Stories News Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa's MultiChoice News Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Banijay Group groups Banijay Entertainment with its live events business, which saw its revenues zoom up nearly 50% on the back of the Winter Olympic Games and the FIFA World Cup. Watch on Deadline Earlier this month, Banijay merged its entertainment arm with RedBird IMI’s All3Media, creating an $8B revenue giant that Banijay Entertainment Chair Jeff Zucker claims is the largest indie producer ever created. The combined group owns the likes of MasterChef , Big Brother , The Traitors , Peaky Blinders , Midsomer Murders and Gogglebox , and has a library of more than 265,000 hours. Banijay Group received €801M from the deal, including a payment of €625M from RedBird IMI and a €176M pre-closing dividend. The agreement meant Banijay and RedBird IMI have an equal split of the new Banijay Entertainment, which is led by Marco Bassetti as CEO, Jane Turton, former CEO of All3Media, as Deputy CEO, and Zucker, CEO of RedBird IMI, as chair. Banijay announced today that its shareholders would get an exceptional dividend of €400M following the deal, which works out to €0.93 per share. The plan had first been revealed upon announcement of a deal with All3 back in March. Banijay also noted that a seven-year €750M loan secured last month would go towards refinancing All3’s “outstanding” senior facilities, paying transaction fees and paying “certain” dividends related to the merger. At group level, Banijay posted H1 revenues of €2.58B, up 16.9% year-on-year on a reported basis. Adjusted EBITDA was €502.9M, up 18.5%, though adjusted net income fell 3.7% to €141.5M. The sports betting and gaming unit posted revenues only just behind entertainment, coming in at €1.21B. The unit is currently integrating Tipico, which was acquired in a multi-billion dollar deal in October last year, and is in the process of buying France’s second-largest casino operator, JOA. “2026 is definitely a transformational year for Banijay Group,” said Banijay Group CEO Francois Riahi. “The successful acquisition of Tipico, the completion of the combination of Banijay Entertainment and All3Media, and the proposed acquisition of JOA in France grant to the group more scale, more diversity in terms of geography, channels of distribution, and a better strategic positioning to achieve all its strategic goals, creating new opportunities for both growth and value creation.” Jared Leto Accused Of Criminal Sexual Conduct By Four Women In BBC Documentary ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Huge $465M Global Bow; Review & Red Carpet Pics Ari Emanuel Backs Par-WBD Deal In WSJ Op-Ed, Calls AGs’ Antitrust Suit “Trash” CBS’ Bari Weiss-Led ‘60 Minutes’ Adds Big-Name Correspondents & Contributors Read More About: Comments

The revenue figure, disclosed in accounts filed at the UK’s Companies House, was up 24% on 2024 and smashed the previous record of £26.7M in 2018. Agatha Christie Limited generated a pre-tax profit of £20M last year, up form £13.7M in 2024, according to the earnings. James Prichard, the CEO of Agatha Christie Limited, declined to comment. articles.title: Michelle Yeoh EP’d Martial Arts Picture ‘Nak Muay’ Co-Starring Suablack, Buakaw & Saenchai To Begin Filming In Thailand On August 2
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Kavinsky Dies: French DJ Whose ‘Nightcall’ Track Opened Nicolas Winding Refn’s ‘Drive’ Was 50 Michelle Yeoh EP’d Martial Arts Picture ‘Nak Muay’ Co-Starring Suablack, Buakaw & Saenchai To Begin Filming In Thailand On August 2 Georgia Native Danny McBride To Be Honored With Rome Int’l Film Fest’s Flannery O’Connor Award View All July 29, 2026 1:03am Nak Muay Disruptive Element Films EXCLUSIVE: Tinge Krishnan’s Michelle Yeoh EP’d action picture Nak Muay – starring Muay Thai boxing stars Suablack, Buakaw and Saenchai – will begin shooting in Thailand next week. Disruptive Element Films – Krishnan’s UK and Thailand-based joint company with Colin Pons – has announced an August 2 start for principal photography, with filming due to take place on location in Bangkok and the rural district of Pranburi. It is the third feature for medic-turned director Krishnan, who broke out with Bafta-winning short Showscan , and has since taken directing credits on TV shows such as A Thousand Blows , The Mosquito Coast , Industry , WeCrashed as well as features Been So Long and Junkhearts . Related Stories News Deadline From Local To Global: Producers Of 'Gohan', '9 Temples To Heaven' & More Discuss How Thai Cinema Is Travelling News 'Death Whisperer' Star Mim Rattanawadee Wongthong Joins Cast Of Fearfolks' 'Cher' Tapping into the culture and world of Thailand’s traditional martial art and national sport Muay Thai, the film co-stars Buakaw as Magic Lotus, a revered fighter with a legendary deadly touch in the ring, alongside Saenchai as Tongchai, Magic Lotus’ longtime friend and partner in crime, who hides his fighting skill behind the persona of a buffoonish farmer. Watch on Deadline When Magic Lotus becomes secretly depressed after another death in the ring at his hands, Tongchai supports his exile into nature from the boxing world. Together they reignite their passion for Muay Thai when they decide to train young fighter Yod, played by Sua Black (aka Natthaphum Kaeowatthanameth). Yod is also hiding a secret. As Thailand’s undefeated Muay Thai champion, he is a national icon, the face of global brands, and a fixture in Bangkok’s elite circles. But behind the flashbulbs and footwork, he’s cracking under the weight of guilt. Years ago, a brutal match left his childhood best friend Krit with irreversible brain damage. Now Krit is dying, and Yod is spiralling. “As a director with roots in sci-fi, fantasy, and martial arts, this film is the chance to make the film I’ve always wanted to make as a woman and a martial arts practitioner,” said Krishnan, who also takes writer and executive producer credits on the production. “ Nak Muay wrestles with that desire, centring on Yod. His transformative relationship with the strong women around him is interwoven with his journey as a Muay Thai fighter grappling with his craft’s meaning and his own moral compass after a devastating breakdown.” The film is produced by BAFTA award-winning Dominic Buchanan ( Gimme the Loot, The End of the F***ing World ) with four-time Emmy award winning consultant producer Scott Hornbacher ( Boots , Mad Men, The Sopranos ). Cinematography will be by Gavin Kelly ( American Horror Story ). Yeoh ( Everything Everywhere All At Once , Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon ) is also on board as an executive producer alongside Pons, Krishnan and David Ismalone. The film is being shot and produced entirely in Thailand with support from the Thai government and the UK Global Screen Fund. articles.title: Jared Leto Accused Of Criminal Sexual Conduct By Four Women In BBC Documentary
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations Benedict Cumberbatch Says Paramount-Warner Deal Is A “Calamity” That Must Be Blocked ‘The Deb’ Star Charlotte MacInnes Attacks Rebel Wilson In Appeal Against Court Defeat View All July 29, 2026 1:46am Jared Leto attends the 'Tron: Ares' premiere in 2025 Getty Jared Leto , the Oscar-winning star of Dallas Buyers Club and Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman, has been accused of unlawful sexual conduct by four women. The BBC has released a new documentary, titled Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret , in which 10 women detailed their encounters with Leto between 2002 and 2016. Nine of the women were publicly recounting their experiences for the first time. Leto’s representatives have been contacted by Deadline for comment. The Suicide Squad actor, now aged 54, did not respond to the BBC’s requests for comment. He has previously denied sexual impropriety following a 2025 report by Air Mail , the media outlet founded by former Vanity Fair editor Graydon Carter. Related Stories News Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations News Netflix Now First Port Of Call For UK Audiences Over BBC - Ofcom Media Nations Isabel, a pseudonym used by the BBC, alleged that she was sexually assaulted by Leto in a Las Vegas motel bathroom in 2002, when she was 17. Isabel accused Leto, who was in his 30s, of grabbing her hand and using it to masturbate himself while he was in the shower. Watch on Deadline “Alarms started going off in my head,” she said. “In that moment, I definitely realized I was not in a great situation.” Visibly emotional in the BBC documentary, she remembered recoiling and leaving the room. Alex, a second woman, accused Leto of making a sexual threat after attending a Thirty Seconds to Mars concert at London’s O2 Arena in 2013. She was 19 at the time and recalled being encouraged to attend an after-party, but claimed she walked into a dark hotel room containing just Leto. Alex felt unsafe, suggested she sleep on the chaise longue in the room, before Leto allegedly told her that she would wake up “with a dick in her ass.” Alex said she left the room and later texted a friend about her experience. “He was threatening sexual assault, you should report him,” her friend replied. A third woman, identified as Clara in the BBC documentary, described how in 2006 she had sex with the actor at his home in California when she was 17, which would be classified as statutory rape in the state. Leto was aged 34 at the time. Clara recalled having a conversation about the age of consent, but claimed Leto “kind of shrugged it off, like it wasn’t a huge concern for him.” A fourth woman alleged that she received sexual phone calls from Leto when she was aged 16 after meeting the Requiem for a Dream star at a Los Angeles modelling agency in 2014. Identified as Etta by the BBC, the woman said she was later asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement by Leto. She refused but showed the relevant document to the BBC. Allegations about Leto first emerged last year when LA DJ Allie Teilz posted on Instagram saying she had been assaulted by the actor when she was 17. The post was a screenshot of a Facebook status update she published in 2012, in which she said: “Youre [sic] not really in LA until Jared Leto tries to force himself on you backstage at an M83 show.. In a Kilt.. And a snow hat.” The post prompted a flurry of replies from other women, who alleged that they had similar experiences. This led to Air Mail’s report last year, in which nine women accused Leto of engaging in inappropriate behavior. At the time, Leto’s rep “expressly denied” the women’s accusations, including Teilz’s, which was said to be “demonstrably false.” Leto is repped by WME. He most recently featured in Masters of the Universe as Skeletor. Upcoming projects include Soviet spacecraft story Lunik Heist for Disney-owned Searchlight Pictures.
