articles.title: FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm Banijay Entertainment H1 Revenues Dip Slightly In First Earnings Update Since All3Media Deal ‘Blast’ & ‘Idhayam Murali’ Actress Preity Mukhundhan Lands IMDb Breakout Star Award View All July 29, 2026 2:18am UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, President Donald Trump and FIFA boss Gianni Infantino Getty Controversial plans to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup to private investors have sparked a furious response from football authorities and politicians. UEFA , the body that governs European football, took the unprecedented step of releasing a statement condemning FIFA’s plan, which involves creating a new entity that would house the commercial rights to its men’s and women’s tournaments. The World Cup “is not FIFA’s to sell,” said UEFA. JP Morgan Chase, the bank that financed the failed breakaway European Super League in 2021, is working with FIFA to create the business, which is being valued at around $20B, per various reports. Though the World Cup is not a commercial enterprise, the formation of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) would allow it to be exploited by private investors. Related Stories News Noah Kahan Calls Out Donald Trump's Administration For Using "American Cars" Song In White House Social Media Post News Judge Says Donald Trump Can Amend Complaint In Defamation Lawsuit Against The New York Times FIFA confirmed the plan to create FFE and said it would be the controlling shareholder, but the controversial governing body hopes to raise $4.2B by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.” Watch on Deadline Thrive Capital, an investment firm led by Joshua Kusher, the brother of President Donald Trump ‘s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, has been approached about investing, it is reported. We have contacted Thrive for comment. Investigations in the Financial Times and The Times newspapers first revealed the FFE plan, which comes on the back of the recent World Cup. New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among notable names slamming FFE, writing that the World Cup is “not a product, and that “once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Even Sepp Blatter, the disgraced predecessor of FIFA President Gianni Infantino , wrote on social media: “The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football. No one has the right to sell our game.” Under-fire FIFA President Infantino stands to personally make millions from the deal by becoming its commissioner after his expected third term at football’s governing body expires in 2031, the Times reported. We have contacted FIFA for comment. Infantino said FFE would see “the commercial side of the game [operate] as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world,” with FIFA claiming more than $10B would be redistributed back to its 211 member associations following the deals. The recent World Cup in the U.S., Canada and Mexico was heavily criticized in some quarters for the implementation of mandatory drinks breaks, which effectively divided matches into quarters rather than the traditional halves, for Trump’s intervention into the suspension of USMNT player Folarin Balogun and the extended half-time break in the final to allow for musical performances. UEFA President Aleksander Čeferin boycotted the final in response to the various issues. FIFA made record revenues from the tournament, which it has touted publicly. Critics say finances are being put before the best interests of the game. UEFA considers World Cup boycott It has been reported today that UEFA members are meeting to discuss their response to FIFA’s plan, with a boycott of the World Cup one serious option on the table. While UEFA cannot stop it moving ahead, it is the strongest continental body in football with many of the world’s top international teams hailing from the continent. Of the eight quarter finalists at the World Cup, six were UEFA members, and Spain won the tournament. There were similar statistics in the 2018 and 2022 tournaments, and a World Cup without European participation would be a huge commercial and political hit to FIFA. The next World Cup is due to be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with other games held in South America. In its statement in response to FFE, UEFA said: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.” European dominance of world football has been a sore point for many years, and the Swiss-born Infantino has consolidated his power base by redirecting more funding and support to Africa, the Americas and Asia. It is expected that FFE would need to be ratified by a majority of FIFA members, though there’s no word on when or how the vote will take shape. articles.title: Kavinsky Dies: French DJ Whose ‘Nightcall’ Track Opened Nicolas Winding Refn’s ‘Drive’ Was 50
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Kavinsky Dies: French DJ Whose ‘Nightcall’ Track Opened Nicolas Winding Refn’s ‘Drive’ Was 50 Michelle Yeoh EP’d Martial Arts Picture ‘Nak Muay’ Co-Starring Suablack, Buakaw & Saenchai To Begin Filming In Thailand On August 2 Georgia Native Danny McBride To Be Honored With Rome Int’l Film Fest’s Flannery O’Connor Award View All July 29, 2026 2:22am Kavinsky performs during the closing ceremony of Paris 2024 Summer Paralympic Games Michael Reaves/Getty Images French DJ Kavinsky , who was best known internationally for his ‘ Nightcall ’ track which opened Nicolas Winding Refn ’s 2011 film Drive , has died at the age of 50. French media reported that the music artist, producer and DJ was found dead at his home in Paris on Tuesday evening (July 28). The Paris Prosecutors Office said in a statement said that an investigation had been opened into the cause of his death, noting that “first responders found no suspicious elements at the scene”. Born Vincent Belorgey in Paris on July 31, 1975, Kavinsky was a key figure in the French Touch electro music scene alongside the likes of Daft Punk. Related Stories News 'The Odyssey' Scores $21M+ Record Tuesday For Christopher Nolan; 2nd U.S. Weekend Could Top 'Dark Knight' Pics - Box Office News Charles Gaines Dies: 'Pumping Iron' Author Who Helped Launch Arnold Schwarzenegger Was 84 He achieved worldwide fame with his 2010 ‘Nightcall’ track after Winding Refn used it for his 2011 film Drive starring Ryan Gosling opposite Carey Mulligan as a Hollywood stunt driver moonlighting as a getaway driver. Watch on Deadline Kavinsky had released the track – produced by Daft Punk’s Guy-Manuel de Homem-Chriso – the previous year. His cinema connections preceded the Drive breakout through his long collaborative friendship with musician and DJ turned director Quentin Dupieux. He starred under his real name in Dupieux’s medium-length 2002 work Nonfilm , as the actor-protagonist who wakes up to find himself on a surreal film set, and also appeared in Dupieux’s first feature Steak (2007), which also featured his music. More recently, he made a cameo appearance i n Netflix French-language original Banger opposite Vincent starring Vincent Cassel as a jaded DJ. Across his career, Kavinsky released two albums: ‘OutRun’ in 2013 and ‘Reborn’ in 2022. OutRun was created around the concept of a young man who crashes his red Ferrari Testarossa in 1986 and reappears in 2006 as zombie producer, with Kavinsky citing 1980s video games, Miami Vice and the films of Dario Argento as influences. Kavinsky’s recent musical engagements include performing at the closing ceremony of the Paris 2024 Summer Games as part of a celebration of French electronic music at the Stade de France. At the time of his death, he was scheduled to perform at events in France, Mexico and L.A. in the coming months. articles.title: Korean Box Office Up 42% In 2026 H1, Driven By ‘The King’s Warden’ & Other Local Hits; ‘Project Hail Mary’ Tops Imports
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Netflix Sets Awards-Qualifying Theatrical Release For Lee Chang-dong’s Venice & Toronto Title ‘Possible Love’ Prime Video Inks Multi-Year Deal With CJ ENM Bringing More Than 100 Korean Shows To India Hong Kong International Film Festival Society Appoints Fred Tsui As Executive Director View All July 29, 2026 3:01am The King's Warden Showbox South Korea clocked a 41.9% increase in box office revenue in the first half of 2026, according to figures released today by the Korean Film Council (KOFIC), driven by local hits including The King’s Warden , Colony and Salmokji: Whispering Water . KOFIC figures reveal that overall box office from January to June 2026 reached $396.6M (KRW579BN), compared to $279M (KRW408BN) in the same period last year. Admissions also increased during the period – up by 34.2%, compared to the first half of last year, to reach an encouraging 57 million. Korean films powered the recovery with a whopping 81.7% year-on-year increase in revenue to $254M (KRW370.2BN) and a 74.9% increase in admissions to 37.37 million. Related Stories Agencies Artists First Signs 'Project Hail Mary's James Ortiz News Hong Kong Box Office Up 25% In 2026 First Half Topped By Local Hit 'Night King' Compared to pre-pandemic levels, revenue for Korean films recovered to 94.2% of the average during the first halves of 2017–2019 (KRW392.9BN). Korean films also accounted for a 63.9% market share of overall revenue and 65.5% in admissions. Watch on Deadline The King’s Warden , Jang Hang-jun’s period drama starring Yoo Hae-jin, Park Ji-hoon and Yoo Ji-tae, topped the first half year box office with $111.7M (KRW163.1BN) from 16.9 million ticket sales, also becoming the highest-grossing Korean film of all time. It’s also the first Korean title in two years to cross the 10 million admissions benchmark and is second of all time in terms of admissions behind The Admiral: Roaring Currents . Korean films also took the number two and three positions in the first half year chart – Yeon Sang-ho’s zombie thriller Colony , which premiered in Cannes Midnight Screenings, grossed $41M (KRW60.5BN) while low-budget horror Salmokji: Whispering Water pulled in $22.8M (KRW33.3BN). Foreign films saw a 2.3% increase in revenue during the January-June period, with a combined $143M (KRW208.8BN), but ticket sales decreased by 6.9% to 19.68 million. Project Hail Mar y was the highest-grossing import with $22.6M (KRW33BN) followed by Avatar: Fire And Ash and Michael . A24’s Backrooms was the highest-grossing indie film among both local and foreign releases with $8.5M (KRW12.4BN) in revenue and 1.16 million admissions. KOFIC figures also revealed the growing importance of special format screenings with revenue from brands including IMAX, 4D, ScreenX and Dolby Cinema increasing by 56.3% year-on-year to $31.3M (KRW45.7bn) and powering a big chunk of the box office for Avatar: Fire And Ash and Project Hail Mary . Korean studio Showbox, which released all of the top three films, was the biggest distributor during the period with a 48.6% market share, followed by Disney which ranked second with a 13.8% market share. articles.title: ‘Blankety Blank,’ ‘Celebrity Mastermind’ & ‘Live At The Apollo’ All Canceled By The BBC Under Sweeping Content Cuts
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations Benedict Cumberbatch Says Paramount-Warner Deal Is A “Calamity” That Must Be Blocked ‘The Deb’ Star Charlotte MacInnes Attacks Rebel Wilson In Appeal Against Court Defeat View All July 29, 2026 4:08am 'Blankety Blank' BBC The BBC has chopped a trio of entertainment shows under plans to save £500 million ($664M) over the coming years amid a funding crisis at the UK broadcaster. Blankety Blank , Celebrity Mastermind , and Live At The Apollo have all been canceled by the BBC, in what the corporation described as “difficult decisions.” “We are incredibly proud of all three of these much-loved shows and would like to thank everyone involved, both in front of and behind the camera, for bringing them to screen and making them such a success over many years,” the BBC said. Related Stories News Jared Leto Accused Of Criminal Sexual Conduct By Four Women In BBC Documentary News Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations “Unfortunately, we have to make some really tough choices in light of our funding challenges, and these savings have been identified from the entertainment genre.” Watch on Deadline Blankety Blank first launched on British television in 1979, but was revived by the BBC in 2021 with Bradley Walsh on hosting duties. It is produced by Fremantle-owned Thames. Celebrity Mastermind is a spin-off of the iconic Mastermind quiz show. It first landed on the BBC as a special in 2002, before going on to air across 24 seasons. The format is owned by the BBC, but is produced on a contract by Hat Trick Productions, with Clive Myrie hosting. Celebrity Mastermind still has a series left to broadcast before it leaves the screen. Live at the Apollo is a 22-year-old stand-up comedy institution on the BBC. Launched in 2004, it has helped boost the careers of comics including Michael McIntyre and Alan Carr. The show is produced by Open Mike Productions and still has a series left to air on the BBC. The cuts form part of savings target of £100M for the BBC’s content division, which feeds into the wider £500M savings goal as fewer people pay the licence fee. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap. The celebration will take place during the fest’s awards gala at the Marriott Burbank on Saturday, Aug. 8. articles.title: Netflix Sets Launch Date for Lee Chang-dong’s Awards Hopeful ‘Possible Love’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 27, 2026 8:44pm 'Possible Love' Netflix In a welcome piece of news for fans of Asian arthouse cinema, Netflix has set Lee Chang-dong ‘s much-anticipated drama Possible Love — the revered Korean auteur’s first film since 2018’s Burning — for a limited release in U.S. theaters on Oct. 23 ahead of its worldwide streaming launch on Nov. 6. Netflix is positioning the film — one of its most highbrow features of the fall — for an awards-season run. Possible Love will make its world premiere in September at the Venice Film Festival , where it will vie for the Golden Lion, followed by a North American debut as a gala selection at the Toronto International Film Festival. Related Stories TV Panta Mosleh's Queer Interfaith Comedy 'Pass the Salt' Adds to Cast (Exclusive) Movies Whoopi Goldberg, Jenifer Lewis, Vanessa Williams, Vivica A. Fox to Star in 'Women Like Us for Netflix Possible Love reunites Lee with two of his most accomplished earlier collaborators. The film stars Jeon Do-yeon, who won the Cannes best actress prize as the shattered lead of Lee’s Secret Sunshine in 2007, and Sul Kyung-gu, the unforgettable lead of the director’s early masterpieces Peppermint Candy (1999) and Oasis (2002). They are joined by Zo In-sung ( Moving , Escape from Mogadishu ) and Cho Yeo-jeong (best known globally as the gullible rich wife of Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite ). Netflix also shared a poster and a first-look still from the film on Tuesday along with the release plans. The poster shows the film’s two female leads, Jeon and Cho, standing apart beneath moonlit trees at dawn — the frame’s pervasive stillness carrying an unmistakable charge of unease. Similarly, the still shows the ensemble cast standing by the sea, with their glances carrying a complicated sense of emotional intrigue. Beyond the cast and art, little has been revealed about Lee’s new feature beyond an official plot summary: “ Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) — a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence.” Although he’s never received an Oscar nom or had a film make much international commercial impact, Lee’s work has accrued a level of reverence among global cineastes that few auteurs can match. Across six features in three decades, the novelist-turned-director — who also served, improbably, as South Korea’s culture minister in the early 2000s — has picked apart the emotional fault lines of Korean society with a spare, literary intensity. Along the way, he picked up Venice’s special director’s prize for Oasis , the Cannes screenplay award for Poetry (2010) and, with Burning , the Cannes critics’ prize and the distinction of becoming the first Korean film shortlisted for an Oscar in the international feature category. Lee co-wrote Possible Love with his Burning writing partner Oh Jung-mi. Pinehouse Film, the Korean outfit that also backed Burning , produces alongside Anonymous Content and NOWFILM. The film is a U.S.-Korea co-production. “I’m not the type of filmmaker who can make movies easily,” Lee said in a statement accompanying the release date announcement on Netflix’s Tudum site. “Before I begin a film, I must be certain of what it means — to me, to the audience, and to cinema itself. That is why Possible Love took so long to make.” Netflix THR

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom Voice Gave ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Directors “Chills”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 8:49pm Robert Downey Jr. speaks onstage during the Marvel Studios Panel in Hall H at SDCC in San Diego, California on July 27, 2024. Jesse Grant/Getty Images Logo text The Russo brothers , who are directing the highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday , are recalling the first time they heard Robert Downey Jr. ‘s Doctor Doom voice. While chatting with People at Comic-Con 2026 over the weekend , Anthony and Joe Russo said they already knew Downey Jr. was perfect for the villain role after early conversations with him. But once they heard the voice the Oscar winner had crafted for the character from the Fantastic Four comics, that’s when their decision was solidified. “That was something that Robert surprised us with one day,” Anthony recalled. “You know, we were talking about all the details of the character — the voice, of course, is a key part of it, especially in the mask.” Related Stories Movies Marvel, 'Lanterns' and Johnny Depp: Here's What Hit (and Missed) at Comic-Con 2026 Lifestyle Custom 'Spider-Man'-Inspired Ping-Pong Table With Stan Lee Signature Hits Market for Close to $500K “So one day I think it was in the trailer, we were just sort of talking about some ideas and he broke out into the voice. And we knew at that moment, that was it,” the filmmaker continued. Joe added that he got “chills” when he initially heard the Doctor Doom voice. It also reminded him of another iconic Downey Jr. scene from 2019’s Avengers: Endgame . “I mean, it was one of those moments. It’d probably be one of the more memorable moments — that and the ‘I Am Iron Man’ [scene] when he snapped his fingers,” Joe says of the fan-favorite sequence . “Robert tends to present a lot of those super memorable moments.” The upcoming film’s stacked cast includes many Marvel superheroes from the legacy Avengers and X-Men to the Thunderbolts and The Fantastic Four. They’re all expected to team up to face off against Doctor Doom. Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters Dec. 18. THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: First Reactions From the Premiere
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 10:02pm Spider-Man in Columbia Pictures Spider-Man: Brand New Day Matthew Towers/Sony Pictures Logo text It’s finally here, and judging by initial reactions, it’s going to be a monster hit. Sony and Marvel’s Spider-Man : Brand New Day held its glitzy, star-packed world premiere at the Dolby Theater in Hollywood on Monday night, and not long after the screening ended, the first reactions began to flood social media. Destin Daniel Cretton ‘s Brand New Day is the fourth standalone Spider-Man film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — as well as the 38th film overall in the MCU — and picks up the action after 2021’s near $2 billion-grossing Spider-Man: No Way Home. The films once again are led by Tom Holland as Peter Parker/Spider-Man, as well as Zendaya as Michelle “MJ” Jones-Watson and Jacob Batalon as Peter’s best friend Ned Leeds. Related Stories Movies Tom Holland Says Some of His Movies Are "Sh**," Making Them Hard to Promote Movies The Doom Boom: Marvel Studios Brings 'Doomsday' and More to Its Most Crowded Comic-Con Panel Ever The MCU’s Jon Bernthal’s Frank Castle/Punisher, Michael Mando’s Mac Gargan/Scorpion and Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner/Hulk also appear in the film. New cast members include Severance ‘s Tramell Tillman and Stranger Things star Sadie Sink , the latter of whom is playing an unknown character which has led to feverish speculation online. “Keeping what Sadie’s doing under wraps, you’ll honestly understand when you see the movie. The movie is a better movie if you don’t know certain things,” Cretton said in a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter . The plot of Brand New Day follows the end of No Way Home , with the world — including MJ and Ned — having forgotten who Peter Parker is. Four years on, Peter is still protecting New York City as Spider-Man and he links up with street vigilante the Punisher to take on the likes of the Scorpion, all while his own powers undergo a new evolution. Brand New Day is written by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, who both co-wrote the other Holland Spider-Man films, including Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017), Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021). The film is produced Kevin Feige, Amy Pascal, Avi Arad and Rachel O’Connor. The film is part of Phase Six of the MCU and is followed by December’s Avengers: Doomsday in the Marvel continuity. Full critics reviews for Brand New Day are embargoed till July 28, the movie hits theaters on July 31. Below see a selection of the early social media reaction to the film posted on Monday evening. Don’t mind me. I’m just sitting here crying after watching #SpidermanBrandNewDay It’s a massive movie that balances like 5 different through lines in equal measure, each better than the last. It can feel a little overwhelming but it all comes together so beautifully it works. pic.twitter.com/5dHvcF58Sk — Germain Lussier (@GermainLussier) July 28, 2026 My flabber has been ghasted. I loved #SpiderManBrandNewDay ! Destin Daniel Cretton and Tom Holland put their hearts and souls into this thing, and it pays off HUGE! This movie is going to be massive and we’re going to be talking about it for a while. I was floored by how well… pic.twitter.com/lO0I9thr3m — Adam Hlaváč (@adamhlavac) July 28, 2026 SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY is a much more cerebral followup than the crowd pleasing No Way Home. It’s Tom Holland’s best performance as Peter Parker and the best Spider-Man movie since Raimi’s SPIDER-MAN 2. Also the costume finally looks incredible #spidermanbrandnewday — Mike Ryan (@mikeryan) July 28, 2026 It really is a brand new day for Peter Parker as Destin Daniel Cretton takes over for Jon Watts in the director’s chair for SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY. articles.title: Tom Holland Says He’ll Play Spider-Man “For as Long as They’ll Have Me” After ‘Brand New Day’: “If This Movie Does Good, I Guess We’ll See!”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 10:06pm Tom Holland attends the Los Angeles premiere of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" at Dolby Theatre on July 27. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Logo text Tom Holland is swinging into his fourth Spider-Man film — and don’t expect it to be his last. At the Los Angeles premiere for Spider-Man: Brand New Day on Monday, the star reflected on his long journey with the character, telling The Hollywood Reporter , “There’s a family here at Marvel and Sony. We’ve been making these movies for 10 years and we’re all really good friends and we all still really love working with together and there’s a shorthand, there’s a collaboration, there is a shared love for this character that is Peter Parker. When we all get together, it always feels like something magical happens, and to get to do it time and time again is something that will never really sink in for me. It still feels like this is my first-ever premiere for this character. It has been the gift of my life.” Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day': First Reactions From the Premiere Movies Matt Damon Drops by Criterion Closet, Reveals Lesson Learned From Frequent Collaborator Steven Soderbergh: "You Want to Keep Pushing" The new movie is set four years after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home , where Peter Parker has been anonymously protecting New York City until his superpowers undergo a surprising and potentially dangerous evolution. First reactions to the film hit social media soon after the premiere ended. Asked about his future as the superhero, Holland responded with a smile, “I will do it for as long as they’ll have me. So if this movie does good, I guess we’ll see!” That’s probably a pretty safe bet, as Brand New Day is expected to be one of the biggest movies of the year at the box office — on the heels of fellow smash The Odyssey , also starring he and Zendaya. Tom Holland says he’d return for another #SpiderMan film at the #SpidermanBrandNewDay premiere. pic.twitter.com/vHcxmaRO94 — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) July 28, 2026 Holland has spoken about how he called Sony Pictures head Tom Rothman and persuaded him to push back the production of Spider-Man so that he could first film The Odyssey , with the filming dates originally conflicting. At the premiere, Rothman explained why he was willing to do so, saying, “We sort of recognized that it was a rare opportunity for him. It’s unusual, to say the least, that the two movies came out so close together but I’ve always believed that a rising tide lifts all boats. People are going to the movies again and The Odyssey is a great movie and people enjoy it. I think that’s ultimately going to be very good for Spider-Man as well.” The schedule meant Holland arrived to the superhero set with many lessons from Christopher Nolan fresh on his mind; director Destin Daniel Cretton recalled that as soon as they kicked off filming, his “work ethic was incredible, the passion for the craft, the ability to make daring choices. I think when he stepped onto our set, he was just like pumped and ready to go, and he wanted to make something really great. It was wonderful — I’ll take any actor coming off of a Christopher Nolan set because they’re like ready to work their butts off to get the best product possible.” Spider-Man: Brand New Day hits theaters on Friday. Tiffany Taylor contributed to this report. THR

articles.title: Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 27, 2026 11:00pm 'Bruton' Courtesy of JIB LLC Famous, or infamous, people make for good subjects of movies, whether documentaries, essay films or fiction features. Just look at the lineup of this year’s Locarno Film Festival , whose 79th edition , running Aug. 5-15, features all sorts of screen stories about bold or recognizable names. From a German entertainment figure and an Italian film and series creator to a U.S. prisoner sentenced for an “unintended crime,” the program of the Swiss festival allows you to learn more about people who have been in the headlines. Plus, there is also a cinematic letter to a documentarian of modern Lebanese history and a fiction feature about infamous Nazi Heinrich Himmler’s massage therapist. Related Stories Movies 'Heated Rivalry' Producer Brendan Brady Backs Yukon-Set Rom-Com 'From Me to You' (Exclusive) TV Think You Can Beat Darts Superstar Luke Littler? Netflix Opens Entries for Live Sports Show If you are curious about diving deeper into the lives of the famous and the infamous at Locarno 2026 , THR has compiled some possible picks for you below. Sixteen Moments of My Life ( Seize Moments De Ma Vie ) by Albert Serra Section: Out of competition ‘Sixteen Moments From My Life’ The new movie from Spain’s Albert Serra ( Afternoons of Solitude ) focuses on German actress and singer Ingrid Caven. Yes, that is THE Ingrid Caven who is best known for her roles in films directed by her former husband Rainer Werner Fassbinder, including Love Is Colder Than Death , Why Does Herr R. Run Amok? and The American Soldier . You may also remember her from her role as Miss Vendegast in Luca Guadagnino’s Suspiria (2018). Since this is a Serra film, this is not your typical documentary, of course. Here is how the Locarno festival website teases Sixteen Moments of My Life : “Ingrid Caven sings about 16 moments from her life in a unique concert at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris.” And Locarno artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro tells THR : “It’s a live concert that Albert worked on with Ingrid,” adding: “It’s one of the out-of- competition section films that could be very, very interesting” for audiences. Bruton by Vincent Grashaw Section: Out of competition ‘Bruton,’ courtesy of JIB LLC Last year, Vincent Grashaw was in Locarno with the indigenous crime drama Keep Quiet , starring Lou Diamond Phillips and Elisha Pratt. This year, he returns with a very different story set in the world of crime, a biopic about Bryan Bruton, who was sentenced to a decade in a Florida prison for an “unintended crime.” Or, as the Locarno festival synopsis reads: “A tragic accident leads Bryan Bruton on a wild and unforgettable experience in the Florida prison system.” The film stars Theo Rossi. Bruton was charged in the early 2000s with a manslaughter conviction for a fatal hit-and-run in Jacksonville, Florida. The movie follows Bruton’s journey through the correctional system. After his release, he moved to California and turned to making the YouTube video series Bryan Bruton Crazy Prison Stories . It covers life in the Florida prison system, from how inmates obtain and conceal drugs, alcohol and weapons to cutting the window out of a jail cell. Marco Bellocchio: La porta della Realtà by Fabio Lovino Section: Out of competition ‘Marco Bellocchio: La porta della Realtà,’ courtesy of Fabio Lovino The director worked as set photographer for legendary Italian writer-director Marco Bellocchio ( Portobello , The Traitor , Kidnapped ) for more than 20 years – long enough to have something to tell the world. “After 20 years of working with Marco Bellocchio, I felt the need to share what I experienced with him and give voice to the emotions and lessons I received,” reads a synopsis of the film. “An exclusive portrait of the man and artist told through interviews and unseen images from the set.” Among the people featured in the film are Bellocchio’s family, long-term collaborators and such prominent actors as Pierfrancesco Favino and Fabrizio Gifuni, as well as such directors as Marco Tullio Giordana . I Is Another by Felix Randau Section: Piazza Grande ‘I Is Another’ Courtesy of Anke Neugebauer/Ostlicht Filmproduktion/Wega Filmproduktion Fall 1952. Journalist Hedda and her husband ambush Felix Kersten, the former massage therapist to Nazi SS leader Heinrich Himmler, on a train. “Kersten claims to have helped thousands of concentration camp prisoners to freedom during the Nazi era,” reads a synopsis. “But Hedda has doubts, and what started as an interview quickly leads to a psychological cat-and-mouse game.” Writer-director Randau’s fiction feature has a star-studded cast, including Claes Bang ( The Square , Bad Sisters ) as Kersten, Valerie Pachner ( Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore , The Stories , Four Minus Three ) as Hedda and Susanne Wuest ( Sound of Falling , Goodnight Mommy ) as Kersten’s wife. What awaits audiences? Randau puts it this way in a director’s note: “Every story has three sides. Yours. Mine. And the truth…” Revolutionaries Never Die by Mohanad Yaqubi Section: Filmmakers of the Present Competition ‘Revolutionaries Never Die’ Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Yaqubi’s goal was to celebrate the legacy of the late Lebanese filmmaker Jocelyne Saab by tracing 16 of her films documenting Arab revolutions and struggles between 1973 and 1983. The result is Revolutionaries Never Die , a cinematic letter to the female filmmaking pioneer in response to an invitation that Yaqubi received from the late Lebanese director and that suggested a collaboration just two months before her death. “Since his reply can never reach her, the film transforms into a lyrical expedition through the life, political commitments and artistic vision of a singular voice from the era of revolution,” the Locarno website highlights. And Yaqubi notes in a director’s statement: “Jocelyne Saab’s film archive from 1973 to 1983 brought forward several questions about the striking resonance between her historical depictions and our contemporary realities five decades later, when no answers can ever be given.” Transition by Peter Badel and Chris Wright Section: Out of competition ‘Transition,’ courtesy of Grischa Meyer This film has a very personal story behind it; actually, more than one. Documentarian Thomas Heise began a film about Berlin’s Schönhauser Allee, the road he lived on for decades. A few months later, Heise died unexpectedly. Heise’s long-time cinematographer Badel and editor and co-director Wright stepped up to complete the film, though. “With exclusive material from his archives, the film reveals lived history and a great thinker,” Locarno’s website promises. Heise ( Vaterland , Material ), born in East Berlin in 1955, when Germany was divided into the GDR and West Germany, was known for chronicling the reality of life in East Germany and, after German reunification, the societal and social changes in the country. THR

articles.title: How the World Cup Boosted Canal+ Results
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 28, 2026 2:02am Teboho Mokoena #4 of South Africa is challenged by Tomas Soucek #22 of Czechia during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group A match between Czechia and South Africa at Atlanta Stadium on June 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Lars Baron/Getty Images The $2 billion acquisition of Africa’s MultiChoice Group boosted Canal+ Group’s first-half financials, with the 2026 FIFA World Cup contributing to strong subscriber growth at the pay-TV giant’s South African business. “Following the acquisition of MultiChoice, our increased scale is starting to deliver the benefits we expected,” Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada said on Tuesday in unveiling the results. “We have achieved half of our €250 million ($284 million) synergies target and remain well on track for the year, and we confirm our full-year and medium-term guidance.” Related Stories Movies Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven Movies Netflix Sets Launch Date for Lee Chang-dong's Awards Hopeful 'Possible Love' Canal+ touted that “subscriber acquisition [was] up 40 percent, compared to the first half of 2025 in MultiChoice countries,” adding that June was the “best subscriber acquisition month in South Africa in a decade.” In that context, the company also mentioned “successful content and marketing initiatives, including the World Cup advertising campaign featuring Idris Elba and the launch of the Novelas+ channel in South Africa.” BNP Paribas analyst Nicolas Langlet was optimistic about the momentum at MultiChoice, writing in a report: “Trend at MultiChoice improved sequentially … driven by the success of FIFA World Cup and the first effects of the key initiatives implemented as part of the plan to boost growth. Thanks to the new strategy and reinvestment plan, we expect the subscriber base to improve in the second part of the year and support positive organic sales momentum exiting 2026.” Meanwhile, at production unit StudioCanal, Saada lauded “excellent six months on and off screen,” mentioning such box-office hits as Guru in France and Pressure in the U.S. “With a slate including Paddington 4 , Zack Snyder’s remake of Escape From New York , our first major South African film production, The Road Home , and Danny Boyle’s Ink , StudioCanal’s momentum looks set to continue,” he said. Canal+’s “content production, distribution and other” segment, which includes StudioCanal and streaming service Dailymotion, saw first-half revenue jump 9.9 percent, but adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) dropped 3 percent. Total Canal+ group revenue jumped 40 percent to €4.29 billion ($4.88 billion), driven by the MultiChoice takeover. Adjusting for the deal, growth came in at 1.4 percent. Adjusted EBIT jumped by 68 percent or, when excluding MultiChoice, rose 13 percent. THR

articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 4:01am 'Tender Loving Care' © Joseph Lynn / ©️ Thin Man Films Ltd New films from Mike Leigh , Pablo Larrain and Hans Petter Moland are among the titles in the running for the Golden Shell at this year’s San Sebastian film festival . San Sebastian on Tuesday revealed additions to its 2026 competition selection, including Leigh’s British drama Tender Loving Care ; Moland’s Growth of the Soil ; and Larrain’s My Sad Dead — a Netflix mini-series that will be screened as single, 4-hour feature. Other competition highlights including Milo from director Nicole Garcia ( Oran ), a French drama featuring Marion Cotillard and Lurker star Théodore Pellerin ; and In My Father’s Room , the directorial debut of Japanese novelist Maha Harada. Related Stories Business How the World Cup Boosted Canal+ Results Movies Locarno Films About (In)Famous People: From an Ex-Florida Prison Inmate to Albert Serra on Ingrid Caven Two previous festival winners return, with Argentine director Benjamín Naishtat, winner of the Silver Shell for best director for Rojo in 2018, and the best screenplay honors for Puan in 2023, back in competition with Glaxo , a 1950s-set drama based on the novel of the same name by Argentine writer Hernán Ronsino and starring Lali Espósito, Marcelo Subiotto and Esteban Bigliardi. Turkish filmmaker Yeşim Ustaoğlu, whose Pandora’s Box (2008) won the Golden Shell, with lead Tsilla Chelton taking best actress, will present her latest, What Remains , at San Sebastian this year. San Sebastian previously announced three Spanish films in official competition: El mal padre from Roberto Bueso; 5 more minutes from Javier Ruiz Caldera; Saints from Mikel Gurrea. Out of competition, San Sebastian will screen two Spanish series: El castillo , created and written by Isabel Peña and Eduardo Villanueva and directed by Elena Martín Gimeno and Sandra Romero, and Beyond Society , from Carlos Torres. Special screenings include The Last Goodbye from Koldo Almandoz; Pray for Us from Daniel Monzón; The Harvester from David Pérez Sañudo; and Bajañí from Fernando Trueba. The 74th San Sebastián Festival runs from September 18-26. THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 10:35pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’ 5 hours ago Sean Astin Says ‘I Had to Sell My House’ During ‘Lord of the Rings’ Era Because $250,000 Payday Was So Low: ‘I Negotiated Such a Small Amount on the Trilogy’ 14 hours ago Ryan Gosling Pitched His Own ‘Ghost Rider’ Movie to Marvel as Studio Slows Down Output to Restore Quality: ‘When Quantity Is So Much, You Get Spread Thin’ 14 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection “ Spider-Man : Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland ‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounded Spider-Man tale” that is “thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.” Fandango correspondent Erik Davis shared a glowing review on X , writing that director Destin Daniel Cretton’s sequel “feels deeper, more thoughtful and more mature than the previous trilogy.” Related Stories 'Avatar Aang' Team Reveals More Spinoffs in the Works, Nearly Making Katara Pregnant and Why Fans Shouldn't Watch the 'Dark Web' Leak Guillermo del Toro Says There Is 'Absolutely No Goddamn AI' in 'Pan's Labyrinth' 3D Re-Release: 'We're Protecting a Lineage of Art' “That maturity extends beyond the story to the action, with Cretton crafting some of my favorite Spider-Man fight sequences of the Holland era,” he added. “Part detective story, part psychological thriller, part buddy comedy (the Spider-Man/Punisher banter is so much fun), it stretches in exciting new directions before becoming a genuine love letter to the fans. When you see it, you’ll get it.” Popular on Variety Critic Wendy Lee Szany wrote on X that she has “no notes” for “Brand New Day,” which delivered “top-tier action” and a few “tearjerker” moments. TV host and entertainment journalist Brandon Pope echoed the praise. He wrote in his X review , “‘ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘ may be the most Marvel Marvel movie I’ve ever marveled. Destin Daniel Cretton honors beloved Spider-Man media — especially Raimi — to create something soulful + thrilling. Hulk, Punisher deliver. Big reveal lives up. The best of the Tom Holland Spidey series.” Film critic Peter Howell likewise adored the Marvel sequel. He wrote on X that “Brand New Day” cut back on the “multiverse tedium to give us a grounded Spider-Man tale that’s back to the city roots of the comic book hero we knew and loved.” “Tom Holland finally nails the sarcasm, angst and love hassles of Spidey/Peter Parker as Stan Lee first envisioned the character,” Howell added. “The film negotiates the emotional landmines left by ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ five years ago while a seriously scary villain emerges in the person of a malevolent telepath. Solid support from Zendaya , Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Mark Ruffalo and ‘Stranger Things’ star Sadie Sink.” Nexus Point staffer Kevin Verma wrote on X , “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is exactly the refresher Marvel needed. Tom Holland has never been better and the Spidey-Punisher pairing is pure gold. Destin Daniel Cretton outdoes himself, but the script is the real superhero- thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.” Holland returns as Peter Parker/Spider-Man in “Brand New Day,” which is set four years after the events of “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” That movie ended with Doctor Strange casting a spell in which Peter is erased from everyone’s memory, so now the web-slinger is fighting crime in New York City without the support of MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon). A new threat emerges in the form of Sadie Sink’s mysterious villain at the same time as Peter’s spider powers begin evolving beyond his control. The supporting cast includes Mark Ruffalo as Hulk and Jon Bernthal as Punisher. Expectations for “Brand New Day” are sky high after 2021’s “No Way Home” became a pop culture sensation with $1.9 billion at the worldwide box office. It was Holland’s second billion-dollar-grossing “Spider-Man” movie after 2019’s “Far From Home” earned $1.1 billion on the heels of “Avengers: Endgame.” While Marvel has had its ups (“Deadpool and Wolverine”) and downs (“Captain America: Brave New World”) in recent years, “Brand New Day” should get the MCU back on strong box office footing ahead of December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.” Holland played a greater role in the development of “Brand New Day” compared to his previous “Spider-Man” movies. He took deep dives on the internet to understand what exactly Spider-Man fans wanted to see in his latest outing as Marvel’s iconic web-slinger, then took these fan ideas directly to studio executives and the movie’s screenwriters. “What’s been really fun about this most recent movie is designing the suit and being a part of that process and understanding what we wanted to try and achieve,” Holland told LADbible about having greater involvement in the movie’s development this time around. “I have been actively sifting through the internet and trying to best understand what it is that the fans want from a ‘Spider-Man’ movie, and that’s been my driving force in these pitch meetings,” he added. “I think the producers, at times were like, absolutely sick of me, but I think it’s really important, because we make these movies for [the fans].” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opens in theaters nationwide July 31. Check out more first reactions in the posts below. #SpiderManBrandNewDay reminded me why the story of Spider-Man resonates w/ me so much. He's hope. But he's also painfully human so bring tissues 😭 Also the Tom/Zendaya chemistry was rom-com levels. And we need more Punisher in everything. And Sadie Sink… just wow! Liza too! pic.twitter.com/68jgm3htfs — Lyra Hale 🇵🇷🏳️‍🌈✍🏼 (@MsLyraHale) July 28, 2026 #SpiderManBrandNewDay is a triumph from Destin Daniel-Cretton. Bursting with heart, sincerity, hope. A story about the need to be vulnerable and human, to not let the world turn you into a monster, to recognize your pain in an effort to help others feel less alone in theirs. It's… https://t.co/ud5pao6ojw pic.twitter.com/DCJBMrqr9A — Griffin Schiller (@griffschiller) July 28, 2026 #SpiderManBrandNewDay is easily my favorite Holland-led Spider-Man movie. It isn’t CGI goop or a bunch of fan-service nonsense. It’s exciting, emotional, and the best-looking MCU movie in a long time. Really good stuff. It'll meet your expectations in some places and defy them in others. pic.twitter.com/iA0XsLl9rL — Brian Davids (@PickYourBrian) July 28, 2026 Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a solid new entry for Marvel. The story and themes of loneliness, change, and friendship all hit incredibly hard. It’s a bit overstuffed with too much going on at points. Sadie Sink’s story is the most weighty and shocking. #SpiderManBrandNewDay pic.twitter.com/QO6EKTkgXC — Hunter Bolding (@HunterBVideo) July 28, 2026 Destin Daniel Cretton brings incredible energy to the #Spiderman franchise. #Brandnewday is action-packed from start to finish. articles.title: ‘Kill Jackie,’ Starring a Glamorous, Lethal Catherine Zeta-Jones, Acquired by Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 1:01am PT ‘Kill Jackie,’ Starring a Glamorous, Lethal Catherine Zeta-Jones, Acquired by Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max (EXCLUSIVE) A 'gonzo' revenge thriller, 'Kill Jackie' has been picked up for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France and Belgium where the series will debut in 2026 By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More 1 hour ago ‘Kill Jackie,’ Starring a Glamorous, Lethal Catherine Zeta-Jones, Acquired by Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago See All Catherine Zeta-Jones in 'Kill Jackie' (Credit: Unai Mateo) Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired revenge thriller “ Kill Jackie ,” starring Catherine Zeta-Jones , for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France and Belgium. The deal takes in two of HBO’s most established streaming markets, the Nordics and Spain, where SVOD services HBO Nordics and HBO España launched as far back as 2012 and 2016 with HBO Max set to pass Prime Video to become the second largest streamer in Spain by the end of 2026, according to Ampere Analysis. Related Stories 'Family Guy' Casts Kieran Culkin to Play the Devil in New Halloween Special for Hulu 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' TV Series Casts Audiobook Star Jeff Hays as Princess Donut's Voice Produced by Fremantle , which handles all international distribution outside the U.S., and Steel Spring Pictures, the eight-part series is scheduled to debut in 2026. “Kill Jackie” looks set to give Zeta-Jones, an Oscar, Bafta and Tony Award winner (“Chicago,” “Wednesday”), as she has recognised, a “multifaceted” role encompassing “empowerment, identity and redemption.” Popular on Variety Zeta-Jones plays a drug dealer turned glamorous art dealer whose past suddenly caches up with her as she becomes the target of The Seven Demons, a hit squad of the world’s most terrifying assassins. When a tragic event makes her hell-bent for revenge, Jackie determines to take out the Demons one by one, unleashing her old killer instincts. “However, she soon realises her own demons are much more terrifying than the ruthless killers on her trail…and her buried secrets ultimately lead her much closer to home, with surprising consequences,” the synopsis runs. A buzz title at the London TV Screenings, “Kill Jackie” co-stars Daniel Ings (“The Knight of the Seven Kingdoms”) as Jackie’s foil, her distinctly sensitive-about-violence tax lawyer, who, according to reports, provides much of the humor in a consistently high-octane, twisting, comedic thriller. Written by Tom Butterworth (“Gangs of London”) and Conor Keane, “Kill Jackie” is lead directed by Damon Thomas (“Killing Eve”), adapting “The Price You Pay” by Sunday Times best-selling author Nick Harkaway, writing as Aidan Truhen. Key cast also takes in another HBO alum, Sidse Babett Knudsen (“Prime Target,” “Borgen”),and Óscar Jaenada , Hattie Hook, Darci Shaw, Raff Law , Enzo Cilenti, Christine Adams, Julian Rhind-Tutt, Karlis Arnolds Avots, Set Sjöstrand, Tadashi Ito, Sebastian Armesto, Julian Barratt, Gavin Spokes , Jonathan Cake, Bamshad Abedi-Amin and Bill Paterson. “HBO Max has an outstanding track record of partnering on the very best projects, making it the perfect home for ‘Kill Jackie,’ said Jamie Lynn, EVP co-production & distribution EMEA. “As the platform continues to grow across Europe, we couldn’t be more delighted to embark on this adventure together. With its relentless pace, thrilling action and unforgettable central performance, we know ‘Kill Jackie’ is in the very best of hands. “ “I loved Nick’s gonzo thriller of a book,” Butterworth has said . “Our ambition is to twist and expand his world into something equally funny, dark, crazed and unique. Or die trying.” “Kill Jackie” is a “sly character study that asks what happens when you’re forced to act out your darkest impulses in order to survive. But at its heart, it’s a grounded, universal story about family: the kind we’re born with and the kind we choose,” Fremantle told Variety is the run-up to Mipcom. “Kill Jackie” is produced in partnership with José Luis Escolar’s Deabru Kalea Filmeak which supervised production in and around Bilbao. So expect the propulsive thriller to make full use of Bilbao’s extraordinarily chic post-industrial cityscape, taking advantage of its Guggenheim Museum, belle époque and modern plate glass architecture, estuary-adjunct walkways and green countryside. “Killing Jackie” is co-created by Conor Keane, Butterworth Peter Lawson (“John Wick”) and Thomas. Butterworth serves as both writer and showrunner. Executive producers are Lawson and Jose Agustín Valdés for Steel Springs Pictures, Butterworth, Thomas, Zeta-Jones, Rebecca Dundon, Dante Di Loreto and Jeffrey Levine, with Nick Harkaway serving as executive consultant. With the WBD deal, a multi-territory sales to Prime Video and a recent AMC+ U.S. sale, “Kill Jackie” has closed the lion’s share of major territories in the world. Zeta-Jones is represented by UTA and Ziffren Brittenham LLP. Butterworth is represented by Curtis Brown. Daniel Ings is represented by United Agents, WME, TFC Management, ColorCreative, Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern and CLD Communications. articles.title: Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 1:31am PT Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘The Odyssey’ Holds Top Spot as Vijay’s ‘Jana Nayagan’ Bows at No. 5 at U.K. and Ireland Box Office 18 minutes ago Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ 57 minutes ago ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago See All Netflix Lee Chang-dong ‘s “ Possible Love ” will open in Korean theaters September 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia Oct. 22 and in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland and Japan Oct. 23, before streaming globally on Netflix starting November 6. The film’s world premiere will be at the Venice Film Festival and North American Premiere at the Toronto Film Festival. “Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages. Related Stories 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' TV Series Casts Audiobook Star Jeff Hays as Princess Donut's Voice Ryan Reynolds Snuck Into Comic-Con as Deadpool With 'No Handlers' and 'No Security': 'I Felt So Lucky' The cast brings together Jeon Do-yeon (“Secret Sunshine”), Sul Kyung-gu (“Peppermint Candy”), Zo In-sung (“Escape From Mogadishu”) and Cho Yeo-jeong (“Parasite”) in what stands as one of the largest gatherings of top-tier Korean acting talent in a single film. Popular on Variety Lee also co-wrote the screenplay with Oh Jung-mi. The film is produced by Pinehouse Film Co., Ltd., Anonymous Content, LLC and Nowfilm Co., Ltd, with South Korea as its country of origin. With festival berths at Venice and Toronto locked in ahead of its theatrical rollout, “Possible Love” positions itself as one of the more closely watched Korean auteur releases of the fall season before landing on Netflix worldwide. articles.title: CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 2:26am PT CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’ 2 hours ago Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’ 23 hours ago Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 1 day ago See All Screenshot courtesy The Daily Show on YouTube/Getty Images CNN ‘s Kaitlan Collins was “not surprised” that U.S. President Donald Trump insulted her during his speech at Friday night’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner. During an appearance on “The Daily Show” on Monday, Collins — who serves as CNN’s chief White House correspondent — debriefed the event with Jon Stewart. “In the room, I was not surprised when he insulted me. That happens pretty regularly inside the Oval Office. This is just a bigger venue where it was happening,” Collins said. “What was most surprising to me was — the room was filled with a lot of his staffers, his cabinet, his allies, Republicans in Congress — it was so quiet in the room during the president’s remarks.” Related Stories Ryan Reynolds Snuck Into Comic-Con as Deadpool With 'No Handlers' and 'No Security': 'I Felt So Lucky' Neon Bringing Na Hong-Jin’s 'Hope' to Comic-Con (EXCLUSIVE) “Do you think it’s because of how much they respect him?” Stewart asked, to which Collins cheekily replied: “Who’s to say.” Popular on Variety Collins received an award for her coverage of Trump’s contentious meeting with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky during the dinner, which was rescheduled from April after a gunman crashed through security at the original event. In his speech, the president said Collins “shouldn’t get the award” and that it was “fake,” and then went on a tangent about how she should smile more. Trump also compared Collins to trans advocate Dylan Mulvaney, mentioning the 2023 Bud Light controversy where conservative customers boycotted the beer brand after Mulvaney posted a social media ad featuring her face on a can. “I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said in his speech. Mulvaney responded to Trump in a TikTok video on Sunday, saying she was “honored” to be compared to Collins and the president’s attack was perhaps the “greatest compliment of all.” As Collins said, Trump has a history of insulting her and deflecting her questions, which Stewart pointed out are often pretty straightforward. “That’s why I ask the questions the way I do, is because I want anyone to be able to listen to what I’m asking — whether that’s at a briefing or during a moment with the president — and think, you know, I want to know the answer to that, too, or that is a good question,” Collins said. “I don’t want it to only serve one audience or one political leaning, I want anyone — from my family in Alabama, to people in the White House, to people in Washington — to be able to hear that question and think, ‘What is the answer to that?'” Collins also thanked her CNN colleague Wolf Blitzer, who presented the awards to journalists at the dinner, saying that “he’s called me every day since Friday.” She concluded that despite Trump’s speech, “It’s really not about me and I don’t want it to be about my reaction.” “I think if you let it become about that, then it becomes a back-and-forth between the two of us,” she said. “And instead, I think it’s more effective to remind people in those moments where he is insulting me or he is criticizing me, about the question I asked or the reporting I did that he was so angry about in this moment — and the fact that I got an award for it really bothered him, clearly.” Watch Collins’ full interview on “The Daily Show” below. articles.title: San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 2:31am PT San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More Nicole Garcia’s ‘7:40 ce matin-là/Milo,’ ‘In My Father’s Room,’ from Maha Harada, Hans Petter Moland’s ‘Growth of the Soil’ and Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s ‘What Remains’ also make San Sebastián’s main competition cut By John Hopewell , Emiliano De Pablos 'My Sad Dead' Credit: Pablo Larraín / Netflix Buzzy new projects from “Jacky,” “Spencer” and “Maria” director Pablo Larraín , and Benjamín Naishtat will be joined by Mike Leigh ’s “Tender Loving Care” in main competition at September’s San Sebastián Film Festival . Also making the cut are new titles from Nicole Garcia – Marion Coillard starrer “7:40 ce matin-là/Milo,’ as well as Maha Harada’s “In My Father’s Room,” Hans Petter Moland’s “Growth of the Soil” and Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s “What Remains.” Announced Tuesday, the new titles reflect San Sebastián’s hallmark mix of international name auteurs – often drawn from its key source markets of Latin America, France and the Nordics – and newer talent, a key focus for San Sebastián whose New Directors strand, set to be announced on Friday, is one of the most prestigious in Europe. Related Stories 'Star Trek' Sets 60th Anniversary & 'Strange New Worlds' Comic-Con Hall H Panels, Fan Screening, Activations (EXCLUSIVE) 'Futurama' to Release Three New Supersized Specials, Including a Christmas Episode, Starting Next Year on Hulu A feature version of Larraín’s Netflix four-part horror miniseries produced by Fabula, “My Sad Dead” (“Mis muertos tristes”) adapts Argentinean writer Mariana Enriquez, who suggests that the true terror is not the supernatural itself, but the horrors that society hides. Top Argentine actors Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi and Alejandra Flechner star. Popular on Variety Leigh’s “Tender Loving Care” stars Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson in what the festival describes as his “insightful exploration of the modern world.” From the director of “Rojo,” a big hit at San Sebastián, Naishtat’s “Glaxo” is a tale of shattered friendship set in a small provincial town between the late 1950s and the 1980s and described as “about desire and revenge, set at a time when a whole country lost its innocence.” San Sebastián’s newly announced Golden Shell contenders join three Spanish features in main competition which were announced on July 17: Mikel Gurrea’s “Sants,” with “The Beloved” star Vicky Luengo, top comedian Berto Romero’s time-loop relationship comedy “Five Minutes More” and Roberto Bueso’s family dramedy “El mal padre.” The 74th edition of the San Sebastian Film Festival, the biggest film event in the Spanish-speaking world, runs Sept. 18-26 in the capital of Gipuzcoa, in Spain’s verdant and stunning Basque Country. Newly Announced San Sebastián Main Competition Titles “Glaxo” (Benjamín Naishtat, Brazil/Argentina) Cast: Lali Espósito, Esteban Lamothe, and Marcelo Subiotto Produced by Brazil’s RT Features and Argentina’s Rei Pictures with a top Argentine cast of Espósito (“Permitidos,” “Sky Rojo”), Esteban Lamothe (“The Student”) and Marcelo Subiotto (“Puan”) and a tale which explores macro historical transformation via an intimate narrative, a winning combination in Rojo’s pre-junta portrayal of “moral apocalypse,” as Variety noted. “Growth of the Soil” (“Markens Grode,” Hans Petter Moland, Norway-Denmark-Germany) Cast: Herbert Nordrum, Asta Kamma August, Gard B. Eidsvold A stranger crossing the mountains of northern Norway anchors Moland’s adaptation of Knut Hamsun’s 1917 Nobel Prize-winning novel. Rootless Isak settles on barren land and attempts to build a life with Inger, a solitary woman marked by resilience and secrecy. Together they endure the elements, cultivate the soil and raise a family, only for time, hardship and desire to reshape them. Moland’s “Zero Kelvin” won San Sebastián’s Special Jury Prize in 1995. “In My Father’s Room” (“Muyou no hito,” Maha Harada, Japan) Cast: Aoi Yu, Ogata Issey, Nagayama Eita, Watanabe Eri Best-selling novelist Harada makes her director’s feature debut with an adaptation of her novel “An Unnecessary Man.” The film follows an art museum employee led by a mysterious key to a room once used by her recently deceased father. Retracing his final days, she discovers a life sustained by language, tea ceremony and overlooked beauty. Bitters End handles international sales and will release the drama in Japan in January 2027. ‘Milo’ Courtesy: San Sebastian Film Festival “Milo” (“7:40 ce matin-là,” Nicole Garcia, France) Cast: Marion Cotillard, Théodore Pellerin, Artus, Laure Calamy Garcia reunites with Oscar winner Cotillard after “From the Land of the Moon” for the story of a woman newly released from prison who takes a café job in a provincial town to approach Milo, a young mechanic unaware of their shared past. As buried tensions surface, both face the possibility of rebuilding a bond shattered decades earlier. From Garcia, a three-time Cannes competition contender (“From the Land of the Moon,” Selon Charlie,” “The Adversary”) And 14-time Cesar Award nominee. “My Sad Dead,” (“Mis muertos tristes,” Pablo Larraín, Argentina-Chile) Cast: Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Carolina Álvarez A world premiere. Ema, who can see and hear the dead, receives an unexpected visit from her niece Julie, who shares the same unsettling gift. As family secrets and wounds, resurface the entire neighborhood senses presences and hear the distinctive sounds of their own dead. Written by Larráin and among co-scribes, Guillermo Calderón, co-writer of “Neriuda” “El Conde,” and adapting Mariana Enríquez. “Mariana’s writing is particularly visual, always brilliant, and always dangerous. It’s a casual, domestic horror that inspires,” says Larraín. “What Remains” (“Artakalan,” Yeşim Ustaoğlu, Turkey-France-Luxembourg-Bulgaria) Cast: Öykü Karayel, Metin Akdülger, Ali Kayra Kul, İlyas Salman The portrait of a poet’s attempt to reclaim her inner voice. Breaking free from a suffocating domestic order, she reconnects with her conscience and begins questioning accepted ideas of family and the meaning of life. Her choices also open a different path for those around her. Ustaoğlu returns to San Sebastián, where “Pandora’s Box” won the Golden Shell in 2008 and Tsilla Chelton shared the acting prize. ‘Tender Loving Care’ Courtesy: San Sebastian Film Festival “Tender Loving Care,” (Mike Leigh, U.K./U.S./Singapore) Cast: Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, and Alice Bailey Johnson. articles.title: San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 2:49am PT San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 31 minutes ago San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 52 minutes ago Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow 2 hours ago See All Bitter's End San Sebastian Film Festival competition title “In My Father’s Room” has been added to Bitters End ‘s fall sales slate. The film marks the feature directorial debut of best-selling novelist Maha Harada . Known in Japan under the title “Muyou no Hito,” the drama is adapted from Harada’s own short story “An Unnecessary Man.” The cast includes Aoi Yu (“Wife of a Spy”), Ogata Issey (“Onoda,” “Silence,” “Yi Yi”), Nagayama Eita (“Monster”) and Watanabe Eri (“Shall We Dance?”). Kitagawa Yoshio, whose credits include “Evil Doesn’t Exist” and “Lost Land,” serves as cinematographer. Related Stories Tony Nominee Lila Neugebauer Boards Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’ as Pilot Director (EXCLUSIVE) TV's Upfront Market Has Nearly Wrapped, Even if Big TV Won't Say So (EXCLUSIVE) The story follows Satomi, an employee at an art museum, after an envelope arrives bearing an unfamiliar key. It unlocks a room left behind by her father, dead a month earlier and alone at the time. Tracing what he did in his last days, Satomi uncovers a figure society had largely written off, one who nonetheless took quiet comfort in language, in tea ceremony and in small, overlooked beauty, and she comes to recognize the grace in how he lived. Popular on Variety The project marks a screen debut for Harada, one of Japan’s most widely read authors, with more than 10 million copies of her books sold since she began publishing in 2006. Harada trained in Japanese literature and art history, then spent time at a trading firm and at museums, among them New York’s Museum of Modern Art, before shifting into freelance curatorial and cultural writing work. Her art-themed novels include “Canvas of Paradise” and “Guernica Cover-Up.” Bitters End will handle both the film’s international sales and its local release, which is scheduled for January 2027 in Japan. The distributor has spent more than 30 years bringing international auteur cinema to Japanese audiences, including work by Hamaguchi Ryusuke, Bong Joon Ho, the Dardenne brothers, Jia Zhangke, Roy Anderson and Gianfranco Rosi. Recent releases handled by the company include “Below the Clouds,” “Young Mothers,” “Sex/Love/Dreams,” “Anora” and “The Odyssey.” On the production front, its credits as a producer include the Oscar-winning “Drive My Car,” “Two Seasons, Two Strangers,” which took the Golden Leopard at Locarno, Cannes prizewinner “All of a Sudden” and “All the Lovers in the Night,” an Un Certain Regard selection at Cannes. articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 3:10am PT ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘The Odyssey’ Holds Top Spot as Vijay’s ‘Jana Nayagan’ Bows at No. 5 at U.K. and Ireland Box Office 10 minutes ago Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ 48 minutes ago ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago See All courtesy Chrysalis Film LLC “ Chrysalis ” has secured a theatrical distribution deal in Vietnam through CJ CGV Vietnam, the country’s leading multiplex operator and distributor, with a nationwide release set for Sept. 11. The film will open locally as “Mãi Nợ Một Lời Tạm Biệt,” rendered in English as “The Farewell I Never Gave.” The international title remains “Chrysalis.” The deal marks a significant distribution milestone for the U.S.-Vietnam production, which is set in Vietnam and draws on the childhood memories of its subject and executive producer, Sir Daniel K. Winn. “Bringing ‘Chrysalis’ to theaters in Vietnam is deeply personal,” Winn said. “This story grew out of my childhood and the love of my grandmother, and I hope Vietnamese audiences see something of their own families and memories in it.” Related Stories 'Haunting Adeline' Adult Graphic Novels in the Works Based on H.D. Carlton's Divisive Dark Romance Amid Film Adaptation Backlash (EXCLUSIVE) Winston Duke Trusts David Jonsson to Take On ‘Black Panther’: ‘I Think It's Going to Be Great’ Directed by J. Robert Schulz from a screenplay by Andrew Creme, based on a story by Winn, Randall J. Slavin and Schulz, the film stars Kieu Chinh as Bà Nội, the grandmother at the heart of the story, with Winn appearing in the present-day storyline. The cast also includes Uy Nhan, Samuel An, Lan Thy, Le Anh Huy, Tien Pham and Trinh Tu Trung. WS Productions produced. Popular on Variety “This Vietnam release is an important milestone for ‘Chrysalis’ and reflects the collaboration between our U.S. and Vietnamese cast, crew and producing teams,” executive producer Slavin said. “We are proud to bring the film to audiences in the country where its story begins.” The film made its market debut at the 2026 Cannes Film Market with two market screenings before going on to compete at the fourth edition of the Danang Asian Film Festival, where it was one of 13 films selected for the Asian Competition. At DANAFF, Kieu Chinh received the Screen Excellence Merit Award, recognizing a screen career spanning nearly seven decades and more than 100 roles. “‘Chrysalis’ is a deeply moving story that explores the powerful themes of family and memory,” CJ CGV Vietnam said in a statement. “We look forward to bringing this remarkable award-winning film to audiences across Vietnam this September.” The Vietnam theatrical run is part of the film’s broader release schedule, which includes a Beverly Hills engagement in October and a worldwide rollout planned for November. articles.title: Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’
articles.full_text: Jul 28, 2026 3:24am PT Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’ 36 minutes ago ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE) 51 minutes ago San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago See All MIFFest Xinemarte , the immersive cinematic art platform developed by Los Angeles-based creative technology company SQNXR, has made its Malaysia premiere as a special program at the recently concluded 9th Malaysia International Film Festival in Kuala Lumpur. The platform’s Kuala Lumpur rollout began a day ahead of MIFFest ‘s opening, and marks the second stop in Xinemarte’s Asian expansion following a soft launch in Taipei. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Says There Is 'Absolutely No Goddamn AI' in 'Pan's Labyrinth' 3D Re-Release: 'We're Protecting a Lineage of Art' 'Coyote vs. Acme' Director and Star Lana Condor on Finally Showing Their Film to the Fans at Comic-Con: 'The Fight Was For a Good Reason' The Malaysia program centers on “The Room Remembers,” Xinemarte’s inaugural thematic chapter, and its first presentation, “Fluid” – a 25-minute audiovisual work by SQNXR Creative Director Ray Tijssen, who operates under the alias 0010×0010. The work treats the movie theater itself as the primary artistic medium, drawing on cinematic-scale projection and Dolby Atmos surround sound to create a shared sensory environment. Popular on Variety “You have canvas, you have screens, you have sculpture and you have movie theatre rooms,” Tijssen said. “The room becomes the audience. The room remembers.” Tijssen described “Fluid” as “organic forms adrift in a single current, where solid and liquid move as one, somewhere between deep ocean and deep space.” MIFFest audiences attended a special post-screening Q&A session with Tijssen, in which he discussed the creative process behind the work and the concept underpinning “The Room Remembers.” The screenings drew a positive response from festival-goers, with many describing the experience as calming and meditative. Jazzy Group of Companies, the Malaysia-based entertainment company and MIFFest organizer, holds the exclusive Asia sales mandate for Xinemarte. CEO Joanne Goh founded the festival. “Cinema infrastructure is underutilized for significant portions of the day,” Goh said. “Xinemarte allows operators to activate those spaces with premium experiential content that appeals to audiences who might never attend a traditional film screening. We see enormous potential across the region.” Structured around 25-minute cycles with staggered start times, the platform allows audiences to enter and exit freely, with programming updated monthly across family-friendly and adult-oriented categories. Rather than adapting conventional content for cinema screens, Xinemarte was built to exploit the full capabilities of contemporary theatrical infrastructure. Following its Malaysia run, the platform is set to expand to Singapore, Hong Kong and additional markets across the region. Tijssen, who was born in the Netherlands and is now based in Los Angeles, has previously mounted installations at MOCA Bangkok, W1 London and TODA Dubai. Christopher Nolan’s epic spectacle added £11.8 million ($15.7 million) in its sophomore frame, representing a remarkably light holdover drop and elevating its local gross to £35.3 million ($46.9 million) after 10 days of wide theatrical release. In a dramatic turn of events in May, Vijay’s political party won the Tamil Nadu elections and he assumed office as the state’s Chief Minister.
