articles.title: ‘Obsession’s Michael Johnston In Early Talks To Join Next ‘Mummy’ Film From Universal Pictures
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Obsession’s Michael Johnston In Early Talks To Join Next ‘Mummy’ Film From Universal Pictures New Line Wins Heated Bidding War For Theo James Krekis Horror Package ‘Jealous People Are Ugly People’ Sean Woods Launches Management & Production Company Intangible View All July 27, 2026 4:04pm Michael Johnston attends the premiere of Focus Features' 'Obsession' on May 11, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Brianna Bryson/FilmMagic Michael Johnston , star of Curry Barker’s breakout Focus Features horror film Obsession , is in early talks for a role in The Mummy , the next installment in the iconic horror franchise from Universal Pictures , Deadline has confirmed. No word yet on the role to be played by Johnston. But he’ll star opposite the returning Brendan Fraser, Rachel Weisz and John Hannah should the deal make. Reps for Universal Pictures had no comment on the casting. Radio Silence’s Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett are directing the next Mummy movie from a script by David Coggeshall ( The Family Plan , Orphan: First Kill ). Franchise veteran Sean Daniel is set to produce alongside William Sherak, James Vanderbilt and Paul Neinstein of Project X Entertainment, as well as Clayton Townsend, with Fraser and Hivemind’s Jason F. Brown exec producing. Pic is slated for release on October 15, 2027. Related Stories News Universal Responds To Online Leak Of 'The Odyssey' With Takedown Protocols News 'Obsession's Michael Johnston Wants To Play "Intentional, Meaningful Queer Role": "Maybe I'll Write It Myself" Revolving around one of Universal’s original movie monsters of the early 20th century, the Mummy films of the ’90s and ‘2000s contributed to Fraser’s rise as one of Hollywood’s biggest stars. The films follow the overseas adventures of his roguish American adventurer and former French Foreign Legion soldier, Rick O’Connell, who alongside English Egyptologist Evelyn Carnahan (Weisz), battles ancient curses from the likes of the resurrected Egyptian high priest Imhotep. Stephen Sommers directed both 1999’s The Mummy and 2001’s The Mummy Returns , both of which topped $400M worldwide, leading to Dwayne Johnson spinoff The Scorpion King and other titles. Watch on Deadline Johnston plays Bear, the lovelorn twenty-something whose life is ruined by the One Wish Willow, in Obsession , which is now Focus’ top-grossing film of all time at over $458M worldwide. The project marks the actor’s big break, nearly 15 years into his screen acting career. Johnston’s talks for The Mummy were first reported by The InSneider . articles.title: D4vd Ordered To Stand Trial For Murdering, Dismembering 14-Year-Old Girl
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Denise Petski , Dominic Patten July 27, 2026 4:20pm D4vd looks on from behind his defense attorney Marilyn Bednarski during his arraignment Monday Getty UPDATED: A Los Angeles judge has ordered singer D4vd (real name David Anthony Burke) to stand trial on murder charges in the killing and dismemberment of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has been charged with one count each of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains. The criminal complaint also includes special circumstance allegations of murder of a witness, murder for financial gain and murder by means of lying in wait as well as a special allegation that Burke personally used a deadly and dangerous weapon, a sharp instrument, to commit the crime. “The people have met their burden on all counts,” Judge Charlaine Olmedo said. She ordered that Burke continue to be held without bail. He has pleaded not guilty. Watch on Deadline If convicted, Burke could face the death penalty or life in prison without parole. A decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made at a later date. “What was presented by our Office over the course of the last week is a small but illustrative fraction of the evidence investigators have accumulated that proves defendant Burke is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt of the brutal murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez,” Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said. “This has been a parent’s worst nightmare, hearing the ghoulish details of how their child was killed, dismembered and left as trash.” Burke is to be arraigned on August 31. PREVIOUS, April 20, 2026: Seeking a quick trial, D4vd entered a not guilty plea Monday in a brief appearance in a downtown Los Angeles criminal court. Facing first-degree murder and continuous sexual abuse charges with the death penalty over the dismembered killing last year of teen Celeste Rivas Hernandez, the 21-year-old singer (whose real name is David Anthony Burke) sat behind a glass barrier this afternoon in L.A. Superior Court Judge Theresa McGonigle’s courtroom. Related Stories Legal D4vd Faces Possible Death Penalty Over Murder Of Teen & “Unlawful Sexual Acts” Charges News Singer D4vd Arrested In Connection With Celeste Hernandez’s Murder After Dismembered Body Found In Tesla “We believe the actual evidence will show David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez,” defense lawyer Blair Berk told the judge and attendees after entering pleas for her client. “We would like to have the evidence come into the light of day, at the earliest opportunity,” Berk added, requesting a fast-tracked preliminary evidentiary hearing. Berk made a point of wanting everything open in court, noting “there have been four months of secret grand jury proceedings.” In response, Deputy DA Beth Silverman said that her boss Nathan Hochman and the prosecution’s office would be “very happy to put on the evidence we’ve collected against Burke. A formal felony complaint ( read it here ) against D4vd was filed at the same time in LASC. Before the judge, Berk lamented the lack of discovery the defense has received so far, and at the same time, as Silverman objected that the evidence collected so far was “voluminous” noted the DA’s office had the time for a detailed press conference on the case earlier Monday. As Silverman cast doubt on there being much material available for a planned follow up hearing later this week, Berk asked the prosecution to endeavor with “conscientious earnestness” to get as much discovery as possible to her team. Amidst all that, Hernandez’s parents were seated nearby in the the Clara Shortridge Foltz Criminal Justice Center during the arraignment proceedings. The booking photo of D4vd aka David Anthony Burke, revealed before the start of a press briefing Monday Getty Earlier in the day at a press conference on the case, LA County DA Hochman said the “Romantic Homicide” singer could be executed if found guilty by a jury due to “special circumstances” that permit the rare use of the death penalty in California. Part of that special circumstance, according to the DA, is for D4vd “lying in wait, murder for financial gain and killing a witness in a criminal investigation” last April. That witness was the then-13-year-old Hernandez, who was allegedly the victim of sex crimes perpetrated by the TikTok sensation. Hernandez was last seen April 23, just before she went over to D4vd’s L.A. home. D4vd is also facing charges of “lewd and lascivious sexual acts” with an individual under 14 years of age. Similar to the alleged murder of Rob and Michelle Reiner last year by their youngest son Nick, the DA has not made public whether prosecutors will seek the death penalty or go for life without parole for D4vd. After months of investigation, D4vd was arrested last week at his rented Hollywood Hills residence . The arrest came almost eight months after Hernandez’s decomposed and mutilated body was discovered in the trunk of an impounded Tesla registered in the singer’s name. At that time, D4vd was on tour and out of L.A. Through representatives, he promised to cooperate with the LAPD and other law enforcement on the matter. Now behind bars without bail, D4vd is scheduled to be back in court Thursday. Also in court today, Judge McGonigle (who is overseeing the Reiner case as of right now) ordered the L.A. County medical examiner’s office to release the autopsy report for Hernandez. The report is not available because “the Department of Medical Examiner has not yet received notice the court order sealing the case has been lifted,” the department told Deadline. That paperwork is expected to arrive in one form or another at the medical examiner’s office by Tuesday morning, I’m told. Denise Petski contributed to this report . articles.title: Co-Founders Of Magic Hour Entertainment And Rebelle Media Plus Author Duo Christina Lauren Advise Studios & Streamers To Devote Resources To “Elevated” And “Prestige” Romance Through Casting, Chemistry & More
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi David Jonsson To Play T’Challa’s Grown Son In ‘Black Panther 3’; Pic Hits Theaters In December 2028 – Comic-Con ‘Dark Matter’ Season 2 Trailer Debuts In Hall H At Comic-Con, Teasing Endless Possibilities With The Box ‘Spaceballs: The New One’ Invades Comic-Con With Send-Up Of Marvel’s Hall H Panels Of Yore View All July 27, 2026 5:10pm L-R: Rebelle Media's Laura Lewis and Amanda Palley & Max Siemers of Magic Hour Entertainment Rebelle Media/Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Paramount+ As Divergent author Veronica Roth pointed out in her opening of the “Romance: On the Big Screen: Why It’s About Damn Time” panel Friday at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, romance accounts for 23% of all book sales. So, while it may seem like the genre is having a moment on the big and small screens, it’s really always been a mainstay, and the entertainment industry is just loading up on what women audiences have wanted for a long time. Roth moderated the panel, which included Christina Lauren author duo Christina Hobbs and Lauren Billings, The Love Hypothesis and Love, Theoretically author Ali Hazelwood , One and Only author Maurene Goo plus Magic Hour Entertainment co-founder Max Siemers and Rebelle Media co-founders Laura Lewis and Amanda Palley . Related Stories Books Rebelle Media & MGM Television Win Rights To Adapt ‘When In Rome’ Series By Sarah Adams News Colleen Hoover Producing Ali Hazelwood’s Bestseller ‘Love, Theoretically’ At Amazon MGM Studios; Sofia Alvarez Directing “Romance onscreen has, and when I say onscreen, I’m talking about the theatrical screen, has dropped over 75% the last 20 years,” Rebelle Media ’s Laura Lewis said. “That audience hasn’t disappeared, and because of all the things that inspired us to get into the business — those Richard Curtis, Nancy Meyers and Nora Ephron movies and TV shows — we want to bring them back. So that’s what’s inspiring us to get on these books. Watch on Deadline Lewis’ partner Palley broke the news at the end of the panel that Rebelle Media has added Sarah Adams’ When in Rome series to their slate of book adaptations in development . The panel discussion revolved around the draw of romance, both in book form and tv and film form — whether adapted from novels or based on original screenplays — with insights from both authors and executives about how to get past the generic formula of putting a romance together. Most of the panelists favored leaning into specificity and the details that lovers of the genre latch onto while consuming a book, show or rom-com film. “It’s a really cool genre to be a part of because it is written primarily by women, not exclusively [and] primarily for, but not exclusively for women,” Billings said of romance. “It is a genre that embraces diversity. It embraces queerness, embraces so many things, and it has so much cultural and socio-economic power.” Billings and Hobbs, who have their book In a Holidaze coming to Netflix as a film adapted by Tiffany Paulson later this year, met 17 years ago sleeping on the sidewalk at the San Diego Convention Center waiting in line for the The Twilight Saga: New Moon panel featuring the cast of the then upcoming film. Reflecting on this anniversary, Billings commented on the growth of romance publishing’s presence at the convention. Max Siemers, co-founder of the newly-formed Magic Hour Entertainment, which is now behind an adaptation of Christina Lauren’s Love & Other Words , broached the idea that certain times of year (likely Christmas and Valentine’s Day) provide windows to release romantic comedies and dramas set specifically around those holidays but with only really that as the framework.

articles.title: Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa’s MultiChoice
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Stars Emma Sidi & Jack Shep To Join Sky & NBCU For Edinburgh TV Festival Masterclass Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa’s MultiChoice Curiosity Entertainment Enlists Execs Laurie Seidman And John Maatta & Sets Storyteller Media’s Debut Page-To-Screen Slate View All July 28, 2026 12:29am Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada Sylvain Lefevre/Getty Images The $2B acquisition of Africa’s MultiChoice has helped Canal+ post higher half-year revenues and earnings . Unaudited total group revenues saw revenues grow 40% to €4.29 billion ($4.88 billion), though without MultiChoice the growth shrinks to just 1.4% year-on-year compared to 2025’s €3.07B. Similarly, adjusted EBIT (before exceptional items) was up 68% to €433M, from €257M, and had a 10.1% margin. Excluding MultiChoice, the number drops to 13% growth. The market update comes just hours after London-listed Canal+ pledged more than €980M to French and European cinema over five years in a fresh deal with French entertainment bodies. The news was heralded as of unprecedented length for the Paris-based pay-TV giant. Related Stories News Canal+ Pledges More Than $1 Billion For French & European Cinema Over Five Years News Thabo Rametsi Unveiled As Apartheid-Era Music Legend Hugh Masekela In First-Look Image For Bill Condon's 'The Road Home' Canal+ this morning revealed it had hit its target of €250M in synergies resulting from its takeover of African pay-TV giant MultiChoice last year . Watch on Deadline The company has sought to significantly reduce costs in Africa since the buyout, with streamer Showmax discontinued earlier this year in one move that shocked the local industry. The H1 figures reveal Showmax made a €52M loss in H1 of 2025 on revenues of €23M. “Following the acquisition of MultiChoice, our increased scale is starting to deliver the benefits we expected,” said Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada . “We have achieved half of our €250M synergies target and remain well on track for the year, and we confirm our full-year and medium-term guidance.” Studiocanal Canal+’s production arm, Studiocanal, had an “excellent six months on and off screen,” according to Saada, who pointed theatrical successes such as Guru in France and Pressure in the US, and the biggest film deal at Cannes 2026, for The Midnight Library, which sold to Paramount for $36M . The content production, distribution and other segment, which includes Studiocanal and streamer Dailymotion, posted revenues of €356M, up 9.9% YoY. This accounted for 7.8% of Canal+’s overall revenues, down from 9.3% last year. Adjusted EBIT was €28M, which was 3% lower than 2025. “With a slate including Paddington 4 , Zack Snyder’s remake of Escape From New York , our first major South African film production, The Road Home , and Danny Boyle’s Ink , Studiocanal’s momentum looks set to continue,” he added. Back at group level, Saada pointed a systematic review of costs in France last year 2025 was benefitting finances, along with “strong D2C subscriber acquisition and lower churn, plus an ongoing shift to streaming in Poland. In Africa, adjusted EBIT was up 9% excluding MultiChoice, driven by pay-TV growth among other factors. Canal+ said its “turnaround” of MultiChoice was underway and pointed to a long-term rights deal for the Premier Soccer League in South Africa, the 2027 men’s and 2029 women’s rugby world cups across sub-Saharan Africa and a production slate including The Road Home , Heist of Benin and a screen adaptation of bestselling novel Americanah Subscriber acquisition was up 40% in MultiChoice countries compared to H1 2025 in MultiChoice countries, with June the best month “in a decade.” Adjusted EBIT at MultiChoice was up 160% to €143M, from €55M a year ago. This was primarily put down to synergies of €120M, including the impact of Showmax’s discontinuation. articles.title: Black Lives Matter Commitments Failed To Bring About “Structural Change” In UK TV Industry, Finds Diamond Diversity Report
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Cristiano Ronaldo Reportedly Lining Up First Drama Series With Matthew Vaughn, Damian Lewis & Some Big Name Guest Stars Chris Brown Pleads Guilty To Affray Over UK Nightclub Confrontation View All July 28, 2026 1:00am The BBC & HBO's 'I May Destroy You': launched summer 2020 BBC/HBO Commitments made following the Black Lives Matter movement of summer 2020 failed to generate “embedded, structural change” in the UK TV industry, according to the latest Diamond diversity report. Paul Moore, chair of the Creative Diversity Network (CDN), which compiles the annual reports, said the recent decline in representation of Black, Asian and minority ethnic people both on and off screen shows progress has “stalled or drifted backward” since broadcasters made major promises more than five years ago. According to the report, the percentage of on-screen roles taken by Black, Asian and minority ethnic actors and presenters has plateaued since 2022 at 23.2%, while off-screen it has fallen by 1 percentage point to 13%. The latter figure is comfortably below the 17.9% national workforce average. Related Stories News Emmys On-Screen Diversity Hits 11-Year Low With 2026 Nominees News 'Police Academy' Reboot With Key & Peele Was Scrapped After Mike Brown Shooting, Says Writer: "We're Not Making A Cop Comedy Right Now" Sparked by the murder of George Floyd, the Black Lives Matter movement initially felt as though it was having a long-lasting impact across the pond. All broadcasters unveiled lofty commitments to improve diversity on and off-screen, while the topic dominated chatter at that year’s Edinburgh TV Festival amid critiques of sluggish diversity gains in an industry dominated by gatekeepers from privileged backgrounds. Watch on Deadline Diamond’s findings will therefore be a big disappointment to those at the coalface of improving representation for non-white people in the UK TV industry. They come a year after a weighty study found that Black professionals were experiencing systemic racism and faltering career progression, despite years of industry diversity initiatives. Of all the major networks based in the UK, Paramount, which owns Channel 5 (now 5), had the lowest proportion of contributions from Black, Asian and minority ethnic people, with the BBC top for on-screen and Channel 4 off-screen. The proportion of non-white people in senior roles has also fallen since 2022 to 12% and remains stubbornly at 2019 levels, the report found. Last year, this group took up only 10.9% of executive producer roles, for example. There were some green shoots, such as lead actors from non-white backgrounds hitting 34.9% last year, almost double the national workforce average, while writers from non-white backgrounds was up at 21.3%. But ultimately, Moore said Diamond’s tracking of UK TV industry diversity data over the past nine years shows flatlining progress. “The real power of Diamond lies in its ability to look beyond headlines and track changes over time to expose where progress has stalled or drifted backward,” said Moore, who is communications and corporate affairs chief at ITV. “For example, the recent decline in Black representation suggests that initial commitments made following the Black Lives Matter movement did not lead to embedded, structural change.” Earlier this year, the CDN revealed it was revamping Diamond , allowing for improved reporting, which will come into force later this year. articles.title: Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ & Pablo Larraín Series ‘My Sad Dead’ Among Titles Added To San Sebastian Lineup
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Animaginary Partners With Gersh To Rep Worldwide Rights On Michael Mankowski’s ‘Getting Lost’ Animated Series Armand Assante To Narrate Documentary Feature ‘The Streets of Little Italy: 100 Years Of San Gennaro’ Christine Vachon, Ewan McGregor & Sarah Brocklehurst Among Names Set For Edinburgh Film Festival’s 2026 Industry Programme View All July 28, 2026 2:29am Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care' © Joseph Lynn / Thin Man Films Ltd. Mike Leigh’s latest feature Tender Loving Care and My Sad Dead , a new series from Chilean filmmaker Pablo Larraín, are among the titles that were announced this morning for the San Sebastian Film Festival. Scroll down for the full list of titles. My Sad Dead will screen at San Sebastian in its feature-length format. Starring are Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, and Carolina Álvarez. The project is based on four short stories by Mariana Enríquez, and tells the story of Ema, a woman with the ability to see and hear the dead. The San Sebastian screening will be a World Premiere. Related Stories Festivals San Sebastián Film Festival Appoints New Director News 'Los Domingos' Claims Golden Shell, 'The Voice Of Hind Rajab' Takes Audience Award At San Sebastián Film Festival - Full List Of Winners Leigh’s Tender Loving Care will arrive at San Sebastian after a world premiere at TIFF. Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, and Alice Bailey Johnson star in the film. No synopsis for Tender Loving Care has been provided on either the San Sebastian or TIFF website. San Sebastian simply describes the film as an “insightful exploration of the contemporary world.” Watch on Deadline Other titles added to San Sebastian today include 7:40 ce matin-là / Milo , the latest feature film from Nicole Garcia. Marion Cotillard and Théodore Pellerin star in the project, which tells the story of a woman fresh out of jail as she takes on a waitress job in a café to get closer to a young boy who works in the area. Norwegian filmmaker Hans Petter Moland also returns to the San Sebastian Official Selection with Markens Grode / Growth of the Soil , a story set in northern Norway about a couple who must put their love to the test when faced with looming challenges. The film is based on the Nobel Prize-winning novel by Knut Hamsun. Today’s titles join the nine films already announced for the Official Selection. Those titles include El mal padre , from Roberto Bueso; Sants / Saints , from Mikel Gurrea; and 5 minutos más / 5 more minutes , from Javier Ruiz Caldera. The 2026 San Sebastian Film Festival runs from September 18 to 26. San Sebastian 2026: 7:40 ce matin-là / MILO Nicole Garcia (Algeria) Country(ies) of production: France. Cast: Marion Cotillard, Théodore Pellerin, Artus , Laure Calamy, Alexis Manenti, Anne Brochet, Eric Elmosnino, Charles Berling Alice arrives in a quiet provincial town and takes a job at a local café, blending easily into a life that isn’t hers. Her presence is no coincidence. She is there because of Milo, a young mechanic who works at a nearby garage. To him, Alice is a stranger. To her, he is someone tied to a past she has never truly left behind. As buried tensions begin to surface and Milo drifts toward uncertain ground, both are pushed to a crossroads: is it possible to rebuild a bond that shattered decades ago? Artakalan / What Remains Yeşim Ustaoğlu (Turkey) Country(ies) of production: Turkey – France – Luxembourg – Bulgaria. Cast: Öykü Karayel, Metin Akdülger, Ali Kayra Kul, İlyas Salman A poetess breaks out of her suffocating life in order to get back in touch with her inner voice and conscience, questioning accustomed concepts of family and the meaning of life and paving a new path for her family members, as well. Glaxo Benjamín Naishtat (Argentina) Country(ies) of production: Brazil – Argentina. Cast : Lali Espósito, Marcelo Subiotto, Esteban Bigliardi, Esteban Lamothe, Manu Fanego, Alan Sabbagh Chivilcoy, 1957. In a quiet Argentinian town, the arrival of an ominous former police commissioner and his seductive wife fractures the bond between four inseparable young men. Decades later, the past resurfaces, forcing them to confront old wounds, guilt, and the possibility of revenge in a country which has lost its innocence. Markens Grode / Growth of the Soil Hans Petter Moland (Norway) Country(ies) of production: Norway – Denmark – Germany. Cast: Herbert Nordrum, Asta Kamma August, Gard B. Eidsvold A stranger appears over the mountain, carrying little more than his determination. Isak, a man without a past, seeks a place to settle and carve life from the earth. High above the tree line, he finds a barren stretch of land, as unforgiving as it is full of promise. The land tests him to his limits, until he meets Inger, a solitary woman shaped by resilience and quiet secrecy. Together, they endure the elements and build a life, cultivating both the soil and a growing family as the seasons turn. Yet as years pass and the world closes in, and time, hardship, and desire reshape them. Mis muertos tristes / My Sad Dead Pablo Larraín (Chile) Country(ies) of production: Argentina – Chile. Cast: Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Carolina Álvarez Based on the work from Mariana Enriquez and directed by Pablo Larraín, My Sad Dead follows Ema, who can see and hear the dead. After her mother’s death, Ema receives an unexpected visit from her niece Julie, with whom she shares the same unsettling gift. With Julie’s return, family secrets and wounds that never fully healed will resurface —but so will a strange phenomenon from which no one will emerge unscathed. The entire neighborhood will sense presences and hear the distinctive sounds of their own dead. Muyou no hito / In My Father’s Room Maha Harada (Japan) Country(ies) of production: Japan. Cast: Yu Aoi, Issey Ogata, Eita Nagayama, Eri Watanabe Satomi works at an art museum until an envelope arrives, containing a mysterious key. It leads to an unknown room once belonging to her late father, who died alone a month earlier. Drawn by this small object, she retraces his final days: a man seemingly left behind by society, yet sustained by a quiet devotion to words, the art of tea, and subtle beauty. Through the traces of his solitude, Satomi slowly discovers the quiet grace of the world he inhabited. Tender Loving Care Mike Leigh (United Kingdom) Country(ies) of production: United Kingdom – USA – Singapore. Cast: Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson Cannes Festival’s Palme d’Or winner and Academy Award nominee Mike Leigh returns with his next feature film, continuing his insightful exploration of the contemporary world. articles.title: Marion Cotillard New Image & First Sales Unveiled For Nicole Garcia’s San Sebastian-Bound ‘Milo’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Canal+ Pledges More Than $1 Billion For French & European Cinema Over Five Years Italian Film Bodies Slam Venice Over Lack Of Women In Competition: “It’s A One-Dimensional, Male-Dominated Selection” Michael Pomeroy’s ‘Paul & Greg & Amelia’ With Quinn Jackson, Christopher Ryan, Matt Hardy & Terra Layne Wraps Ahead Of TIFF Sales Push View All July 28, 2026 2:50am Milo ©️ 2026 TRÉSOR FILMS - STUDIOCANAL - FRANCE 3 CINÉMA - MARCEL FILMS - LES FILMS PELLEAS - ARTEMIS PRODUCTIONS EXCLUSIVE: Studiocanal and Trésor Films have unveiled a new image of Marion Cotillard and Théodore Pellerin in Nicola Garcia’s Milo to coincide with the film being announced for competition in San Sebastian Film Festival’s 74th edition in September. Studiocanal, which co-produces and is handling international sales, has also posted a handful of early deals on the work with the film acquired for Canada (Mongrel Media), Scandinavia (Scanbox), Switzerland (Frenetic), Greece (Spenzos), Portugal (Lusomundo), CIS (Capella) and Ex-Yugoslavia (MCF). Studiocanal will handle the release in Germany. Related Stories News Mike Leigh's 'Tender Loving Care' & Pablo Larraín Series 'My Sad Dead' Among Titles Added To San Sebastian Lineup News Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa's MultiChoice Billed as a tale of “buried wounds, impossible choices and the fragile hope of rebuilding the bonds that define us”, Milo stars Cotillard as a woman called Alice who arrives in a quiet provincial town and takes a job at a local café, blending easily into a life that isn’t hers. Watch on Deadline It soon becomes apparent that her presence is no coincidence. She is there because of Milo (Pellerin), a young mechanic who works at a nearby garage. To him, Alice is a stranger. To her, he is someone tied to a past she has never truly left behind. It has been a high profile year on the festival circuit for Vie en Rose Oscar winner Cotillard who was at Cannes in May in Guillaume Canet’s Karma and Bertrand Mandico’s Roma Elastica, as she steps up the pace on her acting commitments. She previously worked with Garcia on her penultimate film, the post-WW2 romantic drama From the Land of the Moon . “The new role is diametrically opposed to the role of From the Land of the Moon . There was an emotional romanticism in that film, while here, on the contrary, it’s a much quieter role, contained, and deeply felt,” Garcia told Deadline of Cotillard’s role back in February . “There’s a silence filled with emotions and confessions that are difficult to express. You can sense her character has grown accustomed to the silence but is also grappling with it. It’s a real balancing act and it takes a great actress to pull that off.” Co-star Pellerin has made waves over the past year for for his performance as a young man diagnosed with throat cancer in Pauline Loquès’ 2025 Cannes Critics Week title Nino, for he won the Best Male Hope Cesar in February as well as the Louis Roederer Foundation Rising Star Award. Further cast members include Artus ( A Little Something Extra ), Alexis Manenti ( Undercover ), Anne Brochet ( Cyrano de Bergerac ), Éric Elmosnino ( The Belier Family ) and Charles Berling ( What’s In A Name ). Garcia directs from a screenplay she co-wrote with longtime collaborator Jacques Fieschi, with the collaboration of Laurette Polmanss and Olivier Demangel. The film marks the fourth collaboration between producer and Trésor Films head Alain Attal and Garcia, after Charlie Says , A View of Love and From The Land of the Moon . The film is co-produced by Canal+ subsidiary Studiocanal – which holds worldwide distribution rights and handles worldwide sales – with France 3 Cinéma, Marcel Films and Artémis Productions, with the support of CANAL+, Ciné+ OCS and France Télévisions. The picture will be released in French cinemas on January 20, 2027. articles.title: Revealed: The Early-Stage Plans For A New TV Festival In Edinburgh
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Cristiano Ronaldo Reportedly Lining Up First Drama Series With Matthew Vaughn, Damian Lewis & Some Big Name Guest Stars Chris Brown Pleads Guilty To Affray Over UK Nightclub Confrontation View All July 28, 2026 3:15am Richard Gadd; Edinburgh Fringe and Phoebe Waller-Bridge Josh Telles for Deadline/Getty EXCLUSIVE: With the TV Festival leaving Edinburgh for the first time in its 51-year history, organizers in the Scottish capital are refusing to rest on their laurels. Deadline can reveal that early-stage plans are afoot to launch a new TV festival in Edinburgh. These plans have been hatched prior to the final one taking place in less than a month’s time and are understood to have been discussed at a recent roundtable with figures from the local sector. Screen Scotland , the body that represents the interests of the Scottish film and TV industry, commissioned a piece of work earlier this year examining what a new fest might look like along with the implications of the TV Festival’s relocation for the Scottish screen sector and wider Edinburgh festivals landscape. The expectation from many was that Edinburgh would lose its role as host city to Greater Manchester , home of new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham , and organizers in Edinburgh wanted to get ahead of the game. Related Stories Festivals Christine Vachon, Ewan McGregor & Sarah Brocklehurst Among Names Set For Edinburgh Film Festival's 2026 Industry Programme News Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film 'These Violent Delights' -- First Look Trailer Rowan Woods, the former creative chief at the Edinburgh TV Festival , has been leading on this work for months as an independent consultant. Woods, whose role was limited to the research and report itself, has just reported back to Screen Scotland with a set of recommendations and range of options. Watch on Deadline While we have not seen the recommendations, Deadline is told that Woods delivered a number of them and they are varied. They were discussed at a roundtable last week in Glasgow with around 20 figures from the local TV industry, we understand. The decision whether to push on with a new festival now lies with Screen Scotland. We hear an announcement could be made in the coming weeks, possibly before the final TV Festival starts on August 25. A Screen Scotland spokeswoman told Deadline the body has been “working with partners since the spring to explore options should the TV Festival’s board decide – as it now has – to break with the event’s history and move the festival to England.” The spokeswoman added that Screen Scotland is “looking at the opportunity for innovation in August provided by the TV Festival’s departure and exploring the best way to continue to support Scotland-based production businesses to access key TV decision makers in Edinburgh during August.” Were this new Edinburgh fest to run in August, which given the timing of the world-famous Edinburgh Fringe would make perfect sense, it would be parking its tanks almost directly on the lawn of the TV Festival in Greater Manchester , which will also likely take place in August. The relocation of the TV Festival has been a huge story for the industry this year and connected sources said there is now a political will in Scotland to get behind another event. Scottish government officials were clear to TV Festival executives and its board members during the bidding process that they would back a new event if Edinburgh lost the fest, we understand. Our story also comes as the Edinburgh International Film Festival expands. Deadline revealed last month that the fest is launching a conference , with first speaker set as BFI chief Ben Roberts, while the majority of last year’s competition titles landed distribution in the UK and U.S. “The world comes here in August” Hollywood royalty Shonda Rhimes was awarded , ast year’s inaugural Edinburgh Fellowship. Image: Edinburgh TV Festival Unsurprisingly, in what is an incredibly connected Scottish TV industry, there have been rumblings and mutterings about the potential for a new festival for weeks. Deadline spoke to a number of executives, all of whom had heard these rumors but were split on the shape they thought a new fest should take, or whether Edinburgh should host one at all. One indie boss, who has been heavily involved with the fest over the years, said the Edinburgh Fringe in August allows the city to offer something “different and unique.” Organizers of any new fest must therefore think big, think global and be talent-led, this source said, providing something that contrasts with other UK industry events that have become a crucial part of the annual TV calendar like Content London, the London TV Screenings and the Creative Cities Convention, along with, of course, the new TV Festival in Greater Manchester. “The world comes here in August,” said the indie boss. “American agencies, book publishers, high-profile talent and decision makers arrive in Edinburgh and want to be there. If there’s a date in your calendar that allows you to have fun and maybe find the next [ Baby Reindeer creator Richard] Gadd, well which would you choose?” This indie boss put forward the argument made by many prior to the fest relocation decision being made, which was that relocating the fest would sever talent pipelines by ending the TV Festival’s alchemy with the Fringe. Speaking to Deadline back in March, a frustrated Jon Thoday, who runs agency-producer Avalon, said “no-one from Avalon [will be going to the TV Festival in Greater Manchester] if I’ve got anything to do with it.” His argument goes that TV commissioners and executives discover the talent of tomorrow like Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Gadd and many more via the Fringe when they come to the TV Festival. On the other side of the coin, one Scottish industry executive said a new fest gifts an opportunity to think locally. “I think the money would be better spent on helping freelancers or production companies with training,” he added. “We could do a freelancers festival that is more sustainable and affordable.” This person questioned whether those in charge of the new fest will opt for a “glamor project” over their more local proposal. However, a different indie boss based out of Scotland pondered whether a local fest would feel “small, parochial and poorly attended” when compared with the might of the relocated TV Festival. In difficult times and with commissioning opportunities dimming, this source queried whether there needs to be a festival at all. “It’s too late,” they mused. “If there is any spare money honestly I would spend it on grants to enable good quality program ideas to happen. We need to create jobs for freelancers and production companies.” Regardless of its potential to be seen as a break from the past, any new fest would have big shoes to fill. The Edinburgh TV Festival has spent 50 years attracting thousands of the great and the good of the industry along with plenty from the other side of the pond including, just last year, Hollywood royalty in Shonda Rhimes and Tina Fey. Its annual MacTaggart lecture is often a headline grabber and it always features talks from the top network heads including the new BBC Director General this year for what will be his first big set-piece address. In what is a crowded UK events calendar, the Edinburgh – soon to be Greater Manchester – TV Festival clearly remains one of the year’s focal points. Industry eyes are trained on what happens next. Work has already begun. articles.title: Tom Holland Says Some of His Movies Are “Sh**,” Making Them Hard to Promote
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 26, 2026 1:09pm Tom Holland Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Tom Holland is getting candid about the challenge of promoting a film that he wasn’t exactly a fan of. During a recent interview on the Dish Podcast , the actor said he’s been “absolutely loving” his press tours this summer for The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day because he’s really proud of those movies. But he can’t say that about all the projects in his filmography. “When you’re doing press for movies you’re really proud of, it’s really easy,” he explained. “Because when they ask you questions about why should people go and watch this movie, you’re not lying to anyone. You really feel like people should go see it.” Related Stories Movies Universal Responds to 'The Odyssey' Leaks on Social Media Movies 'The Odyssey' Holds Strong for Big Second Weekend of $87M, Passes $600M Globally “I’ve had experiences before when people say, like, ‘Why should you see this movie?’ And in the back of your mind, you’re like, ‘You shouldn’t, because it’s shit,'” he added with a laugh. Holland didn’t name the specific films he was referring to, as he would have much rather continued the high praise of his latest pics. “It’s felt really like a bit of a victory lap, to be honest,” Holland said of The Odyssey and Brand New Day . “I’ve really enjoyed it. I’m super proud of both of the films.” The Christopher Nolan-directed pic , based on Homer’s ancient Greek poem, follows King Odysseus’ (Matt Damon) dangerous voyage back to Ithaca after the Trojan War, including battles with mythical creatures, as he attempts to reunite with his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway), and son, Telemachus ( Holland). The film also stars Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong’o, John Leguizamo , Elliot Page, Mia Goth, Corey Hawkins, Jon Bernthal , Samantha Morton, Travis Scott and Benny Safdie. Since The Odyssey has already hit theaters — where it’s been dominating, sailing past $600 million globally in its second weekend — The Crowded Room actor has turned his attention back to Spider-Man promotion, which releases on July 31. But he’s still grateful for everything he’s learned from his Odyssey co-stars throughout the film’s respective press tour. “I’ve had the pleasure of sitting down with Anne Hathaway for the last three days and doing press with her,” Holland said. “For me, that’s been an awesome learning experience. She’s such a pro.” As for Brand New Day , Holland reunites with his wife, Zendaya, onscreen and Jacob Batalon for the fourth installment. The film sees Holland’s Peter Parker living entirely alone as Spider-Man in a world that doesn’t remember him. That’s until mounting pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him triggers a dangerous change, while a powerful new villain emerges. THR
