articles.title: Martin Scorsese Stars in ‘Family Blend’ Directed by Daughter Francesca for Coffee Brand Lavazza
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All July 26, 2026 4:53pm Francesca Scorsese and Martin Scorsese attend the 5th annual Academy Museum Gala at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles on Oct. 18, 2025. (Photo by Amy Sussman/Getty Images) Lights, camera, caffeinate. Martin Scorsese took a break from the director’s chair to step in front of the camera for a change for Lavazza’s new branded miniseries Family Blend celebrating “the magic of coffee.” True to its title, Scorsese isn’t alone in the project as it’s directed by and co-starring his daughter, Francesca Scorsese . A few other famous faces help fill out the five-episode project, including Jason Biggs and Adrien Brody . There’s a lot of blending going on, too, in the locations and content as Francesca filmed the branded series in places that have helped shape her father’s life and creative efforts, like the Little Italy neighborhood in New York and his own virtual production center in Brooklyn. Per Lavazza, the series is meant to explore “the deep bond, shared memories and passing of the torch between two artistic visions” with coffee playing a prominent role. But they also get a playful assist from familial banter. Related Stories Movies Ellen Burstyn to Receive Venice Lifetime Golden Lion Movies "The White Devil" Takes Karlovy Vary: Robert Richardson Receives Honor From a Paper-Ripping Harvey Keitel “The Family Blend series shows how coffee acts as a universal bridge, bringing together different stories and creative visions,” said Lavazza Group chief marketing officer Carlo Colpo of the project, which aligns with the brand’s communication platform “Pleasure Makes Us Human.” “With this project, we are thrilled to portray coffee as a cultural gesture that spans generations and languages, serving as a meeting point for creativity and identity. The collaboration with Martin and Francesca Scorsese brings to life a unique dialogue that blends the depth of cinematic language with modern digital formats.” Credit for Family Blend goes to Romilda De Luca of RDL Worldwide/Publicis Group and Lisa Frechette of Sikelia Productions. Propagate Content produced the series with Ben Silverman, Howard T. Owens and Drew Buckley producing on behalf of that company. Maruri Group helped develop the creative vision with support from Joey Payne. The first episode dropped earlier this week, with new installments rolling out once a month through November on the brand’s and talents’ global social channels. See the first one, “But First … Coffee,” below. It was filmed at Martin Scorsese NYU Virtual Production Center in Brooklyn, New York, a site launched in fall 2024 by NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts. “Elizabeth Street,” which drops in August, features a nostalgic walk down the street where Martin grew up with his parents amid the “relentless chaos of New York constantly interrupting their talk.” “Back to Tisch,” releasing in September, finds the father and daughter returning to their alma mater, NYU, in the 1960s. The October release of “Where Everybody Knows Your Name” finds Francesca offering a tour inside Di Palo’s Fine Foods in Little Italy while waiting on her father. Lastly, in November comes “But Last … Coffee,” a finale set in an iconic New York cafe where Francesca (joined by Biggs) challenges her father to break his strict black coffee routine and try new blends and modern preparations. Francesca previously directed the shorts Crimson Ties and Fish Out of Water and an episode of Martin Scorsese Presents: The Saints. THR

articles.title: On Heels of World Cup, Polo Star Nacho Figueras Says Horseback Sport Has “All the Ingredients to Be the Next Big Thing”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tim Chan Plus Icon Tim Chan @mrtimchan Follow Sign Up View All July 26, 2026 6:57pm Nacho Figueras and Aurora Figueras Blaquier join St. Regis Hotels & Resorts in celebrating the St. Regis British Open for The Cowdrey Gold Cup Polo Final at Cowdray Park Polo Club on July 19, 2026 in Midhurst, England. Dave Benett Polo legend Nacho Figueras says the centuries-old horseback sport could finally be poised for a mainstream breakthrough thanks to the recent success of the World Cup . Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter at The St. Regis British Open Polo Championship for the Cowdray Gold Cup in the UK last weekend, Figueras says the resounding buzz and fan engagement around the World Cup has him believing that polo could find a similar audience. “I think it’s been an incredible moment for sports in America,” he says, also citing the New York Knicks’ recent NBA championship win. “People are learning to love sports events, especially when it’s very well put together, and polo, I think, has all the ingredients to be the next big thing.” Related Stories TV WNBA on Sling TV: Here's How to Watch the 2026 WNBA All-Star Game Live Online TV Spain Scores World Cup Docuseries at Prime Video While Figueras appeared in the 2024 Prince Harry-produced Netflix documentary, Polo , the Argentine sporting icon says he’s working on his own real-life project to “bring polo to the cities.” Describing it as “Formula 1 meets Sail GP meets Padal [and] mixed with the Longines equestrian series ,” the polo star says he envisions events that will be “like the F1 version of polo,” complete with a film crew to capture how it all comes together. “The idea is to do a Drive to Survive -type thing, because I think that giving people access to our kitchen and the kitchens of the athletes, really helps you feel connected to the person on the horse,” he says. Plus, he adds, “Polo has horses, good looking men and women, athleticism and beautiful spots [where the matches take place]. What else could you want?” Assouline ASSOULINE CLASSICS COLLECTION Polo Heritage Co-written by Figueras $120 Buy Now AT ASSOULINE Figueras was among the VIP guests taking in the Cowdray Gold Cup in West Sussex last weekend from the St. Regis tent. As the official “St. Regis Connoisseur ,” the athlete and model got to enjoy a rare day off from the polo field, instead watching the proceedings alongside stars like Andrew Scott, Gwendoline Christie, British designer Giles Deacon and writer Jack Guinness, who all enjoyed storied St. Regis rituals like a champagne sabrage, and sips of the brand’s signature Bloody Mary (the tomato-based cocktail was said to have originated in the U.S. at the King Cole Room inside the St. Regis Hotel in New York in 1934). Giles Deacon, Gwendoline Christie, Jack Guinness and Andrew Scott at the St. Regis British Open for The Cowdrey Gold Cup Polo Final at Cowdray Park Polo Club on July 19, 2026 in Midhurst, England. Photo by Dave Benett Guests at the polo event also got a preview of the St. Regis London, expected to open in the city’s Mayfair neighborhood this fall. Occupying the former Westbury Hotel location at the intersection of Bond Street and Conduit Street, the new property will feature 193 guest rooms inspired by its Savile Row and luxury fashion house and auction house surroundings. The property will also open with Le Perroquet, a French brasserie-style restaurant from acclaimed Chef Daniel Rose, best known for La Bourse et La Vie in Paris and the Michelin-starred Le Coucou in New York. “St. Regis is an old brand with heritage, with family values, and with an actual history and connection to polo,” Figueras says, noting that the hotel chain’s founding family, the Astors, were a prominent fixture at polo matches on New York’s Governors Island. “This event and this partnership just makes sense.” Agata Noweta Studio The Gaston Polo Team, led by Chilean patron Jean Paul Luksic, was crowned Cowdray Gold Cup champions after a nail-biting 9-8 victory over the previously unbeaten Dubai Polo Team. While Figueras was mum on who he was cheering for — explaining that he has friends and fellow Argentine players on both teams — he says the weekend event in England was further proof that the sport is ready for a U.S. invasion. And in addition to his planned polo event series and documentary, Figueras says he has one other idea he’d like to pitch. “I feel very bullish about doing a scripted thing,” the memorable Gossip Girl guest star says, noting that, “what Yellowstone did for Western was incredible. I would love to work with a guy like Taylor Sheridan, who is really one of the most incredible storytellers out there and who loves horses, and say, ‘Hey, I think that polo could be a perfect anchor for one of your amazing shows.” “I also love Succession ,” Figueras adds, “so I believe that this polo show could be the perfect marriage between Yellowstone and Succession .” Has he been in touch with Sheridan? “No, I don’t know him, so maybe this [article] will help,” the dashing polo star says with his magazine-cover smile. “Taylor when you read this, please get in touch.” THR

articles.title: Dylan Mulvaney Responds After Trump Mocks Her and CNN’s Kaitlan Collins at White House Correspondents’ Dinner
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All July 26, 2026 8:59pm Dylan Mulvaney Maya Dehlin Spach/Getty Images Transgender advocate and actress Dylan Mulvaney has responded to President Donald Trump after the latter mocked both her and CNN’s Kaitlan Collins during his speech at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner on Friday night. At the event, which had been postponed from April after a gunman fired shots as the first dinner was under way, Trump gave a speech wherein he compared the two women after Collins accepted an award for her working covering the administration.. “I want to personally congratulate CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on receiving her award,” Trump said. “It was all about me. It’s a fake — she shouldn’t get the award, it was a fake. But I didn’t mind. I said, ‘Kaitlan, congratulations.’ But it was fake, there’s no question about it.” Related Stories News President Trump Roasts Media at Rescheduled, Pared-Down White House Correspondents' Dinner News Spencer Pratt Tears Into Gavin Newsom, Rob Bonta Over Paramount Lawsuit in Lengthy Video Rant After criticizing Collins for her facial expressions, Trump then compared her to Mulvaney, mentioning the 2023 controversy surrounding the latter’s Bud Light commercial . Three years ago, Mulvaney made an ad for Bud Light that was met with criticism from conservatives who launched a boycott against the beer brand, leading to a decline in sales. “I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said Friday. “Dylan Mulvaney cost Bud Light $35 billion in market cap. That was the worst commercial ever made by the way, for those few people who want to hear that. Most people don’t care, but I would. I wouldn’t want to hire Dylan any time soon.” For her part, Collins posted a series of photos on Instagram after the event that included a quote from Eleanor Roosevelt: “No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.” She captioned the post: “he second best part of last night’s White House Correspondents Dinner was receiving an award from my friend and mentor, @wolfblitzer. The first was reminding everyone why the First Amendment — and asking uncomfortable questions that people in power don’t like — matters.” On Sunday morning, Trump doubled down on his comparison of the two women, posting a photo of Mulvaney from her Bud Light ad that had been edited to show Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body. Later that day, Mulvaney posted a nearly four-minute video on social media in which she noted that Trump had mentioned her four times on Friday night and she felt the need to respond. She started by congratulating Collins on her award and giving her praise. “I would like to … tell her that I’m incredibly honored to be compared to her in any way, and I hope that she keeps doing all the great work,” Mulvaney said. Mulvaney continued: “Now, the president also brought up a video I did over three years ago, and mind you, I’ve been kind of flying under the radar, keeping up a pretty low profile, just like doing my little musicals, singing, dancing. And yet I am still his topic of conversation all these years later. And it seems to me that I might be like the one that got away for these men. Like, I am permanently burned into their retinas. I am microchipped into their minds.” Mulvaney noted that a few weeks ago, she might have been more upset about Trump’s comments, but shared that she’d been “ghosted last month by a hookup who I really liked,” which taught her something about how she wanted to be treated. “What I realized from that experience was that I shouldn’t want to be with someone who doesn’t really want to be with me,” she said. “So maybe I shouldn’t want to be professionally supported by an administration that doesn’t personally support me or so many others in this country. Food for thought. In fact, maybe being publicly mocked and criticized by this administration is actually like the greatest compliment of all, because it puts me in the company of some of like the most brilliant, empathetic people in our world today.” She continued: “But I do still wonder, like, why is it so important to them that I don’t find success? Like, what is it that I have that they don’t? Oh my God, freedom. I am free in a way that they will never have the privilege to experience, and they want to use their power to take away my freedom, but what they don’t understand is that my freedom has like zero contingency on what they can provide for me because my freedom is fully dependent on the moment that I acknowledged my real authentic self and every day since. And sharing that with the world, it’s just icing on the cake, but they don’t want me to be able to share that because it would mean young people realizing that if someone like me can be themselves and find success and freedom, then they can find success and freedom for themselves too.” She wrapped up her video by encouraging viewers to support trans and non-binary people. “And lastly, to the president, thank you for reminding me that I am more powerful than I even knew,” she added. Watch her video below. @dylanmulvaney A response 🇺🇸❤️ please support trans and non binary people today and every day ♬ I Am America – Shea Diamond THR

articles.title: ‘President Curtis’ Creator Dan Harmon on Trump, Obama Influencing Show and His Vision for ‘Rick and Morty’ Movie
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 26, 2026 10:21pm A scene from Adult Swim's 'Rick and Morty' spinoff 'President Curtis.' Courtesy of Adult Swim Logo text President Curtis is getting sworn into the Rick and Morty universe. Veteran actor Keith David voices the titular commander in chief on President Curtis , the Rick and Morty spinoff that premiered Sunday on Adult Swim following the season nine finale for the flagship series. Stephanie Beatriz and Jim Rash round out the cast for the new project that centers on the leader of the free world and his quirky staff as they navigate an array of unusual crises. David originated the role of President Andre Curtis during a season two episode of Rick and Morty back in 2015 and has continued to return periodically throughout the series. President Curtis co-creator James Siciliano recalls talk of a spinoff happening as a natural extension of the Rick and Morty team working on the Thanksgiving episode for season five, with Rick seeking a presidential turkey pardon. Related Stories Movies The Doom Boom: Marvel Studios Brings 'Doomsday' and More to Its Most Crowded Comic-Con Panel Ever Movies Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool Crashes Comic-Con to Beg for 'Avengers: Doomsday' Role “We started to see a more dialed-in world for Curtis there, with spider-FDR, the French assassin hidden in the Statue of Liberty — the National Treasure element of that stuff,” Siciliano, a longtime member of the Rick and Morty staff, tells The Hollywood Reporter . “We could see more of an X Files world that could be built out and wouldn’t necessarily be redundant with the Rick and Morty universe.” President Curtis Courtesy of Adult Swim Siciliano and fellow President Curtis series creator Dan Harmon recall the writing team initially suggesting qualities that have cemented previous real-life U.S. presidents as particularly memorable. Harmon notes that he personally has been fascinated by Harry S. Truman, while other writers brought up Teddy Roosevelt — and, of course, Donald Trump and Barack Obama . “The conversations about Obama and Trump were inevitable,” Harmon admits. “Curtis has a naïveté that you could overlap with Trump, who is like, ‘I’m an outsider, and I consider this job simple, and I don’t care about the bureaucracy of it.’ On the Obama side, it’s the charmer and the guy who gets organic joy in being liked — that whole rock star aspect of Obama. But mostly just more legendary aspects of presidents from the past, all Serpentor’d into a test tube baby that then becomes our version of maybe Martin Sheen in West Wing , where it’s our fantasy president, warts and all.” For fans hoping to catch Rick and Morty popping up on President Curtis (mild spoilers ahead), rest assured that the adventure-seeking duo are indeed part of the pilot, although they will not appear again in the first season. Luckily, there is more President Curtis to come, as the show’s team announced Saturday at San Diego Comic-Con that the spinoff had scored an early renewal for a second season . Rick and Morty Everett “If we didn’t do that, people would be waiting for it,” Siciliano says of writing Rick and Morty into the President Curtis pilot. “In the first season, that’s their only appearance, but that’s not to say that we have anything against them appearing in the future. We really wanted to have this show just be able to get its own identity and breathe a little bit, so that people felt like it was its own show.” Harmon concurs: “If the show has a life of its own, then we can go Dick Wolf nuts with the crossovers and have Detective Munch all over SVU . But we look forward to earning that.” The President Curtis launch arrives just weeks after Rick and Morty landed its third Emmy Award nomination for best animated series, having won in 2018 and 2020. This year marks the show’s first such nomination after a turbulent stretch in recent years that saw Justin Roiland (who co-created the series with Harmon) exit following felony domestic abuse charges that have since been dismissed. The titular voice roles were recast in light of Roiland’s firing, with Ian Cardoni replacing him as inventor Rick Sanchez, while Harry Belden took over as teen grandson Morty. “It is an incredibly important nomination for us because the show has gone through transitions of such peril,” Harmon candidly shares. “To me, it feels like we are an athlete back on a field after a major injury, and so it is an honor to be nominated. It is all I need. I’m happy to go and watch Smiling Friends win or whatever the case, but I’m so grateful for that nomination.” President Curtis Courtesy of Adult Swim President Curtis is not the only potential opportunity for expansion for the Rick and Morty world. THR recently reported that supervising director Jacob Hair was in talks to helm an animated feature version of the series for Warner Bros. Although the possible film does not yet have a script, Harmon notes that it does have “a technically approved idea that we’re dreaming away on.” He was late to checking out Denis Villeneuve’s Dune films but reveals that they now might serve as inspiration: “I just watched the Dune movies because of messing around with the Rick and Morty movie script. I was like, ‘Oh, my God, I’m so late to Dune.’ It’s so rad.” As for his hopes with the Rick and Morty film, Harmon adds, “It would be my goal, however self-destructive, to make it the greatest movie ever to exist. That might make it hard to write. It would probably be a sci-fi epic, transcending time and space, but not in a way that was unsatisfying. It would probably blend colors as varied in its palette as Lethal Weapon 2 and Dune 2: Toon , as well as Indiana Jones and everything. One could argue that it’s a concept that would be my undoing and the franchise’s as well, since me having permission to think about stuff is not the recipe for success that people would think. It’s more of a trailhead to hell, traditionally.” THR

articles.title: Don’t Miss the Swiss at Locarno: From a Hunt for Loot, ‘The Chilean’ and Don Quixote to ‘Small Talk’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 26, 2026 11:59pm ‘The Chilean’ Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Ready for a bit of Swiss bliss on the big screen? The 79th edition of Switzerland’s Locarno Film Festival is set to be a showcase of adventurous new cinema from around the globe, including homegrown productions from Swiss filmmakers and/or producers. Various sections of the fest, running Aug. 5-16, will serve up homemade cinematic fare. In addition, the popular “Panorama Suisse” section will put the spotlight on “Swiss films that have enjoyed success at festivals, found an audience in cinemas, or are currently released in the country.” Plus, the Locarno Kids Screenings program also includes two titles with Swiss participation. Related Stories Movies Ontario Wildfires Prompt Mask-Up Orders and Drone Bans on Film Sets -- But Production Rolls On TV After Atsuko Okatsuka Came to America, Social Media Knocked Down Barriers to Global Reach For those looking for some Swiss cinematic bliss and trying to avoid having Swiss cheese-sized holes in their Locarno schedules, THR is below highlighting a selection of Swiss treats screening at Locarno79. The Chilean Director: Sergio Castro-San Martín Piazza Grande program International sales: Fandango A political thriller telling the story of a fugitive is ready to explode onto Locarno’s screens. The big-screen epic The Chilean is a co-production between Italy, Chile and Switzerland that starts off in 1976 Chile. Amid mining protests, Aldo, skilled in explosives, is forced into exile, leaving his wife and newborn child behind. He moves to Italy, where he must survive on menial jobs in Torino and where people simply call him Il Cileno, The Chilean. But everything changes when he meets Luciana, a doctor involved with anarchist groups. She offers him the chance to reunite with his family. But in exchange, he must return to his old trade – making bombs for revolutionary groups. “Reconstructing an era means not only designing its atmosphere, but understanding the personalities that embody it,” the director says about The Chilean . “The exiled Aldo Marín leads us to one of the most pressing issues: immigration, omnipresent in the film.” Happiness Is So Close! Director: François-Christophe Marzal Out of competition program International sales: Point Productions ’Happiness Is So Close!,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Jean-Luc, an actor in his 80s, is set to play Don Quixote in a prestigious theater. It is the big role that he has been waiting for to bid farewell to the stage. But his health problems make rehearsals difficult, so the production team hires an understudy in case he is unable to perform. The result is paranoia. Says a synopsis: “Jean-Luc gradually sinks into an obsessive delusion, convinced that his understudy will take his place until he disappears completely.” Jean-Luc Bideau, Gilles Privat and Aurore Clément star in the Swiss production, written by the director and Nicolas Frey, who also served as the editor. Ahead of the Aug. 9 world premiere of Happiness Is So Close! , Bideau will receive a special honorary Leopard at Locarno. Small Talk Director: Matteo Yberra Filmmakers of the Presence Competition program International sales: Urban Sales ‘Small Talk,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival How’s this tease for the hybrid feature that serves up a peek behind the curtain of an elite institution? “Hoping to launch a career in the luxury world, Charlie enrolls at Institut Villa Pierrefeu – the last finishing school still operating in Switzerland. Here, women from all over the world are prepared to move within the circles of the international elite.” Over the course of a summer, their daily life is all about lessons in elegance, protocol and the art of conversation. Written by the director, the actress, along with Louis Rebetez, Hélène Bares, Milan Alfonsi,, the film features actress Hélène Bares. Says the director: “By working with an actress within a real educational setting, the film explores the porous boundary between performance and social behavior, questioning how identity is shaped by learned codes and expectations.” O Jacaré Director: Basil Da Cunha International competition program International sales: Thera Production ‘O Jacaré,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Director Basil Da Cunha has dual Swiss and Portuguese citizenship, which explains this co-production and its elements that don’t sound quintessential Swiss: such as alligators and its setting, namely Reboleira, a suburb of Lisbon. The haul from a robbery has mysteriously disappeared. Within the area sealed off by the police, rumors spread and speculation runs wild. Among the residents, a whole cast of colorful characters dream of getting their hands on the loot. But who will be first to find it? For the filmmaker, who also wrote the script for the movie, the production marks a farewell of sorts. “For the past 15 years, I have been filming the Reboleira neighborhood, which is due to be demolished,” he explains. “ O Jacaré is like a final dance before its disappearance: a vibrant, light-hearted film, infused with comedy and a sense of freedom.” The Angel Maker Director: Marina Klauser Out of competition program International sales: tellfilm ‘The Angel Maker,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival This four-part documentary series from Switzerland, written and directed by Klauser, is not for the faint of heart, but it will appeal to fans of true-crime and cult stories and audiences beyond that. After all, the series tells the story of “the Swiss religious community of Methernitha, which still exists today, its founder Paul Baumann — the inventor of a mysterious energy machine — and the young women who brought him down on charges of child abuse,” as a synopsis reads. Klauser has previously written and directed short films and served as head writer of the writers’ room for the dramedy series How to Be Sad – The Right Way . Frank & Louis Director: Petra Volpe Piazza Grande program International sales: TrustNordisk Kingsley Ben-Adir (left) and Rob Morgan in ‘Frank and Louis.’ Rob Baker Ashton/Courtesy Sundance Last but not least, Locarno will showcase a well-established Swiss cinematic voice’s latest movie, but not in a world premiere, which happened at Sundance. But the film will still get a big square screening at the festival. Swiss-Italian writer-director Petra Volpe followed up her box office and critical success Late Shift with Frank & Louis , her English-language debut, putting a spotlight on another often-overlooked care issue: the care needs of the aging incarcerated. Set within the walls of a U.S. prison, it Frank, portrayed by Kingsley Ben-Adir , who is serving a life sentence and takes on a caretaking role for aging inmates suffering from memory loss. Rob Morgan stars as one of those inmates, Louis. “The theme of care and caretaking, what that means and how we all need it, is such an important societal issue,” Volpe told THR about her motivation for the film in a previous interview. “We take for granted that there are people who take care of us. It’s also a taboo, because nobody wants to think about being old and sick and needy. And especially in the context of prison, we never really think about it deeply.” THR

articles.title: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming, Benedict Wong Pen Op-Ed Urging U.K. to Block “Dangerous” Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 1:20am Cumberbatch, Cumming, Wong have called the merger "dangerous." Courtesy of Getty Actors Benedict Cumberbatch , Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have penned an op-ed in The Guardian calling for the U.K. to block the Paramount – Warner Bros . merger, arguing that the deal threatens to inflict “immense harm on the British public.” The U.K. culture secretary Lisa Nandy — who has remained in her post amid a cabinet reshuffle with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham taking office — has previously said she was “minded to intervene” in the $111 billion mega-deal that, if successful, will undoubtedly change not just Hollywood, but the global film and TV industry. Related Stories Movies Don't Miss the Swiss at Locarno: From a Hunt for Loot, 'The Chilean' and Don Quixote to 'Small Talk' Movies Ontario Wildfires Prompt Mask-Up Orders and Drone Bans on Film Sets -- But Production Rolls On Among a host of issues, the actors cite concerns over the livelihoods of British film and TV crews, independent film financing, and the consolidation of news publications. “As actors and public figures who have spent our careers in the arts in Britain — working with British crews, on British stages and sets — we have a responsibility to the public who support, enjoy and consume the art we make,” wrote the famed Marvel actors (Cumberbatch and Wong), as well as Cummng ( The Traitors ), on Monday in a piece titled “A TV and cinema calamity could be disastrous for what you watch and what you know. Act now to stop that.” “The U.K. is being threatened by a media merger that would harm our workers, our culture and the public — but we can stop it.” They mention that they are encouraged by Nandy’s statements that she wants to investigate the threat to public interest, and acknowledge that she is not acting alone. This month, 12 U.S. states, led by California, sued in federal court to block the merger, warning that it would “raise prices, shrink the number of films made and degrade the quality of what audiences see,” said the men. And over the weekend, news broke that Larry Ellison’s Paramount agreed not to close the takeover until the court decides whether the deal violates antitrust laws. “Their lawsuit confirms the danger; it cannot, however, do the U.K.’s work for it,” continue Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong, who add that the EU has conditionally backed the merger and makes its own decisions. “The fight against this merger now runs on two fronts, and Nandy commands one of them. Should her department decide to intervene, it may prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for U.K. film, television and media in a generation,” they explain. “This is why. We have spent our lives working in this industry. We know what it looks like from the inside: the sound stages at Leavesden [studio], the crews who move from production to production, the editors and camera operators and costume designers whose names scroll past in the credits at the end of a film. These are our cherished friends and colleagues, who create the shows we all love, who produce the news that educates the public and film the sport events we enjoy together,” write the actors. The men say that U.K. film and TV are not just “images on your screens; they are lives and livelihoods of thousands of workers and families, whose work supports local economies.” They cite buoying figures, such as the 180,000 jobs supported through the industry and the £6.8 billion production spend reported last year. “It is one of the things the U.K. still does better than almost anyone, and a cultural heritage we must protect,” they say. They add that they have watched “with growing alarm” what consolidation does to the “breadth and depth of the work we produce,” before recognizing that independent film acquisitions at the leading independent film festival, Sundance, fell by half between 2019 and 2025. “Award-winning documentaries – films that won Oscars and topped festival juries – have struggled to find commercial distribution because they touched subjects the remaining handful of buyers found inconvenient. Every merger of this kind narrows the funnel through which stories can reach audiences.” To service Warner Bros.’ estimated $84 billion in debt, executives have promised investors around $6bn in “synergies,” Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong mention. “In plain English, that means redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken,” they add. “That is precisely what makes the Paramount-WBD merger so dangerous,” they write, adding that it has happened so many times before, such as Discovery’s merging with WarnerMedia in 2022, which led to the shelving of finished films and thousands of job losses, or Skydance’s merger with Paramount last year when around 2,000 people were laid off. They admit they are extremely concerned about the consolidation of news outlets like Channel 5, one of the U.K.’s public broadcasters, as well as CNN International . “The CNN and CBS news archives [are] among the world’s most important broadcast news collections, with more than 4.25m videos, images and media spanning nearly half a century of history. If one commercially interested owner controls access to both, they control the raw material of our historical memory… Fold those newsrooms into a single company, and one boardroom’s commercial anxieties — or political debts — determine what millions of people see and what they never learn existed.” “And we know something about this particular proprietor’s intentions. Paramount’s chief executive reportedly told Donald Trump that he would make ‘sweeping changes’ to CNN if the deal went through,” they add. “Actors are often told to stay out of legal arguments,” write Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong. “We understand the instinct. But we have spent our lives on enough U.K. sets, worked alongside enough U.K. crews and watched enough brilliant work from the U.K. struggle to find a buyer to know that this is not someone else’s argument. It is ours.” THR

articles.title: Prime Video Picks Up 100-Plus Korean Dramas From CJ ENM in Multi-Year India Deal
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 27, 2026 4:25am Executives from CJ ENM and Amazon's Prime Video Prime Video Prime Video is deepening its investments in Korean content for the world’s most populous country. The streamer’s India arm on Monday unveiled a multi-year licensing deal with Korean entertainment giant CJ ENM that will bring more than 100 Korean titles to Indian subscribers over the next two years. The pact covers a slate of 26 new series rolling out across the period alongside a broad array of library titles, all of which will be included with a standard Prime membership. Every new title will carry English subtitles and dubbing in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu. Related Stories Business Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming, Benedict Wong Pen Op-Ed Urging U.K. to Block "Dangerous" Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Movies Don't Miss the Swiss at Locarno: From a Hunt for Loot, 'The Chilean' and Don Quixote to 'Small Talk' The new agreement extends the global distribution deal the two companies struck in May 2025 at the WAVES market in Mumbai, which gave Prime Video worldwide rights, outside Korea and China, to a collection of new series from CJ ENM, Studio Dragon and CJ ENM Studios through 2026 — launching with the fantasy romance Head Over Heels — plus library titles. The first CJ series headed to India under the new pact will be Yumi’s Cells season three, the latest installment of a franchise the companies say has topped streaming charts in 81 countries. The pipeline also includes Filing for Love , which the partners credit with reaching No. 1 in 105 territories, alongside The Legend of Kitchen Soldier and romantic comedy My Bias, My Boss . Library additions range from such recent breakouts as Dear X and Study Group to catalog favorites Search: WWW , Prison Playbook and Legend of the Blue Sea . “Building on our strong global relationship with CJ ENM and the deal announced last year, we’re excited to deepen this collaboration with a sharper focus on India,” said Shilangi Mukherji, director and head of SVOD business at Prime Video India. “Prime Video’s unmatched reach in India, combined with its deep investment in local audiences, makes it the ideal partner to amplify our content to millions of new viewers,” added Jangho Seo, executive vp of CJ ENM’s platform division. The India pact is the latest in a rapid series of deals that have seen CJ ENM — the Korean studio giant behind Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite and production houses Studio Dragon and Fifth Season — ink output deals with various major streamers across Asia ‘s top territories. Last October, the company struck a partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery that installed a branded hub for its TVING streaming service on HBO Max across 17 Asia-Pacific markets, with the two sides also co-producing original K-dramas for global release. Weeks later, Disney+ signed on as the exclusive home in Japan for up to 60 TVING and CJ ENM titles. The company’s production prowess was also foundational to Netflix’s global success as a distributor of Korean content, with CJ’s Studio Dragon feeding the U.S. streamer many of its early K-content hits. THR

articles.title: Diego Luna to Receive Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award at Bosnian Film Festival
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 27, 2026 4:35am Diego Luna Sarajevo Film Festival Mexican star Diego Luna will receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the Bosnian film festival this year, in recognition of his “indelible” contribution to cinema. He’ll also be presenting his latest directorial feature, a movie called Ashes , which had its world premiere in Cannes earlier this year. Also accepting the Heart of Sarajevo at the 32nd installment of the festival are British actress and Sarajevo jury president Emily Watson , as well as Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi . Luna said on Monday: “It’s been many years since I’ve wanted to go to Sarajevo, so many colleagues have spoken beautifully about the festival and their personal experience there. I feel honored with the recognition of my work and very excited to share Ashes with the audience.” Related Stories TV Prime Video Picks Up 100-Plus Korean Dramas From CJ ENM in Multi-Year India Deal Business Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming, Benedict Wong Pen Op-Ed Urging U.K. to Block "Dangerous" Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Jovan Marjanović, director of the Sarajevo Film Festival , added: “A quarter of a century ago, Diego Luna won our hearts with his unforgettable performance in Y Tu Mamá También . We hoped then and know now that we were witnessing the emergence of an artist who would never cease to explore and surprise, moving seamlessly from major Hollywood productions to intimate human stories that reveal the richness of Latin American culture. Through his exceptional body of work, Diego Luna has left a profound mark on contemporary cinema, and it is our great honour to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.” Luna first captured international attention with his breakout performance in Alfonso Cuarón’s Y tu mamá también (2001), a role that established him as one of Mexico’s most compelling screen talents. This led to further collaborations across Mexico, Spain, the U.S., U.K., and Germany, working with directors such as Steven Spielberg, David Trueba, Gus Van Sant, Harmony Korine and Agustín Díaz Yanes. Most recently, he starred in and executive-produced the Disney+ series Andor (2022), earning two Golden Globe nominations and two Critics’ Choice Award nominations for best actor for his work in both seasons. The series received widespread critical acclaim, including eight Emmy nominations for its first season and fourteen for its second season in 2025, including outstanding drama series. As a director, Luna made his debut with the documentary J.C. Chávez (2007). His first narrative feature, Abel (2010), earned the Horizontes Latinos Award at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and a Mexican Academy Award for best screenplay, which he co-wrote. He later directed Mr. Pig (2016), which premiered at Sundance. The Sarajevo Film Festival 2026 runs Aug. 14-21. THR

articles.title: Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Holds Firm at No. 1 as Market Slows
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 12:19am PT Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Holds Firm at No. 1 as Market Slows By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sasikumar’s ‘Vadhandhi’ Season 2 Sets August Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier,’ ‘Yumi’s Cells’ Lead Prime Video India’s Slate of 100-Plus New CJ ENM Titles 3 hours ago Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Holds Firm at No. 1 as Market Slows 5 hours ago See All Courtesy of Plus M Entertainment Science-fiction thriller “ Hope ” maintained its powerful grip on the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 24–26. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the big-budget film generated $5.5 million from 767,366 admissions over the three-day window, securing a commanding 66.8% share of total market revenue. Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) Directed by Na Hong-Jin , the film features an ensemble cast led by Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender , and Alicia Vikander . The narrative chronicles the desperate struggle for survival in a secluded harbor town after residents discover a mysterious alien entity on their outskirts. Following its record-setting opening frame, the local tentpole has now accumulated a gross of $25.3 million from 3,415,707 total viewers. “Minions & Monsters” was in second place, pulling in $793,103 from 117,916 admissions over the weekend. The film has lifted its cumulative total to $3.9 million from 562,965 total ticket buyers since its Jul. 15 debut. Popular on Variety Disney’s live-action musical adaptation “Moana” took third place in its third weekend of release, collecting $593,187 from 87,033 admissions. The Pacific island adventure has reached an overall haul of $6.6 million from 909,270 admissions. “Toy Story 5” took fourth place, bringing in $376,522 from 53,975 ticket buyers. The animation is now nearing the $20 million mark in South Korea, boasting a local cumulative total of $19.8 million from 2,837,123 viewers since its mid-June launch. Faith-based animated production “David” claimed fifth place, adding $302,409 from 46,493 admissions over the frame. The biblical story of the shepherd boy turned king has pushed its local cume to $1.4 million from 220,351 viewers. Local psychological thriller “The Eyes” placed sixth, generating $269,004 from 37,141 admissions. Directed by Yeom Ji-ho and starring Shin Min-ah and Kim Nam-hee, the Korean remake of the Spanish thriller “Julia’s Eyes” has a gross of $10.6 million from 1,511,619 ticket buyers. Japanese anime feature “Dream Animals The Movie” debuted in seventh place, drawing $92,720 from 15,300 admissions over its opening weekend. Directed by Hitoshi Takekiyo and based on Ginbis’s popular long-selling animal biscuit brand, the animated adventure follows the colorful biscuit characters on a fantasy journey. Including previews, the title has earned $148,892 from 24,404 viewers. Josh Safdie’s table tennis comedy-drama “Marty Supreme,” starring Timothée Chalamet and Gwyneth Paltrow, took eighth place with a weekend gross of $37,623, bringing its total local cume to $923,581. Showbox’s action-horror hit “Colony,” directed by Yeon Sang-ho and starring Jun Ji-hyun, Koo Kyo-hwan, and Ji Chang-wook, took ninth place with $27,867, lifting its lifetime haul to $42.6 million from 5,949,979 total admissions since its May 21 rollout. Rounding out the top 10 was thehorror feature “Hokum,” which opened to $22,398 from 3,322 admissions over the frame. Since its Jul. 22 launch, the film has collected $50,203 from 7,972 viewers. The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $8.2 million, plummeting from last week’s $17.1 million. articles.title: Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 2:13am PT Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 2 hours ago Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’ 3 hours ago Why David Cronenberg’s Feature on Charli xcx’s ‘Music, Fashion, Film’ Gets to the Heart of What the Album Is Really About 3 days ago See All Getty Images Dylan Mulvaney has hit back at U.S. President Donald Trump after he mocked the trans advocate, actress and singer in his White House Correspondents’ Dinner speech on Friday. “My name is Dylan Mulvaney and the president said my name four times in his speech on Friday night,” she began a TikTok video response posted on Sunday evening. At Friday’s rescheduled dinner, which had been postponed after a gunman opened fire at the original event in April, Trump mentioned Mulvaney after CNN’s Kaitlan Collins accepted an award for her covering the White House. Trump compared the two women and brought up the 2023 Bud Light controversy, where customers boycotted the beer brand after Mulvaney posted a social media ad featuring her face on a can. Related Stories Kevin Feige on Marvel's Failed 'Blade' Reboot: 'I Feel Like a Gigantic Loser and Failure That We Didn't Get Off the Ground With Mahershala Ali' Netflix's 'Little House on the Prairie' Writer on Landing Fan Favorite From Original Series for That Scary Cameo “I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said in his speech. “Dylan Mulvaney cost Bud Light $35 billion in market cap. That was the worst commercial ever made by the way, for those few people who want to hear that. Most people don’t care, but I would. I wouldn’t want to hire Dylan any time soon.” Popular on Variety In her response, Mulvaney — who most recently starred in the Broadway musical “Six” — first congratulated Collins, saying: “I’m incredibly honored to be compared to her in any way and I hope that she continues doing all the great work.” She then marveled at the fact that she’s “been kind of flying under the radar” since the Bud Light video, but is “still his topic of conversation all these years later.” “It seems to me that I might be the one that got away for these men, like I am permanently burned into their retinas, I am microchipped into their minds,” Mulvaney said, adding that perhaps “being publicly mocked and criticized by this administration is actually, like, the greatest compliment of all because it puts me in the company of some of the most brilliant, empathetic people in our world today.” Since his speech on Friday night, Trump has doubled down on his comments about Collins and Mulvaney, posting an AI-generated photo from the beer ad placing Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body. “But I do still wonder, why is it so important to them that I don’t find success? What is it that I have that they don’t?” Mulvaney asked. “Oh my God… freedom! I am free in a way that they will never have the privilege to experience, and they want to use their power to take away my freedom. But what they don’t understand is my freedom has zero contingency on what they can provide for me, because my freedom is fully dependent on the moment that I acknowledged my real, authentic self, and every day since. And sharing that with the world, it’s just icing on the cake. But they don’t want me to be able to share that, because it would mean young people realizing that if someone like me can be themselves and find success and freedom, then they can find success and freedom for themselves, too.” Mulvaney then gave her viewers some “action items,” emphasizing that it is more important than ever to support trans and nonbinary people, especially young people seeking acceptance. “When they try to judge you for your support of us, take that as the greatest compliment,” she said. “Ladies, when they tell you that you look like a trans woman, wear it like a medal. Men, when they tell you that being attracted to trans women makes you gay, I want you to Hilary Duff PSA their ass so hard that they don’t even know what just happened. And to the dolls, let’s have each other’s back.” She concluded her video response with a message directly to Trump, saying: “To the president, thank you for reminding me that I am more powerful than I even knew. And to quote my favorite recording artist Shea Diamond: I am America.” Watch Mulvaney’s full video below. @dylanmulvaney A response 🇺🇸❤️ please support trans and non binary people today and every day ♬ I Am America – Shea Diamond Alfonso Ribeiro on Social Media Fueling ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Success and Urging Contestants to Ignore the Trolls: ‘Why Are We So Mean to One Another? ‘Office Romance’ Star Betty Gilpin on Using a Prosthetic Vagina for Her Birthing Scene: ‘I Was Pretty Freaked Out’ ‘I Will Find You’: Logan Browning on Sam Worthington Teaching Her How to Reload a Gun and the Show’s Wild Action Scenes: ‘I Can Hop Buildings, Didn’t You Know That?’ Gay Romance Podcast ‘Drive Thru Magic’ Casts Daniel J. articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 2:36am PT Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong Urge U.K. Government to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger in Op-Ed: ‘It Threatens to Inflict Immense Harm’ By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest Netflix Executives Considered Pulling ‘Michael Jackson: The Verdict’ Docuseries a Week Before Its Release (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago ‘Game of Thrones’ Play ‘The Mad King’ Still Set to Open Next Month Despite Canceling Previews (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago Leslie Odom Jr. Returning to ‘Hamilton’ on West End Tonight After Exiting Mid-Performance (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago See All Getty Images Benedict Cumberbatch , Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have urged the U.K. government to intervene in the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger, saying it “threatens to inflict immense harm on the British public.” In an op-ed addressed to culture minister Lisa Nandy, the trio said her intervention could be “prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation.” Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) They argue that the merger will result in “redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken,” although they acknowledge that aspect of the merger is less within Nandy’s remit than the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), which is also reviewing the deal. Nandy’s is to decide whether the merger is in the public interest, to which Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong say “It most certainly is not.” The trio point to the fact that Paramount currently owns public service broadcaster Channel 5 as well as CBS in the States: the acquisition of WBD would see CNN and CNN International also come under the same umbrella. Popular on Variety “If one commercially interested owner controls access to both [the CNN and CBS news archives], they control the raw material of our historical memory,” the op-ed, published in the Guardian, states. “Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes U.K. television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger.” Nandy has already said she is “minded to intervene” in the deal, although Parliament is now in recess until Sept. 1. The culture secretary, who managed to cling on to her job in the wake of a cabinet reshuffle by incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham, currently has a number of high-profile media matters to attend to, including the equally if not more impactful acquisition of ITV by Comcast-owned Sky as well as the BBC’s royal charter renewal. Last week the European Commission approved the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, albeit with some conditions. In the U.S., however, it is facing opposition from numerous sources. articles.title: Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 2:42am PT Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 2 hours ago Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’ 3 hours ago Why David Cronenberg’s Feature on Charli xcx’s ‘Music, Fashion, Film’ Gets to the Heart of What the Album Is Really About 3 days ago See All Getty Images Bill Oddie , the English comedian and conservationist known for hosting wildlife programs including BBC’s “Springwatch,” has died. He was 85. Oddie’s agent, David Foster, confirmed his death in a statement to BBC News on Monday, calling him “the country’s best-loved birder.” Foster continued: “Bill was a multi-talented celebrity — wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment. He taught us the wonder of it. He protested, lobbied and campaigned for it. He led the way and people of all ages and backgrounds responded to his call. And such a massive contribution to conservation will never be forgotten.” Related Stories 'House of the Dragon' Star Fabien Frankel on Criston Cole's Suicide Mission and His 'Nihilism': 'He's Losing the Will to Motivate' Netflix's 'Little House on the Prairie' Writer on Landing Fan Favorite From Original Series for That Scary Cameo Oddie got his start on the TV comedy series “The Goodies” alongside his Cambridge classmates Tim Brooke-Taylor and Graeme Garden, which ran from 1970 to 1982. He then shifted to presenting and focused on his love of wildlife, specifically birds. He hosted a slew of successful nature programs for the BBC from the mid-80s to 2008, including “Birding With Bill Oddie,” “Bill Oddie Goes Wild,” “Springwatch,” “Autumnwatch” and more. Popular on Variety Born on July 7, 1941, in Rochdale, Lancashire, England, Oddie moved to Birmingham at a young age and was raised by his father and grandmother. He went on to study English literature at Cambridge University, and it was there that he became interested in comedy, appearing in several productions of the sketch comedy troupe Footlights. In the late ’60s, he began his venture into show business as a key member of the BBC radio program “I’m Sorry, I’ll Read That Again,” on which several of his musical compositions were featured. After writing and performing on comedy series including “Twice a Fortnight” and “Broaden Your Mind,” Oddie got his big break with “The Goodies,” known for its surreal sketches and situational comedy. In addition to writing and acting on the series, Oddie wrote all the music including co-penning the show’s theme song. In the mid-’80s, Oddie became increasingly interested in wildlife, drawing from his lifelong passion of birdwatching. This kickstarted the second phase of his career, in which he became a beloved nature presenter known for programs including “Oddie in Paradise” (1985), “Birding With Bill Oddie” (1997-1998, 2000), “Bill Oddie Goes Wild” (2001-2003), “Bill Oddie’s How to Watch Wildlife” (2005-2006), “Springwatch” (2005-2008), “Autumnwatch” (2006-2008) and “Bill Oddie’s Wild Side” (2008). In 2003, he was made an OBE for his services to wildlife conservation. Oddie is survived by his wife Laura and daughters Bonnie, Kate and Rosie. The agreement covers 26 new titles from CJ ENM alongside a broader slate drawn from the studio’s existing library, and extends the companies’ existing global partnership with a dedicated focus on India. New and upcoming titles under the deal will carry English subtitles and dubbing in the Hindi, Tamil and Telugu languages. By bringing a curated slate of premium Korean titles to Prime Video, we’re doubling down on our commitment to making the most innovative and captivating stories from Korea accessible to audiences in India.” The India-focused pact builds on a run of recent moves by CJ ENM to widen its footprint in the country. This partnership reflects our ongoing commitment to expanding the global reach of Korean storytelling. We look forward to connecting more deeply with Indian audiences and sharing the richness and emotional depth of K-dramas with viewers across the region.” Prime members will be able to stream the new titles at no additional cost. “At Prime Video India, we keep a keen eye on what our customers are watching and what stories resonate with them,” said Manish Menghani, director and head of content licensing, Prime Video, India. “The surge in popularity of K-content is undeniable. articles.title: Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 4:18am PT Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Locarno’s First Look Section Reveals Six Uruguayan Titles, From Family Stories to Drama About Desire That ‘Persists Across Oceans’ 1 week ago Rosemary Who? Get Ready for Emma’s Baby as ‘Birth’ Seduces Tallifornia Film Fund With ‘Grotesque and Terrifying’ Take on Pregnancy (EXCLUSIVE) 2 weeks ago See All StepIn speakers Courtesy of Locarno Pro Now in its 15th year, Locarno’s think tank StepIn will debate “Power, People, Data and the Future of Film.” “Last year, StepIn focused on one of the defining qualities of independent cinema: the willingness to embrace risk. One of the strongest conclusions from those discussions was that playing it safe is rarely the smartest strategy,” said Marcello Paolillo, Locarno Pro , StepIn and U30 Project Manager. Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) “After all, audiences fall in love with films because they’re original, surprising and emotionally truthful. Yet we are increasingly surrounded by algorithms, sophisticated data analysis, AI and systems designed to reduce uncertainty, predict outcomes and optimize decisions.” Popular on Variety The event will explore how power structures, human capital, politics, AI, data-driven decision-making and increasing industry consolidation are reshaping the future of independent cinema. Approaching the subject from “four interconnected perspectives,” it will allow the participants to discuss the following topics: “Films vs. Formula: Algorithms, Consolidation and Creative Freedom,” “Sustainable Indie Financing: Connecting Private Investors with Sales Agents and Market Realities,” “Why Cinema Still Matters: Activism, Social Relevance and Audience Renewal” and “Gender Equality and the Cost of Inclusion: Who Can Afford to Build a Career in This Industry?” “For many people, algorithms have become synonymous with the death of art. At the same time, there’s another perspective. Used intelligently, data can become a valuable tool rather than a creative constraint,” noted Paolillo. The same is true of AI. “Whether we like it or not, it’s already impacting every stage of the filmmaking process, from development and financing to marketing and distribution. Ignoring it is no longer an option. StepIn wants to create a space where these questions can be discussed openly and honestly, acknowledging both the opportunities and the risks.” The out-of-the-box introduction called “Fear, Lies, and the Illusion of Control” will be delivered by analyst Stephen Follows. “For a century, this industry has bought tools that promise to control the inherent uncertainty in an arts-based business. This has included the use of stars, test screenings, tracking surveys, franchises, and now algorithms,” he told Variety . “My thesis is that while most of them do work to some degree, (a) they don’t work nearly well enough; and (b) the industry uses them wrong. They test what they test and they produce real numbers. Sometimes those numbers even make things marginally better – or at the very least more defensible. The trouble starts with what we do next, because we mistake a marginal edge for control.” He added: “Once you’ve bought a hammer, everything starts to look like a nail, and the questions the tools can answer begin to crowd out the questions that matter. I’m not saying the tools are bullshit – just that we use them wrong. They are expensive comfort, and the side effects often cost more than the edge is worth.” Familiar IP and sequels “do shift the odds,” he noted, but “safe choices still fail all the time, and we never book those failures as risk.” “We call it franchise fatigue or bad marketing, or star casting. Fame genuinely lifts returns, but the star captures most of that uplift in salary. The insurance mostly ends up in the star’s pocket, while the film underneath has become more expensive to save.” Then there’s “the complete misuse and misunderstanding” of the frequently repeated line “nobody knows anything.” “People quote Goldman as if it’s humility and use it as cover for not doing the work,” said Follows. “Right now, there’s a booming trade in certainty. Every stage, every panel, every feed has someone selling the film industry a dream – that this tool, this model, this dataset will finally crack the code. And we are the perfect customers. A hundred years of terrible odds makes people desperate, and desperate people buy dreams.” While the platforms “measure everything and share nothing” – “Netflix has redefined what a ‘view’ is four times and Apple has never published a single audience figure” – people ignore the algorithms that already decide what gets seen. “On the big streaming services, under 6% of titles take around three-quarters of all viewing. The threat is not currently to creation but to discovery. And the one move the machine cannot make is a person with taste saying: ‘This one.’ That’s what festivals are. The counter-algorithm is a human being who gives a damn, and Locarno is full of them.” The opening panel will feature distributor Andrea Occhipinti (Lucky Red), mk2’s Head of Production Yasmine Talli and Doris Ruth Eikhof, professor of cultural economy & policy at the University of Glasgow. “What [Occhipinti] has built with Lucky Red over the past three decades speaks for itself, and the recent partnership between Lucky Red and Studiocanal makes his perspective on consolidation, independent cinema and the changing marketplace particularly timely,” noted Paolillo. Yasmine Talli “has first-hand insight into how ambitious auteur cinema can continue to thrive in an increasingly challenging market,” while Doris Ruth Eikhof is “one of Europe’s leading experts on diversity and inclusion in the cultural economy.” “Statistics about women in film remain discouraging: women are still less likely than men to hold influential positions and be celebrated for their work,” Eikhof told Variety . “It’s important to keep looking at them, as they tell an important story and are powerful evidence, but just focusing on statistics creates an incentive to ‘just bring more women in.’ That’s a big mistake. We need to make sure that women can stay and succeed.” Too often, people tend to take a “one size fits all” approach that dismantles some barriers to women’s opportunity and inclusion but leaves other barriers in place. “We need to support production companies and small businesses to create the conditions in which women of different ages, religions, races and class backgrounds, disabled women, LGBTQ+ women or women with and without caring responsibilities can all do their best work. That’s not a job for statistics. That’s a job we need to do every day, in our workplaces,” said Eikhof. The good news? “It’s possible, we can do it one step at a time, not all of it costs money and it will benefit everybody, not ‘just’ women.” Activism and political engagement will also be discussed, as “the world around us is once again creating a sense of urgency, and filmmakers are responding to it.” “Many of the films that have generated the strongest public debate in recent years have done so not only because of their artistic qualities, but because of the social, political and ethical questions they raise,” noted Paolillo, mentioning the likes of “Parasite,” “The Zone of Interest,” “One Battle After Another,” “Sinners” or “The Voice of Hind Rajab.” “Interestingly, this has also revived an older debate: during this year’s Berlinale, remarks by Wim Wenders, followed in Cannes by comments by Paul Laverty and Park Chan-wook, brought back a question central to the cinema culture of the 1970s: whether films are, by their very nature, political.” Wenders’ comments that filmmakers should “stay out of politics” were widely disputed. “This is something we want to discuss within the broader question whether films are culturally and social relevant in an era shaped by social media, algorithm-driven platforms, fragmented audiences, and an overwhelming flow of images. Does cinema still matter as a cultural and social force? And what strategies can help expand and renew its audience, by finding new ways to engage people across generations?” Overall, Paolillo remains optimistic about the future of film. “I’ve been in this industry long enough to have heard people announce the death of independent cinema countless times. They’re always wrong. Every few years, a new generation of filmmakers, a new movement or a number of unexpected films remind us why cinema still matters,” he argued. That being said, we are now living through a period of “profound transformation.” “The economic model is changing, technology is evolving at an unprecedented pace, and power within the industry is becoming more and more concentrated. We shouldn’t ignore these challenges, but neither should we fear them.” Paolillo added: “That’s ultimately what StepIn is about: bringing together people with very different perspectives, asking difficult questions, challenging assumptions, and collectively imagining what the next chapter of independent cinema could look like.” “I’m genuinely curious to see where this year’s conversations will lead us.” Anonymous Content’s Darren Walker on Company’s 10 Emmy Nominations and Nominee Sally Field’s ‘Motherly’ Dating Advice ‘Today’ Issues ‘Stricter Security Protocols’ for Guests Following Intruder Incident With Craig Melvin (EXCLUSIVE) Mariska Hargitay on Being Courtside for Knicks Game 4 Win: ‘Honored’ and ‘Grateful’ to Say ‘I Was There’ ‘Elle’ Director Jason Moore on Reese Witherspoon’s Set Visit, Season 2’s Archival-Only Wardrobe and What ‘Hardcore’ Fans Can Expect From ‘Murder, She Wrote’ Movie Tom Hanks Says Taylor Swift’s ‘Toy Story 5’ Song Was Kept ‘Top Secret’ From the Cast Until Release Day ‘Kennedy’ Stars Nick Robinson and Laura Donnelly on Why Series Isn’t Leaning Into Family’s Signature Boston Accent Loading comments... articles.title: Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 4:42am PT Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens 30 minutes ago Kino Rebelde Boards Locarno Title ‘September Afternoon’ for International Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago Luxbox Acquires Documentary ‘Life of Jorge Luis Borges’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Corey Nickols Mexican actor, director and producer Diego Luna will be feted at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival , which runs Aug. 14 to 21. Luna will receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo in recognition of his “outstanding career and indelible contribution to cinema.” The festival will screen “Ashes,” his latest directorial feature, which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival, and Luna will also give a masterclass. Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) Jovan Marjanović, the festival’s director, said, “A quarter of a century ago, Diego Luna won our hearts with his unforgettable performance in ‘Y tu mamá también.’ We hoped then and know now that we were witnessing the emergence of an artist who would never cease to explore and surprise, moving seamlessly from major Hollywood productions to intimate human stories that reveal the richness of Latin American culture. Through his exceptional body of work, Diego Luna has left a profound mark on contemporary cinema, and it is our great honor to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.” Popular on Variety Luna responded, “It’s been many years since I’ve wanted to go to Sarajevo, so many colleagues have spoken beautifully about the festival and their personal experience there. I feel honored with the recognition of my work and very excited to share ‘Ashes’ with the audience.” Luna first captured international attention with his breakout performance in Alfonso Cuarón’s “Y tu mamá también” (2001), a role that established him as one of Mexico’s leading actors. This led to collaborations with directors such as Steven Spielberg, David Trueba, Gus Van Sant, Harmony Korine and Agustín Díaz Yanes. Most recently, he starred in and executive-produced the Disney+ series “Andor” (2022), earning two Golden Globe nomination and two Critics’ Choice Award nominations for best actor for his work in both seasons. The series earned eight Emmy Award nominations for its first season and 14 for its second season in 2025, including outstanding drama series. In 2025, he starred opposite Jennifer Lopez and Tonatiuh in Bill Condon’s “Kiss of the Spider Woman” and was nominated for a Golden Globe Award for best supporting actor for his performance in Hulu’s “La Máquina” (2024), which he also produced and starred in alongside Gael García Bernal. Earlier credits include the Netflix series “Narcos: México” (2018), which earned him a Critics’ Choice Award nomination, “Star Wars: Rogue One” (2016), a role that introduced him to an even wider English-speaking audience, and “Bread & Circus” (2020), which won two Daytime Emmys for outstanding daytime talent in a Spanish-language program and best entertainment program in Spanish. As a director, Luna made his debut with the documentary “J.C. Chávez” (2007). His first narrative feature, “Abel” (2010), earned the Horizontes Latinos Award at the San Sebastián Film Festival and a Mexican Academy Award for best screenplay, which he co-wrote. He later directed “Mr. Pig” (2016), which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.
