articles.title: Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 4:43am PT Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) The news comes just after fully English-language ‘La Cathédrale,’ with Will Keen (‘The Crown’) and ’One Piece' star Taz Skylar, also goes into production By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest Buzz Title ‘Third Wheel,’ an ‘Allegory of Post-Colonial Africa,’ Brought to Market at Fantasia’s Frontières (EXCLUSIVE) 5 days ago ‘Sherlock’ Creator Steven Moffat Set as International Guest of Serielizados – Barcelona Series Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 6 days ago World Cup Final Ratings Skyrocket Across Europe, Despite England and France Losses 7 days ago See All Belén Rueda in 'Amor de Dios' Credit: Daniel Mayrit Flexing its muscles as one of the biggest new kids on its film industry block, Spain’s ISII Group has gone into production on “Amor de Dios” headlined by “The Orphanage” star Belén Rueda and produced by ISII banner label Inefable Productions. The news comes as ISII Group distribution-sales house Deep Com Roots has sold “Summer Days” to half the world’s major markets and cameras have rolled on “La Cathédrale,” Inefable’s first fully English production starring “One Piece” icon Taz Skylar . Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) As a mark of its step-up in scale, ISII Group now has four films in production in 2026 and another quartet released or awaiting release, including Spanish Western “Trinidad,” an ambitious Wild West-set Spanish family saga led by “Your Fault’s” Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón. All ISII Group titles are sold and distributed in Spain by Deep Com Roots, a strategic partner. Popular on Variety ‘Summer Days’ Closes Half the World “Summer Days” weighs in as a sun-drenched erotic drama with a thriller edge. Headed by Maggie Civantos , star of “Locked Up,” “Money Heist” creator Alex Pina’s first international breakout, “Summer Days” has closed Latin America, bought by Brazil’s Sofa Digital , plus Germany, Austria and Switzerland (Busch Media Group) and CIS (Kinologistika). Tokyo’s Aya Pro has licensed Japan, Mumbai’s PictureWorks India, distributor of Anatomy of a Fall and Flow, has acquired rights to India, and Scene & Sound those to South Korea. “Summer Days” (“Días de agosto”) begins with college students Juan (Pau Simón, “Nudes”) and Gabriela (Berta Galo, “La moderna”) escaping to his family beachside chalet for an idyllic summer. The film is described as a romantic drama. It acquires almost immediately, however, an erotic charge, in dialog and the arrival of Juan’s father Fernando (Roberto Álamo, “Riot Police”) with his much younger girlfriend Monica (Civantos). Juan and Monica’s feelings for each other build, mixing Juan’s resentment for his father leaving his mother and impossible-to-ignore physical attraction. “Deep Com Roots attended Cannes Market for the first time and was met with strong interest from the international market. Among our slate, Summer Days was one of the films that attracted the most attention from the buyers,” Emir Duzel, Deep Com Roots head of international sales, told Variety. “We believe its powerful story and the strong sense of tension made the film especially appealing. We are currently continuing negotiations for distribution deals for several more territories.” Early fruit of the ISII Group’s new talent support, “Summer Days” is based on a screenplay by David Sueiro, which was one of the seven fiction winners in the ISII Group’s first Break on Time ’59 national screenplay competition in 2024. It also marks a return to fiction of versatile director Chema del Prado, behind “IsiDisi,” a Spanish gross-out classic. Maggie Civantos in ‘Summer Days’ ‘Amor de Dios,’ Led Belén Rueda, Goes Into Production Also the female lead in Alejandro Amenábar’s Academy Award winner “The Sea Inside” and star of upscale genre hits “Julia’s Eyes” and “The Body,” in “Amor de Dios,” Rueda plays Sara Lanes, a renowned dancer and choreographer now living in Paris. When flamenco school Amor de Dios, once rated the world’s best, announces its closure, Sara returns to Madrid with disciple Ángela hoping to save the place where her own career began. “At the School, Sara reencounters a past she has never been able to leave behind. That and her own physical decline turns her return into a profoundly personal journey where she has to decide what she is willing to sacrifice in order to preserve her legacy,” says the synopsis. Inspired in its origins by an original idea by Spanish cinema great Carlos Saura, “Amor de Dios” is also produced by Inefable Productions Key cast also takes in Asier Etxeandia, co-star of Pedro Almodóvar’s “Pain and Glory,” and celebrated French dancer Soleila Chaou, Spanish National Ballet principal dancer Irene Tena and Tania Santana (“Love on a Tightrope”). Scheduled for release in 2027, “Amor de Dios” marks the awaited fiction feature debut of Paula Palacios, winner of the IDA Netflix 2022 Global Emerging Filmmaker Award and a double Goya best doc feature nominee for two stirring and affecting films, set against the context of African immigration to Europe: “Drowning Letters” (“Cartas Mojadas,” 2020) and “My Brother Ali,” (2024). “La Cathédrale,” Headlined by Will Keen and Taz Skylar “A new push for ISII Group’s fiction division,” it has noted, “La Cathédrale,” a double redemption thriller, turns on Thomas (Keen), a renowned violinist, who struggles to rebuild his life after the murder of his teenage daughter. When he agrees to take part in a restorative justice process with the man convicted of her killing (Skylar), the discovery of a mysterious violin among her belongings sets him on what the synopsis calls “a relentless search for the truth.” Beyond Slylar, “La Cathédrale” stars Keen, the distinguished British theatre actor and Private Secretary Michael Adeane in “The Crown,” Venice Horizons best actress Award winner Marta Nieto (“Mother”), Ronald Guttman, whose prolific and long career takes in “The Hunt for Red October,” “Lost” and “Mad Men”; and Catalan actor-pianist Peter Vives (“The Time in Between”). The film stands out for its “narrative tension, a powerful soundtrack and an immersive atmosphere,” Deep Com Roots has said. Now shooting in the Canary Islands, in Tenerife and Las Palmas, ““La Cathédrale” reflects director Eduardo Cubillo’s fascination with restorative justice. “Two people who seem irreconcilable – filled with hatred and countless grievances – can, through a simple conversation – which may or may not be difficult – end up feeling liberated in a way that has to be seen to be believed; it’s truly magical,” he has said. The film is written by Cubillo and scribe-helmer José Ortuño (“The Extraordinary Tale”). Taz Skylar in ‘La Cathédrale’ Deep Com Roots’ Slate “At ISII Group, we conceive each project not only from its creative ambition, but also the commercial career it can have inside and outside Spain,” said ISII Group President Silvia Carvalho. “So we have developed a structure which integrates development, financing, production, services, distribution and sales, with Deep Com Roots as the sales agent on all of our catalog,” she added. “‘Summer Days’ pre-sales and the interest generated by ‘La Cathédrale,’ ‘Amor de Dios’ and ‘Trinidad’ confirm that this model allows us to create value and market opportunities from the first stages of every film.” “Trinidad,” directed by Laura Alvea and José Ortuño, bows Nov. 2026. Gleaning great reviews, beginning in 1969 when Spain was still under the dictatorship of Francisco Franco, “Tal vez” charts the perhaps requited love of Canary Islands poet Natalia Sosa Ayala (“Hierro”) for trapeze artist Pinito del Oro (Adriana Ugarte, “Juileta”), star of New York’s Ringling Brothers. Bowed July 10, it is directed by Arima León, turning on their encounter and their correspondence afterwards. Winner of the 2025 Break on Time competition, “Desde Arriba,” a father-son relationship dramedy, is now in post-production. Martín Cuervo directs from a screenplay by Arturo Ruiz Serrano and José Manuel Carrasco. A realist survival thriller starring Milena Smit (“Parallel Mothers”) and Irene Escolar (“Tell Me Who I Am”) “My Zone” shot in the Canary Islands of Gran Canaria and Fuerteventura from May. It marks the feature debut of best short fiction Goya winner Cristián Beteta (“Ángulo muerto”). Directed by Violeta Salama (“Alegría”), “Auri,” starring Cristina Marcos (“Maravillas,” “Locked Up”), a comedy turning on a housewife’s later life revolution, bowed in April in Spain. ‘Trinidad’ (L-R) Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón in ‘Trinidad’. articles.title: Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’
articles.full_text: Jul 27, 2026 5:15am PT Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’ 13 minutes ago Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85 3 hours ago Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’ 3 hours ago See All Getty Images for NARAS Carly Simon has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. The 83-year-old singer-songwriter, best known for her 1972 hit “You’re So Vain,” revealed the news on Monday in a statement (via People ). “So many people have written to me, kindly wondering about my relative silence, asking how I am and what I have been doing. The truth is, I’ve been learning how to live with Parkinson’s disease,” Simon said. Related Stories Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE) “It has taken me some time to understand the diagnosis, to adjust to it, and to decide how much I wanted to say about it publicly,” she continued. “Parkinson’s is different for everyone, and it can be unpredictable. Some days I’m so tired I can’t get the day moving at all. On others, it gives me a little more room to move, think, work, and feel like myself.” Popular on Variety Parkinson’s disease, a neurological disorder that effects nerve cells in the brain, does not currently have a cure. Symptoms include tremors, stiffness, difficulty balancing and slowness of movement. Simon said that she was diagnosed after her mobility continued to worsen following replacement surgeries on her knees and one hip. “Eventually, there were periods when I could not walk without considerable help,” the Grammy winner wrote. “My family and I knew that something more was going on. After an extensive evaluation at the Mayo Clinic, I was diagnosed with Parkinson’s.” Though Simon has been affected physically, she has also struggled with “anxiety, depression, exhaustion and apathy” after her diagnosis. “That has been one of the hardest things to explain,” she said. “It is not simply sadness or laziness. It is as though the part of the brain that sends out invitations to participate in life has temporarily misplaced the guest list.” In addition to Parkinson’s, Simon also revealed that she was previously diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer, and underwent surgery for it amid her Parkinson’s treatment. “The cancer was removed, but the surgery affected my appearance and made me more self-conscious about being seen in public,” Simon said. “I have always been more critical of my appearance than anyone else could possibly imagine (check out the irony of having written ‘You’re So Vain’), and this gave my inner critic quite a lot of new material.” Simon has stayed out of the spotlight in recent years, with her last public performance being in March 2018. But despite her health struggles, she assured fans that she has “not stopped living” and “not stopped working.” In fact, she has written a new album, titled “Comes in Waves,” her first full-length effort since 2008. “Working on the music gave shape to days that did not always have much shape. It gave me somewhere to go without having to leave the room. It reminded me that illness can change your life without becoming the whole of your life,” she wrote. “I do not consider Parkinson’s a gift or a blessing. It is neither. It is difficult, frustrating, and sometimes frightening. I am still learning how to live with it and how to accept it without feeling that I have surrendered something essential.” Simon concluded her statement by saying: “These days I move more slowly, I lean on others more than I once did, and I have learned to accept that every day will look a little different. But I am still very much here.” Hannah Einbinder Speaks Out Against Spencer Pratt’s Mayoral Campaign: ‘It’s Important to Resist That’ ‘The Hunt for Gollum’ Star Anya Taylor-Joy Has Not Read the ‘Lord of the Rings’ Books Yet, but Is ‘About to’ Soon ‘Dance Moms’ Parody Musical Adds ‘Titaníque’ Director and Co-Creator Tye Blue as Creative Producer (EXCLUSIVE) John Travolta Now Owns a Dozen Berets Because ‘Men Can Have Fun, Too. articles.full_text: Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images A TV and cinema calamity could be disastrous for what you watch and what you know. Act now to stop that The Paramount-Warner Bros merger is being fought in the US and UK. Britain’s culture secretary knows the risks and can intervene. She should View image in fullscreen Though it has yet to become front-page news in the UK, you should know about the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger . It threatens to inflict immense harm on the British public. As actors and public figures who have spent our careers in the arts in Britain – working with British crews, on British stages and sets – we have a responsibility to the public who support, enjoy and consume the art we make. The UK is being threatened by a media merger that would harm our workers, our culture and the public – but we can stop it. We are encouraged by Lisa Nandy, the secretary of state for digital, culture, media and sport, who recently sent letters to Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery , as well as a statement to parliament , indicating that she is “minded to intervene” in Paramount’s $110bn takeover of Warner Bros. She is correct to investigate this major threat to the UK’s public interest. And she will not be acting alone. This month, 12 US states, led by California, sued in federal court to block the merger, warning that it would raise prices, shrink the number of films made and degrade the quality of what audiences see. And they just won a major victory: on Friday, Paramount agreed to delay the merger until trial, which could be months. These states acted even after Washington’s own justice department – despite the reported reservations of career staff – waved the deal through . Their lawsuit confirms the danger; it cannot, however, do the UK’s work for it. US courts fight on the antitrust front for US markets. The EU, which last week conditionally backed the merger , also makes its own decisions. The UK’s public interest, our public service broadcasting, our news plurality, the plurality of voices British audiences hear, can only be defended here, by our own secretary of state and the Competition and Markets Authority. The fight against this merger now runs on two fronts, and Nandy commands one of them. Should her department decide to intervene, it may prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation. This is why. We have spent our lives working in this industry. We know what it looks like from the inside: the sound stages at Leavesden, the crews who move from production to production, the editors and camera operators and costume designers whose names scroll past in the credits at the end of a film. These are our cherished friends and colleagues, who create the shows we all love, who produce the news that educates the public and film the sport events we enjoy together. UK film and television are not just images on your screens; they are the lives and livelihoods of thousands of workers and families, whose work supports local economies. The industry supports more than 180,000 jobs , generated £6.8bn in production spend last year alone and adds roughly £12bn a year in value to our economy. It is one of the things the UK still does better than almost anyone, and a cultural heritage we must protect. We have watched, with growing alarm, what consolidation does to the breadth and depth of the work we produce: independent film acquisitions at the leading independent film festival Sundance fell by half between 2019 and 2025. Award-winning documentaries – films that won Oscars and topped festival juries – have struggled to find commercial distribution because they touched subjects the remaining handful of buyers found inconvenient. Every merger of this kind narrows the funnel through which stories can reach audiences. That is precisely what makes the Paramount-WBD merger so dangerous. It’s why the intervention of Nandy and her department matters so much. Paramount proposes to swallow Warner Bros Discovery in one of the largest leveraged buyouts ever attempted, loading the combined company with an estimated $84bn in debt . To service it, executives have promised investors around $6bn in “ synergies ”. In plain English, that means redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken. We have seen this before. When Discovery merged with WarnerMedia in 2022, it shelved finished films and cut thousands of jobs ; when Skydance merged with Paramount last year, it laid off about 2,000 people . Now the same executives are making the same promise, and UK crews, producers, talent and audiences will pay when the bill comes due. But jobs are mostly a matter for the Competition and Markets Authority, whose review should end in a full phase 2 investigation. The job of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport goes further: to determine whether the merger is in the public interest. It most certainly is not. In her statement to British MPs , Nandy cited the need for a sufficient plurality of views in news media and a sufficient plurality of individuals controlling media enterprises. She has also highlighted the potential impact on streaming services, content homogenisation and children’s television. The Enterprise Act protects something we should all care about: who decides what we get to watch, and what we get to know. Consider the breadth of what this single company would hold. Channel 5, one of our five public service broadcasters , which serves the evening news to people without the cost of a subscription. CNN International, which Ofcom research in 2018 found UK viewers rated above every other TV news source for quality, accuracy, trustworthiness and impartiality. The CNN and CBS news archives – among the world’s most important broadcast news collections, with more than 4.25m videos, images and media spanning nearly half a century of history. If one commercially interested owner controls access to both, they control the raw material of our historical memory. One owner controlling this much of the news, and the truth, endangers the public in a way no ordinary consolidation does. When separate owners run separate newsrooms, a story judged inconvenient by one can still reach audiences through another. Fold those newsrooms into a single company, and one boardroom’s commercial anxieties – or political debts – determine what millions of people see and what they never learn existed. And we know something about this particular proprietor’s intentions. Paramount’s chief executive reportedly told Donald Trump that he would make “ sweeping changes ” to CNN if the deal went through. When the buyer of the world’s most trusted international news channel makes editorial promises to a politician, a British secretary of state is entitled – and, really, obliged – to ask questions before the ink dries. Nandy has been scrupulous in noting that no final decision has been taken. Good. It is important to take the time to get this right. But the case for a full public interest intervention, with Ofcom assessing plurality and reporting back, is overwhelming. Actors are often told to stay out of legal arguments. We understand the instinct. But we have spent our lives on enough UK sets, worked alongside enough UK crews and watched enough brilliant work from the UK struggle to find a buyer to know that this is not someone else’s argument. It is ours. Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes UK television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger. And they just won a major victory: on Friday, Paramount agreed to delay the merger until trial, which could be months. These states acted even after Washington’s own justice department – despite the reported reservations of career staff – waved the deal through . Their lawsuit confirms the danger; it cannot, however, do the UK’s work for it. US courts fight on the antitrust front for US markets. The EU, which last week conditionally backed the merger , also makes its own decisions. The UK’s public interest, our public service broadcasting, our news plurality, the plurality of voices British audiences hear, can only be defended here, by our own secretary of state and the Competition and Markets Authority. The fight against this merger now runs on two fronts, and Nandy commands one of them. Should her department decide to intervene, it may prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation. This is why. We have spent our lives working in this industry. We know what it looks like from the inside: the sound stages at Leavesden, the crews who move from production to production, the editors and camera operators and costume designers whose names scroll past in the credits at the end of a film. These are our cherished friends and colleagues, who create the shows we all love, who produce the news that educates the public and film the sport events we enjoy together. UK film and television are not just images on your screens; they are the lives and livelihoods of thousands of workers and families, whose work supports local economies. The industry supports more than 180,000 jobs , generated £6.8bn in production spend last year alone and adds roughly £12bn a year in value to our economy. It is one of the things the UK still does better than almost anyone, and a cultural heritage we must protect. We have watched, with growing alarm, what consolidation does to the breadth and depth of the work we produce: independent film acquisitions at the leading independent film festival Sundance fell by half between 2019 and 2025. Award-winning documentaries – films that won Oscars and topped festival juries – have struggled to find commercial distribution because they touched subjects the remaining handful of buyers found inconvenient. Every merger of this kind narrows the funnel through which stories can reach audiences. That is precisely what makes the Paramount-WBD merger so dangerous. It’s why the intervention of Nandy and her department matters so much. Paramount proposes to swallow Warner Bros Discovery in one of the largest leveraged buyouts ever attempted, loading the combined company with an estimated $84bn in debt . To service it, executives have promised investors around $6bn in “ synergies ”. In plain English, that means redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken. We have seen this before. When Discovery merged with WarnerMedia in 2022, it shelved finished films and cut thousands of jobs ; when Skydance merged with Paramount last year, it laid off about 2,000 people . Now the same executives are making the same promise, and UK crews, producers, talent and audiences will pay when the bill comes due. But jobs are mostly a matter for the Competition and Markets Authority, whose review should end in a full phase 2 investigation. The job of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport goes further: to determine whether the merger is in the public interest. It most certainly is not. In her statement to British MPs , Nandy cited the need for a sufficient plurality of views in news media and a sufficient plurality of individuals controlling media enterprises. She has also highlighted the potential impact on streaming services, content homogenisation and children’s television. The Enterprise Act protects something we should all care about: who decides what we get to watch, and what we get to know. Consider the breadth of what this single company would hold. Channel 5, one of our five public service broadcasters , which serves the evening news to people without the cost of a subscription. CNN International, which Ofcom research in 2018 found UK viewers rated above every other TV news source for quality, accuracy, trustworthiness and impartiality. The CNN and CBS news archives – among the world’s most important broadcast news collections, with more than 4.25m videos, images and media spanning nearly half a century of history. If one commercially interested owner controls access to both, they control the raw material of our historical memory. One owner controlling this much of the news, and the truth, endangers the public in a way no ordinary consolidation does. When separate owners run separate newsrooms, a story judged inconvenient by one can still reach audiences through another. Fold those newsrooms into a single company, and one boardroom’s commercial anxieties – or political debts – determine what millions of people see and what they never learn existed. And we know something about this particular proprietor’s intentions. Paramount’s chief executive reportedly told Donald Trump that he would make “ sweeping changes ” to CNN if the deal went through. When the buyer of the world’s most trusted international news channel makes editorial promises to a politician, a British secretary of state is entitled – and, really, obliged – to ask questions before the ink dries. Nandy has been scrupulous in noting that no final decision has been taken. Good. It is important to take the time to get this right. But the case for a full public interest intervention, with Ofcom assessing plurality and reporting back, is overwhelming. Actors are often told to stay out of legal arguments. We understand the instinct. But we have spent our lives on enough UK sets, worked alongside enough UK crews and watched enough brilliant work from the UK struggle to find a buyer to know that this is not someone else’s argument. It is ours. Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes UK television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger. Alan Cumming, Benedict Cumberbatch and Benedict Wong are actors working in the UK and Hollywood

articles.title: ‘House Of The Dragon’s Benjamin Evan Ainsworth Discusses Daeron Targaryen’s Choices & Future Motives As Season 3 Hits Home Stretch
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Major League Soccer Boards Danny Ramirez Soccer Drama ‘Baton’ As Key Partner Artists Equity, Hidden Content, Ultraboom Media And Icki Eneo Arlo Partner On Doc ‘Shot in the Dark’, Following First U.S. Paralympic Blind Soccer Team Sony Pictures Circling Ridley Scott’s ‘Treasure Island’ Package Starring Hugh Jackman View All July 26, 2026 7:01pm Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Daeron Targaryen in 'House of the Dragon' Courtesy of HBO SPOILER ALERT: This story contains details from episode 6 of House of the Dragon on HBO . With only two episodes left of the third season of HBO’s House of the Dragon, the pieces are falling in to place for Ormund Hightower (James Norton) as Daeron Targaryen ( Benjamin Evan Ainsworth ) watches in the wings. Related Stories News ‘House of the Dragon’ Season 3 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Air? Festivals 25 Tons Of Propane, 314 Shooting Days & Lots Of Practical Naval Warfare: How Ryan Condal & Team Pulled Off ‘House Of The Dragon’ Season 3 — ATX TV Festival In the first half of the season, Targaryen kept his guard up and was mindful of his actions in front of his captor, fearing harm may come to him by Hightower if he mades any missteps. On Sunday’s episode, he is finally able to tell someone these fears as his uncle, Ser Gwayne Hightower, vistits Tumbleton to give updates on the war throughout Westeros. Daeron makes it clear to his uncle that he has only been following Ormund’s orders and agreeing with his decisions for self-preservation, not because what Ormund is doing is right. He also lets it be known to Gwayne that while Ormund tells him all this is being done so Daeron can take his seat on the Iron Throne, he is very aware that the chances of becoming king one day are highly unlikely. Watch on Deadline The episode also features a failed assassination attempt on Ormund by Rhaenyra that is thwarted by Gwayne. The scene ends with a number of dead bodies and also shows Gwayne and Daeron how Ormund feels about lost limbs and blood as he vomits in front of them. Ainsworth sat down with Deadline to discuss this week’s episode, including if his character admires some of the schemes Ormund is plotting, his first season on the show, and whether there is more drama to come in Tumbleton before the season comes to an end. DEADLINE: Congrats on the first season Ben, how are you finding it so far? BENJAMIN EVAN AINSWORTH: Well, it’s been it’s been an honor, really. I was a huge fan of Game of Thrones and the first two seasons of Dragon , so I kind of came into the audition process as a fan. So when it came to doing the audition, it was like, the coolest thing ever in itself, but now to be here, having wrapped and watching these episodes come out and seeing the reception, it has been kind of like a whirlwind, but a dream come true. DEADLINE : So the first five episodes, it’s pretty clear Daeron is minding his steps when he’s around Ormond. This is the episode where he’s finally able to say, “I feel like a puppet” and “I’m only doing these things so he doesn’t harm me.”Is he in complete survival mode right now? Or is there a part of him that kind of like weirdly admires the way Ormond is playing the Game of Thrones? AINSWORTH : I think the relationship he has with Ormond is twisted and controlling and manipulative in many ways, but I think it has a bedrock of love that’s binding it together. However warped it may be, I remember in episode 4 where in the beginning he’s kind of talking to the people of Tumbleton and gelding the man who had who had done wrong. There’s almost like a pride and an admiration there in a moment like that. But then the complete opposite, in another moment, where he’s being forced to kill Leo by Ormond. I think he has his guard up all the time with Ormond. He has to, because anything could happen at any moment. He’s had to learn how to deal with him as a character out of survival. There is an aspect of him which has an admiration and wants to be admired by Ormond as well. He’s a 17-year-old kid who’s has no parental figures. He’s sent away from his mother and I think he longs for that kind of affection. DEADLINE: So Ormond’s assassins are raising havoc in King’s Landing, killing Daemon’s men under Ormond’s orders, but in the name of King Daeron. Do you actually think he has the aspirations to be king or, if he had a choice, would he rather just be a high lord and just not have bear the responsibility? AINSWORTH : If you asked him two weeks before Season 3, he would never have dreamed of being king. It wasn’t on his mind. This kind of prospect has been thrust upon him in this season. He’s been thrown in the middle of the dance between Hightower and Targaryen. I think he’s still kind of grappling with the shock of it as well as questioning himself. What do I want? I find kind of that one was more interesting than the answer in many ways, the aspect of him coming of age and figuring out who he is through this chaotic time. But if he were to think about being king, it comes from a position of almost getting out of this domineering relationship. Like a sense of freedom away from that. I suppose leading with his awareness, with his kind of empathy, but also I think he has no idea nor decided on any path. DEADLINE: You’ve spent a lot of this season basically talking a lot; there’s not a lot of action going on. You get your first big set piece even though you’re not quite involved, more of an observer. While it’s an awesome scene, there’s a very important moment, I feel, where we see how Orman reacts when he’s in a situation like this. The actual sight of blood and dead bodies makes him vomit. I’m curious, while Daeron looks rattled because of what he just witnessed, he looks over and part of me wonders, does Daeron now see Orman as a weaker leader, and not this powerful person? Does that moment give Daeron thoughts about how he can control the situation and maybe get out of this because of how Orman reacts in that moment? AINSWORTH : I think it’s definitely a change in the way Daeron is seeing things. A lot of it is the shock of the moment, but also there is certainly something to the idea that I’ve been controlled and kind of molded by this person. As soon things become real and dangerous, he’s debilitated. And so there’s almost a frustration with that. How can I be controlled by someone who has been taken out this easily? I don’t think it computes to something directly I can use against him in that moment, but I suppose it really feels like a kettle boiling in this episode. The power dynamics are really kind of teetering and getting closer to switching the other way. DEADLINE: I wanted to talk about the filming in general. This is your first season and this show is so broad in scope and epic action scenes, dragons, etc. I find it fascinating for you and James, it’s almost like a play where it’s grounded, you’re almost in the same room the whole time talking. Has it helped with this being your first season on the show for the two of you? To be slowly moved in where you’re not involved with these grand battles and stuff where you’re able to kind of find your footing as character,s or are you a little jealous when you see your co-stars flying dragons and in big battles? AINSWORTH : Oh, yeah, good question. I don’t know. To be able to have your group and to be able to move around the world with your couple of actors, it just means that I’ve found at least that I’ve made these great connections between the characters, but also just as people on set, to be able to be together and have scenes where it’s just the four of us for half the show, I think it makes it easy to make communities. DEADLINE: Is there one big move we can expect from Daeron within this home stretch or is it too early to say with what will come with him and Ormond? AINSWORTH : I think the stage is set for a fun finish, certainly in Tumbleton. So, yeah, keep an eye on Gwayne and Daeron’s relationship and whatever Orman’s got cooking in the oven. I hope fans enjoy the last couple episodes. articles.title: Dylan Mulvaney Responds To Trump’s WHCD “Diss Track,” Feels Like “The One That Got Away” For MAGA Men
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ Writer-Director Reveals Sequel Has Been Written, Hasn’t Been Made For “Financial Reasons” Dylan Mulvaney Responds To Trump’s WHCD “Diss Track,” Feels Like “The One That Got Away” For MAGA Men Mary Beth Barone Says She & Benito Skinner Tried To “Get Out” Of ‘Ride’ Podcast Contract Over Dear Media CEO’s Politics: “Hard To Reconcile That” View All July 26, 2026 7:08pm Dylan Mulvaney responds to Trump's WHCD mention. Mandel Ngan/AFP/Mike Marsland/WireImage More than three years after sparking conservative backlash with her Bud Light social media partnership, Dylan Mulvaney was as surprised as anyone to hear her name in Donald Trump ‘s mouth at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner. Counting “four times” the POTUS mentioned her name in his speech on Friday, the Broadway actress, TikTok personality and transgender advocate reacted to being “the one that got away” for MAGA men after Trump attempted to roast her in his hour-long “diss track” at the WHCA’s annual event. “Firstly, I would like to congratulate CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on her award and tell her that I’m incredibly honored to be compared to her in any way, and I hope that she keeps doing all the great work,” prefaced Mulvaney in a TikTok video . Related Stories News Donald Trump Delivers Rally-Like Hour Of Rehash In White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech Politics Dylan Mulvaney Addresses Firestorm Of Hate Sparked By Bud Light Endorsement For The First Time After the WHCA awarded Collins the Excellence in Presidential News Coverage Under Deadline Pressure, Trump joked in his set that he “thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” to which the audience had no reaction. Watch on Deadline “And Dylan Mulaney cost Bud Light $35 billion dollar in market cap,” Trump continued as the crowd stayed silent. “That was the worst commercial ever made, by the way, for those few people that want to hear that. Most people don’t care, but I would. I wouldn’t want to hire Dylan anytime soon. Think of it, they hired Dylan Mulaney and their market cap has gone down by $35 billion. Who wrote that commercial?” @dylanmulvaney A response 🇺🇸❤️ please support trans and non binary people today and every day ♬ I Am America – Shea Diamond Noting the Bud Light video Trump mentioned was more than three years ago, Mulvaney said in her video, “Mind you, I’ve been kind of flying under the radar, keeping up a pretty low profile, just doing my little musicals, singing, dancing, and yet I am still his topic of conversation all these years later. It seems to me that I might be like the one that got away for these men. I am permanently burned into their retinas. I am microchipped into their minds.” Mulvaney added, “Maybe being publicly mocked and criticized by this administration is actually the greatest compliment of all, because it puts me in the company of some of the most brilliant, empathetic people in our world today. … They want to use their power to take away my freedom. But what they don’t understand is that my freedom has zero contingency on what they can provide for me, because my freedom is fully dependent on the moment that I acknowledged my real authentic self and every day since, and sharing that with the world is the icing on the cake. “They don’t want me to be able to share that,” she continued. “Because it would mean young people realizing that, if someone like me can be themselves and find success and freedom, then they can find success and freedom for themselves too.” In April 2023, Bud Light sent a can of their beer with Mulvaney’s face on it to her, which she featured in a TikTok video, prompting intense conservative backlash and a boycott of the brand. After spectacularly bombing with his WHCD speech, Trump continued to take swipes at his enemies on Truth Social over the weekend with a flood of AI-generated images, including one post featuring Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body in the Bud Light video. articles.title: Ryan Reynolds Thanks ‘Deadpool’ Fans For “Unapologetic Devotion” After Undercover Comic-Con Appearance – Watch Video
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ Writer-Director Reveals Sequel Has Been Written, Hasn’t Been Made For “Financial Reasons” Dylan Mulvaney Responds To Trump’s WHCD “Diss Track,” Feels Like “The One That Got Away” For MAGA Men Mary Beth Barone Says She & Benito Skinner Tried To “Get Out” Of ‘Ride’ Podcast Contract Over Dear Media CEO’s Politics: “Hard To Reconcile That” View All July 26, 2026 7:43pm Ryan Reynolds goes undercover as Deadpool at San Diego Comic-Con. Ryan Reynolds/X With Deadpool regenerating for a fourth blockbuster outing, Ryan Reynolds is already getting back into character as the wisecracking mercenary. After his surprise in-costume appearance at Comic-Con during Marvel’s Hall H presentation on Saturday, the Golden Globe nominee shared a behind-the-scenes video of his undercover visit with fans as he walked the floor at the San Diego Convention Center. “The fans got Deadpool off the ground so many years ago,” wrote Reynolds on X with the video. “Yesterday, 10 years after the first film and exactly 2 years after Deadpool & Wolverine , I felt so lucky to be on the #SDCC floor with everyone whose unapologetic devotion brings so much joy to this world.” Related Stories News Ryan Reynolds Confirms New ‘Deadpool’ Movie In Works News ‘Transformers: The Movie’ Getting Fall Theatrical Re-Release From Hasbro & Fathom – Comic-Con The video also featured a clip of Robert Downey Jr. calling on him while hitting the stage with his Avengers: Doomsday co-stars. “Who’s this guy with the swords and stuff?” asked the Doctor Doom actor. Watch on Deadline “Long-time listener, first-time caller,” said Reynolds into the mic as the crowd cheered. “This seems an awfully expensive way to announce a film. When do you start filming?” The fans got Deadpool off the ground so many years ago. Yesterday, 10 years after the first film and exactly 2 years after Deadpool & Wolverine, I felt so lucky to be on the #SDCC floor with everyone whose unapologetic devotion brings so much joy to this world. pic.twitter.com/IM7DSIjNfs — Ryan Reynolds (@VancityReynolds) July 26, 2026 Reynolds’ surprise appearance comes after he teased last week at New York’s Fantastic Fest that Deadpool 4 is in the works . “There’s a few really deep cuts that I think are missing behind the movies. I think there’s a few deep cuts missing from some of the comics,” said Reynolds. “There’s certainly some stuff that I love that [ Deadpool co-creator] Fabian Nicieza wrote that is incredible. Gerry Duggan, who was a friend, was an incredible comic writer. There’s stuff upcoming. There’s eventually, remotely another Deadpool film. It’s going to be great.” After test footage of Reynolds as the Marvel anti-hero leaked in 2014, five years after he originated another version of the character in X-Men Origins: Wolverine (2009), the actor earned a Golden Globe nomination for his performance in 2016’s Deadpool . He’s since reprised the role in Deadpool 2 (2018) and Deadpool & Wolverine (2024), the latter earning $1.3B globally and catapulting the franchise past the $2B mark. Jonathan Goldstein , who co-wrote and co-directed Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves with John Francis Daley, revealed at Comic-Con that they wrote a sequel to their 2023 adaptation of the tabletop role-playing game. “We actually wrote a sequel to Dungeons & Dragons . We were hired to write it,” Goldstein told ScreenRant . “I don’t know that it will see the light of day for a number of financial reasons. They’re expensive movies to make, but it’d be great fun to do it. We love that cast, and we think we wrote something that fans would like. Related Stories News Dungeons & Dragons Live-Action Series ‘The Forgotten Realms’ In Works At Netflix From Shawn Levy, Drew Crevello & Hasbro News ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ Locks Up $38.5M Opening: Is This Enough To Start A Franchise? – Sunday Box Office Despite a solid 91% critic rating and 92% from fans on Rotten Tomatoes, Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves grossed $205M worldwide on a $150M budget . Watch on Deadline While a live-action Dungeons & Dragons series was ordered for Paramount+ in 2023, the streamer opted not to move forward with the Rawson Marshall Thurber-created show the following year. Hasbro has since shopped the project around, finding a new home at Netflix with a new iteration, entitled The Forgotten Realms , from Shawn Levy and writer-showrunner Drew Crevello. articles.title: Netflix India Boss Monika Shergill Eyes Global Format Adaptations After “Captive Reality” Series ‘Lock Upp’ Hits 50 Million Hours
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Netflix India Boss Monika Shergill Eyes Global Format Adaptations After “Captive Reality” Series ‘Lock Upp’ Hits 50 Million Hours Carlton Cuse On How Sports Rights Fights Are Hurting Scripted, Fair Residuals, AI & Netflix Series ‘The Secret Of Secrets’ International Insider: Venice Lineup Analysis; Rebel Wilson Legal Victory; Lisa Nandy, Troublemaker-In-Chief View All July 26, 2026 11:30pm Monika Shergill (left) and 'Lock Upp' Netflix EXCLUSIVE: Is Netflix eyeing an Indian version of Love is Blind or Too Hot to Handle ? In an exclusive interview with Deadline, Netflix India VP of Content Monika Shergill revealed her service was working on developing Netflix-owned unscripted formats locally, without revealing their identities. “We are working on a couple of very interesting, big global formats, which are Netflix formats, and they will be coming to India,” she said. While Netflix does not own either Too Hot to Handle and Love is Blind , it the has exclusive international production deals in place for both and has created numerous versions. The underlying format rights remain with Too Hot to Handle program maker Fremantle and The North Road Company-owned Kinetic Content, the maker of Love is Blind . Related Stories News Kalshi Threatens Netflix With Defamation Suit Over "Misleading" Prediction Market Doc Trailer News How 'Ransom Canyon' Season 2's Thomas Rhett & Jordan Davis Music Festival Concert Came Together, Starting With Josh Duhamel Pushed on the identity of the shows, Shergill said: “I am not at liberty to share right now, but something exciting will be announced very soon.” Watch on Deadline The news came as Shergill was outlining the breakout success of another format for which Netflix is rights owner – the Balaji Telefilms -produced “captive reality” show Lock Upp . The show, which debuted on June 27 and will continue playing until August 5, follows celebrity contestants, known as inmates, who live in a jail-themed setting and compete in tasks while facing eliminations. Shergill and Lock Upp creator Ekta Kapoor said the show has become “the most defining entertainment conversation,” with the Netflix chief revealing it has amassed 50 million hours viewed since launch last month (“the equivalent of 5,700 years,” according to Shergill) and accrued 2.5 billion social media interactions within three weeks of launch. The spent two weeks in the Global Top (Non-English) Series list, as Indian unscripted series grow in global popularity. It began with five episodes in the first week, but the “on-audience demand and overwhelming success” has seen this upped to six. “Up to the finale, we’ll just be going nonstop,” she added. Netflix’s most recent What We Watched data dump revealed the show is the second-most watched series by hours. Kapoor, a veteran film and TV producer in India, outlined her theory behind the show’s popularity. “It’s the fact that celebrities are coming in with tags and judgment, and they’re able to discuss that why they are like that, or what has made them like that, so their secrets become their lifelines,” she said. “It’s one way they touch base with their own humanity, their own understanding, their own traumas.” The series actually began life in 2022 on ALTBalaji, the now defunct streamer that Balaji Telefilms operated, and MX Player, which was recently subsumed into Prime Video India. Netflix revitalized it with Bollywood stars Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh hosting, and a contestant cast including actors Dheeraj Dhoopar, Shivangi Joshi, Harshad Chopda and Shilpa Shinde. Kapoor was quick to credit Shergill and Netflix for supporting her vision to revive the show, revealing she rejected two other offers to move ahead with the Los Gatos-based streamer. “When you work with a platform, you want to work with a platform that takes your concept or your idea bigger than you thought, and supports your vision,” she said. “For a creator, there is nothing bigger than support – and it doesn’t have to be only financial. It is also because sense of ownership is mutual, and respect is mutual. If make a show for Netflix, I know that Netflix won’t abandon me midway, because it’s not doing well. They will run with me until the last mile.” Pressed by Deadline, Shergill and Kapoor declined to confirm a second season of Lock Upp on Netflix or if the show will be adapted outside of India. However, Shergill did say: “The format is getting a lot of interest internally. I cannot confirm either of those questions, but since it’s doing so well, I think it has a long life.” Comedy focus Besides adapting global formats, Shergill’s other focus at Netflix India is in comedy and growing local talent. One example is stand-up Samay Raina, who first appeared on the streamer on long-running talk series The Great Indian Kapil Show . His chemistry with host and fellow comedian Kapil Sharma was such that Shergill, who had already ordered a stand-up special from him, began a conversation about bringing his YouTube show, India’s Got Latent , to Netflix. A co-exclusive deal for Season 2 was struck, which Shergill calls a “great experiment” and potentially the precusor to similar agreements with both platforms, Raina and his audience all responding positively. “The thinking was very simple, actually,” she said “We really want to be the best home for comedy and the best comedic talent in the country. Samay had come for The Great Indian Kapil Show , and their partnership and that episode worked so well that when we were talking about his stand-up special, and it came up that Latent Season 2 was coming out, it was just intuitive that, uh, the show could exist on Netflix in an ad-free version for his fans. “It just shows that the best kind of creative actually should sit in experiences and different kinds of experiences. We have a huge audience for it on Netflix India.” The Great Indian Kapil Show , which followed on from Sharma’s network shows The Kapil Sharma Show and Comedy Nights with Kapil , is headed for a fifth season and stand-up specials from many of India’s top performers such as Zakir Khan have become top-performing productions. As such, the comedy space “is something that we want to own in India,” said Shergill, and projects are underway wth several big names. While Shergill feels the momentum is with Netflix right now, the service is competing in one of the toughest streaming markets in the world, where JioHotstar, Sony LIV and Prime Video, now including MX Player, are all key players. Indeed, in March 2024, Mike Hopkins, the Head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, said India was responsible for new streaming subscribers than anywhere else bar the U.S. for his service. However, only about a quarter of the 601 million streaming consumers in India pay for services, according to Ormax Media research from September 2025, so Netflix has a fight on its hands, but Shergill and her team are taking a bullish outlook. “We’ve been having great momentum,” said. Shergill. “We are one of the most loved entertainment, streaming entertainment services in India. Yes, there is fierce competition, but everyone’s offering and value proposition is different. “What defines Netflix is the ability to do premium and aspirational content and yet make it the most accessible. If I were to just give you a sense of where we are today, the biggest theatrical movies are on Netflix across languages. The biggest premium dramas are on Netflix. The biggest unscripted entertainment is on Netflix today with Kapil Sharma , Lock Upp , Fabulous Lives of Desi Wives and Desi Bling , and the biggest original documentaries consistently are on Netflix. So are most of the awards. “I have great regard for all our competitive services, and we learn a lot from them, but I think the the value and the edge that Netflix brings is our constant experimentation and innovation. No one programs as diversely as we do. No one takes as many bets as we do, whether big, medium or small, and that is what has consistently made our offering the strongest. “We are actually seeing India being one of the biggest growth markets for Netflix all over the world.” ‘Operation Safed Sagar’ While much of the recent focus has been on unscripted, the next big bet from Netflix in India is Operation Safed Sagar , a high-budget military drama series focused on the Indian Air Force’s 1999 aerial campaign during the Kargil War against Pakistan. Shergill calls the show, which is latest in India’s long line of productions on its military prowess, “a very large format VFX extravaganza.” Matchbox Shots and Feel Good Films are making the show in direct collaboration with the Indian Air Force. “The Lock Upp finale is going to be a very big conversation wave in India given the way the pre-finale weeks are looking, and immediately after that, we have Operation Safed Sagar , our biggest show in the tenth year of Netflix in India. There are a whole slew of shows after that, which will be addressing the different audience tastes and moods that we cater to – really the whole spectrum of audience.” Netflix’s Monika Shergill On ‘Lock Upp’ As Indian Series Hits 50M Hours Marvel: Gosling As Ghost Rider; Jonsson In ‘Black Panther 3’; Latest Pics ‘The Odyssey’s $87M+ 2nd Frame Sets Nolan Record, Tops ‘Dark Knight’ Agrees Not To Close WBD Merger Until Next Year; Opponents Cheer Delay Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Benedict Cumberbatch Says Paramount-Warner Deal Is A “Calamity” That Must Be Blocked
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake ‘The Deb’ Star Charlotte MacInnes Attacks Rebel Wilson In Appeal Against Court Defeat Mark Jermin, TikTok-Famous Agent Who Discovered ‘Harry Potter’ & ‘Wednesday’ Stars, May Have Broken UK Agency Law Paramount’s Takeover Of Warner Bros. Discovery Gets EU Greenlight View All July 27, 2026 1:32am Benedict Cumberbatch in Paramount Pictures movie 'Star Trek Into Darkness' Paramount Pictures Benedict Cumberbatch has co-authored an op-ed with Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong in which the actors argue that Paramount ‘s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery should be blocked in the UK. In The Guardian article , headlined ‘A TV and cinema calamity could be disastrous for what you watch and what you know. Act now to stop that,’ the actors called on Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to intervene in the $111 billion merger for the good of the British screen industry. It follows Nandy telling UK Parliament that she is “minded to intervene” in the takeover, but she is yet to make a final decision on whether to submit the union to a full public interest investigation. She is expected to reach a conclusion when Parliament returns from its summer break in September . Watch on Deadline Related Stories Legal Paramount-WBD Merger Opponents Cheer Legal Delay, Stocks Slide As Industry Absorbs Latest Plot Twist Legal Amazon Hit With Poaching Lawsuit By Warner Bros Discovery Over Hire Of HBO Max Marketing Exec Pia Barlow Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong wrote: “Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes UK television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger.” Paramount declined to comment, but a spokesperson pointed to a February open letter CEO David Ellison wrote to the UK creative community, committing to content investment, theatrical windows, and preserving HBO. The actors voiced concerns about the Paramount-Warner merger putting the “livelihoods of thousands of workers” at risk in the UK. They are also anxious about the concentration of news services, given that the combined company would control 5 News, CNN International, and CBS News. “One owner controlling this much of the news, and the truth, endangers the public in a way no ordinary consolidation does,” they said. “And we know something about this particular proprietor’s intentions. Paramount’s chief executive reportedly told Donald Trump that he would make ‘sweeping changes’ to CNN if the deal went through. When the buyer of the world’s most trusted international news channel makes editorial promises to a politician, a British secretary of state is entitled – and, really, obliged – to ask questions before the ink dries.” The trio added: “Should her department decide to intervene, it may prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation.” Their op-ed follows WarnerMount securing regulatory clearance in the European Union last week, before the deal was put on ice until June 2027 , or until shortly after the merits of lawsuits brought by state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America are resolved. The pause makes Nandy’s decision slightly less pivotal, given it looked at one point that the UK could stand in the way of Paramount meeting its closure deadline of September 30. Paramount’s deal could close without UK clearance because the merger control regime is non-suspensory, though Ellison has always intended to respect the British process. Cumming has previously made his feelings known about the merger. Earlier this month, The Traitors host posted a video as part of a coalition calling itself Block the Merger UK , which urged people to contact the Department for Culture, Media and Sport or regulator Ofcom, demanding they examine the merger in more depth. articles.title: Bill Oddie Dies: British TV Presenter & Birdwatcher Was 85
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Netflix India Boss Monika Shergill Eyes Global Format Adaptations After “Captive Reality” Series ‘Lock Upp’ Hits 50 Million Hours Carlton Cuse On How Sports Rights Fights Are Hurting Scripted, Fair Residuals, AI & Netflix Series ‘The Secret Of Secrets’ International Insider: Venice Lineup Analysis; Rebel Wilson Legal Victory; Lisa Nandy, Troublemaker-In-Chief View All July 27, 2026 2:43am Bill Oddie Mark Milan/GC Images Bill Oddie , Britain’s most beloved birdwatcher and wildlife TV presenter, has died aged 85. His death was confirmed by his agent, David Foster, in at a statement carried by several British news outlets. “It is with deep sadness that I announce the passing of Bill Oddie, the country’s best-loved birder. “Bill was a multi-talented celebrity – wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Related Stories News BBC Buys 'Kabul' Drama Series About American Withdrawal From Afghanistan Starring The Late Eric Dane News 'Ted Lasso' Star Toheeb Jimoh & 'Snow White's Dujonna Gift Leading BBC's 'Open Water' Adaptation “Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment. He taught us the wonder of it. He protested, lobbied and campaigned for it. He led the way and people of all ages and backgrounds responded to his call. And such a massive contribution to conservation will never be forgotten. Watch on Deadline “As Bill’s agent I witnessed close-hand his intelligence and wit. He was my friend and it was an honour and a privilege to represent him for so many years. I will miss him terribly. My thoughts and love are with Bill’s wife, Laura, and his daughters Bonnie, Kate and Rosie, who have asked not to be contacted at this sad time. Please respect their wishes.” Oddie is best known for his BBC wildlife programs, especially those tracking the UK’s bird life, but he was also a script writer, composer and comedian. His BBC shows include Springwatch , Autumnwatch , How to Watch Wildlife , Birding with Bill Oddie , Britain Goes Wild with Bill Oddie and Bill Oddie Goes Wild . Oddie’s career in entertainment began, like many others, in the Cambridge Footlights sketch comedy group. While he was there, one revue was so popular that it played in the West End and on Broadway in 1964. Around this time, he also contributed to BBC comedy series That Was the Week That Was . Oddie went on to form The Goodies with Tim Brooke-Taylor and Graeme Garden, whom he had met at Footlights. They worked on various TV and music projects, with Oddie and Garden later spending ten years on IBBC’s The Goodies sketch comedy show between 1970 and 1980. A special later ran in 1981 and the show was revived for another season in 1982 on ITV. As an avid birder, Oddie behan contributing to BBC wildlife shows in the 1970 and went to become one of the UK’s most well-known and beloved presenters in the genre. He also wrote several books on birdwatching and was a trusted voice in debates about conservation in Britain, and subject on 1985 special Nature Watch Special: Bill Oddie – Bird Watcher . His BBC2 show, Britain Goes Wild , set a channel ratings record of 3.4 million viewers in 2004. The show was later renamed Springwatch , which remains a staple on the channel. He presented the show until 2008. Oddie became an unseen fixture in the life Steve Coogan’s fictional TV presenter Alan Partridge, who consistently referred to their unusual friendship, which included Partridge receiving dressing gowns and borrowing binoculars to spy on his estranged wife. The collaboration spans more than 100 titles in total and is an extension of the existing global deal between Prime Video and CJ ENM, further strengthening the association. All new and upcoming titles under the deal will feature subtitles in English and dubbing in Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu. “Building on our strong global relationship with CJ ENM and the deal announced last year, we’re excited to deepen this collaboration with a sharper focus on India,” said Shilangi Mukherji, director and head, SVOD business, Prime Video India. Compelling narratives, diverse genres, and memorable characters that transcend borders have fueled a K-content wave that continues to gain momentum year on year. By bringing a curated slate of premium Korean titles to Prime Video, we’re doubling down on our commitment to making the most innovative and captivating stories from Korea accessible to audiences in India.” Watch on Deadline The slate kicks off with Yumi’s Cells Season Three , the latest instalment of CJ ENM’s flagship franchise that topped streaming charts in 81 countries, including the U.S., Brazil, France and the UAE. For us, this deal is not only the natural step forward, backed by customer preferences, but also a reflection of commitment to making Prime Video India the go-to destination for the best international content.” Jangho Seo, EVP of Platform Division at CJ ENM, said” “We are pleased to collaborate with Prime Video India to bring CJ ENM’s acclaimed K-dramas to a wider audience in one of the world’s most dynamic entertainment markets. “Prime Video’s unmatched reach in India, combined with its deep investment in local audiences, makes it the ideal partner to amplify our content to millions of new viewers. This partnership reflects our ongoing commitment to expanding the global reach of Korean storytelling. articles.title: Diego Luna To Receive Honorary Heart Of Sarajevo Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Full Competition Lineup European Film Academy Chief Matthijs Wouter Knol & Greek Filmmaker Athina Rachel Tsangari Join Emily Watson On Sarajevo Film Festival Jury Asghar Farhadi To Receive Honorary Award At Sarajevo Film Festival View All July 27, 2026 4:57am Diego Luna Photo courtesy of Corey Nickols Diego Luna is set to be awarded an Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award at the upcoming Sarajevo Film Festival in recognition of his career and contribution to world cinema. The Mexican actor-director-producer, whose work spans across film, TV and theater, will touch down at the Bosnian festival to present his latest directorial feature Ashes , which premiered at Cannes earlier this year. Luna will also give a masterclass, sharing his experience and perspectives on contemporary artistic practice with emerging talents, film professionals and festival audiences. Related Stories Festivals Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Full Competition Lineup Festivals European Film Academy Chief Matthijs Wouter Knol & Greek Filmmaker Athina Rachel Tsangari Join Emily Watson On Sarajevo Film Festival Jury Luna’s international breakout performance was in Alfonso Cuarón’s 2001 title Y tu mama también , a role that established him as one of Mexico’s top screen talents. He went on to collaborate with directors such as Steven Spielberg, David Trueba, Gus Van Sant, Harmony Korine and Agustín Diaz Yanes. Watch on Deadline More recently, he starred in and executive produced the Disney+ series Andor , which saw him earn two Golden Globe nominations and two Critics’ Choice Award nominations for his work in both seasons. The series earned eight Emmy nominations for its first season and 14 for its second season, including Outstanding Drama Series. Luna also received two Normal Felton Award nominations alongside his team in the PGA Awards for his work as a producer in Andor . He recently starred in Netflix’s México 86 on which he also serves as executive producer and will appear in the thriller Eleven Days and Disney’s live-action adaptation of Tangled . Luna’s further credits include: Bill Condon’s Kiss of the Spider Woman ; La Máquina , which he also produced and starred in alongside Gael García Bernal; Netflix’s Narcos: México ; Star Wars: Rogue One ; and Bread & Circus . As a director, Luna made his debut with the documentary J.C. Chávez in 2007. His first narrative feature, Abel , earned the Horizontes Latinos Award at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and a Mexican Academy Award for Best Screenplay, which he co-wrote. He later director Mr. Pig , which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. Beyond his creative work, Luna is deeply committed to social impact initiatives. In 2005, he co-founded Ambulante, a traveling documentary film festival created to foster cultural exchange. The festival was founded alongside García Bernal, Pablo Cruz, Elena Fortesand El Día Después, a Mexico City-based NGO that connects citizens with longstanding organizations to drive civic engagement and social change. “A quarter of a century ago, Diego Luna won our hearts with his unforgettable performance in Y Tu Mamá También ,” said Jovan Marjanović, Director of the Sarajevo Film Festival. “We hoped then and know now that we were witnessing the emergence of an artist who would never case to explore and surprise, moving seamlessly from major Hollywood productions to intimate human stories that reveal the richness of Latin American culture. Through his exceptional body of work, Diego Luna has left a profound mark on contemporary cinema, and it is our great honor to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.” Luna added: “It’s been many years since I’ve wanted to go to Sarajevo. So many colleagues have spoken beautifully about the festival and their personal experience there. I feel honored with the recognition of my work and very excited to share Ashes with the audience.” The 32 nd Sarajevo Film Festival will take place from August 14-21, 2026. articles.title: Thabo Rametsi Unveiled As Apartheid Era Music Legend Hugh Masekela In First Look Image For Bill Condon’s ‘The Road Home’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Thabo Rametsi Unveiled As Apartheid Era Music Legend Hugh Masekela In First Look Image For Bill Condon’s ‘The Road Home’ Oscar Documentary Contender ‘House Of Hope’ Secures North American Distribution Film Financiers & Producers Flock To Inaugural African Film Investor Roundtable In Cape Town View All July 27, 2026 5:01am The Road Home South African actor, writer, director and producer Thabo Rametsi ( Silverton Siege ) has been unveiled with in his role as activist and music legend Hugh Masekela in Bill Condon’s The Road Home as the filming continues in South Africa . A first look image released by the film’s backers and producers Canal+, Studiocanal and Flora Film as well as South African co-producer Blue Ice, shows Rametsi as Masekela, who lived in exile in the UK and the U.S. for 30 years after fleeing his native South Africa in the wake of the 1960 Sharpeville Massacre, playing his trumpet. The film follows Masekela as he finds himself at a crossroads when the Anti-Apartheid Movement, led by anti-apartheid advocate and mentor Archbishop Trevor Huddleston, launches a boycott against his friend Paul Simon over his township music-inspired album ‘Graceland’, accusing Simon of violating the United Nations’ Cultural Boycott. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Film Financiers & Producers Flock To Inaugural African Film Investor Roundtable In Cape Town News 'Terminator 2: Judgment Day' Sets 35th Anniversary Global Re-Release Masekela, who saw music as a powerful weapon in the anti-apartheid struggle, would split with Huddleston to join forces with fellow exile and lifelong collaborator, powerhouse vocalist Miriam ‘Mama Africa’ Makeba to create the Graceland band, a super group designed to bring South Africa’s voice to the world. As previously announced, Rametsi is joined in the cast by Guy Pearce as Huddleston; Johnny Flynn as Simon and Cynthia Erivo as Makeba. “When you tell the story of Giants you must shout it from the highest mountain. These are our giants and this film is the highest mountain we could find. We hope our humble tribute honours them accordingly,” said Rametsi, who is EP on the film. Condon ( Gods and Monsters ) directs from an original script written by Michael Bronner ( The Mauritanian, United 93 ), from a story by Bronner and Zakes Mda. The Canal+ and Studiocanal-backed feature is produced by Academy Award-Nominated producer Laura Bickford ( Traffic, Che Part 1 and Part 2, Arbitrage ), Bronner, Greg Yolen ( Kiss of the Spider Woman, The Good Liar ), and Anant Singh ( Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom, Sarafina! ), in association with Blue Ice’s producers Tebogo Maila and Adam Friedlander and with executive producers Fiona Druckenmiller, and Rametsi.
