articles.title: ‘Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees’ Final Act Gets Title and Cover (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All July 25, 2026 2:15pm Patrick Horvath Courtesy of IDW Logo text Cuddly serial killer comic book Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees is heading into its final bloody act. The final six-issue chapter of the hit franchise will be titled Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees: The Summer and the Fall and will debut in February 2027. Creator Patrick Horvath and publisher IDW are announcing the title and giving a first look Saturday at a San Diego Comic-Con panel discussing horror in comics. The ending is bittersweet for Horvath, who launched the book in 2024 with little fanfare and saw it not only gain accolades such as Eisner nominations and a Harvey Award, but also an unexpected continuation of its story; as its success continues to play out, it has launched a spinoff, an art book, and even bloody plushies. Related Stories Movies Comic Creators James Tynion IV, Tony Fleecs Tackling 'Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees' Halloween Special (Exclusive) General News Dan Stevens Joins 'Dexter: Resurrection' Season 2 in Serial Killer Role “When I initially pitched the first arc, I honestly thought that would be the end of it, but about halfway through writing and drawing that, I had the spark of what would grow into a second and third installment,” said Horvath in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter. “It’s bittersweet to be bringing this to a close now, but mostly I’m filled with a lot of gratitude for IDW taking a chance on me and the global comics community for giving me such an insanely warm welcome.” With its Dexter meets Richard Scary tones, it centered on a brown bear named Samantha Strong, a seemingly mild-mannered hardware store owner (who is actually a serial killer) living in a bucolic suburban town of Woodbrook. The first story was set in the 1980s while the second volume, recently wrapped, was set in the 1990s, at the dawn of the Internet age and culminated with a shocking finale that left readers’ jaws on the forest floor. Taking another decade leap forward, the story takes place in 2004 as small-town America has died and the country is seemingly locked into a forever war in the Middle East. Strong, once the most infamous and most wanted person in the country, had faded into obscurity. She’s now in her 60s and attempting to live a quiet life off the grid in the desert. She kills when the opportunity presents itself, but she spends her time surviving. But it’s only a matter of time until she’s recognized. “Samantha Strong now finds herself having to answer for all of her deeds to a world that has become obsessed with true crime, global terrorism, and the slippery notion of righteous violence, stated Horvath, before teasing, “It might all lead to a major change for her, or this might just be the end of the road.” Beneath the Trees has proven to be a massive hit for IDW. The two series so far, including comics and collections, have sold more than 400,000 copies, a massive amount for what is still a relatively new and original title from an indie publisher. On top of the two story volumes, an oversized Artist’s Edition, spotlighting Horvath’s original painted work, goes on sale July 28. And an anthology spinoff issue, a Halloween Special with talents such as James Tynion IV and Tony Fleecs, is being published in October. The plushies are on pre-order from IDW. THR is revealing the cover for issue No. 1 of The Summer and the Fall below. Said Horvath, “With the cover, I wanted to allude to the notion that Samantha’s past life has been abandoned, sort of like a gunslinger burying their pistols, but there’s also that idea in there of excavation and forensics.” Courtesy of IDW THR

articles.title: Christopher Nolan Says He Would Be “Terrified” to Direct a Romantic Comedy
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 25, 2026 4:31pm Christopher Nolan Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images for Kodak Film Awards Christopher Nolan has directed everything from sci-fi thrillers such as Interstellar , Tenet and Inception to historical dramas like Dunkirk and Oppenheimer , mysteries like The Prestige and Memento and superhero films with his Dark Knight trilogy. But there’s one genre the Oscar-winning filmmaker said he’d be “terrified” to tackle: romantic comedies. During his first appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon Thursday, Nolan discussed the lengths he went to shoot his adaptation of Homer’s Greek epic The Odyssey on 70mm IMAX cameras, making it the first feature film to do so. Fallon jokingly asked the director if he ever thinks about doing an “easy” next film, specifically asking, “How about a Christopher Nolan rom-com?” Related Stories Movies 'The Odyssey' Holding Strong for Big Second Weekend in $84.5M Range Lifestyle It Took Nearly 3,000 Years, But Odysseus Finally Got His Funko Pop “I think doing a rom-com would be incredibly difficult,” Nolan replied. “I love watching those movies. But, no, I think people who direct comedy, people who do comedy, I think that’s one of the hardest things in the world to make people laugh that way.” “Particularly the risk they take,” he continued. “When you make a film … you know, if I show a film to people and maybe they don’t respond to bits of it, I’m like, ‘Ah, they don’t get it. Whatever.’ There’s no hiding behind that when you do comedy.” When it comes to the genre, Nolan admitted, “I would be terrified of doing anything like that.” While romantic comedies aren’t on his radar, horror is another story. In a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter , Nolan was asked whether The Odyssey had whet his appetite for directing a horror film, given that it features several horror-like sequences. “It very much whets my appetite for more,” he responded. “But I’ve always believed that horror as a genre has to be approached very carefully from a conceptual point of view. In other words, you have to have an amazing idea,” Nolan added. “When you go see a film like Obsession , that’s an amazing idea. That movie works like a motherfucker. It’s not about the technical side. It’s not about what technical itches I would have to scratch. It’s about story. So I’m always looking.” The Odyssey is now playing in theaters , starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway and more. (See THR’s cast guide to all the stars and who they’re playing here .) THR

articles.title: John Cena Races to Find a Nuclear Warhead in ‘Matchbox the Movie’ Trailer
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 25, 2026 5:39pm John Cena in 'Matchbox the Movie.' Courtesy of Apple TV Logo text John Cena is revving up the action with the trailer for Matchbox the Movie . Apple TV debuted the first footage from filmmaker Sam Hargrave ‘s feature during the streamer’s panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday. Jessica Biel , Arturo Castro, Sam Richardson , Teyonah Parris, Danai Gurira , Golshifteh Farahani, Corey Stoll and Bill Camp also star in the movie that begins streaming on Oct. 9. Inspired by Mattel ‘s line of toy cars, Matchbox the Movie centers on a group of longtime friends who discover that their leader, Sean (Cena), is an undercover CIA agent. Soon, Sean’s complicated life has thrust them into a globe-trotting adventure to save the world. Related Stories TV Hudson Williams and Carrie-Anne Moss Star in Equal Parts Steamy and Spooky 'Yaga' Teaser TV 'Widow's Bay' Creator on Writing Season 2 After Buzzy Launch: "I Learned a Lot About What You Don't Need" “It’s been a long since we played Matchbox cars together,” Biel says wistfully in the trailer. Later, Cena realizes that he and his pals appear to be in hot water. “A nuclear warhead went missing,” he says. “The CIA thinks it was me — or us.” Eventually, Biel comes up with a solution that is not exactly simple: “We need to re-steal the bomb so we can get our lives back.” Hargrave ( Extraction and its sequels) helmed the film from a script by David Coggeshall. Producers include David Ellison , Dana Goldberg and Don Granger for Skydance, alongside Robbie Brenner and Ynon Kreiz for Mattel Studios. Jules Daly also produces, while Patrick Newall and Elizabeth Bassin serve as executive producers. Cena can soon be seen in Coyote vs. Acme , which hits theaters next month, and will star opposite Jennifer Garner in Netflix’s forthcoming comedy One Attempt Remaining . THR

articles.title: Prime Video Unveils Teaser, Release Date for Mike Flanagan’s ‘Carrie’ Series
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All July 25, 2026 5:50pm From left: Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan Prime Video Logo text Prime Video and Mike Flanagan are giving more of a glimpse at their reimagining of Stephen King ’s classic debut novel Carrie . Ahead of the Carrie panel at San Diego Comic-Con , Prime Video debuted the official teaser trailer for the eight-episode series, which expands on King’s original story about a high school girl with telekinetic powers. The official teaser hints at “new dimensions still to come,” Prime Video described of the trailer. At the end of the panel, Flanagan announced that all eight episodes of the series will premiere on Prime Video on Oct. 7. Key art featuring a nod to the infamous bloody prom was also shared. Related Stories Movies John Cena Races to Find a Nuclear Warhead in 'Matchbox the Movie' Trailer TV 'Widow's Bay' Creator on Writing Season 2 After Buzzy Launch: "I Learned a Lot About What You Don't Need" King’s Carrie was published in 1974, spent 14 weeks on The New York Times bestseller list and has been translated into more than 35 languages. Brian De Palma’s 1976 film adaptation of Carrie , which starred Sissy Spacek and Piper Laurie, earned Academy Award nominations for Spacek and Laurie. The upcoming reimagining from Flanagan marks the first time the story has been adapted for television. Summer Howell stars as the series’ title character Carrie White and Samantha Sloyan as Margaret White. The show synopsis reads: “Misfit high‑schooler Carrie White (Howell) has spent her life hidden away inside the walls of her home with her fiercely protective mother, Margaret (Sloyan). After her father’s sudden, untimely death thrusts her into the unforgiving ecosystem of public high school, Carrie is forced to navigate a viral bullying scandal that tears through her community, the relentless pressure and casual cruelty of the social‑media age, and the awakening of mysterious telekinetic powers that rise alongside her adolescence.” Siena Agudong, Alison Thornton, Joel Oulette, Josie Tota, Arthur Conti, Thalia Dudek, Amber Midthunder and Matthew Lillard also star. In addition to being the showrunner, Flanagan also writes and exec produces the series. He also directs four episodes. King serves as executive producer on the series from Amazon MGM Studios production. THR

articles.title: Ryan Gosling to Star in Ghost Rider Movie for Marvel Studios, Director Shawn Levy
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit , Aaron Couch July 25, 2026 6:10pm Ryan Gosling, Shawn Levy and Kevin Feige at Comic-Con Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney Logo text A new Ghost Rider just rode into town. Ryan Gosling will play supernatural horror hero Johnny Blaze, aka Ghost Rider, in a new big-screen incarnation of the Marvel character that will be directed by Deadpool & Wolverine ‘s Shawn Levy. Gosling and Levy are keeping the good time going after shooting Star Wars: Starfighter , due out next year. The announcement was met with pandamonium when it was made Saturday during Marvel Studio’s Hall H presentation at San Diego Comic-Con. Related Stories Movies 'La La Land' 10th Anniversary Poster Finally Corrects Ryan Gosling's Flat Hand Movies Nicolas Winding Refn Reveals the Chaotic Making of 'Drive': "Most Everyone Hated It" The plan is for the movie to open in 2028. A return for Ghost Rider and Gosling’s involvement had been whispered for at least a year but the actor’s appearance in Hall H made it real. Ryan Gosling is GHOST RIDER. Movie coming in 2028 to be directed by Shawn Levy. Hall H losing its mind. pic.twitter.com/xQ76QUrB8y — Borys Kit (@Borys_Kit) July 26, 2026 In recent weeks, journalist Josh Horowitz teased Marvel boss Kevin Feige at the Spider-Man: Brand New Day junket, asking why Gosling wasn’t yet Ghost Rider. In a full circle moment, Horowitz participated in a comic bit during the panel, asking Feige from the crowd about Gosling. Feige responded by bringing Gosilng out. “As you know, this is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time. So, Kevin, Josh Horowitz, Hall H, thank you,” said Gosling. Levy, who helmed Marvel’s super successful Deadpool & Wolverine , was also brought on stage and said that he and Gosling had been talking about Ghost Rider while shooting Starfighter . “Gosling is the absolute shit,” he said, adding, “I say that with tremendous respect.” Levy said they riffed on set — and after a while, he “was, like, ‘Bro, let’s ride.'” Nicolas Cage starred as Blaze in two Ghost Rider movies released in 2007 and 2011 by Sony, which continues to have the film rights to Spider-Man. Gabriel Luna played Ghost Rider in TV’s Agents of SHIELD . The character of Blaze was created by writer Gary Friedrich and artist Mike Ploog and first appeared in 1972’s Marvel Spotlight No. 5. A year later, the character received his own series. Readers were captivated by Blaze, a stunt motorcycle driver who, in a deal made with the devil, is bonded with a demon named Zatharos. He becomes a flaming skull-headed, fiery motorcycle-riding spirit of vengeance. Decades later, several other characters held the mantle of Ghost Rider, Danny Ketch and Donnie Reyes among them, but Blaze has always kept the fire burning in comics fans’ hearts. This is the first superhero or comic book movie outing for Gosling, who was once up for the part of Green Lantern in the late aughts. In recent years, the actor has shown a willingness to take on big studio blockbusters or franchise plays. This year he toplined Project Hail Mary and next year stars in Star Wars: Starfighter. THR

articles.title: ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Star as T’Challa’s Son, Sequel Set for 2028
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski , Borys Kit , Aaron Couch July 25, 2026 6:45pm David Jonsson at Comic-Con Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney Logo text Black Panther 3 is ready to claw its way into theaters. Kevin Feige and director Ryan Coogler announced during Marvel Studios ‘ panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday that the sequel feature will film on 70mm and hit theaters Dec. 15, 2028. The duo also revealed that David Jonsson is set to star as an adult version of the son of T’Challa, portrayed by the late Chadwick Boseman in the 2018 original. “Thank you to this amazing family that I have the honor and privilege and the blessing to join,” Jonsson said from the stage as the audience screamed and cheered, with some sections breaking out in Wakanda chants. He will don the mantle of the Black Panther for the film. Related Stories TV Prime Video Unveils Teaser, Release Date for Mike Flanagan's 'Carrie' Series Movies John Cena Races to Find a Nuclear Warhead in 'Matchbox the Movie' Trailer David Jonsson, announced as the new BLACK PANTHER, humbly says thank you as he takes the stage. Black Panther 3 to be released Dec 15, 2028 pic.twitter.com/cPiX7Dk9Hr — Borys Kit (@Borys_Kit) July 26, 2026 The actor is a recent Hollywood breakout, with key roles in Alien: Romulus and The Long Walk . Jonsson was also part of the main cast for the first two seasons of Industry. Black Panther: Wakanda Forever ended with the revelation that Boseman’s T’Challa had a young son with Lupita Nyong’o’s Nakia. Given that this is Marvel, it’s possible that some sort of time jump or other factors are involved to age him up for the sequel. The film also will come after next year’s Avengers: Secret Wars and will likely affect the larger MCU. The Black Panther film franchise kicked off with the 2018 title, starring Boseman as T’Challa. With a cast that included Michael B. Jordan, Lupita Nyong’o, Danai Gurira, Martin Freeman, Daniel Kaluuya, Letitia Wright , Winston Duke and Angela Bassett, the film was a smash hit, collecting $1.3 billion at the global box office and becoming the first superhero feature to land an Academy Award nomination for best picture. Boseman was set to reprise his lead role in a planned sequel before his death in 2020 after a private battle with colon cancer. The follow-up film’s focus shifted to Wright’s character, Shuri, taking up the mantle of Black Panther following the death of brother T’Challa. The sequel, Wakanda Forever , hit theaters in 2022 and surpassed $850 million at the worldwide box office. It won an Oscar from five nominations, with Bassett becoming the first performer nominated for an Academy Award for a performance in a Marvel movie. Among the highlights of this year’s Marvel panel at SDCC included Ryan Gosling taking the stage to reveal his role as Ghost Rider in a forthcoming feature from Shawn Levy, his director for next year’s Star Wars: Starfighter. THR

articles.title: Warner Bros. Sues Amazon, Accusing Company of “Seeking to Pirate Away Employees”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 25, 2026 8:02pm The Warner Bros. studio lot in Burbank, California. Mario Tama/Getty Images Warner Bros. Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon for “hurriedly seeking to pirate away a number of contracted employees,” citing the recent hiring of Pia Barlow as a “better example of Amazon’s lawless employee shopping spree.” Warner Bros. alleges intentional interference with contractual relations, breach of contract, intentional interference with prospective economic advance and unfair competition against Amazon in the suit that was filed on Tuesday. In using Barlow, HBO Max’s former EVP originals marketing, as an example, the company notes that her contract was not set to expire until Oct. 31, 2027. Barlow was announced as Amazon MGM Studios ‘ new head of original series marketing on Friday, when most outlets began reporting on the suit. Related Stories Movies Sacha Baron Cohen's Secret Ali G Movie Sets Fall Release Movies Kane Parsons, Curry Barker and the Multi-Million Dollar Battle for Gen Z Eyeballs “Though it was aware of Barlow’s ongoing contractual commitment to WMS, of which WBD is a beneficiary, Amazon has brazenly and deliberately induced Barlow to breach the employment agreement by packing up and decamping to Amazon more than 16 months before its expiration,” the suit reads. Warner Bros. also alleges in the filing that “Barlow is not the first ( nor, apparently, the last ) WBD employee that Amazon has targeted or will target in the future.” The suit alleges that “a few weeks before Amazon’s interference with Barlow’s term employment contract with WMS, Amazon similarly endeavored to tortiously induce another WBD employee to breach their term employment agreement, which was not set to expire until December 2027.” “Fortunately, in that instance, Amazon ultimately was unsuccessful in its efforts to raid WBD’s workforce as to that particular executive,” the suit continues. Warner Bros. is seeking compensatory damages, punitive damages and injunctive relief. THR

articles.title: Ryan Reynolds’ Deadpool Crashes Comic-Con to Beg for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Role
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 25, 2026 8:10pm Ryan Reynolds appears as Deadpool from the crowd of Marvel's 2026 San Diego Comic-Con panel. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Logo text Ryan Reynolds gave maximum effort while angling for a role in Avengers: Doomsday during San Diego Comic-Con . As the star-studded team for the forthcoming Marvel Studios film was onstage at SDCC on Saturday, Reynolds surprised fans when he appeared among the crowd while dressed in Deadpool ‘s gray suit that has not yet appeared on the big screen but can be seen in X-Force comics. Doomsday directors Anthony Russo and Joe Russo were among those participating in the panel alongside Kevin Feige to promote the Disney film that hits theaters Dec. 18. Related Stories Movies 'Black Panther 3': David Jonsson to Star as T'Challa's Son, Sequel Set for 2028 Movies Ryan Gosling to Star in Ghost Rider Movie for Marvel Studios, Director Shawn Levy Reynolds joked that his name was Ricky and that he was “cosplaying hard.” He went on to say, “First question is for Mr. Paul Rudd . Where is Thor, and why was he crying?” This referenced a moment in 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine , during which Chris Hemsworth’s Norse God of Thunder appears to hold a dying Deadpool in a scene set in the future. Ryan Reynolds dresses up as #Deadpool during the Hall H presentation at #SDCC asking the #AvengersDoomsday cast if they need any last minute additions pic.twitter.com/YLYyHChMc7 — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) July 26, 2026 Rudd quipped, “He’s a Wrexham fan?” in a dig at the soccer team that Reynolds and friend Rob Mac own. Reynolds fired back, “You know goddamn well why he was crying.” Reynolds’ Deadpool continued, “This seems like an awfully expensive way to announce a film. When do you start filming?” This spurred Robert Downey Jr. , who stars as Doctor Doom after initially playing Iron Man in the MCU, to reply, “It’s in the can, bro. Look around you. Did you bump your head?” Ryan Reynolds appears from the crowd as Deadpool at Marvel’s San Diego Comic-Con panel. Joe Scarnici/Getty Images After a pause, a deflated Deadpool responded, “I see. So there’s no additional photography, no overages, hot costs — maybe last minute additions?” The star then said abruptly, “No further questions. Happy Hogan, fetch the Audi. We’re leaving.” Reynolds dropped the microphone and made his way out of Hall H. Although Reynolds has not been officially confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday , media rumors have persisted about a possible role for Deadpool. The opinionated anti-hero was last seen on the big screen opposite Hugh Jackman in Deadpool vs. Wolverine , which surpassed $1.3 billion at the global box office. Earlier this month, Reynolds confirmed during an appearance at Fanatics Fest that a new Deadpool film would indeed come to fruition at some point. Other highlights from this year’s Marvel panel included Ryan Gosling teasing his starring role in a Ghost Rider movie that Shawn Levy will direct. Additionally, Black Panther 3 filmmaker Ryan Coogler took the stage to announce that David Jonsson will star as T’Challa’s adult son for the movie that will hit theaters in 2028. THR

articles.title: The Doom Boom: Marvel Studios Brings ‘Doomsday’ and More to Its Most Crowded Comic-Con Panel Ever
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit , Aaron Couch July 25, 2026 9:39pm Pedro Pascal, Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans and Hayley Atwell at Comic-COn Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney Logo text After years of massive Comic-Con panels with full Avengers casts, it didn’t seem possible that Marvel Studios could go bigger. But, boy, did they. In a first for Hall H, the studio surprised the 7,000-strong crowd by revealing a hidden stage in the back of the cavernous room, with castmembers from Thunderbolts* and the 2000s X-Men movies appearing. After giving brief speeches, the actors made their way from the back, through the entire hall, high-fiving fans along the way and the crowd screaming like it was a Beatles or BTS concert. They joined the main stage already populated by Pedro Pascal, Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell, and the star attraction, Robert Downey Jr. Related Stories Movies Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool Crashes Comic-Con to Beg for 'Avengers: Doomsday' Role Movies 'Black Panther 3': David Jonsson to Star as T'Challa's Son, Sequel Set for 2028 It was just one part of supersized panel, that included the startling revelations that Alien: Romulus breakout David Jonsson would play the son of T’Challa (the late Chadwick Boseman) in Black Panther 3 for a Dec. 15, 2028 release. He will take the mantle of the Black Panther. Another bombshell: not only would Ryan Gosling play Ghost Rider in a new movie, but Deadpool & Wolverine and Gosling’s Star Wars: Starfighter director Shawn Levy would direct for a 2028 release. Even Ryan Reynolds , who had not attended Apple TV’s presentation of his upcoming action comedy Mayday earlier in the day, crashed the proceedings — in costume as a cosplayer named Ricky, but really as Deadpool. He pointedly asked if production had begun. (Apparently he wasn’t invited.) Downey was having none of it, jokingly seeming annoyed with the Merc with the Mouth. “It’s in the can, bro. Look around you. Did you bump your head?” Downey told Deadpool, who then asked about possible additional photography to add new people to the mix. The crowd “awwed” in sadness. Marvel’s Hall H: A cosplayer named Ricky…really Ryan Reynolds as Deadpool…asks if #Doomsday has already started production and if it’s possible the movie will still add new people. Robert Downey Jr pointedly tells him, “It’s in the can, bro. Look around you.” pic.twitter.com/tdlJ1LCwuF — Borys Kit (@Borys_Kit) July 26, 2026 On some level, there had been pressure all week for Marvel to pull out all the stops for its Comic-Con presentation. On Monday, it released the trailer for Doomsday , and while it racked up record views showing a lot of interest, reaction was not enthusiastic . And with a checkered slate since 2019’s mega-event Avengers: Endgame, the company needed to show that Doomsday isn’t a grasp at past glories. And while not indicative of future quality, Saturday’s panel demolished any negativity from days prior. In addition to the big news drops and the sheer force of actors, it was a massive spectacle with light shows and pop music. And, oh yes, costumes. Each attendee received a Doom mask and cape that they donned when asked by Downey, who in his Doom accent, asked the assembled legion to join his cause. Marvel, with this panel, continued to up the ante. The crowd was continually on its feet; every time it would sit down, some reveal would jolt them back up, to see, to yell, to record on their phones. Marvel in Hall H: Doctor Doom masks handed out to 7000 fans. Atmosphere is electric. pic.twitter.com/nhdcqIBY1g — Borys Kit (@Borys_Kit) July 26, 2026 And in a bit of a redo, Marvel showed a Hall H-only reel that it called an extended look but was, to many fans, what the initial trailer should have been: something that clearly delineated the stakes and the threat. “Victor, did you do this?!” yells Pascal’s Richards to Doom. Doom says, “All of you have lived stolen lives” at one point and raises an army of giant mutant-killing robots known as Sentinels out of the ground. He tosses Thor aside like a doll. And begins with Susan Storm (aka The Invisible Woman) explaining Doom’s motivation, saying “Everything he loved was taken from him.” Ahead of the panel, the feeling in the room was electric. Hundreds, if not thousands, of people camped overnight for a chance at Comic-Con’s hottest ticket. Marvel gave away Doctor Doom masks and capes, while the Fantastic Four robot H.E.R.B.I.E. was onstage. And it began with a sizzle reel of Marvel’s greatest hits — not just of Marvel Studios, but of films made before Iron Man kicked off the MCU in 2008. There was footage of Tobey Maguire’s Spider-Man and Patrick Stewart’s Prof. X. Feige, with the help of Jon Bernthal , also showed an action sequence from Spider-Man: Brand New Day , which opens next week and for which little has been shown. Marvel boss Kevin Feige, a confident and loose speaker, began his talk by giving due to the source of all things at Marvel Studios, the comics. He referred to the change in leadership at the publishing division, thanking outgoing editor-in-chief C.B. Cebulski for his work and giving a shout out for the new chief, Stephen Wacker. “Without the comics, no MCU, no movies, no TV shows, no animation,” Feige said. “Nothing.” THR

articles.title: Fantasia International Film Festival Awards: Hanna Bergholm’s ‘Nightborn’ Wins Top Honor
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 4:32pm PT Fantasia International Film Festival Awards: Hanna Bergholm’s ‘Nightborn’ Wins Top Honor By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Fantasia International Film Festival Awards: Hanna Bergholm’s ‘Nightborn’ Wins Top Honor 11 hours ago ‘Sour Minnows’ Is the Surreal Body Snatching Comedy That Mystified and Delighted Its Premiere Audience — Fantasia 13 hours ago ‘The Dink’ Writer Sean Clements on His Funny, Heartfelt Tribute to the Pickleball Community: ‘I Got Adopted by This Whole Crew of Older Women’ 2 days ago See All Pietari Peltola Hanna Bergholm’s “ Nightborn ” has won the top honor at this year’s Fantasia International Film Festival juried awards. “Nightborn” was awarded the prestigious Cheval Noir trophy for best film. Seidi Haarla, who stars opposite Rupert Grint in the film, was also awarded best actress. Kasper Kalle’s “No Rest for the Wicked” also took home two statues for best director and best actor for Pilou Asbæk. Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub Andrea Corsini’s “Ferine” also took home two top honors: best cinematography for Fabrizio La Palombara and best score for the legendary Pino Donaggio. Popular on Variety See the full winners list — along with jury statements — below. 2026 Cheval Noir Awards Best Film Nightborn (Finland/Lithuania/France/U.K.), dir. Hanna Bergholm “‘It sucks my body, it destroys my career.’ When the anticipated birth and the child who should be loved become the most threatening presence to a mother, she fails to accept the child into her world. To her, the child is not a ‘him,’ but an ‘it.’ This psychological thriller explores the destruction of a woman’s daily life- where everything around her could be reality, or merely an illusion. Ultimately, when she gives up everything and steps into the ‘child’s’ world, we finally discover the “most adorable” child in the world. The suspense keeps you glued to the screen every single second, and the emotion in the ending is bittersweet — making you smile yet feel profoundly sad. This film will stay with us for a long time.” Best Director Kasper Kalle, No Rest for the Wicked (Denmark/Faroe Islands/Iceland) “Like the captain of a sailing vessel, the director is the creative force that unites the crew, bringing all the creative elements and storytelling emotion together on the screen, and one film did that big time for both audiences and the jury. For his skillful helming of a beautifully dark period piece that reveals the discovery and acceptance of identity through a love story, the jury awards Best Director to Kasper Kalle.” Best Screenplay Edwin, Eka Kurniawan, and Daishi Matsunaga, Sleep No More (Japan/Germany/Singapore/Indonesia), dir. Edwin “For a genuinely original storytelling vision that draws Asian folklore, humor, and workers rights, and extreme body horror into a story of family reunification, the jury awards the Best Screenplay Award to Edwin, Eka Kurniawan, Daishi Matsunaga.” Best Cinematography Fabrizio La Palombara, CCS, Ferine (Italy), dir. Andrea Corsini “For its technical and artistic skill, a carefully measured use of the anamorphic format, varied lighting and precise camera composition that wonderfully reflects the narrative and the amazing brutalist Production Design and radical swing character arcs that throttle the audience. For its look that pays homage to the greats of Italian horror while adding its own stamp to a modern genre film while constantly reinventing itself visually, the jury presents the Cheval Noir for Best Cinematography to Fabrizio La Palombara, CCS.” Best Editing Soichi Ueno, Beasts Clutching at Straws (Japan), dir. Hideo Jojo “We are honored to be the first Fantasia jury to present the new award for best film editing. My former boss and co-editor Orson Welles once said that editing is the last stop on the long road between the dream in the filmmaker’s head, and the public to whom that dream is addressed. The editor focuses that dream into reality. For its dynamic pacing, masterful control of non-linear construction, and clever use of imaginative transitions, while never losing track of the characters and story, the jury presents the award for outstanding editing to Soichi Ueno.” Best Score Pino Donaggio, Ferine (Italy), dir. Andrea Corsini “Music has the power to soothe, shock and enchant the viewer as it accompanies the characters through the narrative. For the jury, the dramatic music of one colorful, ravenous film stood out, and it marks the return of a revered screen composer- one who might be familiar to fans of classic films like Don’t Look Now and Carrie. The musical artistry of this 84 year-old legend can be heard in two Fantasia films this year, and the jury is thrilled to present the award for outstanding score to Pino Donaggio.” Outstanding Performance Award Seidi Haarla, Nightborn (Finland/Lithuania/France/U.K.), dir. Hanna Bergholm “Genre film is built on risk-taking performances, and this year the jury was completely captivated by a transcendent portrayal of a very different kind of determined mother. With dark humor, astonishing physicality, and heart-wrenching body horror, this actor brings to life a woman struggling beneath the weight of her family’s expectations (and her own) as she unravels and transforms before our eyes.” Outstanding Performance Award Pilou Asbæk, No Rest for the Wicked (Denmark/Faroe Islands/Iceland), dir. Kasper Kalle “Genre cinema has always been drawn to mysterious strangers, but few arrivals have felt as quietly transformative as this one. Through effortless magnetism, and extraordinary emotional precision, this actor crafts a character who belongs as much to the sea as the shore. Every movement, every silence, every knot tied and glance exchanged reveals a soul shaped by freedom, isolation, and the courage to embrace his own identity.” Special Mention of the Jury: Full Ensemble Hot Spot (Sweden/Greece/Norway/Poland), dir. Agnieszka Smoczyńska “The jury wishes to recognize the achievement of an ensemble cast of individual performers and the monsters are pretty cool too. The story and world building of this film is conveyed by the core characters- a family that communicates without speaking and with intense physicality that transforms them all- and by the supporting performances of the extras- such as a group of religious refugees who move and breathe together in unison. For its exceptionally nuanced collective performance, the jury awards a Special Mention to the ensemble cast of Hot Spot.” Special Mention of the Jury: Special Practical Effects Jabrik Hellworker, Benedictus A.K., Rizal, and Issei Oda, Sleep No More (Japan/Germany/Singapore/Indonesia), dir. Edwin “One film impressed the jury with its handmade practical effects and the VFX they engage with — an angry and ravenous hair monster, a character that grows back missing limbs — all beautifully integrated into the surreal nightmare of the story. For its amazingly original use of practical effects, a Cheval Noir Special Mention goes to Sleep No More.” Jury President: Youngjoo Suh (founder and CEO of Finecut Co., Ltd. and producer). Jury: Catherine Corcoran (actor, writer, producer, and festival programmer), Karim Hussain (cinematographer, director, and screenwriter), Bob Murawski (Oscar-winning film editor and co-founder of Grindhouse Releasing), and Junnie Punter (journalist with Variety , Toronto Film Critics Association, producer, and editor at Musicworks Magazine ). 2026 New Flesh Competition for Best First Feature New Flesh Award for Best First Feature Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant (New Zealand), dirs. THUNDERLIPS “This debut feature was a wild ride from start to finish, with zany design complementing its shock, horror, and humor. The filmmakers have conceived a world that is both funny and extreme, navigating themes of bodily autonomy for both males and females through the playful and the monstrous. This year’s New Flesh competition winner — and best alien penis of the festival — goes to Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant.” Special Mention of the Jury: Best Performance Dilnaz Kurmangali and Ayan Utepburgen, Sicko (Kazakhstan), dir. Aitore Zholdaskali “We are delighted to present an honorable mention for best performance to these two leads. This male and female duo navigated the film’s tonal shifts between horror and comedy with ease. Balancing each other’s intensity to create a memorable dynamic, their performances made an impact, bringing humanity and dimension to unlikable characters just trying to survive in a gritty, complex world. The honorable mention for best performance goes to Dilnaz Kurmangali and Ayan Utepburgen from Sicko.” Jury President: Brandon Hill (Senior Director of Acquisitions and Co-Productions, Lionsgate). Jury: Jasper Basch (partner and head of distribution of Greenwich Entertainment, former head of theatrical at IFC, and former head of distribution at Variance), Julien Fonfrède (director, producer, screenwriter, critic, and festival programmer at Festival du nouveau cinema), Markus Keuschnigg (film critic, writer, and co-founder and artistic director of Slash Filmfestival Vienna), and Hillary Webber (production manager for Film Tampa Bay and industry programmer at Gasparilla International Film Festival). 2026 International Short Film Competition Best Film Mancave (Norway), dir. Jean-Paul Guigue and Dimitri Planchon “We were struck by how this film transforms social anxiety, people-pleasing, and painfully uncomfortable silences into something hilarious. Its flat, collage-like, strangely realistic world perfectly reflects these awkward characters who are constantly trying to fit into everyone else’s expectations. What impressed us most is that beneath the comedy is a film full of empathy, reminding us that we’re all a little awkward sometimes and through that humor, it reminds us that finding the confidence to be ourselves and sometimes simply saying no isn’t always easy. The Award for Best Feature goes to Dimitri Planchon and Jean-Paul Guigue for Blaise.” Special Mention of the Jury Cherry and Virgin (Japan), dir. Masanao Kawajiri “The honorable mention goes to a film whose characters felt so authentic, with emotions that are honest, messy, and relatable. It’s a story with so much heart, and one where the animation technique and storytelling couldn’t be a better fit. Bringing two completely different visual styles together is no small feat, and this film makes it look effortless, it’s playful, seamless and a joy to watch. It beautifully captures what it feels like to navigate insecurity, vulnerability, and human connection. The honorary mention goes to Masanao Kawajiri for Cherry and Virgin.” Satoshi Kon Award for Best Short Film — Gold Jeem 1983 (Lebanon), dir. Jorj Abou Mhaya “A life in the arts can be a struggle. But it’s nothing compared to a life living among war. Using art to escape into a reality that imagines beauty where there is none is one of the most powerful statements art can make. A glimpse into a world of Arabic animation that rarely gets to the west in festivals like Fantasia, and hopefully more submissions will be encouraged by this. A young boy travels through 1983 Beirut suspending the horrors and using fantasy for a momentary reprieve. Did we mention Goldorak shows up? The Gold Satoshi Kon Award for Excellence in Animation goes to Jori Abou Mhaya’s Jeem 1983.” Satoshi Kon Award for Best Short Film — Silver Fingerbang (South Korea), dir. Kim Yeon-woo “Plenty of films can be surreal, but this one makes you believe in the relationship. Through the most unusual premise, it explores how obsession and longing can distort love, reminding us that the things we desire most can ultimately consume us. The Silver Satoshi Kon Award for Excellence in Animation goes to Kim Yeonwoo’s Fingerbang.” Satoshi Kon Award for Best Short Film — Bronze The End of the End (U.S./South Korea), dir. Junar Kim “Executed with an astounding atmosphere through low-key lighting, theatrical staging this film transforms the contemplation of death into a breathtaking work of art. The animation perfectly complements its contemplative pace, drawing us deeper into its haunting world. The Bronze Satoshi Kon Award for Excellence in Animation goes to Junar Kim for The End of the End.” Jury President: Sylvie Trouvé (co-founder and creative director, See Creature Animation). For its comprehensive examination of zombie culture and its reflection on the Haitian diaspora, this award goes to Maya Annik Bedward’s Black Zombie.” Special Mention of the Jury Insectasy (Canada), dir. This feature manages to simultaneously be a post-COVID cautionary tale about bug addiction and a celebration of kink. articles.title: Stephen King’s ‘Carrie’ Series Sets October Release Date, Drops Horrifying New Trailer
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 5:50pm PT Stephen King’s ‘Carrie’ Series Sets October Release Date, Drops Horrifying New Trailer By Tanya Fedak Plus Icon Tanya Fedak Latest Winston Duke Trusts David Jonsson to Take On ‘Black Panther’: ‘I Think It’s Going to Be Great’ 7 hours ago Stephen King’s ‘Carrie’ Series Sets October Release Date, Drops Horrifying New Trailer 10 hours ago Guillermo del Toro Says There Is ‘Absolutely No Goddamn AI’ in ‘Pan’s Labyrinth’ 3D Re-Release: ‘We’re Protecting a Lineage of Art’ 1 day ago See All Amazon Prime Video has released a new teaser trailer for “ Carrie ,” the TV adaptation of Stephen King’s classic horror novel. All eight episodes of the series will debut on Oct. 7. The series is a “bold and timely reimagining of the story of misfit high-schooler Carrie White, who has spent her life in seclusion with her domineering mother,” the logline teases. “After her father’s sudden and untimely death, Carrie finds herself contending with the alien landscape of public high school, a bullying scandal that shatters her community, and the emergence of mysterious telekinetic powers.” Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub Summer H. Howell will play Carrie White, with Siena Agudong as Sue Snell and Matthew Lillard as Principle Grayle. Also starring in the series are Samantha Sloyan as Margaret White, Alison Thornton as Chris Hargensen, Thalia Dudek as Emaline, Amber Midthunder as Miss Desjardin, Josie Totah as Tina, Arthur Conti as Billy and Joel Oulette as Tommy. Mike Flanagan serves as the writer, executive producer, showrunner and director, with Trevor Macy executive producing and Amazon MGM Studios producing. This is far from Howell’s first horror project, as she’s previously appeared in “Curse of Chucky,” “Cult of Chucky,” “Hunter Hunter,” “Spirit in the Blood,” “Time Cut,” “Harland Manor” and “Channel Zero.” Sloyan and Flanagan have been long-time collaborators, with Sloyan previously starring in Flanagan’s “The Haunting of Hill House,” “The Fall of the House of Usher,” “The Midnight Club,” “Midnight Mass” and “Hush.” “Carrie” will consist of eight episodes and was first reported to be in development in Oct. 2024. The series was officially greenlit by Amazon in April 2025. King’s novel was first adapted into an Oscar-nominated hit film in 1976, followed by a poorly received sequel in 1999, a television film in 2002 and a remake in 2013. articles.title: Ryan Gosling to Star in Marvel’s Ghost Rider Movie
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 6:07pm PT Ryan Gosling to Star in Marvel’s Ghost Rider Movie By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond 6 hours ago ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set 9 hours ago ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer Rocks Comic-Con: Doctor Doom Raises Army of Sentinels to Take Down Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men 9 hours ago See All Getty Images Ryan Gosling is finally joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The “Project Hail Mary” star will play Ghost Rider in a new standalone movie, Marvel Studios exec Kevin Feige announced onstage from Hall H at San Diego Comic Con. The film will be directed by Shawn Levy and is slated to release in 2028. Levy is no stranger to the world of Marvel, most recently directing and producing the blockbuster “Deadpool & Wolverine” film. He and Gosling also recently collaborated on the upcoming “Star Wars: Starfighter,” which Levy also directed and in which Gosling stars. That film is due to release on May 28, 2027. Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub “I’m having the greatest flashback vibes here, because I was here two years ago when we showed ‘Deadpool & Wolverine,'” Levy said upon taking the Hall H stage alongside Gosling and Feige. “I’ll never forget that night, because I was introduced to the greatest fans. Gosling is the absolute shit. I say that with tremendous respect. We spent a lot of time last year making ‘Starfighter,’ and the opportunity as Ryan started talking about this character, I was like, ‘Bro, let’s ride.’ We’ll see you in 2028!” Popular on Variety Gosling will be the second actor to play the Spirit of Vengeance in a film after Nicolas Cage played the fiery motorcycle rider in two Sony movies. The character was also portrayed by Gabriel Luna as the Robbie Reyes version of the comic book character in the Marvel-ABC series “Agents of SHIELD.” Luna was set to reprise the role in a standalone series for Hulu, but that project was scrapped in 2019 . Cage first starred in Sony’s “Ghost Rider” movie in 2007, playing motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze. In the comics and his origin story movie, Johnny sells his soul to the devil Mephisto in order to cure his father’s cancer. As with any deal with the devil, Mephisto does cure Johnny’s dad, but he still dies in a stunt accident. Johnny then becomes bonded to a supernatural demon called the Spirit of Vengeance and is able to transform into a flaming, skeletal biker. He also has super-strength, wields fiery chain whips and can force someone to experience the emotional pain they’ve inflicted upon others with his Penance Stare. Cage reprised his role for the 2011 sequel, “Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance,” but reviews for both films were mostly negative. The rights to Ghost Rider reverted to Marvel Studios, which reinvented the character for the ABC TV show “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.” Gabriel Luna played the Robby Reyes version of the character, who’s a younger, Latino man who takes on the Ghost Rider mantle. Gosling is having a major year after starring in “Project Hail Mary,” and he’ll join the Star Wars universe in next year’s “Starfighter” spinoff. articles.title: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Director and Star Lana Condor on Finally Showing Their Film to the Fans at Comic-Con: ‘The Fight Was For a Good Reason’
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 6:34pm PT ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Director and Star Lana Condor on Finally Showing Their Film to the Fans at Comic-Con: ‘The Fight Was For a Good Reason’ By Matt Minton , Angelique Jackson If you went back to November 2023 and told “Coyote vs. Acme” director Dave Green that his Looney Toons legal comedy would make its debut at San Diego Comic-Con , he probably wouldn’t believe it. Of course, that’s largely because that’s when Green learned the film had been shelved by Warner Bros. Discovery as a tax write off. “For three years, I was lucky enough to make a movie about Wile E. Coyote, the most persistent, passionate, and resilient character of all time,” Green posted on X at the time after receiving the “devastating” news. “But in the spirit of Wile E. Coyote, resilience and persistence win the day.” Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub And win the day they did. Ketchup Entertainment ultimately rescued the film and set it for theatrical release on Aug. 28. “Coyote vs. Acme” — an animated/live-action hybrid about Wile E. Coyote taking on the Acme Corporation for intentionally releasing defective products — will get its first public screening on Saturday night at Comic-Con. “I’ve waited so long to see their reaction. I feel like the years, to me, have [all led] up to tonight,” said Lana Condor, who stars in the film alongside Will Forte, John Cena and a bunch of Looney Tunes like Roadrunner, Tweety and Bugs Bunny. “I want so badly for them to love it, and I think they will. I’m so confident in that.” The most enduring image of the campaign to save “Coyote vs. Acme” was a lone protester dressed as Wile E. Coyote, holding a picket sign that read “Release Me” outside Warner Bros. Studios in the pouring rain. “We did a call to action, ‘Where are you? Reveal yourselves, we would love to invite you!'” Condor said. But Green confirmed the lone wolf never stepped forward. Still, the anonymous whistleblower’s legacy lives on as the “Coyote vs. Acme” team built one of his masks for last year’s Comic-Con panel. “We figured out how his costume was built, and it was made out of paper!” Green said excitedly. “Coyote vs. Acme” is heading to theaters while Warner Bros. is enduring yet another change of direction — this time, the impending merger with Paramount Skydance, which has many people in the industry on edge. But while the wider implications of the Warner-Paramount merger remain to be seen (especially after the merger’s delay ), for tonight, the entire “Coyote vs. Acme” cast and crew have much to celebrate. “So many people stood up for a film they didn’t even see … which is exactly Wile’s entire journey throughout our entire film!” Condor said. “The reason that it’s going to come out at all, I firmly believe, is because of the fans. That was really incredible to experience. That’s why tonight, we’re so excited to screen it for the first time because this is what you fought for. I’m so confident that the fight was for a good reason.” The film’s script was penned by “May December” scribe Samy Burch from a story by James Gunn and Jeremy Slater. It is based on a 1990 New Yorker article by Ian Frazier. articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer Rocks Comic-Con: Doctor Doom Raises Army of Sentinels to Take Down Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 6:37pm PT ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer Rocks Comic-Con: Doctor Doom Raises Army of Sentinels to Take Down Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond 6 hours ago ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set 9 hours ago ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer Rocks Comic-Con: Doctor Doom Raises Army of Sentinels to Take Down Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men 9 hours ago See All Screenshot: Youtube / Marvel Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige surprised San Diego Comic Con attendees with exclusive footage of “ Avengers: Doomsday ,” shown only to lucky fans inside of the convention center’s massive Hall H. The trailer starts out with Victor Von Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) sitting on a throne as Vanessa Kirby’s Sue Storm (a.k.a. the Invisible Woman) explains how he’s broken as a person. “Victor was always the smartest guy in the room. He used to be different,” she narrates somberly. It’s clear that she and the rest of the Fantastic Four — particularly Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards — already know Doom and have a complicated past with him. “Everything he loved was taken from him,” she explains. Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub The trailer is interspersed with quick shots of the sprawling cast, including Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Captain America (Chris Evans), Black Panther (Letitia Wright), Shang-Chi (Simu Liu), Loki (Tom Hiddleston), Cyclops (James Marsden), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Gambit (Channing Tatum) and more. There’s a shot of a destroyed New York City that’s reduced to rubble, and Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards asks if Victor is responsible for the carnage. Popular on Variety We hear Doom say, “All of you have lived stolen lives.” Thor confronts Doom but the villain catches his magical hammer and throws it aside easily. Doom uses his magic powers to throw Thor aside and raises an army of Sentinel robots — the iconic androids from the “X-Men” movies — from the ground. MCU fans will have to wait until Dec. 18 to see “Avengers: Doomsday” for themselves, but it’s expected to be a massive team up between the Avengers, Fantastic Four, Thunderbolts and even more of Marvel’s stars. The countdown to “Doomsday” began last December as Marvel released four teaser trailers to start hyping up fans for the tentpole film. They featured the return of Chris Evans as Captain America, who now has a child, Chris Hemsworth’s Thor and his daughter Love, the Fantastic Four meeting Black Panther and the Wakandans and the official MCU debut of Fox’s past X-Men team. The “Doomsday” cast is headlined by Downey Jr. as the villainous Doctor Doom, plus “Avengers” stars like Evans, Hemsworth, Paul Rudd, Sebastian Stan, Anthony Mackie and Simu Liu. The “Fantastic Four” and “Thunderbolts” teams, comprised of Pascal, Kirby, Joseph Quinn, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Florence Pugh, David Harbour, Wyatt Russell, Hannah John-Kamen and Lewis Pullman, are also teaming up with the original stars. Fox’s “X-Men” cast members are also crossing over into the MCU for “Doomsday.” The returning stars include Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Kelsey Grammer, Alan Cumming, Rebecca Romijn and Channing Tatum. articles.title: ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 6:41pm PT ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set By Selena Kuznikov , Jordan Moreau , Ethan Shanfeld Black Panther is back! David Jonsson has been cast as the new Black Panther and is playing T’Challa’s son in “Black Panther 3,” out Dec. 15, 2028. The film will follow Jonsson’s character, Prince T’Challa II, as he comes of age after he was introduced as a child in “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.” Director Ryan Coogler will return for the third film, as well as Leticia Wright reprising her role as Shuri and Winston Duke as M’Baku. The news was announced at Marvel’s Comic-Con Hall H panel. Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub Wright took over as Black Panther from her late co-star Chadwick Boseman in “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever,” with Shuri becoming the eponymous superhero. Boseman, who portrayed T’Challa in the first “Black Panther,” died of colon cancer at age 43 in 2020, when Coogler was working on the sequel. The character T’Challa II was introduced as T’Challa and Nakia’s (Lupita Nyong’o) son in “Wakanda Forever.” Popular on Variety Jonsson recently starred in “Alien Romulus” and the adaptation of Stephen King’s “The Long Walk.” Wright told Variety in January 2023 after the release of “Wakanda Forever” that she thought the third film in the franchise was “already in the works.” “You know, we just had a terrific two years of bringing it out and everybody coming together to support it,” Wright said in the interview. “We need a little bit of a break, we need to regroup and Ryan needs to get back into the lab, so it’s going to take a little while, but we’re really excited for you guys to see that.” The first “Black Panther” movie, released in 2018, took in $1.3 billion at the worldwide box office, and starred Boseman, Wright, Lupita Nyong’o, Forrest Whitaker, Michael B. Jordan, Danai Gurira and Angela Bassett. It earned seven Oscar nominations, including best picture, the first superhero movie to do so. The film won three Oscars, including best costume design, best production design and best original score. “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” grossed $859 million worldwide when it was released in 2022, and had one of the most profitable opening weekends post-pandemic, earning $331 million worldwide. The film was nominated for five Oscars, with Angela Bassett’s nomination for best supporting actress marking the first time any actor in a Marvel film was nominated for an Academy Award. Marvel fans won’t have to wait long to see Wright back in action as Black Panther, as she’s part of the sprawling “Avengers: Doomsday” cast. Marvel teased the third “Black Panther” at San Diego Comic-Con , which releases Dec. 15, 2028. Jonsson will play T’Challa’s son, Prince T’Challa II, continuing the late Chadwick Boseman’s legacy. “I trust him as an artist. I also trust the people who chose him,” Winston told Variety about Jonsson joining the franchise. “I trust Ryan [Coogler]. I trust the entire MCU executive team. I think it’s going to be great.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub “Black Panther” was Duke’s first film, and he said he hopes to create a similarly welcoming experience for Jonsson. “How I was greeted and received into this world – which was with a lot of grace, being told it’s a safe space to work, to play — that’s what I wanted to extend to him,” he said. “I don’t have any advice. I know what I have to do with him, which is to play with him. I have to trust him. I have to give him the same grace that was extended to me.” Ryan Coogler will return to direct the film following “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever,” with Leticia Wright reprising her role as Shuri. Winston will also appear as M’Baku in the highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday,” which premieres Dec. 18. The film’s trailer has been viewed 503 million times since being released on Monday. “What I know is that we have their attention,” Winston said when asked about fans’ interest in the future of the MCU. “I think we have their attention because of so much trust that they have for the MCU. We’ve created and delivered so many movies over the years, and it’s never about any one director. It’s about the cohort.” The first “Black Panther” film released in 2018 and earned $1.3 billion at the worldwide box office, also receiving seven Oscar nominations and three wins. articles.title: Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond
articles.full_text: Jul 25, 2026 9:28pm PT Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond 6 hours ago ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set 9 hours ago ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer Rocks Comic-Con: Doctor Doom Raises Army of Sentinels to Take Down Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men 9 hours ago See All Getty Diehard Marvel fans packed into San Diego Comic Con’s massive Hall H Saturday night, some even camping out for more than 30 hours. But as the 40-minute panel wrapped up with just two surprise announcements — a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling and “Black Panther 3” — it’s hard not to feel like, “Is that it?” After a 30-minute delay, the panel got underway with Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige acknowledging writer and producer Stephen Wacker’s new role as Marvel Comics editor-in-chief. He then rolled out a trailer for the “Avengers: Endgame” re-release, dubbed “Endgame Encore,” which will have an exclusive sneak peek at “Doomsday.” But fans were hungry for new announcements, not a re-edited trailer for a movie they’ve likely seen multiple times (and no doubt will see again). Related Stories Chris Brown Pleads Guilty Over ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub Gosling and director Shawn Levy re-teaming for a Ghost Rider movie was a surprise, albeit one that the actor has been attracted to for years. The announcement capped off an extended bit with “Happy Sad Confused” host Josh Horowitz, who recalled all the times he’s asked Gosling about the long-rumored movie in interviews . Unless fans have been glued to every MCU rumor, Gosling’s introduction from Horowitz didn’t track well on stage. After Marvel’s “Blade” movie never fully materialized, it’s hard not to take an “I’ll believe it when I see it” stance on the “Ghost Rider” — despite the fact that “Deadpool and Wolverine” director Shawn Levy is already locked in. Popular on Variety The other awkward moment from Marvel’s panel came during an confusing Deadpool cameo. As the sprawling “Doomsday” cast joined the stage, a very recognizable voice called out from the sea of fans. Deadpool, clad in his gray X-Force costume, appeared in the crowd — but never removed his mask to show who was underneath. It certainly sounded like Ryan Reynolds begging for a role in the movie, but it wasn’t clear if Reynolds himself was in the suit. Joe and Anthony Russo joked that production had wrapped on “Doomsday” but then…that was it. While it’s been highly speculated that Deadpool may cameo in both “Doomsday” and 2027’s “Secret Wars,” Feige skipped the opportunity to confirm Reynolds’ return to the MCU. Instead, Feige and the Russos moved straight into showing an exclusive trailer for “Doomsday,” which featured more backstory for Downey’s villain, but also some recycled footage from the last teaser. We learn more about Doom’s complicated history with the Fantastic Four and his seemingly tortured past, but much of the plot is still shrouded. The most exciting moment came when Doom resurrected a fleet of giant Sentinel robots — robotic villains from the “X-Men” universe — to battle the heroes. The panel ended with another long-rumored announcement, Ryan Coogler’s “Black Panther 3,” but with a major surprise: “Alien: Romulus” actor David Jonsson is taking over the title role. He’ll play T’Challa II, the son of the late Chadwick Boseman’s hero, in what will no doubt be another emotional film for Coogler and the Wakanda crew. Jonsson is an exciting young actor on the rise and was excellent in last year’s adaptation of Stephen King’s “The Long Walk.” It will be impossible to fill Boseman’s shoes, but Jonsson stands to be one of the major pieces in the next era of Marvel. So far, “Ghost Rider” and “Black Panther 3,” both slated for 2028, are the only movies in Marvel’s next phase after “Doomsday” and “Secret Wars.” Fans have long expected — and Feige has stated that — the X-Men to help steer the MCU’s future, but there wasn’t a single X-announcement on stage Saturday. Several of Fox’s “X-Men” stars are returning for “Doomsday,” but there was no indication if they’ll be back for “Secret Wars” or beyond. Rumors about the next cast of X-Men have swirled online, but at the panel, all the focus was on “Doomsday” — not whatever may come next. Maybe expectations were set too high. Last time Marvel attended Comic Con was in 2024, when the studio made the bombshell reveal that Robert Downey Jr ., the actor who carried the MCU on his back for over a decade, would return as its next major villain: Doctor Doom. That announcement nearly blew the roof off of Hall H, but nothing matched that intensity this year. Seeing the crowd of fans dressed in Doom costumes was fun for a few seconds, but watching everyone crowd together for a selfie — and not getting more information on “Doomsday” — was not. Luckily, Disney has its D23 event in just three weeks, where more news will surely come. However, Comic-Con has usually been a film-centric event, where D23 has more TV shows. Everyone expects “Doomsday” to be a much-needed hit for the MCU later this year, but can it ascend to the two billion-dollar heights of “Endgame”? And how will it fare against Warner Bros.’ “Dune: Part 3,” which is hitting theaters the same day on Dec. 18? As the “Dunesday” showdown approaches, Marvel needs every bit of hype it can get to pave the way for its future, and Comic-Con could’ve used a few more major announcements to cement it as a must-see cultural event. articles.title: Seth Rogen & Jonah Hill Interrupted By YouTuber While Filming In Venice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Tom Holland Admits Some Of His Movies Were Hard To Promote “Because It’s Sh*t” ‘Carrie’ Schools Comic-Con With Prime Video Release Date, Trailer Depicts “Cruelty” Of Modern High School, Mike Flanagan Teases “Big Surprise” ‘Widow’s Bay’ Creator Reveals Which Major Character Wasn’t In Original Script: “Burn Every Copy” — Comic-Con View All July 25, 2026 3:47pm Jonah Hill and Seth Rogen attend the Vanity Fair Oscar Party on Feb. 26, 2012 in West Hollywood, California. Kevin Mazur/VF12/WireImage Seth Rogen and Jonah Hill are working together again, according to a viral clip of a YouTuber crashing their Venice Beach set. In a video posted Friday by Yung Mooch, the vlogger ran up to Rogen and Hill while they were sitting on scooters, filming a scene from an upcoming project. “No! We’re working,” Rogen can be heard telling Mooch in the video as he walks up to introduce himself, fist-bumping Hill. Watch on Deadline Mooch then tries at ask Rogen the same question as a friend takes a selfie with Hill. “I would say, don’t fuck with people while they’re trying to make their show. That’s probably not a good idea,” Rogen tells him. Still not reading the situation, Mooch continues to press Rogen for advice. “Be yourself,” Rogen reluctantly told him. “Look at this, y’all,” said Mooch into the camera, finally walking away. “We just caught a mid-movie production. This is Los Angeles right here.” While Rogen has recently been filming Season 2 of Apple TV’s The Studio , and his Apple series Platonic was renewed for Season 3 in December, it’s unclear what he was filming with Hill. Deadline has reached out to Apple. After first starring together in 2005’s The 40-Year-Old Virgin , the pair has appeared in Knocked Up (2007), Superbad (2007) and This Is The End (2013). The last project they both appeared in was Sony’s 2016 animated adult comedy Sausage Party . articles.title: ‘Carrie’ Schools Comic-Con With Prime Video Release Date, Trailer Depicts “Cruelty” Of Modern High School, Mike Flanagan Teases “Big Surprise”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson , Glenn Garner July 25, 2026 7:44pm Nothing is scarier than trying to fit in at high school. During a Saturday panel at Comic-Con , Prime Video revealed an Oct. 7 release date for Carrie and the first teaser trailer that showcased all the hair-raising trauma that is in store: from classmates fainting on the iconic gymnasium floor to revealing Carrie White’s prom queen moment before her harrowing, blood-curdling scream amidst a raging fire. Aiming to be more relevant to today’s culture than ever, Mike Flanagan ‘s Carrie , based on Stephen King’s debut novel of the same name, will be an “honest” and “heartfelt” unearthing of mental health woes that teens go through, such as active shooter drills and the way simple mistakes live on forever on social media. Related Stories ‘Carrie’ First-Look Images Tease Mike Flanagan’s Prime Video Series News Mike Flanagan On Why He Broke His “No Sequels” Or Remakes Rule For ‘Carrie’ Series “Here’s the thing,” said Flanagan. “Carrie was written half a century ago. Carrie was adapted spectacularly by Brian De Palma. It is iconic. It is untouchable. There is no reason whatsoever to try to follow in those footsteps and to try to walk on that path. However, the world has changed quite a lot.” Watch on Deadline Written by King in 1974, De Palma adapted the book into the iconic 1976 horror film starring Sissy Spacek as the titular telekinetic teen. Following the 1999 sequel The Rage: Carrie 2 and the 2002 made-for-TV adaptation, Chloë Grace Moretz played Carrie along with Julianne Moore as her mother Margaret in the 2013 Kimberly Peirce-helmed Sony adaptation. Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan in ‘Carrie’ Marking the book’s first TV series adaptation, Flanagan explained how he updated the series in the 50 years since King created it. Explaining that he invited several high schoolers into the writers room to talk about their real-life traumas that helped shape Carrie’s narrative, Flanagan said: “They shared shocking one-off situations or constant treatment and microaggressions and things that are not necessarily present themselves as targeted harassment. [We will dive into] the cruelty in today’s world and how the internet has encouraged cruelty, rewards and celebrates and amplifies it. This is awful for adults to deal with, and for teenagers even more so.” The eight-episode series follows Carrie White ( Summer Howell ), a misfit high-schooler who has spent her life hidden away inside the walls of her home with her fiercely protective and overtly religious mother Margaret (Samantha Sloyan). After her father’s sudden, untimely death thrusts her into the unforgiving ecosystem of public high school, Carrie is forced to navigate a viral bullying scandal that tears through her community, the relentless pressure and casual cruelty of the social media age, and the awakening of mysterious telekinetic powers that rise alongside her adolescence. Howell, who was chosen from more than a thousand auditions to play Carrie, explained, “It’s funny because it feels like Carrie, my Carrie, goes into this very open and excited for the world, and she wants to make friends and go to school and meet people. She’s never experienced people besides her mom and her dad. “But it felt like this backwards journey because for me, I’ve gone to public school my whole life. I’m done with high school now, but I experienced it all. So it was just this switch of going back to, how would I have reacted if I were Carrie?” Alison Thornton, who plays mean girl Chris Hargensen, noted, “It was so important for us to trust each other from the beginning because the show is very dark and set had to be a safe space. And that’s a credit to everyone here and Mike.” Though it is based on the novel, the cast warned that there were “many surprises in store.” Meanwhile, Flanagan added: “It’s a thrilling way to adapt something. That is how we were approaching Carrie . That’s what got Stephen King very excited about this adaptation. I think a lot of people think they know what the show is. And the biggest thing I’m excited about today is just knowing what a big surprise our Carrie is going to be. It certainly was to me.” After Deadline exclusively announced Flanagan’s Carrie in October 2024, he found his titular telekinetic teen in Howell, rounding out the cast with Samantha Sloyan as Margaret White, Matthew Lillard as Principal Grayle, Alison Thornton as Chris Hargensen, Thalia Dudek as Emaline, Siena Agudong as Sue Snell, Amber Midthunder as Miss Desjardin, Josie Totah as Tina, Arthur Conti as Billy and Joel Oulette as Tommy. Other additions include Heather Graham, Kate Siegel, Michael Trucco, Katee Sackhoff, Rahul Kohli, Crystal Balint and Danielle Klaudt. Production wrapped last October. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Carrie’ Schools Comic-Con With Prime Video Release Date, Trailer Depicts “Cruelty” Of Modern High School, Mike Flanagan Teases “Big Surprise” ‘Widow’s Bay’ Creator Reveals Which Major Character Wasn’t In Original Script: “Burn Every Copy” — Comic-Con Seth Rogen & Jonah Hill Interrupted By YouTuber While Filming In Venice View All July 25, 2026 8:59pm Tom Holland attends 'The Odyssey' world premiere on July 6, 2026 in London, England. Zak Hussein/PMC While Tom Holland is proud of his two summer blockbusters, he wouldn’t recommend certain pieces of his past filmography. The actor, whose movies The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day are in theaters this summer, recently admitted that while those press tours have been “really easy,” some of his past films were “shit” and not as easy to promote. “I’m absolutely loving it,” he said on the Dish Podcast . “When you’re doing press for movies you’re really proud of, it’s really easy. Because when they ask you questions about why should people go and watch this movie, you’re not lying to anyone. You really think people should go see it.” Related Stories News Tom Holland Shares Fred Astaire Biopic Update, Wants To Film Dance Scenes As Oners: “How He Would Have Done It” News ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Final Trailer Shows Tom Holland Swinging With Zendaya & Closer Look At Mark Ruffalo’s Hulk Holland continued, “I’ve had experiences before when people say, ‘Why should you see this movie?’ And in the back of your mind, you’re like, ‘You shouldn’t, because it’s shit.'” Watch on Deadline With The Odyssey crossing the $300M global mark in its first week, Holland has also been promoting his fourth MCU solo outing in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , premiering July 31 in theaters. “It’s felt really like a bit of a victory lap to be honest,” added Holland. “I’ve really enjoyed it. I’m super proud of both of the films.” An adaptation of one of the first stories in human history, The Odyssey follows Odysseus (Matt Damon) through the incredible trials and mythical encounters he faces on his decade-long journey home to wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Holland) after the Trojan War. In Spider-Man: Brand New Day , Holland reprises his role as the titular web-slinger alter ego of Peter Parker, four years after Dr. Strange’s (Benedict Cumberbatch) spell that made the world forget him. Now anonymously protecting New York City as Spider-Man, while his powers go through a strange and dangerous evolution.
