articles.title: Kalshi Accuses Netflix of Defamation Over Trailer for Prediction Markets Documentary
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All July 24, 2026 3:47pm Scott Olson/Getty Images Logo text Netflix has been threatened with legal action by Kalshi , which accuses the streaming giant of defamation over a trailer for an upcoming documentary that showed traders making wagers in a state it’s not allowed to operate. In a cease-and-desist, Kalshi demanded Netflix to immediately take down the trailer for Instadocs: The Prediction Market Games and issue a public retraction. It said that the video falsely suggests that users traded sports events contracts on Kalshi in Nevada in violation of a court order. In the trailer, a brief scene shows several people gathered at a house in Nevada discussing prediction markets during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. One participant holds up what appears to be a Kalshi transaction receipt and says, “I like betting on Kalshi” before claiming he placed a $5,000 wager on Spain to win the tournament. Related Stories Movies '72 Hours' Review: Kevin Hart Throws Himself Into the Slapstick but Netflix's Intergenerational Farce Squanders Its Premise TV Apple Gets Into the Dating Game: New Series Sends Unlikely Couples to World's Most Remote Locations The prediction market operator is currently barred from offering event-based contracts that would allow Nevada residents to place bets on sports under a court order issued as part of ongoing litigation with state regulators. The letter argued that Netflix falsely portrays the company of violating the injunction by implying that the trade in the trailer occurred in July 2026. “These false statements jeopardize Kalshi’s legal standing in litigation that is highly material to Kalshi’s business,” stated the letter, which noted that the company is concerned that the trailer could expose it to court sanctions or other penalties. Kalshi pointed to several details that it says reveal the receipt shown in the trailer isn’t authentic. Among them: The image displayed on the phone is dated May 16, 2025, more than a year before the events depicted in the trailer occurred. It also noted that the phone screen shows the word “crop,” indicating the user was viewing a saved image rather than interacting with the live Kalshi application. Leading up to the legal threat, Kalshi alerted a Netflix employee responsible for editing the trailer about the alleged inaccuracies. According to the letter, the employee acknowledged not realizing the receipt was dated from the previous year or that it appeared to be a cropped screenshot rather than a live transaction. Kalshi said the employee agreed the receipt would not appear in the finished documentary but refused to remove it from the trailer despite being warned that it could create legal complications in the Nevada litigation. Those concerns quickly materialized, with a CNN reporter subsequently contacting the company seeking clarification about where and when the featured trades occurred, Kalshi said. The company argued Netflix’s refusal to remove the trailer after learning of the alleged inaccuracies is evidence of actual malice under defamation law. In a statement, Netflix said none of the footage in the documentary was fabricated. “The footage was filmed at the Winible World Cup Watch Weekend in Las Vegas on July 17, 2026,” a spokesperson added. “The featured trader with the trade on Spain showed us a screenshot of his bet, that was made in May 2025 prior to any Nevada court order. Any specific trades or bets referenced during that weekend are between the individual and the app in which they placed the trades.” THR

articles.title: Malia Baker on Returning to ‘Descendants’ and Her Dream Roles
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Naomi Jeffries Plus Icon Naomi Jeffries Intern View All July 24, 2026 4:45pm Malia Baker stars in the latest ‘Descendants’ film. Cibelle Levi As Descendants enters a new chapter, so does Malia Baker . The 19-year-old Botswana-born actress returns as Chloe Charming in Descendants: Wicked Wonderland , stepping back into the Disney franchise, not as the newcomer who once idolized the original cast, but as one of the faces leading its next generation. “It’s like entering this world as camp counselors this time instead of these nervous campers that we were the first time around,” Baker tells The Hollywood Reporter on a recent Zoom. Related Stories TV 'Descendants: Wicked Wonderland' Stars Malia Baker, Kylie Cantrall Talk Heroes vs. Villains, Favorite Songs and Hopes for a Sixth Film Business Disney Cutting Hundreds More Jobs in New Round of Corporate Streamlining “We put so much pressure on ourselves just because we loved the movies so much. They were so integral, not just for my formative years, but my peers as well,” she continues. “You hold so much respect and love for them, so it was a really big deal. But it was still so much fun to film.” Returning for a second film also meant welcoming a new group of cast mates, who quickly turned into some of Baker’s closest friendships. She’s excited for the “world to fall in love” with her friends and the new characters. Malia Baker. Cibelle Levi Ahead of the film’s release, the Descendants and Zombies casts embarked on a tour, giving Baker the chance to witness fan excitement firsthand. “It’s so wild to be able to literally watch it unfold in front of you and have people be so excited and joyful around something that’s so close to your heart,” she says. The Descendants films are among the most beloved Disney movies in modern time. Baker feels that the films strike a necessary chord of timeless themes and represent young people well, which is why they’ve been able to remain relevant. For Baker, stepping into the character of Chloe meant embracing the legacy of Cinderella and Prince Charming, two of Disney’s most recognizable characters. While audiences were already familiar with Chloe’s parents, the young actress had the opportunity to help define a new character entirely her own. “I think we all put our hearts and souls into it,” she says. “Yes, these are iconic characters, but Chloe Charming has never been done before, which is a lot of trust to put into a person.” Malia Baker and Brandy in ‘Descendants: Wicked Wonderland.’ Disney/David Astorga With Disney’s trust in Baker to represent the beloved character over the course of two films, she says she’s found herself growing alongside Chloe. “As things in your life start changing, you can find different levels and depths to whatever character you’re playing,” she says. “I think Chloe and I have been very fortunate to have been at very similar stages in our lives. It feels like we really are learning these lessons at the same time and inspired by one another’s growth.” The actress hopes that Wicked Wonderland viewers watch it and enjoy it. “It can seem like it’s your responsibility to not enjoy something, because it’s not as ‘serious,’” she says. “But I think there’s something really magical in being able to learn a great lesson while having fun.” While Chloe Charming may be the role she’s most known for today, sitting at the top of her acting bucket list is Starfire from Teen Titans . “I love the role of Starfire, I think she’s the coolest ever she is just such a baddie in her own right,” she says, laughing. “I would swap out the blue for some pink hair any time any place.” The actress says a role in a biopic would also be a dream for her. “I don’t know who, what or when, I keep joking with Brandy about playing her,” she says. “I told her I’ll start practicing for it.” Malia Baker. Cibelle Levi While Starfire, and maybe a Brandy biopic if she ever gives that call, remain on Baker’s manifestation board, she’s still wrapping her head around the fact that she’s become one of the faces of Disney’s newest generation with Descendants . “Sassy little me would’ve been shocked, flabbergasted, everything in between. It’s still a dream now,” Baker says of her younger self. “I have to have little reminders every now and then. I don’t think it’ll ever fully sink in, and honestly, I’m happy it won’t.” THR

articles.title: Ralph W. Hemecker, Veteran TV Director of ‘Blue Bloods,’ ‘Once Upon a Time’ and More, Dies at 65
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All July 24, 2026 5:08pm Ralph W. Hemecker Courtesy Hemecker Family Veteran TV director, writer, producer and showrunner Ralph W. Hemecker has died. He was 65. Hemecker, whose work spanned three decades and included directing 31 episodes of Blue Bloods and 28 episodes of Once Upon a Time , died July 10 at his home in Glendale. He also directed episodes of The X-Files, Millennium, Ghost Whisperer, Numb3rs, The Vampire Diaries, Nikita, V, Legends of Tomorrow, Quantico, Body of Proof, The Flash and Pacific Blue as well as the 2000 TNT TV movie Witchblade , going on to serve as showrunner, writer and executive producer of the Witchblade TV series across its two-season run from 2001 to 2002. Related Stories Movies Chuck Russell, Director of 'A Nightmare on Elm Street 3' and 'The Mask,' Dies at 74 Movies Chris Affleck, Mother of Oscar Winners Ben and Casey Affleck, Dies at 83 And he directed the pilot for Roar , starring a then little-known Heath Ledger, as well as the pilots for Lawless and Dead at 21 . Born on June 12, 1961, Ralph William Hemecker graduated from Bucknell University where he studied English, made short films and developed a passion for visual storytelling. He went on to take filmmaking courses at New York University and began his career in production and post-production. Some of his earliest directing work was on America’s Most Wanted , helming dramatic reenactments of real-life crimes, and he directed episodes of Silk Stalkings , on which he worked behind the scenes, as well as Renegade . “Some losses are impossible to put into words,” Once Upon a Time actress Lana Parrilla wrote in part on Instagram . “Ralph Hemecker was one of the kindest, most generous souls I’ve ever known. One of Once Upon a Time ’s defining directors. A truly passionate, beautiful man and my dear friend. I was lucky enough to shadow Ralph as a director as he knew Once , behind the camera, best. He was always carrying a camera in hand, staying up all night in the director’s office putting his shots together, studying the scripts and endlessly visiting sets in preparation. His passion was infectious. We always knew if Ralph was directing, we were in good hands.” Hemecker is survived by his two stepdaughters as well as his father, sister and brother; two nephews; one niece and one great-nephew. Hemecker admired the Navy SEALs’ courage, discipline, resilience and commitment to service, and he was inspired by their leadership principles. As a result, in lieu of flowers, his family asks that memorial donations be made to the SEAL Future Foundation in Hemecker’s memory. A celebration of Hemecker’s life will be announced at a later date. THR

articles.title: Hollywood Royalty, Michelin-Starred Meal, Cartier Gift Bags: Inside Monaco’s Most Exclusive Event of the Year
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Erin Lassner Plus Icon Erin Lassner E-Commerce Writer View All July 24, 2026 5:45pm Courtesy of The Red Cross If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. The Monaco Grand Prix , the Rose Ball and the Red Cross Gala: the Monégasque social calendar’s trifecta of prestige. Serving as the pinnacle of black tie elegance, Monaco ‘s Red Cross Gala — or the Gala de la Croix-Rouge Monégasque, in French — is the yearly flagship fundraiser for the Monaco Red Cross, which, from 1958 to 1982, was presided over by none other than Grace Kelly , Princess of Monaco. Cut to the evening of July 18, 2026: Even without the Oscar-winning movie star’s physical presence, the Old Hollywood glamour at the 77th annual charity ball was palpable. Related Stories TV Zale Parry, Pioneering Scuba Diver and 'Sea Hunt' Actress, Dies at 93 Movies 'Clueless,' 'The Karate Kid,' 'Glory,' 'The Big Chill,' 'High Society,' 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' Enter the National Film Registry Prince Rainier and Princess Grace of Monaco (aka Grace Kelly) arrive at Sporting Monte-Carlo for the annual Red Cross Gala on July 19, 1958 . Courtesy of AFP via Getty Images Prince Albert II and Princess Charlene of Monaco arrive at Sporting Monte-Carlo for the annual Red Cross Gala on July 18, 2026. Courtesy of The Red Cross On Saturday night at the Sporting Monte-Carlo, esteemed guests eagerly awaited the arrival of Prince Albert II and Princess Charlene, son and daughter-in-law of Grace Kelly and respective President and Vice-President of the Red Cross Society’s Monaco branch. Charlene, Princess of Monaco, statuesque as ever, channeled the timeless style of her late mother-in-law in a custom-made Elie Saab golden draped gown. The couple was joined by niece Camille Gottlieb, one of Kelly’s 11 grandchildren, plus the evening’s hosting duo, actress and model Estelle Lefébure and actor and comedian Michel Boujenah. Following arrivals, guests glided through a sea of white tablecloths to dine on a multi-course meal imagined by three-Michelin-starred chef Marcel Ravin. And while only one lucky winner walked away with the gala’s grand prize, a Cartier Grain de Café jewelry set fit with 58 total diamonds, every guest in attendance went home with a generous parting gift from the luxury House, a supple leather cardholder stamped with the Double C emblem. The gala’s grand prize, a Cartier Grain de Café jewelry set, gifted by the luxury House. Courtesy of The Red Cross On the heels of an otherworldly fireworks show and ahead of the jazz-inspired after party, guests enjoyed the world premiere of SOUL! Where Legends Come Back . This dance-inducing live show, which traces the journey of African-American music, is the newest original production by Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer (SBM), the luxury hospitality and entertainment company that doubles as the annual gala’s organizer and venue host. In many ways, SBM feels like — and, quite honestly, is — the brain behind much of Monaco’s social, cultural and hotel scene, with the sovereign city-state sitting at under one square mile. SBM’s crown jewel has to be the Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo , a palatial escape located at Place du Casino in Monte Carlo, smack dab in the heart of Monaco. Widely regarded as one of the world’s most luxurious properties, Hôtel de Paris is every bit as breathtakingly lavish as you’d hope and expect. It, therefore, only makes sense that a conveyor belt of black cars promptly escorted guests from their accommodations and pre-event drinks to the main festivities at the Sporting Monte-Carlo. So what’s next on the Principality of Monaco’s social calendar? Well, you’ll have to consult Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer’s extensive annual agenda . But for now, a few more highlights from the 77th annual Monaco Red Cross Gala. Camille Gottlieb arrives at 77th annual Monaco Red Cross Gala on July 18, 2026. Courtesy of The Red Cross Princess Charlene and Prince Albert II dance alongside guests at 77th annual Monaco Red Cross Gala on July 18, 2026. Courtesy of The Red Cross Returning to Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo with the Cartier gift bag. Courtesy of Erin Lassner THR

articles.title: The Whole ‘Live PD’ Gang Is Back Together as Tom Morris Jr. Joins ‘On Patrol: Live’

Tom Morris Jr. , the former co-host and analyst on A&E’s Live PD , is set to reunite with Dan Abrams and Sgt. Sean “Sticks” Larkin on Reelz ‘s On Patrol: Live . Abrams is a legit media mogul at this point, and Larkin is a retired Tulsa Police Department lieutenant with more than 25 years of service. The rest of the On Patrol: Live on-air team includes analysts Captain Tom Rizzo (ret.) of the Howell Township Police Department in New Jersey and Deputy Sheriff Curtis Wilson of the Richland County Sheriff’s Department in Columbia, South Carolina. The show also has a rotating panel of other experts as needed. (They may be less needed now.) Related Stories Business Dan Abrams Has the Scars to Prove It Business A+E Networks Settles 'Live PD' Copyright Suit as Part of Amazon Deal “Reuniting with Dan and Sticks is so special for me! We have always been more to each other than just professional colleagues,” Morris Jr. said in a statement. “We are truly friends for life and have remained in close contact over the years. I’m looking forward to kicking it on set with Curtis and Rizzo too. Onward and upward, OP Nation!” “I am thrilled to be working with Tom again, not just for his law enforcement insight but because he brings humor and humanity to his analysis,” Abrams said. “It’s great to have the team back together.” On Patrol: Live follows live news-gathering protocols with 50-plus cameras in communities across the country, documenting for viewers in real time the nightly work of law enforcement officers on patrol. The show airs every Friday and Saturday night from 9 p.m. to 12 a.m. ET on Reelz. Morris Jr. is a former audio technician, camera operator and field producer who became an antiterrorism contractor for the U.S. State Department. Yes, that old story. In addition to Live PD , Morris Jr.’s other television work includes A&E’s Wanted and Fugitives Caught on Tape , as well as appearances on CNN, Discovery ID and Oxygen. Morris Jr. is a Washington, D.C., Special Police Officer with loads of private security work under his belt. THR

articles.title: Rick Moranis Makes Comic-Con Debut for ‘Spaceballs’ Sequel
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All July 24, 2026 6:48pm 'Spaceballs: The New One' panel at Comic-Con 2026. Chris Frawley / Amazon MGM Studios Logo text Laughs and an appreciation of Rick Moranis were plentiful as Amazon MGM’s Spaceballs : The New One , a sequel to the 1987 Mel Brooks Star Wars parody, flew into San Diego Comic-Con ’s cavernous Hall H Friday afternoon. One of the panel’s biggest attractions was seeing Moranis, the comedian who appeared in seminal 1980s films such as Ghostbusters and Honey, I Shrunk the Kid , make his first ever appearance. The actor played villain Dark Helmet in the original 1987 movie but has been largely absent from movies and television for most of this century, so his return with the Spaceballs sequel is headline making. Related Stories TV 'Lanterns' Trailer Reveals Sinestro and Its Manhunter Threat as Aaron Pierre Wins Over Comic-Con TV 'Rick and Morty' Spinoff 'President Curtis' Scores Early Season 2 Renewal at Adult Swim After a “comb the audience” joke, a callback to a line in the original movie that revealed the comedian to be in the audience wearing an oversized Darth Vader-style helmer, Moranis hopped up the stage to a standing ovation and chants of “Rick! Rick! Rick!” “You made our childhoods better,” said Kevin Smith, who ably moderated the panel. Moranis sat between Josh Gad , one of the creative forces behind the sequel, and Daphne Zuniga, who played Princess Vespa in the original and returns for the sequel. Also on stage were director Josh Greenbaum, actors Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman, and writers Dan Hernandez and Benji Samit. Gad described the origins of the sequel, recounting how he had been working on a Honey I Shrunk the Kids sequel with Moranis that ultimately fell apart, but did end up watching Moranis movies with his daughter. “We finished it and she goes, ‘Can we watch part 2?’” he said. “And I said, ‘There is no part 2.’ And she said, ‘Yeah, the weird little alien guy said there was going to be a part 2.’” When he replied, “Oh sweetie, that is called a joke,” she countered, “Well, why isn’t there a part 2?” That night, Gad said, he had a dream about the sequel and soon after was pitching Brooks and his producing partner. He threw in ideas refencing new Star Wars movies and characters such as The Force Awakens and Kylo Ren. Imitating Brooks, Gad summed up his reaction: “Josh, it sounds like you’ve really got your finger on the pulse. I don’t know half of what you’re talking about, but I really like it.” The comedic presence of Brooks, who appeared only by a recorded video early on in the panel where he thanked the nerds for keeping his movie alive close to 40 years, loomed large over Hall H. Amazon MGM bucked the Comic-Con trend by not having a trailer debut or showing any clips from the movie, but it did show videos of Brooks reuniting with Moranis, reuniting with original star Bill Pullman and Zuniga, and recording lines in a booth while praising — or not — the script. Greenbaum recounted meeting the comedy legend early on in the movie’s development, and when it was approaching time to being principal photography, he asked if the man had any words of advice. Brooks paused, and said yes. Greenbaum was thrilled. He leaned in. “Don’t say ‘Cut!’ first. It’s ‘Action!,’ and then ‘Cut!’” Brooks told him. The young director’s takeaway? “It was, don’t take this too seriously and go out there and have fun,” Greenbaum summed up. The new movie, Gad said, takes a look at the state of movies and nostalgia. “The industry it was parodying is a very different industry than this one 40 years later,” said Gad. “We all sort of talked thematically about this word ‘nostalgia.’ And we love movies that look back. We love sequels. We love continuing these stories we grew up with. We analyzed why that is and we thought Spaceballs was the perfect vehicle to catch us up with everything that’s happened in filmdom and in fan filmdom. Interjected Smith, “When they made the first one, there was a trilogy to make fun of. Now there’s a never-ending fount.” “We really wanted to dive into that,” Gad replied. The panel also featured a funny bit where Lewis Pullman read out a letter purportedly written by his father, Bill Pullman, about how great it was to be part of a family, while ignoring his own father-son relationship. And it also showed, on multiple screens, the purported plans of a Spaceballs cinematic universe, sketched out in decade-spanning movie “phases,” a shot at how Marvel Studios has unveiled timeline of its various movie plans. THR

articles.title: Morgan Stewart on Wave of Home Burglaries in L.A.: “Everyone I Know Has Gotten Robbed”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All July 24, 2026 6:52pm Morgan Stewart attends the CFDA Awards at New York's American Museum of Natural History on Nov. 3, 2025. (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images) Morgan Stewart has revealed more about the harsh reality of being burglarized twice at her Beverly Hills home. The reality TV veteran, fashion influencer and podcast host joined Jake Shane on the newest episode of his show, Therapuss , and opened up about experiencing firsthand a crime wave that has impacted such celebrities as Brad Pitt, Lionel Richie, Goldie Hawn and Kurt Russell, Nicole Kidman and Keith Urban, Tracee Ellis Ross, Rachel Zoe, Kathy Hilton, Sutton Stracke and more. “Bought it in France, brought it home, stolen out of my house two days later,” Stewart told Shane of a rare Hermes Birkin purse that was taken. “I was camping with my kids for their school camping trip, and we got a call from security. We had security [and he had fallen asleep] in front of the house. I’ve just now gotten past [him falling asleep], and they smashed through my office door and they went into our bedroom and ransacked my husband’s watches.” Related Stories Business Kalshi Accuses Netflix of Defamation Over Trailer for Prediction Markets Documentary Movies '72 Hours' Review: Kevin Hart Throws Himself Into the Slapstick but Netflix's Intergenerational Farce Squanders Its Premise Stewart then commented on the rash of burglaries and said “this is happening a lot in the area, unfortunately, it’s happening all the time,” so much so she claimed that “everyone I know has gotten robbed.” The robbers took armfuls of her rare purses but left a glass case full of bags untouched. “They didn’t touch because I think they probably would have thought there was an alarm or something attached to it.” “I was just furious. I was angry. I’m pissed. It’s a violation,” she said of the emotions she experienced after the fact. “I saw the video of them climbing over my gate in the middle of the day. And they had six bags on each arm, and they tossed them over the gate onto the driveway. I’m like, ‘You are so disrespectful. Hop politely because you’ve just scratched the Box Kelly I just got.’ It was literally just like trash on the floor.” Stewart also revealed that she experienced a second burglary at her home. “My security caught them on the hillside,” she said. “That was when they took all my jewelry. But we got it back, thank God.” She now says her home is guarded like “Fort Knox.” The Therapuss episode is available on Netflix and Spotify , and finds Stewart also dishing about style trends for summer, what life was like on Rich Kids of Beverly Hills and more. articles.title: President Trump Roasts Media at Rescheduled, Pared-Down White House Correspondents’ Dinner
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 24, 2026 7:25pm U.S. President Donald Trump and CBS News senior White House correspondent and WHCA President Weijia Jiang salute during the 2026 White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) Dinner at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, DC, on July 24, 2026. Photo by Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images President Trump appeared at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner, which took place in Washington, D.C. on Friday with a new location and a drastically reduced list of attendees, following the cancellation of the event in April after a gunman fired shots as the event was underway. Moved to the Waldorf Astoria in the nation’s capital instead of the Washington Hilton and reduced from 2,600 guests down to around 680, it was less a star-studded event that each year sees celebrity guests brush elbows with reporters and editors as they sit with the politicians they cover — the optics of which are criticized each year by journalists and critics alike. Related Stories General News Donald Trump Booed at World Cup Final General News Donald Trump Drops Part of His $10 Billion Defamation Lawsuit Against the BBC For the make-up dinner, the WHCA is also bringing back the Secret Service member who survived the April shooting, when 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen , who allegedly intended to target multiple Trump administration officials, was arrested near the screening area outside the banquet hall after running past the security checkpoint. Plus, the dinner honored the Washington Hilton staff who stayed on the scene and continued tending to rattled guests. Elements of the first dinner remained. The awards were handed out; mentalist Oz Pearlman, who got just one private trick for the White House press secretary at the first dinner before gunshots caused chaos, returned to deliver some levity; and ahead of the event, a group of hundreds of former journalists and press freedom groups sent a letter to the WHCA. Now, they were urging the association to capitalize on Trump’s attendance by calling him out for his administration’s attacks on First Amendment rights, which include recently subpoenaing New York Times reporters over their coverage and threatening to revoke licenses of broadcasters. The president took to the stage around 9:30 p.m. ET and brought up the attempted attack early in his much-anticipated speech, which has been speculated upon heavily in April and again ahead of the July event. Traditionally, the dinner’s speeches are a roast of the attendees and the president himself. “The attempted mass murder at the Washington Hilton-that’s what it could have been-was an assault on our democracy itself,” Trump said. “A very serious situation. Many of you were there with me, and some showed extreme bravery, like Pete Hegseth, Steve Miller, Tom Holman. Really, they were standing on tables. And most of you were under the table,” he said to Friday night’s attendees, which got some laughs. Following some begrudging admiration of the press and the constitutional freedom of speech, the notion of a third Trump term, the White House ballroom project, and Robert Kennedy Jr. mowing down the cow served at dinner with his car were some of Trump’s early jokes. They garnered a new laugh, but his first zinger to fall completely flat came soon and involved a rapper and MAGA convert whom he recently had at a White House event. “After hearing the gunshots, many people yelled, ‘Get down! Get down!’ which caused Nicki Minaj to start twerking,” he said, referring to the dance. “Do you believe it? Get down. She’s the only one that really understood what that meant.” Trump’s speech began to meander as he at first reminisced about the Waldorf Astoria in the 1980s and moved to a number of topics and name-dropped celebrities not in the room and with whom he has personal gripes, some going back for decades. Rosie O’Donnell, Bette Midler and Bruce Springsteen all got a mention, with the latter’s looks as he ages compared to the president’s own. Trump joked that his live show, where he was railing about the administration’s policies, was now called “Bored in the U.S.A.” Attendees were caught on camera in footage streamed live by the Associated Press looking bored and irritated as Trump’s speech went past the 20-minute mark, and it was clear this was not going to be the biting speech some anticipated Trump’s typical airing, but another airing of grievance from Trump peppered with a few jokes that landed with a thud. Even the president was critical of some of the jokes when they received no laughs. At one point, he referred to the “governor of Chicago,” presumably billionaire Gov. of Illinois, J.B. Pritzker, while discussing a staged fight among politicians. “I would say I could mention the governor of Chicago, but I’m going to mention instead Jerry Nadler, and they’re fighting for a big piece of cheesecake, big fat piece of cheesecake,” he said to zero audible laughs. “Who the hell wrote that line?” During the airing of grievances portion of his speech on a night celebrating journalists, Trump, as expected, tore into reporters for perceived unfair treatment, and specifically mentioned CNN anchors Kaitlan Collins (an award recipient honored earlier in the night) and Jake Tapper (a multiple winner of the multiple recipient of the White House Correspondents’ Association Merriman Smith Award). Following mentions of late-night hosts Jimmy Kimmel and Stephen Colbert, whom he called talentless, Trump also admitted that he truly hates some people. “They thought about going with a professional clown for entertainment, but Adam ‘Shifty’ Schiff was not available,” Trump joked. “You know he’s known — I hate some people. You know, I shouldn’t say the surprise. I’m not supposed to hate him. I’m supposed to love everybody, but he’s a terrible person. He’s a liar, and I called him watermelon head because he has the largest head I’ve ever seen with the smallest neck, pencil neck. How does that big fat ugly head stand on a on a little pencil, pencil, pencil neck?” After about an hour of a speech that turned nasty fast and featured few funny lines, Trump ended the speech on an up note and even praised the journalists in the room and their profession. “We have the hottest country anywhere in the world, and we’re going to keep it going,” he said. “And I just want to say, this is a room I have tremendous respect for the people in this room. Sometimes I don’t feel you treat me fair. Maybe you do. I don’t know. I don’t feel that. But sometimes you treat me very fairly, and I have a lot of respect for your profession. Your profession is amazing. And I just want to thank you for having me. And it’s been fun.” THR

articles.title: ‘Widow’s Bay’ Creator on Writing Season 2 After Buzzy Launch: “I Learned a Lot About What You Don’t Need”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 24, 2026 7:30pm Matthew Rhys on 'Widow's Bay.' Courtesy of Everett Collection Logo text The writing process has just begun for the second season of Apple TV ‘s latest hit series Widow’s Bay . Show creator Katie Dippold participated in Collider’ s Showrunners on Showrunning panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, where she opened up about the project’s startling success . Starring Matthew Rhys as the mayor of a New England island that the residents are convinced is haunted, Widow’s Bay quickly became one of television’s buzziest shows after its April launch and went on to land a whopping 19 Emmy Award nominations , including best comedy series. Related Stories Movies Rick Moranis Makes Comic-Con Debut for 'Spaceballs' Sequel TV 'Lanterns' Trailer Reveals Sinestro and Its Manhunter Threat as Aaron Pierre Wins Over Comic-Con “It took a long time,” Dippold said about how soon she got a sense that the show had picked up as many fans as it did. She joked that she remains “terrified” of Reddit but eventually took enough of a look on the social media platform to see that the amount of discussion about Widow’s Bay was increasing wildly. “Seeing that was really shocking.” The writer, also known for her work on such features as The Heat and Snatched , explained that she did not know that the series had been renewed for a second season until just before the news went public. “But I was still always hoping and thinking about it,” she continued, pointing out that the writers room for season two started earlier this week. “It’s a great room, and then we’re going to be writing for the next 20 weeks.” Dippold noted that her goal is to begin filming next year for the show that also stars Kate O’Flynn, Kevin Carroll, Dale Dickey, Kingston Rumi Southwick and Stephen Root. As for lessons from the initial season that the first-time showrunner plans to incorporate for the second one, Dippold said, “I learned pretty quickly in making it.” Dippold pointed out that she felt that the comedy worked because the actors played things straight and dramatic: “Throughout the process, it was making sure everything served that, and so that’s top of mind going into season two. Also, the scripts were longer and pretty dense. I had to make last-minute cuts for time, so I’ll just be more mindful of that because we didn’t need that much.” She added, “In the edit, I just could see, ‘Oh, you actually didn’t need any of this stuff anyway.’ I learned a lot about what you don’t need and getting to things quicker.” In her review of Widow’s Bay for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Angie Han wrote, “At its best, Widow’s Bay highlights the blurry line between comedy and horror.” THR

articles.title: Noah Wyle on ‘The Pitt’ Fan Discourse, Saving Hollywood and What’s Coming In Season 3
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 1:30pm PT Noah Wyle on ‘The Pitt’ Fan Discourse, Saving Hollywood and What’s Coming In Season 3 Awards Circuit Podcast: Also on this episode, the Roundtable dives into the TV Academy's controversial move of five categories out of the Emmy telecast By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest ‘Blue Bloods,’ ‘Once Upon a Time’ TV Director Ralph W. Hemecker Dies at 65 11 hours ago ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Co-Creator Bill Prady Explains the Science Behind the Show’s Multiverse 1 day ago Shaking Up the Emmys By Moving Five Categories Out of the Telecast Might Not Work, But at Least the TV Academy Is Trying Something 1 day ago See All Chantal Anderson for Variety Noah Wyle knows some “ The Pitt ” fans came down hard on his character, Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch, given how the character’s personal struggles caused him to lash out at some of his colleagues in Season 2. But he tries not to pay attention to the online discourse. “The blending of the line between actor and part that I sometimes see, where an actor is blamed for the behavior of a character, or where a character’s dialog stops being representative of the character and starts being representative of the creative team — as if they’re saying something that they believe through this particular vehicle — I think gotten a little blurry as viewers have sort of conflated character message and character,” he tells Variety ‘s Awards Circuit Podcast . “It doesn’t necessarily have an encoded message because somebody’s saying it. Other than the dramatic tension within that one scene, it’s not necessarily trying to be representative of anything larger.” Related Stories Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial States Sue to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, Defying DOJ Wyle says he believes it’s still just a small but very vocal portion of the viewership that is piling on — but he prefers not to be engaged with the more negative conversations that might be out there. “My skin is is too thin to really engage anything that might be coming at me, so I tend to want to say live and let live, and I’ll go do my job, and you can take what you want from me.” Popular on Variety Wyle does say that his son would sometimes warn him when the backlash against Dr. Robby got very heated online: “My son is the one who calls me and goes, ‘Dad, they’re really mad at you.’ He’s my firewall. He’ll go, ‘Dad, you might not want to go to the market today unless you start treating Dr. Mohan better!” Wyle understands that the vitriol that came at Dr. Robby this year “was disappointment that he was acting less heroic than he presented himself last year. But when we’re at our most desperate, we’re not always our most graceful. And we were trying to show somebody who was going through a mental health crisis and was behaving irresponsibly, unprofessionally and out of character for himself as he was asking people to see him in his moment of plight and potentially stop him from doing himself harm. That did get misinterpreted by some people as him just being misogynistic or cruel. I think there was a much bigger picture at play.” On this edition of the Variety Awards Circuit Podcast, “The Pitt” star, executive producer and director Noah Wyle — Emmy-nominated three times this year — discusses the wild fan reaction to Season 2 and Dr. Robby’s storyline, as well as how “The Pitt” is showing how to keep production jobs in Los Angeles. But first, the Roundtable looks at the TV Academy’s decision to move five categories out of the Emmy telecast and the debate over whether this will make a difference in producing a more entertaining ceremony. Listen below! Wyle has been a big advocate of bringing production back to Los Angeles, and “The Pitt” — shot locally here on the Warner Bros. lot — has put him front and center in the conversation. “I’m looking at it from the standpoint of somebody who has grown up in and around this industry and befriended people who are generations deep in this industry who’ve watched it really crater over the last couple years,” he says. “There is still an abundance of talent here, and ‘The Pitt’ is is proof of what you could do with that talent when you when you apply it. That, I feel, is being grossly overlooked in the pursuit of tax credits or to circumvent union protections, as work not only leaves the state but leaves the country. “I think ‘The Pitt’ economically has proven that it’s still cost-effective to shoot in Los Angeles if you keep your footprint small and you make certain considerations at the outset that in the event of a success, a rising tide lifts all boats,” he adds. “When we started shooting the pit on the Warner Bros. lot, it was a bit of a ghost town. The only thing that was happening there were the tours going through empty sound stages, talking about the work that used to be done there. And now it’s a fairly buzzy place, so I’m hoping that there’s a trend.” Despite some of the rougher discourse we mentioned above, Wyle says he’s pleased that most of the reaction about Dr. Robby’s mental health journey in Season 2 has been positive. “We hoped that once you got past the architecture of the protagonist having a nervous breakdown in a mass casualty event, the aggregate toll of an average shift in the average life of an average career would be compelling enough television,” he says. “And Season 2 was a bit more speculative than one because of that, and more gratifying to see the response, because it reaffirms that there’s a narrative here that doesn’t necessarily need to revolve around a stunt, like an air show disaster or something massive to really keep viewers’ attention. “It’s incredibly gratifying to be on a show that has resonance and is being spoken about at all,” he adds. “It’s also really gratifying to be involved in a show that’s saying something that sparks conversation and of an intimate nature. You want to be a water cooler show. You want things that people have differing opinions on, so that those ideas and debates can happen in the marketplace, and people can arrive at consensus and hopefully find commonality in that process. I think a lot more bridges have been built through this show than have been burned.” As for next season, the show is moving to November — a chilly month that will provide a bit of contrast to what we’ve seen so far. “We wanted to play with a different season,” Wyle says. “We just came off of hot July 4, so it seemed appropriate to plot it a little into a different season. We wanted Robby to have been away from the hospital for a little while, and so both of those things felt like fall would be appropriate. Everybody’s turning on their heaters again. The first rains caused slick roadways, different kind of cases, different asthetic.” Wyle’s first appearance in Variety was on Feb. 9, 1990, for the NBC miniseries “Blind Faith.” “Given my level of participation in that event, my grandfather watched both segments and said, ‘I had to watch an awful lot of Blind Faith for a little bit of Noah,'” Wyle recalls. “The real story is that somebody had told me that you had to say seven words to get a SAG card, and my line was five words long. It was ‘What’s going on down there?!’ I spent all morning trying to figure out how to stretch it to seven. And when the director said action, I said ‘Excuse me, what’s going on down there?!’ And then I found out it didn’t matter. I didn’t have to say seven words.” 10 QUESTIONS WITH NOAH WYLE: 1. Childhood nickname: “‘Wile E Coyote,’ from ‘Road Runner,’ I got called Wile E. Coyote a lot growing up, or ‘Noah’s Ark,’ obviously.” 2. Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into it now: “Oh my goodness, I’m still into everything I was into as a kid. But I had an unnatural obsession with ‘Grease 2.’ I know every word to ‘Grease 2,’ and sometimes alone in my car, will do renditions of ‘Cool Rider.’ I’ve befriended Chris McDonald, who played Goose, he was the tall T-Bird, and I’m sure he’s so annoyed with how many times I bring that movie up.” 3. Go-to Karaoke or sing-in-the-shower song: “It’s a massive phobia that I’ve been grappling with for most of my life. I got shamed young and scared to sing publicly, so it’s been one of my great desires to be able to have confidence. Even the mention of the word ‘karaoke’ makes me break out and sweat. Because it usually means I’m being forced to do something I’m not comfortable with. But I’m working on it. I usually warm up slow with something that Rex Harrison could handle.” [What about alone in the shower?] “That’s when I go full ‘Dreamgirls’ cast album.” 4. Give me an alternate title for your show: [Not asked] 5. What’s your secret talent? : “Acting. Don’t tell anybody. It’s my only talent.” 6. Favorite ice cream flavor : “I like McConnell’s mint chip ice cream a lot, but I also like peanut butter and chocolate ice cream from Haagen Dazs. That was when I got in my youth a lot. And I was part of the ’70s sherbert craze.” 7. The one item you couldn’t live without : “My wife. I’m not calling my wife an item. I’m just saying that I really, really depend heavily upon her.” 8. What TV show in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of? : “‘Deadwood,’ without hesitation. I’ve always wanted to do a western, and I loved that show. David Milch’s writing was poetry punctuated with profanity, and I would have given anything to have been in the room with Ian McShane and Tim Olyphant and Keith Carradine and some of the actors on that show. I just loved it. We had Brad Dourif, who played the doctor on ‘Deadwood.’ He’s the father of Fiona Dourif, who plays Dr. McKay. I got to tell him how much I enjoyed his performance, which I thought was so flawless. That man could put more intention into a syllable than anybody I know.” 9. Fictional character you most admire : “I most admire Atticus Finch, probably. It’s infused with Gregory Peck’s performance. I saw it at a formative age, and there’s that moment at the end when up at the balcony, Jim and Scout are told to stand. ‘Stand up, Jim, your father’s passing.’ And the quiet dignity and heroism of Atticus always loomed large for me.” 10. Your favorite piece of advice : “The first one that comes to mind is George Clooney early on saying, ‘Take your work seriously. Don’t take yourself seriously.’ That was a big one. I remember I saw an interview once with former Boston Celtic great Bill Russell — and I don’t like giving any credit to anything Boston Celtic, but Bill Russell is not your average Boston Celtic — and he said that he learned later in life that it was far better to understand than it is to be understood. And that we spend so much time trying to get our own personal points of view across, and so little time trying to listen to everybody else’s, that we sometimes do ourselves a disservice. So I latched onto that one too.” Variety’s “Awards Circuit” podcast, hosted by Clayton Davis, Jazz Tangcay, Emily Longeretta and Michael Schneider, who also produces, is your one-stop source for lively conversations about the best in film and television. Each episode, “Awards Circuit” features interviews with top film and TV talent and creatives, discussions and debates about awards races and industry headlines, and much more. The eight-episode series premieres on HBO on Aug. 16. The show stars Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan, a veteran Green Lantern, and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart, Jordan’s protege who is learning the ropes. The heroes have magical rings that allow them to create any object imaginable out of green light. They patrol the galaxy and keep peace as members of the Green Lantern Corps. In “Lanterns,” the two outer space cops get called into rural Nebraska for a mysterious murder, which may have connections to dangerous extraterrestrials. Nathan Fillion, who played Green Lantern member Guy Gardner in last year’s “Superman” and its upcoming sequel “Man of Tomorrow,” will be back in “Lanterns.” The new trailer revealed the first look at Sinestro, who has a complicated past with Jordan. In the comics, Sinestro was a former Green Lantern and mentor figure to Jordan, but the red-skinned alien flips and becomes one of Jordan’s greatest villains. He later becomes a Yellow Lantern, an opposing space group who uses fear to power their magical rings. There’s also a cameo from Guy Gardner, plus it’s revealed that the murder mystery surrounds the Manhunters, a race of aliens who can shape-shift and look like anyone. “Lanterns” is created by Tom King, Damon Lindelof and showrunner Chris Mundy. They also serve as executive producers alongside DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran. “Lanterns” joins “Creature Commandos” and “Peacemaker” as fellow shows in the rebooted DC Universe. Up next for the DCU is this fall’s body-horror movie “Clayface,” starring Tom Rhys Harries as the classic Batman villain. articles.title: HBO Max Leads the Emmy Drama and Comedy Races for the First Time Since 2017. How Often Do Both Frontrunners Win?
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 2:30pm PT HBO Max Leads the Emmy Drama and Comedy Races for the First Time Since 2017. How Often Do Both Frontrunners Win? Awards Circuit Column: "The Pitt" and "Hacks" look to make history for the network, along with "DTF St. Louis" on the limited side. By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest HBO Max Leads the Emmy Drama and Comedy Races for the First Time Since 2017. How Often Do Both Frontrunners Win? 13 hours ago Anne Hathaway’s Oscars ‘Odyssey’: Will She Campaign for Lead Actress or Supporting? 18 hours ago Oscar Voters Rave Over Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ at First Academy Screenings: ‘The Definitive Filmmaker of Our Time’ 2 days ago See All HBO Max HBO Max wants it all. The most-nominated network enters Phase 2 of the Emmy race with the year’s two most-nominated series, giving the platform a rare opportunity to capture television’s top drama and comedy prizes, and potentially make history across three major program categories. “ The Pitt ,” the sophomore season of the breakout medical drama, leads all programs with 25 nominations. Close behind is “ Hacks ,” which earned 24 nominations, making it the most-nominated comedy series in Emmy history. The next closest is Apple TV’s horror-comedy “Widow’s Bay,” with 19. Related Stories Christopher Nolan Dedicates 'The Odyssey' to Late Imax Pioneer David Keighley Anne Hathaway's Oscars 'Odyssey': Will She Campaign for Lead Actress or Supporting? It’s an uncommon achievement for a single network or platform to produce both the most-nominated drama and comedy series in the same year. Popular on Variety Apple TV accomplished the feat last year with “Severance” and “The Studio,” the latter of which became another comedy record-breaker. A year earlier, FX earned the distinction with “Shōgun” and “The Bear,” which at the time also became the most-nominated comedy series in Emmy history before ultimately losing the top comedy prize to Season 3 of “Hacks.” And now, it is HBO Max’s turn. The platform’s current dominance marks its first time leading both genres since 2017. (I misstated this distinction on this week’s episode of the Variety Awards Circuit Podcast.) For HBO, however, this territory is familiar. The premium network led both drama and comedy nominations in consecutive years, in 2003 and 2004, with “The Sopranos,” “Six Feet Under” and “Sex and the City.” It repeated the feat during the latter half of the 2010s with “Game of Thrones,” “Westworld” and “Veep.” Few programmers in Emmy history have consistently produced the leading drama and comedy contenders in the same ceremony. History, however, shows that nomination dominance does not always translate into Emmy glory. Among the 18 instances in which a single network led the Emmy nominations in both drama and comedy, the series ultimately won only four times (22%). Those successful double victories came twice for NBC with “Hill Street Blues” and “Cheers” in 1983 and 1984, again for NBC in 1987 with “L.A. Law” and “The Golden Girls,” and, finally, for HBO in 2016 with “Game of Thrones” and “Veep.” Leading both genres reflects passion for programs for sure, but hardly guarantees a path to the big stage. Campaign strategy, momentum and voter sentiment during final-round voting will ultimately determine whether HBO Max can capitalize on its historic position and not fall to some of its closest competitors like Apple’s “Pluribus” in drama series and “Widow’s Bay” in comedy. Notably, one statistic strongly favors another win for “The Pitt.” The most-nominated program series of the Emmy year has won its corresponding top series category 41 times across 73 eligible ceremonies (56%). Last year provided a rare exception when “Severance,” with 27 nominations, lost drama series to “The Pitt.” Before that upset, the most-nominated series had won its corresponding top category every year from 2015 through 2024. “The Pitt” enters this part of the season not only with the largest nomination haul but also as the reigning champion after winning its debut season. Only four shows have won drama series for both their first and second seasons: “Hill Street Blues,” “Picket Fences,” “The West Wing” and “Mad Men.” Three of those four — except “Picket” — ultimately won at least four drama series Emmys overall. (CBS’ “Mission: Impossible” and “The Defenders” also won the top drama prize in their first two seasons when the category carried different titles: “Outstanding Dramatic Series” and “Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Drama,” respectively.) WIDOW’S BAY, Matthew Rhys, ‘Welcome to Widow’s Bay!’, (Season 1, ep. 101, aired April 29, 2026). photo: ©Apple TV+ / Courtesy Everett Collection ©Apple TV/Courtesy Everett Collection The stats suggest “Hacks” faces a slightly steeper climb. While the series leads the comedy field in nominations and already owns the comedy series trophy for its third season, the most-nominated comedy has historically converted at a lower rate than its drama counterpart. The most-nominated comedy series has won 25 out of 59 times in the current category format (or 42%). The frontrunner has been especially vulnerable in recent years, losing five of the past eight ceremonies, including 2023, when “The Bear” fell to “Hacks.” Also worth noting: the last comedy series to win in non-consecutive years was “Everybody Loves Raymond,” which won for its seventh season in 2003 and again for its ninth and final season in 2005, with “Arrested Development” winning in between. Other comedies to accomplish the feat include “Murphy Brown,” “Cheers,” “All in the Family” and, in the category’s earliest years, “The Jack Benny Show.” So, if HBO Max completes the coveted drama-comedy double, “The Pitt” appears to be the safer bet for a repeat victory, while “Hacks” will need to overcome some more historical statistics. The streamer also has its sights set on an even rarer accomplishment. Beef. (L to R) Oscar Isaac as Josh Martin, Carey Mulligan as Lindsay Crane-Martin in episode 201 of Beef. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 COURTESY OF NETFLIX In limited series, HBO Max’s “DTF St. Louis” earned 13 nominations, including directing, writing and supporting acting recognition for David Harbour, Jason Bateman, Richard Jenkins, Linda Cardellini and Joy Sunday. The network hopes to overtake Netflix’s “Beef,” which leads the limited series field with 16 nominations. The first iteration won this category. “Beef” stars Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan appear well-positioned in the lead acting categories, while Harbour and Cardellini face a more crowded supporting field because of their co-stars nominated from the same series. Meanwhile, Charles Melton and Yuh-jung Youn enter their respective races without internal competition. That could be helpful down the road. But here are some more numbers to consider. The limited series frontrunner has been the least reliable of the three major program categories. The most-nominated limited series has won 16 of 45 times (or 36%) — compared with 45% for drama and 42% for comedy. Since 2021, the nomination leader for miniseries has lost four out of five times: “WandaVision” (2021), “Dahmer – Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story” (2023), “True Detective: Night Country” (2024) and “The Penguin” (2025), which led with 23 nominations but lost to “Adolescence.” Only “The White Lotus” (2022) managed a victory. The category has long produced “frontrunner” collapses, including HBO’s “Mildred Pierce” (20 nominations, 2011), which lost to “Downton Abbey,” and CBS’ “Lonesome Dove” (15 nominations, 1989), which fell to “War and Remembrance.” Winning the top series prizes in drama, comedy and limited series in the same year remains one of the rarest accomplishments in Emmy history. It has happened only three times: HBO achieved the feat in 2015 with “Game of Thrones,” “Veep” and “Olive Kitteridge,” while NBC accomplished it twice, in 1996 with “ER,” “Frasier” and “Gulliver’s Travels,” and in 1987 with “L.A. Law,” “The Golden Girls” and “A Year in the Life.” So in fairness, HBO has done it before. But can they do it again? That remains to be determined. But it is still early in Phase 2, and plenty can change before ballots are finalized. Final-round voting runs Aug. 17-26 ahead of the Creative Arts Emmy Awards and Governors Gala on Sept. 5-6. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards will air Sept. 14 on NBC. articles.title: ‘Crutch’ Canceled After One Season at Paramount+
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 3:00pm PT ‘Crutch’ Canceled After One Season at Paramount+ By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest ‘Crutch’ Canceled After One Season at Paramount+ 12 hours ago ‘My Little Pony: Forever Friendship’ YouTube Series to Launch in 2027 14 hours ago ‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Sets 2026 Release Date at Paramount+, Drops Apocalyptic First Teaser 2 days ago See All JoJo Whilden/Paramount+ The Paramount+ multi-cam comedy “ Crutch ” is done after just one season, Variety has learned. The series, which starred Tracy Morgan in the title role, originally debuted on Paramount+ back in November 2025. News of the series ending comes as little surprise, as it failed to find a significant audience upon its debut and considering Morgan’s commitment to other projects. Most notably, Morgan now stars in the NBC comedy “The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins.” That show debuted on NBC in January 2026 and was renewed for a second season in May . In addition, cast options expired some time ago with many moving on to other projects. Related Stories Paramount Skydance Agrees to Link Merger Antitrust Case to Pre-Existing Paramount+ Subscriber Suit Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial With the cancellation, Paramount+ just one live-action comedy on its current slate, with that being the Australian import “Colin from Accounts.” The streamer is instead focused on its dramas like Taylor Sheridan’s “Landman” and “Yellowstone” spinoff “Dutton Ranch” as well as the British crime drama “MobLand” among others. Popular on Variety “Crutch” follows its titular character Francois “Frank” Crutchfield (Morgan), who goes by “Crutch,” who is described as “a brash, yet beloved Harlem shop owner who finds his world turned upside down when his highbrow son and free-spirited daughter move back into the Crutchfield family home.” The series was set in the world of “The Neighborhood,” one of CBS’ original comedy series, with Morgan appearing in a crossover episode of that show the same day that “Crutch” debuted on Paramount+. Additional cast members for “Crutch” included Jermaine Fowler, Kecia Lewis, Adrianna Mitchell, Adrian Martinez, Braxton Paul, and Finn Maloney. “Crutch” hailed from Cedric The Entertainer and his production company, A Bird and a Bear Entertainment. The series is executive produced by Cedric The Entertainer and Eric C. Rhone and created by Owen Smith who served as executive producer and showrunner. Executive producers for “Crutch” included Aaron Kaplan for Kapital Entertainment, Wendi Trilling for TrillTV, Mike Mariano and, Morgan. The series was produced by CBS Studios and distributed by Paramount Global Content Distribution outside of Paramount+ markets. articles.title: ‘Blue Bloods,’ ‘Once Upon a Time’ TV Director Ralph W. Hemecker Dies at 65
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 3:59pm PT ‘Blue Bloods,’ ‘Once Upon a Time’ TV Director Ralph W. Hemecker Dies at 65 By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest ‘Blue Bloods,’ ‘Once Upon a Time’ TV Director Ralph W. Hemecker Dies at 65 11 hours ago Noah Wyle on ‘The Pitt’ Fan Discourse, Saving Hollywood and What’s Coming In Season 3 13 hours ago ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Co-Creator Bill Prady Explains the Science Behind the Show’s Multiverse 1 day ago See All Courtesy photo Veteran TV director, writer and producer Ralph W. Hemecker, known for his work on shows including “The X-Files,” “ Blue Bloods ,” “ Once Upon a Time ” and “The Flash,” has died. He was 65. According to an obituary notice, Hemecker died July 10 at his home in Glendale, Calif. Hemecker’s credits over the years also include “Millennium,” “Ghost Whisperer,” “Numb3rs,” “The Vampire Diaries,” “Nikita,” “V,” and many more. He directed the Fox pilot “Roar,” starring a then-unknown Heath Ledger, as well as pilots for “Lawless” and “Dead at 21.” Related Stories How Strong Is the Democratic State AGs' Lawsuit Aiming to Block Paramount's Warner Bros. Takeover? Paramount Skydance Agrees to Link Merger Antitrust Case to Pre-Existing Paramount+ Subscriber Suit Ralph William Hemecker was born on June 12, 1961, and studied English at Bucknell University, where he was already making short films. He later took filmmaking classes at New York University. Popular on Variety Hemecker started his career in production and post-production, and early on was a director on Fox’s “America’s Most Wanted.” He also got early experience on the syndicated series “Silk Stalkings,” which he later directed episodes for, as well as Stephen J. Cannell’s “Renegade.” Another big break came in 2000, when he directed the TNT TV movie adaptation of the comic “Witchblade,” executive produced by Dan Halsted and Oliver Stone. That turned into the “Witchblade” TV series, which he served as showrunner, executive producer and writer for two seasons, from 2001 to 2002. Among his busiest gigs were directing 31 episodes of “Blue Bloods” and 28 episodes of “Once Upon a Time.” “Some losses are impossible to put into words,” “Once Upon a Time” star Lana Parilla wrote on Instagram. “ Ralph Hemecker was one of the kindest, most generous souls I’ve ever known. One of ‘Once Upon a Time’s’ defining directors. A truly passionate, beautiful man and my dear friend. I was lucky enough to shadow Ralph as a director as he knew ‘Once,’ behind the camera, best. He was always carrying a camera in hand, staying up all night in the director’s office putting his shots together, studying the scripts and endlessly visiting sets in preparation. His passion was infectious. We always knew if Ralph was directing, we were in good hands.” Wrote “Once” exec producers Adam Horowitz and Eddy Kitsis: “Ralph Hemecker was a great friend, partner, and a true artist. His contribution to ‘Once Upon a Time’ was immeasurable and he will be missed more than words can express.” Hemecker also directed feature films and television movies such as “Dead On,” “Blade Squad,” “Haunting Sarah,” “Fatal Desire,” “Nora Roberts’ Angels Fall,” “Nora Roberts’ Midnight Bayou” and “Skyrunners.” He launched Mythic Films in 2000. Hemecker is survived by two stepdaughters, as well as his father, sister, brother, three nephews, one niece and a great-nephew. Services will be announced at a later date. articles.title: Norwegian Zombie Comedy ‘Grandmonster’ Wins Big Laughs and Top Outpost Award at Fantasia’s Frontières Market
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 4:00pm PT Norwegian Zombie Comedy ‘Grandmonster’ Wins Big Laughs and Top Outpost Award at Fantasia’s Frontières Market Frontières Shorts-to-Features sci-fi drama 'Reset' and Haitian gothic horror 'Sea Spirits' scoop Outpost special mentions, among six prizes handed out at Frontières' closing cocktail July 24 By Jennie Punter Plus Icon Jennie Punter Latest Vanessa Marano to Produce and Star in Frontières Horror Comedy ‘Ring Leader’: ‘It’s ‘Bridesmaids’ Meets ‘Send Help’’ (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago Guillermo del Toro, Kim Novak, Ari Aster Lined Up for ‘The Fall,’ Investigating Hitchcock’s ‘Biggest Mystery’ – the Stunning ‘Vertigo’ Finale (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago Psychological Horror Feature ‘Ancestral Beasts’ Debuts Trailer Ahead of Fantasia World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago See All 'Grandmonster' image courtesy of Syden Pictures Norwegian director Vegard Dahle’s zombie comedy “Grandmonster” has won the top Outpost Award, and a prize of post-production services, at the Fantasia Festival’s prestigious Frontières Co-Production Market, which handed out six awards at its closing cocktail, July 25. The film, about an American dropout who unintentionally triggers a zombie outbreak at a remote Norwegian nursing home while trying to save her grandmother from dementia, was presented with deadpan, self-deprecating humor by Dahle and producer Jon Vatne, who wore matching sweaters, at a day-long Frontières pitching event on July 22. Related Stories Paramount Faces Drawn-Out Battle With State AGs: 'They Saw the Writing on the Wall' CNN on Edge: Staffers Fear Bari Weiss Takeover as Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal Moves Closer to Finish Line The project, one of the 20 titles in Frontières official selection, received a boisterous, laugh-inducing response from the packed Frontières audience of fellow pitchers and buyer and industry delegates. 300 delegates from 24 countries attended the market, including team members of projects in its official selection, Genre Lab, Shorts To Features, and Music strands. Popular on Variety Back row, L to R: Edson Jean, Eugene Park and Daniel Marino of ‘Sea Spirits’; Jon Vatne, Vegard Dahle of ‘Grandmonster’; Julien Soros (‘Reset’), Jasmine De Silva, (‘Eternal Valley’); Jerry Hsu (‘Reset’). Front Row, L to R: Hans Audric Estialbo (‘Cher’); Cassidy Civiero and Mariel Sharp of ‘Wifey’; Celine Tien (‘Reset’), Tuli Litvak (‘Eternal Valley’). Photo by Ted Geoghegan, Courtesy of Fantasia International Film Festival and the Frontières International Co-Production Market Outpost Special Awards were presented to two titles in the Shorts to Features category. “Reset” is U.S. directors Celine Tien and Jerry Hsu’s sci-fi drama about a program that resets the elderly into children to remain economically useful; the short is screening in Fantasia’s official international short film competition. “Sea Spirits” is director Edson Jean’s Haiti-set gothic folk horror about a guilt-ridden mother haunted by her daughter, who is lost at sea and refuses to leave the country in search of her ghost. The PurpleDOG Award for an official selection project, which comes with a prize of post-production services, went to “Cher,” the first project out of Thailand participating in Frontières, a supernatural folk horror about a vengeance-seeking forest spirit who emerges near a remote mining camp that is trespassing on sacred forestland. The PurpleDOG Award for a project in the Gender Equity in Media Society (GEMS) section of the Genre Film Lab went to “Wifey,” Canadian director Cassidy Civiero’s horror thriller about an independent artist about to transition female-to-male who is is forced into a non-consensual marriage in which traditional gender norms are used as a violent weapon. The Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival Award, which comes with an invitation to pitch at the Sitges festival in October, went to “Eternal Valley,” U.K. director Jasmine De Silva’s dark comedy body horror, a feature project based on her proof-of-concept short film “Beauty Sleep,” which had its world premiere at Fantasia in 2025. “The feedback we’ve received from participants about the projects pitched last Wednesday has been overwhelmingly positive,” Frontières executive director Annick Mahnert told Variety shortly before the award ceremony. “People have praised not only the exceptional quality of the projects themselves, but also the filmmakers’ pitch presentations. Every year, the bar is raised even higher, and I believe that’s why decision-makers return year after year. They trust our curation.” One-on-one meetings and industry seminars conclude on July 25. Here is the full list of Frontières award winners and their prizes: Outpost Award of CAD$15,000 (US$10,637) in post-production services: “Grandmonster” Outpost Special Mention Award of CAD$5,000 (US$3545) in post-production services: “Reset” Outpost Special Mention: Award of CAD$5,000 (US$3545) in post-production services: “Sea Spirits” PurpleDOG award to Official Selection project, CAD$10,000 (US$7091) in post-production services: “Cher” PurpleDOG award to GEMS project, CAD$10,000 (US$7091) in post-production services: “Wifey” Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival: an invitation to pitch at the Sitges Festival next October, “Eternal Valley” Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Has Epic Opening Day With $51 Million Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Movie Is Making Gen Z Listen to the Book (EXCLUSIVE) Matt Damon Shocked Robert Pattinson on ‘The Odyssey’ Set by ‘Screaming and Screaming’ to Blow His Voice Out and Sound Older: ‘A Complete Psycho’ ‘The Odyssey’ Becomes Christopher Nolan’s Biggest Global Debut of All Time With $264 Million Oscar Voters Rave Over Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ at First Academy Screenings: ‘The Definitive Filmmaker of Our Time’ Imax Second Quarter Earnings Rise as CEO Calls Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Transformational Event’ Loading comments... articles.title: Paramount Faces Drawn-Out Battle With State AGs: ‘They Saw the Writing on the Wall’
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 5:54pm PT Paramount Faces Drawn-Out Battle With State AGs: ‘They Saw the Writing on the Wall’ By Gene Maddaus , Todd Spangler Getty Only a few days ago, the states’ antitrust challenge to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger still looked like a speed bump. Now, it looks more like siege warfare — as Paramount has agreed to put the $111 million deal on hold for at least several months. In doing so, Paramount’s lawyers have effectively conceded that they were not likely to prevail in an upcoming fight over an injunction and will instead try to beat the states at trial. Related Stories Hollywood's Favorite Ugg Slippers (To Never Wear on a Christopher Nolan Set) How Long Can 'The Odyssey' Stay on Imax 70mm Screens? Nolan Fans Scramble as New Showtimes Sell Out 7 Weeks in Advance “I think they saw the writing on the wall,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta told Variety on Friday. “They saw that the outcome of a motion for a preliminary injunction was a fait accompli. The die was cast. They were going to lose. Otherwise, why not challenge it?” Popular on Variety David Ellison, Paramount Skydance ‘s chairman and CEO, had hoped to win a ruling denying the injunction by mid-September — allowing him to close the deal in time to avoid paying Warner Bros. shareholders millions of dollars a day. His lawyers pushed for a three-day evidentiary hearing in late August, where they could confront the states’ expert economist and undermine the states’ argument that the deal will result in illegal market concentration. But in a ruling on Thursday, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin denied Paramount’s bid to speed up briefing on that request, signaling she was not inclined to go along with the multiday hearing. The judge had already granted a 28-day restraining order, finding that the states had made a “strong showing” that the merger was likely to harm competition, and the standard to get an injunction would be similar. Paramount could have opted to wait for the ruling and then immediately appeal to the 9th Circuit. But Nexstar tried to do that after its merger with Tegna was enjoined in April — and is still stuck in limbo with no assurance of resolution anytime soon. Paramount would have faced a similar delay, likely pushing any appellate relief into early 2027. So where does it go from here? To trial, where Paramount still believes it has the upper hand against what it terms “one of the weakest merger challenges in modern antitrust history.” The company hopes to get there as soon as possible, ideally before the end of 2026. Whenever a trial is held, it won’t come fast enough to avoid having to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders $7 million per day, starting on Sept. 30. But that is a cost that Paramount will have to bear to get the deal done. The 12-state coalition will push for a later date, arguing that it needs additional time to prepare. “We do think 2027 is appropriate,” Bonta said. “If the judge said April 2027, we would not disagree with that.” Paramount has agreed not to close the transaction until five days after the trial ruling or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first. Bonta argued that Paramount is pushing for a speedy resolution due to “business factors” and not due process considerations. “I’m sure they want a fast trial,” he said. “That’s based on other reasons, not what’s appropriate for a case of this magnitude.” The states will want extra time to obtain extensive discovery, including documents and depositions they were unable to get during their investigation. “Paramount and Warner Bros. were dragging their feet. They didn’t give us everything we wanted,” Bonta said. “If they wanted to have a trial quicker, they could have given us the information we asked for in the pre-litigation discovery process.” The trial will be held in Martinez-Olguin’s courtroom in Oakland, Calif., and could last two to three weeks or more. In the meantime, Paramount could seek to reopen settlement talks with the states. So far, Bonta said, the company has not offered the sort of structural remedies — that is, divestitures of cable or film distribution assets — that would have to be part of a deal. Bonta has said repeatedly that he is not interested in “behavioral” remedies, such as a consent decree guaranteeing a minimum number of film releases or 45-day theatrical windows, saying that those have proven ineffective in the past. “We’ve never gotten anything that would come close to addressing the concerns we’ve raised,” Bonta said. “We’re focused on litigation. We’ve built momentum and we look forward to taking that momentum into trial.” In its statement, Paramount argued that the strategic retreat was the best way to get to a decision on the merits of the deal as soon as possible. “This is the fastest and clearest way to prove that this transaction is good for competition, good for consumers, and good for creators, a conclusion dozens of competition authorities around the world have already reached,” the company said. Bonta argued the opposite — and now it’s clear those arguments present more than a minor obstacle. “This merger, if it is able to go through, will hurt Americans, will hurt Californians,” he said. “It will raise their prices. It shouldn’t break the bank to enjoy your favorite show on the couch.” Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Stuns With $124 Million Opening Weekend, Third-Biggest Debut of the Year Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ The Sound of ‘The Odyssey’: Composer Ludwig Göransson Used Ancient Greek Instruments, Scrap Metals and Gongs My 2 a.m. ‘Odyssey’: Inside the Sold-Out, All-Night Screening of Christopher Nolan’s Epic ‘The Odyssey’ Becomes Christopher Nolan’s Biggest Global Debut of All Time With $264 Million ‘Toy Story’ Franchise Has Generated $51 Billion in Economic Activity, Study Finds Loading comments... articles.title: Nick Hakim’s ‘I Can See’ Is a Hazy Alt-R&B Masterpiece: Album Review
articles.full_text: Breaking News Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial Jul 24, 2026 6:28pm PT Nick Hakim’s ‘I Can See’ Is a Hazy Alt-R&B Masterpiece: Album Review By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Nick Hakim’s ‘I Can See’ Is a Hazy Alt-R&B Masterpiece: Album Review 9 hours ago Charli xcx Cranks Up the Guitars and Launches Her Post-‘Brat’ Era With the Razor-Sharp ‘Music, Fashion, Film’: Album Review 1 day ago Sienna Spiro Plays Intimate Benefit Concert for North Shore Animal League 2 days ago See All “Stoner R&B” is not an insult: It’s the opposite, a loose term to describe a sprawling genre of music that includes everything from Dijon and Frank Ocean to Brent Faiyaz and Jhene Aiko. It’s R&B that has smoked a strong blunt, with languid grooves, heavy bass, psychedelicized production and an unhurried vocal approach. Unlike the tight rhythms, choppy guitars and urgency of traditional R&B, it’s not in a hurry to get anywhere. When Nick Hakim first emerged in 2014 with his “Where Will We Go” EPs and subsequent albums, he was a bright new voice in the genre, but as the years went by, his music sailed further and further out until, by 2022’s “Cometa,” conventional song structures had pretty much drifted off. Related Stories Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ Christopher Nolan Says 'The Odyssey's' Modern English Dialogue 'Was a No-Brainer' Even If 'It Might Bite Me on the Ass' and 'I Was Maybe Being Naïve' But his fourth and latest album, “I Can See,” is his most focused work to date — and despite the unhurried tempos and smoky vibes, it’s a very seriously structured set of songs, with multiple layers of his soft, soulful vocals and shimmering keyboards. “Real Here Now” is one of the most gorgeous R&B songs you’ll hear all year and is almost like an Usher song from a parallel universe, but as always his music has a crossover appeal that defies pigeonholing: The following song, “U Can Make It,” is a densely layered track built around a thudding electronic bass drum, echo-drenched piano and layers and layers of vocals. Popular on Variety The unusually hazy sound of this album is as vital as the songs — the vocals and instruments waft in and out of the mix like music from a passing car or sounds from the apartment next door; you’re not always sure exactly what you’re hearing, not that it matters. Equal parts electronic and organic, it pairs conventional snare and rimshot sounds with heavy digital bass, piano so heavily treated that it sounds like a warped calliope, and backing vocals that float in and out like a chorus of ghosts. After the more-conventionally structured songs of the album’s first half, the last few continue “Cometa”’s journey toward the cosmos, growing murkier and piling on effects reminiscent of dub reggae. Indeed, “I Can See” is a realm beyond alternative R&B — it’s more like R&B from a different planet.
