articles.title: Donald Trump Delivers Rally-Like Hour Of Rehash In White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Agrees Not To Close WBD Merger Until Next Year Or Until Lawsuit Merits Resolved; Opponents Cheer Delay; Stocks Slide Read the full story By Ted Johnson , Dade Hayes July 24, 2026 8:08pm President Donald Trump speaks during the re-scheduled White House Correspondents Dinner in Washington, DC. Eric Lee/Getty Images Speaking at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner on Friday, Donald Trump delivered an hour-long speech blending shopworn rally material with a string of leaden one-liners. He was making his first appearance as president at the dinner, which had to be rescheduled last Aprtil after a shooter attempted to rush the ballroom and was subdued by the Secret Service. While presidents for decades have long used the event’s keynote slot to zing reporters to varying degrees, Trump lapsed into rally mode, only deviating for some personal broadsides at members of the press, marbled with references to their appearance. Related Stories News Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President Politics White House Responds After Alan Ritchson Urges Trump “Go To Jail” Over Epstein Files After one quip about an elderly U.S. senator’s sex life drew crickets, Trump asked, “Does anybody get that? I thought that was actually great. That was actually the only thing I thought was good in this whole frickin’ stupid speech. It was the only good one, and that went down with not exactly great laughter.” Watch on Deadline Over the rest of the meandering speech (watch the whole thing below), Trump seemed to recognize that many of his would-be jokes were not landing. There were few laughs or reactions at all beyond squirming or fidgeting as he veered in stream-of-consciousness fashion from topic to topic. “Tonight’s event is even crazier than the last time,” Trump said. “It’s so successful that I’ve been informed by CBS News’ David Ellison” (Ellison is CEO of CBS parent Paramount) that “next year, they’re going to call it the Trump White House Correspondents’ Dinner.” Changing the name, he added, “is the only way you’re going to get me back here.” The hour-long speech tested the patience of all but the fiercest Trump loyalists in attendance. The audience only sporadically showed a notable reaction, with long periods of near-silence prevailing. Once Trump’s remarks concluded and mentalist Oz Pearlman took the stage, a number of guests streamed toward the exits. Compared with April’s event at the Hilton, the ballroom at the Waldorf-Astoria is much smaller. Trump cabinet members mingled with reporters in an aisle near one of Paramount’s tables. Chief Legal Officer Makan Delrahim was at the dinner just a couple of hours after the decision to push back the company’s planned merger with Warner Bros. Discovery amid an antitrust challenge. At a Paramount table with Delrahim were cabinet members Pete Hegseth and presidential advisor Stephen Miller and his wife Katie Miller. Also at the event: Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert Kennedy Jr. and his wife Cheryl Himes, as well as Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was at the center of one of Pearlman’s mental feats. Prior to Trump’s remarks, there were some awkward moments onstage as annual awards were given out, including to some journalists behind investigations of the president. As Wall Street Journal reporters accepted an honor for their Jeffrey Epstein story, Trump shook their hands and then threw his hands up in the air and smiled a bit. Wolf Blitzer, who was presenting the award, noted that he sued the WSJ over the story for $20 billion . Once at the lectern, Trump went after Josh Dawsey, one of the WSJ winners, and CNN host Kaitlan Collins with highly personal digs, but the room fell nearly silent as the would-be laugh lines were delivered. Weijia Jiang, outgoing president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, was stone-faced as Trump went into the would-be-roast-like digressions. CNN even released a statement during the speech, defending its journalists. The president appeared to have a set of prepared jokes, but he frequently veered off script, or their subjects seemed to remind him of an aside. The result was a speech that weaved through familiar political attacks, like on Adam Schiff’s appearance, to an extended riff on his plans for a White House ballroom. At one point, he pointed to details on the chandeliers at the Waldorf Astoria venue, which he built and previously operated as a Trump hotel. Some of his biting insults at the press were perhaps more muted than they otherwise would have been, given the sheer length of the speech and the topics covered. When Pearlman took the stage, he noted that Trump had made “an announcement that he will attending next year’s event. I thought he was going to speaking until next year, actually.” Trump had been scheduled to speak at the April dinner, but it was interrupted and then ended after a gunman breached a security barricade. The incident took place just outside the Washington Hilton ballroom, but shots could be heard among dinner guests. That sent the Secret Service scrambling to remove Trump and Vice President JD Vance from the dais, as well as other guests seated in the ballroom.

articles.title: Peacock’s ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Series Casts Audiobook Narrator Jeff Hays
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All July 23, 2026 4:00pm Jeff Hays Hampton Stevens Logo text Peacock ‘s Dungeon Crawler Carl series has cast its first actor — one who will be familiar to those who have listened to the audiobook versions of Matt Dinniman’s novels. Jeff Hays, the narrator and producer of the DCC audiobooks, will voice the character of Princess Donut in the live-action series. Princess Donut is a key character in the books, a cat belonging to Carl’s ex-girlfriend who acquires the ability to speak when they become part of a survival game show run by the aliens who have destroyed most of humanity. Hays joined Dinniman and Matt Yost, writer and executive producer of the Peacock series, on stage Thursday at Comic-Con to announce his casting. Related Stories Movies Johnny Depp Surprises Comic-Con as Ebenezer Scrooge on Streets of San Diego TV New 'Avatar' Animated Series at Paramount+ Lands Fall Premiere Date, Releases Teaser Peacock placed a series order for Dungeon Crawler Carl in June. The show comes from Universal Global Television and Seth MacFarlane’s Fuzzy Door Productions, which hold the rights to Dinniman’s book series. Yost ( Maul: Shadow Lord ) is executive producing with MacFarlane, Erica Huggins and Rachel Hargreaves-Heald for Fuzzy Door. Dinniman is a co-exec producer. Here’s the full description of the series: “An alien invasion has wiped out most of humanity and any survivors are forced to fight for their lives on a sadistic intergalactic game show. Sounds bad, right? Now try doing it with bare feet and a stuck-up, self-centered, tiara-wearing talking cat as your partner. Welcome to Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, where the apocalypse will be televised … and Coast Guard vet Carl finds himself stuck with his ex-girlfriend’s award-winning show cat, Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk, as they try to survive the end of the world, fighting monsters, aliens, an insane A.I. and even other survivors … all for the sake of good TV. Survival is optional. Entertainment is not.” The Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks have logged more than 140 million listening hours on Audible to date. Hays narrates and does voices for the characters, including Princess Donut. He is repped by Matthew N. Sugarman at Weintraub Tobin. THR

articles.title: ‘Every Year After’ Star Joseph Chiu on Season One Reception and Hopes for Next Season
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All July 23, 2026 4:20pm Joseph Chiu as Jordie. Prime Video “I was screaming in my bedroom when they called me at 10 a.m.,” Every Year After star Joseph Chiu says of getting the news that Prime Video had renewed the romance series for a second season. The 24-year-old Canadian actor plays Jordie Lin in the streamer’s adaptation of the Carley Fortune romance novel Every Summer After , which was released last month. In the weeks after the release, Prime Video announced that Every Year After would be returning for season two and follow Fortune’s follow-up, Our Golden Summer . In Fortune’s book, Chiu’s character, the best friend of Matt Cornett’s leading man, plays a much smaller role, which allowed the actor some space to find his own Jordie. “I was fully committed to the best friend role and doing the best of my abilities to make Sam seem more well-adjusted,” he says. “I really like Stiles from Teen Wolf . There were a lot of references that I was trying to get that energy of in terms of the best friend [character].” Related Stories TV 'Yellowjackets' Star Sophie Nélisse to Lead Netflix Adaptation of Romance Novel 'This Summer Will Be Different' TV A Little Burnout and a Lot of Lakeside Love, How Carley Fortune Became Canada's Summer Romance Darling The actor was fresh from his college graduation when he booked the part, and he wasn’t exactly expecting things to happen so quickly. He found his way into acting during school after he swapped majors. It also wasn’t the first time he’d had a bit of a pivot. When he was 14, he was a K-pop trainee under Korean entertainment company FNC Entertainment. “I was a trainee for three months,” he says. “I actually did pretty well in that program, but then my mom wanted me to finish high school and finish college.” Below, Chiu discusses making season one, what he’s hoping for in season two and how he feels about Canada’s recent film and television spotlight. Were you feeling good after the first season? Were you hopeful? Honestly, with these things, I have no clue. I was on a show called Motorheads where I did a five-episode arc, and it seemed like people were very excited about season two. But then we didn’t get renewed. I was just happy with how season one worked out for me because the way that I was cast was just crazy in itself. I was just grateful to have work as an actor. You auditioned for a different role, correct? You were just graduating from university, right? When did it all hit you? Honestly, I think everything hit me after the show released. Up until then, I was just so obsessed with the whole preparation aspect of the character and really trying to justify the choices that I made with the character. I poured a lot of myself into this role of Jordie. As a 23-year-old still trying to shop for personalities, it was a little difficult and very vulnerable for me, at least, to decide how much of myself I wanted to actually show. This was my first series regular role, and I’ve never been flown out for a role before. I’ve always worked in Toronto or Hamilton. Once I arrived on set, the first day Amy [B. Harris] invited me to just go see the set. I was a little shy, honestly. But then my first scene was actually my audition scene as Jordie. Once I started doing that, it just became fun again. There was zero pressure to get it right just because, specifically for me, Jordie’s not a character really in the book that much. It was just really going moment to moment and really trying to make. I’m just trying to be as present as possible with the two actresses on the day, which was Sadie and Aurora. What was that shooting experience like? What are you hoping for this next season in that regard? Shooting on Bowen Island was beautiful. We took a boat to work every morning. I struggle with allergies, so I was drugged out of my mind on antihistamines. It made me feel a little drowsy, so I drank a lot of black coffee. In terms of the island itself, it’s really beautiful. I think it’s quite similar to Barry’s Bay, although I’ve never been, so I can’t really be saying. Carly seemed happy with the similarities, so we can take her word for that. What I will say, though, is that it reminded me of where my grandmother used to live, which was Wellington, New Zealand. There’s just a sense of peace and boredom. There’s a big sense of boredom. But honestly, that’s what I’ve realized, now in hindsight, that’s a sense of safety. You know how people say touch grass? Yeah. I was touching grass every day for three and a half months, so it was pretty awesome. Where do you think Jordie’s at going forward? I like this question because I can just become the writer now. Let’s hear some of your fan fiction. My PR answer is that that’s a great question for our showrunner, but what I want to prescribe with the power I have, as one of the actors, would just be, I’d like to see Jordie and Chantal in an actual relationship. Aurora and I, we have a certain kind of chemistry where it can become kind of comedic, but then immediately we can go to the depths of seriousness and just really talk about some cool stuff. As for Delilah, I don’t know, I kind of have in real life, there’s a childhood crush and it was unrequited love. I’d like to use that and try to draw on that and maybe build up this moment of confrontation with Delilah of all these feelings that Jordie has buried. The way the ending scene of her looking, it’s exciting for me as an actor because I’m just excited to entertain all of the possibilities in terms of the stakes. Now that Chantal is involved, I do want to explore the backstory between Delilah and Jordie. They live in a small town, but Jordie’s clearly in love with her or was in love, and how Jordie has coped throughout the years. I want to see some jealousy from Jordie too in the past and how he grew into acceptance. Abby’s a really funny actor, so I think we’ll have some good comedic moments balanced out with maybe a big rain confession. I want to see Jordie sing when he was maybe 17. He got really drunk at a bar and starts saying, “Hey There Delilah.” Something like that. I think it’d be really cool. I love that. Also, Delilah coming to watch Jordie play a basketball game and he’s aura farming the whole time. People are really paying attention to the Canadian film and TV industry at this moment, which I have to imagine as a young actor is quite exciting for you as a young actor. It feels great. Alicia and I are the only Canadian actors, but Alicia is based in L.A. But if you book a series regular role on a US production that films in Toronto, your peers literally celebrate you. Because we’re Canada, we really, really put our people in the spotlight and just try to send them to go further down to Hollywood, so it’s actually insane. It’s everything I could have dreamed of. Now, for me, it’s just about celebrating my friends who are also in pursuit of this career and trying to uplift them and their talent. As Canadians, we don’t really have. The access is less. It’s less spotlight, so I’m just trying to use my platform currently to just to celebrate my friends and also people that I really admire. THR

articles.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Pause Extended
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All July 23, 2026 4:35pm Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Logo text Paramount won’t be able to close its $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery until Aug. 18 at the earliest, with the court extending the temporary restraining order another 14 days. U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín issued the extension to allow lawyers for the studio and the states looking to block the deal to come to an agreement on the schedule and format for legal proceedings on a preliminary injunction, which would freeze the transaction until the case is decided if granted. The states alleged that the acquisition will substantially throttle competition in wide-release and top-grossing theatrical distribution and cable licensing in violation of antitrust laws. Separately, the Writers Guild of America filed a lawsuit claiming that the merger will result in lower compensation and worse deal terms. The court on Monday granted the states’ bid to pause the deal. Legal jockeying followed, with Paramount urging the court to hold a three-day evidentiary hearing next month. That would allow it to “address critical factual issues involving market definition, real-world competitive dynamics, barriers to expansion, and incentives,” wrote Jeffrey Kessler, a lawyer for the studio, in a court filing. Paramount intends to put on expert witnesses and cross-examine the states’ experts to undermine arguments that the merger will suppress the markets at issue in the case. It has maintained that the states’ understanding and calculation of the markets are faulty. The states opposed the bid, arguing that a multi-day hearing isn’t appropriate at the preliminary injunction stage and that Paramount is essentially asking for a trial without giving them proper time. For Paramount, the Sept. 30 deadline to close the deal is a key consideration. It previously offered not to consummate the acquisition for up to a month if the court agreed to schedule preliminary injunction proceedings at the end of August in order for a decision to be rendered before the ticking fee is triggered. The ticking fee in the deal contract would result in a $6.9 million per day penalty if the transaction isn’t closed by Sept. 30. The decision on the preliminary injunction will be key. If it’s not granted, Paramount has signaled that it will close, leaving the states to try and unwind the merger. The court will consider arguments on the motion on Aug. 3. THR

articles.title: ‘Toy Story 5’ Has Given Away 18,000 Toys to Sick Kids
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Naomi Jeffries Plus Icon Naomi Jeffries Intern View All July 23, 2026 4:55pm Toy Story's Woody and Jessie visiting a children's hospital. Courtesy of Disney With $957.3 million at the global box office , Toy Story 5 is on track to become the highest-grossing film in the franchise. But the Pixar sequel’s impact isn’t just being measured in ticket sales. Through Disney’s longtime partnership with Starlight Children’s Foundation, the film’s release is also bringing the magic of Woody, Buzz Lightyear and their friends to hospitalized children around the world. Since 2001, Disney and Starlight Children’s Foundation have collaborated to provide hospitalized children with exclusive screenings, care packages and character-inspired experiences. Through its flagship “Disney Movie Moments” program, the company converted hospital spaces into immersive screening events for patients and their families. Related Stories News Harrison Ford Celebrates Michael J. Fox as the "Most Stubborn Optimist I Know" at THR's Social Impact Summit TV 'Percy Jackson' Gets Season 3 Premiere Date As part of the Toy Story 5 rollout, the film became available to patients in more than 400 children’s hospitals globally, including more than 300 across the United States. Disney says it distributed more than 18,000 Toy Story 5 -themed toys and 34,000 character-inspired hospital gowns to children and families across participating hospitals. Woody and Jessie with a patient in a Toy Story-themed hospital gown. Courtesy of Disney Disney also introduced a first-of-its-kind red carpet activation at the film’s Los Angeles premiere , where cast members and guests stopped at a life-size interactive lily pad to write messages of encouragement for children in hospitals. Tim Allen , Greta Lee , Tony Hale , Conan O’Brien, Joan Cusack and other members of the film’s ensemble participated in the activation. Says Hale, “This is amazing! Disney is sending Toy Story to all these fantastic kids in hospitals around the nation.” The heartfelt messages were shown at hospitals in Washington, D.C., Oakland, and Orlando with another immersive Disney hospital experience. Children were surprised with visits from Woody and Jessie, Toy Story -themed gift packages and drawing sessions led by Pixar animators. Conan O’Brien (Smarty Pants) and Joan Cusack (who voices Jessie, far right) at the Toy Story 5 L.A. premiere. Emma McIntyre/Getty Images “ Toy Story has always celebrated the connections that bring us together, and the cast, crew and premiere guests carried that spirit onto the red carpet by writing personal messages for children in hospitals before the world even saw the film.” said Disney’s Lisa Haines, senior vp corporate social responsibility. “Whether it’s a beloved character by a child’s side or a note from the voice of Buzz Lightyear, those simple gestures are incredibly powerful and can create moments of comfort and joy for kids when they’re needed most.” THR

articles.title: ‘72 Hours’ Review: Kevin Hart Throws Himself Into the Slapstick but Netflix’s Intergenerational Farce Squanders Its Premise
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All July 23, 2026 6:00pm From left: Marcello Hernández, Ben Marshall, Kevin Hart, Kam Patterson and Mason Gooding in '72 Hours.' Courtesy of Netflix There’s an amusing, insightful movie to be made about the culture clash that would inevitably result between a 40-year-old Millennial and several Gen Z twenty-somethings. But that’s not the new Netflix comedy directed by Tim Story ( Barbershop , Ride Along ) and starring Kevin Hart . Instead, as might have been predicted, 72 Hours aims for the lowest common denominator, with a wildly farcical plotline in which Hart’s character is mistaken at various times for a human trafficker, a cop and a Cuban drug lord. He also gets into a brawl with several women in a moving limousine and finds himself in a smuggler’s boat carrying an illegal contraband haul of “whale dicks.” Add to that Hart’s face swollen to monstrous proportions after being stung by a jellyfish, and if all of this sounds hilarious, then this is the movie for you. Related Stories TV Apple Gets Into the Dating Game: New Series Sends Unlikely Couples to World's Most Remote Locations TV Netflix Drops 'Tires' Season 3 Trailer as Shane Gillis' Star Skyrockets 72 Hours The Bottom Line Feels longer. Release date : Friday, July 25 Cast : Kevin Hart, Marcello Hernández, Mason Gooding, Kam Patterson, Ben Marshall, Kevin Dunn, Zach Cherry, Teyana Taylor, Andy Garcia Director : Tim Story Screenwriters : Jon Hurwitz, Hayden Schlossberg, Kevin Burrows, Matt Mider Rated R, 1 hour 45 minutes The script crafted by a quartet of screenwriters features a reasonably clever premise. Hart plays Joe, a marketing executive whose pitch for a new vodka line falls flat. “You don’t seem to get youth culture anymore,” his boss (Kevin Dunn, doing his usual exasperated thing) tells him, adding that if Joe doesn’t get with the times he’ll be passed over for a promotion. It’s fortuitous, then, that Joe finds himself accidentally included in a group chat with several young men planning a bachelor party in Miami. When he impulsively responds with a cash gift, he’s invited to join the revelers, who have no idea that he could be their dad. Desperate to find out what makes the younger generation tick, Joe decides to go, much to the irritation of his longtime girlfriend ( Teyana Taylor ), who is impatient for a marriage proposal. Cue the would-be yucks as Joe meets up with Nick ( Marcello Hernández ), Hunter (Ben Marshall), Freshman (Kam Patterson) — all three comedians Saturday Night Live recruits — and groom-to-be Mason ( Mason Gooding , Heart Eyes , Scream 7 ) in a palatial Miami mansion. The house turns out to be the former home of a deceased drug kingpin, which leads to dangerous complications as Joe suffers a series of misadventures, including several run-ins with a group of criminals led by the menacing Jaze ( Michael Mando , illustrating the dangers of typecasting after his far more serious performance as Nacho Varga in Better Call Saul ). The film’s unfunny nadir comes when the gangsters force Joe to ingest cocaine, which for some reason transforms him into the heavily accented “Riccardo Montana,” complete with Scarface riffs including “say hello to my little friend.” The gag is repeated later on; Hart and the filmmakers apparently are convinced that his Al Pacino impression is a laugh riot. Any stabs at cultural satire about, say, Gen Z’s addiction to documenting their lives on social media, are subsumed by the crazy action-comedy shenanigans, with the younger cast, all of whom have proven themselves funny on prior occasions, unable to elevate the pedestrian material. Hart tries hard (he always tries hard), throwing himself into the slapstick with his usual determination. The fact that he’s able to wrest a few laughs is a testament to his comic chops and professionalism. There are some semi-amusing cameos along the way, including a brief appearance by Mike Epps as a cop, and another performer whose identity has been deemed a spoiler by Netflix. But both are outshone by a hilarious Andy Garcia , who demonstrates that, under the right circumstances, sometimes serious actors can be the funniest of all. It’s a shame, though, to see Taylor, fresh off her Oscar-nominated turn as a fierce revolutionary in One Battle After Another , reduced to playing the disapproving girlfriend. It feels less a departure than a regression. And, of course there are the obligatory outtakes during the end credits, apparently intended to prove that the actors, at least, found the proceedings hilarious. Elliot Casting: Nicole Bruno, LaShawnna Stanley, Mary Vernieu, Michelle Wade Byrd Rated R, 1 hour 45 minutes THR

articles.title: Zach Cregger Teases His ‘Weapons’ Prequel and Its “Crazy” Approach to Gladys’ Origin Story
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 23, 2026 6:30pm Amy Madigan in 'Weapons.' Quantrell Colbert/Warner Bros. Logo text Zach Cregger is ready to work his magic with the prequel to Weapons that will focus on breakout character Gladys. During Collider’ s Directors on Directing panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Thursday, the filmmaker shared a status update on the planned feature follow-up to his 2025 horror hit that won Amy Madigan the best supporting actress Oscar for her role as Aunt Gladys. The Hollywood Reporter previously reported that Cregger and Zach Shields are penning the script for the project that is in development at New Line Cinema with the working title Gladys . Related Stories TV Peacock's 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' Series Casts Audiobook Narrator Jeff Hays Movies Johnny Depp Surprises Comic-Con as Ebenezer Scrooge on Streets of San Diego: "It's Good to Be Back" “First of all, I’m really excited about the Gladys movie, and I loved working with Amy,” Cregger told the crowd. “I loved that character. For the movie Weapons , it really made a lot of sense not to dive into her backstory because the device of Weapons was to keep her very mysterious.” He added, “However, there’s an amazing story to be told about where Gladys comes from and how she became what we know her as. It’s got a lot of twists and turns and mysteries and crazy things, like Weapons does. I think it’s going to be great. The script is in progress now, but we’re taking that super seriously, and it’s moving in the right direction. So yeah, it’s being written, is the short answer.” Centering on a group of children who go missing in the middle of the night, Weapons hit theaters last August from Warner Bros. and collected $270 million at the global box office. In addition to Madigan, the cast included Julia Garner, Josh Brolin, Alden Ehrenreich, Austin Abrams and Benedict Wong. At Thursday’s panel, Cregger screened the latest trailer and additional exclusive footage from his forthcoming video game adaptation Resident Evil , which Sony releases in September. Cregger noted that his next feature will be The Flood , a sci-fi film that he wrote for New Line. Also participating in the panel were Mayday directors John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein , who teased the progress on the new Star Trek feature that the pair are writing and directing . “It won’t be the characters you’ve seen previously,” Goldstein said from the stage. “It will be a little further into the future than what you’ve seen.” THR

articles.title: Mary Kate Golding, ‘The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel’ Set Decorator, Dies at 34 in Stabbing
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 23, 2026 6:46pm Mary Kate Golding Facebook Mary Kate Golding, The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel set decorator, has died after being found stabbed. She was 34. Golding was found dead on Tuesday in her apartment in Astoria, Queens, having suffered a stab wound on her back, an NYPD spokesperson told People . Police were called to her residence after midnight and at roughly 6:39 a.m. they responded to a call of “an unconscious person in the vicinity of Astoria Park South and Shore Boulevard.” That person was Golding’s husband, Joseph Azzaretto, with the police telling People they believe the deaths were a “possible murder-suicide.” Related Stories Lifestyle Anne Russell, Actress in 'Hello, Dolly!' and 'Mame,' Dies at 103 TV Zale Parry, Pioneering Scuba Diver and 'Sea Hunt' Actress, Dies at 93 Golding and Azzaretto’s 11-month old son was found at their residence unharmed. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to the NYPD for comment. Golding is credited as the set decorator for the first six season-one episodes of The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel . According to her Facebook, she graduated from New York University in 2015. She has worked on a plethora of other television shows, including Gotham (2019); The Undoing (2020); The Flight Attendant (2020); season one of Harlem ; the 2021 Marvel series Hawkeye ; two 2024 episodes of Mr. and Mrs. Smith ; Goosebumps (2025); and the Netflix documentary Gone Girls: The Long Island Serial Killer . On the film side, she served as a member of the art department on the 2022 rom-com Marry Me , which starred Jennifer Lopez and Owen Wilson. She is also credited as an assistant set director on Sean Durkin’s forthcoming feature Deep Cuts , starring Drew Starkey and Cailee Spaeny. Years ago, Azzaretto’s younger brother, Nicholas Azzaretto, shot and killed his father at their Pennsylvania family home when he was 20. He pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter in November 2021 and was sentenced to 10 years of probation. THR

articles.title: Charli XCX Brings in the Post-‘Brat’ Era With ‘Music, Fashion, Film’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All July 23, 2026 9:00pm Charli xcx attends the 2026 Met Gala celebrating "Costume Art" at the Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 04, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images) Following much anticipation, Charli XCX is officially back with Music , Fashion, Film , her seventh album overall and her first since her seminal Brat took over the world in 2024. While she hasn’t technically released a solo album since then, pop’s most trendsetting auteur has been certifiably, emphatically, Not On A Break. “The second people are getting sick of you, that’s when you have to go even harder,” Kylie Jenner, playing a fictionalized version of herself, told Charli in one of the most-memorable parts of her mockumentary film The Moment , which came out back in January. Whether that was meant to be delivered with sincerity or irony, it certainly carries some level of poignancy of how Charli has operated since Brat summer started. Related Stories Movies Venice Chief Alberto Barbera on Hollywood's Festival Retreat, Gender Parity Backslide and the AI Question TV 'A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms' Creator Gets Candid on Season 2: "It's Been a F***ing Bastard" She released Brat’ s deluxe version three days after the original album drop, then the Brat and It’s Completely Different but Also Still Brat remix album in October. She embarked on two headlining arena tours — the Sweat Tour with Troye Sivan, and her eponymous Brat Tour. She’s had roles in seven different feature films: The Moment, where she starred and produced, as well as 100 Nights of Hero , Sacrifice , Erupcja , I Want Your Sex, The Gallerist and Faces of Death. She also created the soundtrack for Wuthering Heights and co-wrote the soundtrack for the Anne Hathaway-starring Mother Mary with Jack Antonoff. That exhaustive resume alone certainly puts Charli firmly in contention as one of Hollywood’s hardest working stars, and with Music, Fashion, Film officially here, that’s not stopping any time soon. Charli is ramping up for another extensive tour, with festival headlining dates at Lollapalooza, Outside Lands and Reading and Leeds over the next month, then more arena dates starting in the fall. “I was really, really ready to peace out and take a break and not make music,” she told Rolling Stone in the magazine’s June cover story. “I felt very creatively drained and not inspired to write anything new. Then suddenly, inspiration came.” Charli started the Music, Fashion, Film era seeking to distance herself from the dance floors where Brat held court, declaring that “the dance floor is dead” on the more polarizing lead single “Rock Music.” She followed that with the vibey, synth-y “SS26,” the equally summery, cheekier “Wink Wink,” and most-recent single “Camera,” which featured a music video starring Vincent Cassel. With Music, Fashion, Film firmly in focus, the next few months present an interesting chapter into how Charli enters her most-anticipated era to date. Brat turned Charli XCX from niche iconoclast to mainstream icon. It’d be tempting to milk that well dry — it’s hard to imagine any artist replicating the moment Charli created with Brat anytime soon — but she’s never been one to dwell too long on the past with her work. As she told Rolling Stone in June: “I knew when I was making it that I was never going to make that record again. It’s not creatively rewarding for me to make the same thing twice.” THR

articles.title: Chris Affleck, Mother of Oscar Winners Ben and Casey Affleck, Dies at 83
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 23, 2026 9:21pm Chris Anne Affleck and Ben Affleck. Getty Chris Anne Affleck, the mother of Oscar winners Ben Affleck and Casey Affleck , died June 2, her family announced . She was 83 and diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in December. Christine Anne Boldt was born in New York City in December 1942. She was a graduate of Harvard University and spent 35 years as a public school teacher. She retired in 2008 and was a fierce civil rights advocate throughout her life, having served as one of the original freedom riders who went into the Deep South during the 1960s. Chris and her ex-husband Timothy Affleck welcomed their first child, Ben, in 1972. Ben’s brother, Casey, was born in 1975, around the time their family relocated to Massachusetts, where she continued her teaching career. Related Stories TV Mary Kate Golding, 'The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel' Set Decorator, Dies at 34 in Stabbing Lifestyle Anne Russell, Actress in 'Hello, Dolly!' and 'Mame,' Dies at 103 “My mother taught public school, went to Harvard and then got her master’s there and taught fifth and sixth grade in a public school,” Ben told The Hollywood Reporter in 2012. “My dad had a more working-class lifestyle. He didn’t go to college. He was an auto mechanic and a bartender and a janitor at Harvard.” By the time Ben was 12, his parents divorced. As his passion for entertainment grew during his adolescence, Chris played a hand in his early industry beginnings, connecting her son with her former Harvard roommate, casting director Patty Collins, who helped him audition for commercials and TV movies. From left: Chris Affleck, Ben Affleck, Matt Damon and his mother, Nancy Carlson-Paige, at the 70th Academy Awards. Jim Smeal/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images She was an avid supporter of her sons’ acting careers and attended the 1998 Oscars alongside Ben and Matt Damon, who also brought his mother as his date, after the pair were nominated for best original screenplay for Good Will Hunting — a film the duo also starred in alongside Casey. Ben and Damon would go on to win the Oscar, and the film has become a classic. “We were sitting next to our moms and we won, and we kind of hugged our moms. I remember how everyone had made such a big thing out of it as if this was such a novelty,” Ben told Vanity Fair of the moment. “I remember thinking, being insecure, like, ‘Why? Why is it weird that we’re bringing our moms?’ Who else do you think we would bring?” Casey Affleck and his mom attended the ‘Committed’ premiere in April 2000. Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images Ben would go on to win his second Oscar, for best picture, for Argo in 2012. Casey would win the best actor Oscar in 2017 for his performance in Kenneth Lonergan’s Manchester by the Sea . Chris was given six months to live in December, and her greatest wish after her diagnosis was seeing grandson Atticus graduate high school, her family said. She attended the event with her family on May 31 and died peacefully in her sleep two days later. In addition to her sons, survivors include her five grandchildren: Casey’s kids, Atticus and Indiana, and Ben’s kids, Violet, Fin and Sam. THR

articles.title: Casey Wasserman’s Exit Plan: New Owner of The Team May Be Same As Its Last One
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Erik Hayden Plus Icon Erik Hayden Executive Editor, Business Erik_Hayden Follow Sign Up View All July 24, 2026 3:03am Casey Wasserman Andreas Rentz/Getty Images Casey Wasserman may soon be no longer on The Team. After being pressured to set up an auction for his Westwood-based firm that drew interest from United Talent Agency, Patrick Whitesell’s upstart shingle WIN and other suitors, the sale of his company may not go to any outside party. Wasserman is in talks to sell his stake in the company to private equity firm Providence Equity Partners, Matthew Belloni reported at Puck on Thursday. Providence had already taken a major stake in Wasserman in November 2022 to fuel growth at the company — notably, a major acquisition of Brillstein Entertainment less than a year later — so a buyout of the company’s founder would keep the firm in the same strategic hands it had been in for the past several years. The news of a would-be deal breakthrough arrives three months after the first round of bids were submitted in April to investment bank Moelis & Co, which handled the auction process. (The bank’s leader, Ken Moelis, sits on Wasserman’s LA28 Olympics Committee board). Providence, a source previously told The Hollywood Reporter , had put pressure on the mogul after a wave of headlines and an artist rebellion followed Wasserman being named in a tranche of Department of Justice documents related to convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein and accomplice Ghislane Maxwell in late January. More than 20 artists said they were dropping Wasserman during the height of the February scandal — including Laufey, Chappell Roan, Best Coast and John Summit — and the firm’s social pages were deluged with calls for talent to distance themselves from the mogul. In an email to employees in February, Wasserman conceded “I have become a distraction” to the company’s business. Immediately following Wasserman’s surprise reveal at the time that he was selling his namesake firm, Providence issued a statement on Feb. 14 backing company president Mike Watts and saying, “We remain fully committed to investing in its growth, expanding its capabilities across sports, music, and entertainment, and supporting the extraordinary talent, brands, and properties the Company is proud to represent.” The DoJ documents showed that in 2003, Wasserman and Maxwell exchanged a series of flirtatious messages, though nothing criminal was mentioned in those emails. Wasserman had also, along with Bill Clinton, Chris Tucker and Kevin Spacey, flown on Epstein’s private jet on what was said to be a 2002 AIDS research trip to Africa. The mogul apologized at the time, saying on Jan. 31, “I deeply regret my correspondence with Ghislaine Maxwell which took place over two decades ago, long before her horrific crimes came to light. I never had a personal or business relationship with Jeffrey Epstein.” Wasserman — which rebranded as The Team in March in order to distance itself from its founder (it used to market itself as “Team Wass”) — is one of the biggest players in the sports space. As pro athletes have taken a greater share of the entertainment economy, sports is now one of the most sought after areas in the representation landscape. Wasserman’s sports division generated $266 million in revenue in 2024, 29 percent of the company’s total revenue, an S&P Global report from June of last year detailed. That’s second in Hollywood only to CAA’s sports division, which generated $578 million that year. Providence had invested in Wasserman after taking the place of prior investors RedBird Capital and Madrone Capital Partners. Those firms took ownership stakes in sports teams — football club AC Milan and the NFL’s Denver Broncos — and thus couldn’t own a stake in a sports talent representation firm. In addition to sports, The Team is also home to a notable music agency group built from its 2021 acquisition of Paradigm’s music division, as well as production-management firm Brillstein, a marketing services unit and more properties. Since founding Wasserman in 2002, the company has rolled up multiple creative firms as well as boutique agencies and had 4,000 employees as of earlier this year. As he navigates his exit from management, Wasserman also serves as the chair for LA28, which is organizing Los Angeles’ 2028 Olympics game plan. While city officials, including Mayor Karen Bass, have called upon Wasserman to step down from his high-profile role managing the games over the Maxwell emails, they have deferred to the LA28 board, which has backed Wasserman. In February, LA28 said it hired an outside law firm to investigate Wasserman’s correspondence with Maxwell and it found his “relationship with Epstein and Maxwell did not go beyond what has already been publicly documented.” THR

articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Co-Creator Bill Prady Explains the Science Behind the Show’s Multiverse
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 6:00pm PT ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Co-Creator Bill Prady Explains the Science Behind the Show’s Multiverse By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Co-Creator Bill Prady Explains the Science Behind the Show’s Multiverse 10 hours ago Shaking Up the Emmys By Moving Five Categories Out of the Telecast Might Not Work, But at Least the TV Academy Is Trying Something 12 hours ago ‘Breaking Bad’ Star Giancarlo Esposito Signs With UTA for Representation (EXCLUSIVE) 17 hours ago See All HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers from the series premiere of “ Stuart Fails to Save the Universe ,” now streaming on HBO Max. HBO Max’s “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” opens in a post-apocalyptic Pasadena, an alternative world where zombie hands poke out of the ground, giant moths terrorize, random tears in reality serve as vacuum portals to unknown parts of the galaxy and survivors barter with their last remaining canned goods. Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' About the only thing still operating is the comic book shop run by Stuart Bloom (played by Kevin Sussman ), where the gang on “The Big Bang Theory” would sometimes hang out. But even that store is no longer normal, as geeky fights among patrons quickly turn deadly. It’s not a great place, so when another Stuart from a different dimension arrives, so begins our main character’s quest to save the universe. Popular on Variety According to Alt Stuart, it was “The Big Bang Theory” characters Leonard, Sheldon and Howard who built a quantum interference device that caused reality to be altered. Regular Stuart and Bert (Brian Posehn) embark on a quest to find the device at Cal Tech — and along the way, reconnect with Denise (Lauren Lapkus) and discover that Kripke (John Ross Bowie) has turned into an evil gang leader controlling much of the San Gabriel Valley. They also find Raj (Kunal Nayyar), who’s been imprisoned by Kripke for quite some time and is looking to help them fix the device. They’re all captured, but Bert uses his geology expertise to create bombs with rocks and water — and they make it to the device. All is saved, until Kripke kills Raj — and the device then activates, taking Stuart, Bert and Kripke to another universe. So how much of the show’s multiverse can be explained by science? Sussman credits co-creator Bill Prady with having a handle on where the science works. “There’s a bunch of quantum physics involved in the show, and Bill is an expert on quantum physics theory,” Sussman says. “You can get away with a lot because at the end of the day, it is theory. It’s popular theory, but it’s legit. So I would ask him a question like, ‘how can my character be here and be there at the same time?’ And I had an epiphany at one point when I realized, oh wait, so it’s not just parallel universes — it’s parallel universes with a little time travel mixed in!” Sussman says there were points while filming the show where it would help to understand the quantum physics theory behind what was happening in a particular scene. “I look forward to people on Reddit trying to dissect what’s happening because I know that all of it can be argued,” he adds. “I would try to poke holes in it on set, and Bill always walked me through. ‘No, see, the reason why this does make sense is A, B and C.’” Prady explains that the device that Leonard, Sheldon and Howard built seems to have shifted the primary characters to a universe with a separate, distinct history that has an apocalyptic event that occurs sometime after “The Big Bang Theory” and before we meet them. “The Einsteinian issue that time is a fourth dimension comes into play here,” he says. “Because when the device malfunctions, it alters reality, but it creates a new past as well. So when we meet them in the first episode, the apocalypse is some years ago, and that’s a result of the alteration. Both the past and present and the future are altered from what they should have been.” So then the question is, when the characters move between universes, does the universe they left still exist, or is it being restructured? “That is ambiguous, and they don’t know, and we don’t know,” he says. For example — now that Kripke has killed Raj, that doesn’t seem good right? But in Episode 2, he will point out that either the universe they just left doesn’t exist anymore, in which case he didn’t kill Raj because that Raj never existed, or that they’re we are dealing with an infinite number of universes, and so he just killed one Raj out of an infinite number, which is pretty minor. But “the branching theory of multiverses states essentially that every quantum event that could go one way also could go the other, and at that point there’s a branch, both universes exist side by side… The theory is that the universe branches at every decision point, so there’s a rapidly growing, infinite number of universes. That gets into the very annoying realization that some infinities are bigger than other infinities, which is mathematically true and conceptually uncomfortable. But it would state that from the point of the Big Bang, the number of infinite parallel universes increases with every moment that the universe ticks by. So that was kind of the science and pseudoscience that sort of lays this out.” Prady jokingly adds: “How useless is that?” But it’s a reminder that “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” may be science-fiction, but it’s still grounded in some ways. “When I was teaching at USC, and somebody had a project that involved fantasy elements, I’d say, the most important rule in writing fantasy is that the rules you create for your fantasy have to be as real as the laws of physics. They have to be consistent, and they always have to be the same,” he says. Prady uses “Bewitched” as an example, with its arbitrary rule that only the witch who casts the spell can remove it. “It’s based on nothing, but it keeps every ‘Bewitched’ episode from being three minutes long,” he says. “Because without that rule, Endora would give Darrin donkey ears, and Samantha would remove them, and we’d be done. Now, can your universe be raggedy around the edges? 100%. And that’s ‘Doctor Who.’ The rules are there, but sometimes they don’t quite work out, and the Doctor will explain.” In the case of multiverses, the parameters of what we think of as the “multiverse” has been cemented in pop culture by Marvel films, “Rick and Morty,” “Dark Matter” and more. “I think the reason that you wind up with multiverses with similar stories is that the notion that multiverses exist mathematically. Things like string theory and stuff touch on that. So you can build off of what has sort of percolated through the general consciousness.” Prady notes that not all of it makes sense, and he’s proud of the fact that the characters will acknowledge that. “A guy online did a scientific analysis of what must be happening in this, and where he explains all the various scientific multiverse theories that we are clearly drawing from,” Prady says. “It was thick, thick science. It does state that there’s an infinite number of multiverses. So clearly, we should send that article to HBO Max and say, ‘look, there’s a scientific basis for additional seasons!’” Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired ‘March of Giants’ Game ‘Every Year After’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon; Will Focus on Charlie’s Story From ‘One Golden Summer’ Sequel Book Prime Day Deal: Amazon’s New ‘Framed’ Ember Artline 4K TV Is on Sale for Its Lowest Price Ever Amazon Signs Wide-Ranging Deal With Kevin Durant and Rich Kleiman’s Boardroom Spanning Podcasts, Live Events and More Tubi to Provide Creatorverse Lineup to Amazon’s Fire TV (EXCLUSIVE) Amazon Teams With Papa Johns, Beck, Jill Scott, Omar Courtz for New Alexa Ads Using Agentic AI Loading comments... articles.title: Creepy Twins, Religious Fanaticism and a Loaded Gun Collide in Tense Chamber Drama ‘Godhead’ — Fantasia
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 6:41pm PT Creepy Twins, Religious Fanaticism and a Loaded Gun Collide in Tense Chamber Drama ‘Godhead’ — Fantasia By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Creepy Twins, Religious Fanaticism and a Loaded Gun Collide in Tense Chamber Drama ‘Godhead’ — Fantasia 8 hours ago ‘I’ve Been Scammed Left and Right’: Demand for ‘Odyssey’ Tickets Gives Rise to Sketchy Scalpers 3 days ago Variety Interview Studio Presented by Google TV Returns to San Diego 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Fantasia Festival Mark H. Rapaport’s new film “ Godhead ” is a master-class in ratcheting up tension. Shot in black-and-white with camerawork that makes the audience feel like a voyeur uncovering perverse secrets, the film blends faith, sex, lies and discomfort into an unknowable dance between its leads. The premise begins simply: A rural Catholic priest (Al Warren) is visited by two bizarre twins (Sarah Coffey and Kimball Farley), who look like an unholy blend of Die Antwoord, Grimes and overcooked ravers. They believe they are part of a prophecy and need the priest’s help to fulfill it. They also have a gun. And the priest has a young boy (Luke Speakman) that he seems to keep captive indoors … Related Stories Sky Yang Signs With Range Media Partners (EXCLUSIVE) To say more would ruin the film’s twists and turns, which were met enthusiastically at its world premiere screenings at Montreal’s genre-focused Fantasia Festival this week. Popular on Variety Rapaport, whose well-received 2023 debut feature “Hippo” also premiered at Fantasia, spoke with Variety about his choice to do another film in black and white, how “Godhead” takes aim at crooked authority figures and leaving the audience with challenging questions. What inspired you to develop this story? I always find that in life I come up against authority figures in a way that feels unfair. I often am too nice to people, and I think I have a little bit of second-born’s gullibility. As I grow up and hopefully become a dad, I’m trying to shed that. I think in this movie, I was able to put a finger on that feeling of being aware of the hypocrite or the manipulator. From childhood until adulthood, you have your religious figures, you have your family, you have your bosses. I’m always a very trusting person, and so I found that there’s real horror in that. This movie, although framed as a Hitchcockian thriller of sorts, is really a canvas for me to explore those frustrations. With a film like this that has a twisty plot, how are you able to balance disseminating information to the audience without overexplaining and giving them easy answers? It’s a tough tightrope to walk. I hope I’m able to do that successfully by staying with the characters first and being able to feel with them, and writing the script from their intentions and their heart, and not letting the plot of a horror film take over the greater emotional core. Of course, we do go there and go to dark places and twist and turn, but I try to always bring it back to the characters. I always can do better finding that humanity. There are plenty of dark moments in this film. How did you determine how bleak versus hopeful you ultimately wanted your work to be? It’s funny, there was another version of the ending where it was a massive, obvious F-you to all of these evil characters. I was talking to Al Warren, who plays the priest beautifully and with so much real emotion, and he got me thinking about the end beat. Without spoiling it, he said, “Let’s think about where this could go if you, as the director, practiced forgiveness,” and I found that in doing that I actually ended up with a much more horrifying ending than had I brought the hammer down on his character. I think there’s an eeriness to forgiveness as well, in that the ultimate manipulation is forgiving your manipulator. I wouldn’t mind if the audience felt maybe characters made the wrong decision at the end. That just keeps the question going, because the movie at its core is a question for the audience, less than an answer. In my old version, I tried to provide the answer, and it just wasn’t satisfying. So it was a real exercise in reeling back that sword that the director wields. That’s where we ended up. What was the creative choice to shoot in black and white instead of color? It was my instinct off the bat just because my first film was in black and white and it was such a fun, beautiful little film. People loved the black and white. It felt like a different world. And so it started as a, “Well, if it’s not broke, don’t fix it.” My brain was thinking in black and white. But of course, you need the narrative to deserve black and white. As I started to write the script, I just couldn’t see it any other way. I was very much into Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse.” He makes a ton of great movies, but this three-hander … I wanted to place us in some sort of timeless world. It felt black and white was an effective way to do that. In addition to the beauty of the shadows and the moodiness that it’s able to convey, there’s how it relates to the themes of good and evil, right and wrong, truth and untruth. I had a full-circle moment in writing the script where there’s a gray area that I put in there, because, even though it’s in black and white, it potentially concludes on a gray area, which to me is the most horrifying area of all. We all want to know: Are we black or white? Are we right or wrong? When I was able to think of it as a spectrum and not just black and white, it opened up a whole new visual language for me. Alief is representing “Godhead” for worldwide sales as it searches for distribution. Watch the “Godhead” teaser trailer below. articles.title: ‘Sia: Nostalgic for the Present’ Review: A Concert Performance Film from 2016, but It Channels Sia’s Mystery and Power
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 8:25pm PT ‘Sia: Nostalgic for the Present’ Review: A Concert Performance Film from 2016, but It Channels Sia’s Mystery and Power Made for her tour from a decade ago, it's a dance-video projection of Sia's greatest hits. It makes you wish that she'd craft another one. By Owen Gleiberman Plus Icon Owen Gleiberman Chief Film Critic @OwenGleiberman Latest ‘Sia: Nostalgic for the Present’ Review: A Concert Performance Film from 2016, but It Channels Sia’s Mystery and Power 7 hours ago ‘Summer Tour’ Review: A Documentary About Deadheads That’s as Blissed-Out and Navel-Gazing as Its Subjects 3 days ago ‘Manhunter: The Final Cut’ Shows Why Director’s Cuts Are Almost Never an Improvement. But It’s Still the Greatest Thriller of Our Time 5 days ago See All Courtesy of Trafalgar Releasing When Lady Gaga first ascended to supernova celebrity, with the release of “The Fame” in 2008, there was a time when she kept her face hidden — under the elaborate masks she wore in videos, and even in interviews, for which she would also show up masked. It was a highly elaborate act of camouflage, but the ruse worked. She was only 22, yet she created an aura of mystery around herself, conjuring “Lady Gaga” as a larger-than-life character. (When you heard that she was really Stefani Germanotta from New York City, you would think: Really, who is that?) Related Stories Sky Yang Signs With Range Media Partners (EXCLUSIVE) Sia , born in Australia 10 years before Lady Gaga, had a career that predated hers as well. But by the time Sia hit her solo stride in the late 2000s, she didn’t simply borrow from the Gaga mask playbook. She concealed her face to the point that the mystery became part of who she was. “ Sia: Nostalgic for the Present ,” which opens tomorrow and is showing in select theaters for a limited run, is a performance film that was originally created for Sia’s 2016 Nostalgic for the Present tour, and in the entire movie you never once see Sia’s face. Popular on Variety She’s right there in front of us, standing and singing on a platform at stage left, hidden under a half-blonde, half-black wig with bangs that hang down to her lips. There’s an oversize white bow on top of the wig, and she wears a white dress that resembles a nurse’s uniform from the early ’60s. Sia’s greatest songs, like “Unstoppable” and “Titanium” and “The Greatest,” are anthems of strength, power, fortitude, invincibility, and watching the movie it’s fascinating to behold how her facelessness feeds that quality. She’s an abstract figure, a pair of lips singing, and this creates the sensation that the power she’s singing about doesn’t emanate from her. She’s channeling a force larger than herself — the rising specter of feminine triumph. She’s merely the vessel. I’m not entirely sure what the two-tone wig means (the duality of woman?), but everyone in the movie wears a version of it: the dancers, the actors (Kristen Wiig, Paul Dano, Ben Mendelsohn, Gaby Hoffman) who each appear in one dance video, as well as the choreographer, costume designer, and offstage crew members. They’re all wearing the wig, which looks like the fabled New York black-and-white cookie turned into a fashion emblem of talismanic power. “Sia: Nostalgic for the Present” is basically a 75-minute-long series of dance videos that were designed to be projected onstage during the tour, as the live performers mirrored the movements in the videos. The featured star is, of course, Maddie Ziegler, the whirling dervish of a child dancer who pranced and flung and gyrated her way through three celebrated Sia music videos; she was 14 when the Nostalgic for the Present tour unfolded. This weekend, if you go to “Sia: Nostalgic for the Present,” what you’re seeing is a 10-year-old movie (and a promotional one at that), so it’s severely lacking in the shock of the new. There’s no getting around the fact that it’s a greatest-hits compendium. But though Sia’s last major hit was a decade ago, she had such an intuitive gift for crafting powerfully infectious pop songs that it’s hard to understand why she hit a wall. I think it might have had something to do with the mask/wig/hiding thing. Pop stars, especially the ones who have extended careers, are people who have a primal desire to put themselves out there. Whereas Sia clearly had a primal ambivalence about that. She was a camera-shy exhibitionist. In “Nostalgic for the Present,” her voice is commanding, ringing out with those soul inflections that make her sound like Amy Winehouse if Winehouse were being produced by Giorgio Moroder. The dance performance that’s at the heart of the film is the sort of thing that felt transgressive back then, but now it looks like something out of a 2010s nostalgia reel. Maddie Ziegler, who was born in Pittsburgh and got her start on “Dance Moms,” flings her body around with a kind of airy gymnastic aggression, and she specializes in facial contortions meant to express the underlying ferocity of Sia’s music (and are sometimes just there as psycho flourishes to mess with the audience). Ziegler is like a mime crossed with Daryl Hannah in “Blade Runner,” but there’s also a touch of Sid Vicious to the way that she’ll mug and curl her lips like a teenage brat who’s gone off her meds. The hits remain sublime. I retain a special adoration for “Chandelier,” a song of hedonistic assertion and underlying ambivalence that, for me, is filtered through its brilliant use as the centerpiece of the Broadway version of “Moulin Rouge!” I’m writing about Sia as if she had gone away, but as someone who loves her music, I see no reason on earth why she couldn’t now enjoy a comeback as ferocious as the one that Gaga had with “Abracadabra.” She wouldn’t even need to come out from behind the wig; that would play like gangbusters on the Grammys. But she’d have to rouse herself to do what she used to do: create a dance hook as shiny and fierce and glorious as titanium. ‘Sia: Nostalgic for the Present’ Review: A Concert Performance Film from 2016, but It Channels Sia’s Mystery and Power Reviewed at Regal Union Square, New York, July 23, 2026. Running time: 75 MIN. Production: A Trafalgar Releasing release of a Monkey Puzzle production, in association with Radical Media, Collider, and Serial Pictures. Producer: Jason Baum. Executive producers: Sia, Jonathan Daniel, David Russell, Jennifer Heath, Daniel Askill, Sara Greco. Crew: Directors: Sia, Daniel Askill. Camera: Bobby Shore. Editor: Lorin Askill. Music: Sia. With: Sia, Maddie Ziegler, Nick Lanzisera, Stephanie Mincone, Wyatt Rocker, Paul Dano, Gaby Hoffman, Ben Mendelsohn, Tig Notaro, Kristen Wiig. articles.title: Director Na Hong-Jin Makes Comic-Con Debut With Frightening New ‘Hope’ Footage, Says Casting Hoyeon Was His ‘Best Decision’
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 8:27pm PT Director Na Hong-Jin Makes Comic-Con Debut With Frightening New ‘Hope’ Footage, Says Casting Hoyeon Was His ‘Best Decision’ By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Director Na Hong-Jin Makes Comic-Con Debut With Frightening New ‘Hope’ Footage, Says Casting Hoyeon Was His ‘Best Decision’ 6 hours ago Johnny Depp Makes Surprise Comic-Con Appearance as Ebenezer Scrooge 12 hours ago The Roku Channel Expands Partnership With Create the Writers Room Initiative by Streaming ‘Five Film Fridays’ Selections 18 hours ago See All Getty Images South Korean director Na Hong-Jin made his San Diego Comic-Con debut to preview his latest film, Neon’s alien action movie “ Hope .” Before the action auteur took the stage in Ballroom 20, a sizzle reel of his previous work — from his 2008 debut “The Chaser” to “The Yellow Sea” and “The Wailing,” all set to Ozzy Osbourne’s “Crazy Train” — played for the rapt audience. Related Stories Sky Yang Signs With Range Media Partners (EXCLUSIVE) “Hope,” Na said, “is a continuation in terms of the same metaphor and the same meaning, but in terms of the style and the thought and the content is completely different. Any assumptions you have about my premises and my previous work, I would advise them to completely abandon it before [this one].” “Hope” is set in the remote village of Hope Harbor, where a mysterious creature has wreaked havoc. Police and local hunters set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But not all is as it seems. Popular on Variety The alien action movie stars Hoyeon , who broke out internationally thanks to her Emmy-nominated turn in Netflix’s “Squid Game.” Na said was one of the best decisions he made in bringing the film, a 10 year passion project, to the big screen. Hwang Jung-min, who leads the international cast, recommended Hoyeon for the role of a tenacious police officer. “He said that if you meet her, you realize how special of a person she is,” Na said, explaining that he immediately set up a meeting. The director and star read the script while eating takeout and she quickly signed on for the role. “The funny thing is: Hwang Jung-min actually has never met her, or didn’t even know her very well.” Hoyeon appeared in a special video message to introduce two clips that would play exclusively for the Comic-Con crowd. The first is a tense sequence where Hwang as he and a group of men shoot their way through the wreckage of their town — only to finally come face to face with the gigantic alien preying upon them. The second was an extended look at a chase scene where one character played by must leap from his horse into the police car — all while being chased down the highway by one of the fanged creatures. After the pulse-pounding clips ended, director Na revealed that these weren’t the most difficult scenes to shoot: That honor belongs to another chase scene with the characters fleeing through the forest on horseback. Na also praised Hoeyon’s performance in another scene and shared she spent six months learning to drive a manual stick-shift car. “After six months, she reached a point where she could perform those drafts at very different, difficult angles too,” he said. “So she was driving the car and doing all the performance herself, and I think the word ‘difficult’ is not enough to describe what was going on in that scene. My DP and I almost died of anxiety just watching her.” Speaking of dying, during the Q&A portion of the panel, Na teased that “90%” of the characters in the film might perish… but he won’t reveal who. The exchange got a roar of laughter from the crowd. “Hope,” which also stars Michael Fassbender, Alicia Vikander, Taylor Russell and Cameron Britton, premiered in competition at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, where it electrified audiences. Neon hopes to replicate that same success when releasing the film in the U.S. on Sept. 9. In Cannes, Na revealed that he had plans for a sequel. “I think you can readily imagine this sequel. And there’s a script that’s already been done that I’d like to shoot,” he said during his Cannes press conference. “So if I have the opportunity, I would indeed make a sequel if possible.” Carole Radziwill Confronted About Jeffrey Epstein Connection in ‘RHONY’ Season 16 Trailer: ‘You Think I’m Part of an International Sex-Trafficking Ring?’ The Pulitzer Prize-Winning Journalist Who Has the Entire NBA Spooked Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Jumbo’ Sequel, ‘Queen of Malacca’ Franchise Plans on the Cards as Indonesia’s Visinema Eyes Expansion (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 12:02am PT ‘Jumbo’ Sequel, ‘Queen of Malacca’ Franchise Plans on the Cards as Indonesia’s Visinema Eyes Expansion (EXCLUSIVE) By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Anurag Kashyap, MIFFest Jury President, Searches for ‘a New Cinematic Language’ 3 days ago APOS 2026 Takeaways: IP, Sport, AI Define Asia’s New Content Era 1 month ago ReelShort Looks Beyond Microdramas as Joey Jia Pushes for a New Entertainment Ecosystem 1 month ago See All MIFFest Indonesian filmmaker and Visinema founder Angga Dwimas Sasongko is targeting the first quarter of 2027 for the release of “ Queen of Malacca ,” as the Southeast Asian fantasy epic moves through post-production and attracts interest from potential distribution partners in China, Thailand and other international markets. The project has drawn growing industry attention since Blue Finch Films boarded worldwide sales . “We are currently in discussions with potential distribution partners,” Sasongko tells Variety during the Malaysia International Film Festival ( MIFFest ) in Kuala Lumpur. “It will definitely become the next franchise for Visinema.” Related Stories Sky Yang Signs With Range Media Partners (EXCLUSIVE) “Queen of Malacca” marks Sasongko’s return to directing after a two-year break and is one of the most ambitious productions of his career. “I spent eight years building this fantasy world,” he says. “It combines Southeast Asian martial arts, supernatural elements and extensive visual effects. It’s like creating a universe – a mosaic of modern life inspired by regional mythology and traditions.” Popular on Variety More than a standalone feature, Sasongko sees “Queen of Malacca” as the cornerstone of Visinema’s strategy to develop locally rooted IP with international appeal. Beyond “Queen of Malacca,” Visinema is preparing five films for release in 2027 while developing an animation pipeline extending through 2030. The slate includes a superhero action-comedy animated feature slated for 2028, a sequel to the family IP “Nussa” and a follow-up to its animated blockbuster “ Jumbo ,” one of Indonesia’s biggest box office hits of all time. “For Visinema, international collaboration isn’t simply about securing more financing – it’s about expanding together,” Sasongko says. “Since 2018, we’ve generally limited external investment in our projects to below 40%, because we look at what strategic partners can contribute beyond capital.” Those partners include media companies, foreign producers and distributors that can provide market access, industry expertise and long-term strategic value. Visinema is also looking to deepen relationships across mainland China, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines. For Sasongko, creative ambition and commercial potential should go hand in hand. The goal, he says, is to build stories with a distinctive local identity while creating the partnerships and long-term IP needed to reach audiences across the region. articles.title: Jon Bon Jovi Ends Madison Square Garden Show Early Due to Sinus Infection: ‘We’ll Figure Out How to Reschedule’
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 2:05am PT Jon Bon Jovi Ends Madison Square Garden Show Early Due to Sinus Infection: ‘We’ll Figure Out How to Reschedule’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Jon Bon Jovi Ends Madison Square Garden Show Early Due to Sinus Infection: ‘We’ll Figure Out How to Reschedule’ 2 hours ago Venice Film Festival Lineup: Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime,’ Martin McDonagh’s ‘Wild Horse Nine,’ Oasis Reunion Doc and More 1 day ago Joel Courtney to Star in and Produce Thriller ‘Echo,’ TikTok Creator Zac Stracener’s Feature Directorial Debut (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Getty Images for Bon Jovi Bon Jovi ‘s penultimate show of their Madison Square Garden residency came to an early end on Thursday night after frontman Jon Bon Jovi revealed he was suffering from a sinus infection. About 90 minutes into the set, Bon Jovi told the crowd that he would have to stop the show as he wasn’t feeling his best. “I haven’t talked to anybody about anything, but don’t throw away your ticket stubs,” Bon Jovi said, according to fan video . “I’m going to figure something out, OK? Just hold onto them, we’ll figure out how to reschedule. But I’m going to have to cool it for the night.” Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' He ended the show by saying, “I’ll see you again soon.” Popular on Variety A rep for the band told People : “Jon Bon Jovi spoke from stage and told fans he has been battling a sinus infection which led to the show’s early ending. As part of the Bon Jovi residency at Madison Square Garden, Jon has said numerous times that it has been a joy to return to live shows for the band. Updated information will be available shortly.” Bon Jovi underwent vocal cord surgery in 2022, which prevented frequent live performances. The “Forever” tour, which includes the Madison Square Garden shows as well as upcoming dates in the U.K. and Ireland, marks the band’s first major tour since his surgery. “I’m deeply grateful that the fans and the brotherhood of this band have been patient and allowed me the time needed to get healthy and prepare for touring,” Bon Jovi said when the tour was announced. Bon Jovi’s last Madison Square Garden show of the “Forever” tour is scheduled for Sunday, after which the band will head across the pond to play Edinburgh on Aug. 28, Dublin on Aug. 30 and two dates at London’s Wembley Stadium on Sept. 4 and 6. articles.title: Luxbox Acquires Documentary ‘Life of Jorge Luis Borges’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 2:34am PT Luxbox Acquires Documentary ‘Life of Jorge Luis Borges’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Luxbox Acquires Documentary ‘Life of Jorge Luis Borges’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Venice Horizons Opener ‘The Girl With the Leica’ Boarded by Fandango Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago Venice-Bound Serbian Protest Drama ‘Until the Day Ends’ Boarded by Heretic (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago See All Courtesy of El Pampero Cine Luxbox Films has acquired the world sales rights to Mariano Llinás ‘ epic five-and-a-half -hour documentary “Life of Jorge Luis Borges,” which will world premiere at the Venice Film Festival in the Open – Non-Fiction section. The film forms a biography of Argentine writer and poet Jorge Luis Borges, working from an exhaustive review of the papers he left, the books he read, and the places he went to. Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' The film is also “an attempt to decipher a very peculiar life: someone who lived like a hidden, underground warrior, whose cause was literature, literature conceived as a kingdom and as a landscape,” according to a statement. Popular on Variety “If Cold War spies fought from their desks or from an uninhabited house to defend their half of the world, Borges strove from a library to elevate and broaden the territories of his own tribe: the people for whom the most important part of the universe is books, plots and words.” Llinás is perhaps best known for 2018’s “La Flor,” which, ruling out experimental projects or mere cinematic exercises, is the longest film in the history of cinema. Before that, “Balnearios” (2002) and “Historias Extraordinarias” (2008) both had significant festival play. In 2003, he founded with Alejo Moguillansky, Agustín Mendilaharzu and Laura Citarella the group El Pampero Cine. The producers on “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” are Citarella, Ezequiel Pierr, Mendilaharzu, Moguillanksy and Llinás for El Pampero Cine. Llinás is the screenwriter. The DP is Mendilaharzu. The production designer is Ezequiel Pierri, and the editor is Ignacio Codino. Music is by Gabriel Chwojnik. The protagonists include Ernesto Montequín, Nicolás Helft, Laura Paredes, Milva Leonardi and Pablo Dacal.
