articles.title: Sony Pictures Sets Viral X-Inspired Short-Form Thriller ‘Los Hilos del Miedo’ at Prime Video Spain (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 3:01am PT Sony Pictures Sets Viral X-Inspired Short-Form Thriller ‘Los Hilos del Miedo’ at Prime Video Spain (EXCLUSIVE) The eight-part psychological thriller builds on a mobile-first pilot that generated 28.4 million views on TikTok By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest Sony Pictures Sets Viral X-Inspired Short-Form Thriller ‘Los Hilos del Miedo’ at Prime Video Spain (EXCLUSIVE) 43 minutes ago Studio STIM, Behind ‘The Girl in the Clouds,´Sets Canary Islands Operation, Planning to Create More Than 100 Jobs 1 day ago Spain’s SETT Invests $7.3 Million in New Canary Islands Animation Company Amuse Labs 1 week ago See All Courtesy of Sony Pictures International Productions Spain Sony Pictures International Productions’ Spanish operation is moving into short-form fiction with “Los Hilos del Miedo,” an eight-part psychological suspense series set to launch on Prime Video in Spain . Running approximately five minutes per episode, the production marks the division’s first short-form series and draws on stories by Spanish writer Salvador Gutiérrez Solís that went viral on X, captivating millions of readers across Spain and Latin America. Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' The series builds on “El Garaje,” a mobile-first pilot that generated 28.4 million total views, more than 262,000 likes and nearly 300,000 interactions on TikTok, according to Sony Pictures. Popular on Variety Inspired by the everyday-horror atmosphere of Gutiérrez Solís’ suspense stories, “Los Hilos del Miedo” is designed to translate digitally native storytelling into a premium audiovisual format while retaining the speed and immediacy of its social-media origins. The project also extends Sony Pictures International Productions’ collaboration with Madrid-based TAI Arts University School, integrating members of its international community of young creators into the series’ technical and artistic production. The partnership positions “Los Hilos del Miedo” as both a commercial production and a talent-development initiative, offering some TAI participants their first professional industry experience. “At Sony Pictures, we are always striving to challenge convention, and we are proud to be innovators in short-form entertainment and to premiere ‘Los Hilos del Miedo’ on Prime Video,” said Iván Losada, managing director of Sony Pictures Entertainment, Spain. Losada said the project demonstrates that “cinematic tension is not tied to traditional running times.” “Bringing Salvador Gutiérrez Solís’ massive viral reach on X into a five-minute episodic format allows us to bridge the gap between successful digital-native content and premium audiovisual production,” he said. Gutiérrez Solís, who publishes under the handle @gutisolis, described the adaptation as an unexpected leap for stories originally conceived for a social network. “It is especially exciting — almost unimaginable — to see these stories that I originally created for a social network end up on a platform with the global reach of Prime Video, alongside one of the most respected production companies in the audiovisual industry, Sony Pictures International Productions, Spain,” he said. The writer also highlighted the involvement of TAI’s young filmmakers, some of whom will gain their first professional experience on the series, and said the project could mark the beginning of a new generation of audiovisual creators. “Los Hilos del Miedo” will join Prime Video’s streaming catalogue in Spain at a date yet to be announced. articles.title: BBC Buys War Drama ‘Kabul,’ Featuring Eric Dane in One of His Last Roles
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 3:15am PT BBC Buys War Drama ‘Kabul,’ Featuring Eric Dane in One of His Last Roles By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest BBC Buys War Drama ‘Kabul,’ Featuring Eric Dane in One of His Last Roles 31 minutes ago ‘Burlesque the Musical’ London Opening Postponed to 2027, U.K. Tour Pushed Back (EXCLUSIVE) 21 hours ago International Cinema Union Criticizes Europe’s Approval of Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘It Has Based Its Decision on Too Narrow a Scope’ 22 hours ago See All Courtesy of BBC The BBC has acquired thriller series “Kabul,” starring the late Eric Dane and “Tehran’s” Shervin Alenabi, from Mediawan Rights. The six-part show , which is against the backdrop of U.S. troops’ withdrawal from Afghanistan amid the Taliban’s return to Kabul, follows the chaotic evacuation of various characters including diplomats, soldiers and civilians. The synopsis reads: “Kabul, August 15, 2021. As American troops withdraw, the Taliban enter the city. The Nazany family, like many civilians, is forced to flee, fearing retaliation. In this desperate and chaotic situation – shadowed by the looming threat of an attack by ISIS – French police officers, Italian diplomats, German military personnel, and American intelligence services must somehow coordinate to manage the influx of civilians. How will each of them manage to save their own lives? The countdown has begun.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' Produced by France’s 24 25 Films and Cinétévé, it also stars Jonathan Zaccaï (“Le bureau des legendes”), Thibault Evrard (“The Night of the 12th”), Vassilis Kukalawi (“Kandahar”), Jeanne Goursaud (“Pax Massilia”), Gianmarco Saurino (“L’estate piu Calda”) and Valentina Cervi (“Medici: Masters of Florence”). The series is directed by Kasia Adamik (“No Escape”) and Olga Chajdas (“Imago”) from a screenplay by Olivier Demangel (“Atlantics,” “November”), Thomas Finkelkraut (“Thomas Finkielkraut”) and Joey Lavy (“The Shift”). “‘Kabul’ is a tragedy of the highest stakes,” said Nick Lee, the BBC’s head of program acquisition. “A warzone story which is propelled by the real ticking clock of the evacuation that was just five years ago this summer. Global politics remain complex, but ‘Kabul’ dramatises the biggest view of history through the smallest window of a human family.” Producers are Fabienne Servan-Schreiber and Charlotte Ortiz at Cinétévé, Matthias Weber and Thibault Gast at 24 25 Films (a Mediawan Company). Sandrine Paquot exec produces. The series was made in collaboration with the European Alliance with Mediawan Rights repping global sales. “Kabul” launches on the BBC’s streaming platform iPlayer on Aug. 2 and will be broadcast on BBC Four from Aug. 15. articles.title: Fred Tsui Named Executive Director of Hong Kong International Film Festival Society
articles.full_text: Jul 24, 2026 3:43am PT Fred Tsui Named Executive Director of Hong Kong International Film Festival Society By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Indian Epic ‘Ramayana’ Lands at Sony Pictures for International Distribution 14 hours ago Venice Lesbian Drama ‘Big Little Things’ Boards Moebius Entertainment for Worldwide Sales 23 hours ago Venice Title ‘The Difficult Bride’ Taps Films Boutique for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 24 hours ago See All Hong Kong International Film Festival Society The Hong Kong International Film Festival Society has appointed Fred Tsui , founder and CEO of Moebius Entertainment , as its new executive director, the organization said Friday. Tsui succeeds Albert Lee and assumes the role Sept. 23, reporting to HKIFFS chair Dr. Wilfred Wong and the board. In the new post, Tsui will oversee the society’s full range of initiatives: its marquee event, the Hong Kong International Film Festival, along with the Hong Kong – Asia Film Financing Forum and its HAF Film Lab, the Summer International Film Festival and the HKIFF Cine Fan strand. Related Stories Justin Baldoni Speaks Out on Blake Lively Legal Battle: 'There Have Been So Many Painful Things That Have Been Spoken Into Existence' Tsui arrives with more than 30 years of experience touching nearly every corner of the business, including distribution, financing, broadcasting, exhibition and media operations alongside international sales and co-production. That range has connected him with filmmakers, financiers, distributors, exhibitors, sales agents and festival programmers across Asia, Europe and North America. Popular on Variety He currently runs Moebius Entertainment as founder and chief executive, having built the outfit into a respected international sales agency for celebrated Asian titles. Under his watch, the company has crafted global sales strategies, lined up distribution deals across major territories and steered festival campaigns for award-winning films. The appointment lands amid an active stretch for Moebius: the company recently boarded worldwide sales for Michelle Zhou’s debut feature “Big Little Things,” selected for the Horizons section of the Venice Film Festival, and picked up sales rights outside Taiwan to Fiona Roan Feng-i’s “Happily Ever After,” set to premiere in the Toronto Film Festival’s Special Presentations section. Before launching Moebius, Tsui spent more than two decades at Media Asia Film, eventually taking charge of the studio’s international sales and co-production division as general manager. In that post, he helped extend one of Hong Kong’s major studios onto the world stage, running its global sales operation and striking co-production deals that boosted Hong Kong cinema’s international profile. Earlier in his career, Tsui held senior roles at PCCW and Asia Television, gaining experience in organizational leadership, media operations, strategic thinking and content oversight. Outside the executive suite, Tsui is also known as a film critic and has sat on juries at festivals including those in Hong Kong, Edinburgh, Jecheon, Tallinn, Seattle, Udine, Sitges, Sonoma and Skip City in Japan. He also sits on the Hong Kong Film Development Council. He also belongs to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) and the Hong Kong Film Critics Society. In past years he sat on the boards of the Independent Film & Television Alliance (IFTA) in the U.S. and the MIA International Audiovisual Market in Rome. The Sitges – International Fantastic Film Festival of Catalonia has honored him with its Maria Honorifica Award. “We are delighted to welcome Fred to HKIFFS,” said Wong. “Fred combines strategic leadership with an exceptional understanding of the international film landscape. Throughout his career, he has built bridges between Hong Kong cinema and the global marketplace while earning the trust and respect of filmmakers, festival directors and industry leaders worldwide. Just as importantly, he approaches cinema from the perspectives of an executive, a critic, a festival juror and a lifelong cinephile. We believe he is uniquely qualified to lead HKIFFS into its next chapter, further strengthening its role as one of Asia’s most important cultural institutions and international film platforms.” HKIFFS operates as a nonprofit, non-governmental charity built around fostering film as art and culture, running the HAF financing forum in tandem with the festival. It launched a monthly Cine Fan repertory strand in 2013 and, in 2021, restructured its industry-facing services into HKIFF Industry, which backs non-mainstream production via co-productions, festival guidance and international distribution under the HKIFF Collection label. “It is a tremendous honor to join HKIFFS, an institution that has played such a pivotal role in the cultural life of Hong Kong and in promoting Asian cinema internationally,” said Tsui. “Having worked with film festivals throughout my career – as a sales executive, producer, juror, critic and audience member – I have seen first-hand the unique role HKIFF plays in connecting filmmakers, the industry and audiences. I look forward to working with the board, our partners and the HKIFFS team to build on the society’s remarkable legacy while broadening its international reach, nurturing new talent, deepening audience engagement and ensuring Hong Kong remains at the forefront of global film culture.” Amazon Signs Wide-Ranging Deal With Kevin Durant and Rich Kleiman’s Boardroom Spanning Podcasts, Live Events and More LISTEN: Mike Hopkins on Prime Video’s Evolution, the Bundling Boom, How MGM Changed Amazon, the Future of Bond and No Regrets on ‘Melania’ Prime Video Launches Games With Luna App Integration; ‘Tomb Raider,’ James Bond Titles Won’t Be in the Mix Luca Guadagnino’s Nearly Finished Sam Altman Movie ‘Artificial’ Dropped by Amazon After OpenAI Partnership ‘Every Year After’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon; Will Focus on Charlie’s Story From ‘One Golden Summer’ Sequel Book ‘007 First Light’: Here’s Where to Buy the New James Bond Game Online Loading comments... articles.title: Devon Allman Says “Hot Damn” To Landing First Major Acting Role In AMC’s NASCAR Drama ‘Thunder Road’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Devon Allman Says “Hot Damn” To Landing First Major Acting Role In AMC’s NASCAR Drama ‘Thunder Road’ ‘BMF’ Star Da’Vinchi Joins ‘Chicago Fire’ For Season 15 Natasha Rothwell Joins Hulu’s Cable Guy Pilot View All July 23, 2026 5:33pm Devon Allman Madison EXCLUSIVE: Devon Allman is headed to Hollywood. The musician has been cast in AMC ‘s NASCAR drama series Thunder Road from creator John Fusco ( Young Guns, The Highwaymen ). He will star opposite Dennis Quaid, Chase Stokes, Michael Rooker, Matt Barr, Maggie Grace and West Duchovny. The series is set to begin production this summer and will debut on AMC and AMC+ in 2027. Related Stories Documentary ‘Gregg Allman: The Music of My Soul,’ Documentary On Rock Music Legend, Gets Theatrical Release Date News Dickey Betts Dies: Allman Brothers Guitarist, Singer & Songwriter Was 80 Thunder Road is the multi-generational saga of the fictional Whitlock family, whose legacy in stock car racing is as deep as the family’s ties to the Southern hill country roots that shaped them. Quaid stars as racing legend Duane Whitlock, aka The Wrecking Ball, a towering figure who built a racing empire from a legacy of moonshine runs and dirt tracks and refuses to let it die. With ruthless competitors who will stop at nothing to dethrone and destroy them, the Whitlocks are a blue-collar dynasty at the edge of extinction – and the old king is fighting to hold onto the crown. Watch on Deadline In a recurring role, Allman will play Jimmy Fuchs, a silver-tongued Southern operator whose easy charm and “sportsman’s club” credentials barely conceal the danger underneath. “Hot damn! Being cast in AMC’s Thunder Road is such a thrill,” shared Allman. “I’m excited to act alongside this incredible cast and bring the character of Jimmy Fuchs to life. He’s quite an ornery cuss, and I am right here for every bit of it.” Added Fusco: “We couldn’t be more thrilled to welcome Devon Allman to Thunder Road . As the son of Southern rock icon Gregg Allman, Devon carries a legacy in his blood — but he’s a gifted performer and a magnetic presence entirely in his own right. That’s exactly the alchemy this show runs on. In a story world that mines deep family legacy at a crossroads, Devon brings a lived-in authenticity you simply can’t manufacture. He doesn’t play the next-gen South — he’s of it. As Jimmy Fuchs, he’s going to be electric.” Fusco is set to executive produce alongside showrunner Taylor Elmore, Cliff Roberts with Syndicate Entertainment, Mark L. Smith, and NASCAR Studio’s Tim Clark and John Dahl. Gladys Cheng serves as producer. The show is produced in association with NASCAR. articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ EPs & Composer On Show’s Ever-Changing Title Sequence You “Shouldn’t Skip”, Packed With Messages & Spoilers ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory’ Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return View All July 17, 2026 2:05pm Story Arc (L-R): Brian Posehn, John Ross Bowie, Lauren Lapkus, Kevin Sussman in 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max Let’s hope the writers and producers of HBO Max’s upcoming Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe are not paid by the minute for what they have made. Not shackled by broadcast schedules where half-hour comedies need to be exactly 22 minutes to fit into a 30-min slot with time for ads, episodes of streaming comedies typically run between 25 min – 35 min. Not Stuart Fails To Save the Universe. Despite the fact that they do not have time constraints, the show’s creators, Chuck Lorre , Bill Prady and Zak Penn , went in the other direction with episodes that are very short, even by broadcast standards. Related Stories News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators & Stars On Premiere's Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' EPs & Composer On Show's Ever-Changing Title Sequence You "Shouldn't Skip", Packed With Messages & Spoilers Of the 10 episodes of Season 1, one is 15-minutes long, four are 18 min with the other five at 20 min, 21 min, 22 min, 24 min and 25 min. Why was that? With the elaborate sets and special effects involved to create the different alternate realities in each episode, did the producers run out of money in the budget? “No, no. We just felt that we’d successfully told the story, and to add would be padding, and padding, generally, is a hammock between important scenes, and why would we do that if there’s no real reason,” Lorre said. He and Prady have spent most of their careers working in broadcast comedy, creating episodes to fit the 22-min template with breaks for commercials. “The historic length of a show is entirely arbitrary, it comes from network television where a certain amount of advertising has to be sold to pay the way of making this television, but it’s not an element any longer in streaming,” Lorre said. “So, why not just make the best show we can and hope the audience is entertained and is not looking at their watch, going, ‘Oh, I need five more minutes. You need to go further with this.’ I don’t think that would happen, that’d be my guess. I would think you either loved the episode or you didn’t, and you weren’t looking at your watch.” (You can watch the video below.) This is Lorre’s third single-camera streaming comedy after the Golden Globe-winning The Kominsky Method for Netflix and Bookie for HBO Max. He has adjusted well to the binge-friendly format, with each episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ending with the heroes landing in a new alternate reality to tease what comes next. “The way we structured it, it just fell into our laps, it’s a teaser for the next week but it also felt like a natural way of telling this story,” Lorre said. Added Prady, “We found it in the first episode where we wanted to go, ‘Everything’s all right. Oh wait, no, it isn’t.’ And that was fun, so we kept doing it.” Stuart Fails to Save the Universe premieres on HBO Max July 23 with episodes released weekly. articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Creator Says ‘Big Bang’ Character Was “Worst Choice” To Lead…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Jon Bon Jovi Abruptly Ends MSG Show Amid Vocal Issues, Will Reschedule: “You’re Not Getting The Best Of Me” Cole Hauser On “Challenges” Of Making ‘Dutton Ranch’ Without Taylor Sheridan: “Everything Had Changed” John Leguizamo “Could Not See” For 12 To 14 Hours A Day Playing Blind ‘The Odyssey’ Role View All July 22, 2026 5:45pm Story Arc Kevin Sussman in 'Stuart Fails to Save the Universe' Colin Remas Brown/HBO Max With the Big Bang Theory spin-off machine operating in full force after nearly 20 years, series co-creator Chuck Lorre explained the choice behind the franchise’s latest lead. While discussing Stuart Fails to Save the Universe , premiering Thursday at 9pm ET on HBO Max, Lorre explained that the titular comic book store owner was “the absolute worst choice” for the offshoot as he was a minor character that nobody would expect to step up and save the world. “He was the absolute worst choice to be the hero of this story, which made him the perfect choice,” Lorre told People . “And Kevin Sussman , as I’m sure you know, is just a brilliant comic actor, someone you can root for despite his inadequacies. You can look for him.” Related Stories News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Talk Sci-Fi ‘Big Bang’ Spinoff With “Reluctant Hero” At Center & Romance News ‘Big Bang Theory’ Alum Joins Spinoff ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Lorre noted that “it was always Kevin” he had in mind for the series, adding, “And right from the very beginning it was Kevin, and the comic book story was.” Watch on Deadline Sussman previously admitted to Deadline that leading his own spin-off “ was not on my bingo card ” as a working actor. “I was not expecting this,” he said. Kevin Sussman and Chuck Lorre attend the premiere of ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ on July 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Presley Ann/Getty Images for HBO) In Stuart Fails to Save the Universe , Stuart Bloom (Sussman) must stop a “multiverse armageddon” after accidentally damaging a device created by Sheldon Cooper and Leonard Hofstadter. The adventure leads Stuart and his friends to encounter alternate versions of themselves across other universes. The spin-off, from co-creators Lorre, Zak Penn and Bill Prady, sees Stuart reunite with his pals Bert (Brian Posehn), Denise (Lauren Lapkus) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie). articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ EPs & Composer On Show’s Ever-Changing Title Sequence You “Shouldn’t Skip”, Packed With Messages & Spoilers ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory’ Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return View All July 23, 2026 5:33pm Story Arc (L-R) Kevin Sussman, Lauren Lapkus and John Ross Bowie speak at HBO Max's "Stuart Fails To Save The Universe" Hall H panel during 2026 Comic-Con International: San Diego at San Diego Convention Center on July 23, 2026 in San Diego, California. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Eight years after the cast of The Big Bang Theory made their last Comic-Con appearance ahead of the hit CBS sitcom’s 12th and final season, four Big Bang actors were back at the comic book convention with spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . The single-camera offshoot’s leads, Kevin Sussman (Stuart), Lauren Lapkus (Denise), John Ross Bowie (Kripke) and Brian Posehn (Bert) were joined on the Hall H stage by series creators Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady, who also co-created Big Bang , and Zak Penn. During a panel after a screening of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘s premiere episode, Prady promised more appearances by Big Bang alums. Related Stories Trailers Johnny Depp Crashes Comic-Con Hall H Panel As Scrooge To Reveal 'Ebenezer' Trailer: "It's Good To Be Back" Casting 'Batman: Caped Crusader' Season 2 Adds Matthew Needham To Voice The Joker “Well, you saw one wonderful member of the the Big Bang Theory family in that first episode,” he said. “There are more, and there are also some performers who are some wonderful minor characters that are coming back.” Watch on Deadline A number of them are in the show’s official trailer , released last month. Making a “drive-by” appearance at the panel was DC Comics’ Publisher and Chief Creative Officer Jim Lee who teased a DC-focused episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe. “They requested some DC characters to be involved in an episode,” he said. We saw a glimpse of that in the trailer, which features Mr. Freeze. “It was just amazing that they were trying to do something that was true to our characters, but at the same time find comedy in it,” Lee continued. “What was funny is we had scheduled the set visit to come to the set, and I just see the dialogue, the script. And when I came to the set, I was just blown away. It was completely not what I was expecting, I was expecting a multi-cam setup where they were sitting around, and then they start showing the visual effects that they were going to do, and all the bespoke elements they added to [Stuart’s comic book] store.” Added Lee, “Then Bill start talking about the overall arc of the 10 episodes, and I thought this is super ambitious, this is completely not what I expected. It’s like nerds going through Gulliver’s Travels , and I was sold. I was like, this is awesome, this is fantastic.” Lee closed out with praise for how the show handles the DC IP. “Some of the DC characters they have in it, I think are some of the best versions I’ve seen of those characters, and so I’m super excited for you guys,” he said. Inspired by the set visit, Lee created the cover for an exclusive Stuart Failed to Save the Universe comic book, which is also featured on the show. DC’s Jim Lee made a surprise appearance in Hall H at #SDCC to tease some DC comic book characters who audiences will see in ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,’ which he says are “some of the best” versions of these characters he’s seen. pic.twitter.com/2EOpismjHi — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 23, 2026 Elsewhere on the panel, Lorre said that the goal with Stuart Fails To Save the Universe was to “try to make a science-fiction comedy that the characters of The Big Bang Theory would watch and argue about.” Questioning reality after his experience on the show, star Sussman spoke about being summoned by Lorre in 2022 for a meeting where the comedy uber producer pitched him the idea for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe. “That was nice of him to make it seem like I might say no,” Sussman quipped. ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ star Kevin Sussman jokes that the many iterations of the Comic Center of Pasadena are starting to make him question reality. “Are you real?” he asks Hall H at #SDCC before reminiscing on the early days of the spinoff’s conception. pic.twitter.com/18vCKXUoNx — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 23, 2026 In Stuart Fails To Save the Universe, which premieres July 23 on HBO Max, comic bookstore owner Stuart Bloom (Sussman) is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. Stuart is aided in this quest by his girlfriend Denise (Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Posehn), and quantum physicist/all-around pain in the ass Barry Kripke (Bowie). Along the way, they meet alternate-universe versions of characters we’ve come to know and love from The Big Bang Theory. As the title implies, things don’t go well. Katie Campione contributed to this report. articles.title: trailer forResident Evil
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar , Patrick Hipes July 23, 2026 9:19am UPDATED with new trailer: Ahead of a Comic-Con Hall H appearance today by Zach Cregger , Sony has dropped a new trailer for Resident Evil , the Weapons helmer’s take on the iconic video game and the six-film franchise that started back in 2002. This comes as the new movie, from Columbia Pictures and Constantin Film in association with TriStar Pictures, preps for its September 18 release in theaters. Related Stories News Austin Abrams In “A Seriously F*cked-Up Situation” In First Look At Zach Cregger’s ‘Resident Evil’ – CinemaCon News Comic-Con 2026 Movie & TV Panel Schedule: Apple TV Debuts In Hall H, ‘Percy Jackson’ Kicks Things Off The new pic follows Bryan ( Austin Abrams ), a medical courier headed for a drop-off at Raccoon City General hospital who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos. Zach Cherry, Kali Reis and Paul Walter Hauser also star. Cregger co-wrote the script with Shay Hatten. Watch on Deadline Check out the trailer above. PREVIOUSLY, April 30: Sony has dropped the first teaser trailer for their Resident Evil film from Weapons and Barbarian helmer Zach Cregger that was previewed in room only at CinemaCon earlier this month. Here it is: The trailer finds star Austin Abrams trudging through a snowy night and up to a dark, empty house. He had a problem on the road, he says, and wants to use the phone. Calling his girlfriend from inside, he says, “Some things have happened,” he’s in “a seriously f*cked-up situation,” and “we might not get to talk to each other again.” We later hear the screech of creatures and a view at one large one who resembles Stellan Skarsgård’s Baron Vladimir Harkonnen from Denis Villeneuve’s Dune films, along with shots of bloodied zombies, an overturned vehicle, bodies falling and exploding bloodily in the snowy street, and more. Abrams’ character is Bryan, a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in a nonstop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos. The film marks the latest big-screen adaptation of Resident Evil , the popular horror video game series from Capcom, which has translated into one of the highest-grossing video game-based movie franchises ever. In his appearance at CinemaCon in Las Vegas, Cregger said the film is “a big, scary ride” he hoped would be “true to the spirit of the games.” In comparison to his past films, he said, his take on Resident Evil will have “no narrative acrobatics, time jumps or disorienting chapter things.” Rather, viewers will be “locked in with a protagonist on a foot journey through a world hell-bent on destroying them.” Launched in 1996, the Resident Evil video game franchise centers on the outbreak of a deadly virus tied to the shadowy Umbrella Corporation. Milla Jovovich led the original six-film series, which launched in 2002 and led to more than $1.2 billion in worldwide box office grosses. More recently, Sony returned to the world of Resident Evil with the Johannes Roberts-helmed 2021 reboot Welcome to Raccoon City. Coming off of Weapons — a critical and commercial smash for Warner Bros. that earned Amy Madigan an Oscar and grossed over $269M worldwide — Cregger directed the new Resident Evil from a script written with Shay Hatten. Constantin Film produced the pic and co-financed. The cast also includes Zach Cherry, Kali Reis and Paul Walter Hauser. Producers included Robert Kulzer, Cregger, Roy Lee, Miri Yoon, Carter Swan and Asad Qizilbash. Executive producers are Oliver Berben, Victor Hadida, Richard Wright and Robert Bernacchi. From Columbia Pictures and Constantin Film, in association with TriStar Pictures, Resident Evil hits theaters September 18. articles.title: John Leguizamo “Could Not See” For 12 To 14 Hours A Day Playing Blind ‘The Odyssey’ Role

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory’ Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return Zosia Mamet Joins HBO’s ‘Industry’ For Season 5 View All July 23, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the premiere episode of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . The Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe starts off with Stuart (Kevin Sussman) in a post-apocalyptic Pasadena getting a visit from an alternate version of himself who urges him to restore reality after he had broken a quantum interference device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. The mission begins with a quest to break into CalTech to retrieve the machine. On the way there, Stuart and Bert ( Brian Posehn ) bump into Stuart’s old flame Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ) — now a common thief — and her boyfriend Gary (Tommy Walker) who decide to help them. Related Stories News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' EPs & Composer On Show's Ever-Changing Title Sequence You "Shouldn't Skip", Packed With Messages & Spoilers News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As 'Big Bang Theory' Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return Gary is swiftly (and meaninglessly) killed per the spoiler in the title sequence — read all about that and the show’s unusual opening credits here — but there was a bigger death waiting inside. Stuart, Bert and Denise are captured and imprisoned alongside Raj (original Big Bang star Kunal Nayyar ) who had been locked up there for years under the orders of “the evil one,” the Great Khalif of South Pasadena, who turns out to be none other than Big Bang ‘s Barry Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ). After some action hero heroics, Stuart, Bert, Denise and Raj get to the device and Raj is seconds from fixing it when he is shot dead in the back by Kripke, determined to protect his reign. Deadline asked Stuart Fails to Save the Universe creators Chuck Lorre, Bill Prady and Zak Penn about the shocking development involving a legacy Big Bang character. “Well, he’s only gone in this one universe, as Kripke points out in the next universe,” Lorre and Prady said. Added Penn, “We liked the idea, I think we all thought it would be fun to do because we knew that we could bring them back,” he said of Raj and other OG Big Bang characters. “But I think it’ll be fun for people watching the first episode, don’t you? That there’ll be this moment of like, oh my God, they killed Raj!” During Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘s Thursday Comic-Com panel that followed a screening of the premiere, Prady teased more Big Bang returns . “You saw one wonderful member of the the Big Bang Theory family in that first episode,” he said, referring to Nayyar. “There are more, and there are also some performers who are some wonderful minor characters that are coming back.” Speaking to Deadline, Bowie addressed the evil turn Kripke takes in the premiere, capped by the coldblooded murder of Raj. “I would be very curious as to how America reacts to that, I gotta say,” he said. “It moves the plot forward, and in the very next episode, he makes the point that maybe that universe doesn’t exist anymore, in which case, I did not kill Raj, or I killed one of an infinite number of Rajes, so it is after all a ‘wounding ewwow’ — which is harder to say than it sounds.” As you can see in the video of his comments below, Bowie slipped into character, saying “rounding error” with Kripke’s signature rhotacism speech pattern. “So they kind of rationalize it, but that said, Kunal is the sweetest, he is made of puppies, basically, and to have to shoot him in the back, no less, didn’t feel great, I won’t lie to you,” Boiwe added. “But then immediately, what happens? Burt kicks my ass in the most extended fight scene either of us has ever done. Burt hands me my ass immediately following — which was apparently Zak Penn’s idea — like, if he’s going to do this, he has to immediately have his comeuppance.” Bowie got a lot of flak from fans — and his co-stars — for what his character did to Raj during the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘s Comic-Com panel. “He’s the most likable character maybe in TV history, it’s like shooting Fonzie, I feel terrible,” Bowie said of Raj before reassuring the audience, “I only do it once. Sorry, I will spoil that.” Later, Bowie was teased again, this time by Posehn, over the killing. “You saw that Raj comes back, right? I really wanted them to show that Raj comes back, or else I wasn’t going to come out here,” he told his co-stars, adding, “Why couldn’t I have just shot Howard?” That last line — referencing one of Big Bang ‘s main characters, Kripke’s engineering rival Howard Wolowitz (Simon Helberg) — got the entire Hall H laughing. *SPOILER ALERT! Do not listen if you haven't watched Episode 1 of 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Bill Prady teases more 'Big Bang Theory' fan favorites will return for #StuartFailsToSaveTheUniverse And John Ross Bowie chimes in on Kripke's role in Raj's shocking death in… pic.twitter.com/Zc9xKaObxk — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 24, 2026 As Penn explained to Deadline , Kripke was added to Stuart Fails To Save the Universe by Prady to serve as an antagonist in the mold of Dr. Zachary Smith from Lost In Space . “Obviously, he’s sort of the in-house villain of the show — much as he was on the last program — but the necessity of this group is that he eventually has to learn how to work with other people,” Bowie said at Comic-Con. “So he’s actually got a cool arc over the course of the 10 episodes. He’s Kripke, don’t get me wrong, you’re going to hear some awful stuff from Kripke’s mouth. But he has a little bit of an arc, and it’s fun to take him on that journey.” *SPOILER ALERT! Do not listen if you haven't watched Episode 1 of 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' John Ross Bowie on Kripke being the "in house villain" of #StuartFailsToSaveTheUniverse and his role in an OG 'Big Bang Theory' character's (Raj portrayed by Kunal Nayyar)… pic.twitter.com/whjH7w2KZH — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 24, 2026 Indeed, while the character went very dark in the premiere, there is always a path to redemption. As Kripke says in a subsequent episode, “Being an asshole is a hobby, not a vocation” in one of the season’s more memorable lines. “I love that line too,” Bowie told Deadline. “That was really fun to say, it was a really fun moment for me too.” While he appears sympathetic to Kripke, there is one thing Bowie would change about his character. “I would love for Kripke to be just a little taller,” Bowie, 5’8″, quipped. articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ EPs & Composer On Show’s Ever-Changing Title Sequence You “Shouldn’t Skip”, Packed With Messages & Spoilers
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ EPs & Composer On Show’s Ever-Changing Title Sequence You “Shouldn’t Skip”, Packed With Messages & Spoilers ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory’ Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return View All July 23, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes a detail about the premiere episode of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Each episode of The Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe tells a story of its four protagonists, Stuart ( Kevin Sussman ), Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ), traveling to another alternate reality as they try to fix the device built by Sheldon and Leonard and the multiverse Armageddon it created. Each episode’s opening credits also tell their own story via a series of fourth wall-busting amusing messages to the viewer embedded into the animated title sequence set to a differently arranged theme song by Danny Elfman. The series of notes are capped by a spoiler, which in the Episode 1 credits reads “Barry Dies.” Related Stories News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators & Stars On Premiere's Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As 'Big Bang Theory' Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return Who is Barry? He turned out to be Denise’s boyfriend in post-apocalyptic Pasadena who dies pretty meaninglessly when he says “Follow me!” and charges first into the heavily guarded CalTech, leading Stuart and Bert, joined by Denise, in their mission to break in and take Sheldon and Leonard’s machine. While the title sequence spoiled one death, the series’ premiere featured a bigger, more shocking killing of an original Big Bang character, Raj (Kunal Nayyar), who had been imprisoned at CalTech by Barry Kripke (Bowie). You can read all about it here . Deadline asked Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators Chuck Lorre, Bill Prady and Zak Penn about the clever, custom title sequences. DEADLINE: Was this about one of you being really unhappy with the streaming culture of people skipping opening credits? LORRE : Me. PRADY : Chuck said people make these brilliant opening credit sequences that people watch one time. LORRE : And then you can click on the button that says ‘Skip Titles’, and I went, “Well, it’s a terrible waste of time and money and creativity. What if we made a title sequence that you could skip but you shouldn’t? And that would mean every title sequence have to be different and worth watching. And then we got a gift from the gods when Danny Elfman said yes, I’ll write a theme and produce a theme song, and he rearranged it and and remixed it and did variations on it throughout the 10 episodes as well, so the end result was a title sequence that hopefully is surprising and fun to watch. DEADLINE: And the spoiler part, where did it come from? Chuck, was it you again? Because some of them are really spoilers; ‘Barry Dies’ is a real spoiler. PENN : Yeah, that was I think something we all liked the idea of right off the bat is, why not? Who cares? We were like, let’s try it. Let’s just see what happens if we put a spoiler in the title, and we were just trying to keep ourselves entertained and do things that were different. PRADY : I mean, not much more than it made us laugh, the notion that, especially in the online television watching culture, there’s all of this stuff about spoilers, people hunting for spoilers, people trying to avoid spoilers. What if there’s a spoiler and it’s just sort of kind of meaningless? PENN : Also, I always felt like if we say “Spoiler: Gary Dies,” a lot of people are going to think, well, It’s not going to be that simple. So it would still be shocking when he actually does die. I’m counting on people being cynical about it. LORRE : I’m counting on people laughing. PRADY : The answer to a lot of questions is because it made us laugh, and we hope it makes other people laugh. DEADLINE: Some of the spoilers are really mild, but this one was like, first: who’s Gary?, and then it was that simple, he just died. PRADY : He died, didn’t he? And he really just died. PENN : Yeah, it’s just totally pointless. LORRE : “Follow me.” PRADY: “Follow me.” Oh. Musical Variations The Simpsons theme composer Elfman recalled “the crazy thing” that happened after he was asked to write main title music for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe and, as a Big Bang fan, agreed to do it. “I wrote it, Chuck loved it, and he said, ‘So here’s the thing. I need you to do 10 variations on it,'” Elfman said. “I thought about it for two seconds. No one’d ever asked me to do that before but I just said, ‘You got it.'” And he did it, drawing inspiration from the particular episode for its unique theme music. “It wasn’t even difficult,” he said. “Each episode, just mix it up and try things. It was really just fun.” Danny Elfman recalls how Chuck Lorre requested 10 different variations of the 'Stuart Fails to Save the Universe' theme: "No one's ever asked me to do that before" pic.twitter.com/MmlmZScV7o — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 22, 2026 Judge Extends TRO, Pausing Paramount-WBD Merger By Another Two Weeks Surprise Depp Visit As Scrooge For ‘Ebenezer’; Thursday Photo Gallery; Panels Atari, Universal Ink Film Deal For ‘Missile Command,’ ‘Asteroids’, Other Classic Games Lineup, Talking Points, Q&A With Festival Chief & More From Lido More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 23, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath July 23, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory’ Franchise Makes Comic-Con Return View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Cole Hauser On “Challenges” Of Making ‘Dutton Ranch’ Without Taylor Sheridan: “Everything Had Changed”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Jon Bon Jovi Abruptly Ends MSG Show Amid Vocal Issues, Will Reschedule: “You’re Not Getting The Best Of Me” Cole Hauser On “Challenges” Of Making ‘Dutton Ranch’ Without Taylor Sheridan: “Everything Had Changed” John Leguizamo “Could Not See” For 12 To 14 Hours A Day Playing Blind ‘The Odyssey’ Role View All July 23, 2026 6:45pm Cole Hauser discusses making 'Dutton Ranch' without Taylor Sheridan. Rob Latour/PMC/Emerson Miller/Paramount+ Although the Duttons are still keeping things interesting on our screens, it’s a whole new behind-the-scenes family for the cast of Taylor Sheridan ‘s western TV franchise. Cole Hauser , who reprises his role as Rip Wheeler, recently opened up about the “challenges” of filming Dutton Ranch without parent series Yellowstone creator Taylor Sheridan at the helm, following Dutton Ranch creator, EP and director Chad Feehan’s departure after completing the first season. “There were challenges, you know?” explained Hauser to Film Inside NYC . “Not having Taylor [Sheridan] there, for us to really kind of be able to work with these new writers, these new directors, these people—everything had changed. Related Stories News Benjamin Cavell Joins ‘Dutton Ranch’ As Showrunner Following Chad Feehan Exit News Ed Harris Returning To ‘Dutton Ranch’ For Season 2 After Character Arc Frustrations & Showrunner Change Hauser noted the “only normality that we had whatsoever on set” was himself and returning Yellowstone co-stars Finn Little and Kelly Reilly, as well as director Christina Alexandra Voros. Watch on Deadline “I enjoy a challenge, it certainly was a challenge. We worked our asses off this year,” he added. “And I don’t think a lot of the outside noise or the thought of ‘what’s the weight of the show?’ was really apparent to me at the time.” View this post on Instagram While the new on-set environment was an adjustment for Hauser, he explained that the experience brought the cast closer together while filming the Paramount+ spin-off series. “It was about putting my head down and working my ass off with what I had around me. The writers that we had, the new writers that we had, that we had to figure out on our feet how to really perform and tell a story. So, I’m proud of what we accomplished, and I look forward to doing it again,” said Hauser. Last month, SEAL Team creator Benjamin Cavell was tapped to take over as showrunner for Season 2 of Dutton Ranch . As for why Feehan exited the series, sources tell Deadline he delivered as a writer, but faced challenges handling the bold-faced cast , a key component of a showrunner’s job. articles.title: Brad Bird Thinks ‘1906’ Would “Lend Itself” To Multiple Episodes As TV Miniseries About S.F. Earthquake
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Rebelle Media & MGM Television Win Rights To Adapt ‘When In Rome’ Series By Sarah Adams Audiobook Narrator Jeff Hays Joins Peacock’s ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ TV Series To Voice Princess Donut The Cat ‘Ransom Canyon’ Showrunner Breaks Down Season 2: Grift, Love Triangles, Surprise Pregnancy & Ending That Is “Launch Of Next Story” For Possible Season 3 View All July 23, 2026 7:38pm Brad Bird speaks at the 'Brad Bird: My Cinematic Journey' Hall H panel during 2026 Comic-Con International: San Diego at San Diego Convention Center. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Ray Gunn director Brad Bird has made several lasting films in his day, but he has yet to venture into television. He hasn’t ruled out the opportunity to make a miniseries with a project he has long pursued. “Actually yeah, I have a project that, it’s hard to explain, but it would lend itself to multiple episodes,” he said at the “Brad Bird: My Cinematic Journey” panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, moderated by Collider’s Steven Weintraub in Hall H. “It has to do with the 1906 earthquake in San Francisco.” This answer was prompted by Patton Oswalt via video message, in which the Ratatouille voice actor asked if a multi-episode form project was in Bird’s future. Oswalt also snuck in a quick “and also Ratatouille 2 ?” Related Stories Casting Brad Bird’s ‘Ray Gunn’ Adds Sam Rockwell, Scarlett Johansson & Tom Waits To Voice Cast – First Look News Netflix Sets Release Date For Brad Bird’s ‘Ray Gunn’; Unveils Clip, Images For Sam Rockwell & Scarlett Johansson-Voiced Protagonists – Annecy Based on James Dalessandro’s 2004 historical novel about the catastrophic earthquake and fire that killed more than 3,000 people and destroyed more than 80% of San Francisco, Bird has sought to adapt the book since 2007. Watch on Deadline “There’s a lotta BS on the Internet about the reason it didn’t happen,” Bird added of the long-stewing project. “They said the budget went out of control or something like that. We never got that far.” Brad Bird teases that he has thought about “1906” as a TV series with eight episodes, prompted by Patron Oswalt, during his career retrospective panel at #SDCC in Hall H pic.twitter.com/HNXWtylc08 — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 24, 2026 The Incredibles (2004) helmer likened the process to packing up supplies for a hot air balloon, and having to lighten the load in order for lift-off, losing his darlings in the process. “The problem with it is, the more you research that time, the more amazing it is,” Bird continued. “And the stories that are happening are insane. The deeper I dug, the more stuff I [had to include]. I was like, ‘This has to be in it!’ but it has to be big like a movie.”

articles.title: ‘Resident Evil’s Zach Cregger & Austin Abrams Tease Film’s Last 30 Seconds, Tricky Camerawork & Potential Fan Favorite Set Pieces
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny USC Games Expo Shaping Next Generation Of Game Creators Through ‘Aftertaste’, ‘Sisyphus’s Worst Day (Again)’ & ‘Unrealtor’ ‘Marvel’s Wolverine’ Video Game Unpacks Formidable Foes, Jean Grey Relationship & Leaning Into Logan’s “Trauma” At Comic-Con Shailene Woodley Talks ‘Paradise’ Emmy Nomination, “No Drama” Work Environments & Teases ‘Count My Lies’ Adaptation View All July 23, 2026 8:17pm Austin Abrams in 'Resident Evil' Columbia Pictures It may be “no sweat” for Austin Abrams ’ character Bryan in the latest trailer for Resident Evil , but for writer-director and horror aficionado Zach Cregger , his upcoming adaptation is all blood, all guts and all gory. Co-written with Shay Hatten, Sony’s Resident Evil follows Bryan, a medical courier tasked with delivering an important package to the infamous in-game dwellings of Raccoon City. However, when Bryan arrives, he finds himself in a nonstop race for survival as the treacherous night unfolds around him. The film marks the latest big-screen adaptation of Resident Evil , the popular horror video game series from Capcom, which also doubles as one of the highest-grossing video game franchises ever. Related Stories News Zach Cregger Recalls 'Resident Evil' Near On-Set Accident That "Would've Killed" Austin Abrams Trailers 'Resident Evil' Trailer: Zach Cregger's Take On Iconic Video Game Is Coming For You (And Comic-Con) While attending the Resident Evil x Discord Fan Event at Comic-Con celebrating the film’s impending September 18 release, Cregger and Abrams spoke to Deadline about the intimate fan-loving details that went into bringing the horror game to life. Watch on Deadline DEADLINE: What about Zach Cregger made you want to open yourself up to the large, passionate Resident Evil fanbase with this film? AUSTIN ABRAMS: For me, it was Zach doing his own thing with this series. I just loved working with him so much. I knew that even though it was Resident Evil , I was excited and not nervous because he loved Resident Evil . He’s played so much of it that I felt I can really trust him. It was very much about trusting him and being like, “Let’s do fucking whatever, let’s make some shit.” DEADLINE: What kind of fears is Bryan experiencing? In the latest trailer, he seems to be having some relationship troubles. What kind of things did you keep in mind while playing this character? ABRAMS: Yeah, he is dealing with relationship troubles, and then that’s juxtaposed with immediately having to survive and fight for his life, which I think makes him have to look at what he’s so afraid of in his regular day and in his relationship with fresh eyes. ZACH CREGGER: I think of Brian as someone who is just starting his adult life. He has a job, but not a career. He’s got a relationship that he really loves, but there’s a crisis in that relationship and he feels like he’s in a horror movie of his own when we start. His girlfriend is pregnant, he’s not ready. He’s thinking, “What is my life going to be?” And he feels like he’s in his own little horror movie, and then all of a sudden, a real horror movie interrupts him and it puts all of that into perspective. DEADLINE: What was the non-negotiable essential to preserving the taste of the Resident Evil franchise in the film? CREGGER: Well, there’s a couple of things you have to have. First, you have the source of all the chaos of the T-virus, which is the thing that was developed by the Umbrella corporation. If you don’t do that, for me, it’s not Resident Evil . I feel like setting it in Raccoon City on the eve of the viral outbreak felt like, “OK, that’s me laying the table.” But to me, the most important thing to make it a Resident Evil story is the tone and the rhythm. It’s like this kind of slow progression deeper and deeper into hell. And in the first act of the movie, he’s creeping into darkness, and then at a certain point, he’s running for his life. It sounds like an action movie, but it’s not. Resident Evil is a survival horror, not a survival action. He’s not a badass going around and karate kicking these zombies. It’s more intense, grounded dread, tone and atmosphere. One of the things those games do so well is that they lay out such a distinct and effective atmosphere. And so, I feel like to me, what makes this a real love letter to those games is I’m trying to replicate that experience of feeling dread and tension. DEADLINE: Now Zach, this movie is only 95 minutes. You didn’t want to make a longer movie or more movies? CREGGER: I think movies are too long, dude. I’ve got a dog at home, and if I go to a movie, I sit through a half hour of trailers and then the movie, and I’m driving back home. I’m half-joking, but I think it was just a challenge to tell a really efficient story without any extra calories. I wanted to be lean and mean and tight. DEADLINE: Were there fan favorites like Lady Dimitrescu or Wesker or other easter eggs that landed on the cutting room floor as a result of the tightness? CREGGER: I intentionally didn’t want to put any of the characters in the games into the movie because what I don’t want to do is cannibalize all these things that the games do so well. It’s kind of like when you read your favorite book and then you realize they’re going to turn it into a movie, and then they cast someone you don’t agree with, and you’re just like, it hurts. I love those games. I don’t want to step on their toes. I want to celebrate those games, and I want to make something that other people who love the games like me are going to recognize as Resident Evil . But I certainly don’t think I’m going to do a better job of representing someone like Leon than the games. DEADLINE: Was there a particular shot or set piece that made you really feel like, “Oh yeah, this is the movie I want to make and what I want audiences to see”? CREGGER: The Jump Street sequence that’s in the trailer where he’s running down the street and these zombies are leaping off the buildings while things are exploding all around him — we did it practically and it was super intense. I was really proud of what we did there. ABRAMS: That one for me too. CREGGER: But then, there’s also the first half hour. It’s short like one big long scene in a way that I think works so well. Then the last 30 seconds of the movie to me are so—I’m very proud of the last 30 seconds. So when I watch that, when the movie ends, I’m always really happy. DEADLINE: Resident Evil is known for resource management and making impossible choices. Were there any filmmaking choices that mirrored this dynamic? CREGGER: Well, resource management is every movie ever made. We have almost enough to do what we want. How do we make it work? So yeah, every scene, you’re kind of like, “How is this possible?” But impossible choices, no. I mean, no, you kind of have to just decide what you’re going to do and lock in and make it happen. DEADLINE: In bringing this game to life, were there any moments for you as an actor that really made you break a sweat? ABRAMS: We were doing a lot of camera work. It was a real dance with the camera. James [Van Der Reyden], our camera operator, had to be really precise, and I had to be really precise to his shots and come around to the camera at the same time. It was about forming a language. CREGGER: Yeah. The reason for that is because in the video games, you’re following your avatar [because it’s a third-person game], so when you look left the camera swings left, and when you look right the camera swings to look right. I wanted to do that also with the movie, which means Austin and James have to be in lockstep. When he goes up the stairs, we look at the stairs, in the kitchen, we look at the kitchen and then back to another thing. So that was fun to dial in, and I think it works well. DEADLINE: Are there any easter egg references that you’re especially excited for longtime fans to see come to life? I know in the trailer there were some herbs and a typewriter… CREGGER: Yes, there’s a lot of objects directly from the game, like the ones you mentioned. And locks and padlocks play a big role in the movie. He’s constantly getting stopped by locks, which is a thing in the games. I think that’s the thing that fans are going to recognize beyond overt one for one references, is the flow of the movie is the same as the flow of the game. You’re moving from one set piece to set piece. And each set piece contains its own unique threat. And I think that’s what the games do well. It’s a naturally cinematic rhythm. So it was fun to port the DNA of the games in terms of their story, pacing and into the movie. articles.title: Jon Bon Jovi Abruptly Ends MSG Show Amid Vocal Issues, Will Reschedule: “You’re Not Getting The Best Of Me”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Cole Hauser On “Challenges” Of Making ‘Dutton Ranch’ Without Taylor Sheridan: “Everything Had Changed” John Leguizamo “Could Not See” For 12 To 14 Hours A Day Playing Blind ‘The Odyssey’ Role ‘Obsession’s Michael Johnston Wants To Play “Intentional, Meaningful Queer Role”: “Maybe I’ll Write It Myself” View All July 23, 2026 9:11pm Jon Bon Jovi performs onstage at the Forever Tour kick-off on July 7, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Theo Wargo/Getty Images for Bon Jovi Two weeks into Bon Jovi ‘s latest tour, the band had to reschedule a stop after Jon Bon Jovi had to end the show early. During Thursday’s Madison Square Garden show, the frontman performed through vocal issues before pulling the plug early, telling the audience that he plans to reschedule the show at the famed New York City venue. “I’m sorry, I’m hurt and you’re not getting the best of me,” he said in videos posted online from the concert. Just hold onto it, we’ll figure out how to reschedule,” added Bon Jovi. “But I’m gonna have to cool it for the night.” The lead singer previously underwent reconstructive surgery on his vocal cords in 2022 after issues with his voice since 2015, which he opened up about in the Hulu docuseries Thank You, Goodnight: The Bon Jovi Story . articles.title: Hong Kong International Film Festival Society Appoints Fred Tsui As Executive Director
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Michelle Zhou’s Venice Horizons Title ‘Big Little Things’ Boarded By Moebius Entertainment For Sales Billkin Putthipong To Star In GDH’s ‘Untitled Snooker Project’, Produced By Team Behind ‘Gohan’ & ‘How To Make Millions Before Grandma Dies’ Edko Films Picks Up World Rights To Yeung Leung Chuen’s Toronto Discovery Title ‘We Are Born Good’ View All July 24, 2026 12:49am Fred Tsui Hong Kong International Film Festival Society Hong Kong International Film Festival Society (HKIFFS) has announced that veteran sales agent and producer Fred Tsui will succeed Albert Lee as executive director of the Hong Kong International Film Festival Society. In his new role, commencing on September 23, Tsui will oversee the Hong Kong International Film Festival and its year-round activities, the Hong Kong-Asia Film Financing Forum (HAF), HAF Film Lab, Summer International Film Festival, and the HKIFF Cine Fan programme. He will report to HKIFFS chairman Wilfred Wong and the Board of Directors. Related Stories News Hong Kong International Film Festival To Open With Anthony Chen's 'We Are All Strangers' & Closing With Philip Yung's 'Cyclone' News Asian Film Awards Pauses 2026 Competitive Categories & Red Carpet Tsui has worked across nearly every sector of the film industry, from film sales, co-production and financing to distribution, exhibition, broadcasting and media management – building extensive international networks among filmmakers and industry execs. Watch on Deadline In his most recent role, Tsui has established sales agency and festival consultancy company Moebius Entertainment, which recently picked up Venice Horizons title Big Little Things and Toronto Special Presentations title Happily Ever After . Prior to Moebius, Tsui spent more than twenty years at Media Asia Film, where he served as General Manager and Head of International Sales & Co-Production, helping the studio expand internationally and position Hong Kong cinema on the world stage. Earlier in his career, Tsui held senior management positions at PCCW and Asia Television, where he developed expertise in organisational leadership, media operations, strategic planning and content management. Tsui also serves as a member of the Hong Kong Film Development Council and has been invited to serve on juries at leading international film festivals, including Hong Kong, Edinburgh, Jecheon, Tallinn, Seattle, Udine, Sitges, Sonoma and Skip City in Japan. He is a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS), Hong Kong Film Critics Society, and has previously served on the Board of Directors of the Independent Film & Television Alliance (IFTA) in the U.S., as well as the board of the MIA International Audiovisual Market in Rome. “We are delighted to welcome Fred to HKIFFS,” said HKIFFS chairman Wilfred Wong. “Fred combines strategic leadership with an exceptional understanding of the international film landscape. Throughout his career, he has built bridges between Hong Kong cinema and the global marketplace while earning the trust and respect of filmmakers, festival directors and industry leaders worldwide. “Just as importantly, he approaches cinema from the perspectives of an executive, a critic, a festival juror and a lifelong cinephile. We believe he is uniquely qualified to lead HKIFFS into its next chapter, further strengthening its role as one of Asia’s most important cultural institutions and international film platforms.” Tsui said: “It is a tremendous honour to join HKIFFS, an institution that has played such a pivotal role in the cultural life of Hong Kong and in promoting Asian cinema internationally. “Having worked with film festivals throughout my career—as a sales executive, producer, juror, critic and audience member – I have seen first-hand the unique role HKIFF plays in connecting filmmakers, the industry and audiences. I look forward to working with the Board, our partners and the HKIFFS team to build on the Society’s remarkable legacy while broadening its international reach, nurturing new talent, deepening audience engagement and ensuring Hong Kong remains at the forefront of global film culture.” Judge Extends TRO, Pausing Paramount-WBD Merger By Another Two Weeks Surprise Depp Visit As Scrooge For ‘Ebenezer’; Thursday Photo Gallery; Panels Atari, Universal Ink Film Deal For ‘Missile Command,’ ‘Asteroids’, Other Classic Games Lineup, Talking Points, Q&A With Festival Chief & More From Lido Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Christine Vachon, Ewan McGregor & Sarah Brocklehurst Among Names Set For Edinburgh Film Festival’s 2026 Industry Programme

The programme will begin on August 14 with the EIFF Industry Networking Brunch in partnership with Women in Film and Television. This will be followed by an EIFF Industry Talk with veteran indie producer Christine Vachon hosted by journalist, moderator and film festival consultant Wendy Mitchell. The Vachon session will be followed by an on-stage EIFF In Conversation session with legendary documentary filmmaker Ken Burns hosted by journalist Dave Calhoun. Related Stories News Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film 'These Violent Delights' -- First Look Trailer News 2026 Edinburgh International Film Festival: 10 Films To Debut In Competition; Kenneth Branagh To Receive Honorary Award The programme will continue with an EIFF In Conversation event, hosted in partnership with BAFTA Scotland, with Scottish actor Ewan McGregor. The first day will end with an EIFF Industry Talk titled ‘The Business of Film Roadshow,’ which will see leading industry experts sharing insights about the business side of the sector, hosted by Mia Bays, Director of the BFI Filmmaking Fund. Watch on Deadline The festival’s inaugural UK Film Conference begins on August 15. The event will start with an in-conversation session with British Film Institute CEO Ben Roberts and Clare Binns, who will discuss the future of independent film in the UK. That will be followed by the EIFF Industry session ‘Would This Get Made?’, an innovative concept where industry professionals will be quizzed on how they would approach the production of a range of projects from the past if they came across their desks in 2026. The EIFF Industry Talk session ‘New Nightmares’ will conclude the UK Film Conference with speakers discussing the current state of genre work embracing its moment. Speakers include actor and filmmaker Max Minghella (The Handmaid’s Tale, Clayface) and filmmakers Prano Bailey- Bond (Censor), Chee Keong Cheung (Bad Day at the Office) and Joby Stephens (Abandoned). Hosted by horror content creator Chris Mayo (Big Fat Cult). Elsewhere, Bruce Dern will take part in a career Q&A with film critic Guy Lodge and documentary filmmaker Paul Sng will host a session titled ‘Unmaking the Colonial Gaze in Cinema.’ Discussing this year’s industry lineup, EIFF CEO and Festival Director, Paul Ridd said: “We could not be prouder of this year’s Industry Programme at EIFF which offers up a diverse and starry range of guests, talks, lively discussions and networking opportunities for Scottish, UK and international folk looking to make connections and hear from some leading experts in their fields, all more accessible than ever before. The Mediawan drama for the European Alliance of broadcasters kicks off as American troops withdraw from Kabul and the Taliban enters the city. articles.title: ‘The Deb’ Star Charlotte MacInnes Attacks Rebel Wilson In Appeal Against Court Defeat
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Mark Jermin, TikTok-Famous Agent Who Discovered ‘Harry Potter’ & ‘Wednesday’ Stars, May Have Broken UK Agency Law Paramount’s Takeover Of Warner Bros. Discovery Gets EU Greenlight BBC Considers Locking Down iPlayer For Viewers Who Refuse To Pay License Fee View All July 24, 2026 3:56am Rebel Wilson with Charlotte MacInnes in 2023 Getty The chaotic legal fight over Rebel Wilson ‘s directorial debut is far from over. The Deb star Charlotte MacInnes has formally appealed after the Federal Court of Australia ruled that Wilson did not defame her in a series of social media posts from July 2024. MacInnes claimed that Wilson damaged her reputation by alleging that she was sexually harassed by The Deb producer Amanda Ghost, and then walked back her claims to benefit her career. Justice Elizabeth Raper, the Australian judge who presided over the case, did not agree, ruling this week that “MacInnes has failed to establish that the publications have caused or were likely to cause serious harm.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Legal Rebel Wilson Triumphs In Explosive Court Battle With 'The Deb' Co-Star Charlotte MacInnes Trailers Rebel Wilson's 'The Deb' Gets First Trailer & Digital Release Date; Pic Sparked High-Profile Legal Battles MacInnes’ legal team has filed an eight-page appeal, in which they argue that Justice Raper “erred” in reaching her conclusions. The filing also goes on the attack against Wilson. MacInnes argued that the judge failed to give “adequate weight” to matters that “affected” Wilson’s reputation. The appeal accused Wilson of giving “false evidence” and “destroying, concealing or otherwise failing to produce relevant documents.” The appeal also accuses Justice Raper of failing to take proper account of Wilson’s role in a so-called “smear website,” which made incendiary allegations about Ghost being the “Indian Ghislaine Maxwell.” Wilson has denied any involvement in the website. Representatives for Wilson have been approached for comment. At the heart of the case is an incident in September 2023, when Ghost shared a bath with MacInnes in a Sydney apartment after they had been swimming on Bondi beach. Ghost and MacInnes do not deny that they bathed together , but both say it was a non-sexual encounter, during which they were wearing swimsuits, after Ghost experienced a medical incident. Wilson claimed that MacInnes told her that the incident made the young actress uncomfortable. Wilson further alleged that MacInnes later withdrew her complaint after being given career opportunities by Ghost. MacInnes denied that the incident made her uncomfortable, suing Wilson over four Instagram posts, in which the Bridesmaids star discussed the events. Justice Raper agreed with Wilson. “MacInnes changed her story about feeling uncomfortable about what happened in the bathroom,” the judge ruled, adding that Wilson’s social media posts about MacInnes were not defamatory “by reason of these findings.” Justice Raper was not convinced by the testimony of MacInnes, Ghost, and Wilson but ultimately deemed that Wilson’s actions after the bathing incident supported her story. “I have serious misgivings as to the truthfulness of the testimony of each of Ms. MacInnes, Ms. Ghost and Ms. Wilson,” the judge said. “Whilst I accept that Ms. Wilson has a propensity to exaggerate events and her evidence could be found to be untruthful on occasion, the evidence establishes that Ms. Wilson acted in a manner consistent with a complaint being made and her own contemporaneous documentary trail supports this.” As well as the proceedings in Australia, The Deb ‘s producers are suing Wilson in the Los Angeles Superior Court, accusing the Pitch Perfect star of pursuing an unjustified vendetta after being denied a writing credit on The Deb . articles.title: Netflix Reteams With Yeon Sang-ho for ‘Parasyte: Tamiya’ Series
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 22, 2026 4:00pm Yeon Sang-ho Courtesy of Contents Panda Korean hitmaker Yeon Sang-ho’s Parasyte universe is getting an all-new host body to infect. On Thursday morning from Seoul, Netflix unveiled Parasyte: Tamiya , an upcoming Japanese season of the hit sci-fi horror series that has delighted fans with its inspired K-drama reimagining of artist Hitoshi Iwaaki’s best-selling manga. Yeon, fresh off the release of Netflix thriller series Human Vapor and zombie blockbuster Colony , returns as the lead creative force behind the show, having developed its story and co-written all episodes with his regular collaborator Ryu Yong-jae. Netflix says the new season is already in post-production and will premiere on the service sometime in 2027. Related Stories Movies Inside the Gen Z Film Publicity Stunt That Had Manosphere Poster Boy Kyle University Stationed Outside L.A., London Studios (Exclusive) Business Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal Blessed by European Union Regulators The original Parasyte: The Grey spent four weeks on Netflix’s Global Top 10 Non-English TV list in 2024 and topped the rankings in 34 countries upon its release. Whereas the original season’s novelty came from transplanting Iwaaki’s classic manga to a South Korean setting, the new chapter is said to burrow more deeply into the original source material. Japanese actress Shioli Kutsuna, best known to global viewers for her recurring part in the Deadpool franchise, stars as Ryoko Tamiya, a parasite who seizes the body of a high school teacher and — initially as ruthless as the rest of her kind — gradually comes to suspect that coexistence with humans, rather than predation, may offer her species its best chance of survival. The series tells that story from her side of the divide, with Kutsuna playing the character in three registers: the original human, the violent creature that takes her over and the evolving being caught between the two. Japanese actress Shioli Kutsuna as Ryoko Tamiya. Netflix “Ryoko Tamiya is a truly captivating villain in the original manga,” Yeon says. “Her struggles over the nature of her own existence are what elevate the original Parasyte from a simple hero-based manga aimed at kids to something deeper.” “I wanted to convey her perpetual struggle over the need for parasites to coexist with humans and the issue of their survival, and how she suffers setbacks and learns over time,” the filmmaker adds. “I think the anguish she experiences is the essence of Parasyte .” Kutsuna, who previously worked with Netflix on the sumo drama Sanctuary and will appear in the streamer’s upcoming live-action Gundam film, calls Tamiya “the most challenging role I have ever played in my acting career.” She adds: “During the six months I spent living as Tamiya, I experienced many emotions I had never encountered before.” Yeon adds: “She did a wonderful job of portraying the process of a non-human creature coming to understand both humanity and its own existence.” Yeon has become one of Netflix’s most consistent and prolific collaborators in East Asia . His projects at the streamer as a creator, director or writer include Hellbound (two seasons), sci-fi feature Jung_E , occult chiller The Bequeathed , Parasyte: The Grey , last year’s Revelations and the just-launched The Human Vapor , his big-budget Japanese series collaboration with Toho. He’s kept just as busy as a theatrical filmmaker. Colony , the Cannes Midnight-premiered zombie thriller starring Jun Ji-hyun that returned him to Train to Busan territory, has grossed $42.4 million in South Korea since late May, making it one of the year’s biggest Korean hits. He’s simultaneously been experimenting with ultra-low-budget filmmaking, having released mystery thriller The Ugly last year, and with the AI-themed thriller Paradise Lost set to premiere at the Toronto Film Festival this fall. For Parasyte: Tamiya , Yeon reunites with Grey co-writer Ryu Yong-jae, while Japanese filmmakers Kensaku Kakimoto ( Glass Heart ) and Kazuhiro Nakagawa ( Double , Bullet Train Explosion ) direct the episodes. WOWPOINT, the production house behind The Grey , The Human Vapor and Colony , produces. Iwaaki’s manga, published by Kodansha from 1988 to 1995, has previously spawned an anime series and a two-part Japanese film franchise directed by Godzilla Minus One ‘s Takashi Yamazaki. Says Yoshihiro Sato, manager of live-action creative at Netflix Japan: “‘What makes a human?’ ‘Can we coexist with beings that are different from us?’ — These questions posed by Parasyte more than 30 years ago feel much more pressing for our modern society that has placed non-sentient AI at all of our fingertips.” He adds: “Our purpose in making this series was to take the universal questions posed by the original manga 30 years ago and bring them into the modern spotlight.” THR

The company is also showing off publicly, for the first time, its upcoming sets for Star Trek , Donkey Kong and Shrek .
