articles.title: Travis Scott Says He Was “Nervous as F” About Acting in Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 22, 2026 5:42pm Travis Scott and Christopher Nolan Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images; JC Olivera/Variety/Getty Images Logo text Travis Scott is opening up about how Christopher Nolan cast him in The Odyssey . During a Tuesday night appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , Scott recalled receiving an unexpected phone call from the Oscar-winning director, who asked if he’d be interested in acting in the Greek epic. “My phone went off and it just said, ‘Chris.’ And I’m thinking, ‘OK, I don’t know what this is about. Maybe he wants to go to a show?'” Scott said. “So I pick up and he’s like, ‘Would you be interested in acting in a movie?’ And I’m like, ‘I mean, I guess, you know? What’s the [role]?’” Related Stories Movies Married With Tentpoles: Tom and Zendaya's Blockbuster Honeymoon Movies 'The Odyssey' Proves It: Audiences Want Movies Made the Hard Way Scott recalled Nolan telling him the film would be “coming out soon” and that he wanted him to be part of it. Surprised by the ask, Scott responded: “I’m like, ‘Whoa, hold on. Wait. You know I make music?’” before Nolan gave him “his whole thesis on why.” “I really enjoy his time. I’m really inspired by him. He’s a real mentor of mine outside of this,” Scott said of the Oppenheimer filmmaker . “So I’m like, ‘Yo, whatever you’re down with, I’m down. However it goes, I’m with it.’” Scott played Demodocus, the bard who narrates Odysseus’ journey in the opening scene and is the first voice and face audiences see in the film. Though he admitted, “I was actually nervous as ‘F,’” Scott said he initially assumed his scenes would be with extras. “I didn’t know that it was going to be Anne Hathaway, Tom [Holland] and Robert Pattinson — a bunch of amazing people,” he said. “I don’t know what the fuck I’m doing. But they were such an amazing cast.” Scott continued to praise Nolan and the cast for making it a comfortable experience. The pair previously collaborated on the soundtrack for Nolan’s 2020 film Tenet , which starred Pattinson. “Chris is an amazing director,” Scott said before adding of the cast, “Everybody made me feel comfortable. I was just glad to be there and just watch him. And being in such a world of them. So I’m just glad to be here.” Nolan recently spoke with Time magazine about why he cast Scott, saying, “I wanted to nod towards the idea that this story has been handed down as oral poetry, which is analogous to rap.” In addition to acting, Scott also recorded the original song “When I’m Home” for The Odyssey ‘s closing credits alongside James Blake, with production from the film’s composer Ludwig Göransson. Nolan is credited as a co-writer. The Odyssey is now playing in theaters. THR

articles.title: Spencer Pratt Tears Into Gavin Newsom, Rob Bonta Over Paramount Lawsuit in Lengthy Video Rant
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 22, 2026 6:24pm Spencer Pratt at the 2025 American Music Awards held at the Fontainebleau Las Vegas on May 26, 2025, in Las Vegas, Nevada. Getty Images Los Angeles mayoral hopeful and former reality TV star Spencer Pratt released a lengthy, artificial-intelligence-assisted screed taking down the lawsuit filed by 12 state attorneys general against Paramount over its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. In a TikTok video, he shouts that Hollywood is kaput if the suit succeeds. On July 20, a coalition of 12 states led by California filed a suit against Paramount to block its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The coalition includes New York and Colorado, among others. A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order pausing the merger earlier this week. Related Stories Business Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal Blessed by European Union Regulators TV After German Broadcaster Yanks "Antifascist" Song, Musicians Give Guerrilla YouTube Concert Pratt, the former MTV star who played the villain of reality TV hit The Hills 20 years ago, began leaning into Los Angeles city politics in 2025 after his Pacific Palisades home burned in one of the fires that engulfed parts of the city. Pratt and other area property owners filed a suit against the city of Los Angeles and its Department of Water and Power, alleging the fires were DWP’s fault; he also began blaming Mayor Karen Bass, citing a slow response. @spencerpratt Greasy Gavin and Bonehead Bonta are the real life slick-haired archetypal douchebag villains we’ve seen in every movie. Now they’re coming to destroy the Hollywood for good, over petty politics. The Paramount sabotage is…way worse than you think. ♬ original sound – Spencer Pratt Mad as hell about L.A. politics in the wake of the fires, he launched a campaign for mayor on the fire’s anniversary, positioning himself as a common-sense populist. In June, he came in third place behind Bass and City Councilmember Nithya Raman, after an initial count had put him more than eight percentage points ahead of her. He refused to accept the result and drew support from President Donald Trump (who already doomed his chances in L.A. with his vocal support) and House Speaker Mike Johnson; both claimed the race was fraudulent, once again without evidence. Pratt had said he’d stay in L.A. to remain laser-focused on local politics. But with this new video, he’s gone national, training his screed on every state suing Paramount. Being a Californian, he naturally singles out Gov. Gavin Newsom and Attorney General Rob Bonta, claiming the two are destroying Hollywood as they try to “cripple two of the greatest film studios of all time over politics.” “[Newsom and Bonta] are everything Paramount isn’t,” Pratt claims. “While Paramount and Tom Cruise have spent the last decades building up Hollywood, [these two] have been destroying it — chasing productions out of town, sending projects to Budapest, neglecting film tax credits and incentives to win back production, doing everything they can to cripple the film industry while Atlanta and Hungary steal our lunch. And now they’re suing Paramount to make sure the industry crumbles further, all because Paramount wants to invest $110 billion into Warner Bros.” The 10-minute-plus clip splices in A.I.-generated cutaways from Pratt to clips of popular Hollywood movies. The former candidate channels Alex Jones, sitting behind a desk and yelling into the camera as he argues the state’s leaders want jobs out of California. Citing a clip from a podcast interview with Bonta, he notes that tech giants like Amazon aren’t named in the lawsuit despite making blockbusters with major theatrical releases — Pratt cites Top Gun: Maverick and dubs its star “Saint Tom Cruise.” In the clip, Pratt also tries to shoot down Bonta’s claim that a Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery merger would reduce production, arguing other factors were at play. “They claim that after Disney acquired Fox, production decreased. Notice they specifically say after they merged — they don’t say because they merged, because something else happened after that 2019 merger that may have had an impact on production,” he says. “Yeah, they merged right before COVID, but Gavin Newsom shut down the entire state and followed that with the biggest, most prolonged labor dispute in Hollywood history. Everybody’s production decreased.” Pratt also points to what he calls political motivation behind the opposition, noting the lack of similar scrutiny over Amazon’s MGM acquisition, and that streamers like YouTube weren’t named in the suit — inconvenient, he argues, for the theory of a Paramount monopoly. “This isn’t the ’80s, Rob. Streaming has changed everything. More and more people get their content online, which means fewer and fewer are watching traditional cable. The trend line only goes in one direction,” he says in the clip. Pratt closes out the rant with high praise for Paramount, which he credits with saving the industry. “There’s a ton of competition for these studios,” Pratt claims. “This whole lawsuit is a scam. He needs to quit playing petty politics and crippling Hollywood.” THR

articles.title: ‘Brave New Love’ Dives Into Lust, Infidelity, Norms, Motherhood and Shame (Exclusive Clip)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 22, 2026 11:30pm 'Brave New Love' Courtesy of Snowglobe Can you be happily married while leading a double life? Especially if that double life involves another person? One way to explore that question is to watch Kate, the protagonist of Brave New Love , the new feature film from writer-director Maria Bäck ( I Remember When I Die , Psychosis in Stockholm ) that will world premiere on Aug. 9 in the international competition of the 79 th edition of the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland. But be warned: things may get awkward at times. After all, Kate, a hypnotherapist, lives happily with her husband, Orla, and their daughter, Athena. But she also shares a secret romantic relationship with another man, Andreas. “After years of secrecy, the fragile balance of her double life begins to unravel,” reads a synopsis. “As a role model to her daughter, she struggles to navigate her existential quest – a journey filled with body fluids, intimacy, Greek mythology, laughter, madness, and clumsiness.” In the process, Kate struggles to redefine love. Kathrine Thorborg Johansen ( Post Mortem: No One Dies in Skarnes ) stars as Kate, Simon Sears ( Shadow and Bone ) is husband Orla, and Anders Danielsen Lie ( Sentimental Value , Everybody Digs Bill Evans , The Worst Person in the World ) portrays Andreas. Young Noemi Carbone Mannov plays Athena, and Angeliki Papoulia ( Dogtooth , The Lobster ) also features in the cast. Related Stories Movies Inside the Gen Z Film Publicity Stunt That Had Manosphere Poster Boy Kyle University Stationed Outside L.A., London Studios (Exclusive) Business Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal Blessed by European Union Regulators Produced by Anna-Maria Kantarius, Brave New Love features cinematography by Maria Von Hausswolff, with editing handled by Julius Krebs Damsbo. Reinvent Yellow is in charge of International sales. “There are so many rules and inherited expectations attached to love,” Bäck says about the film. “I wanted to explore these often absurd ideas through wit and sensuality, and create a mirror for the loneliness and power of a heart set on fire.” THR can now exclusively premiere a clip from Brave New Love that introduces you to Kate in a scene that is likely to take your breath away – and not necessarily in the way you may expect. You might remember that Madonna, in her 1998 hit “Frozen,” sang: “Love is a bird; she needs to fly.” Well, the scene here fits in with that line – but again, not necessarily in the way you may expect. Watch the exclusive clip from Brave New Love right here. THR

articles.title: Robert Pattinson, Penélope Cruz, Alicia Vikander and Oasis Lead All-Star Venice Line-Up
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 23, 2026 2:00am John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell in 'Wild Horse Nine' Courtesy of Searchlight Pictures/Diego Araya Corvalán Venice, it seems, has done it again. The line-up for the 2026 Venice Film Festival , unveiled on Thursday, looks like another star-studded affair featuring plenty of titles with strong award-season potential. Bold-faced names including Robert Pattinson, Penélope Cruz, Alicia Vikander and, according to artistic director Alberto Barbara, Oasis rockers Noel and Liam Gallagher, will be heading to the Lido this year. The 83rd Biennale will also feature new features from festival faves, including Werner Herzog, Hirokazu Koreeda and Martin McDonagh. Related Stories Movies 'Brave New Love' Dives Into Lust, Infidelity, Norms, Motherhood and Shame (Exclusive Clip) TV Netflix Reteams With Yeon Sang-ho for 'Parasyte: Tamiya' Series Irish director McDonagh, whose Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri won Venice’s Golden Lion in 2017 and who was last on the Lido with The Banshees of Inisherin (2022), returns to competition with Wild Horse Nine. John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell star in the black comedy as a pair of veteran CIA officers who, ahead of the 1973 Chilean coup, are sent far from the action to Easter Island. Steve Buscemi, Tom Waits, and Parker Posey co-star. Three Billboards and Banshees both received an Academy Award nomination for Best Picture, with the former won acting Oscars for stars Frances McDormand and Sam Rockwell. McDonagh’s house studio, Searchlight Pictures, will be hoping for a similar run for Wild Horse Nine after its Venice launch next month. French director Florian Zeller, last on the Lido in 2022 with The Son , returns to comeptition with Bunker. The psychological thriller stars Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz as a couple whose marriage buckles after he, a celebrated architect, accepts a commission to build a bunker for a billionaire. Stephen Graham, Paul Dano and Patrick Schwarzenegger co-star. Sony Pictures Classics has picked up Bunker for North America. FilmNation Entertainment is handling international sales. Legendary German director Werner Herzog, whose documentary Ghost Elephants screened out of competition in Venice last year, arrives in the main selection this year with Bucking Fastard . Herzog reportedly turned down an out-of-competition slot in Cannes for his new feature, which stars siblings Rooney and Kate Mara in their first on-screen collaboration. Orlando Bloom and Domhnall Gleeson co-star. Hanway Films is selling Bucking Fastard worldwide and is still hunting for a domestic distributor. Danish director May el-Toukhy ( Queen of Hearts ) will make her Venice debut in competition with Woman Unknown. The period drama stars Mathilde Arcel as Marie, a young nanny and housemaid who is set to marry her boss, the wealthy older widower, Christian (Carsten Bjørnlund). But Marie’s past — her shameful affair with a German soldier during occupation — threatens to catch up with her. TrustNordisk is handling world sales. In a more surprising move, Cannes darling Nanni Moretti will be returning to the Lido. Moretti’s It Will Happen Tonight , a romantic drama starring Louis Garrel and Jasmine Trinca, will premiere in competition. The Italian auteur, winner of the Palme d’Or for The Son’s Room (2001), was last in Venice with Palombella rossa back in 1989. Playtime and Pan-Européenne are handling world sales for It Will Happen Tonight . Two of South Korea’s most acclaimed directors, Hirokazu Koreeda and Lee Chang-dong, will present their latest features, Look Back and Possible Love , respectively, in competition. Also in competition for the Golden Lion this year are Casey Affleck’s 1970s-set gothic mystery Company starring Nick Nolte and Ben Mendelsohn, and A Bit of Light from Iranian director Ali Asgari. Robert Pattinson will hit the Lido red carpet for the world premiere of Primetime , the feature debut of documentary director Lance Oppenheim ( Some Kind of Heaven ), playing NBC newsman Chris Hansen, whose To Catch a Predator format becomes a media sensation. A24 is releasing the film stateside and handling worldwide sales. Venice has already confirmed that Danny Boyle’s Ink , a biographical drama starring Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce and Claire Foy, about Rupert Murdoch and his British tabloid empire, will open this year’s event, on Sept. 2. Dio Ride , an Italian period drama from director Giovanni Veronesi starring Pierfrancesco Favino ( Maria , Rush ) will close the fest on Sept. 12, screening out of competition. Maggie Gyllenhaal ( The Lost Daughter, The Bride! ) will head up this year’s Venice competition jury as president, picking the winner of the Golden Lion for best film. George Clooney, a Lido regular, will receive an honorary Golden Lion lifetime achievement award . Among the titles screening out of competition are Place to Be from Hungarian director Kornel Mundruczo ( Pieces of a Woman ) with Ellen Burstyn, Taika Waititi and Pamela Anderson; Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors , the latest from Filipino auteur Lav Diaz ( Season of the Devil ); Paul Schrader’s new film, The Basics of Philosophy ; and the Luc Besson-produced crime thriller Father Joe , from director Barthelemy Grossman starring Kiefer Sutherland and Al Pacino. Announcing the lineup on Thursday, Venice Festival artistic director Alberto Barbara began with the Venice Spotlight sidebar, whose highlights include Conversation With the Sea from Palestinian director Muayad Alayan, and Hombre Al Agua from Mexican star Gael Garcia Bernal. The Spotlight line up looks like a particularly political one this year, with other highlights including Ground Floo r from Hungarian director Gabor Reisz, which Barbara described as a metaphor for the Victor Orban “dictatorship;” and I Matter , from director Alina Serban, the first film from a Roma director to screen in the section. Among the highlights of Venice’s main sidebar, the Orizzonti or Horizons section, include Lovers in the Blue Night , the new film from India’s Anuparna Roy, whose Songs of Forgotten Trees won best director in the section last year; and Too Much Sugar , the new documentary from Procession director Robert Greene. Another new section, the Venice Open Non Fiction sidebar for documentary films, will see the world premiere of several of this year’s most hotly-anticipated docs, including Alex Gibney’s Elon Musk documentary Musk , My Undesirable Friends Part II – Exile , Julia Loktev’s follow-up to her 2025 film tracing Russia’s crack down on independent journalists; and Union Town , from two-time Oscar winner Barbara Kopple ( Harlan County U.S.A. , American Dream ). It remains to be seen if this year’s Biennale will live up to its initial promise. Venice last year included several high-profile premieres, but many — Benny Safdie’s The Smashing Machine , Noah Baumbach’s Jay Kelly , Kathryn Bigelow’s A House of Dynamite — were award season flops. The only 2025 Venice title to go on to score at the Oscars was Guillermo del Toro’s Frankenstein , which picked up 9 Academy Award nominations, winning three, for Best Costume Design, Best Production Design and Best Achievement in Makeup and Hairstyling. Bugonia , from Yorgos Lanthimos, another Venice world premiere, picked up three Oscar nominations but won none. Kaouther Ben Hania’s The Voice of Hind Rajab , which won Venice’s Silver Lion last year, was nominated for Best International Feature but lost out to Joachim Trier’s Sentimental Value . articles.title: Alex Gibney’s Elon Musk Documentary to Premiere in Venice — With a Nearly 4-Hour Runtime
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 23, 2026 3:46am Elon Musk in a fateful appearance at The New York Times Dealbook Summit 2023 at Jazz at Lincoln Center on November 29, 2023 in New York City Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images for The New York Times Alex Gibney ‘s long-gestating Elon Musk documentary is finally ready for showtime. Musk , the Oscar winner’s years-in-the-making portrait of the controversial technocrat cum oligarch, will premiere at the Venice Film Festival in September — and it arrives at a scale perhaps befitting the world’s first trillionaire: 232 minutes, just shy of four hours. Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera revealed the selection in Rome Thursday while unveiling the festival’s 2026 lineup, and he paused to make sure the audience appreciated just how much Elon has been packed into Gibney’s examination. “I invite you to look at the duration of the movie — four hours,” Barbera said with a wry smile. Related Stories Movies Venice Unveils 2026 Lineup (Updating Live) Movies 'Brave New Love' Dives Into Lust, Infidelity, Norms, Motherhood and Shame (Exclusive Clip) “[Gibney] traces the whole career — the contradictions, and the conditioning power that is centralized in the hands of a single man,” the festival chief added. “Consider a genius of capitalist entrepreneurship, but also a dangerous technocrat, with no moral scruples.” Few recent documentaries of such high profile have had such a long and tricky trip to screen. Gibney first revealed he was at work on the film in March 2023, billing it as a “definitive and unvarnished examination” of the Tesla, SpaceX and X chief. The director reportedly delivered a finished cut in early 2025 — only to return to the editing suite amid Musk’s vocal support and financial backing of Donald Trump’s presidential campaign, followed by his stint next door to the Oval Office as the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). As Musk continued generating controversial headlines, those following Gibney’s project naturally began to wonder when and how the director would ever be able to wrap up the movie. Last summer, the film’s backers, HBO Documentary Films and Bleecker Street, acknowledged their director’s predicament, putting out a joint statement, saying: “The film continues to grow in scope as the story evolves.” And there was still more to come… Last month, SpaceX’s record-shattering IPO — the largest public offering in history, raising some $75 billion at a roughly $1.8 trillion valuation — lifted Musk’s fortune to the mind-bogglingly obscene point that he is now regarded as the world’s first trillionaire. Musk has been characteristically unrestrained in his reaction to the documentary. “It’s a hit piece,” he posted on X when the project was first reported in 2023, prompting Gibney to reply: “How would you know?” Musk also once tweeted — “Gibney is a douche” — to which, Gibney has said he responded: “douché.” Bleecker Street will release Musk in U.S. theaters on Oct. 16, with HBO Documentary Films holding North American television and streaming rights and Black Bear handling international sales. Gibney’s Jigsaw Productions produced with Zhang Xin’s Closer Media, Double Agent and Anonymous Content. Gibney has spent the past three decades of his career critiquing powerful institutions and the men who run them. He won the best documentary feature Oscar for 2007’s Taxi to the Dark Side , was nominated for Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room and won widespread critical acclaim for Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison of Belief . He’s tackled Silicon Valley icons and villains before, too, with projects like Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine and the Elizabeth Holmes exposé The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley . He is no stranger to the Lido, having premiered his Mikhail Khodorkovsky portrait Citizen K there in 2019. The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs Sept. 2-12. THR

articles.title: Sarajevo Film Fest Unveils 51 Films in Competition, Including Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 23, 2026 4:15am 'Everytime' Courtesy of Sarajevo Film Festival A total of 51 films are in contention for the Heart of Sarajevo Awards at the Bosnian Film Festival. The lineup, released on Thursday, spans across four competition selections: narrative feature film, feature and short documentary film, narrative short film and student short film. From these, 21 are to have their world premiere at the August event. One will screen out of competition. “At a time when films are more accessible than ever, the value of a film festival lies not in making films available, but in returning them to public life,” said Izeta Građević, creative director of the Sarajevo Film Festival , whose selection team saw 1,215 films ahead of the fest. Related Stories Movies Venice Unveils 2026 Lineup (Updating Live) Movies 'Brave New Love' Dives Into Lust, Infidelity, Norms, Motherhood and Shame (Exclusive Clip) “Over more than three decades, the Sarajevo Film Festival has earned the trust of an audience willing to embrace films it might never have chosen on its own. This is an audience that does not come to the cinema seeking confirmation of its own taste, but for the excitement of discovering a different perspective on the world,” she continued. “It is for this audience that we selected this year’s programs. They reflect the vitality and diversity of contemporary Southeast European cinema. Each film speaks in its own distinct cinematic voice, yet they all share a search for a different perspective on reality.” Director of the European Film Academy Matthijs Wouter Knol and Yorgos Lanthimos’ producer Athina Rachel Tsangari are among the industry professionals tapped to join British star Emily Watson on the Sarajevo Film Festival jury. articles.title: Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Competition Programs With 21 World Premieres, Six International Premieres
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 1:35am PT Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Competition Programs With 21 World Premieres, Six International Premieres By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Competition Programs With 21 World Premieres, Six International Premieres 2 hours ago Square Eyes Acquires ‘I Plant My Hand in the Garden’ Ahead of World Premiere in Venice Days (EXCLUSIVE) 19 hours ago Emily Watson Joined on Sarajevo Film Festival Jury by Athina Rachel Tsangari, Igor Bezinović and More 22 hours ago See All "17" (Courtesy of Black-Cat-Production) The Sarajevo Film Festival , the leading festival for South-East European cinema, unveiled the lineups for the four competition sections on Thursday, which include 21 world premieres, six international premieres, one European premiere and 23 regional premieres. The 32nd edition runs from Aug. 14 to 21. The narrative feature films section includes nine films from South-East Europe, of which one film will have its world premiere, one its international premiere, one its European premiere, and six their regional premieres. Related Stories ‘An Icon Is Here’: Juliette Binoche Takes Over Karlovy Vary, Talks Directorial Debut ‘In-I in Motion’ and Explains Why ‘We’re All Creators’ Jesse Eisenberg on Why It Would Be ‘Silly’ to Leave U.S. Because of Trump, Says ‘The Debut’ Is ‘The Opposite of AI’ Following A24 DeepMind Partnership Elma Tataragić, the programmer of the section, said, “The selection is dominated by second and third features, alongside one debut and two fifth feature films, reflecting both the emergence of new voices and the continued development of established auteurs. Together, these nine films offer a rich panorama of contemporary regional cinema, spanning intimate family dramas, coming-of-age stories, social realism, and formally adventurous works. With six of the nine films directed by women, this year’s competition reflects not only the artistic diversity of the region but also the growing strength and plurality of voices shaping its cinematic future.” Popular on Variety Competition Program – Narrative Feature Film: EVERYTHING THAT’S WRONG WITH YOU, Urša Menart (Slovenia, Germany, Serbia, 2026, 97 min.) – World Premiere After the emotional collapse that follows her mother’s death, Maruša builds an online bond with Alja, a nurse living in a small coastal town in Germany. Bonding through humor over their shared struggles, Maruša and Alja quickly develop a friendship that is put to the test when they finally meet in person. SMALL THINGS, Zvonimir Jurić (Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia, 2026, 80 min.) – International Premiere During a winter weekend, sisters Anica and Irena, accompanied by Irena’s two children, travel to an island to visit their father and their brother Ivan, a quiet loner. The reason for the gathering is their father’s decision to sell the family land. Confined in the worn-down family house, the members of the family are forced to confront long-suppressed tensions and difficult choices, while one of them will have to make the ultimate sacrifice. SKATEBOARDING IS NOT FOR GIRLS, Dina Duma (North Macedonia, Belgium, Slovenia, Croatia, 2026, 82 min.) – European Premiere In Skopje, 11-year-old Adela and her elder sister Zara share a deep bond shaped by their navigation of two contradictory worlds. At school, they are typical, rebellious teens with skateboards, social media, crop tops, and boyfriends. After school, in a quiet and disciplined mode, they help their mother with cleaning jobs to make ends meet. When poverty shakes the family, Adela tries to find a way to save her sister – still a minor – from a fate that is becoming almost inevitable: an arranged marriage. 17, Kosara Mitić (North Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia, 2026, 105 min.) – Regional Premiere Seventeen-year-old Sara is hiding a secret during a school trip. When the excursion spirals out of control and Sara witnesses her friend Lina being sexually assaulted, the two girls try to break the cycle of casual violence. This seals an everlasting bond between them. DUA, Blerta Basholli (Kosovo, Switzerland, France, 2026, 101 min.) – Regional Premiere Pristina, Kosovo, late 1990s. As war looms and ethnic tensions escalate, 13-year-old Dua struggles to find her place among her peers and within her changing body. After an incident shakes her community, she becomes a target herself and bonds with a fearless girl who draws her toward an unexpected form of resistance. Between the daily violence and the growing threat of exile, there is little room for quiet awakenings. EVERYTIME, Sandra Wollner (Austria, Germany, 2026, 121 min.) – Regional Premiere A tragedy brings a mother, a daughter, and a teenage boy together. Struggling with blame and forgiveness, the unlikely trio takes a trip to Tenerife for a family holiday that never happens. Under the glow of the sun, past and present quietly start to overlap. SHAME AND MONEY, Visar Morina (Germany, Kosovo, Slovenia, Albania, North Macedonia, Belgium, 2026, 129 min.) – Regional Premiere A couple in their forties live with their extended family in rural Kosovo, where they make a modest living from their farm. Following a familial dispute, their livelihood is lost. They are forced to move to Pristina, where the pressure to provide for their family weighs heavily on the parents as they do their best to find work and a place to stay. A journey into a hyper-capitalist society begins. SUPPORTING ROLE, Ana Urushadze (Georgia, Estonia, Türkiye, 2026, 139 min.) – Regional Premiere Niaz Ninua has seen brighter days. Once a leading man, he stepped away from cinema some 15 years ago. When he decides to return, he discovers a landscape that no longer revolves around him. He attends a casting session for a supporting role in a debut feature directed by a young woman. The encounter bruises his pride, and he leaves unconvinced, dismissing the role as pretentious. Yet, as he replays the encounter, Niaz begins to sense a pull toward the role he so quickly dismissed. What seemed beneath him starts to reveal contours he did not anticipate. YOU DON’T BELONG HERE, Florin Șerban (Romania, 2026, 154 min.) – Regional Premiere Marius, the chief medical officer at a hospital in his small hometown, is raising his teenage son Ioan alone after the death of his wife. Marius is a confident professional who has no idea what his son gets up to at night: cycling through town vandalizing cars with a gang of masked vigilantes. Marius’ world is shaken when he learns the police have come to suspect his son of murder. articles.title: Daniel Wu on ‘Cold War 1994,’ ‘Twilight of the Warriors’ and Coming Home to Hong Kong: ‘The Craft Still Challenges Me’
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 1:41am PT Daniel Wu on ‘Cold War 1994,’ ‘Twilight of the Warriors’ and Coming Home to Hong Kong: ‘The Craft Still Challenges Me’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Venice Title ‘The Difficult Bride’ Taps Films Boutique for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 13 minutes ago Isabel Davis Named Director of BFI Filmmaking Fund – Global Bulletin 18 minutes ago Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ 54 minutes ago See All ©Crystal Li Daniel Wu received the Best from the East Award at the New York Asian Film Festival , capping a stretch that has put him back at the center of Hong Kong’s two biggest franchises: “ Cold War 1994 ” and the “Twilight of the Warriors” series. “Cold War 1994” is the third installment in the “Cold War” series, a prequel written and directed by Longman Leung and produced by Bill Kong and Ivy Ho, set in the run-up to Hong Kong’s 1997 handover. The first two films, released in 2012 and 2016, were the highest-grossing Hong Kong productions of their respective years. In the new film, Wu plays Peter Choi opposite Terrance Lau’s M.B. Lee, a character previously portrayed as a full-blown villain by Chang Kuo-chu in “Cold War 2.” Related Stories Myanmar-Set ‘Fruit Gathering’ Wins at Karlovy Vary: ‘Harrowing Drama of Obsession and Queer Desire’ Harvey Keitel Shooting 'No Bias,' Written by Wife Daphna Kastner, Calls Out ‘Danger’ of AI When Mentioning Michael Caine AI-Narrated ‘The Odyssey’ Audiobook Wu tells Variety he never consciously stepped away from Hong Kong film. The pandemic simply thinned out a schedule that had settled into a rhythm of one American project and one Asian project a year. When “Cold War” came along, the pull was the production itself. Popular on Variety “It’s going to be a quality production, the scale of it, the script,” Wu says of what drew him back, pointing also to the chance to work alongside three generations of Hong Kong actors, including Lau, whom he singles out as representative of the industry’s new generation. The film folds a police procedural into a much larger political canvas, tracking the British colonial government, the Hong Kong police, a powerful business dynasty and the criminal underworld as the territory changes hands. Wu, who was 22 at the time of the actual handover, says the setting let the production dig into a period of corruption and upheaval he lived through but never fully understood until now. Playing a younger version of a character already established as an antagonist gave Wu a different kind of challenge than he’s used to. He calls the role the most morally ambiguous he’s taken on, since it required tracing how a man who becomes an “evil mastermind” gets there gradually, through a series of compromised choices, rather than starting out that way. Returning to a Hong Kong set after several years away felt less like a job and more like a reunion, Wu says. He recalls arriving for his costume fitting and recognizing nearly everyone in the room, a small-industry familiarity he doesn’t get on American productions, where he’s lucky to know one or two people on a given crew. Sitting down on set with his rice box for lunch, eating char siu fan alongside people he’d worked with for decades, brought back what he calls a genuinely warm feeling. He credits Hong Kong crews with a particular work ethic: “efficient, fast, and no bullshit,” a directness he links to a broader Hong Kong attitude of simply getting things done. Wu spent much of his “Cold War 1994” press tour in Hong Kong wearing a hat that, it turns out, was hiding a new haircut for his role in “Twilight of the Warriors: The Final Chapter,” the sequel to director Soi Cheang’s “ Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In .” That 2024 film, adapted from Yu Yi’s novel “City of Darkness” and the manhua of the same name by Andy Seto, became Hong Kong’s second-biggest commercial hit ever and swept the Hong Kong Film Awards. Where “Walled In” was set in the 1980s, the new installment moves the story to 1993, the year Kowloon’s Walled City was demolished. Wu, who studied the Walled City’s architecture in school, calls the setting a rare chance to build a mainstream action franchise around a genuinely singular piece of Hong Kong urban history. He sees both projects as part of a broader shift in how Hong Kong cinema treats its own past, using the 1990s, a decade he says filmmakers “glossed over” while living through it, as material for reflection rather than backdrop. That shift, Wu says, is happening at a moment when Hong Kong productions can draw on newer digital tools while still leaning on the practical, in-camera stunt work the industry built its reputation on, recalling a time when performers “threw themselves off the top of a building and just did it for real in camera.” He pushes back on the long-running narrative that Hong Kong film is dying, arguing instead that it’s in something closer to a renaissance, even with a fraction of the annual output it had in the 1980s and ’90s. “There’s a lot of interesting films being made, whether big scale or small scale, a lot of great performances, a lot of great scripts being written,” he says. The kinds of roles Wu is offered in Hong Kong have shifted too, from the younger leading-man parts that defined much of his career to more mature, fatherly characters, a change he credits partly to age and partly to the character work he’s done in the U.S., where his credits have included the AMC martial-arts series “Into the Badlands,” HBO’s “Westworld,” the film “Tomb Raider” and the animated series “American Born Chinese.” He says that kind of opportunity has thinned out generally, arguing Hollywood has moved past a period of genuinely interesting roles for Asian American actors and back toward “crumbs” or stereotypical parts. He’s more pointed about the ceiling he still sees in the industry, where he says opportunities for Asian American actors, and especially Asian American males, remain narrow. Moving between the two industries has left Wu with what he describes as an unusual sense of identity, neither fully of one world nor the other, but both at once. He notes that his experience differs from most Asian American peers, many of whom have never topped a call sheet, while his own career has run the opposite path: character roles in the U.S., leading roles in Asia. He also points to a structural difference between the two systems: Asian productions tend to run through a single director’s vision, while larger American productions are often shaped by committee, with multiple producers weighing in, leaving him unsure at times whose direction to follow. Looking back over 25 years, Wu points to his collaboration with director Derek Yee, spanning six films including “One Nite in Mongkok,” “Drink-Drank-Drunk,” “Protégé” and “Triple Tap,” as the turning point that pulled him away from the romantic leads he was initially cast in and toward the darker, more complex characters he prefers. He likens the partnership to Robert De Niro’s with Martin Scorsese, a shorthand so complete that he’d commit to a Yee project without reading the script. “That put my career in a direction that I wanted it to go,” he says. Wu is now developing two scripts for the American market and one for the mainland Chinese market, a deliberate move toward more proactive control over his own projects, with an eye toward eventually returning to directing, nearly two decades after his 2007 feature debut, “Heavenly Kings.” Whatever comes next, he says the appeal hasn’t changed. Whether it’s a script’s demands or the actors around him, every project still teaches him something new. “I would say the craft, the craft still challenges me,” Wu says. articles.title: Venice Film Festival Lineup: Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime,’ Martin McDonagh’s ‘Wild Horse Nine,’ Oasis Reunion Doc and More
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 1:50am PT Venice Film Festival Lineup: Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime,’ Martin McDonagh’s ‘Wild Horse Nine,’ Oasis Reunion Doc and More Pattinson and both Liam and Noel Gallagher will be on the Lido to present their projects By Nick Vivarelli , Ellise Shafer Getty Images/Searchlight Pictures/Disney Buzzy new projects from top international directors, including Martin McDonagh, Florian Zeller, Danny Boyle, Werner Herzog, Lance Oppenheim, Nanni Moretti and Hirokazu Kore-eda, are set to bow at the Venice Film Festival . Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera has unveiled his lineup for the upcoming 83rd edition that, somewhat similarly to Cannes earlier this year, is dominated by works from indie filmmakers peppered with plenty of A-list stars despite a dearth of Hollywood studio or streamer-backed fare. Related Stories ‘An Icon Is Here’: Juliette Binoche Takes Over Karlovy Vary, Talks Directorial Debut ‘In-I in Motion’ and Explains Why ‘We’re All Creators’ ‘3 Weeks After’ Director on Tackling ‘Everyday' Peer Violence and Why Conversations About Suicide in Serbia Happen Too Late: ‘We Don’t Notice the Fire’ Which is not to say that the Lido selection lacks lustre or awards consecration potential. It’s a bit more subdued than recent editions, with less Hollywood glitz. But there’s still enough star-wattage and mouth-watering movies to keep film buffs’ pulses racing. Plus, this yearw’s fest will have a dose of rock ‘n’ roll with the world premiere of Oasis reunion doc “Don’t Look Back in Anger,” with British brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher expected to attend. Popular on Variety McDonagh – whose last two features “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri” and “The Banshees of Inisherin” both premiered in Venice – will be vying for the Golden Lion again with “Wild Horse Nine,” a dark comedy about CIA Agents who are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup. It stars John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Tom Waits and Parker Posey, with Searchlight Pictures distributing. Zeller will be back on the Lido with “Bunker,” his hotly anticipated follow up to “The Son.” It’s an elevated psychological thriller starring Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz as a real-life couple as a mysterious construction project — a bunker, commissioned by a powerful tech mogul — begins to infiltrate their lives. Paul Dano, Stephen Graham and Patrick Schwarzenegger also star. Sony Pictures Classics has North American and Southeast Asian rights. The previously announced in-competition opener is Boyle’s “Ink” starring Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch and Jack O’Connell as Larry Lamb, editor of Murdoch-owned British tabloid “The Sun.” Set in 1969, the film charts how Murdoch and Lamb launched what became Britain’s best-selling tabloid. Claire Foy plays Lamb’s fictional wife, Jules Davies, who also serves a deputy editor of the controversial newspaper. “Ink” will mark Boyle’s first time on the Lido. Netflix recently acquired the U.S. and Latin American rights to the film. Herzog is in competition with “Bucking Fastard” starring sisters Rooney and Kate Mara as twins who “in search of an imaginary land where true love is possible, start digging a tunnel through a mountain range,” according to an official plot description. It marks the first time the Rooney sisters have appeared on screen together. Orlando Bloom and Domhnall Gleeson also star. Herzog’s latest was invited to Cannes earlier this year but he declined after it wasn’t offered a competition slot. U.S director Lance Oppenheim, who directed buzzy HBO documentary series “Ren Faire,” will be in Venice with A24-produced “Primetime” starring Robert Pattinson as a journalist who takes on an underworld of crime and ends up changing television forever. An under-the-radar-title from the U.S. indie trenches set to compete in Venice is Casey Affleck-directed Gothic mystery “Company” starring Nick Nolte, Adelaide Clemens, Ben Mendelsohn, Scoot McNairy, Emily Alyn Lind and Caylee Cowan. Set on a winter night in 1975, “Company” involves parallel tales told by a mysterious woman named Evelyn who arrives uninvited at a holiday gathering. Her stories span across generations. It marks Affleck’s third directorial feature and first since 2019’s “Light of My Life.” The single Hollywood major studio title in the Venice selection is Disney’s “Don’t Look Back in Anger” which follows Oasis’ recent reunion world tour and is touted as featuring the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 25 years. “Don’t Look Back In Anger” has been created by BAFTA and Oscar-nominated writer, producer, and director Steven Knight (“Peaky Blinders”) and is directed by Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace (“Shut Up and Play the Hits,” “Meet Me in the Bathroom”). The Oasis doc – which is playing in Venice as a special event – will open in IMAX venues and cinemas worldwide for a limited theatrical engagement beginning September 11th 2026, before streaming exclusively on Disney+ internationally and on Hulu and Disney+ in the U.S. later this year. Russell Crowe is expected in Venice for “What Love Builds,” his feature-length documentary chronicling performances and tours of his band “Indoor Garden Party” across Europe, the U.S,, UK, and Australia. Luc Besson-penned and produced action thriller “Father Joe” starring Kiefer Sutherland as a man of faith who wages a violent war against 1990s New York City’s criminal underworld is among other out-of-competition titles. Al Pacino plays a powerful mob boss whose empire collides with Father Joe’s crusade. Barthélémy Grossmann (“Arthur: Malediction”) directs. Then there is Paul Schrader’s “The Basics of Philosophy” about a philosophy professor, played by Jack Huston, who has been contending with guilt over a decision from his past when the victim suddenly returns to his life. Daniel Zovatto, Bill Pullman and Shiloh Fernandez and Sofia Boutella also star The drama is said to continue Schrader’s “man in a room” stories that began with his script for Martin Scorsese’s “Taxi Driver.” These have also included Schrader’s more recent features “First Reformed,” “The Card Counter” and “Master Gardener.” Other out-of-competition standouts include Hungarian filmmaker Kornél Mundruczó’s “Place to Be,” starring Ellen Burstyn, Taika Waititi, and Pamela Anderson. The drama which follows the unlikely friendship of an elderly woman and middle-aged man as they travel from Chicago to New York to return a lost racing pigeon home. Alex Gibney will bow his Elon Musk documentary “Musk” that’s described as an epic investigation behind the public persona of one of the world’s most influential and controversial business figures. Barbara Kopple will be in Venice with her new doc “Union Town,” interweaving interconnected labor stories in and around New York City, involving delivery workers, including those working for Amazon, UPS and food-delivery apps. Palestinian director Ahmed Hassouna will be in Venice with doc “Citizen Osama” which portrays a photographer as he attempts to juggle his roles as father and a journalist while capturing the realities of war in Gaza. Kurdish/Norwegian director “Hiding Saddam Hussein” will unveil his feature “No Paradise if You Are Killed by a Woman” which follows a Kurdish-Norwegian female sniper who returns to the battlefield she once escaped, driven by vengeance and by the desperate hope of rescuing her younger sister, still imprisoned by ISIS. Back to the competition. Veteran auteur Nanni Moretti leads a robust Italian contingent with “It Will Happen Tonight” featuring French star Louis Garrel and Italian A-lister Jasmine Trinca (“La Storia,” “Supersex”). Though the plot is being kept under wraps, it’s loosely based on the short story collection “Hungry Heart” (Lev Raev) by Israeli writer Eshkol Nevo. “Happen Tonight” will mark the first time in more than two decades that Moretti – who has had nine movies in competition at Cannes – will launch a movie from the Lido. Chilean-Italian helmer Marco Bechis (“Olympic Garage”) is competing with “Back to Buenos Aires,” his new drama about the crimes of the Argentine dictatorship. “The Echo Chamber,” the latest drama from Andrea Pallaoro starring Alicia Vikander and Luca Marinelli as enraptured lovers and featuring Susan Sarandon, based on an unfinished script by Bernardo Bertolucci, is among other Italian competition standouts. Italy’s younger generation is also repped by Paolo Strippoli’s high-concept thriller “The Spiral” (“L’estranea”) about a problematic mother-daughter relationship starring Jasmine Trinca and Valeria Bruni Tedeschi and dark tragicomedy “Il Fuoco che ti Porti Dentro” by Edoardo De Angelis. The copious French contingent comprises Stéphane Brizé’s “A Good Little Soldier” toplining Italy’s Alba Rohrwacher as a woman navigating a corporate environment where vulnerability is not an asset. Vincent Lindon also stars. Then there is Cédric Kahn’s “15/18” (aka “A Place to Heal”) that is set in a French public hospital’s adolescent psychiatry unit, and Nicolas Pariser’s “A Bit Before Midnight” with Melvil Poupaud as a man examining his life after his father dies. Léonie Simaga, Chiara Mastroianni, and Golshifteh Farahani also star. Asian entries competing include Japanese festival circuit darling Hirokazu Kore-eda’s “Look Back,” a live-action adaptation of a Tatsuki Fujimoto manga story about two girls chasing their dreams of becoming manga artists. It marks Kore-eda’s second premiere this year after his sci-fi fable “Sheep in the Box” which competed at Cannes. There is also beloved Korean helmer Lee Chang-dong’s Netflix movie “Possible Love” that centers on two couples whose vastly different lifestyles create unexpected intersections. The film marks Chang-dong’s first feature since 2018’s “Burning.” And cult Japanese director Shinya Tsukamoto’s “Mr. Nelson, Did You Kill People?” starring U.S. stage actor Rodney Hicks and Geoffrey Rush in a portrait of Vietnam veteran Allen Nelson. Japanese filmmaker Sabu’s detective comedy “Arrested Memory,” starring Taiwan’s Ethan Juan, is screening out-of-competition. Danish-Egyptian director May el-Toukhy who made a splash with 2019 Sundance audience award-winner “Queen of Hearts” will bow post-WWII drama “Woman, Unknown” about a former housekeeper named Marie who while preparing to celebrate her engagement to the patriarch of the house, is haunted by secrets of her past. El-Toukhy, who has also directed episodes of Netflix’s “The Crown,” is the single female director in the 20-title competition. Berlin-based Ilya Khrzhanovsky will unveil the new entry in his monumental DAU project, which he spent over two and a half years finishing. “DAU. Natasha” and “DAU. Degeneration” previously premiered at the 2020 Berlinale. Khrzhanovsky renounced his Russian citizenship and has been an outspoken critic of Putin’s regime. But he also faced allegations about the way he treated women on the set of “DAU. Natasha.” Iranian director who was in Venice Horizons last year with dark satire “Divine Comedy,” in back – in competition this time – with his new feature “A Bit of Light.” Opening the Horizons section dedicated to more cutting-edge works is Alina Marazzi’s “La Ragazza Con La Leica” (“The Girl With the Leica”) about war photographer Gerda Taro, the first woman photojournalist killed in war who was also Robert Capa’s muse As previously announced, Maggie Gyllenhaal will preside over the jury. Gyllenhaal will also be presenting an out-of-competition short titled “Flesh Impact” with Ellen Burstyn, Dakota Johnson, Peter Sarsgaard, and Sepideh Moafi. She will be joined on the jury by Hong Kong filmmaking giant Johnnie To, Tunisian director Kaouther Ben Hania, Afghan filmmaker Shahrbanoo Sadat, French director and screenwriter Xavier Giannoli, “The Brutalist” composer Daniel Blumberg and U.S.-based Italian film academic Francesco Casetti. George Clooney and Ellen Burstyn will also be honored with lifetime achievement awards. The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs from Sept. 2 to 12. See the full lineup below. articles.title: Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 3:07am PT Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Venice Title ‘The Difficult Bride’ Taps Films Boutique for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 5 minutes ago Isabel Davis Named Director of BFI Filmmaking Fund – Global Bulletin 10 minutes ago Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ 46 minutes ago See All Kristina Bumphrey/Variety/Getty Images Whoopi Goldberg used Tuesday’s episode of “The View” to push back on conservative anger over Elliot Page ‘s casting in Christopher Nolan ‘s “ The Odyssey ,” dismissing a clip of commentator Ben Shapiro calling the choice a mistake. Shapiro called Page’s role an “absolute puzzler” before pointing out that he is “about 5’2 and 105 pounds soaking wet and has the voice of a woman. It doesn’t work.” Related Stories ‘An Icon Is Here’: Juliette Binoche Takes Over Karlovy Vary, Talks Directorial Debut ‘In-I in Motion’ and Explains Why ‘We’re All Creators’ '3 Weeks After' Review: A Bruising, Fiercely Controlled Study of High Schoolers in Moral and Psychological Freefall “A lot of conservatives who see this are going to feel the same way. That’s okay. But I don’t understand. Why go see the movie? If you don’t want to see it, don’t go see it. Why do you care who’s cast in it?” Goldberg said. Popular on Variety Page has a supporting role in the film as Sinon, a cousin of Matt Damon’s Odysseus. The Variety review described Page’s role as “tersely vulnerable.” Goldberg didn’t stop at defending Page. She also went after the word “woke” itself, telling viewers that the label gets thrown at ordinary people just trying to hold down jobs, raise families and get an education, not at anyone pushing an agenda. Critics on the right had first seized on inaccurate rumors that Page would be cast as Achilles, with Elon Musk among those weighing in before the actual casting was known. A similarly hostile response met Lupita Nyong’o’s involvement in the project, rooted in racist objections to her casting. The criticism has had zero effect on box office for “The Odyssey.” Nolan enjoyed the biggest opening of his career with the film, with the global collections now having crossed $300 million. articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 3:25am PT Comcast Q2 Boosted by World Cup, Peacock Swings to First Quarterly Profit By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest TelevisaUnivision Posts Q2 Loss Despite Boost From Mexico World Cup Telecasts 11 minutes ago Comcast Q2 Boosted by World Cup, Peacock Swings to First Quarterly Profit 46 minutes ago World Cup May Be Over, but Fox Sports CEO Eric Shanks Thinks Hydration Breaks Could Return 20 hours ago See All Courtesy of Comcast Comcast said its second quarter was boosted by revenue tied to World Cup telecasts on the company’s Spanish-language Telemundo network as well as the Peacock streaming service, which achieved profitability for the first time, but the company still faced headwinds in its cable and broadband business and saw profit in the period decline due to comparisons with the year-earlier period, which included a sizable gain tied to the sale of its stake in Hulu to Walt Disney. Related Stories Karim Kassem Broaches Migrant Issues in Lebanon With ‘Pipes’: ‘A Lot of People Are Being Affected by War but We Don’t See the Whole Picture’ ‘An Icon Is Here’: Juliette Binoche Takes Over Karlovy Vary, Talks Directorial Debut ‘In-I in Motion’ and Explains Why ‘We’re All Creators’ The Philadelphia owner of NBC and the Universal movie studio posted net income of $3.5 billion, or 99 cents per share, compared with $2.98 per share in the year-earlier period, or $11.1 billion. Comcast gained $9.4 billion from the sale of its interest in Hulu. Earnings, adjusted for non-recurring costs, came to $1.04 per share. Popular on Variety Revenue came to $29.9 billion, off 1.2% from the year-earlier quarter. Comcast said Peacock generated a profit for the first time since its launch in 2020, with paid subscribers now totaling 48 million, up by two million net additions during the period. The company said it also generated an extra $440 million in revenue due to its World Cup telecasts. Indeed, the World Cup tournament helped power the company’s NBCU operations, which generated a 22.9% increase in revenue, to $10.7 billion in the quarter. U.S. advertising rose 55%, and would have increased 23.5% without World Cup activity, thanks to Peacock and interest in the NBA. Revenue also increased at the company’s studios and theme parks. Revenue was off at the company’s large cable and broadband operations, falling 3.2%. Comcast said it continued to lose subscribers to both cable and broadband, but noted an increase in wireless subscriptions. The company ceded 230,000 subscribers, and now has 47.7 million. articles.title: ‘Oasis,’ Exploring Fear, Exclusion and Violence, Picked Up by Totem Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 3:25am PT ‘Oasis,’ Exploring Fear, Exclusion and Violence, Picked Up by Totem Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Competition Programs With 21 World Premieres, Six International Premieres 2 hours ago Square Eyes Acquires ‘I Plant My Hand in the Garden’ Ahead of World Premiere in Venice Days (EXCLUSIVE) 19 hours ago Emily Watson Joined on Sarajevo Film Festival Jury by Athina Rachel Tsangari, Igor Bezinović and More 22 hours ago See All Courtesy of Zeitgeist Filmproduktion FFM Totem has picked up international sales rights for “Oasis,” by writer-director Jannis Lenz , which has its world premiere in the Horizons competition section at the Venice Film Festival . The film joins Totem’s sales slate as the company shifts its primary focus to production. The film centers on a school where a viral video of a student threatening his classmates surfaces online, and the situation spirals into escalating violence. Crushed by the pressure of teachers and parents, three outcasts take refuge in a nearby forest. There, play hardens into ritual and pain becomes an escape, until old wounds surface and the boundaries between them are redrawn. Related Stories How Filmmaker Tonia Mishiali Tackles Immigration, Patriarchy and Women’s Resilience in ’The Lion at My Back’ Switzerland Shows Its Dark Side in Jan-Eric Mack's ‘A Happy Family’: ‘People Don’t Talk’ “ ‘Oasis’ captures the fragility of adolescence with great precision, exploring fear, exclusion and violence through a deeply human perspective,” producer Markus Katsch of Zeitgeist said. Popular on Variety Bérénice Vincent, CEO at Totem, commented: “Jannis is a hugely promising talent, with a rare assurance behind the camera. What impressed us is the way he exposes the contradiction between the violence we’ve normalized and the violence we condemn – and the world as it stands proves his point every day.” Lenz’s previous work includes the short “Wannabe” (2017), which won the Prix Clermont-Ferrand and was nominated for the European Film Award, while his graduation film “Soldat Ahmet” (2021) premiered at Visions du Réel and won several international awards. He is a Vienna Film Academy graduate, mentored by Jessica Hausner, has been an assistant to Michael Haneke, and is a Berlinale Talents alumnus. “Oasis” features newcomer Florian Geißelmann (“Sound of Falling”) and acclaimed actor Godehard Giese (“Rose”), as well as upcoming German actors Anton Petzold and Mathilda Smith. The film is produced by Germany’s Zeitgeist Filmproduktion FFM and co-produced by Austria’s Wega Film and Germany’s Third Picture in collaboration with We Fade to Grey, Ocean Pictures Filmproduktion and Totem Films. It is supported by Der Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien BKM, Deutscher Filmförderfonds DFFF, Österreichisches Filminstitut ÖFI+, MFG Medien- und Filmgesellschaft Baden-Württemberg, Film- und Medienstiftung NRW, Kuratorium junger deutscher Film and Filmförderungsanstalt FFA. articles.title: Venice Title ‘The Difficult Bride’ Taps Films Boutique for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 3:48am PT Venice Title ‘The Difficult Bride’ Taps Films Boutique for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics of Elliot Page’s Casting in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Then Don’t Go See It… Why Do You Care Who’s Cast in It?’ 41 minutes ago Daniel Wu on ‘Cold War 1994,’ ‘Twilight of the Warriors’ and Coming Home to Hong Kong: ‘The Craft Still Challenges Me’ 2 hours ago Yeon Sang-ho Returns to ‘Parasyte’ Universe With ‘Tamiya,’ Starring Shioli Kutsuna, at Netflix 12 hours ago See All Films Boutique Films Boutique has boarded international sales on “ The Difficult Bride ,” Rubaiyat Hossain ‘s supernatural feminist drama selected for the Horizons competition of the Venice Film Festival , where it will become the first Bangladeshi feature film to screen. The cast includes three Bangladesh National Film Award winners – Azmeri Haque Badhon, Rikita Nondine Shimu and Sunerah Kamal – alongside Zaineen Chowdhury Karim in her lead acting debut and Dameer Khan in a guest appearance. Related Stories Jeffrey Wright Says Being Black Is a 'Political Term,' Talks Racist Abuse Against Kylian Mbappé: ‘They Think They Can Diminish How Powerful He Is With Their Stupidity' 'Robert Richardson: The White Devil' Review: Candid Documentary Turns the Camera on a Cinematography Legend “The Difficult Bride” unfolds at Mayfair, a longtime Dhaka beauty parlor, and follows Zaineen Chowdhury Karim’s character as her wedding preparations draw her into an unsettling world shaped by beauty, faith, memory and fear. The screenplay draws on an urban legend Hossain heard as a child, about a bride who reportedly died at the salon under mysterious circumstances. Popular on Variety Principal photography was in Bangladesh, with post-production completed in Paris and Lisbon. The film is Hossain’s fourth feature and received post-production support from the inaugural Fondazione Prada Film Fund. Hossain’s debut feature, “Meherjaan” (2011), picked up awards at the Northampton and Tiburon festivals. Her second feature, “Under Construction” (2015), screened at Locarno and Stockholm. Her third feature, “Made in Bangladesh” (2019), premiered in Toronto’s Contemporary World Cinema section, also screened at Locarno and BFI London, and brought her a first Asia Pacific Screen Award nomination. Jean-Christophe Simon, CEO of Films Boutique, said: “We’re particularly proud to be trusted with Rubaiyat’s new film. Following the success of ‘Made in Bangladesh,’ she has created yet another genuinely unique cinematic work, that will allow for an uncompromising female character to reach audiences worldwide. Both from an esthetic and topical standpoint, her powerful and particularly entertaining movie will speak to many about the situations so many women are still confronted with, when it comes to the way patriarchal society looks at their body.” “The Difficult Bride” is produced by France’s Les Films de l’Après-Midi, in co-production with Portugal’s Midas Filmes, Bangladesh’s Khona Talkies, Norway’s Barentsfilm and Germany’s Tandem Production. The film’s producers are François d’Artemare, Pedro Borges, Rubaiyat Hossain, Aadnan Imtiaz Ahmed, Ingrid Lill Høtgun and Anna Katchko. Md Shariful Islam and Kevin Chaty serve as executive producers. The film also received backing from Eurimages, France’s CNC, Portugal’s ICA, Norway’s Sorfønd and Germany’s World Cinema Fund. The film was shot by cinematographer Leonor Teles, who claimed the Berlin Film Festival’s Golden Bear for a short film in 2016 at a younger age than any prior winner. British composer Jim Williams, whose credits include Julia Ducournau’s “Raw” and “Titane,” wrote the score. Hossain said: “A film is born from the long years of work, sacrifice, patience, creativity and love of many people. I am deeply grateful to our entire team, our actors, crew members, co-producers and collaborators.” In 2010, Ishtiaque Zico’s short film “720 Degrees,” produced by Khona Talkies, became the first Bangladeshi short to screen in Horizons. The selection of “The Difficult Bride” comes as women’s rights in Bangladesh face pressure from extremist religious groups. The festival runs Sept. 2-12. articles.full_text: Jul 23, 2026 4:00am PT TelevisaUnivision Posts Q2 Loss Despite Boost From Mexico World Cup Telecasts By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Comcast Q2 Boosted by World Cup, Profits at Peacock 35 minutes ago World Cup May Be Over, but Fox Sports CEO Eric Shanks Thinks Hydration Breaks Could Return 20 hours ago Zoom, With New Story, Bets on Indie Journalist to Tell It 2 days ago See All Getty Images Spanish-language media giant TelevisaUnivision said it posted a loss in the second quarter despite a swell of revenue from its rights to air the World Cup in Mexico, a sign of the challenges the company, formed from the combination of Univision in the U.S. and Grupo Televisa in Mexico, continues to face. The company posted a loss of more than $10 million on revenue of nearly $1.33 billion. Revenue for the period soared 10%, compared with $1.21 billion in the year-earlier period. TelevisaUnivision attributed much of the increase to advertising and licensing fees associated with its Mexican sports rights. Related Stories Šimon Holý Turns Drag, Family and Small-Town Life Into a Tender Political Statement in ‘Chica Checa’ 'Black Money for White Nights' Review: A Cycle of Corruption Endangers a Marriage in a Bitter, Gripping Bulgarian Tragicomedy Indeed, advertising from operations in Mexico rose 19%, driven in large part by commercials tied to telecasts of FIFA World Cup , compared with lackluster results in the U.S,. where advertising revenue slumped 22%. Overall ad revenue fell 9% during the period. TelevisaUnivision in April replaced its ad-sales chief , just days before holding its annual “upfront” presentation. Popular on Variety Subscription and licensing revenue rose 40% during the second quarter, to $621 million. Approximately $90 million in revenue came from sublicensing the company’s FIFA World Cup rights to media properties in other Spanish-speaking Latin American countries. TelevisaUnivision has been working to bolster its balance sheet since Wade Davis, the former Viacom CFO who orchestrated a buyout of Univision in 2020, ceded his CEO role to Daniel Alegre, a former senior executive at Activision Blizzard. Since Alegre joined in 2024, TelevisaUnivision has worked to streamline operations that had previously been siloed by geographic region. In a statement, Alegre gave credit to the power of the soccer spectacle. “The tournament reinforced why soccer is a cornerstone of our strategy and why we are the ‘Home of Soccer’ for Hispanics. Sports, together with our continued investments in live events and premium entertainment, ensure that we remain the destination for culturally relevant moments that matter,” the executive said. “Combined with our unique connection to our audience and the importance of our platforms heading into the U.S. election cycle, this momentum positions us well to drive sustained profitability while creating even greater value for our audiences, advertisers, and partners.” Operating expenses increased 16% to $940 million, mainly driven by sports costs associated with the FIFA World Cup. Operating income was $224 million, a decrease of $17 million versus prior year, which the company attributed to higher direct operating expenses. articles.title: Kevin Feige Wants To Add Miles Morales’ Spider-Man To MCU After ‘Spider-Verse’ Films End: “We Definitely Have Plans”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics Of Elliot Page’s ‘The Odyssey’ Casting: “Don’t Go See The Damn Movie” Kevin Feige Wants To Add Miles Morales’ Spider-Man To MCU After ‘Spider-Verse’ Films End: “We Definitely Have Plans” ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Creator Says ‘Big Bang’ Character Was “Worst Choice” To Lead Spin-Off, “Which Made Him The Perfect Choice” View All July 22, 2026 6:50pm Miles Morales (voiced by Shameik Moore) in 'Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse' (2018) Columbia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection After the MCU expanded on Peter Parker’s Spider-Verse , Kevin Feige hopes to have fan-favorite Miles Morales swing by the franchise. The Marvel Studios boss recently teased plans for Spider-Man’s Black alter ego make a live-action appearance in a future movie, once he’s done saving the world in Sony Pictures’ animated Spider-Verse franchise, which concludes on June 18, 2027 with Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse . “The good news is, Sony has the Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse series, which are very popular and excellent, and Beyond the Spider-Verse is coming out next year,” Feige told China’s Watching Hollywood . “But yes, we definitely have plans [for a live-action Miles], and I think a live-action Spider-Man movie has this destiny: to add Miles sometime after the Spider-Verse series ends.” Related Stories News Marvel Boss Kevin Feige Teases ‘Blade’ Still Alive, Scarlet Witch’s Return & Miles Morales’ Future News ‘Spider-Man: Beyond The Spider-Verse’ Footage, The Final Chapter Of Miles’ Story – CinemaCon Following Miles Morales’ big screen debut in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018) and Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023), Shameik Moore reprises his voice role as the Marvel web-slinger in next year’s Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse , which sees Miles trapped in an alternate universe and on the run while trying to save his family. Watch on Deadline In Spider-Man: No Way Home , Tom Holland’s Peter Parker is introduced to predecessors Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire’s versions of the character when they chase down some of their own villains across the multiverse. “Somewhere there’s bound to be a Black Spider-Man,” says Electro (Jamie Foxx) in one scene. ‘Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse’ Sony “Audiences around the world were thrilled because they knew it might be a hint at Spider-Man Miles,” said Feige. Feige added, “We’ve been thinking and discussing more Spider-Man adventures, regardless of agreements or contracts. My production partner, Amy Pascal, is already working on it, and we’ve had in-depth discussions about what the next two, three, four, and five Spider-Man movies might be about.” In 2023, Pascal confirmed that a live-action Miles Morales movie was in the works . “You’ll see all of it. It’s all happening,” she told Variety . Meanwhile, Holland’s Peter Parker returns for a fourth solo outing in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , premiering July 30 in theaters. articles.title: Reid Scott Leaving ‘Law & Order’, James Badge Dale To Succeed Him In Season 26 Of NBC Drama
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Reid Scott Leaving ‘Law & Order’, James Badge Dale To Succeed Him In Season 26 Of NBC Drama ‘Stewie’ Voice Cast Set: Kenan Thompson, Vanessa Bayer, Melissa O’Neil, Mike Henry & More Join Seth MacFarlane In ‘Family Guy’ Spinoff Kenneth Branagh Stars In Scottish Highland Drama ‘Laird’ Ordered By Paramount+ From Jez Butterworth & 101 Studios View All July 22, 2026 8:07pm (L-R) Reid Scott in 'Law & Order'; James Badge Dale Joe Pugliese/NBC/Michael Schwart EXCLUSIVE : The police force on Law & Order is undergoing some major staff turnover. Reid Scott , who has played Senior Detective Vincent Riley for the past three seasons, is leaving the venerable NBC crime drama. The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel and Veep alum will be succeeded by another high-profile name, James Badge Dale ( 13 Hours, 1923 ). He is set to play a new Senior Detective who will replace Riley. For Scott, who is believed to have one more year on his contract, the departure is said to be his decision, related to the strain caused by the cross-country commute and being away from his family for nine months of the year while filming Law & Order in New York. His exit was amicable. Related Stories News Emmys Cuts Number Of Televised Categories For 2026 Primetime Ceremony News Craig Melvin Says "Everyone Is Safe" After Intruder Gained Access To 'Today' Studio; Police Identify Suspect Det. Riley will get a proper ending as Scott is back on the set, filming a few episodes to wrap the character’s arc before Dale is introduced. The exact time of the transition is unclear. Watch on Deadline Law & Order is known for its revolving cast, with changes between seasons an annual occurrence. Scott’s Det. Riley was most recently partnered with Junior Detective Theo Walker (David Ajala) this past season. His previous partner, Junior Detective Jalen Shaw, was played by Mehcad Brooks who left last summer . Scott, in turn, replaced Jeffrey Donovan. In addition to Ajala, Dale is joining returning Law & Order cast members Tony Goldwyn, Hugh Dancy, Maura Tierney and Odelya Halevi. Season 26 premieres Oct. 8 at 10 PM, behind the season opener of Law & Order: SVU. In TV, Dale has had major roles on Fox’s 24 , HBO’s The Pacific, Starz’s Hightown, Peacock’s Devil In Disguise: John Wayne Gacy and Paramount+s 1923. He is also in the Jessica Chastain thriller series The Savant whose release has been put on hold by Apple TV. Dale’s film credits include The Departed, The Grey, Iron Man 3, 13 Hours and World War Z. He recently signed on for psychological thriller The Guide and will next be seen in Jeremy Saulnier’s A24 fugitive thriller October after starring in the director’s 2018 film Hold the Dark . Dale is repped by CAA, MJ Management and Michael Auerbach. articles.title: Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics Of Elliot Page’s ‘The Odyssey’ Casting: “Don’t Go See The Damn Movie”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Whoopi Goldberg Slams Transphobic Critics Of Elliot Page’s ‘The Odyssey’ Casting: “Don’t Go See The Damn Movie” Kevin Feige Wants To Add Miles Morales’ Spider-Man To MCU After ‘Spider-Verse’ Films End: “We Definitely Have Plans” ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Creator Says ‘Big Bang’ Character Was “Worst Choice” To Lead Spin-Off, “Which Made Him The Perfect Choice” View All July 22, 2026 8:16pm Whoopi Goldberg defends Elliot Page's casting in 'The Odyssey'. ABC/Universal Pictures As The Odyssey surpasses $300M after a record opening weekend , conservative critics should be eating their words. On Tuesday’s episode of The View , panelist Whoopi Goldberg called out social media trolls who have been “losing their minds over the cast” and are “still trashing the movie” amid its box office success, responding to a video of Ben Shapiro complaining that it’s “stupid to cast Elliot Page as a dude” in the Christopher Nolan adaptation. “Listen, a lot of conservatives who see this are going to feel the same way. That’s okay,” she prefaced. “But I don’t understand. Why go see the movie? If you don’t want to see it, then don’t go see it. Why do you care who’s cast in it?” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Christopher Nolan Dismisses ‘The Odyssey’ Casting Backlash As “Irrelevant”: “That’s What Adaptation Is” News Lupita Nyong’o Says She’s “Not Spending My Time” Dignifying ‘The Odyssey’ Racist Casting Criticisms Goldberg continued, “I don’t understand this idea that if we hate it, everybody must hate it because we hate it for this reason. You don’t like Elliot Page? Don’t go see the damn movie. Don’t do it. We will be okay if you don’t go see it.” Fellow panelist Alyssa Farrah Griffin called the movie “a masterpiece,” arguing that despite the “woke” criticisms, the film has “a real conservative message.” “It’s about devotion to family, it’s about faith, it’s about upholding institutions. It’s about how war is dangerous and has repercussions for all of us,” she explained. “And the fact that conservatives can’t take the win and just be like, ‘oh no, this is a really excellent film with a good message for families,’ I’ll never understand.” Joy Behar quipped, “but they’re stuck on ‘woke,'” to which Griffin noted, “But there’s nothing woke in this film.” Sarah Haines also chimed in on the discourse around trans actor Page playing Greek soldier Sinon, following online outrage over speculation that he would star as Achilles. “There’s a unique ignorance to someone who comments on something they’ve never seen,” said Haines. “You’re taught from a young age, do your research, learn, and then you can join the conversation. But it’s like not voting and then complaining about what you get. You cannot not see the film and complain about how awful it is, when you haven’t seen the film. Because this film—and I echo Alyssa—is a masterpiece.” Christopher Nolan attends ‘The Odyssey’ premiere on July 11, 2026 in Mumbai, India. Aalok Soni/Getty Images for Universal Pictures Tuesday’s segment comes after criticism from the likes of Elon Musk and Matt Walsh over Oscar-winning Black actress Lupita Nyong’o’s dual casting as Helen of Troy, “the face that launched a thousand ships,” and her sister Clytemnestra. Others have also criticized Nolan for casting Black musician Travis Scott. Meanwhile, Nolan has dismissed the backlash as “ irrelevant ” since the movie had not yet been released, noting that it “comes with the territory” of adapting a major piece of IP. An adaptation of one of the first stories in human history, The Odyssey follows Odysseus (Matt Damon) through the incredible trials and mythical encounters he faces on his decade-long journey home to wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) after the Trojan War. The film also stars Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Jon Bernthal, Benny Safdie, John Leguizamo, Himesh Patel, Bill Irwin, Samantha Morton, Jesse Garcia, Will Yun Lee, Rafi Gavron, Shiloh Fernandez, Mia Goth and more.
