articles.title: Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film ‘These Violent Delights’ — First Look Trailer
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film ‘These Violent Delights’ — First Look Trailer TIFF 2026: ‘Stuffed’ Starring Jodie Comer & Harry Melling Among Discovery Titles View All July 23, 2026 1:00am EXCLUSIVE: The Scottish Ballet company and production house Forest of Black have partnered with the indie distribution company Tull Stories to release their dance film These Violent Delights in UK and Irish cinemas. Tull Stories will release These Violent Delights in cinemas from October 21, following the film’s world premiere at this year’s Edinburgh International Film Festival. The film, based on Shakespeare’s Romeo & Juliet , was shot across various locations in Scotland and marks the Scottish Ballet company’s first major feature-length film project. The full synopsis reads: “In this vivid, contemporary re-telling without words, Juliet awakens from a fever dream. The lines between hallucination and memory blur as cinema and dance collide in a kaleidoscopic journey of belonging, defiance and self-discovery as fate is rewritten on the dance floor.” Related Stories News 2026 Edinburgh International Film Festival: 10 Films To Debut In Competition; Kenneth Branagh To Receive Honorary Award News Daniel Goldhaber's 'Faces Of Death' To Close Edinburgh's Midnight Madness Strand; Signature Entertainment Acquires Title For UK & Ireland Oscar Sansom (Biffy Clyro: A Celebration of Endings) and Christopher Hampson (Director and CEO/Artistic Director of Scottish Ballet) co-directed the feature. Starring are Kayla-Maree Tarantolo and Ishan Mahabir-Stokes alongside Scottish Ballet artists. The choreography was directed by Julia Cheng, Morgann Runacre-Temple, Myles Thatcher, Sophie Laplane, Nicholas Shoesmith, and Andrea Azzari. Beth Allan and Tony Currie produced the film. Watch on Deadline Discussing their retelling, Hampson said: “The film is a Romeo and Juliet story told very much from the viewpoint of Juliet and their reminiscences, their remembering and misremembering in real time.” He added: “It’s probably only two or three minutes of Juliet’s awakeness, but the film delves much deeper into their unconsciousness. Scottish Ballet has made a name for itself in dance film over the last ten years, winning awards for short films and digital innovation, but this is on a whole other level, and I’m thrilled we’ll be in cinemas across the UK, reaching new and established audiences.” The film will screen on August 14 at Edinburgh. Check out a trailer for the film above. articles.title: Netflix Steps Back Into ‘Parasyte’ Universe With ‘Tamiya’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Canadian Entertainment Biz Veterans Team To Launch Paper Route Studios Alon Shtruzman & Scott Einbinder Launch Microdrama Studio New Short Media BuzzFeed Studios & MuVPix Set 100-Title Microdrama Production Pact, Starting With ‘Romeo & Juliet, Reimagined’ View All July 23, 2026 1:47am 'Parasyte: Tamiya' Netflix Netflix has returned to the Parasyte manga universe that began in 2024 with Parasyte: The Grey . A new live-action series, Parasyte: Tamiya will star Shioli Kutsuna ( Sanctuary , Deadpool 2 ) and will stream in 2027. Parasyte: The Grey creator Yeon Sang-ho is returning, having developed Tamiya and co-written the scripts with Ryu Yong-jae. Wowpoint , the Grey producer, is also back, with Kensaku Kakimoto ( Glass Heart ) and Kazuhiro Nakagawa ( Double , Bullet Train Explosion ) directing. Parasyte: The Grey spent four weeks at the top of Netflix’s Global Top 10 Non-English list in 2024, and reached number one in 34 countries. Tamiya will develop the story further. Related Stories Casting Taylor Zakhar Perez, Owen Thiele, Nasim Pedrad & Supriya Ganesh Among Final Additions To Netflix's '13 Going On 30' Reboot News Rory Scovel Sets New Netflix Comedy Special 'Show Must Go On' In the original manga, Ryoko Tamiya is a parasite who takes over the body of a high school teacher. Initially brutal and indiscriminate, she gradually learns from her human surroundings — and upon witnessing a parasite and human sharing a body, begins to wonder whether coexistence might offer her species a better chance of survival than conflict. Watch on Deadline Parasyte: Tamiya will tell Ryoko’s story from the inside: the original human, the parasite who inhabits her and the evolving creature caught between two worlds. Kutsuna plays the character, and said it was “the most challenging role I have ever played in my acting career.” “Ryoko Tamiya is a truly captivating villain in the original manga,” said Yeon. “Her struggles over the nature of her own existence are what elevate the original ‘Parasyte’ from a simple hero-based manga aimed at kids to something deeper. She’s a fascinating character, which drove me to want to tell the story of Parasyte through her perspective. “I wanted to convey her perpetual struggle over the need for parasites to coexist with humans and the issue of their survival, and how she suffers setbacks and learns over time. I think the anguish she experiences is the essence of Parasyte .” Parasyte is a major IP in Japan, having previously been adapted as a film series, an anime and a Korean drama. “This series, which is currently being edited, brings new things to the table compared to past entries in terms of story, cinematography, action, production, you name it,” said Yeon. “It firmly reflects the vision of both directors and is made with great respect for the original manga.” Reid Scott Leaving ‘Law & Order’, James Badge Dale To Succeed Him In Season 26 ‘Stewie’ Voice Cast Set With Thompson, Bayer & Others In ‘Family Guy’ Spinoff Company Seeks 3-Day Hearing As Judge Mulls Injunction; EU OKs Merger Sony Circling Ridley Scott’s ‘Treasure Island’ Starring Hugh Jackman Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Star Toheeb Jimoh & ‘Snow White’s Dujonna Gift Leading BBC’s ‘Open Water’ Adaptation
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max CAA Hires Free Focus Talent Chief For UK Creators Division Candle True Stories Bosses On Revisiting Michael Jackson 20 Years After Martin Bashir Doc & Building A ‘20/20’ True Crime Franchise In The UK Lily Allen Feature Doc Coming To Prime Video View All July 23, 2026 2:26am Toheeb Jimoh (left) and Dujonna Gift Emilio Madrid / Marco Sirisi Emmy-nominated Ted Lasso star Toheeb Jimoh and Snow White ’s Dujonna Gift are leading the BBC ’s adaptation of Caleb Azumah Nelson’s debut novel Open Water . Jimoh plays Marcus opposite Gift’s Effie. Marcus works in retail while trying to develop a career as a photographer. Effie is studying dance at university in Dublin. From the moment they meet, they feel an immediate, undeniable connection. But, as Marcus soon learns, Effie is in a relationship with Marcus’ friend Samuel. It’s a boundary that Marcus is unwilling to cross. Jimoh was Emmy nominated for his role as Sam in Apple TV’s smash comedy Ted Lasso. Gift hasn’t acted in TV before but played Maple, Snow White’s best friend, in Disney’s 2025 live action adaptation. Related Stories News BBC Considers Locking Down iPlayer For Viewers Who Refuse To Pay License Fee News BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: "It's Insulting" Joining Jimoh and Gift are Rhianna Dorris ( Lockwood & Co. ), Lamar Waves ( The Tower ), Nadine Marshall ( Random ), Henrietta Pearl Quartey, Hope Ikpoku Jnr ( Top Boy ), Sekou Diaby ( Animol, Boarders ), Tara Tijani ( Death in Paradise ), Enva Lewis ( How To Have Sex ), Nash Nørgaard ( Death of Ivan Ilyich ), Stevie Odu ( Boiling Point ), Renee Bailey ( Call The Midwife ), Jayden Fowora Knight ( The Nutcracker and the Four Realms), Janina Elkin ( The Queen’s Gambit ), Sherise Blackman ( Bridgerton ), Matthew Dunster ( Coronation Street ), Neve McDonnell ( G’wed ), Javier Bonaparte, Beaux Bryant ( Stolen Dreams Redemption ) and Mo Sesay ( The Diplomat ). Watch on Deadline Unveiled by the BBC two years ago , the show is an adaptation of one of the buzziest books of the decade, with Azumah Nelson set to adapt and direct it himself. His second novel, Small Worlds, was previously optioned by Brock Media. Azumah Nelson said: “The process of bringing Open Water from page to screen has been amazing, and I’ve found some truly outstanding collaborators. We rarely see love stories like this and everyone, from crew to cast, has put their whole heart into this production to make it happen. I can’t wait to share what we’ve been working on.” Jimoh added: “This is a dream project for me. I fell in love with Marcus and Caleb’s story immediately. It’s such a sensitive, character rich, love story, delicately told and full of all the details of the south London I grew up in. It’s such an honour to be a part of this team and I can’t wait to share this one with you all.” Open Water is made by Banijay -backed Mam Tor Productions and B-Side Productions for BBC iPlayer and BBC One. It was commissioned by Lindsay Salt, Director of BBC Drama. Banijay Rights handles international distribution. Azumah Nelson is the lead writer and director and will also serve as executive producer alongside Tally Garner for Mam Tor Productions, Matimba Kabalika for B-Side Productions, and Rebecca Ferguson for the BBC. The series is produced by Karlvyn Dove. Acclaimed composer and musician Cassie Kinoshi will create an original score. articles.title: Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film ‘These Violent Delights’ — First Look Trailer TIFF 2026: ‘Stuffed’ Starring Jodie Comer & Harry Melling Among Discovery Titles View All July 23, 2026 2:30am BFI Isabel Davis has been appointed Director of the BFI Filmmaking Fund. Davis joins the BFI in October 2026 for a five-year fixed term after eight years as Executive Director of Screen Scotland. Before Screen Scotland, Davis served a lengthy term at the BFI, including as the Head of International. Davis takes over from Mia Bays, the outgoing Director of the Filmmaking Fund, who has been in the role since October 2021. Films backed by the BFI during Bays’ tenure include Kneecap, My Father’s Shadow , and the BAFTA-winning animated short Two Black Boys in Paradise . Related Stories News BFI Adds Six Members To Board Of Governors News Edinburgh International Film Festival To Launch UK Film Conference; BFI Head Ben Roberts Set As Inaugural Keynote Speaker Discussing the hire, BFI CEO Ben Roberts said: “Isabel is tenacious when it comes to doing the right thing for UK independent film and filmmakers. This is such a huge job, a cornerstone of UK independent film, and Isabel brings experience, passion, and a national and a global outlook, and a firm commitment to fairness and public service. She will be an asset to the film community and the BFI.” Watch on Deadline Roberts led the recruitment process alongside the BFI’s Deputy CEO Harriet Finney. External panellists were also included during the interview process. They were producers and BFI board members Elizabeth Karlsen and Hakan Kousetta and Nicky Bentham, co-chair of Pact’s Film Producers’ Group. In a statement, Davis said she was “honoured to be stepping into this role at a time when this public funding is critical to building a successful future for UK film and the public value it represents.” “It’s a challenging moment for UK independent film, economically and structurally,” she continued. “But audience appetite for great stories, and for the communal experience of cinema-going, is strikingly resurgent and our filmmaking talent continues to be among the world’s best. Enabling filmmakers to produce work that connects with a broad range of audiences across the UK – through ambition, inventiveness and heart – has to be at the core of our response. Daunting, yes, but exciting too.” Davis ended her statement: “I’ll bring my experience in Scotland to this role, and with it a truly UK-wide perspective on the BFI’s support of independent film. So Scotland hasn’t seen the last of me – nor indeed have Northern Ireland, Wales and the English regions.” Films backed by the BFI Film Fund this year include Shalini Adnani’s Our Share of Sand , which is set for Venice, Theo Rhys’s Stuffed , a Toronto world premiere starring Jodie Comer and Harry Melling, and Clio Barnard’s I See Building Fall Like Lightning , which won the People’s Choice award in Directors’ Fortnight at Cannes. articles.title: Venice Biennale President Slams EU For Pulling Funding Over Russia’s Presence At Art Biennale At Film Festival Conference
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Vertical Takes North America For SXSW Thriller ‘The Saviors’ With Adam Scott & Danielle Deadwyler Charles Gaines Dies: ‘Pumping Iron’ Author Who Helped Launch Arnold Schwarzenegger Was 84 Venice Giornate Degli Autori Unveils 2026 Selection Dedicated To Late Founder Giorgio Gosetti View All July 23, 2026 3:37am Pietrangelo Buttafuoco Getty Images Venice Biennale Foundation President Pietrangelo Buttafuoco hit out at the European Commission on Thursday for its move to withdraw funding over Russia’s participation in its Art Biennale earlier this year. Speaking in opening remarks of the press conference unveiling the lineup for 83rd edition of the Venice Film Festival, Buttafuoco suggested the European Commission was “abandoning” the Biennale and its different chapters. “They are abandoning us today because of a political decision, certainly not a legal decision, and certainly not a cultural decision. They are abandoning us in our journey, but La Biennale cannot accept that,” he said. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement -- Follow Live News Venice Giornate Degli Autori Unveils 2026 Selection Dedicated To Late Founder Giorgio Gosetti His comments follow an announcement earlier this week by the European Commission’s Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) that it was following through with a threat to end €2M ($2.3M) grant in response to the Biennale’s invite to Russia to participate in the Art Biennale. The Biennale responded in a statement that it would lodge an appeal, noting that the withdrawn funds were not used for the Art Biennale but rather the activities of its Cinema Department, and in particular its Biennale College and the Venice Production Bridge initiatives. The stand-off began with the opening of the Art Biennale in April, which was marked by protests over Russia’s return and the resignation of the international jury. The European Union’s head of foreign policy Kaja Kallas said at the time that the invite to Russia violated EU sanctions imposed on Russia in the wake of its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and the subsequent ongoing war. Continuing his rebuttal at the film festival press conference, Buttafuoco said bowing to the EU’s demands would fly in the face of the Biennale’s principles. “We would renounce our principles of freedom of expression, of research, fantasy, imagination, values that for 131 years have been characterized this institution,” he said. Referring to the fable of The Wolf & the Lamb, Buttafuoco detailed three letters the European Commission had sent to the Biennale, suggesting the European Union was tantamount to the wolf, and the Cinema Department to the lamb. “In the third letter, the wolf simply eats the lamb,” he said. articles.title: Venice Film Festival Lineup: Casey Affleck, Werner Herzog, Hirokazu Koreeda, Lee Chang-Dong & Martin McDonagh In Competition
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Venice Film Festival Lineup Announcement — Follow Live Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund Scottish Ballet & Forest Of Black Partner With Tull Stories To Release Dance Film ‘These Violent Delights’ — First Look Trailer TIFF 2026: ‘Stuffed’ Starring Jodie Comer & Harry Melling Among Discovery Titles View All July 23, 2026 3:52am Jack O'Connell In 'Ink' Danny Boyle Alberto Barbera presided over a lengthy press conference Thursday morning, during which he announced the stacked lineup for this year’s Venice Film Festival, which runs from 2-12 September. Scroll down for the full list of titles. The lineup is expansive, with several big names returning to the festival across its many strands. However, there are notably no big studios titles in competition. In competition, Casey Affleck will debut Company , his latest film as a director. Previously described as a “gothic horror”, the film stars Nick Nolte ( Cape Fear ), Adelaide Clemens ( The Great Gatsby ), Ben Mendelsohn ( The Dark Knight Rises ), Scoot McNairy ( A Complete Unknown ), Emily Alyn Lind ( We Were Liars ) and Caylee Cowan. Related Stories News Venice Giornate Degli Autori Unveils 2026 Selection Dedicated To Late Founder Giorgio Gosetti Festivals Venice Critics' Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia South Korean filmmaker Lee Chang-Dong returns to feature filmmaking with Possible Love, his first film since Burning (2018). Japanese filmmaker Hirokazu Koreeda lands at Venice with Look Back , his second festival title of 2026. The filmmaker was also at Cannes in May with Sheep in the Box. Martin McDonagh returns to Venice with Wild Horse Nine , his first feature since The Banshees of Inisherin , which won Best Screenplay and Actor at Venice in 2022 before landing 9 Oscar noms. Veteran Italian filmmaker Nanni Moretti returns to Venice with a film for the first time since 1989. The feature is Succederà Questa Notte and stars Louis Garrel. Watch on Deadline Out of Competition, Paul Schrader will screen a new project titled The Basics Of Philosophy starring Jack Huston and Sofia Boutella. The film is said to follow a repressed philosophy professor who has been grappling with lingering guilt over a decision from his past when the victim suddenly returns to his life. Venice regular Luca Guadagnino will be on the Lido this year but not with his Open AI feature Artificial . The Italian filmmaker will instead screen his long-gestating Bernardo Bertolucci documentary Joie De Vivre . The film runs seven hours long. Wim Wenders is also out of competition with a doc on the Swiss architect Peter Zumthor. The festival has already announced that this year’s opening title will be Danny Boyle’s Rupert Murdoch biopic Ink. The film, starring Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce and Claire Foy, will screen on September 2 in the Sala Grande at the Palazzo del Cinema on the Lido. Boyle directs the feature from a screenplay written by James Graham (Dear England), based on his Tony-nominated play Ink . O’Connell stars as The Sun newspaper editor Larry Lamb with Pearce as Rupert Murdoch. Claire Foy is Jules Davies. Announcing the title earlier this summer, Barbera described the title as an “account of publisher Rupert Murdoch’s acquisition of the daily newspaper The Sun, which he entrusted to the unscrupulous Larry Lamb, turning it into Britain’s best-selling tabloid at the expense of its rival, The Mirror. ” The festival’s closing title will be Dio ride , written and directed by Giovanni Veronesi ( The King’s Musketeers ). The film will screen out of competition. Pierfrancesco Favino, Silvio Orlando, Alma Noce, Francesco Gheghi, Maurizio Lombardi, Paolo Rossi and Carlo Cecchi star in the film. George Clooney and Ellen Burstyn will be the recipients of the Venice Film Festival ’s Golden Lion for lifetime achievement this year. Maggie Gyllenhaal will serve as the competition jury president. She will be joined by Kaouther Ben Hania, Daniel Blumberg, Francesco Casetti, Xavier Giannoli, Shahrbanoo Sadat, and Johnnie To. The festival will run from September 2 – 12. The film follows a woman who returns to her hometown of Harbin after years living in the United States and finds herself caught between two realities: the life she has built with her girlfriend, and the expectations of her family and community. Produced as a Hong Kong-US collaboration, the film explores identity, family, cultural displacement, and the difficult choices faced by those navigating between tradition and self-determination. Related Stories News Venice Film Festival Lineup: Casey Affleck, Werner Herzog, Hirokazu Koreeda, Lee Chang-Dong & Martin McDonagh In Competition News Venice Biennale President Slams EU For Pulling Funding Over Russia's Presence At Art Biennale At Film Festival Conference “ Big Little Things represents the arrival of a distinctive new filmmaking voice,” said Fred Tsui, founder and CEO of Moebius Entertainment. “Michelle Zhou captures the quiet but profound conflicts that define many lives today – the tension between personal truth and the roles we inherit. Her film is deeply intimate yet universally resonant, and we believe audiences around the world will connect with the heroine’s journey.” Watch on Deadline The film was previously presented with the Activator Market Potential Award at the 2025 Golden Horse Film Project Promotion (FPP) in Taipei, where it was selected among the year’s most promising projects from emerging Asian filmmakers. Moebius Entertainment is handling festival representation and worldwide sales rights. The company also recently picked up Taiwanese filmmaker Fiona Roan Feng-I’s Happily Ever After , which will make its world premiere in the Special Presentations section of the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF). articles.title: How Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Conquered the Box Office
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All July 21, 2026 5:21pm Matt Damon and Zendaya in 'The Odyssey.' Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Christopher Nolan ‘s box office journey with The Odyssey has gotten off to an eye-opening start . If there were any questions regarding whether a nearly three-hour, R-rated adaptation of a 2,700-year-old Greek poem — not to mention a movie that initially got caught up in the culture wars — would find success, those concerns were swiftly vanquished. In landing 2026’s biggest live-action opening weekend, The Odyssey brought home $123.5 million domestically with a global launch of $263.7 million, with the latter marking the accomplished filmmaker’s highest-grossing worldwide opening ever. Related Stories Movies Snoop Dogg Biopic Lands Summer 2027 Release From Universal Movies 'Other Mommy' Trailer: Jessica Chastain Returns to Horror as a Body-Twisting Doppelganger It’s not news that Nolan, hot off his first best director Oscar for 2023’s Oppenheimer , has become a brand unto himself as he continues his run as one of Hollywood’s most sure-thing filmmakers. But the fact that half of the movie’s audiences were between the ages of 18 and 34 confirmed that he has captured the excitement of Gen Z and younger millennial filmgoers as much as that of older viewers who might typically be more drawn to an adaptation of classic literature. Audiences cited Nolan as their top reason for seeing The Odyssey , according to PostTrak surveys, which is no small feat, given that the star-studded cast includes Matt Damon , Tom Holland , Robert Pattinson , Anne Hathaway , Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya , Charlize Theron and no shortage of others. The Odyssey Universal “We had high expectations for the movie and high expectations for our performance, and it exceeded both,” IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond tells The Hollywood Reporter . Indeed, fans were focused on experiencing the film on IMAX after The Odyssey became the first narrative feature shot entirely on the company’s cameras. “Chris knows how to use IMAX technology and the IMAX brand as well as anyone on the planet.” The Odyssey is unlikely to drift away anytime soon, with Gelfond pointing out that IMAX presales for the Universal Pictures film’s forthcoming sophomore frame “are equivalent to some of our really best movies’ opening weekends.” Competing studios presumably anticipated the high demand, as there are no wide releases scheduled for this coming weekend in between The Odyssey and the July 31 release of Sony’s similarly anticipated Spider-Man: Brand New Day , representing a rarity for a coveted July frame. “Presales are just incredibly backloaded because we see people waiting to get the best seat that they can and see it in the way that the filmmaker intends it to be seen,” notes Fandango director of analytics and Box Office Theory founder Shawn Robbins. “There are plenty of theaters around the country where shows are almost — if not totally — sold out into the second, third, fourth weekend of the film’s run. So it definitely signals that The Odyssey will be around in theaters for quite a while, just like Oppenheimer was.” Director Christopher Nolan (left), with Matt Damon (as Odysseus) and Zendaya (as Athena), on the set of The Odyssey. Universal Pictures The appeal for younger audiences can be felt not just in ticket sales but through engagement in other ways, as social media memes embraced The Odyssey , which centers on Damon’s Odysseus making his arduous trip back to Ithaca after the Trojan War. Additionally, the film became the fastest to hit a million watches on Letterboxd by accomplishing the feat in six days, half the time that it took previous champ Barbie and other titles since, like Project Hail Mary and Backrooms . Notably, 2010’s Inception was the first feature to reach the seven-figure milestone, proving Nolan’s longstanding credibility with cinephiles. “Nolan has cultivated such an incredibly diverse audience, and a lot of it is that Gen Z and younger millennial side,” says Robbins. “That’s really all thanks to his library of films, especially over the last 10 or 15 years. We point to The Dark Knight and Inception and his earlier work, but also look at [2014’s] Interstellar . We saw high demand when Interstellar rereleased in theaters about a year and a half ago. It just kept gaining a following, and a lot of that was among younger moviegoers. With all of his films, there are tons of content creators breaking down his storytelling, his writing, maybe the cinematography or the music. There are just so many elements to his movies that intrigue and envelop people.” In recent years, studios have emphasized the importance of eventizing filmgoing, hoping for buzzy word of mouth to encourage audiences to experience a project in a way that they can’t from their couch, and premium large format screens have emerged as a key way to accomplish this. The word of mouth was clearly stellar, between the film’s A CinemaScore and a 94 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, tied for Nolan’s best mark ever. This meant that viewers flocked not only to IMAX theaters — which pulled in $51.8 million globally to account for 23 percent of The Odyssey’ s haul — but especially to the 41 theaters worldwide that screen IMAX 70mm film. As for whether IMAX can expand the number of screens showing 70mm, Gelfond notes that the theater count is up from 30 at the time of the Oppenheimer release. “There are some inherent limitations on our ability to do it, including finding boxes that big to fit the right aspect ratio and finding projectors that we can refurbish,” he says. “We’re always looking, but it’s complicated.” The exec notes that he did see online conversation surrounding some individuals feeling priced out of the IMAX experience and adds about the company that does not set its ticket prices: “We’re as aggressive as we can be. We want to provide a great experience. We want the right aspect ratio. We want the projector to show the best image they can. We’re sensitive to the demand, but we’re not going to lower our quality standards.” After a bumpy stretch of July weekends that saw underperforming openings for such franchise entries as Supergirl , Minions & Monsters and Moana , the industry is quickly embracing the newfound optimism. And while Nolan may have stood out among his movie’s bold-faced names, there’s no doubt that the starry cast added to the spectacle. Among those sparking social media chatter for The Odyssey was Holland, whose role as Odysseus’ son, Telemachus, gave him the opportunity for a high-profile performance without his superhero suit (although he’ll be onscreen as Spidey soon enough, too). “His performance in The Odyssey shows a new side of him that will really just continue to grow his fan base,” observes Robbins. Perhaps Nolan himself best summed up a key element of his own movies’ appeal when recently explaining to THR about a goal that he carries throughout his work: “I try to leave each film I do with thematic concerns and questions that stay a little bit open for me — and hopefully the audience, too.” THR

articles.title: ‘La La Land’ 10th Anniversary Poster Finally Corrects Ryan Gosling’s Flat Hand
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 21, 2026 5:25pm 'La La Land' 2026 poster. Lionsgate Ryan Gosling can finally sleep at night. After nearly a decade of joking that his pose on the original La La Land poster “haunted” him, Lionsgate has finally fixed it with a new poster celebrating the film’s 10th anniversary. The updated artwork arrives as La La Land heads back to theaters beginning Aug. 16, when the Oscar-winning musical will return to Dolby Cinema at AMC Theatres for its anniversary re-release. A La La Land musical is also currently in development for Broadway . Related Stories Movies Nicolas Winding Refn Reveals the Chaotic Making of 'Drive': "Most Everyone Hated It" Movies 'Passion of the Christ' Set For Theatrical Return The original poster for the 2016 film features Emma Stone and Gosling dancing against the Los Angeles skyline. Both actors have one arm raised, but while Stone’s hand is extended up, Gosling tilted his hand flat — a choice he has since joked he regretted. Speaking to The Wall Street Journal in 2024, the Barbie star reflected on why the pose still “haunts” him. “Maybe La La Land ,” he said when asked if there was a role he’d like to do over. “There’s a moment that haunts me where we’re dancing, Emma and I, and I didn’t know this would become the poster for the movie, but I thought we were supposed to have our hands up and I thought it’d be cool to put my hand [flat].” “Even though everyone told me it wasn’t cool, I was sure it was cooler,” he continued. “Now when I look at it, and I have to see it all the time, you know what would’ve been cooler… [the correct pose]. It just killed the energy that way. I call it La La hand.” Gosling even poked fun at the moment earlier this year while promoting Project Hail Mary , releasing a video in March in which he finally corrected his “La La hand.” Directed by Damien Chazelle , La La Land follows aspiring actress Mia (Stone) and jazz musician Sebastian (Gosling) as they chase their Hollywood dreams while falling in love. The film won six Academy Awards, including best director for Chazelle and best actress for Stone. It is also remembered for the infamous best picture mix-up at the 2017 Oscars, when La La Land was mistakenly announced as the winner before it was revealed that Moonlight had actually taken home the award. articles.title: ‘In the City’ Reunion Recap: Lindsay and Whitney’s Heated Exchange, Amanda Reveals She and West Haven’t Said “I Love You”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 21, 2026 6:36pm 'In the City' reunion. Charles Sykes/Bravo Logo text [This story contains spoilers from part one of the In the City season one reunion.] There’s more drama in New York City. Bravo aired part one of the In the City reunion Tuesday night, bringing together Lindsay Hubbard , Kyle Cooke , Amanda Batula , Danielle Olivera, Eoin Heavey, Andrea Denver, Lexi Sundin, Nick Barber, Yvonne Najor, Georgina Ferzil, Whitney Fransway, Kenny Martin and Gavin Moseley for the Summer House spinoff’s first-ever reunion. Sitting down with Andy Cohen , the cast revisited the season’s biggest moments — and everything that’s unfolded since season one wrapped filming. Related Stories TV 'In the City' Concludes With Two-Part Reunion: Where to Watch 'Summer House' Spinoff's Cast Sit-Down Online TV Between 'Summer House' and 'In the City,' Lindsay Hubbard Doesn't Have Time to Slow Down The reunion opened with Amanda, who shared an update on her relationship with West Wilson. After addressing the viral photos from Italy that made it look like she was spitting into his mouth — “It was an olive,” she clarified — Amanda also reflected on the Summer House reunion , admitting she was on beta blockers too, not just West, and was “disappointed” by how defensive she came across. When Andy asked whether she and West had taken the next step and said “I love you,” Amanda initially responded, “Not really.” Pressed further, she confirmed they still haven’t — though the pair are now monogamous. (The reunion was filmed June 11.) Danielle admitted she was disappointed and shocked to learn Amanda and West were still together. “I honestly hate that you doubled down and are pursuing this relationship with him all the way, going to Italy with him,” Danielle said. “I know you had to make a decision one way or the other. I just wish, for you, that you would take some time just for yourself. Be alone.” Amanda and West publicly revealed they were dating just two months after she and Kyle announced the end of their marriage, drawing criticism from fans because West had previously been romantically involved with Amanda’s friend, Ciara Miller. Bravo also recently announced that Amanda won’t return for season 11 of Summer House , which is currently filming. Amanda went on to praise Kyle for supporting her through the backlash, despite their divorce. “I’m eternally grateful for Kyle. I think it just shows how much we do have love for each other, and I think it’s something that we’ve made clear from the very beginning,” she said. “Unfortunately, we could not communicate, we could not get along in our marriage, but that doesn’t take away from the friendship and the love that we’ve had for each other this whole time. Which is also why, when we first separated, I was standing up for him because I didn’t want people to attack him. And I’m just really appreciative that he’s been there for me as well because if anyone knows each other better, it’s the two of us.” Elsewhere, Kyle shared that he’s dating again and recently spent time with Southern Charm star Salley Carson, while Lindsay said she isn’t looking for anything serious. The night’s most heated exchange, however, centered on Lindsay and Whitney, whose feud over Whitney’s “single mom card” comment exploded during last week’s finale . During the finale, Whitney accused Lindsay of using the “single mom card” to get her way when she took the primary bedroom instead of giving it to Yvonne and Nick following the drama surrounding their wedding. Whitney also criticized Lindsay for having a nanny. “I almost threw up watching this,” Lindsay said. “It was so much worse than it was explained to me.” Despite Whitney’s repeated apologies, Lindsay wasn’t ready to forgive. “I cried about what you said for six months. You’re gonna need about 15 more apologies to any mom in the entire world,” Lindsay fired back. “Really poor choice of words.” Kenny defended Whitney, explaining earlier in the reunion that some of his actions throughout the season were influenced by grieving the loss of his mother. “Lindsay, you collect apologies like you collect souls,” he said. Gavin also clarified his earlier comments about Whitney, explaining that when he called her “boring” during the season, he was actually frustrated that she and Kenny were portraying their relationship as perfect while they were still working through issues behind the scenes. Some arguments remained unresolved, and based on the preview for part two, the tension is only escalating. Based on the teaser trailer, next week’s reunion sees Amanda once again accuse Kyle of having an affair during their marriage — but this time, she claims she only recently learned about it. The In the City reunion part two airs Tuesday, July 28, at 8 p.m. ET. All episodes of In the City are streaming on Peacock. THR

articles.title: Zendaya’s Best Press Tour Looks, From ‘Dune’ to ‘Challengers’ to ‘The Odyssey’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 21, 2026 9:42pm Published on July 21, 2026 Zendaya for 'Spider-Man: No Way Home,' Dune: Part Two,' 'Challengers' and 'The Drama' press tours. Amy Sussman/Getty Images; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Warner Bros. Pictures; Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images; Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images One thing about Zendaya: She and her longtime stylist, Law Roach, are always going to deliver on a red carpet. The pair has become known for fully committing to a theme, specifically when it comes to dressing for a film or television show’s press tour. They’ve become modern pioneers of “method dressing,” where they match Zendaya’s wardrobes on the red carpet to her projects’ themes and narratives. From the Dune films to Challengers to the Spider-Man movies and The Odyssey , the actress has turned promotional opportunities into high-fashion moments with archival looks, bold outfits and designs that align with her characters. Below, The Hollywood Reporter ranks Zendaya’s press tour styling over the years. ‘Spider-Man: Homecoming’ Image Credit: Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images; Carlos Alvarez/Getty Images As Zendaya started pivoting away from Disney Channel, she scored her first Hollywood blockbuster role in 2017’s Spider-Man: Homecoming . It’s also where she met her now-husband, Tom Holland, who plays Peter Parker. With this being her first major press tour, Zendaya still seemed to be finding her voice in fashion. Though her looks weren’t fully cohesive and aligned with a theme just yet, she and Roach still brought stunning looks to the red carpet. At the film’s L.A. premiere, Zendaya wore a pink Ralph & Russo gown, Casadei heels and Bulgari jewels. At a photocall in Madrid, Spain, she sported a blue Jonathan Simkhai dress and Rihanna x Manolo Blahnik heels. See more of her Spider-Man: Homecoming press tour looks here . ‘Space Jam: A New Legacy’ Image Credit: Kevin Winter/Getty Images For the Los Angeles premiere of 2021’s Space Jam: A New Legacy , Zendaya knew she had one moment to make a statement and she left it all on the table (or the red carpet, so to speak). The actress didn’t do a ton of press for this live-action/animated hybrid film, so she really made the premiere a moment with a colorful look, channeling Lola Bunny, the character she voiced. Zendaya wore a colorblock ensemble that featured a jacket and short shorts by Moschino. She paired it with Bulgari small hoop earrings and rings, as well as white stiletto heels. ‘Euphoria’ Image Credit: Monica Schipper/Getty Images; Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic for HBO; Frazer Harrison/Getty Images The premieres for Euphoria — the hit HBO show that earned Zendaya her first two Emmys and cemented her status as a serious dramatic actress post-Disney — really highlight her style evolution over the years. While there’s not a set theme for her looks, as there weren’t lengthy global press tours for each of the show’s seasons, she still managed to serve on the carpet. For season one in 2019, Zendaya went for a more innocent look with a white, spaghetti-strap mini dress, featuring a sheer ruffle detail, from the Nina Ricci Fall 2019 collection. She paired it with white Le Silla heels. Fast forward to 2022, and Zendaya delivered an edgier look at the season two premiere, similar to the show’s second installment. She wore a vintage Valentino black-and-white striped form-fitting dress. And more recently, at the season three premiere in 2026, the actress stepped out in a much more mature look from Ashi Studio. The deep brown sleeveless halter dress featured a high neckline, low back and flowy train. ‘Spider-Man: Far From Home’ Image Credit: Kevin Winter/Getty Images; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Sony For the Spider-Man: Far from Home press tour in 2019, Zendaya brought her own version of the famed superhero to the red carpet. Though she plays MJ, Peter Parker’s romantic interest in the film franchise, the actress channeled Spider-Man himself at the Los Angeles premiere, sporting a geometric red and black sequin Armani gown. She paired the dress with black Christian Louboutin “So Kate” pumps (which have become her signature red carpet shoe). “If Spider-Man were a girl, this would be her Spidey suit or her uniform,” Roach previously told THR of the look. As for the London photo call at the Tower of London, Zendaya stood on business in a chic, structured Alexandre Vauthier suit, paired with a white button-down shirt and black Christian Louboutin pumps. She also tied the look all together with red hair, a nod to Peter Parker’s favorite color. ‘The Greatest Showman’ Image Credit: Lisa Maree Williams/Getty Images; Carlos Tischler/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images; Michael Loccisano/Getty Images The press tour for 2017’s The Greatest Showman was really the first time Zendaya fully leaned into cohesive themed looks for the red carpet. She and Roach went the whimsical route, inspired by the movie’s circus and ethereal creatures. Some of the most memorable outfits include a custom Moschino monarch butterfly dress designed by Jeremy Scott, paired with black strappy heels, for the Australian premiere. At the film’s premiere in Mexico City, the actress sported a ringmaster-inspired look from Ralph Lauren Collection. It featured a red tuxedo jacket, black tuxedo trousers and a white collared shirt, paired with black pumps. Lastly, but certainly not least, Zendaya stunned at the world premiere in New York City in a black and red tiered tulle ball gown from the Viktor & Rolf Spring 2018 collection. ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ Image Credit: Amy Sussman/Getty Images; Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images Zendaya was really channeling her Spidey-senses for the Spider-Man: No Way Home press tour in 2021. The Emmy winner stepped in multiple looks that featured spiderweb motifs — it doesn’t get much more on brand than that. At the world premiere in Los Angeles, she left everyone speechless (even Holland, as seen in an interview with Entertainment Tonight ) once she arrived, wearing a sheer, beige custom Valentino gown covered in black spiderweb embroidery. She also paired it with a spiderweb-designed lace mask and Christian Louboutin pumps. Zendaya brought more spiderwebs to the London photo call with her menswear-inspired Alexander McQueen outfit. The look included an oversized gray blazer embellished with a crystal spiderweb-like design and thigh-high black boots with the same embellishments. She also wore spiderweb earrings. ‘Dune: Part One’ Image Credit: Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images; Jeff Spicer/Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Warner BrosKristy Sparow/Getty Images; If Zendaya’s Dune: Part One red carpet outfits had your jaw on the floor (truthfully, mine was), just wait until we get to Part Two . But first, let’s take a moment to appreciate the high-fashion looks that kicked off the film franchise’s promotions. The actress and Roach were fully committed to the movie’s desert and warrior themes with her attire during the 2021 press run. At the Venice Film Festival premiere, she walked the carpet in a custom, wet-look Balmain gown. The dress’s sand-colored leather was molded to her body for a sculpted, draped effect. When Zendaya attended the Paris photocall at Le Grand Rex, she wore a plum two-piece Maison Alaïa look that featured a knitted, backless top and a matching pencil skirt with an extravagant fur hem. At the Dune U.K. Special Screening in London, she arrived in a Rick Owens sculptural sequin cream-colored gown that felt quite sci-fi inspired. ‘Challengers’ Image Credit: James Gourley/Getty Images; Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images; Monica Schipper/Getty Images Zendaya is used to bringing the heat to the screen rather than the court, but that doesn’t mean she can’t shut down a red carpet with some Tennis-inspired looks when needed. And it was absolutely needed (and wanted by her fans) during the press tour for Luca Guadagnino’s Challengers . The actress started on a high note at the Australian premiere with a look that screamed tenniscore: a custom Loewe gown designed by Jonathan Anderson — who costumed the film — that featured a tennis player and ball motif. Zendaya continued the theme at the London premiere with a white sequined country club-esque halter dress by Thom Browne that also featured a tennis racket motif. As for the Los Angeles premiere, though the actress stepped away from tenniscore for a moment, she still served in a Vera Wang black-and-pink gown. Some other honorable mentions that also deserve to be highlighted below include the archival look by Vivienne Westwood from the Spring/Summer 1994 “Café Society” ready-to-wear collection, a custom silver-colored Loewe tennis dress and a retro-chic mini dress from the Louis Vuitton by Marc Jacobs archives. Zendaya for ‘Challengers’ press tour. Jeff Spicer/Getty Images; Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images; Kristy Sparow/Getty Images ‘The Drama’ Image Credit: Phillip Faraone/Getty Images; Aurore Marechal/Getty Images; Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images; Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images Zendaya had a specific theme in mind going into The Drama press tour. With the dark romantic comedy/psychological thriller being centered on a wedding that goes wrong, the actress chose to stun in several bridal-inspired looks that align with the wedding tradition of “something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue.” The actress kicked things off with “something old” at the L.A. premiere, sporting a white Vivienne Westwood gown that she previously wore at the 2015 Academy Awards. Next came “something new,” and she wore a custom Louis Vuitton dress that featured an oversized black bow in the back at the Paris premiere. As for “something borrowed,” Cate Blanchett loaned Zendaya a black dress made custom by Giorgio Armani Privé for the film’s Rome premiere. Lastly, but certainly not least, she stunned at the New York premiere in a black and blue Schiaparelli gown to complete her method dressing streak with “something blue.” ‘Dune: Part Two’ Image Credit: Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Warner Bros. Pictures; Angel Delgado/Getty Images; Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images It’s safe to say that some of Zendaya’s looks during the Dune: Part Two press tour will definitely be remembered for decades to come. At every event for the film, she kept everyone stunned, delivering futuristic sci-fi and desert-chic looks that fully highlighted the film’s mood and themes. At the New York premiere, she wore a cream-colored gown with gold detailing at the hem, designed by Stéphane Rolland couture. One of Zendaya’s most daring and iconic looks to date was at the London premiere, where she sported an archival 1995 Thierry Mugler chrome cyborg suit . The actress’ method dressing continued at the premiere in Mexico City, wearing a custom Bottega Veneta two-piece look that featured a cropped wool flannel turtleneck and matching high-slit skirt. Then at a photo call in London, she turned heads in a “pre-runway” ensemble from Roksanda that featured a three-piece dark plum suit. See more memorable looks from the Dune: Part Two press tour here . ‘The Odyssey’ Image Credit: Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images; Aurore Marechal/Getty Images; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Universal Pictures; Shane Anthony Sinclair/Getty Images Zendaya quite literally served goddess during the press tour for Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey . The actress embodied her character in the film, Athena — the Greek goddess of wisdom and warfare who serves as Odysseus’s (Matt Damon) divine protector — on the many red carpets around the globe. In one of her first looks, she wore a custom ivory-colored Jacquemus draped dress with a low-plunging back for a photo call in London. She finished the look off with large Glenn Spiro gold earrings. Then at the Paris premiere, she stunned in a custom white-colored Louis Vuitton gown that features ruffle puff sleeves. At the world premiere held in London, Zendaya stunned in a couture Schiaparelli gown that was fresh off the runway earlier in the day. The dress featured a sculpted white bustier breastplate and a beaded fringe skirt. And the actress definitely saved one of her best looks for last with the jaw-dropping Matières Fécales dress at the New York City premiere. The look featured feather embellishments throughout, paired with large white feathered angel wings. *** Zendaya is booked and busy this year, with two more projects on the way: Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Dune: Part Three . And it’s safe to say I’m already sat at the dinner table, waiting for which stunning looks she’s going to feed everyone with next. THR

articles.title: Rebel Wilson Cleared in ‘The Deb’ Defamation Case
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All July 22, 2026 1:29am Rebel Wilson and Charlotte MacInnes. Sitthixay Ditthavong / Sydney Morning Herald via Getty Images; Don Arnold/Getty Images A Sydney court has cleared Rebel Wilson of defamation claims made by Australian actress Charlotte MacInnes, who starred in Wilson’s 2024 film The Deb . MacInnes had sued Wilson for Instagram posts the Pitch Perfect star had made on her own account in 2024 and 2025 that saw Wilson accuse MacInnes of retracting her complaint of sexual harassment against a film producer so she could further her career. MacInnes has denied Wilson’s claim. On Wednesday, the BBC reports that Australian federal court jude Elizabeth Raper dismissed the case against Wilson, saying that the claim that MacInnes had changed her story about the incident was not defamatory and that the actress had failed to establish the posts had caused or were likely to serious harm. Additionally, MacInnes was ordered to pay Wilson’s legal costs. Related Stories Movies 'The Brutalist' EP, 'Nawi' Makers Strike Three-Film Co-Pro Deal, Set Kenya Soccer Doc 'Champions of Nowhere' (Exclusive) Movies Nicolas Winding Refn Reveals the Chaotic Making of 'Drive': "Most Everyone Hated It" The defamation sprung from a September 2023 incident, where The Deb’s lead actress MacInnes went for a swim at Bondi Beach with Amanda Ghost , a British entertainment executive, a former president of Epic Records and one of the producers of Wilson’s film. According to the BBC, Ghost suffered an allergic reaction and both Ghost and MacInnes returned to the producer’s apartment, where they ended up in the bath together wearing swimsuits. Justice Raper cited the bath incident in her decision. “To say that the circumstance surrounding how they came to be in the bath are unusual would be an understatement,” she told the court. The Sydney defamation case is part of a larger set of legal cases related to The Deb , the Australian musical film comedy that Wilson produced, directed and had a support role in. In July 2024, Wilson revealed the acrimony behind the scenes, accusing the film’s producers Gregor Cameron, Vince Holden and Ghost of blocking the film’s premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival as well as making claims of embezzlement of $900,000 from the The Deb ‘s budget and Ghost’s inappropriate behavior towards the film’s lead actress MacInnes. In response, Cameron, Holden and Ghost filed a defamation lawsuit against Wilson. In January , a Los Angeles judge has tossed most of Wilson‘s lawsuit against The Deb producers, calling many of the allegations “conclusory without specific facts” and “abusive.” THR

articles.title: After German Broadcaster Yanks “Antifascist” Song, Musicians Give Guerrilla YouTube Concert
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 22, 2026 2:31am Pianist Igor Levit and singer Danger Dan at a 2022 concert in Berlin. Carsten Koall/picture alliance via Getty Images Let’s talk about fascism, baby. That was the message from German musicians Danger Dan and Igor Levit at a benefit concert in Berlin Tuesday night. The duo, known for their political activism, were set to perform their new “antifascist” song “Keine Angst” (No Fear), on Die Anstalt , a popular German topical comedy show. But the network, public broadcaster ZDF , pulled them. The channel said the song could be considered an incitement to violence and was not in line with their program guidelines. Related Stories News Rebel Wilson Cleared in 'The Deb' Defamation Case Movies Snoop Dogg Biopic Lands Summer 2027 Release From Universal So the pair put on a concert at Berlin’s Columbia theater, and live-streamed it on YouTube. Instead of talking about being canceled by ZDF, and the fierce debate it has sparked in the German media about freedom of speech, the band focused on raising the alarm about the rise of Germany ‘s far-right. “How should we deal with the fascists who are entering parliaments and taking to the streets?” Danger Dan asked the Berlin audience. “How do we deal with right-wing violence that is exploding and becoming increasingly brutal?” “How do we help people [who] fear leaving their homes because Nazis are patrolling?” added Levit. “How can one alleviate their fear and show them they are not alone?” ZDF director General Norbert Himmler defended the decision to pull the band. Their new song is “a manual for violent left-wing resistance,” Himmler told German newspaper Süddeutschen Zeitung . The lyrics to “Keine Angst” include lines suggesting activists out “nazi pigs” by doxxing far-right extremists. The song ends with a what appears to be a friendly greeting to left-wing activists who have been either convicted of, or are on trial for, violent attacks against members of the far-right. But not everyone agrees with ZDF’s decision. The hosts of Die Anstalt called the network’s decision “cowardly,” and used their show to argue that ZDF should have let Levit and Danger Dan perform. The comedians attended Tuesday’s concert, sitting in the front row. In an open letter on Monday, eight members of ZDF’s television council called out Himmler for pulling the song. “ZDF missed an opportunity to spark a debate about right-wing extremism in Germany and the various ways to combat it,” the letter reads. “The cancellation of the performance by Danger Dan and Igor Levit thus demonstrates not only a lack of courage but also a lack of trust in the program’s editorial team…We fear this could have a chilling effect.” The debate is coming against the backdrop of rising support for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), a xenophobic and anti-migrant party that is currently leading national opinion polls. Many consider the AfD a threat to German democracy and have called for the party to be banned. The party is not currently in power anywhere in the country but that could change this year. The AfD is within striking distance of achieving an absolute majority in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt in September. THR

articles.title: Elon Musk Says Grok Will Make Feature-Length, AI-Generated and “Historically Accurate” ‘The Odyssey’ Movie Before the Year Ends
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 22, 2026 2:55am Jimmy Gonzales, Matt Damon, Himesh Patel in 'The Odyssey.' Melinda Sue Gordon/© Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection And so Elon Musk ‘s anti- Odyssey campaign continues: The X owner and recently-anointed trillionaire has vowed that his AI social media bot, Grok, will make “a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer” before the end of the year. His post on Wednesday was accompanied by a three-minute AI-generated short that a follower had made using Grok Imagine. It comes as the South African businessman continues to rile up his supporters in a real culture war over Christopher Nolan ‘s box office behemoth. His commentary on the film dates to January, when rumors of Lupita Nyong’o’s casting as Helen of Troy first began circulating. He has criticized Nolan and Hollywood for their “woke” agenda, despite wide acknowledgement from actual historians that Homer’s work is, of course, a piece of fiction. Related Stories Movies How Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' Conquered the Box Office Movies Matt Damon Reveals Why He Had Female Stunt Double for 'Odyssey' Scene: "Greatest Arms I've Ever Seen" Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer https://t.co/bVHzUmY9WN — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) July 22, 2026 In May, Musk agreed with a racist comment made by a far-right journalist who took aim at the Oscar-winning actress’ involvement: “We’re told that we shouldn’t object to Helen of Troy being portrayed as a black woman,” said Daily Wire ‘s Matt Walsh. “And yet if a major Hollywood studio made a film set in Africa and cast a white woman as ‘the most beautiful woman in Africa,’ those same people would literally riot in the street. If, say, Sydney Sweeney was cast in the role, they’d be driven to murderous violence. We all know this is the case.” Musk chimed in via the comment section of Walsh’s post: “Absolutely true. Such hypocrisy in Hollywood.” It isn’t the only cast announcement that the Tesla and SpaceX founder has taken issue with. When rumors surfaced that trans actor Elliot Page might be cast as Achilles, he reacted even more forcefully, saying: “One of the dumbest and most twisted things I’ve ever heard.” (Musk, who has a trans daughter from his first marriage, Vivian Jenna Wilson, has historically made transphobic attacks against his own daughter. She has cut ties with him.) It’s also worth noting that Page does not play Achilles in Nolan’s film — he portrays Sinon, a Greek soldier incorporated into the story from Virgil’s epic poem The Aeneid . So, it isn’t entirely surprising Musk would attempt to make his own Odyssey with what will be — judging from the short snippet he reposted on Wednesday — an all-white cast. Grok Imagine’s retelling of the Homer epic will likely only make Nolan’s feat look even more of a masterpiece, especially since it was shot entirely on Imax film and used extremely little CGI. Nolan himself has called the backlash over historical accuracy “irrelevant.” He said: “Comes with the territory… These conversations that happen before people see the film — they’re always irrelevant, because no one having them knows what the film actually is yet.” And for all of the outrage Musk has drummed up around The Odyssey , the film has not notably suffered at the box office at all. The retelling of classical Greek mythology got the box office back on track over the weekend, scoring $124.5 million on 3,900 North American screens. Earning an A CinemaScore from audiences, the film sailed away to 2026’s biggest live-action opening, with only Toy Story 5 ($159 million) and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie ($131 million) debuting above it. The Odyssey also claimed the top R-rated opening of the year and Universal’s highest weekend launch ever for an R-rated movie. Globally, The Odyssey collected $264.1 million, adding $139.6 million from 73 international markets. The film marks Nolan’s biggest worldwide opening of all time, topping The Dark Knight Rises’ $249 million global launch in 2012. THR

articles.title: Mia Wasikowska, Catherine Deneuve, Rupert Friend in 2026 Venice Days
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 22, 2026 3:00am 'Agata the Writer' Courtesy of Venice Days Venice Days , the independent sidebar of the Venice International Film Festival , has unveiled the lineup for its 23rd edition, the first since the death in March of section founder and longtime head Giorgio Gosetti. This year’s Venice Days, running Sept. 2-12 alongside the 83rd Venice Festival, is dedicated to his memory. The sidebar, and its accompanying Italian cinema section Venice Nights, includes 25 world premieres, more than half of which (14) are directed by women. My Notes on Mars from Hungarian director Lili Horvát ( Preparations to Be Together for an Unknown Period of Time ) will open Venice Days, screening in competition. Horvát’s English-language debut stars Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend in the story of a young scientist who mysteriously disappears only to show up weeks later at her own memorial service with no memory of what happened. Related Stories TV After German Broadcaster Yanks "Antifascist" Song, Musicians Give Guerrilla YouTube Concert News Rebel Wilson Cleared in 'The Deb' Defamation Case Kuba Dorabialski’s Agata the Writer , starring Mia Wasikowska as an Australian author in Sarajevo, will also premiere in competition, alongside Pauline Julier and Nicolas Chapoulier’s period drama The Indies ; Boris Hadžija and Hoda Taheri’s hybrid fiction-documentary I Plant My Hand in the Garden ; and Nicola Sorcinelli’s debut Balcanica , the only Italian title in competition, about an Afghan father and son who, after music is banned in their country, try to flee to Europe. ‘Camouflage’ Courtesy of Venice Days Other highlights include María Aparicio’s Sadness Sometimes, Other Times Revolt , a drama centered on two Argentines in Madrid; Mykyta Gibalenko’s debut Camouflage , about a young Ukrainian in Germany whose separation from home is transformed by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine; a Damilola Orimogunje’s family melodrama Dear Ajayi , which will be the first Nigerian movie to screen in Venice Days competition. Léa Domenach’s Man’s Skin , a queer feminist musical comedy set in the Italian Renaissance and featuring Catherine Deneuve, will close Venice Days, screening out of competition. ‘Man’s Skin’ Laurent-Champoussin An all-woman jury, headed by Spanish filmmaker Carla Simón ( Alcarràs , Summer 1993 ) with Italian director Sara Fgaier ( Weightless ), and Hania Mroué, director of Beirut’s Metropolis Cinema, will pick the winner of the GdA Director’s Award, which carries a €20,000 ($23,000) cash prize to be split between the director and the film’s international distributor. The Lido audience will vote for the Audience Award, while the Europa Cinemas jury will choose the Europa Cinemas Label from the European films in the lineup. Roberta Torre’s Scarpe rotte will open Venetian Nights, the sidebar’s Italian cinema program. The film, starring Barbara Ronchi, is freely inspired by the life of Natalia Ginzburg and is set in wartime Rome. articles.title: European Film Academy CEO and Greek New Wave Director Join Emily Watson on Sarajevo Jury
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 22, 2026 3:13am (L-R) Matthijs Wouter Knol, Athina Rachel Tsangari, Igor Bezinović, Sara Klimoska. Courtesy Sarajevo Film Festival Director of the European Film Academy Matthijs Wouter Knol and Yorgos Lanthimos’ producer Athina Rachel Tsangari are among the industry professionals tapped to join British star Emily Watson on the Sarajevo Film Festival jury. Alongside filmmaker Igor Bezinović and actress Sara Klimoska, they will judge the feature film competition at the Bosnian film festival, running for a week in mid-August. Watson joins a rich constellation of auteurs who have previously presided over the Sarajevo jury in past editions, including Mike Leigh, Jeremy Irons, Asghar Farhadi, Ruben Östlund, and Mia Wasikowska. Related Stories Movies 'The Brutalist' EP, 'Nawi' Makers Strike Three-Film Co-Pro Deal, Set Kenya Soccer Doc 'Champions of Nowhere' (Exclusive) Movies Nicolas Winding Refn Reveals the Chaotic Making of 'Drive': "Most Everyone Hated It" The group will award the Heart of Sarajevo Awards in the feature film competition at the ceremony on Aug. 21. Watson most recently starred as Mary Shakespeare in Chloé Zhao’s adaptation of Maggie O’Farrell’s award-winning historical novel Hamnet . Her notable film credits include Lars von Trier’s Breaking the Waves , A24’s God’s Creatures opposite Paul Mescal, Small Things Like These , Netflix drama Steve , and the Oscar-winning Gosford Park . On television, Watson currently leads the HBO/Max series Dune: Prophecy and has just finished shooting the second season. Croatian director Bezinović is best known for his 2025 film Fiume o morte! , which won numerous awards, including the European Film Award for best documentary, as well as AFA Awards (Adriatic Film & TV Awards) for best film, best director, and best screenplay. His other works include the documentaries The Blockade (2012) and Veruda – A Film About Bojan (2015), both of which received the Oktavijan Award for best Croatian documentary film. His debut feature, A Brief Excursion (2017), premiered at Rotterdam and went on to win the Grand Golden Arena for best film at the Pula Film Festival. Klimoska is an actress from North Macedonia whose latest leading role is in Sister Brother Manhole Cover , directed by Milcho Manchevski, which is set to premiere in 2026. This marks her third collaboration with the acclaimed director, following Willow and Kaymak . Her credits also include You Won’t Be Alone by Goran Stolevski, which premiered at Sundance, and Housekeeping for Beginners , which screened at the Venice Film Festival. Internationally, she has appeared in Nico by Eline Gehring, Family Secrets by Malik Vitthal, and Replay by Jason Lester. Klimoska has been part of the Talents Sarajevo program at Sarajevo Film Festival, and the corresponding scheme at the Berlinale. In 2022, she was nominated for the Heart of Sarajevo award for her role in the TV series Underneath . Knol is an industry-renowned film producer, lecturer, editor and journalist from the Netherlands. Since 2021, he has been the CEO and director of the European Film Academy. He is responsible for the executive management, the vision and all related programming of current and future activities of the Academy, including brand and audience development, knowledge sharing and film heritage projects, and the annual European Film Awards. Knol has been part of the main jury at the festivals of Buenos Aires, Jerusalem, Istanbul, and Locarno. Greek director-screenwriter-producer Tsangari is considered a principal instigator of the Greek New Wave. Her genre-bending films explore power and desire in gender, class and alterity. Her debut project, The Slow Business of Going (2001), was a sci-fi road movie shot in hotel rooms across nine cities around the globe. It went on to garner several best film and best director awards worldwide, and now resides in MoMA’s permanent film collection. Her sophomore feature Attenberg (2010) premiered at Venice in competition, where it won the Coppa Volpi and the Lina Mangiacapre Directing award. Chevalier (2015) won best film at the BFI London Film Festival and was nominated for best foreign film at the Independent Spirit Awards. Both movies were Greece’s official submissions for best international film at the Oscars. Under the banner of her Athens-based company Haos Film, she has produced a number of award-winning films such as Yorgos Lanthimos’ Kinetta and Alps , Georgis Grigorakis’ Digger , and was co-producer on Richard Linklater’s Before Midnight . Her latest feature, Harvest , a neo-western starring Caleb Landry Jones and Harry Melling, was shot in the Scottish Highlands and premiered at Venice in 2024. THR

articles.title: Rebel Wilson Wins Defamation Case Against Charlotte MacInnes Over ‘The Deb’ Bath Dispute
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 12:16am PT Rebel Wilson Wins Defamation Case Against Charlotte MacInnes Over ‘The Deb’ Bath Dispute By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Tak Sakaguchi Joins Iko Uwais in ‘Pendekar: Warrior’ as Nemesis (EXCLUSIVE) 13 minutes ago Rebel Wilson Wins Defamation Case Against Charlotte MacInnes Over ‘The Deb’ Bath Dispute 4 hours ago FAST Provider Wedotv Launches in India With Samsung TV Plus (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Variety via Getty Images Rebel Wilson has prevailed in a defamation case brought by Charlotte MacInnes , the lead actor in Wilson’s feature directorial debut, “ The Deb .” Justice Elizabeth Raper of the Federal Court of Australia in Sydney dismissed MacInnes’ defamation and breach-of-confidence claims on Wednesday and ordered her to pay Wilson’s legal costs. MacInnes sued over four sets of Instagram posts published between September 2024 and July 2025. She argued that the posts portrayed her as having changed her account of an incident involving “The Deb” producer Amanda Ghost in order to benefit her career. Related Stories ESPY Awards 2026 Livestream: Here's How to Watch the Sports Awards Ceremony Online John Lasker, a Top ESPN Streaming Executive, to Exit in September The dispute centred on events on Sept. 5, 2023, when MacInnes and Ghost went swimming at Bondi Beach before returning to the Sydney apartment where they were staying. Popular on Variety Ghost said she suffered a severe reaction to the cold water. MacInnes and Ghost subsequently entered a bath together while still wearing their swimsuits. Wilson alleged that MacInnes told her the following day that the situation had made her uncomfortable and later changed her story. MacInnes denied making such a complaint and said she had not felt uncomfortable. “To say that the circumstances surrounding how they came to be in the bath are unusual would be an understatement,” Raper wrote. The judge found that only one of the meanings alleged by MacInnes was conveyed by any of the four posts. That meaning, contained in Wilson’s Sept. 23, 2024, post, was that MacInnes had changed her account of feeling uncomfortable about what happened in the bathroom. Raper ruled that the meaning was not defamatory, finding that an assertion that someone had changed their story would not necessarily cause an ordinary reasonable person to think less of them. The judge also made two alternative findings. She ruled that MacInnes had not shown that the post caused, or was likely to cause, serious harm to her reputation. She further found that Wilson had established that the conveyed meaning was substantially true. Raper found on the balance of probabilities that MacInnes had felt uncomfortable about the situation, had said something about it to Wilson the following day and later changed her account. The judge described the versions given by MacInnes and Ghost as inconsistent and called both women “unreliable historians.” Raper found that Ghost, then 49, had placed MacInnes, then 25, in an awkward and stressful position by requiring the younger actor to care for her during the episode. The judgment did not determine that Ghost’s behaviour was sexual or that sexual harassment had occurred. Raper explicitly said the parties had not asked the court to decide whether the conduct had a sexualized dimension. The court instead found that MacInnes had complained about feeling uncomfortable in a situation that could be explained without reference to sexual harassment. MacInnes had argued that Wilson’s posts exposed her to online abuse and harmed her professional standing. Raper found no evidence that the posts had deprived her of work or other career opportunities. The judgment noted that MacInnes signed a recording contract with Atlantic Records in October 2025 and subsequently released two singles. Her agent did not identify any specific opportunity lost because of Wilson’s publications. MacInnes’ breach-of-confidence claim also failed. Raper found that MacInnes had not established that she made a complaint of sexual harassment, which was the information she alleged Wilson had improperly disclosed. The judge also found that the other required elements of the claim had not been proven. During closing arguments in May, MacInnes’ barrister, Sue Chrysanthou SC, strongly attacked Wilson’s credibility. “She is a fantastical liar who has made up terrible, terrible allegations about multiple people and her own witnesses have discredited her,” Chrysanthou told the court. Raper said in the judgment that she had serious concerns about the reliability of the evidence given by MacInnes, Ghost and Wilson. She nevertheless accepted Wilson’s evidence on the central question of whether MacInnes had raised her discomfort and subsequently changed her position. The ruling concerns MacInnes’ Australian case against Wilson. Separate legal disputes involving Wilson and producers of “The Deb” remain distinct from the proceeding. Following the decision, Wilson thanked the court for considering the evidence and said she was relieved that the proceedings had concluded. “This has been a long process and throughout I have tried to stay grounded in my values and what I believed was right,” Wilson said in a statement. Wilson also reiterated her support for “The Deb,” describing it as a film about individuality, resilience and the courage to be oneself. “Right now, what I’m focused on is what matters most, my family and my work,” she said. Wilson also addressed the ruling in an Instagram post , writing that she was “grateful this chapter has reached its conclusion” and was looking forward to returning to “what I love most, my family and my work.” She thanked “the Judge and the Australian legal system,” saying she has “the utmost respect” for both. ‘S.W.A.T’ Spinoff ‘Exiles’ Lands at Starz, Sets September Release Date Longtime Disney Exec Jim Kapenstein, Who Helped Oversee Some of Its Biggest Acquisitions, Joins Starz as Chief Legal and Strategy Officer ‘Power: Legacy’ Starring Joseph Sikora, Michael Rainey Jr. Greenlit at Starz Starz Acquires Russell T Davies’s Drama ‘Tip Toe’ for the U.S. and Canada Alliance of Women Directors and Starz Reveal Creative Leadership Lab’s Inaugural Class Designed to Support Female TV Directors (EXCLUSIVE) Starz to Develop ‘Bone Parish’ Series Executive Produced by Curtis ’50 Cent’ Jackson Loading comments... articles.title: Elon Musk Says Grok Will Make an AI ‘Odyssey’ Film That Is ‘Historically Accurate’ by the End of the Year
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 2:07am PT Elon Musk Says Grok Will Make an AI ‘Odyssey’ Film That Is ‘Historically Accurate’ by the End of the Year By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Final Trailer Unveils Action-Packed New Footage of Mark Ruffalo’s Hulk Battling the Web-Slinger 19 hours ago ‘Jason Statham Stole My Bike’ Action-Comedy Adds Eddie Peng, Daniel Ings and Artie Wilkinson-Hunt to Cast (EXCLUSIVE) 20 hours ago ‘Sunny Dancer’ Starring Bella Ramsey Bought by Quiver, Plans North American Theatrical Release (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago See All Getty Images/Everett Collection Elon Musk has — finally — broken his silence on “ The Odyssey ” (well, at least since Christopher Nolan’s epic was released and started breaking various box office records). The tech mogul and recently-crowned trillionaire — who spent some time before the film’s launch rallying against various casting decisions — wrote on his social media platform X that his AI tool Grok Imagine would make a “historically accurate” full-length feature version of Homer’s ancient Greek poem. He noted that his AI “The Odyssey” would be ready by the end of 2026 (just in time for awards season). Related Stories ESPY Awards 2026 Livestream: Here's How to Watch the Sports Awards Ceremony Online John Lasker, a Top ESPN Streaming Executive, to Exit in September “Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer,” he posted, together with an AI-generated 3-minute short of “The Odyssey” posted by an X user. Popular on Variety Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer https://t.co/bVHzUmY9WN — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) July 22, 2026 Given the presence of cyclops, six-headed monsters and a witch who turns sailors into pigs in “The Odyssey,” a nearly 2,800 year old epic considered to be a work of fiction, how “historically accurate” any retelling — AI generated or otherwise — can be is likely to be called into question. Presumably, Musk is referring to the racial element, with him having been the most prominent voice attacking the casting of Lupita Nyong’o as Helen of Troy. In March he wrote that “Chris Nolan is an anti-White racist,” claiming that he only cast Nyong’o because “He wants the awards.” While not confirmed, the all-white AI cast of the short film he posted on X would appear to be more in line with what Musk would prefer. Musk had also supporting transphobic posts about Elliot Page, who many initially asserted was playing Achilles. Page was later confirmed as playing Sinon. For all Musk’s complaints about “The Odyssey” before its release, the movie has been nothing short of a triumphant success for Universal and appears destined to become Nolan’s highest-grossing film to date. The film earned a massive $264 million in its worldwide opening weekend and looks set to continue its own box office odyssey into the coming weeks.
