articles.title: Top Trumps Panel Show, New Seasons of ‘Mock the Week’ Unveiled as Part of Warner Bros. Discovery U.K.’s TLC Comedy Slate
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 2:40am PT Top Trumps Panel Show, New Seasons of ‘Mock the Week’ Unveiled as Part of Warner Bros. Discovery U.K.’s TLC Comedy Slate By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest Top Trumps Panel Show, New Seasons of ‘Mock the Week’ Unveiled as Part of Warner Bros. Discovery U.K.’s TLC Comedy Slate 1 hour ago Lisa Nandy Stays in Post as U.K. Culture Secretary, Kanishka Narayan Appointed First AI Minister 1 day ago World Cup Final Ratings Skyrocket Across Europe, Despite England and France Losses 2 days ago See All Courtesy of TLC TLC in the U.K. has ordered a Top Trumps-themed panel show set to be hosted by comedian Katherine Ryan. Based on the card game and tentatively titled “Top Trumps: The Comedy Pack,” it will see Ryan in charge of proceedings as team captains Joel Dommett and Jon Richardson battle it out with classic card face-offs, live studio challenges and bluffing games. It is produced by TalkbackThames with Naked and set to launch early next year. “Everyone knows Top Trumps, but no one has ever played it quite like this,” said Ryan. “We’re taking this iconic game and supersizing it into something bigger, louder and much funnier. And with Jon and Joel captaining rival teams, chaos is pretty much guaranteed.” Popular on Variety The news comes as part of a bumper comedy slate for the newly free-to-air channel, which is owned by Warner Bros. Discovery U.K. & Ireland. It includes a three-season order of “ Mock the Week ,” which will take the series up to Season 5 in 2027. The long-running panel show, which went on hiatus in 2022 after two decades at the BBC, was revived for the network earlier this year and has already broadcast Season 1 plus a summer special (Season 2 is set to air on Sept 13). It is hosted by Dara Ó Briain and produced by Angst productions. The network has made a concerted effort to invest in comedy since re-launching at the beginning of this year. As well as “Mock the Week,” TLC debuted another new format, “Unacceptable,” hosted by Ed Gamble which launched last month and has already been renewed for a second season. “Six months on from TLC’s successful launch as a free-to-air, broad entertainment channel, it’s hugely exciting to bring another brand-new original format to the schedule in ‘Top Trumps: The Comedy Pack’ (w/t),” said Graham Lafferty, WBD’s SVP for content strategy and networks in the U.K. and Ireland. “We are thrilled to have the brilliantly funny Katherine Ryan at the helm, no stranger to TLC after appearances on ‘Mock the Week’ and ‘Unacceptable,’ along with an exceptional comedy pairing in Joel Dommett and Jon Richardson. articles.title: Venice Days Unveils Female-Centric Selection, Kicking Off With Lili Horvát’s ‘My Notes on Mars’ Starring Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 3:00am PT Venice Days Unveils Female-Centric Selection, Kicking Off With Lili Horvát’s ‘My Notes on Mars’ Starring Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend The independently-run section's all-female jury is headed by Catalan director Carla Simón By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Venice Days Unveils Female-Centric Selection, Kicking Off With Lili Horvát’s ‘My Notes on Mars’ Starring Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend 55 minutes ago FIFA World Cup and Olympic Ceremonies Producer Balich Wonder Studio Expands Footprint to North America and Mexico 21 hours ago World Cup Final Ratings Skyrocket Across Europe, Despite England and France Losses 2 days ago See All Courtesy Giornate degli Autori Hungarian filmmaker Lili Horvát’s first English-language feature, “My Notes on Mars,” starring Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend, will open the Venice Film Festival ’s independently run Giornate Degli Autori . The section has unveiled a richly assorted lineup featuring works by female directors and exploring the female universe, regardless of who is behind the camera. This years’s selection of the Giornate – which is also known as Venice Days – comprises 25 world premieres across several sections, 14 of which are directed by women. The hotly anticipated “My Notes on Mars” by Horvát — whose last film “Preparations to Be Together for an Unknown Period of Time” debuted at Venice and Toronto in 2020 — centers on an astrophysicist with a troubled marriage named Margot who vanishes while hiking with her husband, Sam. Weeks later, she suddenly reappears on the day of her own memorial service. Margot remembers nothing about her life — except her Mars research. Popular on Variety “Notes on Mars” is among 10 Venice Days competition entries that will be judged by an all-female jury headed by Spanish director Carla Simón (“Alcarràs,” “Romeria”). The other jurors are Hania Mroue, founder and director of Beirut’s beloved Metropolis Cinema, and Italian director and producer Sara Fgaier. Polish-born director Kuba Dorabialski’s “Agata the Writerm” starring Mia Wasikowska as a Polish-Australian satirical novelist who travels from Sydney to Sarajevo to write a novel about the Bosnian war only to be challenged by locals, is also ensconced in a competition berth. Other standout Venice Days competition titles include Italian director Nicola Sorcinelli’s “Balcanica,” about Afghan musicians traveling along the Balcan route after music has been banned in their country, starring Matilda De Angelis (“Citadel: Diana”) who is also a co-producer on the film; Nigerian director Damilola Orimogunje’s “Dear Ajayi,” about two estranged Nigerian sisters who reunite at the wake of a tragedy; and French filmmaker Robert Guèdiguian’s “A Woman Today,” about a young woman named Juliette who holds a top job in finance and whose world collapses when she is assaulted by a colleague at a company event. Special events include Italian director Francesca Archibugi’s doc “Carla Lonzi, dentro e fuori dal mondo,” about radical feminist activist and art critic Carla Lonzi; Dutch-Egyptian director Ashgan El-Hamus’ debut “Al Baraneya,” about a young, pregnant, woman in an Egyptian village who is mulling the prospect of a promising future in the city if their family land is sold; and the closing film, which is French director Lèa Domenach’s queer and feminist musical comedy “A Man’s Skin,” which is set in the Italian Renaissance and re-teams the director with Catherine Deneuve after their collaboration on Bernadette Chirac comedy “The President’s Wife.” Shorts by Mona Fastvold and Claire Denis will unspool as part of the Prada-commissioned Miu Miu Women’s Tales, a series of short films directed by women. In a statement, the section’s artistic director Gaia Furrer pointed out the variety of narrative forms on display. She described them as: “sentimental science fiction, experimental documentaries, history films, family melodramas, anti-hero westerns, musical comedies and other works that freely cross the borders between documentary film and fiction, autobiography and invention.” “It’s a patchwork of genres that reflects the vibrancy of contemporary cinema and its ability to evolve along with the world itself,” Furrer said. This edition of Venice Days is dedicated to the memory of Italian film critic Giorgio Gosetti, who in 2004 founded the Venice Days section – which is modeled on Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight and supported by Italian film directors’ associations ANAC and 100autori. Gosetti died in March in Rome at 70 years old. “For 23 years, without interruption, he was its [Venice Days’] guiding spirit, the lifeblood of the organization, motivating and uniting the professionals that turned it into a festival that is known and respected the world over,” a statement noted. The 23nd edition of Venice Days will run Sept. 2-12, in tandem with the official Venice Film Festival selection. See the full lineup below. IN COMPETITION “Sadness Sometimes, Other Times Revolt,” Maria Aparicio “Agata the Writer,” Kuba Dorabialski “Balcanica,” Nicola Sorcinelli “Camouflage,” Mykyta Gibalenko “Dear Ajayi,” Damilola Orimogunje “I Plant My Hand in the Garden,” Boris Hadžija and Hoda Taheri “Les Indes,” Pauline Julier, Nicolas Chapoulier “My Notes on Mars,” Lili Horvàt – Opening Film “Salón De Bellezza” Nathalia Acevedo “A Woman Today,” Robert Guédiguian OUT OF COMPETITION “Man’s Skin,” Léa Domenach SPECIAL EVENTS “Al Baraneya,” Ashgan El-Hamus “Carla Lonzi, A Feminist Story,” Francesca Archibugi “The Phantom,” Ignacio Masilorens, David Lamelas “The Massacre,” Cosimo Messeri “Even if Hell Came,” Samuele Rossi WOMEN’S TALES PROJECT (shorts), in collaboration with Prada’s Miu Miu Label “Discipline,” Mona Fastvold “Avec Kim,” Claire Denis ‘S.W.A.T’ Spinoff ‘Exiles’ Lands at Starz, Sets September Release Date ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Introduces Young [SPOILER], Character to Appear in ‘Power: Origins’ ‘Power: Legacy’ Starring Joseph Sikora, Michael Rainey Jr. Greenlit at Starz Longtime Disney Exec Jim Kapenstein, Who Helped Oversee Some of Its Biggest Acquisitions, Joins Starz as Chief Legal and Strategy Officer ‘The Wolf King’ Romantic Fantasy Books in the Works as a Starz Series Alliance of Women Directors and Starz Reveal Creative Leadership Lab’s Inaugural Class Designed to Support Female TV Directors (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Guillermo del Toro, Kim Novak, Ari Aster Lined Up for ‘The Fall,’ Investigating Hitchcock’s ‘Biggest Mystery’ – the Stunning ‘Vertigo’ Finale (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 3:11am PT Guillermo del Toro, Kim Novak, Ari Aster Lined Up for ‘The Fall,’ Investigating Hitchcock’s ‘Biggest Mystery’ – the Stunning ‘Vertigo’ Finale (EXCLUSIVE) Alexandre O. Philippe’s documentary two-parter is set to be unveiled July 22 at Fantasia’s Frontières By Jennie Punter Plus Icon Jennie Punter Latest Psychological Horror Feature ‘Ancestral Beasts’ Debuts Trailer Ahead of Fantasia World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago ‘The Plague’ Exec Producer James Presson Boards Frontières Biopic Parody ‘Humpty: American Dream’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago Frontières Juicy Dark Horror Comedy ‘Gro(ceries),’ Starring and Co-Written by ‘Sex Education’s’ Chinenye Ezeudu-Sterling, Adds French Co-Production Partners (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago See All 'The Fall' (working title) writer-director Alexandre O. Philippe, courtesy of the production Guillermo del Toro, Kim Novak, and Ari Aster are among several star “witnesses” already lined up for Alexandre O. Philippe ’s two-parter doc feature “The Fall,” which is set to be unveiled July 22 at Fantasia’s Frontières as part of its International Co-Production Market pitch event. A two-part film, “The Fall” will be produced by Medianoche Productions, behind Philippe’s 2025 Venice-premiering doc “ Kim Novak’s Vertigo .” Medianoche producer Terri Piñon and writer-director Philippe are reunited with France’s Tell Me Films, their producing partner on the Novak film. The partners are also teamed up with France’s Thunderbug Productions for the new title. Related Stories Sundance Film Festival, International Federation of Film Critics Establish Jury to Assess Movies From First-Time Foreign Directors (EXCLUSIVE) With a pre-sale to France’s Cine+ also locked, Piñon and Philippe land at Frontières looking for an international sales agent and financing partners for a project that is not only in production – with roughly a year to go – but also gathering momentum as it moves towards a milestone plot point in cinema history. Popular on Variety “We’re building ‘The Fall’ as a two-part event, with separate premieres for Part I and Part II, for ‘Vertigo’s’ 70th anniversary in 2028 that will be the cinephile event of the year,” Piñon said. “With the cast we’re securing, the French pre-sale, the co-production structure, and early interest from some of the most prestigious festivals, it’s set up for a spectacular rollout to ride the ‘Vertigo’ anniversary buzz throughout 2028.” The working title “The Fall” refers to the iconic and fascinatingly ambiguous finale of Hitchcock’s “Vertigo.” When Judy plummets to her death from the belltower, the viewer is never shown exactly how it happens, and instead is shown 57 frames of Scottie’s face as he watches. The film is structured as a film-noir investigation of the fall and the emotions and ideas it inspires. Philippe, whose 2024 Venice Classics Lion winner “Chain Reactions” explores the impact of Tobe Hooper’s “The Texas Chain Saw Massacre” 50 years after its release, said he wants to “inhabit” rather than solve the riddle of the fall. Each interview subject offers “a different version of the truth,” said Philippe, who has called te “Vertigo” finale Hitchcock’s ‘biggest mystery.’ “Each version reveals something intimate about the person telling it. It’s the culmination of everything I’ve chased for 20 years: the film I was born to make.” Fantasia’s four-day Frontières Market runs July 22-25 in Montreal. articles.title: Tak Sakaguchi Joins Iko Uwais in ‘Pendekar: Warrior’ as Nemesis (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 22, 2026 3:58am PT Tak Sakaguchi Joins Iko Uwais in ‘Pendekar: Warrior’ as Nemesis (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Han Chae Young Scores a Hit With FlareFlow Korean Remake of Global Microdrama ‘Raising His Mistress’s Child’ 3 hours ago Rebel Wilson Wins Defamation Case Against Charlotte MacInnes Over ‘The Deb’ Bath Dispute 4 hours ago FAST Provider Wedotv Launches in India With Samsung TV Plus (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Asia Media Alliance Group Japanese cult action star Tak Sakaguchi has signed on to play the nemesis of Iko Uwais in “ Pendekar: Warrior ,” an upcoming martial-arts feature marking Sakaguchi’s first major screen role outside his home country. Principal photography is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026. Sakaguchi, known to action devotees for his cult roles in “Versus” and “Re:Born,” has built his reputation on an unrelenting physical approach to screen fighting. He is widely associated with one of the more extraordinary sequences in action cinema: a 77-minute single-take fight in “Crazy Samurai Musashi” in which he faces down some 400 opponents. His pairing with Uwais – internationally recognized for “The Raid,” “The Raid 2,” “Headshot,” “The Night Comes for Us,” “Mile 22” and “Expend4bles” – brings together two performers from rival martial-arts traditions who have not previously shared a screen. Related Stories John Lasker, a Top ESPN Streaming Executive, to Exit in September ESPN Plunges Back Into Shohei Ohtani Money Transfer Scandal With New Tisha Thompson Podcast “Iko and Tak share something incredibly rare: when they fight on screen, the audience feels that every movement has purpose and consequence,” director, filmmaker and cinematographer John Radel ACS said. “They come from different martial-arts traditions, but they have the same uncompromising commitment to truth in performance. Watching these two finally face one another will be visceral, emotional and unlike anything audiences have seen from either of them before.” Popular on Variety Set on the streets of Jakarta, “Pendekar: Warrior” centers on a former silat master who leaves prison intent on putting violence behind him, only to find a crime syndicate has taken hold of his old neighborhood. Forced to fight again to protect those closest to him, the character becomes the vehicle through which the film aims to bring Indonesian silat to a global audience. Both Uwais and Sakaguchi are in active physical preparation, working with the production’s action team to develop sequences that blend silat’s speed with Sakaguchi’s close-quarters style. “This is more than a clash between two great action performers,” Radel added. “We are creating action that comes from character and emotion. When Iko and Tak finally collide, it has to feel like two unstoppable forces meeting, and like a moment action fans have been waiting years to witness.” The film is produced by Asia Media Alliance Group alongside leading Indonesian producer Delon Tio of Nation Pictures, Erika North and Nick North of Yeti Entertainment, and veteran action producer Mike Leeder of Hong Kong-based Red Packet Media. Uwais and Ryan Santoso are attached as executive producers through Uwais Pictures, with K-Movie Entertainment serving as co-producer and international sales agent. “Bringing Iko Uwais and Tak Sakaguchi together is a landmark moment for Asian action cinema,” Tio said. “They are two extraordinary performers who have each built a global following through authenticity, discipline and fearless physical storytelling. ‘Pendekar: Warrior’ represents exactly the kind of bold, internationally focused Indonesian film we want to bring to audiences around the world.” “I’ve been a huge fan of Tak and his work since the early days, going right back to ‘Versus,'” Leeder said. “I’ve always wanted the chance to work with him, and now we get to pit his close-quarters combat against Iko’s silat in one hell of a movie.” Uwais is represented by Brett Norensberg at Gersh and Vault Entertainment. ‘The Wolf King’ Romantic Fantasy Books in the Works as a Starz Series ‘S.W.A.T’ Spinoff ‘Exiles’ Lands at Starz, Sets September Release Date ‘Power: Legacy’ Starring Joseph Sikora, Michael Rainey Jr. Greenlit at Starz ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Introduces Young [SPOILER], Character to Appear in ‘Power: Origins’ Longtime Disney Exec Jim Kapenstein, Who Helped Oversee Some of Its Biggest Acquisitions, Joins Starz as Chief Legal and Strategy Officer Starz to Develop ‘Bone Parish’ Series Executive Produced by Curtis ’50 Cent’ Jackson Loading comments... articles.title: ‘The Odyssey’ Posts Powerful $20M Tuesday; 2nd U.S. Weekend Could Top Christopher Nolan’s ‘Dark Knight’ Pics – Box Office
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘The Odyssey’ Posts Powerful $20M Tuesday; 2nd U.S. Weekend Could Top Christopher Nolan’s ‘Dark Knight’ Pics – Box Office Snoop Dogg Biopic From Universal Hits Theaters Next Summer Black Bear Hires Bianca Parkes As Head Of Marketing, Heather Phillips As Head Of Publicity View All July 21, 2026 4:42pm Matt Damon in 'The Odyssey' Universal The Odyssey is on its way to a $20M Tuesday, we understand, and if it gets past $20.86M today, it will become Christopher Nolan’s best Tuesday ever at the domestic B.O., ahead of 2008’s The Dark Knight. Currently, among all Tuesdays this year, the pic starring Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jon Bernthal and Mia Goth is second behind Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 5 ($23.69M, June 23). The Odyssey is currently second among all Tuesdays for a Universal movie behind Jurassic World ($24.3M, June 16, 2015). Related Stories Reviews ‘The Odyssey’ Review: Christopher Nolan Takes On Time, Myth And War In Epic Retelling News The 62 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office The Odyssey will hold all Imax and PLF screens in its second weekend, charting a course for a 40%-50% ease in the $61.8M-$74M range. There’s a chance that the movie bests the second frame of Nolan’s Dark Knight movies, meaning either 2008’s The Dark Knight ($75.1M, -61%, the director’s highest-grossing sophomore frame) or 2012’s The Dark Knight Rises ($62.1M, -61% his second-highest). Superhero movies typically are front-loaded, which is reason why no one is expecting Odyssey to comp to the Dark Knight holds. Again, this is an by-appointment film with moviegoers eyeing the best seats, formats and showtimes. Oppenheimer, in a Barbie -dominated 2023 market, saw its second weekend dip by 43% with $46.7M. articles.title: Jacob Elordi On Filming ‘Euphoria’ Death Scene & Returning For Final Season: “I Think Sam Brought Me Back To Torture Me”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Matt Damon Says His Female Stunt Double In ‘The Odyssey’ “Had The Greatest Arms I’ve Ever Seen” Jacob Elordi On Filming ‘Euphoria’ Death Scene & Returning For Final Season: “I Think Sam Brought Me Back To Torture Me” ‘La La Land’s 10th Anniversary Poster Fixes Ryan Gosling’s Hand That Haunted Him View All July 21, 2026 5:40pm Jacob Elordi Disney / Randy Holmes Jacob Elordi had a gruesome death on the final season of Euphoria and is giving insight into how that scene was shot. While making an appearance on ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel Live ! , Elordi had a mini Euphoria reunion with co-star Colman Domingo, who is guest-hosting the late-night talk show in Kimmel’s absence. Domingo brought up his character’s death in the HBO series with the audience audibly letting out an “Aww.” Related Stories News ‘Euphoria’ Season 3 Finale: How Things End For Zendaya’s Rue & The Rest Of The Cast News ‘Euphoria’ Season 3 Premiere Red Carpet Photos: Zendaya, Jacob Elordi, Sydney Sweeney, Hunter Schafer & More “Thanks,” Elordi jokingly said to the audience. “Finally, after eight years of all of you saying, ‘F*** Nate, kill Nate, Nate’s a piece of sh**…’ Yeah, I read your tweets… Now you’re sad.” Elordi played high school bully Nate, who in Season 3 dealt with some goons who tormented him and brutally physically assaulted him. Watch on Deadline “I think Sam [Levinson] brought me back to torture me,” the actor said of the series creator. “It was like, six weeks of me just getting beat by a seven-foot guy. I was just running the whole time.” For filming his character’s death, Elordi explained, “I got locked in a coffin for two days straight with prosthetics and a fake tongue, and I couldn’t see out of my eyes. And then Sam put snakes into the coffin.” Of his reptilian co-star, Elordi said, “he had a very nice personality,” adding, “He was very docile and very sleepy. I don’t think he’d had a lot of sun … So I was kind of nudging him, trying to get him to get active and do the scene, because he was meant to be threatening. But he was like a little dog. He just kept curling up at my feet.” Watch Elordi’s full interview in the video below. articles.title: Dixon Dern Dies: Attorney For CAA, CBS, TV Academy & Desilu, Was 97
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom Dixon Dern Dies: Attorney For CAA, CBS, TV Academy & Desilu, Was 97 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Jennifer Finch Dies: L7 Bassist Who Battled Brain Cancer Was 59 View All July 21, 2026 7:22pm Dixon Dern The Television Academy/YouTube Dixon Q. Dern, the longtime entertainment attorney who worked at CBS , Desilu and United Artists TV; who represented clients such as Desi Arnaz and the Television Academy; who often served as an arbitrator for labor disputes; who helped incorporate CAA and who was a pioneer in syndicated sales and pre-financing for TV, died on July 19. That, according to an obituary posted by Forest Lawn, Hollywood Hills. He was 97. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Donald Trump Says ABC And NBC Should Lose Broadcast Licenses Because They Didn’t Carry His Primetime Address On Election Claims Dern began his career as an in-house counsel for United Artists Television, Desilu and CBS before founding his own firm where he represented Desi Arnaz, the Television Academy, Village Roadshow, the Bob Hope Estate and many others. Dern was often at the nexus of power in Hollywood. One day in the mid-seventies, Michael Ovitz showed up, closed Dern’s office door and told him he and his associates would be back for a meeting the next day. The subject of the proposed meeting was not disclosed. “The next day five guys showed up,” said Dern. “It was the five founders of CAA. They were basically the top five guys in William Morris’ television division and they told me they were leaving William Morris and wanted to set up a new agency. So I formed a corporation. They rented a little office with fold-up desks fold-up tables. We did their legal work for them for about six months.” Dern often served as an arbitrator under various industry collective bargaining agreements, specifically the DGA and WGA. Dern represented the Television Academy for decades. He played a key role in settling a long-simmering feud between its Los Angeles and New York contingents. From the Academy’s official history : By 1976, the situation had exacerbated to the point where, at the semiannual official national board meeting at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel, each chapter designated five-man negotiation teams to meet separately from the rest of the attendees for a two-day summit convened to broker a detente. The Los Angeles contingent consisted of Michael Baugh, Dixon Dern , Hank Rieger, the late Bob Sweeney and then Los Angeles chapter president Larry Stewart , who was chairman of the negotiating committee. Reaching a settlement took far longer than two days. Again, from the Academy’s official history: After much legal wrangling, the two groups agreed to sever in 1977. According to the terms of the dissolution, both would retain their national status, with the group in Los Angeles retaining its original name, the Academy of Television Arts & Sciences, and the New York body retaining the name of National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences. Each group would also control specific award shows: the Los Angeles-based Television Academy kept the Primetime Emmys, and jurisdiction over the Los Angeles chapter; the New York entity retained the Daytime, News, Documentary and Sports Emmys, as well as jurisdiction over the 19 chapters throughout the U.S. that produced their own local Emmy events. Dern also learned a lot about the business while in the legal department at CBS. “When I got there it was pre Fin-Syn, the financial interest syndication rule which later barred the networks from owning distribution rights,” he said in a 2021 interview with the Beverly Hills Bar Association, of which he was a former president. “But at the time…CBS could own its own shows. In fact, in most cases, it did and we did all the production work on them.” Among those shows were classics like Gunsmoke , Have Gun Will Travel and Perry Mason . Dern later moved to Desilu when Desi Arnaz and Lucille Ball were still involved there. “One thing we did there that was, I think, instrumental to the industry: We decided to set up a syndicated sales organization. We set up Desilu Sales which became the forerunner of Paramount Television today.” He left Desilu after Paramount acquired the company. When Dern set up his own practice, Desi became one of his first clients and stayed with him until the day the actor/producer died. Even after Desi’s death, Dern maintained a working relationship with the family. In fact, Dern represented Lucy and Desi Arnaz Jr. in negotiating rights for Amazon’s Being the Ricardos . Through the years, Dern also became involved in back-end television financing and pre-sales to foreign distributors. “I had a number of clients who were producing shows and they would get the funds from the network but they wouldn’t have enough money to to finish production,” he recalled. “So you’d go out and get distributors. They were guaranteed to put up the money on delivery. Then I would go to a bank — or really I went to Lew Horowitz. He would set up the financing with a bank and then as soon as the picture was delivered the distributor would pay the bank and everybody would be happy. It’s very similar to the structure that was done in the independent film market.” Services will be held at Forest Lawn, Hollywood Hills from 9:30 a.m. – 10 a.m. on July 31. articles.title: Sony LIV Welcomes Graphic India’s Animated Series ‘The Legend Of Karna’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Elon Musk Claims Grok Imagine Will Create “Historically Accurate” AI Version Of ‘The Odyssey’ PBS Dials Up Deal For Alternative Music Doc ‘CFNY: The Spirit Of Radio’ Plimsoll Unveils Studios Rebrand & Rejigs With U.S. Chief Alan Eyres Overseeing Creative Divisions View All July 21, 2026 10:30pm 'The Legend Of Karna' Sony LIV EXCLUSIVE: Sony LIV is getting deeper into the animation game. The India-based streamer has quietly greenlit The Legend of Karna , which comes from Sharad Devarajan and Jeevan J. Kang and their production house, Graphic India . The series, inspired by the Hindu epic Mahabharata, will debut on July 31. The Legend of Karna will follow Karna, a warrior from the Mahabharata who is born to Kunti and the Sun God Surya but raised in a charioteer’s household. He possesses the gift of bow mastery that rivals the greatest warriors of his age, compelling him to enter a grand tournament usually reserved only for kings and princes, altering the course of an empire forever. Related Stories Acquisitions Sony LIV Lands Aamir Khan's Feel-Good Basketball Comedy-Drama 'Sitaare Zameen Par' News 'Real Kashmir Football Club' Adds The Drama To A 'Welcome To Wrexham'-Like Story From India - Global Breakouts Per the synopsis: “Crowned king by the ambitious prince Duryodhana but rejected by a court that judges him by his perceived birth, Karna rises from the dust of a village workshop to the royal halls of Hastinapura. His journey is one of exceptional talent, unwavering loyalty and an enduring struggle against a world governed by lineage. As politics, prophecy and hidden truths converge, Karna must confront the conflict between the destiny imposed upon him and the legacy he seeks to create.” Watch on Deadline “We couldn’t imagine a better home for this journey than with our partners at Sony LIV and the incredible honor they are giving us,” said Devarajan, the co-creator and showrunner. “Karna has always been the tragic heart of the Mahabharata. What the world refused him by birth, his own hands took with skill, and that question feels more urgent today than ever. Does greatness come from where you are born, or from what you do? “With The Legend of Karna, we wanted to tell his story the way it deserves to be told, as an epic saga of unbreakable loyalty, unbearable secrets, and a talent that shook the world, seen through the eyes of a hero who has always stood at the center of the epic but never at the center of its telling.” Devarajan is known for collaborating with the late Stan Lee, collaborating to create Indian superhero series Chakra – The Invincible for Cartoon Network India in 2013. The Marvel creator’s influence on Devarajan was such that in the past he has been called “the Indian Stan Lee.” His credits include producing Netflix live-action film The Archies and The Legend of Hanuman , which has become one of the top-rated series on Disney+ Hotstar. Devarajan also created the Spider-Man India character for Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse , and teamed with SS Rajamouli on the Baahubali movie franchise, overseeing gaming, publishing and digital media and creating Prime Video series Baahubali: The Lost Legends . More recently, we revealed he is working with The Adjustment Bureau writer-director George Nolfi on a Hindi-language version of the 2011 film, and with Gladiator writer David Franzoni to turn his graphic novel about Alexander the Great into a scripted series alongside Starlings Television. As for the Sony Pictures Networks India-owned Sony LIV, which is known for originals such as Rocket Boys , Scam and Freedom at Midnight , the series joins other animated originals such as Jiyo Gopuda . articles.title: Rebel Wilson Triumphs In Explosive Court Battle With ‘The Deb’ Co-Star Charlotte MacInnes
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Considers Locking Down iPlayer For Viewers Who Refuse To Pay Licence Fee Rebel Wilson Triumphs In Explosive Court Battle With ‘The Deb’ Co-Star Charlotte MacInnes BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: “It’s Insulting” View All July 21, 2026 10:45pm Charlotte MacInnes and Rebel Wilson Getty Rebel Wilson did not defame Charlotte MacInnes , the Australian actress who stars in her directorial debut The Deb , a Sydney court has ruled. After an explosive and often bitter court battle earlier this year, Wilson has emerged victorious, saying she was “thankful” that the dispute had concluded for now. MacInnes plans to appeal, Deadline understands. There are also numerous other legal fronts in the messy wrangle over The Deb , including unresolved arguments between Wilson and the producers. MacInnes claimed that Wilson damaged her reputation by alleging that she was sexually harassed by The Deb producer, Amanda Ghost , and then colluded with Ghost to cover up what took place. Related Stories Trailers Rebel Wilson's 'The Deb' Gets First Trailer & Digital Release Date; Pic Sparked High-Profile Legal Battles Legal Rebel Wilson Branded A "Fantastical Liar" After Claiming 'The Deb' Actress Made Harassment Complaint At the heart of the case is an incident in September 2023, when Ghost shared a bath with MacInnes in a Sydney apartment after they had been swimming on Bondi beach. Ghost and MacInnes do not deny that they bathed together , but both say it was a non-sexual encounter, during which they were wearing swimsuits, after Ghost experienced a medical incident. Watch on Deadline Wilson claimed that MacInnes told her that the incident made the young actress uncomfortable. Wilson further alleged that MacInnes later withdrew her complaint after being given career opportunities by Ghost. MacInnes denied that the incident made her uncomfortable, suing Wilson over four Instagram posts, in which the Bridesmaids star discussed the events. Justice Elizabeth Raper, the Australian judge who presided over the case, agreed with Wilson. “MacInnes changed her story about feeling uncomfortable about what happened in the bathroom,” the judge ruled, adding that Wilson’s social media posts about MacInnes were not defamatory “by reason of these findings.” Delivering her verdict on Wednesday in Sydney, the judge added: “MacInnes has failed to establish that the publications have caused or were likely to cause serious harm.” In a statement, Wilson said: “I’m grateful the court has taken the time to carefully consider the evidence and reach its decision. This has been a long process and throughout I have tried to stay grounded in my values and what I believed was right. I’m thankful that process has now reached its conclusion. “I have always believed in the importance of telling stories that reflect real experiences and give people the opportunity to see themselves represented. The Deb is a story I’m incredibly passionate about because it celebrates individuality, resilience and the courage to be yourself. I hope audiences will experience the story for themselves and connect with the values at its heart. “Right now, what I’m focused on is what matters most, my family and my work.” MacInnes has been approached for comment. The ruling will not only be a blow to the actress, but also to Ghost and other The Deb producers, who gave evidence in support of MacInnes. They are suing Wilson in the LA Superior Court, accusing the Pitch Perfect star of pursuing an unjustified vendetta after being denied a writing credit on The Deb . Justice Raper was not convinced by the testimony of MacInnes, Ghost, and Wilson, but ultimately deemed that Wilson’s actions after the bathing incident supported her story. “I have serious misgivings as to the truthfulness of the testimony of each of Ms MacInnes, Ms Ghost and Ms Wilson,” the judge said. “Whilst I accept that Ms Wilson has a propensity to exaggerate events and her evidence could be found to be untruthful on occasion, the evidence establishes that Ms Wilson acted in a manner consistent with a complaint being made and her own contemporaneous documentary trail supports this.” The ruling comes as Sunrise Films has set an August 25 U.S. digital release date for The Deb . Wilson’s second feature, Girl Group , will also premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival. articles.title: BBC Considers Locking Down iPlayer For Viewers Who Refuse To Pay Licence Fee
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Considers Locking Down iPlayer For Viewers Who Refuse To Pay Licence Fee Rebel Wilson Triumphs In Explosive Court Battle With ‘The Deb’ Co-Star Charlotte MacInnes BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: “It’s Insulting” View All July 22, 2026 1:36am 'The Traitors' host Claudia Winkleman BBC/Studio Lambert EXCLUSIVE : The BBC has said it is open-minded about closing off iPlayer to British viewers who decline to pay the licence fee. In an all-staff call on Monday, the BBC’s chief customer officer Kerris Bright said locking down iPlayer could be an “opportunity” in the future as the corporation looks to stem the tide of people opting out of the licence fee. Bright told colleagues that blocking iPlayer does not currently make sense because it could cause unwelcome friction for viewers who do pay the licence fee, but she said the BBC will keep the idea under review as streaming technology improves. Related Stories News BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: "It's Insulting" News Gordon Ramsay Profiled In BBC Landmark Series 'Rise Of The Rockstar Chef' “iPlayer is the only service really that’s licensable where you could actually decide to put a gate in front of it, but the data today says that actually [there’s] not really the return on investment for doing that,” Bright told employees, per audio obtained by Deadline. Watch on Deadline “The vast majority of evasion is not on iPlayer. The vast majority of people that are watching iPlayer are people that are paying their TV licence, and so to put a gate in front of iPlayer, the data today says that you actually would make it a very difficult experience for people that are paying for the licence.” iPlayer viewers do have to sign into the BBC to watch the streamer. The service also occasionally asks users if they have a licence fee, though it does not require proof. “It’s quite a difficult experience if you have to ask them to find their TV licence to put it into iPlayer,” Bright said. She continued: “As we go into the future, more of an IPTV world, audiences changing behavior, new ways of creating experiences that maybe aren’t so full of friction for audiences … that might absolutely be an opportunity for us, depending on the funding model. “The data says today [that] absolutely [it] is not the silver bullet to generating more revenue. There’s probably more cost in it than revenue, but it is something we should absolutely keep looking at because it might be something that you actually would want to do in the future.” More than half a million people opted out of the licence fee in the BBC’s most recent financial year, contributing to a funding crisis for the British broadcaster. Some 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap and can no longer dip into its cash reserves to fund operations. In comments earlier this month, BBC director general Matt Brittin said: “We can and should be doing as much as possible on [enforcing] licence fee collection under the current model, but it’s yesterday’s model, it’s a busted flush, it’s no longer fit for purpose, and that’s why we need to make the case for the BBC and a shift of the licence fee model.” The BBC is in talks with the government about a new charter, which will likely lead to funding model changes. The BBC is not being prescriptive about what could replace the licence fee, but thinks the government should reconsider a compulsory household levy, which it previously ruled out. Another idea under consideration is extending the licence fee to include subscribers to streamers like Netflix, Disney+ and Prime Video. The plan has already drawn the ire of the Motion Picture Association, representing U.S. streamers and studios. articles.title: Analysis: As The New UK Prime Minister Cosies Up To Donald Trump, Lisa Nandy Could Be About To Become The Most Consequential Culture Secretary In America In Recent Memory
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Analysis: As The New UK Prime Minister Cosies Up To Donald Trump, Lisa Nandy Could Be About To Become The Most Consequential Culture Secretary In America In Recent Memory Apple TV Seeking Local Language Boss Catherine Zeta-Jones Thriller ‘Kill Jackie’ Sells To AMC+ View All July 22, 2026 2:24am Lisa Nandy speaks onstage during the Greater Together Los Angeles welcome reception at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in L.A. Jerod Harris/Getty for Greater Together Los Angeles UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy was widely expected to change jobs when her good friend Andy Burnham became Prime Minister this week, but she has remained in post and is now comfortably the longest-serving in that role for well over 10 years. Now, a set of decisions that Nandy is due to make over the coming months could make her one of the most consequential Culture Secretaries in recent memory… in America that is. This trio of major calls that loom over Nandy could end up upsetting or possibly ingratiating virtually all the major U.S. studios, streamers and tech giants, coming at a time when Burnham will be attempting to keep relations with Donald Trump rosy after the solid work put in by his predecessor Keir Starmer. Related Stories Ratings Netflix's 'Little House On The Prairie' Gathers Steam In Second Week As 'The Hawk' Opens Under Par Ratings Michael B. Jordan Animated Pic 'Swapped' Breaks Into Netflix's Most Popular Movies List First up, it was just before UK Parliament broke for recess and just before Burnham became PM that Nandy left the Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) $110B mega-merger unread. Watch on Deadline She had initially said she was “minded to intervene” in the deal on media plurality grounds but failed to provide an update in time. David Ellison and co will now have to wait until September 1 at the very earliest to discover if the deal will be either probed or greenlit by British regulators. This, as a reminder, could be an incredibly costly Nandy intervention, because the agreement has a “ticking fee” commitment to WBD shareholders of 25 cents a ​share — roughly $650 million — for every quarter its takeover does not finalize beyond Q3. Ellison attempted to charm Nandy back in Jan during a much-publicized trip to Europe but any charm will dissipate if she causes his beloved deal to run into the “ticking fee” period. In the U.S., of course, he continues to hit stumbling blocks and the merger is currently on pause in response to a lawsuit from a dozen states. With the Paramount-WBD deal firmly remaining in the spotlight, WBD’s previous suitor Netflix will be fuming if Nandy pushes on with a controversial plan for the BBC licence fee to expand to subscribers to streamers like Netflix , Disney+ and Prime Video. The BBC has floated the plan in a desperate bid to generate more from the £180 ($240) annual fee. It has repeatedly stressed that while 94% of the UK population use its services every month, fewer than 80% pay the £180, leading to a loss of hundreds of millions of pounds per year. Without a great deal of info about how it would actually work in practice, Nandy recently signaled that she is behind the proposal that would see people who watch non-live content on streamers forced to pay the licence fee, and would even task streamers with helping collect the charge. The Motion Picture Association, which represents big streamers and studios, had already pushed back , saying the plan will have a “downstream impact on viewers and their viewing experience,” yet this doesn’t appear to have halted Nandy. She says she has had conversations with the streamers over various ideas and continues to point out that the government will never bring in a streamer levy, an idea taken up by several other nations that would force the SVoDs to pay a small amount of their UK subscription revenue to a cultural fund for British content. Netflix in particular is already on the European regulatory warpath. It has bristled frequently at other nations that force the streamer into local content quotas and funding obligations but has regularly praised the UK for leaving it free to do what it wants in the nation that birthed Adolescence and Baby Reindeer. Forcing its subscribers into effectively funding a rival would surely go against this grain. And then there is the tech giants. In amongst everything else, the UK is going ahead with a full social media ban for under-16s while also drawing up legislation that would require YouTube and TikTok to carry public service content prominently, which could prove quite the algorithmic headache for these tech behemoths. This idea was first floated at the RTS Convention by, you guessed it, Lisa Nandy, who said it will be “vital in the fierce battle against mis and disinformation.” Had Nandy been removed from her post earlier this week, it is impossible to tell if her successor would have changed tack on any of these three crucial upcoming decisions. But as it stands, she appears keen to follow through, and the American entertainment and tech giants that would be impacted would be numerous. Many of these companies have got closer and closer to Trump during his second presidency, some relying on his or his allies’ say-so to force through various deals. In their first-ever call during his first few hours as PM, Burnham invited Trump to his home city of Manchester, which also happens to be where Nandy is from. Were Trump to take up this offer, the Culture Sec may fancy making herself scarce.
