articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Edward Stourton Dies: UK Broadcaster Whose Most Recent Work Charted 250 Years Of American History Was 68 Venice Critics’ Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston Join Guy Pearce, Jared Harris & Merab Ninidze In ‘The Price Of Peace’ As Filming Begins in London View All July 22, 2026 3:05am My Notes On Mars GdA Venice parallel section Giornate degli Autori (GdA) has unveiled a female focused lineup for its 2026 edition. Hungarian director Lili Horvát’s first English-language film My Notes on Mars will open the edition. The sci-fi romance stars Mackenzie Davis as a scientist who vanishes during a hiking trip to reappear on the day of her own memorial service with no memory of the life she has lived in between. Rupert Friend co-stars. Horvát previously made waves with Preparations to Be Together for an Unknown Period of Time , about a talented surgeon who ditches her career for a man who then claims to have never met her before. That film debuted in the GdA’s 2020 edition and then went on to win numerous awards including a Golden Hugo in Chicago’s New Directors Competition. Related Stories Festivals Venice Critics' Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia News Giovanni Veronesi's 'Dio Ride' To Close Venice Film Festival Léa Domenach’s A Man’s Skin , described as a queer and feminist musical comedy set in the Italian Renaissance, and featuring Pomme, Karin Viard, and Catherine Deneuve in the cast, will close the section. Watch on Deadline Drawn from 1,036 submissions from 114 countries, the lineup features 25 world premieres, of which 13 are Italian and 14 directed by women; with 10 films in competition, one closing film out of competition, five special events, and a showcase of nine titles in Venetian Nights (scroll down for the full section). Horvát’s My Notes on Mars is among 10 films being showcased in competition. Further contenders include Polish-born Australia-based filmmaker Kuba Dorabialski’s Agata the Writer , starring Mia Wasikowska as an Australian writer who travels to Sarajevo to work on a novel about the Bosnian war and is forced to acknowledge the limits of her own artistic vision. In other competition highlights include Post Tenebras Lux actress Nathalia Acevedo’s directorial debut Salón de Belleza . Adapted from the radical novel by Mario Bellatin, it unfolds in a beauty salon in a city ravaged by a mysterious disease which becomes a refuge for the afflicted as they linger between life and death. Belgian multi-disciplinary artist Sam Louwyck, and Erwan Kepoa Falé co-star. It is among five first features in the mix alongside Italian director Nicola Sorcinelli’s Balcanica , about father and son musicians fleeing Afghanistan; Ukrainian filmmaker Mykyta Gibalenko’s Camouflage about a young man dealing with Russia’s invasion of his homeland of Ukraine as he tries to build a new life in Germany; Swiss artists Pauline Julier and Nicolas Chapoulier’s 1600s-set tale The Indies , about a mission to transport Velázquez’s portrait of the Infanta of Spain from Madrid to Versailles as a peace offering, as well as I Plant My Hand in the Garden , a docu-fiction by Iranian director Hoda Taheri and the queer Serbian director Boris Hadžija tackling issues at the heart of their identities and lives. Further contenders include Nigerian director Damilola Orimogunje’s second film Dear Ajayi , taking its cue from the complicated relationship between two sisters and the burden of expectations that their families and society place on them, and Argentinian director María Aparicio’s third feature Sadness Sometimes, Other Times Revolt , revolving around the encounters between two Argentinians, a director and a historian, living in Madrid. Established directors in the mix include Robert Guédiguian with A Woman Today . Newcomer Marilou Aussilloux stars as a young woman grappling with the distance between her own idea of freedom and the contradictions of a present day still ridden with violence and inequality, alongside the director’s longtime collaborators Ariane Ascaride, Jean-Pierre Darroussin, and Gérard Meylan. This year’s jury for the GdA Director’s Award, which includes a cash prize of €20,000 to be split between the director and international distributor, comprises Spanish filmmaker Carla Simón, Italian director and editor Sara Fgaier, and Hania Mroué, director of Beirut’s landmark Metropolis arthouse cinema. In other awards, audiences for the GdA screenings at the Sala Perla will decide the Audience Award while the Europa Cinemas jury will choose the winner of the label from among the European films at Giornate degli Autori. The Special Events lineup – featuring the documentary, autobiography, historical film, and experimentation, includes Francesca Archibugi’s Carla Lonzi, A Feminist Stor y, exploring the life and times of one of the most radical feminist voices of 20th-century Italy. In other highlights beyond the main competition, Claire Denis and Mona Fastvold are the guests of honor of the Miu Miu Women’s Tales program. The 15th edition of the initiative in partnership with GdA will see the filmmakers share career lessons in on-stage conversations. GdA’s 23rd edition is dedicated to the sidebar’s founder and longtime champion, film critic and festival exec Giorgio Gosetti who died suddenly and unexpectedly in March. “This edition carries with it a deep void and a deep gratitude,” declares Artistic Director Gaia Furrer. “We owe to Giorgio the very idea for this free arena we inhabit, along with his faith in the new directions of cinema and his stubborn, loving determination to build and consolidate, year after year, a community of men and women filmmakers and audiences. This year, Giornate springs from the desire to honor this legacy by continuing to do what Giorgio taught us: seek out, discover, go wrong, become passionate about, and believe in cinema and in those who make it happen.” The edition, will run alongside the Venice Film Festival from September 2 to 12, with its activities based mainly in the Casa degli Autori and the Sala Laguna on the Venice Lido. OFFICIAL SELECTION IN COMPETITION SADNESS SOMETIMES, OTHER TIMES REVOLT by María Aparicio Argentina, Spain, 2026 AGATA THE WRITER by Kuba Dorabialski Australia, 2026 BALCANICA – debut feature by Nicola Sorcinelli Italy, Serbia, Croatia, 2026 CAMOUFLAGE – debut feature by Mykyta Gibalenko Germany, 2026 DEAR AJAYI by Damilola Orimogunje Nigeria, Germany, 2026, 120’ I PLANT MY HAND IN THE GARDEN – debut feature by Boris Hadžija & Hoda Taheri Germany, Serbia, U.S. The Indies – debut feature by Pauline Julier, Nicolas Chapoulier Switzerland, Spain, 2026 MY NOTES ON MARS – opening film by Lili Horvát Hungary, Austria SALÓN DE BELLEZA – debut feature by Nathalia Acevedo Mexico, France, 2026 A WOMAN TODAY by Robert Guédiguian France, Italy, 2026 OUT OF COMPETITION MAN’S SKIN – closing film by Léa Domenach France, 2026 SPECIAL EVENTS AL BARANEYA by Ashgan El-Hamus Netherlands, Egypt, Belgium, Saudi Arabia, 2026 CARLA LONZI, A FEMINIST STORY by Francesca Archibugi Italy, 2026 THE PHANTOM by Ignacio Masllorens, David Lamelas Argentina, 2026 THE MASSACRE by Cosimo Messeri Italy, 2026 EVEN IF HELL CAME by Samuele Rossi Italy, 2026 Why Lisa Nandy Could Become The Most Important UK Politico In The U.S. Huge $20M Tuesday; 2nd U.S. Frame Could Top Nolan’s ‘Dark Knight’ Pics Sony Looking To Bring Cinerama Dome & Hollywood Arclight Back To Life Disney Cutting Several Hundred Jobs At Pixar, ESPN, Nat Geo & Other Units Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Ryan Reynolds Confirms Another ‘Deadpool’ Movie
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 4:04pm 'Deadpool and Wolverine' Everett Collection Logo text It looks like Ryan Reynolds will be putting on the Deadpool suit once again. The actor confirmed during a recent appearance at Fanatics Fest 2026 that another Deadpool movie is coming, which would follow the box office success of 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine . “There’s a few really deep cuts that I think are missing behind the movies. I think there’s a few deep cuts missing from some of the comics. There’s certainly some stuff that, you know, I love that Fabian Nicieza [co-creator of Deadpool] wrote that is incredible. Gerry Duggan, who was a friend, was an incredible comic writer,” Reynolds said onstage, via a video shared on X. “There’s stuff upcoming. There’s eventually, you know, remotely another Deadpool film. It’s going to be great.” Related Stories Movies 'Mayday' Directors Break Down Trailer for Ryan Reynolds, Kenneth Branagh Cold War Buddy Movie Lifestyle As Taylor Swift Gets Married, Former Best Friend Blake Lively Is Out of Sight The actor-producer didn’t give any additional details on whether the film would be another solo Deadpool installment or more of an ensemble film, with his chaotic antihero becoming more of a supporting player. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to Marvel for comment. Last year, THR exclusively reported that Reynolds was exploring ideas for another movie in the franchise; however, it would feature X-Men characters. The actor has also previously stated that he did not see another solo Deadpool movie in his future. “Centering Deadpool works best if you take everything away from him and put his back against the wall. I can’t really do that again,” he told THR in 2024. “A fourth time feels a little iterative and redundant. That doesn’t mean sacrificing fun. There is still an arc for Deadpool which is fulfilling and powerful.” When Deadpool & Wolverine , starring Reynolds and Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, was released in 2024, it went on to become the top-grossing R-rated movie of all time , collecting over $1.3 billion globally. The film followed 2016’s Deadpool and 2019’s Deadpool 2 , which were also massive box office successes. THR

articles.title: Hunter Biden’s Image Rehab Tour Takes a Hard Right
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 20, 2026 4:06pm Hunter Biden, son of President Joe Biden. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images Hunter Biden ‘s ongoing rehabilitation tour is about to take a hard right turn with an unorthodox sit-down with Nick Fuentes . His conversation with the far-right influencer is slated to premiere on web channel Channel 5 News later this month. The much-discussed interview — which nearly ended in fisticuffs — appears to be part of the former first son’s pivot toward life as an edgy but earnest media personality. Or is it more PR spin from Biden, who is rewriting his chaotic personal story to cast himself as a victim of the Republican smear machine? Biden has been working with an L.A.-based homelessness prevention nonprofit and is starting a foundation for addiction aftercare, since he was disbarred in Connecticut and Washington, D.C. last year following his 2024 conviction on federal gun-possession and tax-evasion charges. He has also spent the past year building a second act as a visual artist. Related Stories News Hunter Biden, Nick Fuentes Interview Nearly Turns Physical, Report Says Business Michael Strahan, Podcaster? 'GMA' Star to Co-Host Show Under His SMAC Banner He’s now slowly stepping back into public view, but clearing his name doesn’t appear to be his only motive. Last week, he won $1.7 million in a defamation suit against former Overstock CEO and 2020 election denier Patrick Byrne, who’d falsely claimed Biden solicited an $800 million bribe from Iran in 2021. He’s fighting the lies, but he’s also owning the mistakes. Not that his motives aren’t being questioned. “There’s an enormous freedom in owning your own story,” Biden told Gavin Newsom last month on the governor’s podcast, after the two joked about each other’s presidential ambitions. He also defended his appearance on right-wing provocateur Candace Owens’ show , telling Newsom he hoped Owens could see the humanity in his situation. “I don’t think these are bad people,” he explained. Now a painter rather than an attorney and globe-trotting lobbyist, Biden splits time between South Africa and the U.S. You are most likely to see him, however, working a growing podcast circuit — including Friends Keep Secrets , Armchair Expert and This Is Gavin Newsom and Candace , among them. But it was his August 2025 interview with Channel 5’s Andrew Callaghan — where he opened up about his addiction, the laptop scandal and the 2020 election — that set his next move in motion: the two are reportedly teaming up on a podcast, giving Biden a full-time pulpit to talk recovery, politics or whatever he likes. A month ago, Biden and Callaghan approached Callaghan’s publicist, Mitchell Jackson — the former Vice wunderkind turned go-to fixer for mostly right-wing disruptors — about landing a heavy-hitting conversation that could “move the needle” in American politics, a source familiar with the plans told The Hollywood Reporter. It was that same day that Jackson found himself on the phone with Fuentes. The far-right pundit — who in 2022 finagled a Mar-a-Lago dinner with President Donald Trump , and now commands his growing following of vocal bigots — was looking for an image rehab interview, Jackson said, hoping to explain how his views have evolved past the antisemitic material that built his brand. Who better to arrange it than the publicist behind Owens, the reigning queen of online controversy? Jackson pitched both camps on staging the interview inside a seedy motel — a wink at the 2019 photos of Biden in the New York Post, where he appeared shirtless and smoking a crack pipe in a motel room. But no Philly-area motel would let them film, so they built a set to match. Biden, Jackson said, had signed off on the concept fully aware of what it referenced. His real motive for sitting with Fuentes, per Jackson, was reach: “The way he explained it was that he wanted to speak with Nick because Nick is one of the most influential people with young men in America. Which is true.” Fuentes commands an unusually devoted audience. His self-styled “Groypers,” named for a Pepe the Frog variant, is a symbol embraced by the far-right since roughly 2016. Fuentes has spent years stoking racism, nativism, sexism, homophobia, Islamophobia and antisemitism, deploying that army with ease, most often against Charlie Kirk’s Turning Point USA, which Fuentes considered insufficiently “America First.” Jackson believes Fuentes, 28, is now trying to put distance between himself and his past remarks. He’s evolved, Jackson argues — he says he never supported violence, never identified as a Nazi, and the “edgelord” trolling of his teenage years isn’t who he is now, even if his America First politics haven’t moved an inch. “I went and looked at some of the stuff he said recently on the show. I needed to watch it outside of clips going viral,” Jackson said. “It was very clear he’s been criticizing his own audience — if anyone would bother to watch, instead of just the clips sent to them by people who hate him.” The interview — already deemed notorious by a press corps that hasn’t seen it — premieres this week. Whether it’s the swing that launches Biden into the podcast big leagues remains to be seen. Until this recent run of appearances centered on sobriety and his personal scandal, Biden kept a low profile, communicating mostly through a recently launched Substack and avoiding cameras in the wake of the controversial pardon his father issued on the way out of the Oval Office (after promising he wouldn’t). Hunter is back now, and being far more candid than anyone might expect from a scandal-plagued former president’s son. In June, he joined X with an opening line built for virality: “I’m Hunter Biden. You’ve never actually heard from me.” (Never mind that his 2021 addiction memoir, Beautiful Things , became a bestseller once the GOP weaponized it). Since his return to public life, he’s leaned into confrontation — sparring with Trump immigration adviser Stephen Miller (he later clarified he’d meant to call Miller “sadistic, infantile” and something cruder, not merely “ugly”) and with CNN’s Jake Tapper over a jab at stepmother Jill Biden’s memoir — while staying self-aware enough to needle himself, too (“I am not posing nude,” he told a Playboy writer angling for a Q&A). Jackson, for one, sees strategy here: Biden is reaching across the aisle in a way Democrats broadly haven’t. “I think the Republicans have been much better at finding common ground with people; the Democrats have been much more resistant to doing that,” he said. “If the Democrats have a brain, they’re going to watch the episode on Friday and send Andrew Callaghan a thank-you note. But I don’t know if Democrats have a brain.” Yet there’s an entirely different read on Biden’s media blitz. In a scathing New York Post column last week , Miranda Devine — author of the data deep dive book, Laptop From Hell — argues that Biden’s press tour is really a promotional run for two things at once: a forthcoming documentary and a new, more convenient answer to the question of his infamous laptop. The documentary, which had cameras, follows Biden from 2021 through his 2024 pardon, was produced by Kevin Morris, the Hollywood lawyer and longtime Biden benefactor who loaned him millions of dollars over the same years the cameras were rolling and who has separately bought pieces of Biden’s artwork (as he explained when dragged into a closed-door meeting with House Republicans). The film, Devine writes, posits that the “laptop from hell,” with its evidence of the Biden family’s Ukraine dealings, among other alleged scandals and all that motel footage, was never a laptop at all, but a database stolen and doctored by Rudy Giuliani, or possibly Russian operatives, or maybe both, then passed off as real with the help of Trump allies and a psychologist who once treated Biden. The forthcoming documentary is directed by S.R. Bindler, of the 1997 cult favorite and Morris-produced Hands on a Hardbody, and coming soon, per Bindler’s website. But last week, Biden sent the stolen-laptop theory wide after previewing the claim in a recent Wired interview promoting his forthcoming book, with posts on X and his Substack. “They called it the laptop. I will call it that too, although the name is not accurate, the provenance was never established, and no court or forensic examiner ever certified the chain of custody that would have made it evidence rather than theater,” he wrote on X, throwing to his Substack, where he writes that “a scandal was constructed, and a laptop was produced to anchor it.” But what about the crackpipe? The motel room trysts? The stolen database does contain real footage of his, he says — the evidence of the years-long struggle with addiction that has become central to his new public persona. “Twenty years of my life, or a version of it. Messages sent at hours that don’t belong to anyone sober. Photographs I would never have taken in daylight,” he shared. “It is accumulation — the slow daily work of an addict doing the thing that is killing him because the alternative feels like dying faster.” THR

articles.title: ‘Never Have I Ever’ Alum Maitreyi Ramakrishnan Teases ‘Elle’ Season 2 Role: “Not Something I’ve Done Before”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 4:14pm Maitreyi Ramakrishnan at the 'Elle' world premiere in New York. Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images Logo text An open casting call. A virtually unknown actress selected to lead a coming-of-age streaming TV sho w executive produced by an ambitious veteran actress-turned-producer with a strong personal connection to the IP. That’s what Maitreyi Ramikrishnan went through when the Canadian actress was chosen among many to lead the Mindy Kaling -executive produced, semi-autobiographical Netflix comedy Never Have I Ever . But the same could also be said about Lexi Minetree , the Atlanta native who was selected from roughly 5,000 audition tapes , again via an open search, to play the star of the Reese Witherspoon executive-produced Legally Blonde prequel, Elle . Related Stories TV Whether It Be Romantic Lead or Writer-Director, Jack Martin's Ready to Tackle Whatever Role Comes Next Lifestyle Hollywood's Top Docs Reveal Their Cosmetic Secrets at THR's A-List Aesthetics Event: "We Have to Be Scientists, Artists, Technicians and Psychologists" Now, three years after the end of Never Have I Ever , Ramakrishnan is going back to the world of teen shows to play the nemesis to Minetree’s Elle Woods in the already renewed (and already filmed) season two of Elle . Though Ramakrishnan’s role might seem like she’s starring in yet another high school series after Never Have I Ever ‘s four-season run, she teases that her addition to the Legally Blonde universe is different. “Without spoiling too much, I like my character’s dynamic in the gang because it’s not something I’ve done before,” Ramakrishnan told The Hollywood Reporter at the recent Elle premiere in New York. Ramakrishnan’s character, Sam, has been described as “possessing all our hero’s ambition and none of her optimism. She’s the founder, editor-in-chief and lord baron of the school newspaper, the commissioner of the grammar police and the enemy of joy,” the description continues. “If Cosmo is Elle’s bible, the AP Stylebook is Sam’s holy grail.” Speaking about what drew her to the role, Ramakrishnan mentioned the “iconic” world of Legally Blonde and called Witherspoon a “legend.” Having worked with Witherspoon on the already filmed second season of Elle and Kaling on Never Have I Ever , Ramakrishnan also shared her thoughts on how the actresses-turned-powerhouse-producers, aiming to improve representation onscreen, are similar. “The biggest thing they have in common, I would say, is that they are both women with audacity, and that’s why I think they hire women with audacity as well,” she said. “Meeting Lexi is such a joy because she works so hard. She’s just amazing. Game recognizes game, and I think Mindy knew what she did casting me, and Reese knew what she did casting Lexi Minetree.” Ramakrishnan described both Kaling and Witherspoon as “hard-working women who want to tell good stories.” All eight episodes of Elle ‘s first season are streaming on Amazon’s Prime Video. THR

articles.title: Peter Lassally, Producer for Johnny Carson and David Letterman, Dies at 93
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 5:08pm Peter Lassally Mark Mainz/Getty Images for AFI Peter Lassally, a concentration camp survivor who became known as the “Host Whisperer” for producing talk shows headlined by Johnny Carson , David Letterman and Craig Ferguson , has died. He was 93. Lassally died Sunday of natural causes at a memory care facility in Los Angeles, his son, Tom Lassally, the partner, producer and manager at 3 Arts Entertainment, told The Hollywood Reporter . Lassally had produced programs starring Arthur Godfrey and Mike Wallace before joining Carson on NBC’s The Tonight Show , then based in New York, in 1969. He served as the quiet behind-the-scenes guy in a producing partnership with the boisterous Fred De Cordova and remained with the show until Carson’s final broadcast on May 22, 1992. Related Stories TV Sylvia Bugg, PBS Programming Chief, Dies at 55 Music Jim Gilstrap, Singer on 'Good Times' Theme and Stevie Wonder's "You Are the Sunshine of My Life," Dies at 79 After just one week off, Lassally jumped to Late Night With David Letterman as an executive producer for what would prove to be the NBC program’s final season. When Jay Leno was picked over Letterman to replace Carson, Lassally advised Letterman what to do next. “I said to Dave, ‘If you’re going to follow Jay Leno at 12:30 when he gets The Tonight Show , you’re going to hate yourself, you’re going to be miserable,'” Lassally recalled in a 2009 chat for the Television Academy Foundation website The Interviews . “You’re going to think, ‘Why am I following Jay Leno when I for 12 years hosted the 12:30 show … and my reward should be The Tonight Show ?’ If you agree, I’ll try to get you an 11:30 show — not knowing when I said that just how I was going to do that.” Lassally hooked Letterman up with powerful CAA agent Michael Ovitz, and the host fielded lucrative offers in syndication, cable and broadcast before deciding to move to CBS in 1993 to topline Late Show With David Letterman from the Ed Sullivan Theater on Broadway at 11:35 p.m. The deal included ownership of a 12:35 a.m. program, The Late Late Show , and Lassally returned to California to set up that program with host Tom Snyder. When Snyder left after four years in March 1999, Lassally disapproved of his replacement, the snarky Craig Kilborn — he had pushed for Jon Stewart — and stepped aside. But when Kilborn quit in a salary dispute in 2004, he got his man in the charming Scottish actor-comedian Ferguson. “I always had a good relationship with the hosts that I worked with because I would tell them the truth. That has really worked well for me. That’s how I got the title the ‘Host Whisperer,'” the two-time Emmy winner said. “I’m not good at pumping sunshine up their rears. If I didn’t like it, I can’t fake it, I can’t pretend it was good. I’m very lucky the hosts respected that.” Peter Eduard Lassally was born on Oct. 14, 1932, in Hamburg, Germany. His father, Paul, was an importer/exporter in the coffee business, and his mother, Elsa, was a housewife. He and his family fled Germany in 1938 on the way to England to escape the Nazis but “didn’t go far enough,” settling in Amsterdam, where he went to the same grade school as Anne Frank. After his father died and the Germans invaded the Netherlands, his mother and older sister were confined to two concentration camps from 1943-45. The second camp, Theresienstadt in Czechoslovakia, “was a very strange place,” Lassally told NPR in 2012. “That’s where the Nazis fixed up the camp with all sorts of phony, wonderful decor and invited the Red Cross to come and visit and see what wonderful things they were doing.” In 1947, Lassally came to live with an uncle in Canton, New York, where he attended St. Lawrence University after graduating from high school in Queens. Back in New York City, he worked as an usher at Radio City Music Hall and as a page (alongside Regis Philbin ) at NBC. Lassally reviewed Broadway plays for a WOR radio program hosted by Ruby Mercer and went on to produce her show, then produced the NBC radio program Nightline , where he hired Mort Sahl , Shelley Berman and Nichols & May to do short comedy bits. “That’s where I found doing what I really love more than anything else, finding talent and developing them,” he said. Lassally produced Godfrey-hosted shows on CBS radio and television — he eventually became president of Godfrey’s production company — and in 1961 moved to PM East , a syndicated talk show from Westinghouse that was hosted by Wallace. He regularly booked Barbra Streisand on that because she lived in an apartment above the studio; she hadn’t even begun her singing career yet. Lassally got to know Carson’s second wife, Joanne, when she asked him to produce a TV pilot for her, and she helped him get a job on The Tonight Show . De Cordova came aboard a bit later, and they enjoyed a complementary relationship, he told Mark Malkoff on a 2014 episode of The Carson Podcast . “He would be Mr. Jolly and schmooze with the guests, which I didn’t like to do, and I would do all the work. And that worked perfectly,” he said. The pair had lunch together every day for more than two decades, often throwing in a game of poker. Lassally had final say on all Tonight Show guests — he recognized Garry Shandling ‘s potential during an appearance on The Merv Griffin Show and pursued Steven Wright after seeing him do stand-up at a Chinese restaurant — and broke in the guest hosts who sat in when Carson was on vacation. “The gift that I keep looking for in people, whether they’re hosts or guests, is likability,” he said. “I don’t care if you have the No. 1 record or the No. 1 movie; if you’re not likable, I’d rather not put you on because I don’t think the audience will stay up.” Joan Rivers eventually became the permanent guest host, and she assumed Lassally would follow her when she landed her own late-night show at Fox in 1986. He stayed loyal to Carson, however. After Carson retired, Lassally convinced him to send jokes to Letterman for his monologues. “He didn’t want to force Dave to use them because of who Johnny was,” he told Malkoff. “I said, ‘No, these jokes are wonderful, and Dave would be honored and proud to do them on his show.’ He finally gave in.” Shandling also bounced talk-show ideas off him for HBO’s The Larry Sanders Show . “Shandling and his writing partner would ask me, ‘Could this have happened?’ I would say yes and no,” he said. In his TV Academy Foundation interview, Lassally noted that Late Show originally was to spend just one year in New York before moving to Los Angeles. However, when the program came out of the gate beating Leno in the ratings, those plans were shelved, and Lassally stayed in New York for about 2 1/2 years, longer than he would have preferred. He was serving as a consultant on Late Late Show when he was asked to oversee the selection of a new host after Kilborn’s exit. Four finalists — Ferguson, D.L. Hughley, Michael Ian Black and Damien Fahey — emerged from more than two dozen guest hosts (among them Stewart) before Ferguson, despite his heavy Scottish burr, got the job. Lassally retired in 2014 as executive producer of Late Late Show when Ferguson left. He collected 13 Emmy nominations during his career, with wins in 1992 for The Tonight Show and 1994 for Late Show . “When Johnny Carson and David Letterman needed counsel and an honest opinion, they immediately went to Peter Lassally, the professor of late night,” NBC said in a statement. “His relationship to each of these giants was immeasurable, and both of them would undoubtedly say his contribution to their success was so impactful that it would be difficult to put in words. [He was] a quiet man whose influence and stature spoke volumes; his brilliance was in shaping what we watch, how we watch and why late night was, and remains, vitally significant.” In addition to his son, survivors include his daughter, Andrea, and his grandchildren, Walker, Eloise, Annabel and Owen. His wife of 60 years, Alice, predeceased him. “I respect talent, I’m in awe of talent,” he once said. “If you are really talented, I will put up with your craziness. Because if you’re that talented, you’re not a normal person; there’s something wacky about you.” THR

articles.title: Matt Damon Reveals Why He Had Female Stunt Double for ‘Odyssey’ Scene: “Greatest Arms I’ve Ever Seen”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 5:55pm Matt Damon as Odysseus in 'The Odyssey.' Melinda Sue Gordon/Universal Pictures As Josh Horowitz points out, Matt Damon had quite an impressive physique in The Odyssey , specifically in the bicep region. However, the actor confessed he can’t take full credit for all the times you see his muscular limbs in the film. During a recent interview with the Happy Sad Confused podcast host , Damon revealed that he actually had a female stunt double for one key scene in Christopher Nolan’s epic action fantasy film . After thanking Horowitz for the “high praise,” The Rip actor explained, “When we did the forced perspective stuff of the Laestrygonians — I don’t know if there’s been a thing about how we did it — there were these stunt men who were all seven feet,” he said, referring to the giant warriors in The Odyssey . Related Stories Business What's Really In the AI Odyssey Film Movies Christopher Nolan on 'The Odyssey' Whetting His Horror Appetite, Making the "Ultimate Dog Movie" and Re-Releasing 'The Prestige' “And then they got stuntmen who were under five feet, and so my double was a woman, a female stunt performer, who had the greatest arms I’ve ever seen,” he added. Damon recalled first meeting the stunt double in the catering tent while filming and going up to hug her and thank her “for all the work she put in.” “So there are those shots in the movie where you see these giants looming over me, and so it was almost 100 percent my arms in the movie, but you gotta give it up where it’s due,” he said. The Odyssey , based on Homer’s ancient Greek poem, follows King Odysseus’ (Damon) dangerous voyage back to Ithaca after the Trojan War, including battles with mythical creatures, as he attempts to reunite with his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway), and son, Telemachus (Tom Holland). The film also stars Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong’o, John Leguizamo , Elliot Page, Mia Goth, Corey Hawkins, Jon Bernthal , Samantha Morton, Travis Scott and Benny Safdie. Following its July 17 release, the film scored a major box office victory , collecting more than $264 million globally in its debut weekend. THR

articles.title: FIFA World Cup Halftime Show Director on Making First-Ever Concert: “Challenging Beyond Challenging”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All July 20, 2026 6:28pm Ronaldinho, Madonna and Ronaldo perform during the Topps Final Halftime Show in the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026, in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Carl Recine/Getty Images Hamish Hamilton has directed over a dozen Super Bowls , the opening ceremony to the 2012 Summer Olympics, six Emmy Awards ceremonies, four Oscars and three Grammy nights, among many more marquee events. None of those, he says, were quite as challenging as the first-ever FIFA World Cup Finals Halftime Show he directed on Sunday. “A lot of that is because it was the first,” Hamilton, co-founder of the production company Done + Dusted, tells The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom from his New Jersey hotel room the morning after the World Cup, calling the show “challenging beyond challenging.” Related Stories TV Was the World Cup Final Halftime Show "Too American"? Rest of the World Seems to Think So: "Glib and Unsubtle" TV Five Things the Cameras Didn't See at the World Cup Final “Along with the Olympics, this was right up there,” he says. “I’m sure the first Super Bowl Halftime show was incredibly difficult, but when I came in they’d already done over 40 of them. By the time you get to Super Bowl 47, the NFL’s got everything super well drilled. But in this kind of scenario, there are so many unanswered questions. There’s all the people who haven’t done it before, a huge amount of nervousness, we’re doing this in daylight, you’ve got the grass, you’ve got a huge collection of superstars. It’s absolutely terrifying because there are so many things can go wrong.” Luckily for Hamilton and FIFA, they didn’t have any technical snags Sunday, and months of prep came and went in a quick-fleeting moment as Madonna, BTS , Justin Bieber, a Gustavo Dudamel-led orchestra, Shakira, Burna Boy, the PS22 Choir and the Muppets all hit the stage in an 11-minute time span. “It’s a mixture of exhaustion, relief and happiness,” Hamilton says of the show’s conclusion. “I’m very proud of what we did to help bring Chris [Martin, of Coldplay, who served as curator] and Global Citizens’ vision to life. They had this dream four years ago. It’s an enormous undertaking and they should be applauded for what they did.” Figuring out how to format the show to fit so many acts in such a short time frame was its own challenge, but as Hamilton says, the bigger question was the “gargantuan kind of logistical undertaking” involved with the broader production. There was the “very strong daylight that just kept coming,” which influenced how they shot the whole show. And whereas the NFL games MetLife Stadium usually hosts are played on artificial turf, the FIFA final was played on grass. The more delicate surface impacts everything for halftime, from what stage sets are possible to what sorts of cameras they could use. Plenty of the pressure was coming from outside as well. The halftime show was the subject of skepticism from soccer fans around the globe, who questioned the need for the show and worried about how adding a concert to a game where halftime is normally just 15 minutes would impact the competition itself. The Cure’s Robert Smith made headlines last week ahead of the finals in his critique of the show, writing “pleasejustfuckoff.” The Guardian , meanwhile, referred to the concert as “ the half-time show nobody asked for.” Hamilton, himself British and a lifelong fan of the Premier League’s Arsenal F.C., acknowledged those sentiments and noted they’re more prevalent in markets outside of the U.S., which is historically much more acclimated to melding music and sport thanks to events like the Super Bowl. “I’m a football fan, and have been my entire life,” he says. “Around the world, certainly around Europe and in the U.K., I saw some people who were like, ‘We don’t want your halftime show. We don’t want the Americanization of the beautiful game.’ I was, of course, very aware of that resistance. It’s not so much in America, because sports, entertainment and music sit a lot closer together here than they do probably anywhere else in the world. But I was very aware of that, and also about disrupting the second half if there were any issues with the grass. It’s hard, it’s pressure.” Will any skeptics be converted now that the first show has come and gone with the rest of the tournament? “It’s a very good question, I was so absorbed and immersed in creating the show within the game,” Hamilton says. “If someone else was directing and I was just watching from London [as a fan], maybe I could comment. But listen, it’s the World Cup Final, it’s the greatest, most-watched sporting event in the world. Having been part of it as a live director, I would say on balance definitely, and I hope that they do another one.” THR

articles.title: Adam Driver Has Passed on So Many Marvel Roles That It’s Become a “Tradition,” Kevin Feige Says
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 7:34pm Adam Driver Aurore Marechal/Getty Images Logo text It seems Kevin Feige has gotten used to Adam Driver telling him no. During a recent interview with Happy Sad Confused podcast host Josh Horowitz , the Marvel Studios president revealed that Driver has turned down joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe so many times that it has become a “tradition.” “It’s no secret we’d like to [work with Driver],” Feige said. “But it’s a tradition to Zoom with him and then he passes. That’s a long-lived tradition. He couldn’t be more cordial. He is usually upfront about how he is feeling.” Related Stories Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Trailer Reveals First Look at Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom Movies NY Film Festival Sets James Gray's 'Paper Tiger' as Opening Night Film The Marvel boss didn’t reveal which roles he’s pitched to Driver; however, rumors have been circulating on social media about the actor potentially boarding the big-screen reboot of the X-Men that’s currently in development. Marvel has yet to confirm any casting for the film, but The Hollywood Reporter reported last year that Jake Schreier was in talks to direct . Though Driver has never shared why he keeps turning down opportunities to join the MCU , it likely wouldn’t be because they’re blockbuster films, as he’s had his fair share in those. Most notably, he played Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, including The Force Awakens (2015), The Last Jedi (2017) and The Rise of Skywalker (2019). In addition to other high-profile pics such as House of Gucci (2021), Ferrari (2023) and Megalopolis (2024), Driver likes to have a nice balance when it comes to his filmography, starring in plenty of indie films as well, including Inside Llewyn Davis (2013), Paterson (2016), Marriage Story (2019) and the upcoming Paper Tiger . Though Driver has no plans as of now to join the MCU, no matter how hard Feige tries, the actor is interested in stepping back into another blockbuster franchise: Star Wars . He had been working on a standalone Kylo Ren movie with director Steven Soderbergh , but Disney axed the film , despite it having Lucasfilm’s support. THR

articles.title: Chloe Fineman Opens Up About Decision to Leave ‘SNL’: “I’m Really Proud of Everything, But It’s Hard”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 8:48pm Chloe Fineman attends the premiere of Apple TV+'s "The Dink" at AMC Century City 15 on July 20 in Los Angeles. Frazer Harrison/Getty Images On Monday night, Chloe Fineman walked the carpet for new movie The Dink , following two big pieces of career news in the last week — first, that she was leaving Saturday Night Live , and second, that she would be joining Netflix show Myron Bolitar as a series regular. Fineman had appeared on SNL for seven seasons and wrote in her announcement post on Instagram that she “decided it’s time for my next chapter.” The new series — an adaptation of Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about an NBA star-turned-sports agent that is being co-showrun by David E. Kelley and Kyle Long — seems to be a big part of that next chapter, as she told The Hollywood Reporter at The Dink premiere. Related Stories TV 'Never Have I Ever' Alum Maitreyi Ramakrishnan Teases 'Elle' Season 2 Role: "Not Something I've Done Before" TV Chloe Fineman Finds Her First Post-'Saturday Night Live' Gig “Seven years is kind of like the classic way [at SNL ], and then like right as my contract was up, this amazing David E. Kelley opportunity came in like completely out of the blue. I did a little chemistry read and it was off to the races; it just felt like a perfect time,” Fineman explained. “I’m really proud of everything, but it’s hard. I’m genuinely really good friends with everybody and I genuinely couldn’t love that job more. So it’s really bittersweet, but I’m gonna be in New York. I’m down the street. Maybe you’ll see me.” She noted that Colin Jost had called her earlier that day because it was her birthday (“I fully cried”) and “everyone’s like really reaching out. It’s the sweetest show. It’s a hard show, but the people — it’s because of hours and everything. But like it really is a family, and I’ve been crying like sweet tears.” The comedian also added that she felt lucky to get to adjust to a more regular, non- SNL schedule while also working on something she was excited about, with filming starting on Myron Bolitar this week. As for larger SNL plans, Fineman said she was looking forward to “just stretching the TV wings and like who better than David E. Kelley? And I’m really excited to like watch SNL as an audience member [in person], which I’ve never done.” Her summer also includes the release of The Dink , starring alongside Jake Johnson and Ben Stiller in a comedy about a washed-up tennis pro who tries to save a club by reluctantly playing pickleball. Johnson joked that they “represent both sides” in the tennis vs. pickleball debate and the project came about when he was looking to do something “just funny and light and kind of easy listening.” “This kind of mid-range comedy with a nice three-act structure that’s kind of light has gone away, and they’ve either become really cool indies that are like very cool or huge franchises, and neither of those were the ones I really dreamt of making,” Johnson, who is a producer on the film, added of the sports comedy. “Being able to make a mid-tier comedy that’s just got like every scene there’s a different funny person who comes in — everybody’s funny in the movie. There’s heart. There’s a real story. There’s a structure. Like I want more movies like this, so I really hope it works.” The Dink , which also stars Mary Steenburgen, Ed Harris and Aaron Chen, premieres Friday on Apple TV. THR

articles.title: Action Xtreme Expands Into U.K., Ireland Distribution With John Hannah-Starring ‘Bad Day at the Office’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 21, 2026 4:00am John Hannah in 'Bad Day at the Office' Action Xtreme Action Xtreme is expanding into the U.K. and Ireland film distribution space with the release of the John Hannah-led Bad Day at the Office . The adrenaline-fueled POV action thriller, produced and directed by Chee Keong Cheung and also starring Radha Mitchell ( Silent Hill , Man on Fire ), will receive its U.K. premiere at the Edinburgh International Film Festival in August. It’s set to open the prestigious Midnight Madness strand before launching nationwide in cinemas across the U.K. and Ireland this October. The move represents a significant milestone for the U.K.-based studio. Alongside an expanding production slate, Action Xtreme is working on international partnerships, talent development initiatives and its pioneering MA in Action Filmmaking with Falmouth University. In addition to overseeing the theatrical release of productions in the U.K. and Ireland, the company will also selectively acquire commercially driven action and genre titles that “align with the brand.” Related Stories Movies 'My Friend the Porn Star' Review: German Documentary About Desire Is a Kooky, Kinky Delight Movies Toronto-Bound 'Onwards and Sideways,' With Laura Linney and Rhys Ifans as People Being Diagnosed With Parkinson's, Gets New Images (Exclusive) Bad Day at the Office is shot entirely from the first-person perspective using GoPro cameras. The film follows a man (Hannah) who wakes in a hotel with no memory of who he is, only to discover a dead body in the bath and an army of assassins closing in. Forced to go on the run and uncover the truth while fighting for survival, he discovers he may not be the man he thought he was. “Shot in the style of first-person shooter video games with cine-literate wit, humor, ferocious pacing and a cracking soundtrack, this is an anarchic, ultra-violent and hilarious thrill ride of pure, cinematic carnage,” said festival director at Edinburgh Emma Boa. “The ultimate Midnight Madness experience.” Cheung, also CEO of Action Xtreme, added: “ Bad Day at the Office is exactly the kind of bold, cinematic experience Action Xtreme was created for… Seeing our first theatrical release launch with a festival premiere at Edinburgh’s Midnight Madness, before rolling out nationwide, makes this an incredibly exciting moment for the company.” Co-CEO Andreas Roald said distribution has been “a key component” of their strategy. “Over the last few years we’ve focused on building Action Xtreme into far more than a production company… We’ve created a platform that develops action filmmakers, produces films and now brings those films directly to action audiences. Distribution has been a key component of our strategy.” The studio’s recent productions include Nigerian action thriller Son of the Soil , which became one of Netflix Africa’s most successful action releases following theatrical runs across multiple territories. Upcoming productions include sci-fi thriller The Experiment , starring Rhona Mitra and Famke Janssen, as well as several international co-productions currently in development. THR

articles.title: Ed Harris Felt ‘Misled’ by ‘Dutton Ranch’ About ‘Inconsequential’ Role: ‘Get Me the F— Out of Here’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 8:47pm PT Ed Harris Felt ‘Misled’ by ‘Dutton Ranch’ About ‘Inconsequential’ Role: ‘Get Me the F— Out of Here’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Marc Malkin , Jack Dunn Emerson Miller/Paramount+ Ed Harris does not sound satisfied with his role on “ Dutton Ranch .” At the Monday night premiere of Apple TV’s “The Dink,” Harris told Variety ‘s Marc Malkin that he felt “misled” about the importance of his role in the “Yellowstone” spinoff, and that halfway through filming Season 1, he was telling his team to “get me the fuck out of here.” “Prior to signing on for it, I was talked to quite a bit about what the season was, and what my character was going to do — and that I was one of the four main characters,” Harris said. “And that wasn’t really the case.” Related Stories Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership Spokespeople for Paramount, series creator Taylor Sheridan and 101 Studios did not immediately respond to Variety ‘s request for comment. Popular on Variety Harris said he expressed his discontent, but did not name Sheridan. “I said, ‘I’m feeling underused and inconsequential,’ and they kind of went, ‘Oh,'” Harris added. “I’m being told my character will have a little bit more to do [in Season 2]. I was just a little frustrated, to tell you the truth.” Ed Harris says he felt “misled” about his “inconsequential” role on “Dutton Ranch,” and that halfway through filming Season 1, he was telling his team to “get me the fuck out of here.” “Prior to signing on for it, I was talked to quite a bit about what the season was, and what… pic.twitter.com/jwafO8ZUih — Variety (@Variety) July 21, 2026 Harris explained that when he actually watched “Dutton Ranch,” he thought it was “pretty good,” and he felt his character was “relatively important to the story.” However, during filming, “it didn’t feel that way.” On “Dutton Ranch,” Harris plays Everett McKinney, a good-humored veterinarian. Harris is currently signed on for two seasons. While Harris suggested he was ready to walk away from “Dutton Ranch,” it is unclear if he is actually looking to exit the show. The “Apollo 13” star then recalled filming a scene where his character sings in a bar, only to have the moment cut from the show. Harris said that “really pissed him off.” “So there’s this scene in there … I’m talking to [Beth Dutton] at the bar, and [Rip Wheeler] comes in and says, ‘OK, Everett, come on, it’s your turn,” Harris said. “I walk up to the mic, and they cut it. They cut the song out. I’m going, ‘Fuck you, people.'” Harris remembered the production telling him they cut the moment because it was “too ‘up’ for the dark ending of that episode.” But Harris said, at the time, he felt like that was “enough reason to say I’m voiding my contract.” “Dutton Ranch” launched its series premiere on Paramount+ on May 15. The show follows Beth Dutton (Kelly Reilly) and Rip Wheeler (Cole Hauser) as they leave Montana to build their own ranch in South Texas. Other cast members include Finn Little, Juan Pablo Raba, Jai Courtney, J.R. Villarreal, Marc Menchaca, Natalie Alyn Lind and Annette Bening. articles.title: ‘Sherlock’ Creator Steven Moffat Set as International Guest of Serielizados – Barcelona Series Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 8:56pm PT ‘Sherlock’ Creator Steven Moffat Set as International Guest of Serielizados – Barcelona Series Festival (EXCLUSIVE) Moffat, also a ‘Doctor Who’ showrunner, will be joined by Sue Vertue, producer of his series and ‘Mr. Bean’ By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest ‘Sherlock’ Creator Steven Moffat Set as International Guest of Serielizados – Barcelona Series Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 7 hours ago World Cup Final Ratings Skyrocket Across Europe, Despite England and France Losses 19 hours ago Brazil’s Gramado Fest Set to Honor ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello and ‘The Secret Agent’ Standout Maria Fernanda Cândido 2 days ago See All Steven Moffat, Sue Vertue Courtesy of Serielizados Currently priming “ Number 10 ,” one of the most awaited of British TV series, “Sherlock” creator and “Doctor Who” showrunner Steven Moffat will attend Serielizados -Barcelona Series Festival as its headline international guest. He will be joined producer Sue Vertue , producer of “Mr. Bean,” “Sherlock” and “Number 10” and CEO of Hartswood Films, the U.K.’s longest-established scripted producer, also behind ITVX and ITV1 hit “Douglas Is Cancelled.” Hartswood Films was majority acquired by ITV Studios in 2024. Related Stories Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Serielizados has yet to reveal what Moffat and Vertue will talk about. If a Series Mania masterclass is anything to go on, their session in Barcelona will most certainly be funny. Popular on Variety “Real life is funny – drama is a lie,” Moffat said at Serielizados in Lille. “You can’t be too funny, too sexy or too pretty. Always go for funny. Humor is truth on speed, that’s what it is. It’s insight with velocity.” British humor is one of the things the British can be very good at, and one of its television industry’s main export values. Serielizados is ever more aligned with the Catalan TV industry while still attracting the Spanish premieres of some of the most talked-about international series of the year – 2025’s festival was won, for example, by Norway’s “A Better Man” and Canada’s “Empathy” – the conference strand at Serielizados industry arm, Serielizados Pro, generated a high-quality debate energized top executives from Nordic broadcasters SVT, DR and YLE, plus also reps from BBC Studios, Arte France, Germany’s Beta Film and Paris-based Slot Machine. In-person attendance soared last year 80% to 16,000, while Serielizados’ online version, hosted by upscale SVOD service Filmin , hit 194,000 viewers. ‘In Vitro,’ ‘Episòdic’ In 2026, running Oct. 19-28, Serielizados will open with “In Vitro,” backed by Catalan public broadcaster 3Cat and HBO Max and set to debut this fall. Created by Marc Crehuet and Alejandra Guimerà, and directed by Creheut (“Pop Ràpid,” “The One-Eyed King,” !Mirror, Mirror”), it turns on Blanca, 37, a biologist, new to a fertility clinic where she confronts the needs and risks of her clients and her own as well. Beta Film picked up international distribution rights for“In Vitro” ahead of Series Mania. Serielizados closes with an experiement, the first season of “Episòdic: El principi d’Arquimedes,” a six-part anthology series, each episode lasting 15 minutes, made by 38 audiovisual students from universities, film schools and educational institutions. The series is directed by Ainhoa Lastra (“La nit del foc,” at the Universitat Pompeu Fabra, and Andrea Morales (Paraules d’amor) and Carlos R. Haro (“Cinc minuts més, si us plau”). The series is written by Daniel Durán Pous – a producer on “Unicorni” with two shorts to his credit, “Hipolit” and “L’ultim tren” – adapting the “The Arquimedes Principle,” from playwright Josep María Miró. An alleged child-abuse drama which cleverly plays with audiences own sense of prejudice, the work is hailed in its native Catalonia as a modern Catalan classic. Shooting ‘Episòdic’ ‘ Segunda Temporada,’ ‘Nissaga de poder,’ ‘Literaturium de séries ‘ Serielizados will also showcase “Segunda Temporada,” the latest Filmin Original from Spain’s upscale SVOD streaming service, turning on Paula, a once bestselling generational voice who, after writers’ block, is reduced to ghosting the bio of a washed up trap music legend, just out of prison, and maybe or maybe not feeling redemption. Created by Miguel Angel Blanca, behind breakout Filmin hit “Autodefensa,” “Segunda Temporada” will contend in Serielizados national competition. ‘Segunda Temporada’ The TV festival will also showcase the 30th anniversary of 3Cat daily soap “Nissaga de poder,” a milestone in its drive for ambitious originals, and “Literaturium de séries,” an exclusive live edition of the comedy podcast reviewing the supposed but fictional best TV series of the year. Mind The Gap Serielizados also announced Tuesday the second edition of Mind the Gap, its project pitching showcase which will take place Oct. 21, forming part of Serielizados PRO. Expanded to 11 selected titles, with its call for submissions now open and extended through Aug. 17, eight will be chosen from an open call and three tapped from winners at Germany’s Seriencamp Co-Production Pitch and Spain’s ECAM Forum and Iberseries & Platino Industria – an indication of how European events are working together to get projects in front of its top commissioners, production executives and sales agents who make up Mind the Gap’s jury. Participants can also expect press coverage. Winners at Mind the Gap’s inaugural edition last year were led by best series laureate “Fortune Cookie,” a low-fi sci-fi drama thriller set in Madrid’s Usera Chinatown, created by Adrián Saba (“The Erection of Toribio Bardelli”) and produced by Kubik Films, Newen Studios Spanish banner headed by brothers Fernando, Jorge and Alberto Sánchez-Cabezudo. “A comedy about two Gen Z misfits dodging eviction, chasing dreams, flipping the finger to adulthood and to the glittering city [Barcelona] that’s leaving them behind,” said producer Anna M. Bofarull, “Precarity Fair,” created by Eli Cruz and Mika Cilindro and produced by KaBoGa, won Mind the Gap’s Konga Music Award. In a further move, Serielizados has released its poster with a slogan, “An Eye for It,” which, it says, “emphasizes the role of its programming team in filtering and curating the ever-growing number of television series, helping audiences discover the most exciting and distinctive titles in an increasingly crowded landscape.” Serielizados has indeed often shown impecable taste in its lineup selection and top prizes, a jury recognising Sweden’s “Pressure Point” in 2024, for instance, as best international series. articles.title: Jon Stewart Says the World Cup Final Was the ‘Reverse Super Bowl’: ‘The Players Spoke Spanish and the Halftime Show Was in English’
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 9:30pm PT Jon Stewart Says the World Cup Final Was the ‘Reverse Super Bowl’: ‘The Players Spoke Spanish and the Halftime Show Was in English’ By Jack Dunn Plus Icon Jack Dunn Latest Ed Harris Felt ‘Misled’ by ‘Dutton Ranch’ About ‘Inconsequential’ Role: ‘Get Me the F— Out of Here’ (EXCLUSIVE) 7 hours ago Ben Shapiro Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Masterpiece’ Despite Conservative Outrage: Christopher Nolan Is the ‘Best Working Director Today’ 2 days ago ‘Shark Tank’ Star Kevin O’Leary Sued For Claiming Utah Data Center Opposition Has Ties to China 2 days ago See All Comedy Central On Monday night’s episode of “ The Daily Show ,” Jon Stewart gave his post-game thoughts about Sunday’s World Cup final match, which saw Spain win out over Argentina 1-0. “Of course, the World Cup ended yesterday, finito, with Spain defeating Argentina 1-0 on the pitch, in the footy,” Stewart said at the top of the show. “The Spain-Argentina final was like a reverse Super Bowl, where the players spoke Spanish, and the halftime show was in English.” Related Stories Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership The World Cup final halftime show, the first in the tournament’s history, featured Madonna, Justin Bieber and the Muppets. Stewart took note of “Sesame Street’s” The Count, who was there to celebrate the match along with Kermit and Miss Piggy. Popular on Variety “You got all the Muppets to choose from, why would in God’s name make the vampire work during the day?” Stewart joked. “Not only is it in the bright glare of the afternoon sun, but for most of the game, the score was 0-0! You’re taunting this poor bastard! ‘I sat in traffic for one, two, three hours for this.’” Stewart then, of course, shifted his attention to President Donald Trump’s presence at the game. He honed in on an awkward moment where Trump lingered on stage to be part of the trophy hoist, a moment usually reserved for “just the players.” “What the fuck are you doing on the stage?” Stewart exclaimed. “It’s for the players! Goddamn! Why must everything be tainted by the overinflated ego of Cankles Muldoon? Why?” Check out the entire monologue below. articles.title: Chloe Fineman Says ‘SNL’ Boss Lorne Michaels Was at World Cup Match When She Called to Say She Was Leaving the Show
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 10:00pm PT Chloe Fineman Says ‘SNL’ Boss Lorne Michaels Was at World Cup Match When She Called to Say She Was Leaving the Show By Marc Malkin Plus Icon Marc Malkin Senior Editor, Culture and Events marcmalkin Latest Chloe Fineman Says ‘SNL’ Boss Lorne Michaels Was at World Cup Match When She Called to Say She Was Leaving the Show 6 hours ago Ed Harris Felt ‘Misled’ by ‘Dutton Ranch’ About ‘Inconsequential’ Role: ‘Get Me the F— Out of Here’ (EXCLUSIVE) 7 hours ago Daniel Radcliffe to Narrate Comedian Kyle Gordon’s Third Album (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago See All Variety via Getty Images “ Saturday Night Live ” boss Lorne Michaels was a bit tied up when Chloe Fineman called to say she was leaving the show. “In classic form, he was watching England vs. Argentina,” Fineman told Variety at Monday night’s premiere of Apple TV’s “The Dink” in Los Angeles. “He was like, ‘I’ll call you back. I’m a the game.’ And I was like, ‘The soccer game?’ Then I made a joke, I was like, ‘I assume you’re rooting for England because you’re energetically very British.’ Then he called me back, and we had a really lovely chat.” Related Stories Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership Chloe Fineman says Lorne Michaels was at the World Cup when she called to tell him she was leaving #SNL : “He was like, ‘I’ll call you back. I’m at the soccer game.’ And I was like, ‘The soccer game? I assume you’re rooting for England because you’re energetically very British.’” pic.twitter.com/yXMV0zUP7r — Variety (@Variety) July 21, 2026 Fineman also shared that when the news of her “SNL” exit went live, she was very emotional. Popular on Variety “I cried when it was announced,” she said. “You really become a family [with the cast]… I wept when Colin Jost called me today, like, they really are my family. I’m happy that after seven years, I leave on a high note.” Fineman announced on July 16 that she was exiting the show. “After 7 wonderful seasons at ‘SNL’ I have decided it’s time for my next chapter,” Fineman wrote in an Instagram post . She concluded, “It’s really hard to leave ‘SNL’ but it does feel like the right time. I’m going to miss it a lot. But the people who work there are my family and that place is my home, and I know I’ll never be too far away.” Chloe Fineman says she cried after announcing she was leaving #SNL : “They really are like my best friends. So many people there. But it’s good to leave on a positive. You don’t want to stay past your expiration date.” pic.twitter.com/0W7uAJHVLW — Variety (@Variety) July 21, 2026 The actor-comedian joined “SNL” in 2019. She quickly became known for her range of impressions, which included Jennifer Coolidge, Timothée Chalamet, Drew Barrymore, Britney Spears and JoJo Siwa. Chloe Fineman says “we just scratched the surface” of her Melania Trump impression on #SNL . After announcing this week that she's leaving the sketch comedy series following seven seasons, Fineman says “you never know” when asked if she could return to play the First Lady during… pic.twitter.com/hniYeeG109 — Variety (@Variety) July 21, 2026 Fineman’s first post-“SNL” gig will be as a series regular role in the “ Myron Bolitar ” series currently in the works at Netflix . Series regulars will also include Jabari Banks (“Bel Air”) and Jamie McShane (“Task,” “Wednesday”). Ben McKenzie (“Everyone is Lying to You for Money,” “Gotham”) will appear in a recurring guest star role. Series leads include Colin Woodell, KJ Apa, and Diane Guerrero. Netflix originally announced the series pickup in May as part of their upfront presentation to advertisers. The show is inspired by Harlan Coben’s popular Myron Bolitar books, of which 12 have been published. The logline for the show states, “After an injury ends his NBA dreams, Myron Bolitar (Woodell) reinvents himself as a sports agent — using charm, smarts, and a ruthless partner to navigate the high-stakes and dirty world of sports, where saving his clients often means risking himself.” In addition to Fineman, the cast of “The Dink,” a sports comedy about pickleball, includes Jake Johnson, Ben Stiller, Christine Taylor, Patton Oswalt, Martin Kove, Mary Steenburgen and Ed Harris, as well as tennis legends Andy Roddick and John McEnroe. “The Dink” premieres on Apple TV on July 24. Rahman , the two-time Oscar-winning Indian composer behind “Slumdog Millionaire” and “127 Hours,” is launching ARR Immersive , an app bringing his decade of immersive storytelling work to Apple Vision Pro on July 22. The app draws on Rahman’s ongoing work in immersive formats, tracing back to “Le Musk,” a 360-degree virtual reality film that debuted at the Cannes XR Festival. ARR Immersive marks the first time content from “Le Musk” has appeared on Apple Vision Pro, with the footage reworked for the headset’s spatial format. This is about bringing together music, storytelling and innovation to create experiences that are deeply personal, emotionally engaging and truly immersive. I believe this is an exciting new canvas for creators, and this is only the beginning.” ARR Immersive can be downloaded through the Apple App Store, debuting first on Apple Vision Pro, with a Meta Quest release to follow. Rahman Launches ARR Immersive App for Apple Vision Pro (EXCLUSIVE) 5 hours ago See All ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection The U.K. and Ireland box office experienced a massive tentpole shift as Universal’s “ The Odyssey ” captured the top spot, storming the market with a spectacular debut weekend of £12.5 million ($16.8 million). The performance registered as Nolan’s second-biggest opening frame in the market, landing well ahead of “Oppenheimer.” Driven by an unprecedented showing on premium large formats, “The Odyssey” achieved the biggest opening Friday of the year and recorded Universal’s fifth-biggest opening Friday ever. The BFI Imax – the U.K.’s largest screen – reported its highest three-day opening weekend in history, bringing in a $294,249 from the single venue. This historic frame broke the previous all-time BFI Imax weekend record held by “Star Wars: The Last Jedi” ($289,682) in 2017, with “Oppenheimer” now sitting in third place with $277,936. To date, the London site alone has logged over 82,000 admissions, generating $2.9 million in ticket sales and maintaining a 94% occupancy rate, making it the venue’s third highest-grossing title of all time with 173 consecutive sold-out showtimes. The film’s five-week running cume is now $60.6 million. Disney also took the No. 3 spot with its live-action “ Moana .” In its sophomore session, the film added $2 million, taking its running total to $7.4 million. Popular on Variety Universal secured fourth place with “Minions & Monsters,” which took $1.5 million in its third week, pushing its cume to $12.5 million. Studiocanal’s horror feature “Evil Dead Burn” was in fifth place in its second weekend, banking $406,258 for a running total of $2.2 million. Black Bear’s ensemble comedy-drama “The Invite” occupied sixth place during its third weekend, adding $318,749 to its cume, which now rests at $3.3 million. Universal’s “Obsession” followed at No. 7 in its 10th frame, pocketing $249,169 to push its total to $24.9 million. Warner Bros.’ superhero holdover “Supergirl” hit eighth place in its fourth frame with $123,852, boosting its cumulative haul to $7.4 million. Universal’s Steven Spielberg sci-fi thriller “Disclosure Day” sat at ninth place with $91,904 in its sixth week, taking its total to $16.9 million. Paramount’s “Jackass: Best and Last” finished 10th in its fourth week, adding $57,313 for a total of $2.9 million. Park Circus is re-releasing the classic Aardman animation “Chicken Run” into over 100 locations, while Curzon has a 4K restoration rollout for Andrei Tarkovsky’s masterpiece “Nostalghia.” Trafalgar is opening Sia’s music event “Sia: Nostalgic For The Present (Concert)” and Altitude “Pinocchio Unstrung.” Verve Pictures launches Helen Walsh’s contemporary drama “On The Sea,” featuring a cast led by Barry Ward and Lorne Macfadyen. Jean.” Zee Studios International is opening “The India Story,” while Vue Lumière brings “Animal Farm” to select sites. articles.title: Anurag Kashyap, MIFFest Jury President, Searches for ‘a New Cinematic Language’
articles.full_text: Jul 21, 2026 2:34am PT Anurag Kashyap, MIFFest Jury President, Searches for ‘a New Cinematic Language’ By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Anurag Kashyap, MIFFest Jury President, Searches for ‘a New Cinematic Language’ 2 hours ago APOS 2026 Takeaways: IP, Sport, AI Define Asia’s New Content Era 1 month ago ReelShort Looks Beyond Microdramas as Joey Jia Pushes for a New Entertainment Ecosystem 1 month ago See All Getty Images Indian auteur Anurag Kashyap , whose latest directorial feature “Bandar” marks his return behind the camera, is at this year’s Malaysia International Film Festival ( MIFFest ) as jury president while also leading a masterclass titled “Unfiltered Realism.” But rather than having all the answers, the veteran filmmaker is hoping to discover something new. “As jury president, what I’m really looking for is a new cinematic language,” Kashyap tells Variety . “I’m interested in seeing how younger filmmakers tell stories in ways my generation couldn’t.” Related Stories Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Kashyap believes today’s filmmakers are entering an entirely different creative landscape. AI tools, social media and an overwhelming abundance of information have transformed not only how films are made but also how audiences receive them. Popular on Variety Looking back on more than two decades of filmmaking, Kashyap pushed back on a common assumption. “Staying real isn’t a choice,” he added. “Whether I’m directing, producing or acting, you have to stay real. Only then can you fully play out reality and truly engage your audience.” He acknowledges that earlier in his career, limited budgets and available technology naturally pushed his films toward grounded storytelling. But he argues that authenticity has never been about visual style. Rather than seeing authenticity as a branding strategy, Kashyap believes local stories resonate globally precisely because they remain deeply rooted in their own cultures. Across Asia, Kashyap sees filmmakers share many of the same challenges despite working in different industries. “South Korea, Japan, China and India all have mature film industries,” he says. “But we’re all facing the same problem – audiences have shorter attention spans, and streaming platforms have created endless choices.” Those concerns echo comments Kashyap made earlier this year about the pressures facing contemporary cinema, particularly independent filmmaking in an increasingly fragmented viewing environment. Rather than offering a blueprint for filmmaking, Kashyap hopes the masterclass will become a conversation – one where he’s as eager to learn as he is to share his own experiences. “I have many questions myself as well,” he says. “I’m hoping to find some answers, have meaningful conversations during the festival and maybe discover another clue about the future of cinema.” ‘Scrubs’ Revival Ups Ava Bunn to Series Regular, X Mayo and Joel Kim Booster Exit Peter Lassally, Legendary Late Night Producer for Johnny Carson, David Letterman and Craig Ferguson, Dies at 93 ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Limited Edition DC Comic Book, Experiential Space for Fans Planned for San Diego Comic-Con (EXCLUSIVE) Variety’s Faith & Media Impact Report 2026: Nominations Are Open Chloe Fineman Says ‘SNL’ Boss Lorne Michaels Was at World Cup Match When She Called to Say She Was Leaving the Show TIFF Announces Star-Studded Gala and Special Presentations, Led by ‘Rocky’ Biopic ‘I Play Rocky’ and Chris Rock’s ‘Misty Green’ Loading comments... Nandy, who has been a member of Parliament since 2010 as representative for the constituency of Wigan, was appointed secretary of state for culture, media and sport by previous Prime Minister Keir Starmer in July 2024, shortly after the Labour party won the general election, making her the 12th minister in the post in almost as many years. She previously served as the shadow cabinet minister for international development and shadow housing minister. Popular on Variety Nandy took office during a period of uncertainty for the U.K.’s screen sector in the wake of the Hollywood writer and actor strikes, post-pandemic inflation coupled with a downturn in the ad market and slashed budgets from broadcasters and streamers. She is currently overseeing the BBC’s royal charter renewal, including its funding mechanism, as well as the U.K. arm of the Paramount/Warner Bros. Discovery merger, in which she said she was “minded to intervene.” Other major deals in the U.K. include Comcast-owned Sky’s recent acquisition of public service broadcaster ITV, which has yet to receive regulatory approval, as well as potential bidders for its soon-to-be-spun-off production arm ITV Studios. Meanwhile Burnham has also appointed Kanishka Narayan as the first minister for AI, jointly in the Cabinet Office and the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. Narayan was previously parliamentary under-secretary of state in the science, innovation and technology department. He was elected in July 2024 as the MP for Vale of Glamorgan. articles.title: Ryan Reynolds Says There Will ‘Eventually’ Be Another ‘Deadpool’ Movie: ‘There’s a Few Really Deep Cuts That I Think Are Missing’
articles.full_text: Jul 21, 2026 3:56am PT Ryan Reynolds Says There Will ‘Eventually’ Be Another ‘Deadpool’ Movie: ‘There’s a Few Really Deep Cuts That I Think Are Missing’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Michael Urie on Returning to ‘Oh, Mary!,’ His Second ‘Shrinking’ Emmy Nod and 20 Years of ‘Ugly Betty’: ‘That Show Was So Ahead of Its Time’ 20 hours ago Andy Burnham Set to Become U.K. Prime Minister as Former Manchester Mayor Named Labour Party Leader 4 days ago Donald Trump Drops Part of $10 Billion BBC Lawsuit 4 days ago See All ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett C Deadpool ‘s story isn’t over yet. During a panel at Fanatics Fest over the weekend, Ryan Reynolds confirmed that there will “eventually” be another movie starring the Marvel antihero — but it may revolve around “deep cuts” from the character’s comics. “There’s a few really deep cuts that I think are missing from the movies. I think there’s a few deep cuts missing from some of the comics,” Reynolds told moderator Nature Luvz You (via Hobby Nonsense ). “There’s certainly some stuff that I love that [Deadpool co-creator] Fabian [Nicieza] wrote that is incredible [and] Gerry Duggan, another friend and incredible comic writer, that we can put in. But then there’s stuff upcoming. There’s eventually, you know, remotely another ‘Deadpool’ film. So it’s going to be great.” Related Stories Fox's Red Seat Ventures, Amazon Strike Programmatic Advertising Partnership Ubisoft Hires Former Amazon Games Chief Christoph Hartmann as Head of New Division, Including Oversight of Acquired 'March of Giants' Game Marvel did not immediately respond to Variety ‘s request for comment. Popular on Variety Following the huge success of 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine,” Reynolds told “Sunday Today” in April that he’s already started writing Deadpool’s return to the big screen, though he said the Merc With the Mouth wouldn’t be the main focus. “I have some stuff kind of written, but I don’t think I am ever going to center him again,” Reynolds said. “He is a supporting character. He is a guy who is great in a group.” Reynolds has also downplayed rumors that the character makes a comeback in the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday” film, though speculation remains rife about the possibility. In a 2024 interview with The Hollywood Reporter , Reynolds said he’d love for the character to cross paths with the Avengers or X-Men — but doesn’t want him to join either group. “If he becomes either, we’re at the end,” Reynolds said. “Deadpool works so well appearing with the X-Men and Avengers, but he always needs to stay an outsider. His ultimate dream is to be accepted and appreciated. But he can’t be accepted. His coping mechanism of deflecting shame through humor works only when used to pave over his many inadequacies. Wisher Jr. Dies: ‘The Terminator’ & ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Screenwriter Was 71 Kevin Feige On Trying To Cast Adam Driver In Marvel Role Amid ‘X-Men’ Reboot Rumors: “It’s A Tradition To Zoom With Him & Then He Passes” View All July 20, 2026 6:03pm Kevin Feige and Adam Driver Getty Images Kevin Feige has been trying to work with Adam Driver and cast him in a Marvel film role, but so far it has not become official.
