articles.title: ‘The Odyssey’ Rules The World, But Stephen Chow’s ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Scores $214M+ Cume, ‘Toy Story 5’ Nears $1B – Global Weekend Top 10 Box Office
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘The Odyssey’ Rules The World, But Stephen Chow’s ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Scores $214M+ Cume, ‘Toy Story 5’ Nears $1B – Global Weekend Top 10 Box Office ‘The Odyssey’ Doesn’t Stop: Epic Bound For Best Monday YTD Stateside With $17M+ – Box Office Update Sony Dates Bad Robot’s JT Mollner Horror Pic ‘Skeletons’ Starring Brie Larson For Summer 2027 View All July 20, 2026 6:49pm 'The Odyssey,' 'Kung Fu Soccer' and 'Toy Story 5' Universal Pictures / Disney Yes, Universal’s Christopher Nolan epic The Odyssey led by an extreme margin at the global box office with an updated $263.7M , a hands down opening record for the 2x Oscar winning filmmaker fueled by his best ever start overseas with $140.2M from 73 territories and his third best opening in North America with $123.5M. For more of the foreign breakdown on The Odyssey, click here . But here’s how everything else shook out with China elbowing its way into the chart with three, count ’em three blockbusters, despite Odysseus essentially No. 1 everywhere (except Vietnam and Argentina). He doesn’t show up in the Middle Kingdom until August 14. Why is China coming up so big at the B.O. suddenly? Because holidays are in full swing. Related Stories News 'The Odyssey' Doesn't Stop: Epic Bound For Best Monday YTD Stateside With $17M+ - Box Office Update News 'The Odyssey': What Do The Fates Have In Store For Christopher Nolan's Homeric Epic As Awards Season Gets Under Way? Kung Fu Soccer Star Overseas Stephen Chow’s Kung Fu Soccer per AG Reports was a definite No. 2 at the global B.O. with a second frame in China of $73.7M (501.1M Rmb) and a running cume of $214.3M (1,457M Rmb). Two other local titles triumphed over MPA ones there with the No. 2 pic in China being Pearl Studio’s Zhengxing Mu directed animation comedy fantasy All Wishes Come True with a 2-day weekend of $30.6M (207.8M Rmb) and running cume of $39.6M (269M Rmb) since opening on July 18. A solid result for this pic off its 9.7 Maoyan score. Pic’s blurb: Eight grassroot mortals use their street smarts and hilarious schemes to defy powerful gods, earning their title as the “Eight Immortals.” All Wishes come true was No. 6 at the global weekend B.O. Also big in China was the Yingxin Ma directed and written female drama, A Part of Me , from Enlight Pictures which began with $13.6M (92.4M Rmb) ranking third in the country, and No. 8 on the global weekend chart. What was the highest grossing Hollywood movie in China this weekend? Universal’s Minions and Monsters with a third weekend of $3.6M and running cume of $40.3M; still the pic’s biggest offshore territory both weekend and total wise. articles.title: William H. Wisher Jr. Dies: ‘The Terminator’ & ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Screenwriter Was 71
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Mara Wilson Says ‘Matilda’ Sequel “Could Be Possible” & Why It “Annoyed” Her Being Linked To Film William H. Wisher Jr. Dies: ‘The Terminator’ & ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Screenwriter Was 71 Kevin Feige On Trying To Cast Adam Driver In Marvel Role Amid ‘X-Men’ Reboot Rumors: “It’s A Tradition To Zoom With Him & Then He Passes” View All July 20, 2026 7:38pm William H. Wisher Jr. and 'The Terminator' Courtesy / Orion Pictures William H. Wisher Jr., a producer and screenwriter who co-wrote The Terminator and Terminator 2: Judgment Day , has died. He was 71. The Wisher family confirmed news of the filmmaker’s death, saying he “passed away peacefully at home.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Sets 35th Anniversary Global Re-Release “William believed that stories have the power to connect people across generations,” the family said in a statement. “While the world celebrates the unforgettable films he helped create, we will remember him for his kindness, his humor, his brilliant imagination, and the love he gave so freely to his family and friends. We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support during this difficult time.” Wisher helped redefine the science fiction action genre as one of the writers of James Cameron’s The Terminator , which was released in 1984. The screenwriter would return to work with Cameron in the film’s sequel, 1991’s Terminator 2: Judgment Day . Other films on which Wisher worked include Judge Dredd (1995), The 13th Warrior (1999), Exorcist: The Beginning (2004), Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist (2005), Live Free or Die Hard (2007), and I.T. (2016). On hearing of Wisher’s passing, Terminator producer Gale Anne Hurd wrote, “Such terribly sad news…Bill was not only integral to THE TERMINATOR but he was such an all around great guy. RIP” Wisher is survived by his wife, Deborah Lynn Wisher; his siblings, Brian Wisher, John Wisher, Carla DeMaci, and Dana Aboissiere; and many nieces, nephews, cousins, extended family members, and friends. articles.title: Mara Wilson Says ‘Matilda’ Sequel “Could Be Possible” & Why It “Annoyed” Her Being Linked To Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Mara Wilson Says ‘Matilda’ Sequel “Could Be Possible” & Why It “Annoyed” Her Being Linked To Film William H. Wisher Jr. Dies: ‘The Terminator’ & ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Screenwriter Was 71 Kevin Feige On Trying To Cast Adam Driver In Marvel Role Amid ‘X-Men’ Reboot Rumors: “It’s A Tradition To Zoom With Him & Then He Passes” View All July 20, 2026 8:05pm Mara Wilson TriStar Pictures Mara Wilson continues to be remembered for starring in the 1996 film Matilda , the Danny DeVito-directed film based on Roald Dahl’s 1988 novel of the same name. While attending the Fanboy Expo in Tennessee, Wilson opened up about a potential sequel to the fantasy film and why she didn’t like being associated with the character when she was younger. “People always ask me about doing a Matilda 2 . And that could be possible,” she said, according to People . Although Wilson is open to the idea of a follow-up to the film, she does question how they would make it happen. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Mara Wilson Doesn't Want To "Change Myself To Fit Into Hollywood's Mold" After Child Acting Years News 'Matilda' Star Reveals Fears About 'Stranger Things' Kids Getting Caught In AI's "Deepfake Apocalypse" After Her Own Experience “But one thing that people always say is, ‘Oh, maybe it could be Matilda’s daughter.’ And I have some issues with that, because I think Matilda’s powers come from her adversity,” Wilson said at the expo. “They come from the bad things that she went through, and the whole point is that she overcame these things. And she found power in educating herself and in making friends with these people who were really lovely.” She continued, “And so I don’t think Matilda would raise her daughter to be in a position where she developed those powers to protect herself.” Wilson also raised up the question as to who would marry Matilda, adding, “Who’s good enough for Matilda? Matilda’s such an awesome character that I can’t imagine who she would marry and have kids with, you know?” Before starring in Matilda , Wilson also starred in 1993’s Mrs. Doubtfire and 1994’s Miracle on 34th Street. However, after starring in Matilda, people started to refer to her by her character’s name, which she wasn’t initially fond of. “I used to be a little annoyed when people would call me Matilda because I was like, ‘No, I’m Mara. It felt almost a little bit like being called by your sister’s name — your much cooler, smarter sister’s name. And I was like, oh, no, I’m not as cool as she is,” she recalled. Wilson remembered Carrie Fisher once said, “I feel like me and Princess Leia have kind of merged over the years,” and Wilson said that she “sort of feels like that too.” “I feel like Matilda has been a character that I looked up to, and Matilda would do things that I do. She would talk about mental health. She would talk about books. She would be working. She would be writing, she would be loving books and doing stuff for public libraries and things like that. And I do all of those things. Those things are very important to me,” she added. “So Matilda has really taught me a lot of good lessons. And I think I’ve become a lot like her in my own way.” Judge Grants TRO To Pause Proposed Merger For 14 Days Trek Continues With Year’s Best Monday After Stellar Opening Weekend ‘Scrubs’ Ups Ava Bunn To Series Regular Alongside Lead OG Trio; Updates On Season 2 Peter Lassally Dies At 93: Legendary Late-Night Producer Of Carson & Letterman Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: Sadie Sink Keeps Mystery Of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Role & Reveals “I Am Not Aunt May”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Mara Wilson Says ‘Matilda’ Sequel “Could Be Possible” & Why It “Annoyed” Her Being Linked To Film William H. Wisher Jr. Dies: ‘The Terminator’ & ‘Terminator 2: Judgment Day’ Screenwriter Was 71 Kevin Feige On Trying To Cast Adam Driver In Marvel Role Amid ‘X-Men’ Reboot Rumors: “It’s A Tradition To Zoom With Him & Then He Passes” View All July 20, 2026 8:59pm Sadie Sink and Spider-Man Sony Pictures Entertainment Sadie Sink ‘s role in Spider-Man : Brand New Day remains a mystery ahead of the film’s premiere. A new video teased Sink revealing three things about her character in the Sony Pictures production, but left audiences with the same doubts. “Since the trailer dropped, I’ve seen so many theories about who I’m playing,” Sink said in the Instagram clip. “To match your incredible energy, I’ve decided to give you three exclusive, confirmed answers right now.” Related Stories News Sadie Sink On Working With Tom Holland In ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: “He Was Just So Relaxed And Open” News ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Red Carpet Photos: All Of Zendaya & Tom Holland’s Looks From Press Tour Starting off the video, Sink said, “I can confirm I am not Spider-Man.” She continued to joke and said, “I am not Aunt May,” the character that Marisa Tomei played and died in 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home . Watch on Deadline “And third, I can definitely confirm that I am in this movie,” she added. “As for who I really am, you’ll have to find out in the theater.” The Instagram caption for the post read, “We can confirm…she’s in this movie.” In a recent interview, Sink opened up about the positive experience she had working with Tom Holland in the superhero film. “It was interesting stepping into that space and being a little bit of an outsider in that way, but he could not have been more welcoming, and just the whole crew in general,” she told Nylon in an interview. “He was just so relaxed and open, and I felt very at ease.” The logline for Spider-Man: Brand New Day reads, “It’s a brand new day for Peter Parker. But that transformation might also be the only thing that can stop a shocking new threat to the city and those he loves – a powerful villain no one can even see. The world may have forgotten Peter Parker, but he hasn’t forgotten them.” Sink will star in the film alongside Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jon Bernthal, Liza Colón-Zayas, and Mark Ruffalo. articles.title: UK Sticks With Lisa Nandy As Culture Secretary, With Paramount-Warner & BBC Decisions Looming
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: “It’s Insulting” UK Sticks With Lisa Nandy As Culture Secretary, With Paramount-Warner & BBC Decisions Looming ‘Harry Potter’ Series Star Ruari Spooner Joins Bill Burr & Chris O’Dowd In Comedy ‘Bender’ View All July 21, 2026 1:09am Lisa Nandy Getty Andy Burnham, the UK’s new prime minister, has decided to stick rather than twist with his choice of culture secretary. 10 Downing Street has announced that Lisa Nandy will remain in the role overseeing Britain’s film and TV industry, meaning she will extend her stay at the Department for Culture, Media and Sport beyond two years. She is the longest-serving culture secretary since Jeremy Hunt in 2010. Nandy was widely tipped to be reshuffled into a new role by Burnham. Even BBC director general Matt Brittin told staff on Monday that he thought there could be a new culture secretary. Related Stories News Judge Grants Temporary Restraining Order To Pause Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery Merger For 14 Days Obituaries Edward Stourton Dies: UK Broadcaster Whose Most Recent Work Charted 250 Years Of American History Was 68 She will continue to oversee a busy inbox, with her immediate priorities including whether to formally intervene in Paramount’s $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Watch on Deadline Nandy will also be pivotal to the BBC’s future, as the corporation is currently in talks with the government over a new charter, which will effectively be its operating agreement for years to come. Other policy priorities include new legislation that would compel YouTube and TikTok to promote public service content from the BBC and other broadcasters. Some in the entertainment industry would have welcomed a change of culture secretary. Nandy is not viewed as being overly enthusiastic about her brief, with many senior industry figures describing her as aloof. She is, however, a supporter of the BBC, despite her deep misgivings about the Huw Edwards and MasterChef misconduct scandals, as well as editorial issues like the Glastonbury Gaza crisis. Nandy described the BBC as a “light on the hill” amid the tide of disinformation and said she wanted the corporation to have a “sustainable long-term funding model” under charter renewal. These positions are likely to continue, not least because the BBC will have an ally at the heart of government: James Purnell, its former policy and audio chief, will serve as Burnham’s chief of staff. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Na Hong-Jin’s Cannes Competition Title ‘Hope’ Has Strong Opening At Korean Box Office PVR Inox’s Sanjeev Kumar Bijli On India’s Box Office Recovery, Cinema Expansion & Cannes Acquisitions Haul CJ ENM’s Mnet & Universal Music Group’s Republic Partner To Launch Global Girl Group View All July 21, 2026 1:27am Happily Ever After Hong Kong-based international sales company Moebius Entertainment has acquired worldwide sales rights (excluding Taiwan) to Happily Ever After , the sophomore feature from Taiwanese filmmaker Fiona Roan Feng-I . The film will make its world premiere in the Special Presentations section of the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF). The acquisition marks a reunion between Moebius Entertainment founder and CEO Fred Tsui, director Fiona Roan Feng-i and producer Clifford Miu, following their collaboration on Roan’s debut feature, American Girl . Related Stories Festivals TIFF 2026 First Lineup: World Premieres Of 'I Play Rocky', Chris Rock's 'Misty Green', Anton Corbijn's 'A Talent For Murder', John Madden's 'Onwards And Sideways' & More Festivals TIFF Sets Special Presentations Including Riley Keough & Cate Blanchett Comedy 'Alpha Gang', Mahershala Ali's 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' & More American Girl premiered at Tokyo International Film Festival in 2021 and received a global streaming release via Netflix following its international festival run. It also scooped five prizes at Taiwan’s Golden Horse Awards including Best New Director for Fiona Roan Feng-i, Best New Performer for Caitlin Fang, Best Cinematography for Giorgos Valsamis, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Audience Choice Award. Watch on Deadline “ Happily Ever After confirms Fiona Roan’s remarkable talent as a filmmaker with a deeply human voice and an exceptional command of cinematic storytelling,” said Tsui. “After our rewarding collaboration on American Girl , I am delighted to be working again with Fiona and producer Clifford Miu. We believe the film will resonate strongly with audiences around the world, and we’re excited to introduce it to international buyers at Toronto.” Moebius Entertainment will launch international sales activities ahead of the film’s TIFF world premiere, with additional festival and distribution plans to be announced in coming months. Tsui, who was previously general manager and head of sales and international co-production at Media Asia, founded Moebius Entertainment as a boutique sales and consultancy company, working on auteur-driven Asian titles with strong international crossover potential. The company’s recent slate includes Peter Ho-sun Chan’s She Has No Name , Philip Yung’s Papa , Nick Cheung’s Peg O’ My Heart , Jame Hung’s My First Of May , and Wang Tong’s Wild Nights, Tamed Beasts . articles.title: ZDF & ProSieben Strike Streaming Pact As Traditional Rivals Team To Fight Streamers: “A Strong, Forward-Looking Signal”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse All3Media International’s Jonathan Hughes Exits For ITV Studios After Banijay Merger ZDF & ProSieben Strike Streaming Pact As Traditional Rivals Team To Fight Streamers: “A Strong, Forward-Looking Signal” ‘The Earliest Show’ Revival Greenlit At Amplify Pictures & Stay Tuned With Kevin Carroll, Henry Winkler, Ryan Gaul & Brandon Scott Jones Joining Cast View All July 21, 2026 1:41am ProsiebenSat.1 Media and ZDF have struck a streaming pact Matthias Balk/picture alliance via Getty Images; Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images ZDF and ProSiebenSat.1 are the latest traditional European rivals to team on a streaming deal. The pact will see ZDF’s on-demand content integrated into ProSieben’s streaming service, Joyn, from the fourth quarter of this year. This will allow Joyn users to access ZDF news, docs, culture, factual and entertainment programs for free without adverts. ZDF’s on streaming portal will remain “the central digital home of its public broadcasting content.” European players are increasingly looking to pool resources to combat the threat of global tech players, with recent examples seeing Channel 4 in talks with the BBC in the UK. ZDF and ProSieben noted their deal had been struck in an “increasingly international platform landscape” and that they were “deliberately focusing on a partnership that strengthens access to journalistic and cultural content ‘Made in Germany.'” Related Stories News Prime Video Drama 'The Assassin' Season 2 Lands Host Of Global Buyers News 'Deutschland 83' Co-Creator Jörg Winger Joins Dynamic Television To Head Up German Arm As ZDF Puts His New Show 'Conspiracy' Into Development Global streamers have also been striking deals with Euro broadcasters, with France’s TF1 recently rolling out its streaming and channel suite on Netflix, France Télévisions launching channels on Prime Video and Disney+ striking content sharing deals with ITV, RTVE, M6 and ZDF in the past year. Watch on Deadline The deal also ends a dispute between ZDF and Joyn from last year. That saw content from pubcasters ZDF and ARD added to Joyn without agreement, with ProSieben arguing free content was permissible to distribute under European law. Courts later ruled in favor of the public broadcasters, amid the introduction of Germany’s State Media Treaty, which encourages voluntary competition between pubcasters and commercial TV rivals. “Our mission is to reach as many people as possible with our high-quality content,” said Florian Kumb, Director Audience at ZDF. “By making ZDF streaming content available on Joyn in the future, we’re strengthening the visibility of public broadcasting journalism in the digital space.” Nicole Agudo Berbel, Chief Distribution & Partnerships Officer at ProSiebenSat.1: “This partnership demonstrates how public and private media can work together to find innovative responses to digital competition. In doing so, we’re sending a strong, forward-looking signal for the dual system and the media industry as a whole.” Judge Grants TRO To Pause Proposed Merger For 14 Days Trek Continues With Year’s Best Monday After Stellar Opening Weekend ‘Scrubs’ Ups Ava Bunn To Series Regular Alongside Lead OG Trio; Updates On Season 2 Peter Lassally Dies At 93: Legendary Late-Night Producer Of Carson & Letterman Read More About: Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse All3Media International’s Jonathan Hughes Exits For ITV Studios After Banijay Merger ZDF & ProSieben Strike Streaming Pact As Traditional Rivals Team To Fight Streamers: “A Strong, Forward-Looking Signal” ‘The Earliest Show’ Revival Greenlit At Amplify Pictures & Stay Tuned With Kevin Carroll, Henry Winkler, Ryan Gaul & Brandon Scott Jones Joining Cast View All July 21, 2026 2:05am Jonathan Hughes Courtesy Another senior All3Media International exec is exiting the Midsomer Murder firm following its parent’s merger with Banijay . Jonathan Hughes is joining ITV Studios (ITVS) after ten years at All3Media International, and will take on the role of Vice President, Germany and Benelux Sales. ITVS has also promoted Louisa Forsyth to become Vice President, UK and Ireland Sales. All3Media’s parent, RedBird IMI, and Banijay earlier this month completed their merger , creating the world’s largest production studio outside of the U.S. majors. It also brought together two major program distribution businesses, with exits likely given Banijay’s management previously stating they would look to make savings from the unit. Related Stories News Lionsgate Shares Surge Amid Reports 'Hunger Games' Studio Is Courting Euro Buyers Executives Louise Pedersen, CEO Of 'The Traitors' Distributor All3Media International, Exits After Banijay Merger; Cathy Payne Remains Banijay Rights Chief The day after the merger completed, we were first with the news All3Media International’s long-serving CEO, Louise Pedersen, was exiting the merged division , which will be known as Banijay Rights. Cathy Payne, Banijay’s sales boss, is leading the unit as Chief Exec. Watch on Deadline There have been other senior exec exits, with All3 COO Sara Geater and Group Director of Corporate Development Steven Brown leaving. UK trade Broadcast reported Banijay CEO and Executive Director Patrick Holland is expected to take over the UK business, which will comprise 65 production houses. Hughes was All3Media International’s sales lead in German-speaking Europe, France and Benelux, shopping the likes of Midsomer Murders, All Creatures Great and Small , and Fleabag . He is credited with expanding All3Media’s German co-production footprint, securing pivotal deals for Van Der Valk, The Assassin, The Tourist, Boarders , and Generation Z , and oversaw format launches for The Traitors, Race Across the World , and Gogglebox . Prior to that, Hughes spent eight years as Sales Manager at factual specialist Optomen International, whose parent, Optomen, was acquired by All3 in 2010 for £40M ($53.7M). His new employer, ITVS, has also upped Forsyth to lead UK and Ireland sales from her previous role as Vice President of Global Content, Scripted. She has been with the company since 2018, having previously worked at Sky, which is now set to acquire ITVS’s parent ITV. Hughes and Forsyth will both report to Jemma Harvey, ITVS’s EVP, EMEA & UK Sales and Distribution. The appointments follow a spate of hires in ITVS’s unscripted team, namely Zack Wallace, Director, Unscripted, US & LATAM; Eliana Barbosa, Senior Sales Manager, Unscripted, Italy, Iberia, and CEE; and Ben Nohr, Sales Manager, Unscripted, France and Germany; with Lucy Pryke promoted from Sales Executive, Nordics, to Sales Manager, Unscripted, Nordics and Benelux. Set against the backdrop of the Cool Britannia era, The Rise of the Rockstar Chef will explore how the chefs’ unwavering ambition and intense rivalry reshaped Britain’s restaurant industry and redefined what it meant to be a fine dining chef. Watch on Deadline Studio Ramsay Chief Creative Officer Lisa Edwards said: “Nineties and noughties nostalgia is at an all time high for both those of us who were there and those that weren’t – the heady mix of an uprising in fashion, politics and music makes it a decade like no other. But there was another rock and roll revolution happening in the UK. It was the decade that really put British food on the map led by the original Rock Star Chefs, Marco Gordon and Heston. Its the story of rivalry and thepursuit of perfection where the real heat was not just in the kitchen. The Rise of the Rockstar Chef was commissioned for BBC One and iPlayer by Catherine Catton, Head of Commissioning for Factual Entertainment and Events, while Ricky Cooper is BBC commissioning editor. The series director and producer is Zoë Dobson, the EPs are Edwards and Amanda Westwood, the executive in charge of production is Jess Holder and the line producer is Emma Pinching. articles.title: BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: “It’s Insulting”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Staff In Town Hall Revolt Over 1% Pay Rise, Job Cuts & Romesh Ranganathan Ad: “It’s Insulting” UK Sticks With Lisa Nandy As Culture Secretary, With Paramount-Warner & BBC Decisions Looming ‘Harry Potter’ Series Star Ruari Spooner Joins Bill Burr & Chris O’Dowd In Comedy ‘Bender’ View All July 21, 2026 2:39am BBC boss Matt Brittin BBC EXCLUSIVE : Is BBC director general Matt Brittin ‘s honeymoon period already coming to an end? Judging by the mood during a BBC town hall meeting on Monday, the realities of running the UK’s national broadcaster may be coming into sharper focus for the former Google man. Brittin and members of his top team were confronted with a barrage of unhappy questions from employees, who fired shots at plans for a below-inflation 1% pay rise, voiced anxiety about 2,000 layoffs, and lamented the low morale among colleagues. There was also some opprobrium for the big new BBC ad campaign, starring comedian Romesh Ranganathan . Related Stories News Gordon Ramsay Profiled In BBC Landmark Series 'Rise Of The Rockstar Chef' News UK Sticks With Lisa Nandy As Culture Secretary, With Paramount-Warner & BBC Decisions Looming In a written question that captured the mood, one employee said they are treated like “second-rate citizens” and that the 1% pay proposal is “an insult.” Another insider said the pay offer and job cuts are “unfair and demoralizing.” A third person pointedly asked: “A 1% pay rise will eat into my family’s finances so severely, I will have to cut back on something. What do you suggest I cut back on?” Watch on Deadline Others turned to black humor. “Great news that we’ve managed to pinch The 1% Club from ITV,” one employee wrote during the call. “Oh sorry, that’s just the pay proposal.” Bérangère Michel, the BBC’s chief financial officer, responded: “We know that 1% is not much. We wanted to do more, but we can’t afford it. So we implemented a minimum amount to protect those with the lowest pay, and that’s also why the executive team is not getting a pay increase this year.” The BBC is planning to slash costs by £500M ($670M) over the next three years, expanding on an existing target worth £1.5B. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap and can no longer dip into its cash reserves to fund operations. Brittin told staff that the BBC was encountering the same financial pressures as government departments, private sector companies, and charities. “We’re all having to be prudent, and that doesn’t make it easier for people, but we are all in a similar boat here,” he said. The pay rise is under discussion with unions, and speculation is already mounting that it could lead to industrial action. Some BBC employees compared the 1% pay rise with presenter earnings, which increased nearly £3M to a six-year high of £143M in the corporation’s last financial year. “Before he left, Scott Mills was on around £750k, far more than any other radio presenter. What contributed to this enormous salary? £750k could go so far and reduce the amount of staff leaving the BBC,” one insider wrote. A journalist proposed cutting by 10% the salaries of staff earning more than £100,000 to “avoid the current below-inflation 1% pay offer (in effect a pay cut) for the majority.” Brittin stressed it was “right” that the BBC offers competitive pay to attract talent, but the director general said he would examine the number of senior managers across the corporation. “We’ve said we’re definitely going to be looking at at least 10% savings on senior management roles,” he explained. “What I hear from some people, and I haven’t got deep enough yet, is that sometimes it feels like there are very many layers of oversight and not enough empowerment … that’s part of what we need to look at.” Others asked how much the BBC spent on its “What has the BBC ever done for me?” ad, starring Ranganathan. The campaign reboots a 40-year-old promotional video starring John Cleese, and is designed to showcase to UK viewers how much the BBC offers the nation. “How much did the new ‘What has the BBC ever done for me’ campaign cost? Totally excessive!” remarked an insider. Another added: “How much did the Romesh advert cost the BBC at a time we’re being told to both accept a 1% pay rise and be on constant alert that our job might be closed in the coming months?” Others questioned its content, bemoaning its failure to forefront local services, the World Service, and online offerings. On the cost of the campaign, the BBC’s chief customer officer Kerris Bright said: “It’s a really fair challenge, and we’re all facing those challenges. Marketing is facing the same challenges. We’re all having to look deeply at where we invest the resources that we do have and where we think we’ll get the best return for them.” She continued: “I think we need to invest in telling [audiences] the value that we create and how we do it. So I think yes, it is the right time to do that [advert] and to be careful with our investments. We’ve tried to be really smart in how we’ve done it.” Judge Grants TRO To Pause Proposed Merger For 14 Days Trek Continues With Year’s Best Monday After Stellar Opening Weekend ‘Scrubs’ Ups Ava Bunn To Series Regular Alongside Lead OG Trio; Updates On Season 2 Peter Lassally Dies At 93: Legendary Late-Night Producer Of Carson & Letterman Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Sabrina Elba & Ashley Thomas To Star In Rom-Com ‘Not Like Us’ From Ramla Ali And Richard A. Moore
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Simon Field Dies: Former Rotterdam Film Festival Head & ICA Cinema Director Was 80 Giovanni Veronesi’s ‘Dio Ride’ To Close Venice Film Festival ‘S.W.A.T.’ Creator Aaron Rahsaan Thomas & ‘Origin’ Producer Paul Garnes Among Names Set For Inaugural Ghana Creative Economy Initiative View All July 21, 2026 4:00am Sabrina Elba & Ashley Thomas Momodu Mansaray/Getty Images. Writer-director duo Ramla Ali and Richard A. Moore have wrapped production in East London on their debut feature Not Like Us , a romantic comedy starring Sabrina Elba and Ashley Thomas . The film follows a Somali single mother who defies her family and culture by falling in love with a Jamaican man. “The official synopsis reads: Amina Hassan (Elba) is a forty-something pharmacist and a single mother who has built everything herself: her business, her reputation, her beautiful, controlled life, and she would like it to stay that way. Edmund Clarke (Thomas) has other ideas. Related Stories Casting Finn Wittrock & Ashley Thomas Join FX's Witness Protection Pilot News 'In The Shadows:' First Look At Jasmine Jobson Suited Up As Ramla Ali In Boxing Biopic, Altitude Taking Pic To Cannes “Complicating matters are the three community aunties, Hawa, Safia, and Maryam, who have decided that what Amina needs is a husband. Never mind that their own marriages could generously be described as works in progress. Not Like Us is a story about love, desire, and the right to choose your own happiness, told entirely from within the community it depicts.” Sofia Oxenham also stars in the film. Watch on Deadline Ali and Moore co-wrote and co-directed Not Like Us . The pair have a direct connection with the material. The pair married in 2016, and Moore, a white British man, converted to Islam. Ali was born in Mogadishu, Somalia, and grew up in East London. Ali is also a former Olympic boxer. Her life will be chronicled in the feature biopic In The Shadows, which will be released in UK cinemas in October. Not Like Us was independently financed after what Ali and Moore described as difficulties working within the traditional British funding infrastructure. Sunita Mirchandani Hyams and Luke Hyams of Pangaea Group produced the feature alongside Andrew Conrad and Gina Carter of 22 Summers, with Ali and Moore. The executive producer is Richard Fearn of Affine Films. The production team is aiming for a 2027 launch. articles.title: BTS Light Up FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show With “Dynamite” Performance
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All July 19, 2026 3:01pm RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jung Kook of BTS perform during the Topps Final Halftime Show in the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images BTS performed at FIFA ’s first-ever halftime show Sunday, taking part in an 11-minute mega-mix performance during the World Cup 2026 final game between Spain and Argentina. The seven-member global boy group, comprising members RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jung Kook, treated the crowd at New York New Jersey Stadium, known outside of World Cup time as MetLife Stadium, with a rendition of their 2020 hit “Dynamite.” BTS joined Madonna, Justin Bieber and Shakira, along with Burna Boy, the New York Philharmonic’s Gustavo Dudamel and The Muppets, in the jam-packed halftime show. Jason Sudeikis and Brendan Hunt also made an appearance as their characters from Ted Lasso . Sunday’s game comes after cities across the United States, Canada and Mexico hosted matches throughout the tournament. Related Stories TV Jason Sudeikis Brings Ted Lasso to World Cup Halftime Show to Hype Up Justin Bieber TV World Cup Final Star-Spotting: Matt Damon, Tom Cruise, Jay-Z, Beyoncé and Timothée Chalamet in Attendance The youngest member of the K-pop sensation, Jung Kook, kicked off BTS’ segment of the show following a nod to Norway’s viking row celebration. The 28-year-old was dressed, much like his other group members in red, black and white, pairing a cool motto jacket with sunglasses. The rest of BTS trickled in as the song continued. BTS opted to modify the lyrics to “Dynamite” to make them fit Sunday’s game with lines like “King Kong, kick the ball” and “Ding-dong, call me on my phone / Ice tea, and a game of football” — the latter sang by V, whose real name is Taehyung Kim, who pretended to kick a ball as he delivered the line. The halftime was produced by Global Citizen with programming curated by Coldplay’s Chris Martin. The non-profit organization has a goal of raising $100 million for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund — each ticket purchased throughout the World Cup has had $1 donated to the fund. The record-breaking boy group is in the midst of a massive comeback year. All seven members returned to group activities last year following their mandatory military enlistment in their home country of South Korea to world on a new album. They released that album, Arirang , in March. BTS is in the midst of a large scale world tour in support of Arirang . They took a break from their string of sold-out shows in Las Vegas in May to take home three American Music Awards in their post-enlistment return to award shows. They’re scheduled to return to Sin City for the iHeartRadio Music Festival in September. The K-pop group will return to MetLife Stadium in just a few short weeks to perform two sold-out shows of their own at the stadium on Aug. 1 and Aug. 2. Watch BTS and the full halftime show below. articles.title: World Cup Final: Spain Defeats Argentina to Take Second-Ever Win
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All July 19, 2026 3:34pm Ferran Torres of Spain celebrates with Lamine Yamal after scoring the team's first goal during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19. Buda Mendes/Getty Images Spain defeated Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on Sunday. Spain won the match by a score of 1-0 after the game went into extra time. Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the match. This marks only the second time Spain has won the soccer football competition. It also took the crown in 2010, defeating the Netherlands by a score of 1-0. The game was also notable as it marked Argentina superstar Lionel Messi’s third time starting in a World Cup final. He’s the only man to have achieved that feat. Related Stories Music BTS Light Up FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show With "Dynamite" Performance TV Jason Sudeikis Brings Ted Lasso to World Cup Halftime Show to Hype Up Justin Bieber The United States, which hosted many of this year’s games, made it to Round 16 before being eliminated by Belgium with a 4-1 loss. Mexico and Canada also served as hosts for the 2026 World Cup, marking the first time in history that three teams have hosted the competition. The 2030 World Cup will not only be hosted by three nations — Morocco, Portugal and Spain — but it also will take place on three continents, another first, as the opening three matches will be played in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay. Sunday’s final was played at MetLife Stadium (which was referred to as New York New Jersey Stadium for the tournament), located in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The NFL stadium is home to the New York Giants and the New York Jets. The game was broadcast on Fox and Telemundo. articles.title: Donald Trump Booed at World Cup Final
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All July 19, 2026 4:55pm U.S. President Donald Trump (right) and FIFA president Gianni Infantino (second from left) congratulate Lamine Yamal of Spain as they present him with the winners medal on Sunday. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Donald Trump was booed at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on Sunday. The president took the stage at MetLife Stadium (which was referred to as New York New Jersey Stadium for the tournament), located in East Rutherford, New Jersey, with FIFA president Gianni Infantino to present the trophy to tournament champion Spain after the team defeated Argentina in extra time by a score of 1-0. As the two men walked out onto the field, boos could be heard coming from the crowd. On July 6, Trump confirmed that he’d personally intervened to help overturn a suspension for one of U.S. soccer’s star players, striker Folarin Balogun, following a controversial red card against him. Trump said he called Infantino, leading FIFA to suspend the red card decision, thus allowing Balogun to compete in the Round 16 game against Belgium. (The U.S. went on to lose that match by a score of 4-1.) Related Stories General News World Cup Final: Spain Defeats Argentina to Take Second-Ever Win Music BTS Light Up FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show With "Dynamite" Performance The reaction against the move was a mixture of anger and disappointment, particularly among Belgians, as one might expect. The reversal was said to be unprecedented: According to The New York Times, this marked the first time FIFA had reversed a red card since 1962. Trump arrived at the stadium on Sunday in Marine One. The helicopter flew over the stadium about 45 minutes before kickoff. He watched the match from a VIP section behind glass with Infantino. Also sitting nearly were Spain’s king, Felipe VI; Canadian prime minister Mark Carney; and Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum. THR

articles.title: Jim Gilstrap, Singer on ‘Good Times’ Theme and Stevie Wonder’s “You Are the Sunshine of My Life,” Dies at 79
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All July 19, 2026 7:28pm Jim Gilstrap Courtesy of Family James “Jim” Gilstrap, a singer whose credits include the Good Times theme song and Stevie Wonder ‘s “You Are the Sunshine of My Life,” has died. He was 79. Gilstrap’s nephew and family spokesperson, Geoffrey “Geoff Gil” Gilstrap, said he died Saturday from natural causes. Gilstrap sang the song for Good Times, which ran from 1974-79, with Blinky Williams. The catchy, gospel-tinged tune (“Keepin’ your head above water/Making a wave when you can”) was composed by Dave Grusin with lyrics by Alan and Marilyn Bergman . Related Stories Music Freddy Cannon, Rock and Roller Behind Hits "Palisades Park" and "Tallahassee Lassie," Dies at 89 Movies John Kirby, Acting Coach and Son of Actor Bruce Kirby, Dies at 75 Gilstrap was a featured vocalist with Stevie Wonder’s Wonderlove and contributed to many of the singer’s recordings. He sang the first two lines of Wonder’s “You Are the Sunshine of My Life” (“You are the sunshine of my life/That’s why I’ll always be around”). Singer Lani Groves sang the next two lines (“You are the apple of my eye/Forever you’ll stay in my heart”) before Wonder’s vocals kick in, with Gilstrap and Groves continuing to sing backup. The song, from Wonder’s 1972 album Talking Book , won the Grammy Award for best male pop vocal performance. Gilstrap also worked on Wonder’s albums Wonderlove and Innervisions . In 1975, he signed a recording contract with Chelsea Records and released a single, “Swing Your Daddy” that reached No. 4 on the U.K. Singles Chart and No. 10 on the U.S. Billboard Black Singles chart. The song peaked at No. 64 in Australia. He released an album, Love Talk, in 1976. Throughout his career, Gilstrap also collaborated with Quincy Jones , Michael Jackson, The Jacksons, Aretha Franklin, Anita Baker, Whitney Houston, James Ingram, George Benson, Bill Withers, Gladys Knight, Luther Vandross, Patti LaBelle, Kenny Loggins, Dolly Parton, Teddy Pendergrass, Stanley Clarke, Boz Scaggs and others. “Jim was one of the most respected session vocalists of his generation, bringing his powerful and soulful voice to countless recordings that helped define the sound of popular music,” his nephew said. Born Nov. 10, 1946, Gilstrap was the last surviving member of a family of 10 siblings. He is survived by his wife, Gloria, and his children. THR

articles.title: Stephen Chow’s ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Blasts Past $200 Million at China Box Office
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 19, 2026 8:40pm Stephen Chow Keith Tsuji/Getty Images Stephen Chow ‘s perfectly timed return to soccer comedy kept on kicking in its second weekend at China ‘s box office . Kung Fu Soccer , the comedy legend’s Shaolin Soccer spinoff, added $73.7 million (RMB 501.1 million) over the July 17-19 frame, lifting its total to $214.3 million (RMB 1.46 billion) in just nine days, according to data from Artisan Gateway. In a market where second weekends routinely shed half their opening business, the film instead topped its two-day debut frame of $73.6 million (RMB 500.3 million), albeit spread across three days this time. Having crossed $147 million (RMB 1 billion) in its first week, the film has prompted ticketing giant Maoyan to raise its full-run forecast to $441 million (RMB 3 billion), up from the RMB 2.5 billion it projected on opening weekend. The film looks likely to finish just short of Chow’s personal box-office record of RMB 3.39 billion ($500 million-plus), set by the fantasy comedy The Mermaid in 2016. Related Stories Movies 'The Odyssey' Seizes $124M Opening in Box Office Triumph Movies 'The Odyssey' Galloping to $120M in Muscular Box Office Opening Chow, 64, wrote and directed Kung Fu Soccer — his first feature behind the camera since 2019’s The New King of Comedy — but does not appear onscreen, having stepped away from acting after 2008’s CJ7 . Released to mark the 25th anniversary of Shaolin Soccer , and to ride this summer’s FIFA World Cup fever, the film reworks the beloved original’s premise around an underdog, all-female squad whose players integrate martial arts into their game to make an improbable run at a tournament dubbed the Supreme Invincible Cup. Zhang Xiaofei ( Hi, Mom ) leads the cast as the team’s captain, with Dilraba Dilmurat as its star striker and Lay Zhang as its kung fu coach, plus guest turns from Hong Kong screen icon Carina Lau, Japanese star Takeru Satoh and U.S. comedian Jimmy O. Yang. Chow’s singular blockbuster prowess has been demonstrated — yet again — by the way he released the movie with little to no conventional marketing campaign. He set the release date via a casual social media video on his birthday in late June, and the film hit theaters less than three weeks later with minimal advance marketing. A North American theatrical release is expected later this year but remains undated. Singapore’s Encore Films, which handled the international rollout of China’s record-setting animation Ne Zha 2 last year, acquired worldwide rights to Kung Fu Soccer outside the mainland and is lining up territory-by-territory deals. Kung Fu Soccer faced markedly stiffer competition in its sophomore weekend than its first in the form of All Wishes Come True , an animated tentpole from state-backed Pearl Studio, the Beijing outfit formerly known as Oriental DreamWorks, whose credits include Kung Fu Panda 3 , Abominable and the Oscar-nominated Over the Moon . Written and directed by Mu Zhengyang, the comic fantasy reimagines the classic folk tale of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea, following a group of ordinary individuals who outwit the gods to earn their legendary titles. It opened Saturday and brought in $30.6 million (RMB 207.8 million) over two days — a solid start — for an early total of $39.6 million (RMB 269 million) including previews. Pearl and partner CMC Pictures have set a global rollout beginning Aug. 13 in Australia and New Zealand, with the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and other markets to follow from Aug. 14. The rest of the weekend’s top titles trailed the two blockbusters from afar. Enlight Pictures’ A Part of Me , a female-friendship tearjerker starring Zhang Ruonan and Jin Jing — a remake of the 2015 Toni Collette-Drew Barrymore dramedy Miss You Already — opened third with $13.6 million (RMB 92.4 million). Universal and Illumination’s Minions & Monsters held fourth in its third frame with $3.7 million (RMB 25.1 million), nudging its China total to $40.3 million (RMB 274 million). And Triangle , Christopher Smith’s 2009 time-loop thriller starring Melissa George — a curious cult favorite among Chinese movie lovers — took fifth with $3.7 million (RMB 25 million) after arriving in mainland theaters Friday, 17 years after its original release. China’s 2026 box office now stands at $2.97 billion, down 35.3 percent from the same point last year — a comparison skewed by animated mega-blockbuster Ne Zha 2 , which earned over $2 billion in China alone during the first half of 2025. The gap has nonetheless narrowed considerably from the nearly 56 percent deficit of early March, as Chow’s comeback hit has given the country’s summer moviegoing season a healthy kick-start. Curry Barker’s horror phenomenon Obsession , which has grossed more than $400 million worldwide since its mid-May debut, opens in the country on Friday. The film will pose an interesting test of whether the wave of young, internet-bred filmmakers taking Hollywood by storm can help revive the studios’ fortunes in China, where filmgoers have long grown tired of U.S. franchise fare. THR

articles.title: Locarno to Honor James Gray, “the Last Great Novelist of American Cinema,” With Career Leopard
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 20, 2026 2:00am James Gray Theo Wargo/Getty Images for FLC The Locarno Film Festival will pay tribute to James Gray , bestowing upon the U.S. filmmaker the Pardo alla Carriera , the Career Leopard, presented by Ascona-Locarno Tourism, during its 79 th edition . Gray will receive the award in the Swiss town’s Piazza Grande on Sunday, Aug. 9, and present his latest film, Paper Tiger , after the ceremony. Two key titles by Gray, We Own the Night (2007) and Two Lovers (2008), will also screen in the festival program. “Since winning the Silver Lion at Venice for Little Odessa (1994) at age 25, James Gray has forged a singular career rooted, with piercing realism, in his upbringing in New York’s Russian-Jewish community,” Locarno highlighted. “Films like The Yards (2000), We Own the Night (2007), Two Lovers (2008), and The Immigrant (2013), cemented Gray’s place as one of American cinema’s most artistically distinctive voices – a filmmaker as concerned with criminal underworlds, rendered with exacting detail, as with meticulous family portraiture, often situated within theBrighton Beach of his youth and shaped by a dialogue with classic American and European auteur cinema.” Related Stories Movies Stephen Chow's 'Kung Fu Soccer' Blasts Past $200 Million at China Box Office General News World Cup Final: Spain Defeats Argentina to Take Second-Ever Win Continued Locarno organizers: “As he has established himself at the top tier of filmmakers in the United States, Gray’s explorations of the often elusive promise of the American dream have, over the past decade, expanded into more varied thematic terrain – colonial exploration, space travel, racial prejudice – that reshaped the popular understanding of his work while remaining distinctively his own: The Lost City of Z (2016) with Charlie Hunnam and Robert Pattinson, Ad Astra (2019) with Brad Pitt, and Armageddon Time (2022) with Anthony Hopkins.” Paper Tiger premiered in competition at Cannes this year and will open the 2026 New York Film Festival. “James Gray is the last great novelist of American cinema,” said Giona A. Nazzaro, Locarno’s artistic director. “His films form a rich body of work that echoes the Jewish diaspora, film noir, and Russian as well as North American literature. A filmmaker with a humanist sensibility and profound cinephile knowledge, he has experimented with genres such as science fiction and adventure while retaining his own artistic identity and voice. Celebrating James Gray at the Locarno Film Festival means paying tribute to a unique and unmistakable artist, a filmmaker who speaks the language of cinema and knows how to pass it on to future generations.” The Pardo alla Carriera is being handed out with the support of Ascona-Locarno Tourism, the destination partner of the Locarno Film Festival, which focuses on the development and promotion of tourism in the region. Previous winners of the award include Francesco Rosi, Claude Goretta, Bruno Ganz, Claudia Cardinale, Johnnie To, Harry Belafonte, Peter-Christian Fueter, Sergio Castellitto, Otar Iosseliani, Víctor Erice, Marlen Khutsiev, Bulle Ogier, Mario Adorf, Jane Birkin, Fredi M. Murer, Dante Spinotti, Costa-Gavras, Tsai Ming-liang, Shah Rukh Khan , and, last year, Jackie Chan . The 79 th edition of Locarno takes place Aug. 5-15. THR

articles.title: Daniel Ings, Jessica Brown Findlay to Star in Olivia Grant’s Directorial Debut, ‘The Two Week Wait’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 3:00am Ings and Brown Findlay (center) will star in 'The Two Week Wait.' Pip/Pip Bourdillon/Rankin Fresh off the set of Star Wars: Starfighter , Daniel Ings ( A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , The Gentlemen ) has joined Jessica Brown Findlay ( Peaky Blinders , Downton Abbey ) in Olivia Grant’s directorial debut, a short film called The Two Week Wait . Fenella Woolgar ( Call the Midwife ), Rick Warden ( Happy Valley ), and Sophie Colquhoun ( Captain America ) co-star in the project, following a woman in her late thirties (Brown Findlay), who comes up against a series of dissociative experiences as she navigates her deteriorating mental health during the rollercoaster of IVF alongside her incompetent, albeit guileless, boyfriend (Ings). Related Stories General News World Cup Final: Spain Defeats Argentina to Take Second-Ever Win Movies '3 Weeks After' Review: A High-School Field Trip Goes Off the Rails in a Skillful but Sadistic Serbian Shocker The Two Week Wait , penned by Grant, is a co-production between her new production banner Cavalry Films and Symphony Films, headed up by actor-producers Rebecca Night ( Wuthering Heights ) and Harry Hadden-Paton ( The Crown ). The film is set to premiere on Tuesday at the Indy Shorts Film Festival. Grant, best known for her acting roles in Stardust , Lark Rise to Candleford and Indian Summers , told The Hollywood Reporter that her desire to start making film came from a mixture of timing and a new sense of urgency. “I’ve wanted to make my own work for a while now and, like many actors, had a feature script I’d been quietly writing for a couple of years, but there was always enough acting work not to focus exclusively on writing, and I was ambivalent about what I would write about. It was COVID that changed that; firstly because it cleared time to focus on generating new work and, secondly, because it coincided with my personal struggles with IVF and its mental toll. As a way to hold on to my sanity, I ended up writing a 30,000-word diary documenting the rollercoaster of grappling with my infertility and transcribing the arguments my husband and I were having, which felt very specific to the process and uniquely gendered.” She continued about her personal experience influencing the process: “It was only as the world opened up again, and I was able to reconnect with more women and couples, that it became clear that many elements of my mental anguish were remarkably universal. My shame around not being able to have a child and what that meant was normal; my partner’s difficulty salving that particular wound for me was perhaps predictable, and the intense sense of dissociation that permeated that period was again part of the experience for many. Like a lot of women, I did not share the experience with my close friends and family and suddenly felt there was a real need to shed some light on what can be the profound interpersonal effects of this remarkably successful, albeit oft-harrowing, process.” The Two Week Wait is a proof of concept for a feature-length narrative Baby Mine , slated for 2027, she added. Ings and Brown Findlay are also attached, with Amy Hubbard on board as casting director. Ings added: “Olivia is a singular new voice in British filmmaking, with a lot to say on some fairly universal themes affecting many women. Getting to work with her, Nanu Segal and Jessica Brown Findlay on this beautiful film was an embarrassment of creative riches. You haven’t heard the last of Olivia Grant.” Night describes the script as “so instantly unique, compelling and beautiful.” She said: “[It] deals with the choices we make, the relationships we foster, and people seeking love and connection as they journey together through life’s struggles. Full of drama, yes, but so witty and heart-wrenching too.” THR

articles.title: Venice Critics’ Week Unveils Political, Experimental Lineup
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 20, 2026 3:54am 'Rider' Courtesy of Venice Critics Week Venice Critics’ Week, the sidebar section of the Venice International Film Festival , selected by the national union of Italian film critics, unveiled its 2026 selection on Monday. The selection of seven debut features is intended as a showcase for up-and-coming international auteurs. Il Grande Giaffa (Giaffa the Great) from Italian director Marco Santi, the story of an ordinary man drawn into the dangerous illusion of a charismatic performer, will open the section, screening out of competition. Another Italian film, Rider , a star-crossed lovers’ musical set in contemporary Milan, from directors Roan Johnson and Davide Pavanello, will close the section. Related Stories Movies Daniel Ings, Jessica Brown Findlay to Star in Olivia Grant's Directorial Debut, 'The Two Week Wait' (Exclusive) Movies Locarno to Honor James Gray, "the Last Great Novelist of American Cinema," With Career Leopard The competition line-up includes two very different features from Columbia. The experimental documentary essay The End of Times from directors Bibiana Rojas Gómez and Juan David Cárdenas mixes found footage and AI-generated imagery to explore the legacy of historical violence in Latin America. Meteorite from Sebastián Múnera follows two young women on a journey through an extravagant amusement park built on the estate of the late drug lord Pablo Escobar. Other competition entires include the dystopian sci-fi film The H@llow Man from Tunisian director Kamel Laaridhi; London , a drama set around a fetish community, from Brazilian directors Victor Di Marco and Márcio Picoli; and Zoom In, Zoom Out , the feature debut of Chinese director Dong Jie, which follows a young game designer searching through real and virtual worlds to find his missing roommate. This year’s line-up is particularly political, something the organizers said was deliberate, noting that “a festival is not a neutral bubble” separate from the world. But while acknowleging “our cultural activism,” the film critics’ association said artistic and formal criteria were the priority in making the selection. Critics’ Week runs Sept. 2-12 alongside the main Venice festival. Venice will announce its full 2026 lineup on July 23. Check out the full Venice Critics’ Week lineup below. Kamel Laaridhi (Tunisia) London , dirs. Victor Di Marco, Márcio Picoli (Brazil) Meteorite , dir. Sebastián Múnera (Colombia) Our Share of Sand , dir. Shalini Adnani (India, United Kingdom, Greece) Prima Della Guerra , dir. Tommaso Usberti (France, Italy) Zoom In, Zoom Out , dir. Dong Jie (China) Closing Film Rider , dirs. Roan Johnson, Davide Pavanello (Italy) THR

articles.title: AMC Theatres Sees Revenue Rise As Hollywood Box Office Bounces Back
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All July 20, 2026 4:26am AMC Empire 25 in Times Square, New York. The Hollywood Reporter An ongoing and apparently sustained Hollywood box office recovery underpinned solid revenue growth for AMC Theatres during the second quarter. Overall revenue was up 14 percent to $1.59 billion, compared to $1.39 billion in the same period of 2025, even as AMC increased its net loss to $11.4 million, against a year-earlier $4.7 million. The adjusted EBITDA came to $320.6 million, compared to $189.2 million. The second quarter results at AMC follow the exhibition industry seeing gains from steady supply of Hollywood tentpole releases like Toy Story 5 and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , and surprise horror pics like Backrooms and Obsession , to get film lovers back in the habit of going to the multiplex in pre-pandemic numbers. Just this weekend, Christopher Nolan’s epic drama The Odyssey revived the summer box office with this year’s biggest live-action debut and the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s highest-grossing global launch of $124 million. That’s allowed exhibitors to look to full-year 2026 box office likely to exceed the comparable performance for last year, and possibly set a new annual record. “Both our U.S. and European businesses showed great progress in the second quarter. The momentum in the total industry-wide domestic box office was undeniable, reaching approximately $2.99 billion, up 10.7 percent from last year’s second quarter, making this the biggest box office quarter in seven years and the fifth biggest quarter ever,” AMC Theatres CEO Adam Aron said in a statement on Monday morning. U.S. market attendance rose 12 percent to 52.2 million patrons, compared to 46.8 million in 2025, while international markets attendance was also up by 18 percent to 18.7 million cinemagoers, against 16 million patrons. Aron also talked up fortunes for his debt-laden company as it looks to recover from the impact of pandemic-era box office disruptions: “This demonstrates the inherent operating leverage in our business model at a time of rising revenues, combined with the power of AMC’s market leading position, the appeal of our theatres, the increasing numbers of our premium offerings, the prowess of our marketing programs and our ability to keep a tight lid on our costs. The theater chain’s chief added, “Finally, after some admittedly tough years as our industry recovered only slowly from the ravages of COVID-19 and its aftermath, the relentless focus of AMC on delighting our guests as we execute with all cylinders blazing is reflected in our record-setting second quarter financial results.” THR

articles.title: ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel on Criston Cole’s Suicide Mission and His ‘Nihilism’: ‘He’s Losing the Will to Motivate’
articles.full_text: Jul 19, 2026 7:00pm PT ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel on Criston Cole’s Suicide Mission and His ‘Nihilism’: ‘He’s Losing the Will to Motivate’ By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel on Criston Cole’s Suicide Mission and His ‘Nihilism’: ‘He’s Losing the Will to Motivate’ 9 hours ago ‘The End of Oak Street’ Preview: Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor Try Not to Get Eaten Alive by Dinosaurs in 14 Minutes of 4DX Footage 20 hours ago The Cure’s Robert Smith Slams FIFA’s World Cup Final Halftime Show: ‘Just F— Off’ 2 days ago See All Courtesy of Theo Whiteman/HBO SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for Season 3, Episode 5 of “ House of the Dragon ,” now streaming on HBO Max. In tonight’s “House of the Dragon” episode, Ser Criston Cole ( Fabien Frankel ) proclaims that he’s ready to die — and he’s ready to do so honorably. As the war to capture the Iron Throne rages on, Criston marches onward with his men, including Gwayne Hightower (Freddie Fox), to put a stop to the Rivermen reaching King’s Landing and aiding Rhaenyra Targaryen (Emma D’Arcy). But their journey to catch up with the Rivermen proves increasingly difficult, after one of their horses gets caught in a trap. Once they come across a burned-down bridge to cross the river, they realize there is no chance of catching up. Related Stories Alicia Vikander Joins Aaron Taylor-Johnson in 'Enigma Variations' Series at Netflix Netflix Sets Video Licensing Pact With Top Digital Publishers Including Variety, Rolling Stone, Billboard and Other Brands From Penske Media’s PMX Gwayne and Criston regroup and debate what to do next, now down to half the men they started with. Gwayne says continuing forward “would march us toward certain death.” That’s when Gwayne realizes this was Criston’s goal all along, as Criston launches into a revealing monologue: “I have been a servant all my life. To Green or to Black. I have defined myself by oaths, through unyielding devotion. And the highborn have made much of me while it pleased them to do so. But I will not let them diminish me now. I will not return spurned, rejected. I am the realm’s greatest warrior. And I will die as such.” Popular on Variety While Frankel says he doesn’t read fan reactions much these days, it has become easier to tap into his controversial character’s motivations in Season 3: “I can only understand why people feel how they feel about him as a character. It’s tricky for me as an actor, because obviously, I just don’t see him in that way. It serves no purpose for me to see him in that way. You always have to be the bastion of your character, and I feel very much the bastion of Criston Cole.” Frankel spoke with Variety to break down Criston’s suicide mission, why being a soldier is “the only honest version of himself,” and what fans can expect — should the series continue to follow George R.R. Martin’s book “A Song of Ice and Fire,” as expected — from the upcoming Butcher’s Ball. This is a pivotal moment for Criston, proclaiming that he is ready to die an honorable death. Can you talk about his journey throughout this episode, and how he arrives at this point? It’s something that’s been brewing inside of him so much over the course of the show, probably since about halfway through Season 2. These thoughts of, “What am I going to be, and what’s the legacy I’m going to leave behind? In what way do I want to go out?” I suppose that really comes to a head in that fire scene with Gwayne. Does he have a specific vision for how he wants his death to play out? How can he guarantee he’s going to go out the way he wants, and that people will remember him? I don’t know if there’s anything in his head — it’s like he said, “Hell bent in glory,” right? Criston Cole started as a soldier before the 20-year stretch that he spent at King’s Landing — that’s how he started, and that’s how he wants to finish. In his mind, the only honest version of himself is the soldier. Everything else is pretense; the diplomat is pretense; the Hand of the King, there’s a level of pretense; Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, there’s a level of pretense. I suppose they’re all psychological, brain-led jobs. He isn’t that way, he’s very much led by his sword and his fighting instinct. The idea that that’s how he will be remembered, I think, feels honest. Gwayne eventually figures out what’s really going on. Criston is very upfront about his suicide mission once it clicks. There’s a genuine fondness that Criston has for Gwayne; there’s a yin-yang aspect to them. Weirdly, I think Gwayne represents — on the surface — everything that Criston disdains in this world. Yet underneath, Criston’s found someone who will go to battle with him, who does have a heart, who does have empathy, who is much more than he appears. So their relationship is built through this, these guys going to war with each other. You hear any soldier talk about their time in the war, in any war, and they’ll say the relationships they formed are closer than anything you can possibly imagine because you’re living through life and death with these people. You’re risking your lives for each other. As a result of that, there’s a profoundness to their relationship. Theo Whiteman/HBO Why does Criston, then, decide not to tell Gwayne about his suicide mission for this long? I don’t think he’s waiting for Gwayne to figure it out, it’s not a game. Certainly, I didn’t think of it as a game. I think he just knew that as soon as he told Gwayne, that would create a lack of desire to continue. Gwayne’s dislike of this plan would rub off on the rest of the men, and then Criston would lose an army that otherwise would have a good chance of fighting. There’s undeniably a selfishness to Criston’s plan, right? He’s looking out for himself but I think he’s become so accustomed to a world where every single person is looking out for themselves constantly. Unfortunately, any sort of attempt at selflessness falls on itself. For any of the characters, it’s just a very dog-eat-dog world. You’ve spoken in previous interviews about not always knowing Criston’s code, or where his motivations lie episode to episode. As the season has continued on, have you been able to tap into these more? There’s a freedom that comes with nihilism, to a degree. This is a character who, at least at the top of Season 2 and toward the end of Season 3, surrendered himself to the notion that the war is over. That ultimately, we as human beings have no genuinely important part to play in a war that’s ultimately going to be won by dragons or lost by dragons. They are just so much more powerful, and so you meet him at the top of Season 3 in a genuinely kind of — I wouldn’t say nihilistic, because I think that’s a bit reductive. But certainly, there’s an agnosticism to him. He’s losing the will to motivate. He finds that will as the course of the season goes on, and certainly in Episode 4’s planning scene with Gwayne that really gives him the impetus. It re-energizes him and then he certainly has rediscovered his sense of code — not code so much, but a sense of purpose. This episode comes on the heels of Criston finding out that Aemond (Ewan Mitchell) has left him behind, and he’s once again hit with those feelings of abandonment that he’s felt all his life. How does that play into his actions here? It’s tricky, man. I want to think there’s a part of him that is intelligent enough — not intelligent enough — but a part of him that certainly recognizes who Aemond is. I just don’t believe it’s all that surprising that Aemond hasn’t shown, even if he’s playing. Sometimes in order to sell a story as people, we go along with notions that feel like the most natural ones. So Criston saying, “He wouldn’t desert us, I can’t believe that,” I almost feel like that’s him playing into the version of this character that needs that piece of information in order to rediscover a sense of self and purpose. How does he look back on his relationships with Rhaenyra and Alicent Hightower (Olivia Cooke) now — does he have regrets? As he’s spending these long periods traveling to battle, ready to fall on his sword, is he reflecting on his decisions, or is he just focused on charging forward? Haven’t men always done that in history? Just march on, and go to work, “I’m not going to deal with anything that I’m really feeling, I’m just going to go on and get on and do something, and that thing is going to supersede whatever I’m feeling!” But it’s inevitable that Rhaenyra and Alicent are both on his mind all the time. I think Alicent much more than Rhaenyra. Certainly for me, Rhaenyra has become a sort of afterthought. And actually, it’s just the idea of winning the war for Alicent. Has it become easier to tap into Criston’s humanity, despite him being such a controversial character? There’s just genuine insight into who this man is, and what makes him tick. Yeah, I think I have found it easier to tap into the humanity of him. It’s difficult, you can’t undo his actions. He’s done the things that he’s done, and those things have been, at times, very morally reprehensible or questionable, to say the least. And so I can only understand why people feel how they feel about him as a character. It’s tricky for me as an actor because obviously, I just don’t see him in that way. It serves no purpose for me to see him in that way. You always have to be the bastion of your character, and I feel very much the bastion of Criston Cole. How do you look back on your journey on the show and playing Criston? I learned so much from playing Criston Cole. There’s a stillness to him that I don’t naturally have as a person, and I think I’ve learned so much through that. We’re so different as people, but I look back on the last few years with just a ton of warmth towards the people I’ve gotten to work with. Irrespective of playing the character or making the show, it’s the company that you keep that makes any experience. Your former “House of the Dragon” co-star, Milly Alcock, is having a big summer with “Supergirl.” Have you had a chance to see the film, do you keep in touch with Milly at all? I keep in touch with her all the time, yeah! I spoke to her on the phone two weeks ago when she called me from Brazil — I think she was doing press. I’m immensely proud of her, and not in the least bit surprised. I told my agent he should sign her as soon as we did Season 1 of “House of the Dragon” together, and that’s what he did. I’m so happy for her, very proud of her. I haven’t yet had a chance to see “Supergirl,” but I will! I know fans of the book will be looking forward to Butcher’s Ball, which the end of this week’s episode seems to set up. What can you say about the action scenes coming up? All I can say is that it was long and arduous choreography to learn, it’s a brilliantly choreographed fight. There are a ton of unbelievable stuntmen in it that make the fight what it is, and I’m just super excited for people to see that side of Criston. It’s the side of him we haven’t really seen at all — what he is like in a man-to-man situation. This interview has been edited and condensed. articles.title: ‘Shark Tank India’ Sets Season 6 With Parrot Campaign on SonyLIV (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 19, 2026 11:30pm PT ‘Shark Tank India’ Sets Season 6 With Parrot Campaign on SonyLIV (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘New-Gen’ Universe Launches First Consumer Products Line With Comic-Con Trading Cards (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Rules With 66% Market Share 4 hours ago See All SonyLIV “ Shark Tank India” has unveiled “#DontBeATota,” a campaign taking aim at founders who mistake the language of entrepreneurship for the substance of it, as the show opens its sixth season for entries on streamer SonyLIV . The campaign lands at a moment when terms such as valuation, burn rate and EBITDA have become everyday vocabulary. It poses a pointed question: has the language of entrepreneurship begun to overshadow the business itself? “#DontBeATota” argues that conviction, execution, resilience and a grasp of fundamentals matter more than a polished command of buzzwords. Related Stories 'Nemesis' Renewed for Season 2 at Netflix Netflix Paid $587 Million for Ben Affleck's AI Startup InterPositive The campaign’s mascot is Tota, a parrot who believes he can impress the Sharks simply by reciting startup terminology he barely understands. The character is built around a simple contrast: anyone can memorize the vocabulary of entrepreneurship, but only founders who understand their business can actually build one. Popular on Variety Aman Gupta, a Shark on “Shark Tank India” and co-founder of boAt and founder of Off/Beat, said: “If repeating startup buzzwords was enough to build a business, we would all be investing in parrots. That’s the thought behind this campaign. Over the years, ‘Shark Tank India’ has helped make entrepreneurship part of mainstream conversations, and that’s something we are incredibly proud of. But building a company has never been about sounding like an entrepreneur, it is about solving real problems, understanding your business inside out and showing the resilience to keep building every single day. That’s exactly the kind of founders we’re excited to meet in Season 6.” Founders can now submit entries for the new season through SonyLIV, with the network inviting applicants who can demonstrate real conviction and a clear understanding of their businesses. The Script Room conceived and produced the campaign.
