articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 12:05am PT ‘New-Gen’ Universe Launches First Consumer Products Line With Comic-Con Trading Cards (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago ‘New-Gen’ Universe Launches First Consumer Products Line With Comic-Con Trading Cards (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Rules With 66% Market Share 5 hours ago See All Toonz Media Group New-Gen Universe, Inc. is launching its first consumer products initiative at San Diego Comic-Con, debuting an exclusive collector’s trading card set made with Cryptozoic Entertainment to celebrate its Marvel-distributed comic series. Just 300 convention exclusive boxes exist worldwide for the July 23–26 event, making this among the rarest “New-Gen” collectibles released to date. Designed solely for the convention, the set also builds momentum for the upcoming 3D CGI animated series “New-Gen Nanobot Heroes.” Related Stories LISTEN: How David Fincher and Zach Cregger Secretly Shaped Netflix’s Video Game-TV Hybrid 'Unhinged' Netflix Comedy Series 'I Suck at Girls' Casts Anna Konkle, Taegen Burns and More In the comic, twin brothers Sean and Chris learn their bodies have been enhanced by nanotechnology, thrusting them into a fight against the villain Deadalus within a futuristic world where nature and technology exist side by side. Popular on Variety “New-Gen” was created by J.D. Matonti, Julia Coppola and Chris Matonti and has grown from its Marvel-distributed comic book origins into a transmedia franchise spanning publishing, animation and consumer products. The Comic-Con cards give fans a tangible link between the source comics and the animated series still to come. The initiative is led by Debra Joester, president of Joester Loria Group, who is spearheading New-Gen’s expanding consumer products program. “We are thrilled to collaborate with Debra Joester and Cryptozoic Entertainment on this first New-Gen consumer products initiative. We envision many more imaginative opportunities like these as we work with Joester Loria Group, Toonz Media Group, and world class talent to bring our New-Gen Nanobot Heroes story to children of all ages,” said J.D. Matonti, creator of “New-Gen.” Each box holds a set of 13 collectible cards: 11 base cards drawn from artwork in the comic book series, a single rainbow foil card, and one autograph card bearing the signature of either Matonti, voice actor Molly Fahey or voice actor Tony Oliver. Every autograph card carries an on-card signature and a limited run of 100, and select base and foil cards were produced as unique one-of-one pieces. Buyers at the convention will also receive a free “New-Gen” graphic novel, with a foreword penned by Mark Hamill, that traces the franchise’s origin story. “We are delighted to partner with J.D. Matonti, Toonz Media Group, and the extraordinary talent behind New-Gen Nanobot Heroes,” said Debra Joester. “Fans are craving the next evolution of superheroes and J.D. has created the gripping storytelling, compelling characters and rich, imaginative new world that delivers just that.” Attendees can also preview new artwork for “New-Gen Nanobot Heroes” ahead of its animated debut on the franchise’s website, which will show the heroes touching down by spaceship in the series’ utopian setting. A separate giveaway offers fans the chance to win a graphic novel signed by Hamill. The card release also builds momentum for “New-Gen Nanobot Heroes,” the coming 13-episode, 22-minute 3D CGI series from writer-director Matonti, whose representation includes Evan Anglin and Eric Williams at Zero Gravity Management. New-Gen Universe and Toonz Media Group are producing the show, with Chris Matonti, Julia Coppola, Brad Heisman and J.D. Matonti serving as executive producers. Writers on the project include Brent Friedman, known for “Star Wars: The Clone Wars,” and Eugene Son, who worked on “Avengers Assemble,” alongside four other writers. Toonz Media Group will distribute the series internationally, and Ketchup Entertainment will handle its domestic release. Voice talent set to appear includes Finn Wolfhard, Nick Wolfhard, Anya Chalotra, Luke Wilson, Henry Rollins, Taylor Gray, Molly Fahey, Lena Headey and Tony Oliver, and John Loeffler composed the score. New-Gen Universe is a transmedia company built around the New-Gen IP and other properties; its advisory board counts New-Gen’s own creators alongside former Marvel CFO Ken West and Bonnie Arnold, a producer on “How to Train Your Dragon.” Co-producer Toonz Media Group has spent upward of 25 years in the animation business, turning out an estimated 5,000 minutes annually of CGI and 2D programming, with past credits on “Wolverine and the X-Men” for Marvel, “Speed Racer: The Next Generation” for Lionsgate and “Mostly Ghostly” for Universal. articles.title: ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 1:46am PT ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘New-Gen’ Universe Launches First Consumer Products Line With Comic-Con Trading Cards (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Rules With 66% Market Share 4 hours ago See All Sagar Pictures Entertainment Sagar Pictures Entertainment (SPE) has confirmed the launch of a global studio business, moving beyond film and television production into an intellectual property-led growth strategy spanning gaming, music, consumer products and theme parks. The Mumbai-based studio said it is transitioning from a traditional content company into what it describes as a future-focused entertainment enterprise, aiming to build franchises and original stories across multiple formats and platforms. Related Stories 'Nemesis' Renewed for Season 2 at Netflix 'Teach You a Lesson' Director Hong Jong-chan and Star Kim Moo-yul on the Netflix Global Hit That Turned a Korean Classroom Into a World Stage: 'Authenticity Is What Travels Borders' “India is home to some of the world’s most timeless stories, many of which remain underexplored in cinema. These narratives are not only entertaining but also carry profound spiritual and cultural wisdom. At Sagar Pictures Entertainment, our vision is to preserve their authenticity while reimagining them through world-class cinematic storytelling for audiences across generations and geographies. This new chapter reflects our commitment to combining a seven-decade legacy with innovation, global collaborations, and future-ready entertainment experiences,” said Akash Sagar Chopra, CEO, Sagar Pictures Entertainment. Popular on Variety “Our first step in this journey is ‘ Shrimad Bhagavatam ,’ a project that reflects the scale and ambition with which we want to approach storytelling. As we build this and future franchises, our focus is on creating stories that can grow beyond cinema into meaningful experiences across multiple platforms, while staying rooted in the authenticity and values that define India’s cultural heritage,” Chopra said. “Shrimad Bhagavatam” is SPE’s inaugural feature film franchise, conceived as a seven-chapter theatrical saga tailored for premium large-format screens. It is a live-action feature adaptation of the “Bhagavata Mahapurana,” one of Hinduism’s eighteen major Puranas centered on devotion to Krishna as an incarnation of Vishnu, alongside cosmology, genealogy and mythology. The franchise is currently in production and follows the studio’s earlier adaptations of Indian epics “ Ramayana ” and the “ Mahabharata .” SPE builds on the legacy of the Sagar banner, founded in 1954 by filmmaker and producer Ramanand Sagar, a recipient of India’s Padma Shri honor. Under the guidance of chair and director Moti Sagar, the group has produced films and television programming known for adaptations of ancient Indian epics, positioning it as a name in spiritual, historical and family entertainment. The company’s productions have reached over a billion viewers in India, per BAARC India and other sources, with reach extending to the global Indian diaspora. SPE operates as the film studio arm of the Sagar Pix Group, based across Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Built on more than 75 years in storytelling, the studio has produced more than 55 television series and over 25 feature films for audiences in India, South Asia, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region and the global Indian diaspora. Its catalogue includes Indian National Film Award-winning features and award-winning television programming. articles.title: James Gray to Be Honored With Locarno Film Festival Career Award
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 2:00am PT James Gray to Be Honored With Locarno Film Festival Career Award By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Venice Critics’ Week Lineup: Shalini Adnani’s Family Drama ‘Our Share of Sand,’ AI-Assisted Colombian Doc ‘The End of Times’ and More 2 hours ago James Gray to Be Honored With Locarno Film Festival Career Award 3 hours ago Robert De Niro Expected in Rome for 50th Anniversary Screening of Bernardo Bertolucci’s Historical Epic ‘Novecento’ 7 days ago See All Getty The Locarno Film Festival will honor James Gray with a lifetime career award at this year’s edition, where the U.S. auteur’s most recent work, “Paper Tiger,” will screen. Gray will receive the Pardo alla Carriera award on Aug. 9 and will present “Paper Tiger” — which launched in May from Cannes — at the fest’s Piazza Grande outdoor venue. Set in 1986, the film follows two brothers, Irwin (Miles Teller) and Gary Pearl (Adam Driver). Irwin becomes entangled with the Russian mob after embarking on a get-rich-quick scheme to clean up the Gowanus Canal, and his former cop brother, Gary, is the only one who can get him out of trouble. “Paper Tiger” will have its North American premiere as the opening night film of the 64th New York Film Festival on Sept. 25. Related Stories 'Mortal Kombat 2' Sets HBO Max Release Date David and Larry Ellison Sued by Paramount Investor Alleging 'Illegal' Side Deal With Donald Trump to Secure U.S. Approval for Warner Bros. Takeover Two other titles directed by Gray, “We Own the Night” (2007) and “Two Lovers” (2008), will also screen at Locarno as part of the tribute. Popular on Variety “Since winning the Silver Lion at Venice for ‘Little Odessa’ (1994) at age 25, James Gray has forged a singular career rooted, with piercing realism, in his upbringing in New York’s Russian-Jewish community,” the fest said in a statement, citing Gray’s “The Yards” (2000), “We Own the Night” (2007), “Two Lovers” (2008) and “The Immigrant” (2013), which cemented Gray’s standing “as one of American cinema’s most artistically distinctive voices — a filmmaker as concerned with criminal underworlds, rendered with exacting detail, as with meticulous family portraiture, often situated within the Brighton Beach of his youth and shaped by a dialogue with classic American and European auteur cinema.” The Locarno statement continued: “As he has established himself at the top tier of filmmakers in the United States, Gray’s explorations of the often elusive promise of the American dream have, over the past decade, expanded into more varied thematic terrain — colonial exploration, space travel, racial prejudice — that reshaped the popular understanding of his work while remaining distinctively his own: ‘The Lost City of Z’ (2016) with Charlie Hunnam and Robert Pattinson, ‘Ad Astra’ (2019) with Brad Pitt and ‘Armageddon Time’ (2022) with Anthony Hopkins.” Locarno artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro added, “James Gray is the last great novelist of American cinema. His films form a rich body of work that echoes the Jewish diaspora, film noir and Russian as well as North American literature.” He called Gray “a filmmaker with a humanist sensibility and profound cinephile knowledge” who “has experimented with genres such as science fiction and adventure while retaining his own artistic identity and voice.” Previous winners of the Locarno Pardo alla Carriera Award include Francesco Rosi, Bruno Ganz, Claudia Cardinale, Johnnie To, Harry Belafonte, Jane Birkin, Costa-Gavras, Tsai Ming-liang, Shah Rukh Khan and Jackie Chan. The 79th edition of Locarno will run Aug. 5-15. articles.title: Venice Critics’ Week Lineup: Shalini Adnani’s Family Drama ‘Our Share of Sand,’ AI-Assisted Colombian Doc ‘The End of Times’ and More
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 3:00am PT Venice Critics’ Week Lineup: Shalini Adnani’s Family Drama ‘Our Share of Sand,’ AI-Assisted Colombian Doc ‘The End of Times’ and More There are no entries from the U.S., while titles from Italy and Colombia feature prominently By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Venice Critics’ Week Lineup: Shalini Adnani’s Family Drama ‘Our Share of Sand,’ AI-Assisted Colombian Doc ‘The End of Times’ and More 1 hour ago James Gray to Be Honored With Locarno Film Festival Career Award 2 hours ago Robert De Niro Expected in Rome for 50th Anniversary Screening of Bernardo Bertolucci’s Historical Epic ‘Novecento’ 7 days ago See All Venice Critics' Week London-based Chilean-Indian director Shalini Adnani’s debut feature “Our Share of Sand,” about a 12-year-old girl named Maya who returns to rural India to reconnect with her estranged father, is among standout entries in the upcoming Venice Film Festival Critics’ Week. The section, dedicated to first works from around the world, also comprises two titles from Colombia: the fiction-documentary hybrid “The End of Times,” a political piece co-directed by Bibiana Rojas Gómez and Juan David Cárdenas that uses artificial intelligence and explores colonialism and capitalism in Colombian history, and Sebastián Múnera’s drama “Meteorite,” about plans to build an amusement park on the grounds of the former estate of drug lord Pablo Escobar. Related Stories Netflix Inks Exclusive Deal for Video Episodes of Vox Media Podcasts 'Unexplainable,' 'Switched on Pop' Netflix to Stop Releasing Viewership Data Every 6 Months, Will Shift to Annual Reports Italy also features prominently in the lineup, with Paris-based Tommaso Usberti’s “Before the War,” about a young man named Guido raised within a Northern Italian racist milieu who falls in love with a Kosovar immigrant named Sonia, ensconced in a competition slot. Popular on Variety Also from Italy is the section’s out-of-competition opener, existential noir “Giaffa the Great” directed by Marco Santi, while the closer — also out-of competition — is Italian rap musical “Rider,” co-directed by Roan Johnson and the local music producer known as Dade (Davide Pavanello). “Rider” follows a young food delivery driver who delivers a huge sushi order to a luxurious villa on the outskirts of Milan and is invited to stay for the evening. The seven features competing in Venice Critics’ Week are all by first-time directors and all world premieres. Rounding off the section’s competition are Tunisian dystopian drama “The H@llow Man” by Kamel Laaridhi, set in 2059 Tunisia where a biochip regulates memory and suppresses emotion; Chinese drama “Zoom In, Zoom Out,” by Dong Jie, about a young video game designer who embarks on a journey to seek his missing roommate Gao following a clue hidden in an online game; and Brazilian drama “London,” by Victor Di Marco and Márcio Picoli, about a dilemma faced by a disabled young adult. “Whilst the industry at large is grappling with its crises, these works are proof that cinema never stopped asserting its own cruciality,” said Venice Critics’ Week general delegate Beatrice Fiorentino in a statement. “This cinema is fierce and independent, daring and vibrant, resolute in its reminder that our collective imagination can, and indeed must, continue to be rewritten.” All Venice Critics’ Week competition entries will compete alongside titles in the official selection for the fest’s Lion of the Future prize, which is worth $100,000. The 83rd edition of Venice Film Festival will run Sept. 2-12, with its official selection lineup being announced on Thursday. See all the Venice Critics’ Week titles below. articles.title: Former ‘This Morning’ Host Holly Willoughby Heads to YouTube for New Lifestyle Series
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 4:05am PT Former ‘This Morning’ Host Holly Willoughby Heads to YouTube for New Lifestyle Series By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest Former ‘This Morning’ Host Holly Willoughby Heads to YouTube for New Lifestyle Series 32 minutes ago ‘Boys of Tommen’ Finds Its Patrick Feely in Jamie Schneider, With James Craven Joining as Pierce O’Neill (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago ‘The Claudia Winkleman Show’ Canceled at BBC After One Season: ‘I Was Just Too Nervous to Enjoy It’ 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Hungry Bear Media Holly Willoughby , best known until recently as the host of ITV’s daytime show “This Morning,” is set to make a comeback. Rather than return to ITV, however, she has opted to launch her new lifestyle series “Holly Willoughby Together” on YouTube . Premiering July 28, the show is described as a “multi-platform lifestyle series built around real people, real stories, honest conversation, practical advice, celebrity guests, fashion, beauty, health and more” which are apparently “the things Holly genuinely loves.” Related Stories 'Mortal Kombat 2' Sets HBO Max Release Date Does California Attorney General Want to Force Paramount to Sell Off CNN? Rob Bonta Claims 'I Have No Idea' Where That Speculation 'Comes From' The show will be made up of five strands: in-depth coversations, cooking segments, fashion and beauty, health and wellness and, finally, a “hang-out” featuring celebrity guests including Stanley Tucci, Emma Bunton and Katherine Ryan. Popular on Variety Two episodes are set to drop each week on YouTube as well as social media and “digital streaming platforms,” although Willoughby’s rep didn’t reply immediately when Variety asked which ones. The show will be produced by her husband Dan Baldwin’s production outfit Hungry Bear Media, which also makes the hugely successful entertainment show “Gladiators” for the BBC. In a statement, the television host said: “I’m so proud of the work all the team who make ‘Together’ have put into this exciting new project. We’ve had a lot of fun developing it and look forward to seeing what you think.” Willoughby became one of the U.K.’s best-known television personalities thanks to her hosting gig on “This Morning.” But she finally exited the show in 2023 after she found herself caught up in a series of scandals, mostly not of her own making. First there was the “line-jumping” debacle during Queen Elizabeth II’s funeral in 2022, when she and her longtime co-host Phillip Schofield were accused of using their positions to jump the 14-hour line to see the royal’s lying-in-state. That was swiftly followed by the two-part implosion of Schofield’s career the following spring, first when he took a leave of absence while his brother stood trial (and was convicted) for sexually abusing a teenage boy and a short time later when it emerged he had also had an inappropriate relationship with a young staffer at ITV. While Willoughby was not in any way implicated, the collapse of her personal and professional relationship with Schofield inevitably dinged her previously golden reputation. After a brief hiatus she returned to “This Morning” in June 2023 but quit for good four months later after it was revealed she had been the intended victim of a gruesome kidnapping and murder plot. A man was found guilty of plotting to kidnap, rape and murder the star in July 2024. The turmoil led to Willoughby taking a step back from television, aside from a brief stint at Netflix last year on the short-lived “Celebrity Bear Hunt” alongside Bear Grylls, which flopped and was swiftly canceled after one season. Willoughby’s pivot to YouTube comes as the digital platform increasingly dominates viewing figures in both the U.K. and beyond. articles.title: Andy Burnham Becomes U.K. Prime Minister, Succeeding Keir Starmer
articles.full_text: Jul 20, 2026 4:24am PT Andy Burnham Becomes U.K. Prime Minister, Succeeding Keir Starmer By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Andy Burnham Becomes U.K. Prime Minister, Succeeding Keir Starmer 18 minutes ago ‘Shrimad Bhagavatam’ Anchors Sagar Pictures Entertainment’s Global Push, Indian Studio Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago ‘New-Gen’ Universe Launches First Consumer Products Line With Comic-Con Trading Cards (EXCLUSIVE) 5 hours ago See All Getty Images Andy Burnham became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on Monday, taking over from Keir Starmer in a handover choreographed around a visit to Buckingham Palace, where Starmer formally resigned and King Charles III then invited Burnham to form a government. Before heading to the Palace, Starmer delivered a farewell address outside 10 Downing Street, flanked by colleagues and staff who greeted him with cheers and applause. He framed his six and a half years leading the Labour Party and two as Prime Minister around the 2024 landslide election win, pointing to falling immigration numbers, shorter National Health Service waiting times and children lifted out of poverty as markers of his record. He said the job’s most humbling aspect was witnessing everyday “grit, decency, and compassion” across the country, and closed by wishing Burnham “every success,” pledging him “full support” before thanking his family, staff and the wider Labour Party. Related Stories Does California Attorney General Want to Force Paramount to Sell Off CNN? Rob Bonta Claims 'I Have No Idea' Where That Speculation 'Comes From' Paramount Blasts States' Lawsuit Aimed at Blocking Warner Bros. Deal, Claims Litigation Will 'Shield' Netflix and Tech Companies From 'Much-Needed Competition' “My work is done,” Starmer said. “It has been the privilege of my life to serve you and this great country, as Prime Minister, and I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago.” Popular on Variety Starmer’s final days in office brought a run of international recognition. On July 14, French President Emmanuel Macron awarded him the Legion of Honor for his work with France on European security. Two days later, on a final visit to Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy presented him with the Order of Freedom, Ukraine’s highest honor for a foreign national, citing his support for the country throughout the war with Russia. “I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved,” Starmer said. Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, had been confirmed as Labour leader unopposed on July 17, after securing nominations from 379 of the party’s 403 MPs. His confirmation capped a five-week run from his return to Parliament via a by-election win in Makerfield to his installation as the country’s seventh prime minister in a decade. Burnham was the only declared candidate in the leadership contest, which followed a rebellion among Labour lawmakers against Starmer. After Starmer formally resigned as Prime Minister at Buckingham Palace, Burnham followed him and met King Charles III. He has formally become the U.K.’s 59th Prime Minister. A statement from Buckingham Palace said: “His Majesty received in audience the Rt Hon Andrew Burnham MP and requested him to form a new Administration. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Sundance Award Winning Doc ‘American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez’ Starts Rollout In Rare ‘Odyssey’ Weekend Debut – Specialty Preview Is ‘Obsession’ Technically A Blockbuster? Lawyers For Paramount, State AGs Spar At Court Hearing On WBD Merger Judge Says She’ll Rule By Next Week On Emergency Motion In State AGs’ Challenge To Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery Merger View All July 19, 2026 4:44pm William Franklyn-Miller as George Washington in Young Washington Angel Studios Indies The Invite (A24, $15 million cume), Young Washington (Angel Studios, $41 million cume) and Obsession (Focus Features, $258 million cume) are sitting in the top ten in, respectively, week 4, week 3, and week 10. The Olivia Wilde comedy starring herself, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton grossed $3.9 million for the three days on about 2,100 screens. Curry Barker’s massive breakout is eyeing $2.5 million on 1,500 screens. And John Erwin’s biopic starring William Franklyn-Miller as George grossed $3.7 million at 2,200 locations. There’s a sequel in the works , 1776 , for Angel’s strong performing historical epic. articles.title: Jennifer Finch Dies: L7 Bassist Who Battled Brain Cancer Was 59
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom Trump Booed During World Cup Final Telecast Spain Wins 2026 World Cup Final 1-0, Dominating Lionel Messi’s Argentina Hal Williams Dies: ‘Sanford And Son’ Cop & ‘227’ Co-Star Was 91 View All July 19, 2026 7:48pm Jennifer Finch performs with L7 in 2020 Rich Polk/Getty Images for The Art of Elysium Jennifer Finch , the powerhouse bassist of L7 during the band’s creative peak in the 1990s, has died. That, according to her Instagram account. She was 59. A social media post from the band today noted Finch waged “a long courageous fight with brain cancer.” Earlier this month, friends and family launched a GoFundMe page to help pay for “professional in-home nursing care, physical and speech therapy, medical equipment.” As of today, that fundraiser had raised $395,000 on its goal of $350,000. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News John Kirby Dies: Acting Coach, Bruno Kirby’s Brother & Bruce Kirby’s Son Was 75 A Rolling Stone profile of the band once described Finch as “an ill-behaved and untrained bassist who added instant verve to their live act” when she joined in 1986. She left in 1996 in order to get sober and deal with the death of her father. During her first run with the band Finch, who also contributed vocals, wrote the songs “(Right On) Thru”, “Everglade” and “Shirley.” In 1994, Finch and bandmates Suzi Gardner (guitars, vocals), Donita Sparks (vocals, guitars) and Dee Plakas (drums, vocals) played a band called called Camel Lips in John Waters’ Serial Mom , performing the track “Gas Chamber,” which they co-wrote with Waters. Finch also had a small part in the 2017 film Scumbag . She joined Gardner, Sparks, and Plakas in L7 again from 2014 to 2026. Before L7, Finch was in Sugar Babydoll alongside Courtney Love and future Babes in Toyland founder Kat Bjelland. DEADLINE RELATED VIDEO: The band issued a statement today praising “Jennifer Finch, whose fierce spirit, humor and boundless creativity helped shape L7 and changed all of our lives forever. Jennifer was a true original who lived entirely on her own terms, and the impact she made on music, art and everyone lucky enough to know her cannot be measured.” View this post on Instagram The post to Finch’s personal Instagram account read, “We are devastated to announce the death of our partner, sister, daughter, and friend Jennifer Precious Finch. Jennifer’s impact on the world of music was seismic; her impact on our lives, even moreso. We appreciate everyone’s interest and concern, thank you for all the kind messages. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Ofcom Launches Investigation Into ‘Married At First Sight UK’ ‘The Rest Is Football’ Returning To Netflix For Next Two Premier League Seasons Holly Willoughby Launches YouTube Lifestyle Series View All July 20, 2026 1:20am 'The Rest Is Football' Clifton Prescod/ Netflix Netflix is staying in the soccer game with more The Rest is Football throughout the next Premier League season. The streamer greenlit its first daily sports show and has been airing the Gary Lineker podcast as a vodcast every day during the just-finished World Cup , which ended last night with Spain victorious. This morning, the streamer committed to The Rest is Football for the next two Premier Leagaue seasons starting from next month, airing two eps per week, one on Monday and one Friday. Former Match of the Day host Lineker fronts The Rest is Football with former soccer stars Alan Shearer and Micah Richards, with regular guests including, recently, Gordon Ramsay. The popular soccer analysis pod is in the same stable as The Rest is Politics, The Rest is History and others, all produced by Lineker’s indie Goalhanger . Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Spain Wins 2026 World Cup Final 1-0, Dominating Lionel Messi's Argentina News Tom Cruise Makes Appearance At World Cup Final To "Celebrate A Tournament That Brought The World Together": "This Is Unity & This Is Greatness" The Rest is Football aired during the World Cup from a glitzy studio in Time Square, which Lineker joked before the tournament was just one of the benefits of moving from the BBC, which aired its coverage from Salford in the UK. Lineker exited the BBC under a cloud last year after sharing an Instagram video that contained an antisemitic trope. While not a ratings smash, The Rest is Football performed well, appearing in the top 10 of the UK chart every day of its run and peaking top. Its top-rated episode currently sits 40th on Netflix’s most-watched in the UK of the past seven days, viewed by around 170,000 people, placing it behind the BBC’s Football Daily podcast. Netflix has been leaning in to the sports game recently and just released a tranche of sports docs including on Jose Mourinho, Tyson Fury and Jamie Vardy. Goalhanger boss Tony Pastor said: “Netflix allowed us to preserve everything that makes the show special: sometimes serious, frequently hilarious, but always genuine and warm. articles.title: Na Hong-Jin’s Cannes Competition Title ‘Hope’ Has Strong Opening At Korean Box Office
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Na Hong-Jin’s Cannes Competition Title ‘Hope’ Has Strong Opening At Korean Box Office PVR Inox’s Sanjeev Kumar Bijli On India’s Box Office Recovery, Cinema Expansion & Cannes Acquisitions Haul CJ ENM’s Mnet & Universal Music Group’s Republic Partner To Launch Global Girl Group View All July 20, 2026 1:55am Hope Plus M Entertainment Na Hong-Jin ’s Hope , which premiered in competition at this year’s Cannes film festival, raced past 2 million admissions on its five-day opening weekend in Korea, faster than any film released so far this year, according to data from the Korean Film Council (KOFIC). The film, which opened on July 15 ahead of the three-day Constitution Day holiday weekend, passed the 2 million admissions benchmark during the day on Sunday, faster than The King’s Warden which went on to sell 16.9 million tickets to become the highest-grossing Korean film of all time. It also outpaced the opening of Yeon Sang-ho’s Colony , which debuted in Cannes Special Screenings, and passed the 2 million benchmark on the evening of its fifth day. Related Stories News Proposed Merger Of Korean Cinema Chains Lotte & Megabox Collapses News Breaking Baz @ Cannes: How The Filmmaking Esiri Brothers & Sophie Okonedo Put 'Clarissa' In The Spotlight Also supporting Hope ’s opening weekend, the Korean government issued a new round of discount coupons offering $3.90 (KRW6,000) off a ticket just one week before the film’s release. Watch on Deadline Distributed by Plus M Entertainment, Hope stars Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender and Alicia Vikander in the tale of a small Korean town that encounters an invasion of powerful extraterrestrial beings. The film has sparked significant debate amongst audiences, with 53% of viewers giving it a 9 or 10 rating on Naver, while around a quarter took issue with the lack of world-building, high levels of profanity and ambiguous ending. Na’s 2016 occult thriller The Wailing was also a polarising film but drew close to seven million admissions. Korean press is reporting that the film, billed as the most expensive Korean film ever, would have to sell around 20 million tickets to break even in theatres alone, although it has also secured presales in around 200 overseas territories. Much is riding on the success of the film as Plus M Entertainment is one of a group of companies under JoongAng Group that recently filed for bankruptcy protection . Also opening at the Korean box office over the weekend, Minions & Monsters came in second with 308,576 admissions, followed by live-action Moana with 173,555 admissions on its second weekend, and Toy Story 5 , which opened June 17, with 114,718 admissions. articles.title: James Gray To Receive Locarno’s Honorary Career Pardo Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Venice Critics’ Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston Join Guy Pearce, Jared Harris & Merab Ninidze In ‘The Price Of Peace’ As Filming Begins in London James Gray To Receive Locarno’s Honorary Career Pardo Award View All July 20, 2026 2:00am James Gray Amy Sussman/Getty Images The Locarno Film Festival will honor U.S. director James Gray with career achievement award, the Pardo alla Carriera, at its upcoming 79th edition in August. Gray will receive the award on August 9 ahead of an open-air screening of Paper Tiger on the festival’s landmark 8,000-capacity Piazza Grande. Two other key titles in his filmography – We Own the Night (2007) and Two Lovers (2008) – will also play in the line-up. It marks a first trip to Locarno for Gray who first broke onto the international festival scene in 1994 at the age of 25 with Venice Silver Lion-winning drama Little Odessa , inspired by his own upbringing in New York’s Russian-Jewish community. Related Stories Festivals James Gray's Crime Thriller 'Paper Tiger' With Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson & Miles Teller To Open New York Film Festival Festivals Twin Sisters Bianca And Dilara Foscht Co-Star In Locarno-Bound 'Manhunt,' Plot Psychological Horror Film 'Oma' He continued to mine New York’s rich migrant culture and criminal underworlds with The Yards (2000), We Own the Night , Two Lovers , and The Immigrant (2013), branching out into other worlds with The Lost City of Z (2016) with Charlie Hunnam and Robert Pattinson; Ad Astr a (2019) with Brad Pitt, and Armageddon Time (2022) with Anthony Hopkins. Watch on Deadline “James Gray is the last great novelist of American cinema. His films form a rich body of work that echoes the Jewish diaspora, film noir, and Russian as well as North American literature,” said Locarno Artistic Director Giona A. Nazzaro. “A filmmaker with a humanist sensibility and profound cinephile knowledge, he has experimented with genres such as science fiction and adventure while retaining his own artistic identity and voice. Celebrating James Gray at the Locarno Film Festival means paying tribute to a unique and unmistakable artist, a filmmaker who speaks the language of cinema and knows how to pass it onto future generations.” Starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller, Paper Tiger world premiered in competition at Cannes in May and will open the 2026 New York Film Festival in September . The drama, following two brothers whose hopes for a better life draw them into the orbit of the Russian mafia, sees Gray return to the New York milieu of his early work and to the 1980s of his childhood. Gray teamed with his frequent collaborators including Cinematographer Joaquín Baca-Asay, Composer Christopher Spelman, Production Designer Happy Massee, Casting Director Douglas Aibel, Editor Scott Morris, and Costume Designer Amy Roth. Paper Tiger is produced by Gray alongside Rodrigo Teixeira, Anthony Katagas, Raffaella Leone, Andrea Leone, Marco Perego, Gary Farkas, Leonardo Maria del Vecchio, Carlo Salem, Andrea Bucko. Previous recipients of the Pardo Alla Carriere – which is sponsored by local tourism agency Ascona-Locarno Tourism – have included Bruno Ganz, Claudia Cardinale, Johnnie To, Harry Belafonte, Peter-Christian Fueter, Sergio Castellitto, Otar Iosseliani, Jane Birkin, Dante Spinotti, Costa-Gavras, Tsai Ming-liang, Shah Rukh Khan and, in 2025, Jackie Chan. articles.title: Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston Join Guy Pearce, Jared Harris & Merab Ninidze In ‘The Price Of Peace’ As Filming Begins in London
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Venice Critics’ Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston Join Guy Pearce, Jared Harris & Merab Ninidze In ‘The Price Of Peace’ As Filming Begins in London James Gray To Receive Locarno’s Honorary Career Pardo Award View All July 20, 2026 2:32am Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston, Guy Pearce, Jared Harris, Merab Ninidze Getty Image Anthony McCarten’s post-World War Two political thriller The Price of Peace – starring Guy Pearce , Jared Harris and Merab Ninidze as Harry S. Truman, Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin respectively – has begun principal photography in London. The trio have been joined by Mia Threapleton ( The Phoenician Scheme) as Mary Churchill and acclaimed Danny Huston ( Wonder Woman) as General Groves as filming begins. The drama explores the pivotal 1945 Potsdam Conference where the fate of post-war Germany, Europe and the world was decided. Related Stories Acquisitions Netflix Snaps Up Rupert Murdoch Thriller 'Ink' From Danny Boyle Ahead Of Venice Premiere Books Jacob Elordi & Josh Brolin Navigate "Kill Or Be Killed" Post-Apocalyptic World In Final Trailer For 'The Dog Stars' The synopsis reads: “July 1945. In the aftermath of Nazi Germany’s defeat, President Harry S. Truman, Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin converge at the Potsdam Conference to shape the future of Europe and the world. Each man has a personal and political agenda. Newly appointed Truman needs to end the War with Japan. Churchill is facing a pivotal election back home. Stalin has territorial ambitions over occupied territories. As political tensions rise and personal crises unfold, a high-stakes diplomatic chess game emerges. The three leaders’ decisions and balance of power will impact millions and shape global politics for decades to come.” Watch on Deadline “The Potsdam Conference represented a crucial turning point in world history, the moment when World War II transformed into the Cold War. I’m thrilled to begin production with such an extraordinary cast bringing this pivotal moment to life,” said four-time Academy Award-nominated filmmaker McCarten ( Darkest Hour, Bohemian Rhapsody, Theory of Everything, The Two Popes ). SND, which announced the project at the EFM earlier this year, serves as co-producer and also handles international sales and French distribution. “Following the enthusiastic response from international buyers at the European Film Market in Berlin earlier this year, we’re thrilled to see production underway,” said Ramy Nahas, Director of International Sales and Distribution, SND. “The level of interest from distributors worldwide confirms that The Price of Peace will resonate strongly with global audiences.” McCarten is joined on the production by Director of Photography Henry Braham ( Superman 2025) , Production Designer James Merifield ( Mary Queen of Scots) , Costume Designer Tina Kalivas ( Ballerina) Hair and Makeup Designer Suzanne Stokes-Munton (N osferatu ), Prosthetics Designers Vee Holt and Stuart Richards ( Nosferatu ), Editor Fernando Stutz ( The Two Popes ) and Composer Harry Gregson-Williams ( The Martian ). The Price of Peace is produced by Raccoon Features, Muse of Fire Productions, and Salloway Studios, in association with Spark Productions, Sub Rosa Group and Ingara. Producers are Jonathan Saubach, Philipp Klausing, Matthew Salloway, Anthony McCarten, Eric Falkenstein, Igor Nesterenko, Elizaveta Chalenko and Philipp Nesterenko. Executive Producers include Thierry Desmichelle, Rémi Jimenez, Nicolas Rolland, Simon Moores, Oliver Indictor, Thomas Valentin, Marc Frydman, Ken Davenport, Jonathan Hogue, Gary Hamilton and Ying Ye. Acting as Co-Producers are Ari Benmosche, Michael Durden, Marguerite Hoffman, Carl Moellenberg, Dorit Muzicant, Peter Yu and Cecily Colahan. Associate Producers are Kathleen Fitzgerald, Allan Herzog, Alan Mendelson, Dave Peacock, Courtney Berlin, Willette Klausner, Larry Craig & The Bird, Dave and Cheryl Olson, Julia Willbanks and Jonathan Golub. McCarten is repped by CAA and attorney David Fox of Myman Greenspan Fineman Fox Rosenberg & Light; Pearce, by CAA, Independent Talent Group, Shanahan Management, and David Weber at Sloane, Offer, Weber and Dern; Harris, by Agents Sarah Clossey and Jeremy Barber at UTA and Samira Higham at ITG, Manager Amy Guenther at Gateway Management & Production and Attorney Mark Wetzstein at Sloan, Offer, Weber and Dern. Ninidze is repped by the Curtis Brown Group, through Sarah Spear and Grace Clissold; Mia Therapleton, by CAA in the US and Markham Froggatt & Irwin in the UK, and Danny Huston, by Julian Belfrage Associates, UTA, Untitled and Myman Greenspan Fineman Fox Rosenberg & Light. The U.S. is co-repped by CAA Media Finance. articles.title: Venice Critics’ Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Venice Critics’ Week Unveils 2026 Selection With Films From Colombia, China & Tunisia Mia Threapleton, Danny Huston Join Guy Pearce, Jared Harris & Merab Ninidze In ‘The Price Of Peace’ As Filming Begins in London James Gray To Receive Locarno’s Honorary Career Pardo Award View All July 20, 2026 3:30am Zoom In, Zoom Out SIC Venice parallel sidebar Settimana Internazionale della Critica (International Critics’ Week) has unveiled the lineup for its 41st edition. The section, organised by the Union of Italian Film Critics (SNCCI) and focused on works by emerging filmmakers, will showcase seven features in competition and two films out of competition. Colombia has a strong presence this year with two works tapping into the country’s turbulent history. Bibiana Rojas Gómez and Juan David Cárdena will compete with The End of Times , a radical essay film using archive footage and artificial intelligence to reflect on memory and colonialism. They are joined by countryman Sebastián Múnera ’s Meteorite , which is described as an intense female-centred story set in a land still haunted by the ghosts of violence. Related Stories News Giovanni Veronesi's 'Dio Ride' To Close Venice Film Festival Festivals Danny Boyle's 'Ink' To Open Venice Film Festival Further competition titles include Tunisian director Kamel Laaridhi’s dystopian drama The H@llow Man , imagining a future in which emotions and memory are controlled by technology, and London , the debut feature of Brazilian directors Victor Di Marco and Márcio Picoli, a queer story that places physicality, desire and the freedom of self-determination at its centre. Watch on Deadline Chilean-Indian London-based director Shalini Adnani is also in the mix with Our Share of Sand , a timely family drama reflecting on inequality and environmental crisis. It was showcased in Cannes this year at the project stage as part of the British Film Institute’s Great 8 initiative . Italy is represented in the competition with Tommaso Usberti’s Prima della Guerra , described as an intense coming-of-age story set in the Po Valley addressing contemporary masculinity with extraordinary maturity. Completing the lineup is Zoom In, Zoom Out by Chinese filmmaker Dong Jie, a work that weaves together mystery, online gaming and urban alienation to capture the anxieties of Generation Z. Screening Out-of-Competition, Marco Santi’s existential noir Il grande Giaffa, starring Edoardo Pesce, will open the section, while Rider , the latest work from award-winning filmmaking and musical duo Roan Johnson and Davide Pavanello, aka Dade, is the closing film. The latter work is described as an urban musical using the language of rap “to explore precarious work, the desire for emancipation and the conflicts shaping a new Italy”. The selection for the 41st edition is curated by General Delegate Beatrice Fiorentino together with committee members Matteo Berardini, Marianna Cappi, Francesco Grieco and Marco Romagna. The 41st Venice International Critics’ Week will take place on the Venice Lido from September 2 to 12 alongside the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Founded in 1984 by Lino Micciché, has previously showcased the early works of Kevin Reynolds, Mike Leigh, Olivier Assayas, Harmony Korine, Pedro Costa and Pablo Trapero, as well as major names in Italian cinema including Carlo Mazzacurati, Sergio Rubini, Antonio Capuano, Roberta Torre and Gianni Di Gregorio. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Giovanni Veronesi’s ‘Dio Ride’ To Close Venice Film Festival ‘S.W.A.T.’ Creator Aaron Rahsaan Thomas & ‘Origin’ Producer Paul Garnes Among Names Set For Inaugural Ghana Creative Economy Initiative Hungary’s Production Incentive Program Reopens After Orbán-Era Pause View All July 20, 2026 4:05am Simon Field Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for BFI). Simon Field , the pioneering film programmer and champion of filmmakers such as Wang Bing, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and Christopher Nolan, has died. He was 80. Field died on July 16. The news was confirmed by the veteran film critic Geoff Andrew, who posted an obituary of Field on his blog. Andrew was shortly followed by the Rotterdam Film Festival, which shared a tribute to Field over the weekend. Field was Festival Director and Co-Director at Rotterdam from 1996 to 2004. During his tenure, filmmakers who passed through the festival’s Tiger Competition and won awards include Lou Ye, Christopher Nolan, Hong Sang Soo and Pablo Trapero. Related Stories News Jennifer Finch Dies: L7 Bassist Who Battled Brain Cancer Was 59 News John Kirby Dies: Acting Coach, Bruno Kirby's Brother & Bruce Kirby's Son Was 75 Before Rotterdam, Field was a Film Studies writer and lecturer. He was the founding editor of the radical film journal Afterimage , and in 1988 served as the Director of Cinema at London’s Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA), a position he held until joining Rotterdam in 1996. Watch on Deadline After Rotterdam, Field joined Keith Griffiths’ Illumination Films, where he produced titles by filmmakers such as Tsai Ming-liang, Apitchatpong Weerasthakul, and Garin Nugroho. Field continued to work closely with Weerasethakul over the years and produced his Palme d’Or winner Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives (2010) and his most recent title, Memoria (2012). Weerasethakul shared a tribute to Field in an Instagram post. Weerasethakul wrote: “I have lost an important companion, with whom we built the films together with love, over many years. I cannot dream of a more caring and supportive producer, and a kind gentleman. We were up against changing practices in filmmaking and film funding. But Simon never gave up, nor compromised.” Weerasethakul’s tribute ended: “I will carry him in gratitude, and in the work we still have to finish. Our bond through images will continue to bind others. He is in the light that touches the leaves, young and old. We will continue our journey with the love he showed me.” View this post on Instagram UK Has 7th Prime Minister In 10 Years; Culture Sec To Be Replaced $124M+ U.S. Opening Best Live-Action Haul Of 2026; $264M WW A Nolan Best Spain Beats Argentina For Title; Photos From Closing Ceremony, Halftime Netflix’s Official Most Watched Series Of Recent Years: So, Which One Is No. 1? articles.title: Andy Burnham Becomes Seventh UK Prime Minister In 10 Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Ofcom Launches Investigation Into ‘Married At First Sight UK’ ‘The Rest Is Football’ Returning To Netflix For Next Two Premier League Seasons Holly Willoughby Launches YouTube Lifestyle Series View All July 20, 2026 4:08am Andy Burnham Alishia Abodunde/Getty We’ve been here before. The UK has its seventh Prime Minister in a decade as Andy Burnham arrives at Buckingham Palace to greet King Charles III and be sworn in. The former Greater Manchester Mayor has had an odd coronation, running unopposed to be leader of the Labour Party after his predecessor Keir Starmer stepped down amid dreadful poll ratings, a poor set of local election results and scandal involving former U.S. ambassador Peter Mandelson and Jeffrey Epstein. Starmer delivered his final speech before resigning this morning. Related Stories News Paramount-Warner Deal Faces Weeks Of Uncertainty As British Lawmakers Go On Summer Break News Alan Cumming Urges UK Industry To Help Bring Down Paramount-Warner Merger, As Government Poised To Make Intervention Burnham officially became Labour leader on Friday and Prime Minister today, which is ratified when he meets the King. Once he meets Charles III and is invited to form a government, he will give a speech outside his new 10 Downing Street home. The 56-year-old has been a well-known face in British politics for 20 years. He was Culture Secretary then Health Secretary in the Labour government of the late 2000s before twice unsuccesfully running to be Labour leader last decade. Watch on Deadline His near-decade run as Greater Manchester mayor led his popularity to soar owing to a set of popular policies, which he says he will attempt to roll out nationally, and he is widely seen as being far more charismatic than Starmer. He was a vocal backer of Greater Manchester’s successful bid to host the Edinburgh TV Festival , saying it would “open a new chapter defined by the unmistakable character that only Greater Manchester can bring.” Greater Manchester also houses the city of Salford, home to thousands of BBC employees after what is broadly viewed as one of the most successful out-of-London relocations the nation has ever seen. Burnham’s in-tray is bulging as he moves into 10 Downing Street and he is set to pick his cabinet this afternoon, with the country facing a wealth of enormous challenges. Incredibly for a nation that is only supposed to have two per decade, he is the seventh Prime Minister in 10 years, the majority of whom have stood down rather than lost elections. His recent predecessors include Boris Johnson, Rishi Sunak and Liz Truss. New Culture Sec The film and TV industry will be keeping an extremely close eye on Burnham’s pick for Culture Sec. Lisa Nandy , current incumbent and a close Burnham ally, is reportedly leaving the role to run his new “super ministry” in the north of England. Nandy is in the process of making some seriously big decisions, one being whether to intervene in Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery’s $110B merger, which won’t now be decided until early September . Another is the future funding model of the BBC. Nandy recently signaled her backing for a plan to revamp the BBC license fee so that streaming sevice subscribers have to pay the £180 ($240) annual charge. Other policy priorities include new legislation that would compel YouTube and TikTok to promote public service content from the BBC and other broadcasters. The result of all these decisions could make Nandy’s successor rather unpopular in various circles across the pond. articles.title: The True Story Behind the First Foreign Feature to Break Out In Hollywood
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Thomas Doherty Plus Icon Thomas Doherty View All July 18, 2026 6:45am French poster art of 'La Grande Illusion' in 1937. Everett On May 1, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced a major change to the eligibility rules for the best international feature film. No longer would a film have to be nominated by the country of origin; henceforth, it could land in the pool of nominees by winning an award from a list of high-profile international film festivals. Moreover, in recognition of the fact that a person not a nation actually directs the film, the director’s name and not the country’s will be engraved for posterity on the statuette plaque. The new protocols for the best international film category, née best foreign language film, are the latest rejiggering in what has historically been one of the more contentious and confusing Oscar categories. Of course, under whatever rules, Oscar validation can mean the difference between multi-platform distribution and oblivion in the American marketplace. So, despite the provincialism of allotting a mere five slots to the output of the rest of the planet, foreign filmmakers have been eager to perform due obeisance before the Academy, which since 1957 has granted offshore films a regular seat at the festivities. (The first winner was Federico Fellini’s La Strada .) Before that, the Academy doled out an Honorary Oscar when the impact and excellence of a foreign film became too conspicuous to ignore, as with Italy’s The Bicycle Thief in 1949 or Japan’s Rashomon in 1952. The honor was voted on by the Board of Governors, to save the full Academy membership from reading subtitles. (Today the nominees are chosen by an Academy-approved Select Committee). Costa-Gavras’s Z (1969), nominated for best picture and best foreign language Film (it won the latter), was a landmark border crossing and, in 2020, Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite broke the language barrier by becoming the first non-English language film to win best picture. However, of all the foreign-born incursions into top-tier Oscar territory, the first breakthrough is the most curious. At a time when subtitled films were a species of exotica, and with no major studio backing, Jean Renoir’s antiwar classic La Grande Illusion (1937) — easily translated as Grand Illusion — landed a nomination in the best picture slot, which was then called outstanding production and included ten candidates. (The other nominees were Boys Town , The Citadel , Pygmalion , Test Pilot [all MGM] , Four Daughters , The Adventures of Robin Hood , Jezebel [Warner Bros.], Alexander’s Ragtime Band [20th Century-Fox] and You Can’t Take It with You [Columbia] . The last, directed by Frank Capra, won.) To be sure, in 1949 a British invader, Laurence Olivier’s Hamlet , won best picture, but it was at least in English and credited to an A-list screenwriter. But how did Grand Illusion manage to crash the exclusive party? Poster art for ‘La Grande Illusion’ circa 1937. In 1938, Jean Renoir was not a known name in the US, much less a world-famous auteur. It seems unbelievable that two of his early masterpieces — Boudu Saved from Drowning (1932) and The Crime of Monsieur Lange (1936) were not released in the US until 1967 and 1964 respectively. Renoir’s version of Maxim Gorky’s The Lower Depths (1936) and his Popular Front documentary The People of France (1936) got only modest arthouse circulation and critical attention, with reviewers sure to identify the director as “the son of the famous French impressionist Auguste Renoir.” Only after Grand Illusion was Renoir acknowledged in his own right as a French master in another medium. Made in Paris by Les Realisation d’Art Cinematographyque, Grand Illusion was distributed stateside by World Pictures Corp., operated by the legendary foreign film magnate Irvin Shapiro, who began his career importing The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (1920) and capped it by exporting The Evil Dead (1985). Like almost all films about the Great War made in its aftermath but before its sequel, it is somber in tone and pacificist in sentiment. There are no scenes of thrilling aerial combat or over-the-top attacks in no man’s land. “A War Story without War Scenes!” warned the advertising. Renoir knew the material first hand, having served as both a cavalry officer and a pilot in the Great War and been wounded twice. Two French pilots — Captain de Boeldieu (Pierre Fresnay), a white-gloved aristocrat, and Lieutenant Maréchal (Jean Gabin), a gruff former machinist — are shot down over German lines by the ramrod-straight Prussian aviator Captain von Rauffenstein (Erich von Stroheim). A chivalric knight of the air, von Rauffenstein plays the gracious host to his prisoner-guests before they must depart for a prison camp. The accommodations in the German POW camp are not half bad and the company is great. De Boeldieu and Marechal encounter a diverse crew of colorful countrymen — a comedian, a literary scholar, and the son of a wealthy Jewish family, Lieutenant Rosenthal (Marcel Dalio), a stalwart solider who generously shares his bountiful food parcels. (The affirmative portrait of Rosenthal was certainly by way of apology for the treatment of the most famous Jew in French military history, Captain Alfred Dreyfus, who had just died in 1935.) Of course, the prisoners are digging a tunnel to escape. “A golf course is for golf, a tennis court for tennis, a prison camp for escape,” observes de Boeldieu. When not excavating and eating Rosenthal’s bread and cheese, the men rehearse for a musical comedy performance featuring a chorus line of men in drag. The shenanigans are interrupted by news that the French have retaken Fort Douaumont, marking the end of the carnage at Verdun. In an outburst of patriotism, the prisoners rise to sing “La Marseillaise,” a scene that ranks as the second most stirring rendition of the French National anthem in motion picture history. As recidivist would-be escapees, de Boeldieu, Marechal, and Rosenthal are transferred to an impregnable medieval fortress, commanded by Captain von Rauffenstein, now burnt, broken in body, and wearing a neck brace. Knowing their days of bloodline privilege are numbered, the German and the French aristocrat bond, their class affinities binding them more tightly than the uniforms that separate them. Renoir told film historian Arthur Knight that if a French farmer and a French financier dined together, they would sit in uncomfortable silence, but if a French farmer and a Chinese farmer dined together, they would find plenty to talk about. Still, a French prisoner must do his duty: de Boeldieu gallantly stages a diversion so Maréchal and Rosenthal can escape, during which a reluctant von Rauffenstein is forced to shoot his class comrade. On his death bed, de Boeldieu accepts the fortunes of war as Von Ruffenstein grieves. The third act finds Maréchal and Rosenthal scurrying through the woods and fields, squabbling and miserable, until they come upon a farmhouse run by a fetching German war widow (Dita Parlo) with an adorable daughter. She takes them in, gives them shelter and food, and falls hard for Marechal, 1937 being the year of peak Jean Gabin. In too short a time, though, the pair must leave the idyll. Against odds, they escape into Switzerland. The guards on the German side see no point in firing as, in the distance, the men plod through the snow to freedom. In Great War territory, this counts as a happy ending. Marcel Dalio, Jean Gabin and Pierre Fresnay in ‘La Grande Illusion.’ Everett On June 8, 1937, La Grande Illusion premiered at the 1250-seat Marivaux Theater in Paris, to a packed house made up of “members of Paris society, Paris cinema and theater circles, writers and press representatives” who, at the end, “gave long and loud applause.” The French critics, then as now a surly and hard-to-please lot, were unanimous in praise: “an important and extremely happy event in French cinema history” ( Le Temps ); “a masterpiece of cinema”; ( Mariane ); and “a very fine film, a beautiful human work” ( Oeuvre ). In the theater that night was Pierre Autre, Motion Picture Herald ’s man in Paris, who first sent word back to American readers, a rave that has stood the test of time. “ La Grande Illusion is, by far, the best French film of the year, up to date — in fact, it is one of the best French films ever made.” The Hollywood Reporter also predicted that “the smash hit” should “go well in the States.” It did better than well. In America, Grand Illusion became the most widely circulated and highly praised foreign film of the 1930s. On Sept. 12, 1938, Grand Illusion opened at the newly refurbished Filmarte Theater in New York with columnist Dorothy Thompson, novelist Fannie Hurst, playwright Clifford Odets, and actress Aline MacMahon in attendance. The Filmarte was run by a pioneering importer of foreign film, Jean H. Lenauer, whose arthouse was emblematic of what were called “sure seaters” in the trade because a small but devoted clientele was sure to buy a ticket to whatever foreign film happened to be booked. Grand Illusion played the Filmarte for a record-breaking 27 weeks. The lobby was decorated with reproductions of Impressionist paintings by Auguste Renoir. Meanwhile, the word on Grand Illusion was getting out beyond the insular arthouse crowd. Samuel Goldwyn called it “the most brilliantly directed film I have seen in years — a challenge to Hollywood.” Producer Walter Wanger, director Mervyn LeRoy, and the actresses Lillian Gish and Helen Hayes also offered endorsements. The New York Film Critics named Grand Illusion the year’s best foreign film. The National Board of Review dispensed with qualifiers and named it “the best film of the year from any country.” The Film Daily ran out of superlatives and finally just said, “you owe it to yourself to see this picture — it will send you out thinking.” Some of the best notices went to von Stroheim, basically radioactive in Hollywood since Joseph P. Kennedy booted him off the set of Queen Kelly in 1929. In The New York Times , Frank Nugent chided Hollywood for its “folly in permitting so fine an actor to remain idle and unwanted.” Von Stroheim responded in character. “You can’t expect a director to enjoy acting when directing is the nearest thing to being God,” he said. “I have enjoyed acting in pictures directed by a director called Eric von Stroheim, and written by a writer called Eric von Stroheim.” To break out of the arthouse ghetto, however, Grand Illusion needed a transit visa into the mainstream exhibition market, namely a Production Code seal. On July 29, 1938, Irvin Shapiro duly applied for the imprimatur from Hollywood’s censorship regime. Unsurprisingly, the Code guardians asked for a few “slight deletions” — a shot of a prisoner rubbing a pair of silk underwear, the use of the word “damn,” and a reference to a prisoner who tries to escape dressed as a woman (“Quite amusing,” comments a friend. ”Not so amusing when a sergeant mistook me for one,” he replies.). Also concerning was “the racial angle in reference to Rosenthal” — that is, an antisemitic insult aimed at him once in anger, once in jest, by Maréchal. But this was a matter left “solely for [Shapiro] to decide.” Shapiro decided to keep the insults. On Nov. 23, 1938, after the requested cuts were made, the PCA issued Grand Illusion a Code seal. The Roman Catholic Legion of Decency also gave it clean bill of health, rating it “AI: unobjectionable for adults.” With the Code imprimatur, Grand Illusion spread out beyond the arthouses and played the RKO, Warner, and Publix circuits. Reviews and ads were careful to explain to the first-time foreign filmgoers that “English titles translate the dialogue.” The box office thrived on word of mouth, repeat business, and high school French teachers dragging their classes to screenings. Grand Illusion was also fortunate to hit the crest of an antiwar zeitgeist. Another great war, with less chivalric Germans, was looming on the horizon: in March 1938, the Nazis annexed Austria; October saw the invasion of the Sudetenland, and on Nov. 9-10 the Reich-wide pogrom now known as Kristallnacht was launched. For many Americans, a film about what Variety called “the futility of mankind’s armed conflict” had ominous relevance. Not that the antiwar message was universally embraced. Though Grand Illusion won “the most artistic ensemble” award at the Venice Film Festival in 1937, it was banned by the Italians under pressure from Nazi Germany on the grounds that the film “has an anti-German tendency and offends Germany’s honor.” Actually, what offended the Nazis was the sympathetic portrayal of Rosenthal. The Nazis also took more active measures to suppress the film. In 1938, film historian Herman G. Weinberg reported that on the very day that the Nazis moved in to Vienna [March 13, 1938], “ Grand Illusion was taken off the screen in the middle of a reel by the storm troopers.” Renoir regarded the shut-down “as a signal honor — and a decoration.” Jean Gabin, (left), Pierre Fresnay, (center), Marcel Dalio, (right) in ‘La Grande Illusion.’ In America, the reception of Grand Illusion was less violent but still passionate: isolationists and anti-Nazis alike adopted the film for their cause. On Jan. 12, 1939, a special “Congressional Night” screening of Grand Illusion at the Belasco Theater in Washington, DC was arranged for senators and congressmen because, said the management, “the picture’s indictment of warfare will be a message of interest to not only the Committees of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Relations, but to legislators generally.” The ardent isolationist Congressman Hamilton Fish (R-NY) blurbed the film as “an antidote to war hysteria.” From the other side of the ideological spectrum, anti-Nazis interpreted the tolerant and pacifist spirit of the film as a rebuke to Nazi eugenics and militarism. “It will give you hope for humanity and patience and inspiration in the fight against the Nazi syphilis,” said Mike Gold in the Daily Worker . In Los Angeles, the Hollywood Anti-Nazi League sponsored screenings of Grand Illusion. Ultimately, the critical buzz and cultural impact of Grand Illusion reached into the ranks of the Academy voting pool. The timing was fortuitous. In accord with newly agreed to protocols adopted by the Academy Rules Committee on Dec. 20, 1937, selection of the nominees for Outstanding Production was now open to all eligible voters (whereas only directors selected the best director nominees and actors the Best Actor and Actress nominees and so on). On Jan. 23, 1939, the nomination ballots were sent out to 4,000 Academy members; they had to be returned by February 3. By then Grand Illusion had been playing in New York since its premiere in July and in Los Angeles since November 1938. When the voting went down, every savvy person in the motion picture industry had certainly seen it. Its resonant timeliness and manifest excellence (everyone knew it was a work of genius on sight) catapulted Grand Illusion into the top ten. For Jean Renoir and Irvin Shapiro, the cliché was true: it was an honor just to be nominated. Jean Gabin and Marcel Dalio in ‘La Grande Illusion.’ The recognition from the Academy kept Grand Illusion circulating. In New York, after ending its run at the Filmarte, it moved over to the 68th Street Playhouse, another landmark arthouse. In September 1939, upon the outbreak of the war in Europe, World Pictures Corp. re-released Grand Illusion with a new publicity campaign tailored to the moment. “Never so timely!” exclaimed the ads. “They said the Europe of 1914-1918 would never happen again—but!” Renoir’s response — you can picture him giving a resigned Gallic shrug — was laconic. “In 1936, I made a picture in which I tried to express all my deep feelings for the cause of peace. It was very successful. Three years later the war broke out.” By then, von Stroheim had offered his services to the French army, which thanked him politely but declined. Back in Hollywood, he played sinister Nazis in Five Graves to Cairo (1943) and The North Star (1944). In 1941, Renoir also came to Hollywood. Darryl F. Zanuck, a great admirer of Grand Illusion , signed him to a deal at 20th Century-Fox, but after an unhappy experience with the Tobacco Road-ish Swamp Water (1942), Renoir moved to RKO for This Land Is Mine (1943), about French resistance under the Nazi occupation, and United Artists for The Southerner (1945), a social realist drama about sharecroppers that was a genuine hit. After The Woman on the Beach (RKO, 1947), a moody noir with Joan Bennett as the woman, he returned to Europe for a postwar blossoming in Technicolor that included The Golden Couch (1952), which exposed Americans to the Commedia dell Arte, and French Can Can (1955), set during the Belle Epoque. He later made his home in Los Angeles, where he died in 1979, still tormented by a leg wound from the Great War. The story of Grand Illusion has a coda that Captain de Boeldieu and Captain Von Ruffenstein might have appreciated. In June 1940, when the Nazis barreled in to Paris, Henri Langlois, the archivist-programmer of the Cinematheque Francaise, was desperate to protect his collection of French cinema — including the original 35mm negative of Grand Illusion which Nazi Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels ordered seized and destroyed. Before the war, however, at the first meeting of the International Federation of Film Archives, held at the Museum of Modern Art in 1939, Langlois had made friends with Franz Hensel, head archivist for the Reichsfilmkammer, the motion picture branch of Goebbels’s propaganda ministry. Hensel was now a Nazi major stationed in Paris during the Occupation. Going seriously rogue, he collaborated with Langlois to safeguard the treasures of the Cinémathèque Française, which Langlois had hidden in the basement of the Palais de Chaillot Hotel. Described by The Hollywood Reporter as “a Nazi who apparently cared more for cinema than party allegiance,” Hensel rescued the negative of Grand Illusion despite the film being deemed “cinematic public enemy No. 1” by Goebbels. When the Nazis confiscated the negative and shipped it back to Berlin, Hensel safeguarded it in the Reichsfilmarchiv vaults in Berlin until the Allied victory. Berlin was in the Soviet sector. In 1945, according to an account by Stuart Klawans in The Nation , the Russians transported the negative back to Moscow and deposited it at Gosfilmofund, the Soviet film archive, unaware of its value. Eventually, Soviet and French film archivists realized what they had. In 1999, a clean print of Grand Illusion was struck from the original negative and released by Rialto Pictures. This is the definitive version currently in circulation. It probably never happened but I like to think it is just possible that in 1939 Langlois and Hensel cut out from the film conference at MoMA and wandered up to the 68th Street Playhouse to catch a screening of Grand Illusion . *** Author’s note: I want to thank the indispensable Louise Hilton, archivist at the Margaret Herrick Library, for facilitating access to the Production Code files on Grand Illusion . THR

articles.title: Between ‘Summer House’ and ‘In the City,’ Lindsay Hubbard Doesn’t Have Time to Slow Down
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 18, 2026 8:15am Lindsay Hubbard Kristina Bumphrey/Variety/Getty Images Logo text Lindsay Hubbard is always on the go. Whether she’s at the summer house , somewhere in the city , or just tackling her everyday tasks as a mother, there aren’t many opportunities she turns down. “I’m a yes person. I’m not a no person,” Hubbard tells The Hollywood Reporter . It can be hard for the reality star to find time to fit wellness into her schedule, which is why teaming up with Florastor in support of their new Digest + Skin Renew Probiotic was a natural partnership. “Honestly, I don’t have a lot of time to focus on myself,” she says. “So the easier and more simplified that my routine can be, which is basically taking a probiotic in the morning, the better off I am.” Related Stories TV A 'Love Island USA' Season 8 Star on 'Dancing With the Stars'? Don't Bet on It TV 'The Valley' Picks Up Season 3 Filming to Capture Fallout of Jax Taylor Being Spotted With Ex-Wife Brittany Cartwright's Publicist Florastor’s Digest + Skin Renew Probiotic is formulated to work from the inside out, providing digestive balance and botanicals to boost younger-looking skin. Hubbard says the probiotic is particularly important in her daily routine because of its focus on fostering a positive gut-skin connection. “I love that [Florastor] has launched their Digest + Skin Renew, because a lot of people, including myself, don’t realize that your skin is affected from your gut. Beauty starts within, obviously. Like, we all say it, but do we actually know what that means?” Hubbard says. “The direct gut-to-skin connection is so important, and I love that they created this product for those of us who are always focused on having better skin.” Before the Summer House star welcomed her first child, Gemma, she used Florastor’s probiotic products and switched back to the brand after giving birth, she says. Adding the Digest + Skin Renew Probiotic is a convenient option for Hubbard, who juggles starring on two reality shows, motherhood and her stacked professional life. Lindsay Hubbard Courtesy “When I don’t have time to actually work out, go to the gym, or make it to my dermatologist, or even do a full skincare routine at night if I’m in the Summer House … with such a busy routine, at minimum, at least I have the Florastor Digest + Skin Renew,” Hubbard says. And busy Hubbard has been, as filming on season 11 of the Emmy-nominated Bravo series picked up last weekend, all the while the tail end of its spinoff In The City has been airing. Hubbard explains that amid the chaos, she finds time to focus on wellness in ways that work for her, including by leaning into the solitude that can come with being away from external pressures while filming Summer House . “When I’m at the Summer House and I’m not in mom mode and work mode and I’m just in Lindsay free-spirited mode, I tend to dance a lot,” she says. “I like to dance off any tension that I have in my body, and just be free. I’m always just moving. Are my workouts or wellness routines traditional? No, they’re not.” The weekend of July 10, Hubbard and her Summer House co-stars celebrated the show’s first Emmy nomination. “We had a great weekend. It was so much fun,” Hubbard says. “The vibes were high. It was one of the best first weekends that we’ve ever had at Summer House .” It was also their first weekend reunited and filming as a cast amid a mini shakeup, as Amanda Batula and West Wilson both exited the series. Hubbard said not having them in the house has been “business as usual.” She’s looking forward to moving past the headline-making scandal that plagued season 10 with the future of Summer House . “After this entire scandal, I just think everyone needed space from the drama. It was a pretty all-consuming three months of dissecting and asking questions, not getting answers, trying to investigate and figure out what the hell just happened; how did we get here?” Hubbard says. “And that was months and months [of] everyone checking in on everyone’s feelings and filming reunions, having two back-to-back TV shows on air. I think, just in general, we are all ready to put the past behind us and move forward in a positive, exciting, celebratory way.” Lindsay Hubbard on Summer House season 10. Charles Sykes/Bravo Hubbard teases a “fresh vibe” for Summer House season 11, which includes the addition of new faces, a new house and new dynamics amongst the friend group. “We have a new house. It’s a fresh vibe. We have some new people that you guys will be able to get to know,” she adds. “I think for the rest of us returning cast, it’s also a fresh start for us in so many different ways, whether it’s our friendships with each other or just rediscovering new sides of our personality with each other in this new fresh era. As with any season, you never know what could happen because things just tend to happen in our world. But we’re here for it, and we’re excited.” Before Bravo confirmed the season 11 cast, it was unclear if Hubbard and Kyle Cooke would continue with Summer House , as they’re now pulling double duty by also starring on In The City . And Hubbard doesn’t have any plans on saying no to any opportunities that Bravo may bring her way. “Listen, I’m a yes person. I’m not a no person. I think as long as I’m able to share my journey with the world, I’m going to,” Hubbard says when asked if she’s hoping to continue shooting for both unscripted shows. “And as we know, with any one of us at any given time, things tend to happen at any given moment. So having cameras around for all of it, I think, is nice, and we have the ability, not just with me, but with multiple cast members, to capture a lot,” she concludes. THR

Jean Catuffe/Getty Images If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. Just ahead of the 2026 World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, France and England must go toe-to-toe to determine who will take third place. Broadcast live on Saturday, July 18 at 2 p.m. PT/5 p.m. ET on Fox, the match can be livestreamed on any streaming service that carries said network, namely DirecTV (with a five-day free trial ), Fubo , Sling and Hulu + Live TV .
